And the core of sin is from the heart, as it says, “do not stray after your heart” (Bamidbar 15:39)54Bamidbar 15:39: the verse of tzitzis — “וְהָיָה לָכֶם לְצִיצִת וּרְאִיתֶם אֹתוֹ וּזְכַרְתֶּם אֶת כָּל מִצְוֹת ה׳ וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֹתָם, וְלֹא תָתוּרוּ אַחֲרֵי לְבַבְכֶם וְאַחֲרֵי עֵינֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם זֹנִים אַחֲרֵיהֶם” — “and it shall be for you as a fringe, that you may look upon it and remember all the commandments of Hashem and perform them; and you shall not stray after your heart and after your eyes, after which you go astray.” Rashi explains that the heart and the eyes are “the spies of the body” (meraglim la-guf), the go-betweens for sin: the eye sees, the heart covets, and the body commits the transgression. R’ Tzadok builds on this that the root of sin lies in the heart — the dwelling-place of the yetzer hara — and hence that the thought of teshuvah in the heart is the beginning of rectification., for there is the dwelling of the yetzer hara; and they said in Berachos [61a] that it sits “between the two openings of the heart.”55Berachos 61a: “The yetzer hara resembles a fly and sits between the two openings [chambers] of the heart, as it says, ‘dead flies make the perfumer’s oil putrid’ (Koheles 10:1).” R’ Tzadok locates the seat of sin in the heart (desire), as against the mind (thought), which remains essentially pure.

וְעַל יְדֵי הַהִרְהוּר תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, דִּ״לְבָבוֹ יָבִין וָשָׁב״, בָּא לִרְפוּאָה דִּסְלִיחָה עַל לְהַבָּא; וּכְשֶׁשּׁוֹקֵד עַל תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ יוֹתֵר וּמַעֲמִיק בָּהּ, הוּא מַגִּיעַ לְתַקֵּן עַד הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ

And through the thought of teshuvah in the heart — “his heart understands and returns” — he comes to the healing of forgiveness for the future; and when he persists in his teshuvah further and deepens in it, he reaches to rectify up to the thought in the mind.

וְהַמַּחֲשָׁבָה הוּא עִיקַּר הָאָדָם כַּיָּדוּעַ בַּסְּפָרִים, דְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהָאָדָם מְחַשֵּׁב שָׁם הוּא כֻּלּוֹ; וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה [לד, י] ״הָרְשָׁעִים הֵן בִּרְשׁוּת לִבָּן, וְהַצַּדִּיקִים לִבָּן בִּרְשׁוּתָן״

And the thought is the essence of the person, as is known in the sacred works — for wherever a person thinks, there is his whole self; and regarding this they said in Bereishis Rabbah [34:10], “the wicked are in the control of their heart, but the righteous — their heart is in their control,”56Bereishis Rabbah 34:10: “The wicked are in the control of their heart, but the righteous — their heart is in their control,” each proven from verses. R’ Tzadok infers that the mind (not the heart) is the person’s essence: in the righteous the heart’s desire follows the mind’s clear thought, whereas in the wicked the mind is dragged after the heart. Tanya on the mind-heart structure. Tanya, Likkutei Amarim ch. 12 (12:5 in Sefaria's segmentation), states the classic principle: "המוח שליט על הלב ... בתולדתו וטבע יצירתו" — the mind rules over the heart by the nature of man's creation. Even when desire remains alive in the heart, a person can prevent it from passing from potential into actual thought, speech, and deed by directing the will in the mind. Chapter 30 repeats the practical consequence: a person is expected to restrain the spirit of desire in his heart because the mind is naturally given governing power. This is an exceptionally close parallel to R' Tzadok's use of Bereishis Rabbah that "the righteous have their heart in their control." R' Tzadok goes farther in identifying the clear mind as the person's essential human point, while the heart is the seat where desire and the yetzer are felt. Tanya supplies the avodah-psychology: righteousness does not require that every unwanted feeling disappear before one can be called a tzaddik in the relevant behavioral sense; it requires that the Divine-directed mind govern what the heart is allowed to express. This also clarifies why teshuvah can begin in a single true turn of da'as even before every emotional residue has been healed.

מְבֹאָר דְּהַלֵּב אֵינוֹ עִיקַּר הָאָדָם, וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ עִיקָּרוֹ הוּא הַמּוֹחַ; וּבִרְשָׁעִים מַחֲשֶׁבֶת הַמּוֹחַ נִמְשְׁכָה אַחַר הָרָצוֹן שֶׁבַּלֵּב, וְהַצַּדִּיקִים בְּהֵיפֶךְ — רְצוֹן הַלֵּב נִמְשֶׁכֶת אַחַר מַחֲשֶׁבֶת הַמּוֹחַ

which shows that the heart is not the essence of the person; perforce his essence is the mind. In the wicked, the mind’s thought is drawn after the desire of the heart; in the righteous, the reverse — the heart’s desire is drawn after the mind’s thought,
שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ טָהוֹר בְּתוֹלָדָה, וְאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה בְּלִבּוֹ רַק מַה שֶּׁמֵּבִין בְּשִׂכְלוֹ וְחָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁהוּא טוֹב וּרְצוֹן השי"ת
which is wholly pure by nature, and he desires in his heart only what he understands in his intellect and wisdom to be good and the will of Hashem.
וְאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּסוֹטָה ״אֵין אָדָם עוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְנַס בּוֹ רוּחַ שְׁטוּת״, כִּי מִצַּד רוּחַ חָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ אֵין מַנִּיחַ לַחֲטוֹא כְּלָל

And they said in the first chapter of Sotah [3a], “a person does not transgress unless a spirit of folly has entered him,” for from the side of the spirit of wisdom in the mind he would not sin at all.57Sotah 3a: “Reish Lakish said: A person does not commit a transgression unless a spirit of folly [ruach shtus] has entered him, as it says, ‘if any man’s wife go aside [tisteh]’ — read tishteh, [she acts as one who] became foolish.” R’ Tzadok: from the side of the mind’s “spirit of wisdom” one would never sin; teshuvah re-installs that spirit of wisdom in place of the folly.

רַק שהשי"ת יָצַר אֶת הָאָדָם בַּעַל בְּחִירָה; וְעַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמִּתְחָרֵט בַּלֵּב וְרוֹצֶה מֵעַתָּה לִהְיוֹת טוֹב, הוּא מְגָרֵשׁ רוּחַ שְׁטוּת שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ, וְחוֹזֵר לִיכָּנֵס רוּחַ חָכְמָה תַּחְתָּיו

only that Hashem created man with free choice; and through teshuvah — regretting in the heart and desiring from now on to be good — he expels the spirit of folly from the mind, and the spirit of wisdom re-enters in its place.

וּכְשֶׁנִּקְבַּע בּוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לִבּוֹ בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא יֶחֱטָא עוֹד, עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִמֵּילָא נִתְקַן הַקּוֹדֵם; וְזֶהוּ ״עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד״ — מְקוֹם מַחְצַב הַנְּשָׁמוֹת, שֶׁאֵין יַד הַמַּלְאָכִים מַשֶּׂגֶת שָׁם

And when it is fixed in him until his heart is in his control, that he will not sin again — through this the past is of itself rectified; and this is “up to the Throne of Glory” — the quarry-place of souls, where the hand of the angels does not reach.58R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §217): “The essence of the person is the thoughts, reflections, and desires of mind and heart — this is the spirituality of man; whereas the body is physical, called ‘the flesh of man’… ‘the likeness of a man upon the Throne’ (Yechezkel 1:26) — and it is the source-quarry of the souls.” This illuminates §2-1’s ladder of nefesh–ruach–neshamah reaching “the Throne of Glory”: since a man in essence is his thought, and the root of the thinking soul is the “likeness of a man upon the Throne,” the very quarry of souls, the penitent’s thought ascends to its own Source and draws healing down through all three worlds.59R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §144): “In the place where a person’s thought is — there is the whole person; for the essence of the person is not the body but the nefesh, and the nefesh is nothing but the power of thinking, reflecting, and desiring within a man; and the place to which his thought cleaves — such is the entire form of the person at that moment.” This is the very hinge of §2-1: because “the thought is the essence of the person” and “wherever a man thinks, there he is entirely,” a thought of teshuvah does not merely settle the future — it relocates the whole man to the pure neshamah above, and so “reaches the Throne” and heals even the past.

items.h: The theme: Torah is the mind’s study of wisdom, drawing the heart after it — this is “the spice against the yetzer hara.” Yirah is the gate to that courtyard: without it a spirit of folly enters and a man’s own wisdom misleads him. Hence “if there is no yirah there is no chochmah” — and yirah is complete only when it arrives, through itself, at chochmah.

p: [ב] וְזֶהוּ הַתְּשׁוּבָה, דְּ״שָׁם כְּלוּם יֵצֶר הָרָע יֵשׁ בֵּינֵיכֶם?״ — כִּי עִיקַּר הַתּוֹרָה הוּא לִימּוּדֵי הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַלֵּב נִגְרָר אַחֲרָיו

And this is the [essence of] teshuvah, [alluded to in the angels’ words] “is there a yetzer hara among you?” — for the essence of Torah is the mind’s study of wisdom, that the heart be drawn after it.
וְזֶהוּ ״הַתּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין לְיֵצֶר הָרָע״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בָּתְרָא [טז.], וּבְקִדּוּשִׁין [ל:] ״מְשָׁכוּהוּ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ, אִם אֶבֶן הוּא נִימּוֹחַ״

And this is “the Torah is a spice [antidote] for the yetzer hara,” as they said in Bava Basra [16a], and in Kiddushin [30b], “drag him to the study-hall — if he is [hard as] stone, he will dissolve.”60R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §240): “The Torah is a tavlin to the yetzer, as the Sages said; and even one whose heart is not yet wholly clean of the yetzer — if he is filled with Torah as much as he needs, the yetzer itself is ‘spiced’ into a fitting thing; therefore they said (Pesachim 49b) that a talmid chacham may eat meat, but not an am ha’aretz.” This deepens §2-2’s “spice against the yetzer”: Torah does not only fence the heart off from evil — it tempers the yetzer’s own force into something usable, so that the mind’s wisdom, drawing the heart after it, turns the very drive that sinned into an instrument of service.61R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §212): “The Torah and prayer are both only for one who is lacking and seeks his completion — through prayer, or through the Torah, which is a tavlin [antidote] to the yetzer hara and straightens the deficiency of the heart. As it is said in Shabbos [89a], ‘is there a yetzer hara among you? then why would you need [the Torah’s] light?’ [so the angels argued] — and therefore the beginning of both is yirah, the recognition of one’s lack.” This is §2-2 in R’ Tzadok’s own words: the very sugya of the angels (“is there a yetzer among you”) together with Torah as the tavlin that mends the heart’s lack — the study of wisdom in the mind that draws the heart after it and subdues the yetzer.62Bava Basra 16a: “The Holy One created the yetzer hara, and created the Torah as its antidote [tavlin, lit. spice].” Kiddushin 30b: “If this repulsive one [the yetzer] meets you, drag him to the study-hall: if he is stone he will dissolve, if iron he will shatter.” R’ Tzadok: Torah is the mind’s wisdom that masters the heart’s yetzer. A Chassidic reading of Torah as the yetzer's tavlin. R' Tzadok's emphasis that the "help" from Above arrives through Torah belongs to a broad Chassidic pattern: the Torah does not merely suppress the lower force; it can season and redirect it. Tzidkas HaTzadik §240, already cited nearby, states this explicitly. Compare Tanya, Likkutei Amarim ch. 39, where even Torah itself can descend temporarily into kelipas nogah through ulterior motive and then "returns with" the person when he does teshuvah. The two directions illuminate one another: Torah enters the arena of the mixed human heart in order to refine it, and teshuvah can in turn liberate Torah that had been entangled with the person's mixed motive. This reciprocal movement fits the word tavlin, "spice," better than a simple weapon-metaphor. A spice works *within* the food; likewise Torah enters the powers of the person and changes their taste. The Izhbitz school repeatedly stresses that the human task is not to pretend the yetzer does not exist but to subject every power to birur until its true place in ratzon Hashem is disclosed.63Kiddushin 30b: the school of R’ Yishmael taught, “My son, if this vile one [the yetzer hara] assails you, drag him to the study-hall: if he is stone he will dissolve, and if he is iron he will shatter” — as the Holy One said to Israel, “My children, I created the yetzer hara, and I created the Torah as its antidote [tavlin]; if you occupy yourselves with Torah, you will not be delivered into its hand.” This is the “Torah as spice for the yetzer hara” that R’ Tzadok identifies with the mind’s study of wisdom, by which the heart is drawn after the intellect. (The same passage’s teaching that “were the Holy One not to help him, he could not overcome it” is cited by R’ Tzadok in the next se’if.)
וְנִקְרָא יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם ״תַּרְעָא לְדָרְתָא״ [שַׁעַר לְדִירָה] בְּשַׁבָּת [לא:], שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִיכָּנֵס לַחָכְמָה בִּלְעֲדָהּ

And yiras shamayim is called “the gate to the courtyard” in Shabbos [31b], for one cannot enter into wisdom without it,64Shabbos 31b: Rabbah bar Rav Huna: “Any man who has Torah but no yiras shamayim is like a treasurer given the keys to the inner [chamber] but not the keys to the outer — how will he enter?” — yirah is “the gate to the courtyard [tar’a l’darta]” of wisdom. R’ Tzadok: without yiras shamayim in the heart one cannot truly enter wisdom.
וּבְיוֹמָא [עב:] דָּרְשׁוּ עַל זֶה קְרָא דְּ״לָמָּה זֶּה מְחִיר בְּיַד כְּסִיל לִקְנוֹת חָכְמָה וְלֵב אָיִן״

and in Yoma [72b] they expounded upon this the verse, “why is there a price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?”65Yoma 72b: R’ Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of R’ Yonatan, expounding the verse “why is there a price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, seeing he has no heart?” (Mishlei 17:16) — “Woe to the enemies of the Torah scholars [a euphemism for the scholars themselves] who occupy themselves with Torah but have no fear of Heaven within them.” The same passage continues with R’ Yannai’s lament, “Pity one who has no courtyard yet makes a gate for his courtyard” — for Torah study attains its purpose only when it brings a person to the fear of Heaven. This is precisely R’ Tzadok’s image here: yirah is “the gate to the courtyard,” and Torah-wisdom without the fear of Heaven in the heart leaves a person, in the end, with neither.
כִּי מִשְׁכַּן הַיִּרְאָה בַּלֵּב, וּמִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצָאוֹת חַיִּים לַמּוֹחַ גַּם כֵּן; וְכַאֲשֶׁר אֵין יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם בַּלֵּב נִכְנָס רוּחַ שְׁטוּת, וְחָכְמָתוֹ מַטְעָתוֹ, וְיִכָּשְׁלוּ בָּהּ ח"ו

for the dwelling of yirah is in the heart, and “from it are the issues of life” to the mind as well; and when there is no yiras shamayim in the heart, a spirit of folly enters, and one’s wisdom misleads him, and he stumbles through it, God forbid.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ [אָבוֹת ג, יז] ״אִם אֵין יִרְאָה אֵין חָכְמָה, וְאִם אֵין חָכְמָה אֵין יִרְאָה״

And regarding this they said [Avos 3:17], “if there is no yirah there is no chochmah, and if there is no chochmah there is no yirah.”66Avos 3:17: “R’ Elazar ben Azaryah said: If there is no chochmah there is no yirah, and if there is no yirah there is no chochmah.” R’ Tzadok: the two are interdependent — yirah is the gateway into wisdom, and wisdom is the perfection of yirah (“the fear of a wise man, turning from evil”), not “the fear of a fool.”

כִּי רַק הַתּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין לְיֵצֶר הָרָע וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר זוּלַת זֶה; וְגַם שְׁלֵימוּת הַיִּרְאָה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ עַל יָדָהּ לַחָכְמָה, וְאָז יִרְאַת הַלֵּב עַל מְכוֹנָהּ — לֹא יִרְאַת כְּסִילוּת, רַק יִרְאַת חָכָם ״סוּר מֵרָע״

for only the Torah is a spice for the yetzer hara, and it is impossible otherwise; and the completion of yirah, too, is only when one arrives through it at chochmah — and then the yirah of the heart is on its true base: not the fear of a fool, but the fear of a wise man, “turning from evil,” and from it he will not budge.67R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §61): “in the blessing over the Torah we add”and make pleasant [the words of Your Torah]," which is not so in all the other blessings over mitzvos — for choice is in a person’s hand, and how does prayer apply? Only that [it is said regarding] “the inclination of the heart [of man is evil].”" Exactly the se’if: the Torah is the “spice” given against the yetzer, and we must ask that it be made pleasant — for it works by drawing the heart, not by overriding choice.

items.h: The theme: The angels, having no yetzer, are the utmost of yirah and hold that gate — but they cannot enter beyond it. Man alone, a creature of choice whose body inclines to impurity and who subdues it for Heaven’s glory, is himself the place of the King’s glory. And even he cannot reach that subduing by his own power: God’s own call, “Return, Israel,” is the arousal sent into his heart.

p: [ג] וְהַמַּלְאָכִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם יֵצֶר הָרָע הֵם בְּתַכְלִית תֹּקֶף הַיִּרְאָה, וְכָל עִנְיָנָם בְּאֵימָה וְיִרְאָה, וְזֶהוּ ״תַּרְעָא לְדָרְתָא״ דְּחָכְמְתָא
And the angels, who have no yetzer hara, are at the ultimate intensity of yirah, and their whole matter is in awe and fear; and this is “the gate to the courtyard” of wisdom.

וְחָשְׁבוּ לִיכָּנֵס גַּם לִפְנִים לְהַשָּׂגַת חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה, בְּטַעֲנָה שֶׁהָאָדָם מָלֵא יֵצֶר רָע וְאֵין בּוֹ יִרְאָה; וְעַל זֶה אָמַר ״שֶׁמָּא יִשְׂרְפוּנִי בַּהֶבֶל שֶׁבְּפִיהֶם״, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא [שַׁבָּת קיט.] ״אֵין דּוֹמֶה הֶבֶל פֶּה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֵטְא לְהֶבֶל פֶּה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ חֵטְא״

And they thought to enter also within, to the apprehension of the wisdom of Torah, with the claim that man is full of yetzer hara and has no yirah; and to this [Moshe] said, “lest they consume me with the breath of their mouths” — in the manner brought [Shabbos 119b], “the breath of a mouth that has sin in it is not like the breath of a mouth that has no sin.”68Shabbos 119b: Reish Lakish taught in the name of R’ Yehudah Nesi’ah that “the world endures only for the sake of the breath [hevel] of the schoolchildren” — the Torah of little children who bear no sin. When Rav Pappa asked Abaye, “and what of my Torah and yours?” he answered, “the breath in which there is sin is not like the breath in which there is no sin” (eino domeh hevel she-yesh bo chet le-hevel she-ein bo chet). R’ Tzadok applies this to Moshe’s fear of the angels — “lest they consume me with the breath of their mouths”: the sinless breath of the angels would overpower the breath of one who has sinned.
אֲבָל הָאָדָם מֵאוֹחֵז בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד, כִּי כָּל פֹּעַל ה’ לְמַעֲנֵהוּ — לְקִילּוּסוֹ, וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית הַבְּרִיאָה, גִּילּוּי כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרֵךְ
But man “grips the Throne of Glory,” for “all that God made is for His sake” — for His praise; and this is the purpose of creation: the revealing of His glory.

וְתַכְלִית הַבְּרִיאָה הוּא הָאָדָם, שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר יֵשׁ אָדָם בַּעַל בְּחִירָה וְגוּפוֹ נוֹטֶה לִמְקוֹם טוּמְאָה, וְעִם כָּל זֶה כּוֹפֶה יִצְרוֹ וּתְאַוְותָיו בִּשְׁבִיל כְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם — זֶהוּ עִיקַּר מְקוֹם כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים, שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַמַּלְאָכִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם יֵצֶר רָע לְהַשִּׂיגוֹ כְּלָל, רַק הָאָדָם

And the purpose of creation is man — for when there is a person of free choice, whose body inclines to the place of impurity, and nonetheless he subdues his yetzer and his desires for the sake of Heaven’s glory — this is the essential “place of the glory” of the King of kings, which the angels, having no yetzer, cannot attain at all — only man.69R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §187): “Words of Torah are oz [might] to a person — ‘and wisdom gives strength’ (Koheles 7:19), and ‘who is mighty? he who subdues [his yetzer]’ — for through it he overcomes his yetzer, as it says (Kiddushin 30b) ‘drag him to the beis midrash,’ and ‘I created the yetzer hara, I created the Torah [as its antidote]’ — and this is [the meaning of] ‘were the Holy One not to help him [he could not withstand it]’: the help and the assistance come through words of Torah.” R’ Tzadok here reads §2-3’s very proof-text (Kiddushin 30b, “were the Holy One not to help him”) exactly as the se’if does — the “help from Above” by which alone the yetzer is subdued is the Torah itself, the God-given oz that lets flesh-and-blood attain what belongs by nature to the angels.70R’ Tzadok — parallel (Sichas Malachei HaShareis §1): “(Bava Basra 16a) ‘the Holy One created the yetzer hara, [and] created the Torah as its spice.’ And the yetzer hara is the lowliness that comes to a person from the side of the body — as in Sanhedrin (100b) — for as long as [the soul] is not clothed in a body there is no room for a yetzer at all; and the Torah is the spice for this ‘garment.’” This is the se’if’s angels, who have no body and so no yetzer: the Torah’s chochmah is given to man precisely because he bears a yetzer.

וְדָבָר זֶה אֵין בְּכֹחַ אָדָם לְבַד לְהַגִּיעַ לִכְפִיַּית הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע בְּתַכְלִית, עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרֵךְ חוֹפֵף עָלָיו, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין [ל:] ״אִלְמָלֵא הקב"ה עוֹזְרוֹ אֵין יָכוֹל לוֹ״

And this — reaching the ultimate subduing of the yetzer hara — is not in a person’s power alone, until His glory hovers over him; as they said in Kiddushin [30b], “were the Holy One not to help him, he could not overcome it.”71Kiddushin 30b: R’ Shimon ben Levi taught, “a person’s yetzer overpowers him every day and seeks to slay him, as it says, ‘the wicked one watches the righteous and seeks to slay him’ (Tehillim 37:32); and were the Holy One, blessed be He, not to help him, he could not prevail against it, as it says, ‘Hashem will not abandon him in his hand’ (Tehillim 37:33).” R’ Tzadok draws from this that the ultimate subduing of the yetzer lies beyond a person’s own power — it comes only when God’s glory “hovers over him” and He helps him; and so the Holy One told Moshe, “grip My Throne of Glory.”72R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §219): “In accordance with the increase of da’as and chochmah in a person, so do the false imaginings intensify against them in his mind and heart — as in ‘he who adds knowledge adds pain’ (Koheles 1:18); and the Tree of Knowledge is ‘good and evil’ — for through the entry of good da’as, its opposite enters too, as they said (Sotah 21b) ‘wisdom entered, cunning entered.’” This is why §2-3 rules that reaching the ultimate subduing of the yetzer “is not in a person’s power alone”: the very ascent toward the chochmah of Torah rouses a correspondingly greater yetzer against him (Sukkah 52a, “whoever is greater than his fellow, his yetzer is greater than his”) — so that man, unlike the angels, cannot prevail “unless His glory hovers over him.”

וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר דהקב“ה אָמַר לוֹ ״אֱחֹז בְּכִסֵּא כְבוֹדִי״, וְלוּלֵי זֶה לֹא הָיָה יָכוֹל לְאָחְזוֹ; וְכֵן הוּא מַאֲמַר השי”ת בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא ״שׁוּבָה יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד ה’ אֱלֹהֶיךָ״ — מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ דִּתְשׁוּבָה לְהַגִּיעַ עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד, זֶהוּ רַק עַל יְדֵי עֵזֶר השי"ת בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּילֵיהּ שֶׁשּׁוֹלֵחַ לְלִבּוֹ

And therefore [the Gemara] said that the Holy One told him, “grip My Throne of Glory” — for without this he could not grip it; and so is Hashem’s own call, in an arousal from Above, “Return, O Israel, unto Hashem your God” — this rung of teshuvah, to reach up to the Throne of Glory (that his heart be in his control), is only through Hashem’s help, in an arousal from Him that He sends to his heart.

items.h: The theme: “Your God” marks a face-to-face recognition granted to each heart according to its portion — the Throne of Glory, the world of separation, in which levels genuinely differ. Faith is shared by all Israel without gradation; revealed apprehension is graded. David’s teshuvah works from the concealment shared by all, while reaching the Throne itself is Shlomo’s rung.

p: [ד] וְעַל הַשָּׂגָה זוֹ אָמַר ״אֱלֹקֶיךָ״ לְשׁוֹן יָחִיד, כִּי הוּא תַּכְלִית הַשָּׂגַת הָאֱלֹקוּת וְהַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכֵחַ דְּהשי"ת הַמֻּשֶּׂגֶת לַלְּבָבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּזֶה חִילּוּק בִּפְרָטֵי נְפָשׁוֹת, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד טוֹעֵם כְּפִי חֶלְקוֹ

And regarding this apprehension it said “your God” in the singular, for it is the ultimate apprehension of Godhead and the recognition of the “Present One” — Hashem — attained by the hearts of Israel, in which there is a difference among individual souls, each one tasting according to his portion,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר עַל פָּסוּק ״נוֹדַע בַּשְּׁעָרִים בַּעְלָהּ״ — בְּשִׁעוּרִין דִּילֵיהּ, כָּל חַד לְפוּם מַה דִּמְשַׁעֵר בְּלִבֵּיהּ

as they said in the Zohar on the verse “her husband is known in the gates” (Mishlei 31:23) — “in his own measures, each according to what he measures in his heart.”73Zohar (on “her husband is known in the gates,” Mishlei 31:23): “noda ba’she’arim — each one according to what he apprehends [measures, me’sha’er] in his heart”; the Divine “Husband” is “known” to each soul in the measure of that soul’s own vessel. R’ Tzadok: hence the singular “your God” — the graded, individual apprehension of the “world of separation” (the Throne, Beriah). Izhbitz-Radzin and the individualized measure of Divine apprehension. Beis Yaakov, Vayechi 24:1, emphasizes that the illumination of bechirah and da'as is not identical in every soul or at every time: what is "day" for one soul may be "night" for another, and even within a single Jew the clarity of da'as can expand and contract. The avodah established in the clear hour must therefore carry the person through periods when the light of choice and understanding is hidden. This is closely related to "לפום מה דמשער בלביה": the Divine truth is one, but the vessel through which it is presently received is particular. The point protects R' Tzadok's language from being read as relativism. Each soul has its own shiur, not its own Torah. The same Hashem is "known in the gates" according to the measure of the heart, while halachic obligation remains objective. The individualized apprehension concerns the depth, taste, and inner recognition with which the common Torah is lived.74R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §227): “All Israel possess a complete emunah in Hashem — in His existence, His oneness, and His providence — as it says (Shabbos 97a) that they are ‘believers, the children of believers’; and this is called the nefesh of the holiness of Bnei Yisrael. And when one merits more, they grant him ruach — that is, when the heart is further refined, until he feels it in the heart and passes from the rung of emunah to the rung of emes [truth].” This is exactly §2-4’s two tiers: the general emunah by which “Israel believe, without clear apprehension” — believing even what is not grasped at all — and, above it, the face-to-face “recognition granted to the hearts of Israel,” where emunah has ripened into felt emes.75R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §49): “Let each person know that in the very thing in which his yetzer overpowers him most, he is a prepared vessel for those very matters to be pure and clear through him; and in the things in which he sinned much, let him know that he is a vessel made ready to be, in that very thing, clean and pure of heart — as it is said in Vayikra Rabbah (21).” This gives depth to §2-4’s “there is a difference among individual souls, each tasting according to his portion”: the differentiation is not only in how much of the Divine light each grasps, but in which portion is his — and a man’s own portion is disclosed precisely at the point of his fiercest struggle, the place appointed for him to purify.76R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §177): “As they said (Avos d’Rabbi Nasan 37), ‘two who eat from one dish — each tastes according to his deeds,’ for the taste is not the same in all; and this is called a ‘secret’ [sod], which cannot be conveyed at all — for whatever can be told, once told is known to another, [so] how is it a secret? — as it says, ‘the secret of Hashem is to those who fear Him.’” Exactly the se’if’s face-to-face recognition: each Jewish heart tastes the Godhead according to its own portion, an apprehension that cannot be transferred.

וְזֶהוּ כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד, דְּעוֹלָם הַכִּסֵּא דִּבְרִיאָה שָׁם הַתְחָלַת עָלְמָא דְּפֵירוּדָא, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חִילּוּקִים וּפֵירוּד פְּרָטֵי נִבְרָאִים שׁוֹנִים; מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּאֲצִילוּת כּוּלֵּיהּ חַד

And this is the Throne of Glory — for the world of the Throne, in Beriah, is the beginning of the “world of separation,” which has distinctions and the parting-out of differing individual creatures; unlike Atzilus, which is “all one.”

וְנִקְרָא ״אֱלֹקִים״, כִּי הַמַּקִּיף הוּא בִּבְחִינַת עֲגוּלִים, וְדָבָר עָגוֹל אֵין בּוֹ חִילּוּק מַדְרֵגוֹת, כִּי לֹא נוֹדַע מְקוֹם הָרֹאשׁ וְסוֹף כְּלָל; רַק בִּבְחִינַת יֹשֶׁר שֶׁהוּא הַנְּשָׁמָה הַנִּכְנֶסֶת תּוֹךְ הַגּוּף

And it is called “Elokim,” for the encompassing light is in the aspect of “circles,” and a round thing has no gradation of levels, for its “head” and “end” are not known at all; [gradation is] only in the aspect of “straightness [yosher],” which is the soul that enters within the body.

וּמִצַּד הָאֱמוּנָה, שֶׁהוּא מַה שֶּׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל מַאֲמִינִים דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל בְּלֹא הַכָּרָה בְּרוּרָה, מַאֲמִין גַּם בְּמַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ מַשִּׂיג כְּלָל, שֶׁזֶּהוּ גֶּדֶר הָאֱמוּנָה, וּכְטַעַם ״וֶאֱמוּנָתְךָ בַּלֵּילוֹת״ — בַּחֲשֵׁיכָה וְהֶעְלֵם הָאוֹר הַבָּהִיר, שֶׁאָז מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁים בֶּאֱמוּנָה

And from the side of emunah — which is what Israel believe in a general way, without clear apprehension — one believes even in what he does not apprehend at all, for that is the very definition of faith; and this is the sense of “Your faithfulness in the nights” — in the darkness and concealment of the clear light, when one makes use of faith,

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּשַׁחֲרִית ״אֱמֶת וְיַצִּיב״, כִּי אֱמֶת הוּא דָּבָר הַמְבֹרָר אֵלָיו לְגַמְרֵי, שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִטְעוֹן נֶגְדּוֹ בִּהְיוֹתוֹ גָּלוּי לָעַיִן, וְהוּא מִצַּד הַשָּׂגַת הַחָכְמָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּרָכוֹת ה:] ״אֵין אֱמֶת אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה״

unlike the morning’s “emes v’yatziv [true and firm],” for “truth” is a thing wholly clarified to him, which cannot be argued against, being revealed to the eye — and it is from the side of the apprehension of chochmah, as they said [Berachos 5b], “there is no truth except Torah.”77Berachos 5b (and parallels): among the expositions on the manifold names for Torah, “‘emes [truth]’ — this is Torah, as it says, ‘buy truth and do not sell it’ (Mishlei 23:23).” R’ Tzadok contrasts the daytime “emes” (clarified, graded apprehension = chochmah/Torah) with the night’s “emunah” (faith in the concealed, equal in all).

שֶׁבָּזֶה יֵשׁ חִילּוּק — כָּל אֶחָד נִכְוֶה מֵהַשָּׂגָתוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּרָכוֹת נח.] שֶׁאֵין דַּעְתָּן שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם דּוֹמֶה זֶה לָזֶה; אֲבָל הָאֱמוּנָה שֶׁבְּהֶעְלֵם, בָּהּ אֵין חִילּוּק מַדְרֵגוֹת, וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל מַאֲמִינִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [שַׁבָּת צז.] שֶׁזֶּהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל

In this [revealed apprehension] there is difference — each one is “singed” by his fellow’s apprehension, as they said [Berachos 58a], “the minds of people are not alike, one to another”78Berachos 58a: the Sages taught that one who sees multitudes of Israel (six hundred thousand) recites, “Blessed is He who knows all secrets [chacham ha-razim]” — for “their minds are not alike one to another, and their faces are not alike one to another,” and He who knows all secrets knows what lies in each of their hearts. R’ Tzadok cites this for the principle that in the revealed apprehension of Godhead there is a genuine difference among individual souls, each one tasting according to his portion — as opposed to emunah, the concealed faith shared alike by all Israel.; but the emunah of the concealment has no gradation of levels, and all Israel are believers, as they said [Shabbos 97a] that this is the root of Knesses Yisrael.79Shabbos 97a: “Israel are believers, the children of believers” — and one who suspects the worthy is stricken; faith is the shared root of Knesses Yisrael. R’ Tzadok: because faith operates in “concealment,” it admits no gradation — every Jew equally believes; this equal-in-all concealment is David’s rung of teshuvah. Izhbitz-Radzin on emunah that remains when da'as is concealed. Beis Yaakov, Vayechi 24:1, explains that there are times when "אור הבחירה" and the person's felt da'as are hidden; therefore Chazal fixed Krias Shema and tefillah each morning so that the prior acceptance of Malchus Shamayim surrounds and carries him even through the later hours of concealment. This gives a practical form to R' Tzadok's distinction between emunah and revealed apprehension. The equal root-faith of Israel is not a lesser substitute for knowledge but the covenantal hold that persists when individualized spiritual clarity recedes. That is why David's rung can be associated with concealment without being a defect. Davidic emunah means the ability to remain attached precisely where the visible proof is absent — the spiritual condition in which teshuvah begins, before the person's past has been openly transfigured.

וְזֶה דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע“ה, שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ הַהֶעְלֵם הַשָּׁוֶה בַּכֹּל, וְכָל הַשָּׁב מִיָּד זוֹכֶה לִסְלִיחָה וּרְפוּאַת נֶפֶשׁ; אֲבָל הַהַגָּעָה עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד, הוּא דַּרְגָּא דִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ ע”ה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ ״וַיֵּשֶׁב עַל כִּסֵּא ה’ לְמֶלֶךְ״

And this is the rung of David HaMelech — the beginning of teshuvah, from the concealment that is equal in all; and everyone who returns at once merits forgiveness and healing of the soul. But the reaching up to the Throne of Glory is the rung of Shlomo HaMelech, of whom it says, “he sat on the Throne of Hashem as king” (Divrei HaYamim I 29:23)80Divrei HaYamim I 29:23: “וַיֵּשֶׁב שְׁלֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּא ה׳ לְמֶלֶךְ תַּחַת דָּוִיד אָבִיו וַיַּצְלַח, וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ אֵלָיו כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל” — “And Shlomo sat upon the Throne of Hashem as king in place of David his father, and he prospered, and all Israel heeded him.” Scripture uniquely calls Israel’s royal throne “the Throne of Hashem,” for the kingship of the House of David is the earthly embodiment of the kingship of Heaven — as the Gemara puts it, “earthly kingship is a likeness of the heavenly kingship” (Berachos 58a). R’ Tzadok therefore assigns to Shlomo the rung of reaching the Throne of Glory itself, in contrast to David’s rung — the teshuvah that rises from the concealment shared by all Israel. Maharal and the symbolism of the Kisei. Gevuros Hashem ch. 70, in explaining the seven things created before the world, identifies the Kisei HaKavod with absolute elevation and with malchus: "כסא" signifies kingship, the level at which Hashem is revealed as exalted over the created order. Teshuvah and the Kisei are both pre-worldly realities in that sugya. R' Tzadok's assignment of Shlomo to the second rung can therefore be read with precision: "וישב שלמה על כסא ה'" is not merely a royal metaphor but an earthly appearance of the level to which teshuvah reaches. For David the forgiveness is real while its final vindication remains hidden; under Shlomo, the gates open and the truth of David's past is publicly disclosed. The transition from David to Shlomo thus mirrors the movement from concealed teshuvah to the Kisei's revealed malchus..

items.h: The theme: Every king is the root of his whole nation, as the heart is to the body. The malchus of Israel’s kings is the yiras shamayim that rests upon them, over which one blesses “who apportioned of His glory to those who fear Him.” Enemies never ruled over David’s handiwork, for yiras shamayim gives them no purchase — and Israel’s fear holds in affliction as in good.

p: [ה] וּמַלְכוּת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ ע"ה אָמְרוּ עָלָיו מֵהַאי קְרָא בִּמְגִילָּה [יא:] שֶׁמָּלַךְ עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנִים וְעַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים, וּמִלּוֹת ״וְעַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים״ לִכְאוֹרָה מְיֻתָּר

And of the kingship of Shlomo HaMelech they said, from this verse in Megillah [11b], that he ruled “over the upper and the lower [worlds]”; and the words “and the lower” seem superfluous — 81Megillah 11b: “Three ruled over the whole world [ba’kippah]: Achav, Achashverosh, Nevuchadnetzar. And is there no other? Is there not Shlomo? — Shlomo had a different matter, for he ruled over the upper and the lower worlds, as it says, ‘and he sat on the Throne of Hashem’ (Divrei HaYamim I 29:23).” R’ Tzadok presses the “extra” phrase “and the lower” to show a king is the root of his whole nation.

וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ אָמַר דְּמִילְּתָא אַחֲרִיתָא הָוֵי בִּכְלַל מַלְכוּתוֹ, כִּי כָּל מֶלֶךְ הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ כָּל הָאֻמָּה, שֶׁעַל כֵּן נִמְשַׁל מֶלֶךְ בָּעוֹלָם כְּלֵב בַּגּוּף, שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַגּוּף וּמִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצָאוֹת חַיִּים לְכָל הָאֵבָרִים

perforce it says that a “different matter” was included in his kingship: for every king is the root of the whole nation — therefore a king in the world is compared to the heart in the body, which is the root of the body, “and from it are the issues of life” to all the limbs.82R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §68): “All the services of the body’s limbs, and the mitzvos performed through them, are only to straighten the heart; and the essence is the heart, for there is the dwelling-place of Hashem — as the Sages said (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2), ‘the Holy One is the heart of Israel,’ as it says, ‘the Rock of my heart’ (Tehillim 73:26).” This is precisely the image §2-5 invokes — “a king is likened to the heart in the body”: the limbs (the nation) exist to serve and actualize the heart (the king), the single root-organ that is the seat of vitality and of the bond with God, and from which all the rest draws its life.83R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §160): “A person’s soul includes all the souls of his servants and of those subordinate beneath him” — the ruler contains within his own nefesh the very collective he governs. This is §2-5’s premise made explicit: “every king is the root of his whole nation,” so that his dominion over “the lower” is no mere addendum — the nation is comprised within him at the root, and to rule its members is to rule what is already folded into his own soul.84R’ Tzadok — parallel (Peri Tzadik, Rus §22): “Shlomo his son merited all the lower wisdom, which is the Oral Torah; and this began from Rus, when the kingship of the House of David was built — which was the root of the Oral Torah.” The se’if’s Shlomo, “who ruled upper and lower”: as king he is the root of all he rules, gathering the whole of the “lower wisdom” into himself.
וּבִזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל תַּחַת מֶמְשַׁלְתָּם [שֶׁל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם] הוּא גָּלוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה, שֶׁהִיא מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם שֶׁמִּתְלַבֶּשֶׁת בָּהֶם לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יָדָם
And when Israel are under their [the nations’] rule, it is the exile of the Shechinah — which is the “kingship of Heaven” that clothes itself within them to bestow upon Israel through them.

שֶׁהוּא [הַיִּרְאָה] אֵצֶל מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁמְּבָרְכִים עֲלֵיהֶם ״שֶׁחָלַק מִכְּבוֹדוֹ לִירֵאָיו״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּרָכוֹת נח.], שֶׁבָּהֶם תַּכְלִית הַיִּרְאָה בְּתָקְפָּהּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּרָכוֹת לד:] ״מֶלֶךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁכּוֹרֵעַ שׁוּב אֵינוֹ זוֹקֵף״

which [yirah] is [essentially] by the kings of Israel, over whom one blesses “who apportioned of His glory to those who fear Him,” as they said [Berachos 58a] — for in them is the ultimate of yirah in its full force, as they said [Berachos 34b], “a king, once he bows [in prayer], does not straighten up again.”85Berachos 58a: “One who sees the kings of Israel says: ‘Blessed is He who apportioned of His glory to those who fear Him’; and over the kings of the nations one says: ‘Blessed is He who gave of His glory to His creatures.’” Berachos 34b: “A king, once he has bowed [at Modim], does not straighten up again” — from Shlomo, “he arose from before the altar of Hashem, from kneeling on his knees” (Melachim I 8:54). R’ Tzadok: the intensity of yirah belongs to the kings of Israel.

וְהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע“ה, רֹאשׁ לְמַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהוּא עָשָׂה הַשְּׁעָרִים לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ; וְאָמְרוּ זַ”ל עַל פָּסוּק ״טָבְעוּ בָאָרֶץ שְׁעָרֶיהָ״, שֶׁלֹּא שָׁלְטוּ אוֹיְבִים בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו

And this is the rung of David HaMelech, head of the kings of Israel, who made the gates for the Temple; and the Sages said, on the verse “her gates have sunk into the ground” (Eichah 2:9)86Eicha 2:9: “טָבְעוּ בָאָרֶץ שְׁעָרֶיהָ, אִבַּד וְשִׁבַּר בְּרִיחֶיהָ, מַלְכָּהּ וְשָׂרֶיהָ בַגּוֹיִם אֵין תּוֹרָה, גַּם נְבִיאֶיהָ לֹא מָצְאוּ חָזוֹן מֵה׳” — “Her gates have sunk into the ground, He has ruined and shattered her bars; her king and her officers are among the nations, there is no Torah; her prophets, too, find no vision from Hashem.” Rashi, citing the Sages (Sotah 9a), explains that the Temple gates David had wrought sank into the earth rather than fall to the enemy — “they were the handiwork of David, and therefore the enemies had no power over them”; and Eichah Rabbah adds that the gates had once done honor to the Aron, saying “lift up your heads, O gates” (Tehillim 24:7). R’ Tzadok reads this as the mark of David’s rung: his yiras shamayim, the root of Knesses Yisrael, gives the nations no purchase, so his handiwork can never come under their rule., that enemies never ruled over his handiwork.87Sotah 9a: “‘Sing, O righteous, in Hashem’ (Tehillim 33:1) — this refers to Moshe and David, whose enemies did not rule over their handiwork. David — as it is written, ‘her gates have sunk into the ground’ (Eichah 2:9)” [so the gates David made were hidden away, not captured]; “Moshe — for once the First Temple was built, the Tent of Meeting and its boards, clasps, bars, pillars, and sockets were stored away [not destroyed].” R’ Tzadok: David’s gates embody yiras shamayim, to which the nations have no purchase.
כִּי הַשְּׁלִיטָה הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר יֵשׁ לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ, וְיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע"ה, שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, ״לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי״
For [enemy] rule occurs only where they have some connection to that power; and the yiras shamayim of David HaMelech — who is the root of Knesses Yisrael — “He did not do so for any [other] nation.”
כִּי עִיקַּר הַיִּרְאָה הוּא בֵּין בְּטִיבוֹ בֵּין בְּעֵקוֹ, לֹא כְּמִנְהַג אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, כִּי יִרְעַב וְהִתְקַצַּף וְקִילֵּל בְּמַלְכּוֹ וֵאלֹקָיו

For the essence of yirah is [held fast] whether in one’s good fortune or in one’s distress — not like the way of the nations, “when he is hungry he grows furious and curses his king and his god” (Yeshayah 8:21)88Yeshayah 8:21: “וְעָבַר בָּהּ נִקְשֶׁה וְרָעֵב, וְהָיָה כִי יִרְעַב וְהִתְקַצַּף וְקִלֵּל בְּמַלְכּוֹ וּבֵאלֹהָיו וּפָנָה לְמָעְלָה” — “And he shall pass through it hard-pressed and hungry; and it shall be, when he is hungry, that he shall rage and curse his king and his god, and turn his face upward.” Rashi explains that this speaks of those who forsake the Holy One and rely on the kings of Egypt: when famine and siege overtake them, “he curses the calves and the baalim they had worshipped, and turns upward to beseech Hashem — who will not listen, for the decree has been sealed.” R’ Tzadok contrasts this fickle fear with Israel’s: the nations cling to their god only in good times and blaspheme in distress, whereas Israel’s yirah endures “whether in His goodness or in affliction,” and a Jew, when he is stricken, does not “cry out in complaint” (Rosh Hashanah 4a)..

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [ר"ה ד.] לְחַלֵּק בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּשֶׁמְּרִיעִין לוֹ אֵין קוֹרֵא תַּגָּר; וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא צַדִּיק גָּמוּר גַּם בְּיִרְאַת הָעֹנֶשׁ שֶׁלָּהֶם, שֶׁגַּם בָּהּ גָּנוּז יִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת

And as they said [Rosh Hashanah 4a] to distinguish between Israel and the nations, that a Jew — when he is stricken — does not “cry out in complaint”; and therefore he is called a complete tzaddik even in their “fear of punishment,” for even in it is hidden the fear of [God’s] exaltedness.89Rosh Hashanah 4a: “One who says, ‘this coin is for charity so that my children may live’ — he is a complete tzaddik” — the Gemara resolves: “here [a Jew], there [an idolater].” Rashi: a Jew’s heart is to Heaven, and even if he is mistreated in his lifetime he does not “cry out in complaint [korei tigar]”; but an idolater, if not repaid, blasphemes. R’ Tzadok: Israel’s very “fear of punishment” conceals within it the fear of God’s exaltedness, so a Jew is a “complete tzaddik” even there.

items.h: The theme: Shlomo’s kingship came from a different side — the middah of chochmah. Moshe’s wisdom was subordinate to his prophecy, the clear vision of the Written Torah; Shlomo’s is the lower wisdom of ruach ha-kodesh. That lower wisdom spreads even among the nations, which is why they did rule over Shlomo’s handiwork — the root wisdom being Israel’s alone.

p: [ו] אֲבָל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ ע“ה מִדָּה אַחֶרֶת הָיְתָה בּוֹ — הִיא מִדַּת הַחָכְמָה, וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה הָיְתָה מַלְכוּתוֹ; דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ [ר"ה כא:] ״בַּמְּלָכִים קָם״, רָצָה לוֹמַר בְּמִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁהָיְתָה לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע”ה שֶׁהָיָה רַק מִפְּנֵי מַעֲלַת חָכְמָתוֹ, דְּעַל כֵּן מָלַךְ עַל דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר, דּוֹר דֵּעָה

But Shlomo HaMelech had a different middah — the middah of chochmah — and from this side was his kingship; therefore they said [Rosh Hashanah 21b] “among the kings he arose [like Moshe],” meaning in the middah of malchus that Moshe Rabbeinu had, which was only on account of the excellence of his wisdom — which is why he reigned over the “generation of the wilderness,” the “generation of knowledge.”90Rosh Hashanah 21b: “Koheles [Shlomo] sought to be like Moshe; a bas kol went out and said, ‘there arose no prophet again in Israel like Moshe’ (Devarim 34:10). One said: among prophets he did not arise [like Moshe], but among kings he arose.” R’ Tzadok: Shlomo attained Moshe’s malchus-dimension (which flowed from Moshe’s supreme wisdom), but not Moshe’s prophecy.

כִּי כָּל חָכְמָתוֹ [דְּמֹשֶׁה] הָיְתָה טְפֵלָה לִנְבוּאָתוֹ וְנִמְשֶׁכֶת מִמֶּנָּה, שֶׁהוּא חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב שֶׁכֻּלָּהּ נְבוּאָה מִפִּי ה’, שֶׁהוּא בִּרְאִיָּה גְּמוּרָה וּבְאַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא מְאִירָה; מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן חָכְמַת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ ע"ה, הוּא חָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה

For all of [Moshe’s] wisdom was subordinate to his prophecy and drawn from it — it is the wisdom of the Written Torah, all of which is prophecy from the mouth of God, in complete “vision,” through the “shining glass”; unlike the wisdom of Shlomo HaMelech, which is lower wisdom.

דְּעַל כֵּן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע"ה מָלַךְ בַּמִּדְבָּר עַל אוֹכְלֵי מָן, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהֶם חֵלֶק בָּאָרֶץ וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל, וְעַל כֵּן לֹא מָלַךְ עַל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, שֶׁחָכְמָתוֹ הִיא חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה

Therefore Moshe Rabbeinu reigned in the wilderness over the “eaters of the man,” who had no portion in the land or in this world at all, and therefore he did not reign over the nations — for his wisdom is the upper wisdom,
אֲבָל חָכְמַת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ ע“ה הוּא ג’ סְפָרִים שֶׁעָשָׂה, שֶׁהֵם בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, שֶׁהוּא ״נְבוּאַת הַחֲכָמִים״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ”ן [ב"ב יב.]

whereas the wisdom of Shlomo HaMelech is the three books he composed, which are [written] with ruach hakodesh — that is, “the prophecy of the sages,” as the Ramban wrote [Bava Basra 12a].91Ramban, Bava Basra 12a: “Although the prophecy of prophets — which is vision and image — was taken [after the destruction], the prophecy of the sages, which is by way of wisdom, was not taken; rather they know the truth by the ruach hakodesh within them.” R’ Tzadok: Shlomo’s three books (Mishlei, Koheles, Shir HaShirim) are “the prophecy of the sages” — lower wisdom, which (unlike Moshe’s upper, prophetic Torah) spreads even to the nations.

וְהוּא כֹּחַ הַחָכְמָה הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים, שֶׁהִיא מִתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת גַּם בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זַ"ל [איכ"ר ב, יג] עַל פָּסוּק ״וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי חֲכָמִים מֵאֱדוֹם״, ״הָאוֹמֵר יֵשׁ חָכְמָה בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם — תַּאֲמִין״

And it is the power of wisdom that spreads into the lower [worlds], which spreads even among the nations, as the Sages said [Eichah Rabbah 2:13] on the verse “I will destroy the wise from Edom” — “one who says there is wisdom among the nations — believe it.”92Eichah Rabbah 2:13: on “her king and her officers are among the nations, there is no Torah” (Eicha 2:9), the Midrash teaches: “If a person says to you, ‘there is wisdom [chochmah] among the nations,’ believe it — as it is written, ‘I will destroy the wise from Edom and understanding from the mount of Esav’ (Ovadiah 1:8); [but if he says,] ‘there is Torah among the nations,’ do not believe it, as it is written, ‘her king and her officers are among the nations — there is no Torah.’” This is R’ Tzadok’s source that the lower chochmah — the order of wisdom belonging to Shlomo — spreads even among the nations, whereas Torah and yiras shamayim are the portion of Israel alone.93R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §189): “There are two kinds of apprehension of Godhead: one, from the side of creation — recognizing that there is a Creator — and this is called ma’aseh bereishis; the second, from the side of [Divine] governance — how Hashem ‘rides’ upon the creatures — called ma’aseh merkavah.” The first, drawn from gazing at the created world, is the “lower wisdom” of §2-6 that “spreads into the lower [worlds] and even into the nations” — for anyone contemplating creation may reach it (hence “one who says there is wisdom among the nations, believe it”); the higher — the knowledge of His governance — belongs to Israel’s Torah.

וְכֵן אִיתָא בִּמְגִילָּה [טז.] דְּגַם בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם נִקְרָא חָכָם, וּבְפֶרֶק הָרוֹאֶה דִּמְבָרְכִין ״שֶׁנָּתַן מֵחָכְמָתוֹ״ עַל חַכְמֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין אוֹמֵר ״לִירֵאָיו״, דִּלְיִרְאָה אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת, אֲבָל לְחָכְמָה יֵשׁ לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת

And so it is in Megillah [16a], that even among the nations one is called “wise,”94Megillah 16a: on the verse “then his wise men and Zeresh his wife said to him” (Esther 6:13) — which first calls Haman’s counselors “his friends” and then “his wise men” — R’ Yochanan taught, “whoever says a word of wisdom, even among the nations of the world, is called wise [chacham].” R’ Tzadok cites this as a further proof that the title “wise” is granted even to gentiles, since lower wisdom is not the exclusive portion of Israel. and in Perek HaRoeh [Berachos 58a] that one blesses “who gave of His wisdom” over the sages of the nations95Berachos 58a: the Sages taught that one who sees the sages of Israel recites, “Blessed is He who apportioned [chalak] of His wisdom to those who fear Him,” whereas over the sages of the nations one recites, “Blessed is He who gave [natan] of His wisdom to flesh and blood.” R’ Tzadok draws his distinction from the change of verb: the nations are given wisdom, but the blessing does not add “to those who fear Him” — for they have a connection to chochmah but not to yirah; only over the sages of Israel, in whom wisdom and fear are joined, does one say “who apportioned of His wisdom to those who fear Him.” — only that one does not say “to those who fear Him,” for to yirah they have no connection, but to chochmah they do.96R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §226): “Everyone can attain wisdom and words of Torah — even one who has no prior yiras cheit and no awakening-from-below stirring him to study — for Hashem is ever ready to bestow even without an awakening-from-below; and this is ‘He renews in His goodness, each day continually, the work of Creation’ — just as Creation itself was without any awakening-from-below.” This is why §2-6’s chochmah is the universally diffused power: like ma’aseh bereishis, it is poured out freely, not gated by the awakening of Israel’s unique service — so it “spreads into the lower and even into the nations,” whereas the yirah of David, root of Knesses Yisrael, “He did not do so for any nation.”

עַל כֵּן שָׁלְטוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵי שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ ע"ה, וְגַם זֶה רַק מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דִּלְעָתִיד נֶאֱמַר ״וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי״ וְגוֹ’; וְאֵין עִיקַּר חָכְמָה אֶלָּא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁשֹּׁרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתָם שֶׁבְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ שֶׁל כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל

Therefore [the nations] ruled over the handiwork of Shlomo HaMelech; yet even this is only from the side of this world, for of the future it says “I will destroy [the wise from Edom]”; and the essence of wisdom is only in Israel, whose souls’ root at the Throne of Glory is the root of the wisdom in the mind of every single Jew.97R’ Tzadok — parallel (Likkutei Maamarim §16): “Malchus is the root of human wisdom, which is the lower wisdom — the wisdom of Shlomo king of Israel; but for him his wisdom was in ruach hakodesh, ‘and God gave wisdom to Shlomo’ (I Melachim 5:26). And even the nations have a hue of wisdom (as they said,”there is wisdom among the nations, believe it“), but when Esav is ‘searched out,’ his wisdom too is lost, for all their wisdom is the opposite of wholeness of mind.” The se’if’s point: the roots of wisdom that are in every Jewish mind stem from Malchus — Shlomo’s distinct middah of chochmah.

items.h: The theme: David attained the opening of the gates; the manifest rectification of the past came only in Shlomo’s lifetime, who reached “up to the Throne of Glory.” At that rung there is no sin at all — “I shall fear no evil, for You are with me.” This accounts for conduct of his that looks like walking in the valley of the shadow, and for the answer given to those who questioned it.

p: [ז] וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [שַׁבָּת ל.] ״בְּחַיֵּי שְׁלֹמֹה בִּנְךָ אֲנִי מוֹדִיעַ״ כו’; וּבֵירוּר מַעֲלַת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע"ה הָיְתָה בִּפְתִיחַת שְׁעָרִים, שֶׁזֶּהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד [יִרְאָה] כַּנִּזְכָּר

And this is what they said [Shabbos 30a], “in the lifetime of your son Shlomo I will make it known,” etc.; and the [essence of the] rank of David HaMelech was in the opening of the gates — which is the rung of David, [namely] yirah, as mentioned.98Shabbos 30a (see the fuller citation above, on Siman 1): David was told his sin was forgiven, but “in your lifetime I will not make it known; in the lifetime of Shlomo your son I will make it known.” R’ Tzadok: David’s own rung was the opening of the gates (yirah); the manifest, retroactive rectification of the past belonged to Shlomo, who reached “the Throne of Glory.”99R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §20): “Their being revealed in actuality, manifest to the eye, was through Shlomo his son — like the building of the Beis HaMikdash, which is attributed to the name of David HaMelech, for he was the builder ‘in potential,’ and only through his power did it emerge into actuality afterward through Shlomo; therefore the essence is [attributed] to David’s name, but the revelation in actuality [came] through Shlomo — for it was not yet fitting to be revealed [in David’s own time].” Exactly the se’if: David attained the “opening of the gates,” but the making-known — the manifest rectification — came only in Shlomo’s lifetime.

וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הַהוֹדָעָה הַזּוֹ, שֶׁהוּא בֵּירוּר תִּיקּוּן הַקּוֹדֵם [כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל סִימָן א’], זֶה הָיָה רַק בְּחַיֵּי שְׁלֹמֹה, שֶׁהוּא הַמַּגִּיעַ בִּתְשׁוּבָתוֹ עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד, דְּיָשַׁב עַל כִּסֵּא ה’, וְאָז אֵין חֵטְא כְּלָל

And nonetheless this “making-known” — which is the manifesting of the rectification of the past [as I wrote above, Siman 1] — was only in the lifetime of Shlomo, who is the one who reaches in his teshuvah up to the Throne of Glory, “he sat upon the Throne of Hashem”; and then there is no sin at all,100R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §111): “In the era of the footsteps of Mashiach, the essence is only to bring out the precious from the vile — and specifically in the place of the yetzer hara and the surge of sins, ‘from there He will take you,’ precisely through teshuvah, as in ‘ben David comes in a generation wholly guilty’ (Sanhedrin 98a)… and David HaMelech is called ‘he who established the yoke of teshuvah.’” This is §2-7’s very structure: David founded teshuvah — “established” it, opened its gates — but its full manifestation, drawing the precious even out of the vile until the past itself is rectified, is a thing “made known” only afterward, in the son (Shlomo) and ultimately in ben David, in whose day it stands wholly revealed.101R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §94): “Sometimes a person attains an illumination and through it reaches yirah — and this is the ‘face of wrath’; and when through it he comes to ahavah, it is the ‘face of favor’; and by means of the yirah he has, he rectifies the wrath of the face, and it is turned to favor, and afterward he comes to love.” This is the inner shape of §2-7: David’s rung, “the opening of the gates,” is yirah — the “face of wrath” that opens the way; and the manifest rectification of the past, when that yirah is turned to favor and love, is the completion — which in the house of David was “made known” only afterward, in the days of Shlomo.

כְּטַעַם ״גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי״ — ״אַתָּה״ הוּא הַכָּרַת נוֹכֵחַ דהשי"ת, ״עִמָּדִי״ מַמָּשׁ בְּעוֹלָם הַכִּסֵּא שֶׁנִּקְרָא ״אֶת ה’ אֱלֹקֶיךָ״ כַּנִּזְכָּר

in the sense of “though I walk in the valley of the shadow of death I fear no evil, for You are with me” (Tehillim 23:4)102Tehillim 23:4: “גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי, שִׁבְטְךָ וּמִשְׁעַנְתֶּךָ הֵמָּה יְנַחֲמֻנִי” — “Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff — they comfort me.” In its plain sense (Rashi; Metzudat David), David declares that even when passing through places dark as death’s shadow he fears no harm, for Hashem is at his side, and even the “rod” of affliction is for his good and consoles him. R’ Tzadok reads “for You are with me” as the face-to-face recognition of Hashem “in the world of the Throne” — the rung of Shlomo, “he sat on the Throne of Hashem” — at which one “fears no evil at all,” since evil has no independent standing before that presence. — “You” is the face-to-face recognition of Hashem, “with me” literally, in the world of the Throne called “Hashem your God,” as mentioned;

אָז גַּם ״כִּי אֵלֵךְ״ וְאֶעֱשֶׂה מַה שֶּׁאֶעֱשֶׂה, ח"ו, אֵין כָּאן יִרְאַת רָע, דִּ״לֹא יְגֻרְךָ רָע״ כְּתִיב, וְאֵין דָּבָר רַע יוֹרֵד מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם; וְהַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכֵחַ הַיְינוּ דִּ״מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ״, וְאִם כֵּן אֵין מְצִיאוּת לָרַע כְּלָל

then even “though I walk” and do whatever I do, God forbid, there is here no fear of evil, for “evil shall not sojourn with You” is written (Tehillim 5:5)103Tehillim 5:5: “כִּי לֹא אֵל חָפֵץ רֶשַׁע אָתָּה, לֹא יְגֻרְךָ רָע” — “For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil cannot dwell with You.” Rashi: “lo yegurcha ra — evil does not sojourn beside You.” R’ Tzadok takes this literally for the highest rung: since “evil shall not sojourn with You,” no evil thing descends from Heaven, and “the whole earth is full of His glory” — so evil has no real existence at all, and one who is gripped in that recognition fears no evil even as he walks through the “valley of the shadow.”, and no evil thing descends from Heaven; and the face-to-face recognition is that “the whole earth is full of His glory” — and if so, there is no [independent] existence for evil at all.

וְזֶה טַעַם מַה שֶּׁנָּשָׂא שְׁלֹמֹה נָשִׁים נָכְרִיּוֹת, וְגַם מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ עָלָיו בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי [הוּבָא בְּתוֹס’ פ"ק דַּחֲגִיגָה] לְשׁוֹן ״אֵין לְמֵדִין מִתְּקוֹעַ״, דְּהוּא תָּקַע עַצְמוֹ לִדְבַר הֲלָכָה, לְהַכְנִיס עַצְמוֹ לְעִנְיָנִים נִרְאִים כַּהֲלִיכָה בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת

And this is the reason Shlomo married foreign wives, and also what they said of him in the Yerushalmi [cited in Tosafos, first chapter of Chagigah], the expression “one does not learn [halachah] from Teko’a” — for he “drove himself [taka atzmo] into a matter of halachah,” to enter into matters that appear like “walking in the valley of the shadow of death,”104Yerushalmi (Kilayim 8:2; cited in Tosafos, Chagigah 2b, s.v. lisa): “One does not learn [halachah] from Teko’a [mi-Teko’a]” — read as mi-tokea, “from one who drives/forces himself” into a matter of halachah, i.e. Shlomo, who exposed himself to danger (marrying foreign wives, amassing horses) relying on his mastery. R’ Tzadok: this is “walking in the valley of the shadow” without fear, from the rung of “You are with me.”

וְעַד שֶׁבִּקְּשׁוּ לִמְנוֹתוֹ בְּאוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא [בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק], וְהֵשִׁיבוּ לָהֶם ״הַמֵעִמְּךָ יְשַׁלְּמֶנָּה״ — רָצָה לוֹמַר, אַתֶּם סְבוּרִים שֶׁהוּא עִמָּכֶם וְאֱנוֹשׁ כְּעֶרְכְּכֶם, וְאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא ״עִמָּדִי״ וְעַל כִּסְאִי, וְעַל כֵּן לֹא יִירָא רָע כְּלָל

until [the Sages] sought to count him among those who have no share in the World to Come [in Perek Chelek], and they were answered, “shall it be paid from you [rather than from Him]?” (Iyov 34:33)105Iyov 34:33: “הֲמֵעִמְּךָ יְשַׁלְּמֶנָּה כִּי מָאַסְתָּ, כִּי אַתָּה תִבְחַר וְלֹא אָנִי, וּמַה יָדַעְתָּ דַבֵּר” — from Elihu’s rebuke of Iyov. Rashi: “‘From you [me-imcha] should He requite it?’ — was the Holy One to take counsel with you about the payment He exacts from you? Do you suppose He collects according to your mind and your will, that you should choose the recompense and not I?” (Metzudat David likewise: is the reckoning of God’s justice to be settled from you alone, that you decide?). R’ Tzadok reads the phrase homiletically against the Sages who considered numbering Shlomo among those who have no share in the World to Come (Perek Chelek): they were answered, “ha-me-imcha yeshalmenah — is it from your measure that it is reckoned?” — you judge him as “with you,” a man of your own order, but he is “with Me,” upon My Throne, and therefore he fears no evil at all. — meaning: you suppose he is “with you,” a man of your measure; but he is only “with Me,” upon My Throne, and therefore he fears no evil at all.106Tanchuma, Metzora 1 (and Sanhedrin, Perek Chelek): “The Sages of the Mishnah sought to include Shlomo among [the kings who have no share in the World to Come], but a bas kol went out and said, ‘Do not touch My anointed ones’ (Divrei HaYamim I 16:22); and it returned and said, ‘Shall it be paid from you, that you refuse it?’ (Iyov 34:33).” R’ Tzadok reads ha-me’imcha yeshalmena as: he is not “with you,” a man of your measure, but “with Me,” on My Throne.

וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ ע"ה הוּא רֹאשׁ הַשָּׂגַת מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ דְּ״כִי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי״, וְעַד סוֹף כָּל דַּרְגִּין מִי שֶׁאָחוּז בָּהּ לֹא יִירָא רָע כְּלָל, וּמִמֵּילָא נִתְקַן הַקּוֹדֵם וּלְמַפְרֵעַ גַּם כֵּן

And Shlomo HaMelech is the “head” of the attainment of this rung of “for You are with me”; and down to the end of all rungs, whoever is gripped in it fears no evil at all, and of itself the past is rectified — retroactively as well.

items.h: The theme: Shlomo’s wisdom included knowing how to heal the past and to “sweeten the lupine” — turning the bitter itself sweet. All of it was already hinted to Moshe: the waters of Marah were sweetened through a tree, and there is no “tree” but Torah, the spice for the yetzer. The recognition “I am Hashem your God” belongs to the side of Yitzchak — the graded, contracted vision.

p: [ח] וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ זַ“ל [בִּקְהִלַּת רַבָּה] בְּחָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ ע”ה שֶׁהָיָה יוֹדֵעַ ״לְרַפֹּאות אֶת הַקּוֹדֵם״, רָצָה לוֹמַר לְתַקֵּן חֳלָיֵי הַנֶּפֶשׁ בַּחֲטָאִים שֶׁקָּדְמוּ; וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם שֶׁיָּדַע ״כֵּיצַד מַמְתִּיקִין הַתּוּרְמוּס״, רוֹמֵז לַעֲבֵירוֹת, כִּי ״רַע וָמָר עָזְבֵךְ אֶת ה’״, וְצָרִיךְ לְהַמְתִּיקוֹ עַד שֶׁהַמַּר עַצְמוֹ חוֹזֵר לִהְיוֹת מָתוֹק

And therefore the Sages said [in Koheles Rabbah] of the wisdom of Shlomo HaMelech that he knew “how to heal the past” — meaning to remedy the ailments of the soul in the sins that came before; and likewise what they said there, that he knew “how one sweetens the lupine [tormus],” which alludes to transgressions — for “it is evil and bitter, your forsaking Hashem” (Yirmeyah 2:19)107Yirmeyah 2:19: “תְּיַסְּרֵךְ רָעָתֵךְ וּמְשֻׁבוֹתַיִךְ תּוֹכִחֻךְ, וּדְעִי וּרְאִי כִּי רַע וָמָר עָזְבֵךְ אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹקָיִךְ, וְלֹא פַחְדָּתִי אֵלַיִךְ נְאֻם אֲדֹנָי ה׳ צְבָאוֹת” — “Your own wickedness will chastise you and your backslidings will rebuke you; know and see that it is evil and bitter, your forsaking Hashem your God, and that My fear is not in you, says the Lord, God of Hosts.” Rashi: “‘your wickedness will chastise you’ — in the end your own evil will bring suffering upon you”; and “‘My fear was not’ — the fear of Me was not in your heart, to fear Me.” R’ Tzadok takes “evil and bitter [ra va-mar] is your forsaking Hashem” as the very definition of sin — a bitterness that Shlomo’s wisdom knew how to “sweeten,” turning the bitter itself back into sweet. — and one must sweeten it until the bitter itself turns back to being sweet.108Koheles Rabbah (on Shlomo’s wisdom): among the things Shlomo “knew,” he knew “how to heal [le-rapo’us] the past” and “how one sweetens the lupine [tormus]” (a bitter legume made edible by repeated soaking). R’ Tzadok (noting he received the reading le-rapo’us, “to heal,” not hekirum) reads the tormus as sin — “evil and bitter is your forsaking Hashem” (Yirmeyah 2:19) — sweetened until the bitter itself becomes sweet (willful sins into merits).109R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §129): “The instant a person wishes to return, he comes to purify himself, and the [Heavenly] court assists him (Yoma 38b); and when they assist, a spirit of purity is added to him, and he adds to come and purify — and then the help from Above returns with greater strength, and again he adds below, and so it goes round and round.” This is how §2-8’s “healing of the past” acts upon “the ailments of the nefesh from prior sins”: the first turn toward the cure draws down an assisting purity, which compounds turn upon turn until the earlier sins are wholly healed — the wisdom “to heal the past” set in motion.110R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §70): “In the very thing in which a person’s deficiency lies — in that same thing, and through it, is his elevation — as the Sages said (Sanhedrin 70a) on ‘they sewed a fig-leaf’: in the very thing they had spoiled, they were mended; and along these lines, ‘on the day the Temple was destroyed, Mashiach was born’ (Yerushalmi Berachos 2:4).” This is exactly Shlomo’s art in §2-8 of “sweetening the lupine”: the bitterness of the sin is not merely removed but converted — the very place of the fall becomes the place of the rise, so that “it is evil and bitter” is remedied into the sweet at its own root.111R’ Tzadok — parallel (Dover Tzedek, Ner HaMitzvos §2): “Purification is in water — purified from here onward; but to heal the past, that is through da’as — ‘and Hashem is with him,’ as ‘I am Hashem your healer’; as it says (Taanis 27a; Menachos 110a) that ‘one who engages in the Torah of a burnt-offering is as though he offered a burnt-offering.’” The se’if’s Shlomo “knew how to heal the past”: the higher, da’as-rooted wisdom that reaches back and remedies the sins already done.
וְלֵיכָּא מִידִי דְּלָא רְמִיזִי בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, כִּי כְּבָר נִגְלָה הַכֹּל לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע"ה, רַק שֶׁאָז עֲדַיִין הָיָה בְּהֶעְלֵם וּבְרֶמֶז, וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת
And “there is nothing that is not hinted in the Torah,” for all was already revealed to Moshe Rabbeinu — only that then it was still in concealment and by hint, and afterward it came into revelation.

וְגַם זוֹ הַמַּדְרֵגָה, שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַתּוֹרָה, נִגְלֶה תְּחִלָּתוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע“ה בְּרֶמֶז בְּהַמְתָּקַת מֵי מָרָה שֶׁהָיְתָה עַל יְדֵי הַשְׁלָכַת עֵץ; וְאָמְרוּ זַ”ל ״אֵין עֵץ אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה״ שֶׁהוּא תַּבְלִין לַיֵּצֶר, וְעַל יָדָהּ הוּא הִתְהַפְּכוּת הַמַּר לְמָתוֹק; וְזֶה לְשׁוֹן ״וַיּוֹרֵהוּ״, וְתִרְגֵּם אוּנְקְלוֹס ״וְאַלְּפֵיהּ״, וְהוּא מִלְּשׁוֹן תּוֹרָה

And even this rung — which is the beginning of the Torah — its beginning was revealed to Moshe Rabbeinu by hint, in the sweetening of the waters of Marah, which came about through casting in a tree; and the Sages said, “there is no ‘tree’ but Torah,” which is the spice for the yetzer, and through it comes the turning of bitter to sweet; and this is the language “va’yorehu [and He showed/instructed him],” which Onkelos renders “and He taught him,” from the root of “Torah.”

וְשָׁם הָיְתָה הַתְחָלַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּצְטַוּוּ עַל קְצָת מִצְוֹת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר שָׁם ״שָׂם לוֹ חֹק וּמִשְׁפָּט״; וּ״מִשְׁפָּט״ הַיְינוּ דִּינִין דְּאִיפַּקּוּד שָׁם, דַּרְגָּא דְּיִצְחָק שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה, דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה נָפְקַת

And there was the beginning of the Torah, [when] they were commanded regarding a few mitzvos, as it says there, “there He set for them a statute and an ordinance” (Shemos 15:25)112Shemos 15:25: at Marah — “וַיִּצְעַק אֶל ה׳ וַיּוֹרֵהוּ ה׳ עֵץ וַיַּשְׁלֵךְ אֶל הַמַּיִם וַיִּמְתְּקוּ הַמָּיִם, שָׁם שָׂם לוֹ חֹק וּמִשְׁפָּט וְשָׁם נִסָּהוּ” — “and he cried out to Hashem, and Hashem showed him a tree; he cast it into the water, and the water turned sweet. There He set for them a statute and an ordinance, and there He tested them.” Rashi (from Sanhedrin 56b): “‘there He set for them’ — at Marah He gave them a few passages of the Torah to occupy themselves with: Shabbos, the red heifer, and civil law [dinin].” R’ Tzadok reads the tree that sweetened the bitter waters as the Torah — “there is no ‘tree’ but Torah,” the spice for the yetzer — and the “chok u-mishpat” as the beginning of the Torah’s dinim, the rung of Yitzchak and the side of Gevurah from which the Torah issues; and “va’yorehu [and He showed him],” which Onkelos renders “and He taught him,” is of the very root of “Torah.”; and “ordinance [mishpat]” means the dinim they were commanded there — the rung of Yitzchak, who is the root of the Torah, for “the Torah issues from the side of Gevurah,”

וּלְשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא [מַכּוֹת כג:] עַל ״אָנֹכִי״ וְ״לֹא יִהְיֶה״ ״מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה [שְׁמַעְנוּם]״; וְהַהַכָּרָה דְּ״אָנֹכִי ה’ אֱלֹקֶיךָ״ הוּא הַהַכָּרָה דְּ״אַתָּה עִמָּדִי״, וְזֶהוּ מִסִּטְרָא דְּיִצְחָק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [שַׁבָּת פט:] ״מַחְוֵי לְהוּ יִצְחָק להקב"ה בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ״

and the language of the Gemara [Makkos 24a] on “Anochi” and “Lo yihyeh” — “from the mouth of the Almighty [we heard them]”; and the recognition of “I am Hashem your God” is the recognition of “You are with me,” and this is from the side of Yitzchak, as they said [Shabbos 89b], “Yitzchak will show the Holy One to their very eyes.”113Makkos 24a: “‘Anochi [I am the Lord your God]’ and ‘Lo yihyeh [you shall have no other gods]’ — we heard from the mouth of the Almighty [mi-pi ha-gevurah].” R’ Tzadok: the foundational recognition “I am Hashem your God” (= “You are with me”) issues from Gevurah — the side of Yitzchak, root of the Torah.114Shabbos 89b: In time to come, when God says “Israel has sinned,” Avraham and Yaakov will not plead for them, but Yitzchak will argue their defense and then say, “Why do you praise me? Praise the Holy One” — and “Yitzchak showed them the Holy One with their own eyes [machvei lehu Yitzchak la-Kadosh Baruch Hu be-eineihu],” whereupon they lifted their eyes and said “You, Hashem, are our Father” (Yeshayah 63:16). R’ Tzadok: the clear, eye-level vision of God comes through Yitzchak (Gevurah/contraction).

דְּהָרְאִיָּה הַגְּמוּרָה לְנוֹכַח הָעַיִן הוּא עַל יְדֵי יִצְחָק, דְּהַשָּׂגָה זוֹ הַבְּרוּרָה לָעַיִן וּבְחִילּוּק מַדְרֵגוֹת הוּא מִצַּד מִדַּת הַצִּמְצוּם, הַמְצַמְצֶמֶת הַהַשָּׂגָה לְשִׁעוּרִין וּמַדְרֵגוֹת, שֶׁהוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן הַנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה

For the complete vision, “before the eye,” is through Yitzchak; for this apprehension — clear to the eye and in gradations of level — is from the side of the middah of contraction, which contracts apprehension into measures and levels; he [Yitzchak] is the first circumcised at eight days,
שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְקַן שָׁרְשׁוֹ לִהְיוֹת טוֹב מִתּוֹלָדָה, וְטֶרֶם יֵדַע מָאוּס בְּרַע וּבָחוֹר בְּטוֹב כְּבָר הוּא נִימּוֹל וְנִרְשַׁם בִּבְרִית חוֹתָמוֹ שֶׁל השי"ת

whose root is already made good by nature, and before he knows to reject evil and choose good he is already circumcised and sealed in the covenant, the imprint of Hashem, which belongs to his portion and lot — and he fears no evil at all, and through this the bitter is sweetened.

items.h: The theme: With Moshe the sweetening was in water — Torah, which is also “a drug of death” for those who go to its left. The corruptions at issue were of thought and wisdom, in which Israel had sunk in Egypt; sweetening the bitter in deed awaited Shlomo. All of Mishlei is founded on this: chochmah is clear recognition, mussar is what works upon the heart, and this healing is graded to each soul.

p: [ט] אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵצֶל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע"ה הָיָה בַּמַּיִם, וְ״אֵין מַיִם אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה״, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ גַּם כֵּן ״סַמָּא דְמוֹתָא לַמַּשְׂמְאִילִים״ [לְלוֹמְדִים שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ], וְנִמְתַּק עַל יְדֵי ״עֵץ הַחַיִּים״

Only that with Moshe Rabbeinu it was in the water, and “there is no water but Torah,” which also has in it “a drug of death for those who go to its left” [who study it not for its own sake], and it was sweetened through the “tree of life.”115R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Soferim §38): “When he merits that [the Torah] becomes for him a ‘drug of life’ — ‘the Torah is a spice for the yetzer’ (Kiddushin 30b), which is the essence of gevurah, subduing one’s inclination (Tamid 32a) — through this he merits the ‘joy of the heart of those who seek Hashem,’ the joy Hashem desires in His world.” The se’if’s Torah of the “waters”: a “drug of life” for those who learn it for its own sake, but a “drug of death” for those who do not — sweetened only by the “tree of life.”116R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §59): “Torah is called moreh [a guide]… and this does not mean [merely] the laws it teaches — for even one who learns Seder Kodashim is ‘engaged in Torah’ — but rather, as the Sages said (Eicha Rabbah, Pesichta 2), ‘the light in it returns them to good’; and the light of the Torah [which shields and rescues from sin, Sotah 21a] is only through those who go to its right [mayminim bah] — which is the drug of life.” This is §2-9 itself: the very same Torah-water is a “drug of life” to those on its right and “a drug of death to those on its left,” for the healing is the light within it — released when the Torah is learned for its own sake, and turned to poison when it is not.117R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §115): “When one innovates a matter in Torah, it must not come from any bias in the heart — that he wishes it so, or for self-glory, or to dispute another — but only from the longing to know the truth; and then, even if he errs, it is called ‘words of Torah’ and ‘the words of the living God.’” This is the axis on which §2-9 turns: Torah pursued “for its own sake” is study aimed only at truth — which is why “all of Sefer Mishlei is founded on ‘to know chochmah,’” chochmah being the clear recognition (“if the matter is as clear to you as your sister”); learned from bias rather than for truth, that same wisdom becomes “a drug of death to those on its left.”

וְהַיְינוּ קִלְקוּלִים שֶׁבַּמַּחְשָׁבָה וּבַחָכְמָה, שֶׁבָּהּ נִשְׁקְעוּ בְּמִצְרַיִם בְּחָכְמַת מִצְרַיִם; וְדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר נִקְרָא ״דּוֹר דֵּעָה״, שֶׁכָּל עֵסֶק וּמַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן שֶׁל השי"ת עִמָּם הָיָה בְּעִנְיַן הַדַּעַת וְהַמַּחֲשָׁבָה לְבַד, וְכָל הָעֳנָשִׁים שֶׁלָּהֶם הָיוּ כְּפִי הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה

And these are the corruptions in thought and wisdom, in which they had sunk in Egypt, in the wisdom of Egypt; and the “generation of the wilderness” is called the “generation of knowledge,” for all of God’s dealing and give-and-take with them was in the matter of knowledge and thought alone, and all their punishments were according to thought.
וְזֶהוּ רַק לָהֶם מִצַּד מַעֲלָתָם, אֲבָל בְּעָלְמָא קַיְימָא לַן [בפ"ק דְּקִדּוּשִׁין] ״מַחֲשָׁבָה רָעָה אֵין הקב"ה מְצָרְפָהּ לְמַעֲשֶׂה״

And this was [only] to them, from the side of their high standing; but in general we hold [first chapter of Kiddushin, 40a], “an evil thought, the Holy One does not join to a deed.”118Kiddushin 40a: “An evil thought, the Holy One does not join to a deed [to punish for it], as it says, ‘if I had regarded iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not hear’ (Tehillim 66:18).” R’ Tzadok: the “generation of knowledge” was exceptional — judged on the plane of thought — whereas in general thought alone is not punished as deed; the sweetening of bitterness in deed awaited Shlomo.
וְהַמְתָּקַת הַמַּר שֶׁבַּמַּעֲשֶׂה וּבַפֹּעַל לֹא נִגְלָה עַד שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ ע"ה, שֶׁיָּדַע הַמְתָּקַת הַתּוּרְמוֹס — דָּבָר גַּשְׁמִי הָרוֹמֵז לְמַעֲשֶׂה וּפְעֻלָּה גַּשְׁמִית
And the sweetening of the bitter in deed and in action was not revealed until Shlomo HaMelech, who knew the sweetening of the tormus — a physical thing that alludes to physical action and deed.

וְכָל סֵפֶר מִשְׁלֵי מְיֻסָּד עַל זֶה: ״לָדַעַת חָכְמָה וּמוּסָר״ — ״חָכְמָה״ הוּא הַכָּרָה הַבְּרוּרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זַ"ל [סַנְהֶדְרִין ז.] עַל פָּסוּק ״אֱמֹר לַחָכְמָה אֲחֹתִי אָתְּ״ — אִם בָּרוּר לְךָ הַדָּבָר כַּאֲחוֹתְךָ כו’

And all of Sefer Mishlei is founded on this: “to know chochmah and mussar” — “chochmah” is the clear recognition, as the Sages said [Sanhedrin 7a] on the verse “say to wisdom, you are my sister” (Mishlei 7:4)119Mishlei 7:4: “אֱמֹר לַחָכְמָה אֲחֹתִי אָתְּ, וּמֹדָע לַבִּינָה תִקְרָא” — “Say to wisdom, ‘you are my sister,’ and call understanding a kinswoman.” Rashi: “‘you are my sister’ — draw her near to you; ‘moda [kinswoman]’ — a close relative (as in ‘Boaz our kinsman,’ Rus 3:2), that is, keep her ever near you.” The Sages (Sanhedrin 7a) expound the verse for the clarity a ruling demands: “if the matter is as clear to you as [the certainty that] your sister [is forbidden to you], say it; and if not, do not say it.” R’ Tzadok takes “chochmah” here as this clear recognition — the foundation of all of Sefer Mishlei (“to know chochmah and mussar”) — the very apprehension of “You are with me” by which the past is healed. — “if the matter is as clear to you as [the certainty that] your sister [is forbidden to you], say it, and if not, do not say it,”120Sanhedrin 7a: “‘Say to wisdom, you are my sister’ (Mishlei 7:4) — if the matter is as clear [barur] to you as [the fact] that your sister is forbidden to you, say it; and if not, do not say it.” R’ Tzadok defines chochmah as clarified recognition, and mussar (Mishlei 1:2) as that which chastises and turns the heart from evil — the “spice for the yetzer” that mere wisdom (found even among the nations) lacks.
וּ״מוּסָר״ רָצָה לוֹמַר הַמְיַסֶּרֶת לָאָדָם וּפוֹעֶלֶת בַּלֵּב לַהֲסִירוֹ מִדֶּרֶךְ רַע, לֹא כַּחָכְמָה הַמְּצוּיָה גַּם בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁאֵינָהּ מוּסָר וְאֵין בָּהּ תַּבְלִין לְיֵצֶר הָרָע

and “mussar” means that which chastises a person and works upon the heart to turn him from an evil path — unlike the wisdom found even among the nations, which is not mussar and has in it no spice for the yetzer hara.

וְאָמַר ״לָתֵת לַפְּתָאִים עָרְמָה״ — הֵם הַנִּפְתִּים בְּיִצְרָם, [לָתֵת לָהֶם] עָרְמָה אֵיךְ לְהִנָּצֵל מִמֶּנָּה עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין; וְאָמַר ״יִשְׁמַע חָכָם וְיוֹסֶף לֶקַח״, כִּי הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁהִיא הוֹלֶכֶת וּמִתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת בְּלֵב חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד אֵין קֵץ

And it said “to give the simple shrewdness” — they are the ones seduced by their yetzer, [to give them] shrewdness how to be saved from it through the Torah-spice; and it said “let the wise hear and add lekach,” for it is the root of the wisdom of the Oral Torah, which goes on spreading in the hearts of the sages of Israel without end.

וְכֵן רְפוּאַת הַקּוֹדֵם, עַל יְדֵי הַחָכְמָה וְהַכָּרָה גְּמוּרָה דְּ״אַתָּה עִמָּדִי״ וְהַכֹּל מֵאִתּוֹ יִתְבָּרֵךְ, הִיא הַשָּׂגָה חֲלוּקָה בְּמַדְרֵגוֹת הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, וְעַל כֵּן הִיא מִתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת וּמְקַבֶּלֶת הִתּוֹסְפוּתוֹ כְּפִי מָה שֶׁהוּא רָאוּי לְחָכְמַת כָּל נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִי

And so the healing of the past — through chochmah and the complete recognition of “You are with me,” and that all is from Him — is an apprehension differentiated by the levels of the souls of Israel, and therefore it spreads and receives its increase according to what befits the wisdom of each particular soul.
