וְאָמַר בָּזֶה מִלַּת ״לֶקַח״, כְּטַעַם ״וְלָקַחְתִּי אֶתְכֶם לִי לְעָם״, שֶׁהַלְּקִיחָה בָּאָדָם הוּא גָּמוּר, וְעַל יְדֵי הַחָכְמָה פּוֹעֵל הִשְׁתַּנּוּת בְּשֹׁרֶשׁ — הִשְׁתַּנּוּת הַיְּדִיעָה וּרְצוֹן הַלֵּב בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ לְגַמְרֵי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁזֶּהוּ רְפוּאַת הַקּוֹדֵם

And it used regarding this the word “lekach [taking],” in the sense of “and I will take you to Me for a people” (Shemos 6:7)121Shemos 6:7: “וְלָקַחְתִּי אֶתְכֶם לִי לְעָם וְהָיִיתִי לָכֶם לֵאלֹקִים, וִידַעְתֶּם כִּי אֲנִי ה׳ אֱלֹקֵיכֶם הַמּוֹצִיא אֶתְכֶם מִתַּחַת סִבְלוֹת מִצְרָיִם” — “And I will take you to Me for a people, and I will be to you a God; and you shall know that I am Hashem your God who brings you out from under the burdens of Egypt” — the second of the four expressions of redemption. R’ Tzadok fastens on the word “ve-lakachti [and I will take]”: a “taking,” with a person, is total and essence-changing — like betrothal, an utter acquisition — and so the word “lekach [taking]” in Mishlei (“let the wise hear and add lekach”) denotes the way Torah-wisdom effects a change in the very root of a person’s knowledge and will, which is the healing of the past. — for a “taking,” with a person, is total; and through chochmah one effects a change in the root — a change of the knowledge and the heart’s will in its very root entirely, which is [precisely] the healing of the past.

sections.en: Great is teshuvah, for it overrides a Torah prohibition

items.h: גדולה תשובה שדוחה לא תעשה שבתורה.
“Great is teshuvah, for it overrides a negative commandment of the Torah” (the third — corresponding to Tiferes).

The theme: “Overriding a Torah prohibition” means teshuvah is accepted even where, by strict law, it should not avail — as with Menasheh, for whom God burrowed a tunnel beneath His Throne. Acher erred exactly here, not grasping that God’s hand is stretched out to receive penitents even against the line of the law. In the Yerushalmi, Wisdom, Torah and Prophecy were each asked the sinner’s remedy, and only the Holy One answered “let him do teshuvah” — for teshuvah stands above all three.

p: [א] ״שֶׁדּוֹחֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה״, הַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּתְקַבֶּלֶת וּמוֹעִילָה גַּם כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּמִשְׁפָּט שֶׁיּוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא [בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין קג.] בִּמְנַשֶּׁה שֶׁעָשָׂה לוֹ כְּמִין מַחְתֶּרֶת כו’, וְכַיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ [בִּפְסָחִים קיט.] עַל פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל

“That it overrides a negative commandment of the Torah” — meaning that it is accepted and avails even when it is not [within] the [strict] judgment that teshuvah should help, in the manner brought [Sanhedrin 103a] regarding Menasheh, for whom [God] “made a kind of tunnel,” etc., and the like [Pesachim 119a] concerning the willful sinners of Israel.122Yoma 86b: “R’ Yochanan said: Great is teshuvah, for it overrides a negative commandment of the Torah, as it says, ‘Saying: if a man sends away his wife and she goes from him and becomes another man’s, shall he return to her again? Would not that land be utterly defiled? Yet you have played the harlot with many companions; and return to Me, says Hashem’ (Yirmeyah 3:1)” — though a remarried divorcée is forbidden to return to her first husband, God says “return to Me.” R’ Tzadok: teshuvah avails even where the Torah’s own law would bar it. Maharal, Netivos Olam, Netiv HaTeshuvah ch. 2 (§13 in Sefaria's segmentation), comments on these two statements of R' Yochanan together: "גדולה תשובה שמגעת עד כסא הכבוד" and "גדולה תשובה שדוחה את לא תעשה שבתורה." Their juxtaposition is conceptually exact. The Torah's prohibition marks the order appropriate to a world in which a broken marital bond cannot simply be restored after a second union. Teshuvah, however, reaches the Kisei HaKavod — the source above the ordinary created order — and therefore the prophetic "ושובו אלי" can disclose a relationship whose possibility cannot be generated by the legal structure alone. This does not mean halachah is suspended for human beings; the divorced wife remains prohibited by Torah law. Rather, the mashal teaches the transcendent nature of the Divine reception of teshuvah: Hashem can restore the sinner to a closeness that the finite legal analogy would declare irrecoverable.123Cf. Arvei Nachal (Shabbos HaGadol), which treats this very sugya (Yoma 86b) — “teshuvah overrides a negative commandment,” the verse Yirmiyah 3:1, and the resolution “one case is an individual, one a community” — together with the difficulty of the Rif and Maharsha that R’ Tzadok resolves here.124Sanhedrin 103a: “Menasheh did teshuvah, and ‘and He received his entreaty [va-yeichaser lo]’ (Divrei HaYamim II 33:13) — this teaches that the Holy One made for him a kind of tunnel [machteres] in the firmament, to receive him in teshuvah, [past] the Attribute of Justice.” Pesachim 119a: “‘the hands of a man beneath their wings’ (Yechezkel 1:8) — it is written yado [His hand], the hand of the Holy One spread beneath the wings of the chayos, to receive penitents from the hand of the Attribute of Justice.” Chagigah 15a: after Acher sinned, a bas kol announced “‘Return, wayward children’ — except for Acher”; hearing this, he despaired of being received, and gave himself over to sin. R’ Tzadok: Acher failed to grasp that the “hand” receives even against the strict law. The Ishbitzer's reading of Menasheh gives a remarkable inner background to the "machteres." Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Prophets, II Kings 21:1, says Menasheh was born with an overwhelming yirah that human strength could scarcely bear. His sin, in the Izhbitzer's formulation, began from seeking ways to remove that overpowering awe "בכדי שיהיה בעל בחירה" — so that he would possess a felt field of choice — because the intensity of the yirah seemed to take choice away from him. Whether or not one translates every detail of this daring teaching into R' Tzadok's system, its relevance is clear: Menasheh's corruption is not treated as proof that no holy root existed. The very point that became distorted had an original holy form. That makes the tunnel beneath the Kisei especially meaningful. Teshuvah does not merely negotiate with the externally visible record of Menasheh's reign; it reaches beneath it to the buried root from which even the distorted search for "bechirah" had emerged. The Middas HaDin, judging the acts in their revealed form, has no argument for such a return. The Holy One "digs" beneath that plane and receives the soul from its deeper source. This is a characteristically Ishbitz-Radzin way of understanding why even the architect of the churban can become a baal teshuvah: the shoresh and the revealed history are not identical.125R’ Tzadok — parallel (Yisrael Kedoshim §8): “The churban was through the sin of Menasheh, as is explicit in Scripture — yet it was not destroyed in his days, nor even at once in the generation after him, for the Holy One is ‘long of patience, though He collects what is His’; and though they are a later generation, the root of Knesses Yisrael is one in every generation.” This is the same middah by which §3-1 says teshuvah “is accepted even where, by strict law, it should not avail”: the very Menasheh through whom the House fell is met not by immediate justice but by God’s long patience — the attribute that holds justice back and makes room for return, reaching (as the se’if says) even to one for whom God “burrowed a tunnel beneath His Throne.”
וּבָזֶה טָעָה אַחֵר כְּשֶׁשָּׁמַע אוֹתוֹ בַּת קוֹל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בַּחֲגִיגָה טו.], לֹא יָדַע שֶׁיָּדוֹ כִּבְיָכוֹל פְּשׁוּטָה לְקַבֵּל הַשָּׁבִים אַף נֶגֶד שׁוּרַת הַדִּין

And in this Acher erred when he heard that bas kol [saying “return, wayward children — except for Acher”], as they said [Chagigah 15a]: he did not know that His “hand,” as it were, is outstretched to receive penitents even against the line of the law.

וְכָל כ“ד דְּבָרִים הַמְעַכְּבִים הַתְּשׁוּבָה אֵין מוֹנְעִין לְקַבֵּל לְגַמְרֵי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ”ם, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר עוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה; ואע"פ שֶׁעַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה אֵין לְקַבְּלָהּ, זֶהוּ גְּדֻלָּתָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁפּוֹרֶצֶת גֶּדֶר דִּין הַתּוֹרָה

And all “twenty-four things that impede teshuvah” do not entirely prevent its acceptance, as the Rambam wrote — for in truth “you have nothing that stands before teshuvah”; and although by the Torah [-law] it is not to be accepted, this is the greatness of teshuvah: that it breaches the fence of the Torah’s own law.126Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 4:1–6: “Twenty-four things impede teshuvah”; but (4:6) “although these impede teshuvah, they do not prevent it — if a person did teshuvah from them, he is a baal teshuvah and has a share in the World to Come.” R’ Tzadok: “nothing stands before teshuvah,” which breaches even the Torah’s own fence.127R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §78): “(Berachos 10a) ‘what have you to do with the secrets of the Merciful?’ — but behold, Menasheh is of those who have no share in the World to Come, and yet Mashiach ben David and the whole holy chain would have been lost, God forbid, had [his son] not issued from him.” The se’if’s Menasheh, received in teshuvah against the very Attribute of Justice: the “secret counsels of the Merciful” reach where the strict law cannot.
וּבְעִיקַּר קַבָּלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה אָמְרוּ בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי [פ"ב דְּמַכּוֹת] שָׁאֲלוּ לְחָכְמָה כו’, לַתּוֹרָה כו’, לִנְבוּאָה כו’, עַד לקוב"ה — אָמַר ״יַעֲשֶׂה תְּשׁוּבָה״

And regarding the essence of teshuvah’s acceptance they said in the Yerushalmi [Makkos, ch. 2]: they asked Wisdom [what is the sinner’s punishment], then Torah, then Prophecy, until [they asked] the Holy One — He said, “let him do teshuvah [and it will atone for him].”128Yerushalmi Makkos 2:6: “They asked Wisdom: what is the sinner’s punishment? It said, ‘evil pursues sinners.’ They asked Prophecy: ‘the soul that sins shall die.’ They asked the Torah: ‘let him bring a guilt-offering and be atoned.’ They asked the Holy One: He said, ‘let him do teshuvah and it will atone.’” (R’ Tzadok notes the Yefeh Mar’eh’s reading, which includes “Torah.”)
וּשְׁלֹשֶׁת אֵלּוּ עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּרָכוֹת ג:] ״יוֹעֲצִין בַּאֲחִיתוֹפֶל, וְנִמְלָכִין בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין, וְשׁוֹאֲלִין בְּאוּרִים וְתֻמִּים״, שֶׁהֵם חָכְמָה, תּוֹרָה, וּנְבוּאָה

And these three are in the manner they said [Berachos 3b], “they would take counsel with Achitofel, consult the Sanhedrin, and inquire of the Urim v’Tumim” — which are wisdom, Torah, and prophecy.129Berachos 3b: on the conduct of the king and Sanhedrin at times of war — “they take counsel with Achitofel, consult the Sanhedrin, and inquire of the Urim v’Tumim.” R’ Tzadok maps the three onto wisdom (Achitofel), Torah (Sanhedrin), and prophecy (Urim v’Tumim) — the three “counsels” that teshuvah transcends.

וְשָׁלֹשׁ עֵצוֹת אֵלּוּ צָרִיךְ לְכָל דָּבָר, וְאָמַר ״שָׁאֲלוּ״ וְלֹא אָמַר מִי הַשּׁוֹאֵל, רַק רָצָה לוֹמַר כִּי הַתְחָלַת כָּל דָּבָר עַל כָּרְחֲךָ הוּא נִשְׁאָל וְנִמְלָךְ לִפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה יוֹעֲצִים אֵלּוּ אֵיךְ יַעֲשֶׂה, שֶׁיֶּשְׁנָם בִּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל; וְכֵן הֵם בְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִית גַּם כֵּן שְׁלֹשׁ דַּרְכֵי הִתְבּוֹנְנוּת הַלָּלוּ בְּכָל דָּבָר, מִצַּד חָכְמָה אֱנוֹשִׁית וְחָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ — דְּהַיְינוּ הַשָּׂגַת חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּנְבוּאָה אוֹ אוּרִים וְתֻמִּים וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ; וּשְׁלֹשׁ אֵלּוּ הֵם יוֹעֲצִים וּמַנְהִיגִים כָּל דָּבָר בַּעֲצָתָם, וְהַתְּשׁוּבָה הִיא לְמַעְלָה מֵהֶם, שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲמֹד עָלֶיהָ בְּשׁוּם עֵצָה אֱנוֹשִׁית, אֲפִילּוּ נְבוּאָה דְּהוּא הַשָּׂגַת אָדָם מהשי"ת; וְכֵן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם, מִכָּל מָקוֹם מֵאַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר נִמְסְרָה לִבְנֵי אָדָם וְ״לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִיא״, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲמֹד מִצִּדָּהּ עַל עֹמֶק מַעֲלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה

And these three counsels are needed for everything — and it said “they asked” without stating who asks, meaning only that the beginning of everything is perforce consulted and deliberated before these three advisors as to how one should act (advisors that exist within the collective of Israel); and likewise, in every individual soul too, these three modes of contemplation are present in each matter — from human wisdom, the wisdom of the Torah, and ruach hakodesh (that is, the apprehension of Israel’s sages through prophecy, or Urim v’Tumim, or ruach hakodesh) — and these three counsel and direct every matter with their counsel; but teshuvah is above them, for it cannot be grasped by any human counsel — not even prophecy, which is man’s apprehension from Hashem; and likewise the Torah, which is from Heaven — nonetheless, since it has already been given to human beings and “it is not in heaven,” one cannot, from its side, grasp the depth of the greatness of teshuvah.130R’ Tzadok — parallel (Sichas Malachei HaShareis §2): On the Yerushalmi (Makkos ch. 2) — “they asked the Torah… they asked the Holy One, and He said, ‘let him do teshuvah’” — R’ Tzadok explains: “by [the measure of] the Torah and chochmah, through the sin a blemish has been made in his soul, and with what shall that blemish be atoned? It requires something that atones. But by [the measure of] the Holy One — who alludes to the perfect Unity, the clear sensation that ‘Hashem is One’ and that He ‘fills the whole earth with His glory,’ with nothing else here at all — [teshuvah itself suffices].” This is exactly §3-1’s “overriding a prohibition of the Torah”: Torah and wisdom must reckon a residue that demands payment, but from the vantage of God’s own Oneness the sinner simply returns — teshuvah is the remedy above the Torah’s own accounting.

items.h: The theme: “In the place where baalei teshuvah stand, the completely righteous cannot stand.” The righteous never left their bounds — they are masters of fence and border; the baal teshuvah has already breached the world’s fence and returned from where he sank. Rectifying the past with the clear recognition of “You are with me,” he merits the inheritance of Yaakov — an inheritance without borders, a root that nothing can sever.

p: [ב] וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא [בְּרָכוֹת לד:] ״מָקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין אֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים יְכוֹלִין לַעֲמֹד״ — כִּי מְקוֹם הַצַּדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים הוּא הַמַּגִּיעַ לָהֶם כְּפִי מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם, שֶׁהוּא עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה וְהַנְּבוּאָה וְהַחָכְמָה, וְלֹא יָצְאוּ מִגְּדֵרָם, וְהֵם בַּעֲלֵי גָּדֵר וּגְבוּל: אֶת זֶה תַּעֲשֶׂה וְזֶה לֹא, וְעַד פֹּה תָבוֹא וְלֹא תוֹסִיף

And in the manner brought [Berachos 34b], “in the place where baalei teshuvah stand, the completely righteous cannot stand”131Berachos 34b: R’ Abbahu taught, “in the place where baalei teshuvah stand, the wholly righteous do not stand,” deriving it from “peace, peace to the far and to the near” (Yeshayah 57:19) — peace is extended first to “the far one” (the penitent) and only afterward to “the near one” (the ever-righteous). This follows the discussion there of R’ Yochanan, “all the prophets prophesied only for baalei teshuvah, but of the wholly righteous [it is said] ‘no eye has seen’” — though R’ Yochanan himself reads the verse oppositely (the “far one” is the tzaddik, ever-distant from sin; the “near one” is the penitent, once near to sin). R’ Tzadok builds on R’ Abbahu: the “place” of the wholly righteous is bounded — what accrues to them by their deeds, measured by Torah, prophecy, and wisdom, and they never left their bounds — whereas the baal teshuvah, having breached the fence and returned, reaches the boundless “inheritance of Yaakov,” where the “masters of limit” cannot stand. Sefas Emes repeatedly explains "במקום שבעלי תשובה עומדין" as access to a new path drawn from above the ordinary order. In Pekudei 12:3 he writes that after the sin and teshuvah, "ע"י תשובה נתקן דרך חדש" — through teshuvah a new way was repaired — and that baalei teshuvah have a share in the derech of the future. In Acharei Mos 19:2, the entrance "lifnai ve-lifnim" on Yom Kippur becomes the image of the same principle: a gate from the upper world is opened specifically for baalei teshuvah. And in Vayishlach 13:3 he connects the ma'amar directly to "teshuvah reaches the Kisei HaKavod," describing teshuvah as return to the point from which the person's future good is destined to grow. These passages deepen R' Tzadok's language of "place." The baal teshuvah does not simply receive a larger reward than the tzaddik for the same route. His fall and return open a *derech chadash* — a route that did not exist within the bounded map of his earlier avodah. That is why the tzaddik gamur cannot "stand" there: it is not a higher rung on the tzaddik's unchanged ladder but a place generated by the movement of return itself. — for the “place” of the completely righteous is what accrues to them according to their deeds, which is by Torah, prophecy, and wisdom, and they never left their bounds; and they are “masters of fence and limit”: this you shall do and this not, “thus far shall you come and no further.”132R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §102): “‘In the place where baalei teshuvah stand, the completely righteous cannot [stand]’ — and Hashem prepares for him stumblings and obstacles, and he needs teshuvah and atonement for them (which is called ‘sin’), and through this he ‘brings forth the precious from the vile.’ But a tzaddik, who does not depart from the [strict] line — Hashem too conducts [Himself] with him thus, and ‘no iniquity befalls the tzaddik.’” Exactly the se’if: the tzaddik’s “place” is bounded by his deeds, whereas the baal teshuvah, having breached and returned, “brings forth the precious from the vile.”

אֲבָל בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה הוּא שֶׁכְּבָר פָּרַץ גָּדְרוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַנִּגְדָּר עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה וְהַנְּבִיאִים וְהַחֲכָמִים, וְנִשְׁקַע בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁנִּשְׁקַע; וּכְשֶׁחוֹזֵר לָשׁוּב אֶל ה’ וּלְתַקֵּן הַקּוֹדֵם בְּהַכָּרָה בְּרוּרָה דְּ״אַתָּה עִמָּדִי״ וּ״בְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ״, זוֹכֶה לְנַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע"ה, שֶׁהִיא נַחֲלָה בְּלֹא מְצָרִים

But the baal teshuvah has already breached the fence of the world — fenced by Torah, prophets, and sages — and sunk where he sank; and when he returns to Hashem and rectifies the past with the clear recognition that “You are with me,” and “wherever [I] may be, there is none besides Him,” he merits the inheritance of Yaakov Avinu, which is an inheritance without borders,133Shabbos 118a–b: “R’ Yochanan said in the name of R’ Yosei: Whoever delights in the Shabbos is given an inheritance without bounds [nachalah beli metzarim] — as it says, ‘then you shall delight in Hashem, and I will feed you the inheritance of Yaakov your father’ (Yeshayah 58:14): not like Avraham, of whom it is written ‘arise, walk through the land its length and its breadth,’ nor like Yitzchak (‘to you and your seed I will give all these lands’), but like Yaakov, of whom it is written, ‘you shall spread out to the west and east, north and south’ (Bereishis 28:14).” R’ Tzadok: Yaakov’s inheritance is boundless — the rung that teshuvah reaches.134R’ Tzadok — parallel (Dover Tzedek, Likutim §1): one who remains bounded “did not merit the inheritance without borders — which is [a portion] with no bounding whatever of every kind of delight and joy — but only according to the Torah, which fences and bounds a person… whereas Yaakov is without bound, as the Name Havayah alludes to the rung of Yaakov.” This is precisely §3-2’s contrast: the completely righteous are “masters of fence and border,” their portion measured out “according to Torah, prophecy, and wisdom” — while the baal teshuvah, like Yaakov, inherits bli mitzarim, a place unbounded by the very rules that define the tzaddik.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [שַׁבָּת קיח:], דְּזֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דִּידֵיהּ שֶׁהָיְתָה מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה
as they said [Shabbos 118a], for this is his rung — “whose bed was whole.”

דְּיִצְחָק אָבִינוּ ע"ה, אַף שֶׁכְּבָר הָיָה מְתֻקָּן מִשָּׁרְשׁוֹ, וְאַף עֵשָׂו הַנּוֹלָד מִמֶּנּוּ נִקְרָא [בפ"ק דְּקִדּוּשִׁין] יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר, מִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּבָר הָיָה יָכוֹל לְהָמִיר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמֶּנּוּ וְלִהְיוֹת כְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם וְעוֹד גָּרוּעַ מֵהֶם

For Yitzchak Avinu, though he was already rectified from his root [and even Esav who issued from him is called (in Kiddushin) “a Jewish apostate”]135Kiddushin 18a (first chapter): R’ Chiya bar Avin said in the name of R’ Yochanan that a gentile inherits from his father by Torah law, “for it is written, ‘I have given Mount Se’ir to Esav as an inheritance’ (Devarim 2:5)”; the Gemara objects, “ve-dilma Yisrael meshumad shani? — but perhaps an apostate Jew is different,” i.e. Esav was no gentile at all but an apostate Jew, so his inheriting proves nothing about gentiles (the point is instead proven from the descendants of Lot). The very objection establishes that even Esav — the archetypal renegade — is classed not as a non-Jew but as a “Yisrael meshumad,” an apostate who nonetheless retains the name and status of Israel. This is the basis for the settled halachah, which R’ Tzadok invokes, that a Jewish apostate’s “betrothals are valid and his divorce is valid”; for as the Sages said (Sanhedrin 44a), “even though he has sinned, he is [still] Israel” — the name “Israel,” rooted in Yaakov, cannot be uprooted from a Jew by any sin., nonetheless the name “Israel” could still be exchanged out of him, to become like all the nations and even worse than them

מִצַּד מִדַּת הַצִּמְצוּם [שֶׁ]יֵּשׁ גְּבוּל וְגָדֵר, וּמִסִּטְרֵיהּ אוֹרַיְיתָא הַמְּגַדֶּרֶת הָאָדָם בְּפִקּוּדִין דַּעֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה; וְאַף הַתְּשׁוּבָה, שֶׁהִיא אַחַת מִמִּצְוֹת הַתּוֹרָה, הִיא מְצֻמְצֶמֶת בִּגְבוּל, שֶׁלֹּא יוֹעִיל חוּץ מֵאוֹתוֹ גְּבוּל

[for this is] from the side of the middah of contraction, [in which] there is limit and fence — and from its side [issues] the Torah, which fences a person in with mitzvos of “do” and “do not”; and even teshuvah, which is one of the Torah’s mitzvos, is contracted within a limit, that it should not avail outside that boundary.

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע“ה, הִיא בְּלֹא מְצָרִים, שֶׁאֵין שָׁם גְּבוּל הַמַּגְדִּיר כְּלָל; וַאֲפִילּוּ הִגְדִּיל מֵאָה עֳוֹנוֹת, לֹא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמֶּנּוּ לְכָל דָּבָר, דְּקִדּוּשָׁיו קִדּוּשִׁין וְגִטּוֹ גֵּט כַּיָּדוּעַ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [סַנְהֶדְרִין מד.] ״אע”פ שֶׁחָטָא, יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא״

whereas the inheritance of Yaakov is without borders, where there is no delimiting boundary at all; and even had he committed a hundredfold, the name “Israel” is not uprooted from him for any matter — his betrothals are valid and his divorce is valid, as is known — and as they said [Sanhedrin 44a], “even though he sinned, he is [still] Israel.”136Sanhedrin 44a (see the fuller citation on Siman 1): “Even though he sinned, he is [still] Israel” — “a myrtle among thorns is still called a myrtle.” R’ Tzadok: the name “Israel,” rooted in Yaakov “whose bed was whole,” cannot be uprooted by any sin — his betrothals and divorce remain valid — because that root has no dross.
דְּזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְנַתֵּק וְלַעֲקֹר מִזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע"ה הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מִיַּעֲקֹב, שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ פְּסֹלֶת כְּלָל

For this cannot be severed and uprooted from the seed of Yaakov — the root within him from Yaakov, which has no dross at all.137R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §7): “‘In the place where baalei teshuvah stand, the completely righteous cannot stand’ (Berachos 34b) — and through the sin, when he afterward merits teshuvah, he reaches a greater level [than before].” R’ Tzadok makes explicit why the baal teshuvah’s place exceeds the tzaddik’s in §3-2: it is the sin itself, once returned upon, that carries him past the fixed bounds of the righteous — the fall becomes the very rung on which he now stands higher, in the “inheritance without borders.”

items.h: The theme: This rung breaches every boundary of the Torah, and therefore the “masters of limit” cannot stand in it — for contraction is the opposite of the limitless. It answers to the Name that is not grasped in this world at all, and so it is not apprehended by prophecy either. Hence the view that the prophets prophesied only for baalei teshuvah; the dispute concerns the prophets’ grasp, and both are the words of the living God.

p: [ג] וְדַרְגָּא זוֹ דִּתְשׁוּבָה שֶׁמִּצִּדּוֹ הַפּוֹרֶצֶת וְדוֹחָה כָּל גְּבוּלֵי הַתּוֹרָה, הוּא הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁאֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים בַּעֲלֵי גְּבוּל יְכוֹלִין לַעֲמֹד בּוֹ, כִּי כֹּחַ הַצִּמְצוּם וְהַמַּגְבִּיל הוּא הֵיפֶךְ כֹּחַ הַבִּלְתִּי בַּעַל גְּבוּל

And this rung of teshuvah — which from its own side breaches and overrides all the boundaries of the Torah — is the “place” where the completely righteous, masters of limit, cannot stand; for the power of contraction-and-delimiting is the opposite of the power of the limitless.138R’ Tzadok — parallel (Likkutei Maamarim §9): “‘Do all that is in your heart, for Hashem is with you’ — for ‘a king breaches a fence and none may protest’ (Yevamos 76b); and as was said of Amatzyah, ‘counselor to the king,’ for one does not counsel a king, who needs no effort or limit and does all that is in his heart — as with Shlomo and David.” The se’if’s teshuvah, from the side of the King, “breaches the fence” of the Torah’s own limits — the very opposite of the tzaddik’s “power of contraction and limit.”

כִּי מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע“ה הוּא נֶגֶד שֵׁם הֲוָיָ”ה, שֶׁהוּא הַמָּקוֹר שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִתְפָּס בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל, דְּעַל כֵּן אֵינוֹ נֶהֱגֶה, כִּי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא בִּגְבוּל, וְהַשָּׂגָה זוֹ הוּא בְּלֹא גְּבוּל, דְּכָךְ מַשְׁמָעוּתוֹ — שֶׁהָיָה, הֹוֶה, וְיִהְיֶה, בְּלֹא רֵאשִׁית וְלֹא תַכְלִית

For the middah of Yaakov Avinu is over-against the shem Havayah, which is the Source not grasped in this world at all — therefore it is not pronounced; for this world is bounded, and this apprehension is boundless, for such is its meaning: He was, is, and will be, with no beginning and no end.139R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §8): “…whereas the baal teshuvah breaches every kind of boundary [poretz kol minei hagdaros], and in a single hour, in one instant, he can acquire his entire world — and more, they call him ‘Rabbi,’ as with R’ Elazar ben Durdaya (Avodah Zarah 17a).” This is §3-3’s very claim that teshuvah “from its own side breaches and overrides all the boundaries of the Torah”: the tzaddik, “master of limit,” acquires his portion measure by measure, but the penitent’s power is limitless — it bursts every bound and wins the world “in one instant,” a place where the bounded righteous cannot stand.
וּמִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם דִּבְרֵי הַמַּאן דְּאָמַר שָׁם, דְּכָל הַנְּבִיאִים לֹא נִתְנַבְּאוּ אֶלָּא לְבַעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה כו’, הוּא אֱמֶת, דְּ״אֵלּוּ וְאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹקִים חַיִּים״

And from the side of this world, even the words of the opinion there [Berachos 34b] — that all the prophets prophesied only for baalei teshuvah, etc. — are true, for “these and those are the words of the living God.”

וּמִצַּד הַהַשָּׂגָה הַמֻּשָּׂג לַנְּבִיאִים, מַדְרֵגַת הַבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה פְּחוּתָה מִצַּדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים, כִּי דַּרְגָּא זוֹ דִּתְשׁוּבָה אֵינוֹ מֻשָּׂג מִצַּד הַנְּבוּאָה כְּלָל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר שָׁם ר’ יוֹחָנָן עַצְמוֹ ״כָּל הַנְּבִיאִים לֹא נִתְנַבְּאוּ אֶלָּא לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ, אֲבָל לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה אֱלֹקִים זוּלָתְךָ״

And from the side of what is apprehended by the prophets, the rank of the baalei teshuvah is lower than the completely righteous — for this rung of teshuvah is not apprehended from the side of prophecy at all, as R’ Yochanan himself said there, “all the prophets prophesied only for the days of Mashiach, but of the World to Come, ‘no eye has seen a God besides You who acts for the one who waits for Him’ (Yeshayah 64:3).”140Yeshayah 64:3: “וּמֵעוֹלָם לֹא שָׁמְעוּ לֹא הֶאֱזִינוּ, עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה אֱלֹקִים זוּלָתְךָ, יַעֲשֶׂה לִמְחַכֵּה לוֹ” — “From of old none has heard, none has given ear; no eye has seen a God besides You, who acts for the one who waits for Him” — from Yeshayah’s plea for redemption (ch. 63–64). Rashi gives both the plain sense — no other people’s god ever did for its devotees what You do for those who hope in You — and the reading of the Sages (Berachos 34b): “no [prophet’s] eye has seen what the Holy One will do for the one who waits for Him, except Your eyes, O God” — the reward of the World to Come lies beyond all prophetic vision. R’ Tzadok draws on this: the highest rung of teshuvah, which breaches every boundary of the Torah, is — like the World to Come — “not apprehended by prophecy at all,” which is why “the prophets prophesied only for baalei teshuvah” of this world, and not for that boundless rung.141Berachos 34b: “R’ Chiya bar Abba said in the name of R’ Yochanan: All the prophets prophesied only for the days of Mashiach, but of the World to Come, ‘no eye has seen a God besides You’ (Yeshayah 64:3). And R’ Chiya bar Abba said in the name of R’ Yochanan: All the prophets prophesied only for baalei teshuvah, but of the completely righteous, ‘no eye has seen a God besides You’ — and this disputes R’ Abbahu, who said, ‘in the place where baalei teshuvah stand, the completely righteous do not stand.’” R’ Tzadok: this rung of teshuvah is beyond prophetic grasp; “these and those are the words of the living God.”
וְזֶהוּ מַדְרֵגַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁשָּׁאֲלוּ להקב"ה בְּעַצְמוֹ; וְהַפְּלֻגְתָּא הִיא רַק בְּעִנְיַן תְּפִיסַת וְהַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבִיאִים, וְגַם בָּזֶה דִּבְרֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת
And this is the rung of teshuvah which they “asked of the Holy One Himself”; and the dispute is only about the grasp and apprehension of the prophets, and even in that, the words of both are true.

כִּי מַדְרֵגַת הַנְּבוּאָה הוּא תַּכְלִית הַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכֵחַ דְּ״אַתָּה עִמָּדִי״, עַד כִּי ״רוּחַ ה’ דִּבֶּר בּוֹ״ מַמָּשׁ לוֹמַר ״כֹּה אָמַר ה’״, שֶׁזּוֹ הַכָּרָה גְּלוּיָה יוֹתֵר מֵהַהַכָּרָה שֶׁעַל פִּי חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה

For the rung of prophecy is the ultimate of the face-to-face recognition of “You are with me,” to the point that “the spirit of Hashem spoke through him” literally, to say “thus says Hashem” — which is a more revealed recognition than the recognition by way of the wisdom of the Torah.142R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Soferim §32): “though this too is from Heaven — it is the prophecy that was not taken from the wise (Bava Basra 12a) — [yet] it is in concealment and not in revelation, [unlike] that which comes from Heaven as prophecy to the prophets.” This is §3-3’s distinction exactly: the sage’s grasp of Godliness through the wisdom of the Torah is real but hidden, whereas prophecy is the “recognition more revealed” — the face-to-face “Atah imadi,” until “the spirit of Hashem spoke in him” to declare “Thus says Hashem.”

דְּאַף ״חָכָם עָדִיף מִנָּבִיא״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בָּתְרָא [יב.], הַיְינוּ מִצַּד הָעֹמֶק, אֲבָל גִּילּוּי וּרְאִיָּה חוּשִׁית הוּא אֵצֶל הַנָּבִיא יוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל; וְעִיקַּר תִּיקּוּן הַקּוֹדֵם הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַגִּילּוּי הַבָּרוּר דְּ״אַתָּה עִמָּדִי״, כָּעִנְיָן דְּ״מַחְוֵי לְהוּ בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ״ [שַׁבָּת פט:]

For although “a wise man is greater than a prophet,” as they said in Bava Basra [12a], that is from the side of depth; but revelation and sensory vision is greater in the prophet; and the essential rectification of the past is through the clear revelation of “You are with me,” like the matter of “he shows them with their eyes” [Shabbos 89b].143Bava Basra 12a: “R’ Avdimi of Haifa said: From the day the Temple was destroyed, prophecy was taken from the prophets and given to the sages. A sage is greater than a prophet [chacham adif mi-navi].” R’ Tzadok: the sage is greater in depth of apprehension, but the prophet’s is a more vivid, “sensory” vision — and the clear vision of “You are with me” is what rectifies the past.144Shabbos 89b (see the fuller citation on Siman 2): in time to come, “Yitzchak showed them the Holy One with their own eyes.” R’ Tzadok: the prophetic-level eye-vision of God’s presence (“You are with me”) is the instrument of rectifying the past.

וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ מַצִּיל אֶלָּא מֵעׇנְשֵׁי יִסּוּרִין הַמַּגִּיעִין לָאָדָם מִצַּד חֲטָאָיו עַצְמוֹ, וּמְתַקֵּן שָׁרְשׁוֹ מִתּוֹלַדְתּוֹ; אֲבָל אֵין מוֹעִיל לְתַקֵּן שֹׁרֶשׁ חֵטְא דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּגְזַר עֲבוּרוֹ מִיתָה לְדוֹרוֹת

Yet even so it saves only from the punishments of sufferings that come to a person on account of his own sins, and rectifies his root from his birth; but it does not avail to rectify the root-sin of Adam HaRishon, on account of which death was decreed for the generations.

דְּעַל דָּבָר זֶה נִסְגָּר בַּעֲדוֹ דַּלְתֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה, כְּפִי הַנִּרְאֶה מִדִּבְרֵי רז"ל [עֵרוּבִין יח:], דְּמֵאָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה יָשַׁב [אָדָם] בְּתַעֲנִית וְהֶעֱלָה זִרְזֵי תְּאֵיֽנָה כו’ 8, וַהֲרֵי חָזַר בִּתְשׁוּבָה וְלֹא הוֹעִיל לוֹ

For regarding this the doors of teshuvah were shut before him, as appears from the words of the Sages [Eruvin 18b], that [Adam] sat one hundred and thirty years in fasting and raised up fig-girdles, and behold, he repented, and it did not fully avail him.145Eruvin 18b: “R’ Meir would say: Adam HaRishon was a great chasid — when he saw that death was decreed on his account, he sat in fasting 130 years, separated from his wife 130 years, and wore fig-bands [of mortification] on his flesh 130 years.” R’ Tzadok: despite this teshuvah, the root-sin of Adam (the decree of death for the generations) was not rectified — that awaits a rung of teshuvah beyond even prophecy.

items.h: The theme: By Torah-law teshuvah does not nullify the Torah’s own consequences — not court-death, not lashes, not a korban. The four levels of atonement grade what teshuvah alone gains, what Yom Kippur completes, what sufferings scour, and what only death scours. Yet all of that holds only from the side of this bounded world: after death even chillul Hashem is scoured, for teshuvah draws from binah, the secret of the World to Come.

p: [ד] וְהִנֵּה עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה, אַף דְּהִיא וְכָל הַנְּבִיאִים הִזְהִירוּ עַל הַתְּשׁוּבָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין זֶה מוֹעִיל לְבַטֵּל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה — דְּהַיְינוּ לִפְטוֹר מִמִּיתַת בֵּית דִּין וּמַלְקוּת בְּמֵזִיד וְקָרְבָּן בְּשׁוֹגֵג — אֲפִילּוּ שָׁב בְּכָל לִבּוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת

And behold, by the Torah [-law] — though it and all the prophets exhorted regarding teshuvah — nonetheless this does not avail to nullify the words of the Torah: that is, to exempt from court-imposed death and lashes (for a willful sin) and a korban (for an inadvertent one) — even if he repented with his whole heart, in truth.146R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §128): “A baal teshuvah, even though ‘willful sins become merits,’ nonetheless requires afflictions and fasts for atonement, because they are no better than ‘a transgression for its own sake.’ On this it says (Bava Kamma 50a), ‘whoever says the Holy One waives [punishment is mistaken]’ — for on everything a person did he is exacted the fixed punishment and is fit for it, only that there are many remedies in [His] mercy.” Exactly the se’if: by Torah-law teshuvah does not exempt from the punishments — court-death, lashes, korban, and the scouring sufferings — but only “mitigates.”
[וְלֹא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ קְצָת אַחֲרוֹנִים דְּבָזֶה מְחַשֵּׁב רַמָּאוּת וְשֶׁלֹּא שָׁב בֶּאֱמֶת] — לֹא נִפְטַר מִמִּשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה

[and not as some later authorities said, that in this [case] he is deemed to be feigning and did not truly repent — [rather, even in true teshuvah] he is not exempted from the judgment of the Torah,] for from the side of the Torah’s judgment, teshuvah does not avail to exempt him from its sentence for that sin.

וַאֲפִילּוּ בָּעֳנָשִׁים שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שָׁנִינוּ [בְּיוֹמָא פו.] ד’ חִלּוּקֵי כַּפָּרָה: וְעָבַר עַל כְּרִיתוֹת וּמִיתַת בֵּית דִּין, אֲפִילּוּ תְּשׁוּבָה עִם יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים אֵין מְהַנֵּי לְפָטְרוֹ לְגַמְרֵי, וְצָרִיךְ גַּם כֵּן לְיִסּוּרִין מְמָרְקִין

And even for the [heavenly] punishments in this world, we learned [Yoma 86a] the four levels of atonement: and [for] one who transgressed kareis and court-death, even teshuvah with Yom Kippur does not suffice to exempt him completely, and sufferings are also needed to scour [the punishment].147Yoma 86a: the four levels of atonement. “One who transgressed a positive commandment and repented — is forgiven at once. One who transgressed a prohibition and repented — teshuvah suspends and Yom Kippur atones. One who [committed sins bearing] kareis or court-death and repented — teshuvah and Yom Kippur suspend, and sufferings scour [memarkin]. But one who has chillul Hashem in his hand — teshuvah has no power to suspend, nor Yom Kippur to atone, nor sufferings to scour; rather, all of them suspend and death scours.” R’ Tzadok: by Torah-law teshuvah alone never fully exempts — that limitation belongs only to “this world.”148R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §49): “as the Sages said, ‘teshuvah suspends and afflictions purge’ [teshuvah tolah ve-yissurin memarkin] — for the afflictions are only the completion, and atone for a half, and the other half is through teshuvah (which likewise atones a half, as in Vayikra Rabbah), which comes of itself.” This is §3-4’s ruling in R’ Tzadok’s own hand: by the Torah’s measure, wholehearted teshuvah does not by itself discharge the debt — it “suspends,” while the sentence (afflictions, and the graver levels) must still “purge” and complete what teshuvah alone leaves outstanding — the very reckoning of the “four levels of atonement.”149Tanya, Iggeres HaTeshuvah ch. 1: עבר על מצות עשה ושב — אינו זז משם עד שמוחלין לו; עבר על מצות לא תעשה ושב — תשובה תולה, ויום הכפורים מכפר… עבר על כריתות ומיתות בית דין — תשובה ויום הכפורים תולין, ויסורין ממרקין The Baal HaTanya opens Iggeres HaTeshuvah with the very baraisa this se’if expounds, and supplies the reason the se’if presupposes: even where the punishment is pardoned, “the light remains absent” — which is precisely why teshuvah, from the side of this bounded world, cannot of itself restore what was. The opening of Tanya, Iggeres HaTeshuvah, is especially useful for R' Tzadok's distinction between selichah and complete restoration. The Alter Rebbe first cites the four-fold baraisa of Yoma and then insists that the essential Torah mitzvah of teshuvah is the wholehearted abandonment of sin; the subsequent categories describe what is still required for full kapparah and cleansing of the blemish. Thus immediate forgiveness and the remaining need for Yom Kippur or yissurin are not contradictions. A person may already be a genuine baal teshuvah while the spiritual effect of the past has not yet been fully cleared. That structure parallels the architecture of Takanas HaShavin: the earliest rung makes the person "healed" from now on, while later rungs address the harder question of the former reality itself. The Chabad formulation and R' Tzadok's formulation are not identical, but both refuse to reduce teshuvah to a single undifferentiated event.

וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אַחַר הַמִּיתָה מִתְמָרֵק לְגַמְרֵי בְּכֹחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה, אֲפִילּוּ עֲוֹן חִילּוּל הַשֵּׁם הֶחָמוּר מִכֻּלָּם; דְּכָל מַה שֶּׁאֵין תְּשׁוּבָה מוֹעִילָה לְמָרֵק לְגַמְרֵי, הוּא רַק מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דִּתְשׁוּבָה הוּא מִכֹּחַ הַבִּינָה, דִּ״לְבָבוֹ יָבִין וָשָׁב״, שֶׁהוּא סוֹד עָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי

And nonetheless, after death it is scoured completely by the power of teshuvah — even the sin of chillul Hashem, the gravest of all; for all that teshuvah does not avail to scour completely is only from the side of this world, [whereas] teshuvah is from the power of binah — “his heart understands and returns” — which is the secret of the World to Come.

וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה [סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה כב] דְּאָמַר לוֹ קַיִן ״עָשִׂיתִי תְּשׁוּבָה וְנִתְפַּשַּׁרְתִּי״, אָמַר [אָדָם] ״כָּךְ כֹּחָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה [וַאֲנִי לֹא הָיִיתִי יוֹדֵעַ]״ כו’, וְלֹא נִגְלֶה לָהֶם כֹּחָהּ רַק לְפַשֵּׁר, לֹא לְכַפֵּר לְגַמְרֵי

And in Bereishis Rabbah [end of ch. 22], when Cain told him, “I did teshuvah and was granted a compromise [nispashri],” [Adam] said, “such is the power of teshuvah, and I did not know!” — yet its power was revealed to them only to mitigate, not to atone completely.150Bereishis Rabbah 22:13: “Cain went out [from God’s court] joyful. Adam met him and asked, ‘What became of your case?’ He said, ‘I did teshuvah and was granted a compromise [nispashri].’ Adam began striking his face and said, ‘Such is the power of teshuvah, and I did not know!’ Immediately Adam stood and said, ‘A psalm, a song for the Shabbos day, it is good to give thanks to Hashem’ (Tehillim 92).” R’ Tzadok: teshuvah’s power was revealed to them only to mitigate (compromise), not to atone completely.151R’ Tzadok — parallel (Poked Akarim §6): “the sins and deficiencies — death purges them [misah memarkasan], and they go on being consumed until nothing at all remains of them; and only the good remains, fixed in all hearts.” This illumines the far end of §3-4’s ladder of atonement — the “death that purges” of the fourth level (for chillul Hashem): where teshuvah, Yom Kippur, and afflictions do not finish the account, death itself completes the purge — yet, R’ Tzadok adds, it consumes only the dross, leaving the good permanently established.

items.h: The theme: The “compromise” granted after Adam’s sin rectifies going forward, not retroactively — which is why the death-decree was not annulled. “Lest he stretch out his hand and take also of the tree of life” is the withholding of that fuller rectification; and the tree of life is Torah, the spice for the yetzer. Even the prophets did not taste of it, for it belongs not to prophecy but to complete cleaving — and only in the future will the righteous be “called by the Name of the Holy One.”

p: [ה] וְעִנְיַן הֶפְשֵׁר בְּחֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן הוּא לְתַקֵּן מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא, וְלֹא לַעֲקֹר לְמַפְרֵעַ לְגַמְרֵי לִהְיוֹת כְּמִי שֶׁלֹּא חָטָא; וְעַל כֵּן עֹנֶשׁ מִיתָה שֶׁנִּגְזַר עָלָיו עַל זֶה לֹא נִתְכַּפֵּר כְּמִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה, דְּאֵין הַתְּשׁוּבָה מַצֶּלֶת מֵהָעֹנֶשׁ

And the matter of the “compromise” in the sin of Adam HaRishon is to rectify from here on, and not to uproot retroactively and completely, to be as one who never sinned; and therefore the death-penalty decreed upon him for this was not atoned by the Torah’s judgment, for teshuvah does not rescue from that punishment.

וְעַל זֶה אָמַר ״וְעַתָּה פֶּן יִשְׁלַח יָדוֹ וְלָקַח מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים״ וְגוֹ’; וּמַה שֶּׁנִּקְרָא בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב ״חַיִּים״ הַיְינוּ וַדַּאי חַיֵּי עוֹלָם וְחַיִּים נִצְחִיִּים, שֶׁפּוֹעֵל בְּנֶפֶשׁ תִּיקּוּן הַקִּלְקוּל וּגְזֵירַת מִיתָה שֶׁגָּרַם עֵץ הַדַּעַת

And regarding this it said, “and now, lest he stretch out his hand and take also of the tree of life,” etc.; and what Scripture calls “life” means, certainly, eternal, everlasting life, which works upon the soul the rectification of the corruption and the death-decree that the Tree of Knowledge caused.

וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה [פָּרָשָׁה כא] ״אֵין ‘וְעַתָּה’ אֶלָּא תְּשׁוּבָה״ כו’, וְעַיֵּין שָׁם: ״וְהוּא אָמַר ‘פֶּן’, וְאֵין ‘פֶּן’ אֶלָּא לָאו״ — [דְּ]פָתַח לוֹ הקב"ה פֶּתַח לִתְשׁוּבָה, אֲבָל לֹא לְגַמְרֵי

And in Bereishis Rabbah [21:6], “there is no ‘and now’ but teshuvah,” etc., and see there: “yet He said ‘pen,’ and ‘pen’ is always a negation” — the Holy One opened for him an opening of teshuvah, but not completely.152Bereishis Rabbah 21:6: “‘And now [ve-atah], lest he stretch out his hand [and take also of the tree of life]’ — R’ Abba bar Kahana said: this teaches that the Holy One opened for him an opening of teshuvah, [for] ‘and now [ve-atah]’ is always [an expression of] teshuvah; but he [Adam] said ‘pen [lest],’ and ‘pen’ is always a negation.” R’ Tzadok: God offered an opening, but Adam’s sin (the death-decree) was not fully undone — the “tree of life” was withheld. A striking Izhbitz parallel makes the phrase "tree of life" almost a definition of the higher teshuvah discussed here. Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Bereishis 6, on "ועץ החיים בתוך הגן," writes explicitly: "ועץ החיים הוא תשובה אמיתיות שמרפאות את הקודם" - the Tree of Life is true teshuvah that heals what came before. He then associates the river Peras with baalei teshuvah and explains that teshuvah "מגיע למקורו הראשון," reaches the person's first source. This is precisely the distinction of the present se'if: ordinary compromise heals from now on, whereas access to the Tree of Life would mean reaching back to the first source and curing the prior deficiency itself. R' Tzadok himself supplies an essential safeguard in Pri Tzaddik, Shelach §6. He explains that teshuvah can transform the Tree of Knowledge into "very good," so that even deliberate sins become merits; but the mekoshesh erred by imagining that this might make it desirable to spoil first and repent afterward. The higher reading of the past is available only *after* a real fall has occurred and a real teshuvah has transformed it. It can never be used prospectively to authorize what the Torah forbids. Thus the Izhbitz-Radzin language of healing the original source intensifies moral responsibility rather than weakening it.

וְ״עֵץ הַחַיִּים״ זוֹ תּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פ"א], וְהוּא הַמְתַבֵּל הַיֵּצֶר לְתַקֵּן הַקּוֹדֵם גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה בְּצֵירוּף הַתּוֹרָה — זֶה נִמְנָע מִמֶּנּוּ

And “the tree of life” is Torah, as they said [Tana d’Vei Eliyahu Rabbah, ch. 1], and it is what “spices” [subdues] the yetzer and would rectify the past too, through teshuvah joined with Torah — [and] this was withheld from him.153Tana d’Vei Eliyahu Rabbah, ch. 1 (and Mishlei 3:18, “she is a tree of life to those who grasp her”): “the tree of life” is the Torah. R’ Tzadok: the Torah, the antidote to the yetzer, would (joined with teshuvah) rectify even the past — but access to it “to live forever” was barred to Adam, and belongs only to the future world of complete cleaving to God.

וְגַם הַנְּבִיאִים שֶׁזָּכוּ לִצְפּוֹת בְּפַרְדֵּס וּבַמַּרְאוֹת הָעֶלְיוֹנוֹת וְטַעְמוֹ מֵהֶם לֹא זָכוּ עֲדַיִין לִטְעֹם מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים לִחְיוֹת לְעוֹלָם, שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ מִצַּד מַדְרֵגַת הַנְּבוּאָה — שֶׁהוּא שֶׁהָאָדָם נִבְדָּל מהשי"ת וּמְקַבֵּל שֶׁפַע נְבוּאָתוֹ וְדִבּוּרוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ — אֲבָל חַיֵּי עוֹלָם הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַדְּבֵיקוּת הַגָּמוּר בּוֹ יִתְבָּרֵךְ

And even the prophets, who merited to gaze into “Pardes” and the supernal visions and tasted of them, did not yet merit to taste of the tree of life to live forever — for this matter is not of the rung of prophecy (in which the person is separate from Hashem and receives the influx of His prophecy and speech from Him) — but eternal life is through complete cleaving to Him,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְאַתֶּם הַדְּבֵקִים [בַּה’ אֱלֹקֵיכֶם] חַיִּים [כֻּלְּכֶם הַיּוֹם]״

in the manner it says, “and you who cleave to Hashem your God are alive, all of you, today” (Devarim 4:4)154Devarim 4:4: “וְאַתֶּם הַדְּבֵקִים בַּה׳ אֱלֹקֵיכֶם, חַיִּים כֻּלְּכֶם הַיּוֹם” — “But you who cleave to Hashem your God are all alive today.” In its plain sense (Moshe’s rebuke, ch. 4) the verse contrasts the survivors with those who perished at Baal Pe’or (v. 3): those who cleaved to Hashem lived, while those who cleaved to the idol died. R’ Tzadok reads “ha-deveikim… chayim” at its depth: eternal life comes not through prophecy (in which a person remains separate from God, receiving His influx) but through complete cleaving to Him — the “tree of life,” withheld after Adam’s sin. (The Sages, Kesuvos 111b, ask “is it possible to cleave to the Shechinah?” and answer that cleaving to Torah and to its scholars is itself cleaving to Him.).
וְאָז ״יְבֻלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח״, וְיִשְׁתַּלְּמוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּצֶלֶם וּדְמוּת לְגַמְרֵי, עַד שֶׁאָמְרוּ [ב"ב עה:] ״עֲתִידִים צַדִּיקִים שֶׁיִּקְרְאוּ בִּשְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הקב"ה״

And then “death will be swallowed up forever” (Yeshayah 25:8)155Yeshayah 25:8: “בִּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח, וּמָחָה אֲדֹנָי ה׳ דִּמְעָה מֵעַל כָּל פָּנִים” — “He will swallow up death forever, and the Lord God will wipe away tears from every face” — from Yeshayah’s prophecy of the future redemption (ch. 25). The commentators and the Sages (Rashi; and cf. Kesuvos 111b and Sanhedrin on the resurrection) take “bila ha-maves la-netzach” to mean that in the World to Come death — decreed upon mankind through Adam’s sin — is abolished forever. R’ Tzadok draws on this: only then, when death is swallowed up, will the righteous be perfected utterly in “image and likeness,” so that (Bava Basra 75b) “the righteous are destined to be called by the Name of the Holy One” — a completeness impossible while the death-decree, which mars the “image,” still stands., and through this they will be perfected utterly in “image and likeness,” until, as they said [Bava Basra 75b], “the righteous are destined to be called by the Name of the Holy One.”156Bava Basra 75b: “The righteous are destined to be called by the Name of the Holy One, as it says, ‘everyone that is called by My Name, for My glory I created him’ (Yeshayah 43:7).” Together with the Midrash “the Holy One makes the righteous like Himself [ka-yotze bo],” R’ Tzadok reads man’s original “image of God” as a likeness only fully restored when “death is swallowed up forever” — for while death remains, the “image” is incomplete. (The aggadic image of the future — “who places his garment between lion and lioness” — is invoked by the author, from Sanhedrin, as a stage above prophecy.)157R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §45): “‘very good’ — this is for the future, when ‘death will be swallowed up forever’ and the yetzer hara is burned away; [then] it will be clarified how this [very death and evil] was itself part of ‘very good,’ since through it the good came about in judgment.” This deepens §3-5’s promise that “death will be swallowed up forever” and the righteous be “perfected utterly in image and likeness”: not only is death annulled at the end, but Adam’s whole mortal era is retroactively disclosed as “very good” — the long road by which the good is established through mishpat, until the righteous come “to be called by the Name of the Holy One.”158R’ Tzadok — parallel (Yisrael Kedoshim §10): “…and all the nations will stream to it, for ‘death will be swallowed up forever,’ and the yetzer hara will be burned out of the world through the rectification of the root — which is in desire [ta’avah], for that is the root of the yetzer hara [set] in creation.” This is the far horizon of §3-5: the “compromise” that heals only going-forward gives way, in the end, to the uprooting of death itself — but only when the root (the desire that opened Adam’s sin) is rectified; then “death is swallowed forever” and Adam’s flaw is undone at its source, not merely bounded.

וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה, דְּ״מֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם אֵין עוֹשֶׂה אַחֵר כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ, אֲבָל הקב"ה עוֹשֶׂה צַדִּיקִים כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ״; וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה אָמַר בִּיצִירַת הָאָדָם ״בְּצַלְמֵנוּ״ וּ״כְצֶלֶם אֱלֹקִים״, שֶׁהוּא כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ כִּבְיָכוֹל

And this is as they said in Bereishis Rabbah, that “a king of flesh and blood makes no other like himself, but the Holy One makes the righteous like Himself”; and from this side He said, at the forming of man, “in Our image” and “in the image of God” — that he is, as it were, “like Him.”

אֶלָּא שֶׁאַחַר הַחֵטְא, מִלְּבַד דְּנִשְׁתַּנָּה זִיווֹ, הִנֵּה גְּזֵירַת הַמִּיתָה עַצְמָהּ גּוֹרֶמֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵעַתָּה כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ בָּזֶה עַל כָּל פָּנִים, דְּאֵין חַי לְעוֹלָם, וְעַל כֵּן אֵין הַצֶּלֶם שָׁלֵם, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְקָרְאוֹ בִּשְׁמוֹ כִּבְיָכוֹל

only that after the sin — besides that his radiance was changed — behold, the death-decree itself causes that he is no longer “like Him” in this respect at least, for he does not live forever; and therefore the “image” is not whole, and one cannot be “called by His Name,” as it were.
וְאָמְרוּ [בר"ה יז:] ״ה’ ה’ — אֲנִי הוּא קֹדֶם שֶׁיֶּחְטָא, אֲנִי הוּא לְאַחַר שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא וְיַעֲשֶׂה תְּשׁוּבָה״, וּמַשְׁמַע גַּם לְאַחַר הַחֵטְא מַמָּשׁ כְּמִקֹּדֶם

And they said [Rosh Hashanah 17b], “‘Hashem, Hashem’ — I am He before a person sins, and I am He after a person sins and does teshuvah” — implying, even after the sin, exactly as before.159Rosh Hashanah 17b: expounding the doubled Divine Name of the Thirteen Attributes — “Hashem, Hashem” — the Gemara teaches, “I am He before a person sins, and I am He after a person sins and does teshuvah,” for God does not hold the earlier sins against him, being ever “merciful and gracious.” The same passage is the source that “great is teshuvah, for it tears up a person’s sentence [gzar din],” derived from “and he shall return and be healed” (Yeshayah 6:10) — “what is it that requires healing? — say, that is a [sealed] decree.” R’ Tzadok fastens on the wording “I am He after he sins and repents”: the penitent is restored to God exactly as before the sin, with no trace remaining — the full retroactive rectification of the past, the rung that (like the tree of life) awaits the future. Sod Yesharim, Shabbos Chol HaMoed Sukkos 33:1 (Izhbitz-Radzin), develops the doubled Name in a way that closely matches R' Tzadok's "exactly as before." After citing "ה' ה' - אני הוא קודם שיחטא אדם ואני הוא לאחר שיחטא האדם ויעשה תשובה," it explains that the latter Name means that after sin and teshuvah Hashem illuminates the person "ממקום היותר נעלה" - from a still higher place. It further says that there remains a hidden point of connection that is concealed even from the heavenly hosts, and that "יכול רק השי"ת לבדו להראות התיקון איך שמעולם לא נפסק מזה האדם החיבור אף בשעת החטא" - only Hashem Himself can reveal the rectification, namely how at the deepest level the bond was never severed even during the sin. This is not a denial of the sin on the revealed plane; the same teaching distinguishes what can be seen by the created order from what Hashem alone discloses after teshuvah. It therefore gives unusually exact content to R' Tzadok's use of "אני הוא לאחר שיחטא": the restored identity is not merely a new relationship built after the break. Teshuvah can uncover a deeper, hidden continuity of the covenantal bond that the sin never reached, and from that hidden point the revealed rupture can itself be healed.160R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Soferim §11): “Through ‘a cake of figs’ — like the view that ‘the tree Adam ate from was a fig’ — for ‘with the very thing they spoiled, they were rectified’; and so [Chizkiyahu] rectified his root, which hangs on the ‘measure of Adam,’ through which the Holy One wished to make him Mashiach (Sanhedrin 94a), that he would heal the wound of the world through the ultimate lowliness.” The se’if’s Adam: the “compromise” rectifies going forward, but the full uprooting of the death-decree — being “as before the sin” — awaits the healing of the very root, in Mashiach.

items.h: The theme: This is the rung of the shem Havayah, the middah of Yaakov — a Name that sin alters, so that it is “not read as it is written,” and that teshuvah restores. In the World to Come His Name is one, read as written: that is after teshuvah, according to the force of a rung whose root reaches there. And when the question was put to the Holy One Himself, He answered “I am He” — atonement utterly, greater than all the wisdom this world contains.

p: [ו] וְזֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ“ה, מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע”ה; כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַחֵטְא שֵׁם זֶה מִשְׁתַּנֶּה וְאֵינוֹ שָׁלֵם, וְלֹא כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּכְתַּב נִקְרָא, וּלְאַחַר הַתְּשׁוּבָה חוֹזֵר לְמִקֹּדֶם

And this is the rung of the shem Havayah, the middah of Yaakov Avinu; for through the sin this Name is altered and is not whole, and it is “not read as it is written”; and after teshuvah it returns to as before.161R’ Tzadok — parallel (Peri Tzadik, Vayishlach §10): “The middah of Yaakov — ‘truth to Yaakov’ — a vitality that has no cessation; and Scripture concludes, ‘Israel, trust in Hashem, He is their help and shield,’ for according to Israel’s level they trust that even [if] whatever passed has passed, and ‘though I walk [in the valley of the shadow of death],’ Hashem helps to bring them out and save them.” The se’if’s shem Havayah, the middah of Yaakov: through sin the Name is “not read as it is written,” but teshuvah restores it — for Yaakov’s vitality “has no cessation.”

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּפְסָחִים נ.] דְּבָעוֹלָם הַבָּא ״שְׁמוֹ אֶחָד״ — וְזֶהוּ אַחַר הַתְּשׁוּבָה כְּפִי תֹּקֶף מַדְרֵגָתָהּ, שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ עַד עוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁמִּשָּׁם שָׁרְשָׁהּ, וְאָז חוֹזֵר לִהְיוֹת כְּקֹדֶם הַחֵטְא

And as they said [Pesachim 50a] that in the World to Come “His Name is one” [read as it is written] — and this is after teshuvah, according to the force of its rung, which reaches up to the World to Come, whence its root, and then it returns to being as before the sin.162Pesachim 50a: “‘And Hashem shall be King over all the earth; on that day Hashem shall be One and His Name One’ (Zecharyah 14:9) — is He not One now? Rav Naḥman bar Yitzchak said: The World to Come is not like this world. In this world [the Name] is written Y-H and read as A-D [Ado-nai]; but in the World to Come it is all one — read as it is written, Y-H.” R’ Tzadok: after teshuvah that reaches the World to Come, the Name (Yaakov’s middah), altered by sin, is restored to “read as written.”163R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §37): “…[the Name] goes on being revealed more and more, until it is fully revealed and read as it is written [nikra ke-mo she-nichtav]; and this is the war with Amalek — the more this [Name] is revealed within the souls of Israel, the more the root of Amalek is erased, and the rest after the war is Purim.” This is §3-6’s very idiom: through sin the shem Havayah is “not read as it is written,” and its healing is its progressive revelation — until, with the blotting-out of Amalek (the power that obscures the Name), it is read exactly as it is written, “His Name one.”

וְגַם אַחַר הַחֵטְא, כְּשֶׁשָּׁאֲלוּ להקב“ה בְּעַצְמוֹ — שֵׁם הֲוָיָ”ה — הוּא אָמַר ״אֲנִי הוּא״ כו’, שֶׁיֵּשׁ כַּפָּרָה מִכֹּל וָכֹל עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה, שֶׁהִיא גְּדוֹלָה מִכָּל מִינֵי חָכְמוֹת וְהַשָּׂגוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה

And even after the sin, when they “asked the Holy One Himself” — the shem Havayah — He said, “I am He,” etc., [meaning] that there is atonement utterly through teshuvah, which is greater than all the kinds of wisdom and apprehension that exist in this world.164Rosh Hashanah 17b: “‘Hashem, Hashem’ (Shemos 34:6) — R’ Yochanan said: Were it not written, it would be impossible to say it — this teaches that the Holy One wrapped Himself like a prayer-leader and showed Moshe the order of prayer, saying: whenever Israel sin, let them perform before Me this order [the Thirteen Attributes] and I will forgive them. ‘Hashem, Hashem’ — I am He before a person sins, and I am He after a person sins and repents.” R’ Tzadok: the doubled Name (Yaakov’s middah) signals that after teshuvah one stands exactly as before the sin.

שֶׁהֵם בִּכְלַל שְׁלֹשֶׁת הַנִּזְכָּרִים נֶגֶד שְׁלֹשׁ אֲבָהָן, שֶׁבָּהֶם נִכְלְלוּ כָּל הַשֵּׁשׁ קְצָווֹת, שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד אוֹת ו’ דְּבְשֵׁם הוי“ה — בְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכוֹן הַמַּבְרִיחַ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה — וּמְחַבֵּר שְׁנֵי הההי”ן, עָלְמָא עִלָּאָה וְעָלְמָא תַּתָּאָה

which [three] fall under the three [wisdom, Torah, prophecy] mentioned, corresponding to the three Patriarchs, in whom are included all the “six extremities” — corresponding to the letter vav of the shem Havayah, “the middle bar that runs from end to end” — which joins the two hehs: the upper world and the lower world.165R’ Tzadok — parallel (Ohr Zarua LaTzadik §7): “at first He and His Name were one, and His simple Oneness spread without end or limit; and when it arose in His simple will to reveal His kingship and to create beings [the differentiation began].” This gives §3-6 its ground: the wholeness of the Name is its original, undivided state — “He and His Name were one” before creation — which sin fractures and teshuvah mends, and which the World to Come restores, when “Hashem is One and His Name One” stands wholly revealed.

items.h: The theme: That boundless rung belongs to the Avos from their own side, as man was before he sinned. After the sin, the head of the rung in the receiving of teshuvah is David — fourth leg of the Chariot, “who raised up the yoke of teshuvah” — and its consummation is in Mashiach. Wisdom, Torah and prophecy are the three rungs of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, each marking how its bearer first drew near.

p: [ז] אוּלָם זֶהוּ מַדְרֵגַת הָאָבוֹת מִצַּד עַצְמָן, דְּהַיְינוּ כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁ״עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹקִים הָאָדָם יָשָׁר״ קֹדֶם שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא; אֲבָל לְאַחַר שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא, רֹאשׁ הַמַּדְרֵגָה בְּקַבָּלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה הוּא דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע"ה, רֶגֶל רְבִיעִית שֶׁבַּמֶּרְכָּבָה, שֶׁהֵקִים עֻלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה

But this [the boundless inheritance] is the rung of the Avos from their own side — that is, according to how “God made man upright” (Koheles 7:29)166Koheles 7:29: “אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹקִים אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר, וְהֵמָּה בִּקְשׁוּ חִשְּׁבֹנוֹת רַבִּים” — “God made man upright, but they sought many calculations.” Rashi: “‘God made’ — the Holy One made Adam perfectly upright; ‘but they’ — once Chavah was joined to him and they became two, called ‘they,’ they sought ‘many calculations,’ schemes and thoughts of sin.” R’ Tzadok reads “God made man upright” as the state of the Avos from their own side, before sin — the boundless rung; whereas after man sins, the head of the rung of receiving teshuvah is David HaMelech.167R’ Tzadok — parallel (Poked Akarim §1): “[when] one returns to Hashem and restores the matters to their source — as man was upright at the beginning of creation — then all the corruptions are rectified and return to what they were, according to the order of creation.” This is §3-7’s other pole: “as God made man upright before he sins” is the Avos’ rung “from their own side”; and teshuvah — David’s rung — is precisely the return of the fallen to that original uprightness, mending “the corruptions” until the man stands again in the straightness of creation. before he sins; but after one sins, the head of the rung in the receiving of teshuvah is David HaMelech, the fourth leg of the Chariot, “who raised up the yoke of teshuvah.”168R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §6): “The Oral Torah, the middah of David HaMelech, the fourth leg of the Merkavah — that man becomes [a vessel] for the indwelling of His holiness within him; and this is complete unification and the utter eradication of evil, in the manner of ‘his heart was elevated in the ways of Hashem,’ for then pride is [even] permitted, as they said (Kiddushin 32b), ‘a king who forgoes his honor — his honor is not forgone.’” Exactly the se’if: after the sin, the head of the rung of receiving teshuvah is David, the fourth leg of the Chariot, in whom man himself becomes the vehicle of holiness.

וְהָאֲבָהָן דִּבְכָל שְׁאָר ז’ הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת כְּלוּלוֹת בּוֹ בִּפְרָטָיו; וְהוּא רֹאשׁ וּתְחִלַּת הֲקָמָתָהּ בְּתַרְעָא לְדָרְתָא, דְּהוּא נֶגֶד ה’ אַחֲרוֹנָה, וְסִיּוּמוֹ בַּמָּשִׁיחַ שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד ה’ רִאשׁוֹנָה, שֶׁהִיא הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, שֶׁבּוֹ שְׁלֵימוֹת הַתְּשׁוּבָה לְגַמְרֵי

And the Avos of all the other seven rungs are included in him, in his particulars; and he is the head and beginning of its raising, at “the gate to the courtyard” — which is over-against the final heh — and its consummation is in Mashiach, who is over-against the first heh, which is the binah of the heart, in which is the utter completion of teshuvah.169R’ Tzadok — parallel (Et HaOchel §10): “‘very good’ — this is the yetzer hara [made good] through David HaMelech, who raised the yoke of teshuvah — which was not [yet possible] in Egypt; and ‘who is rich? one who rejoices in his portion,’ for the essence of wealth is joy.” This is §3-7’s David exactly: the Avos stand in the uprightness before sin, but the “head of the rung in the receiving of teshuvah” — the power to make even the yetzer “very good” once one has fallen — is David’s; he is the one who first “raised the yoke of teshuvah,” a rung that had not yet been opened.
וְעָלָיו נֶאֱמַר ״יָרוּם וְנִשָּׂא וְגָבַהּ״, וְדָרְשׁוּ רז"ל [תַּנְחוּמָא תּוֹלְדוֹת יד] עַל הָאָבוֹת, שֶׁיִּגְדַּל מֵהֶם

And of him it says, “he shall be exalted and lifted up and very high” (Yeshayah 52:13), which the Sages expounded [Tanchuma Toldos 14] regarding the Avos — that he will be greater than them.170Tanchuma, Toldos 14 (on Yeshayah 52:13, “he shall be exalted [yarum] and lifted up [nissa] and very high”): the servant-Mashiach “will be higher than Avraham, lifted above Moshe, and higher than the ministering angels.” R’ Tzadok: David/Mashiach, the head of the rung of receiving teshuvah, ultimately rises above the Avos’ own-side rung.

כִּי חָכְמָה וְתוֹרָה וּנְבוּאָה הֵם ג’ דַּרְגִּין דְּאַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק, וְיַעֲקֹב: דְּחָכְמָה — יָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ [בב"ב טז:] ״אִצְטַגְנִינוּת גְּדוֹלָה הָיְתָה בְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע“ה״ כו’, וּ״שְׁתֵּי כִלְיוֹתָיו כִּשְׁתֵּי מַעְיָנוֹת״ [וְלִימְּדוּהוּ חָכְמָה], וּתְחִלַּת הִתְקָרְבוּתוֹ להשי”ת הָיְתָה מִצַּד חָכְמָה אֱנוֹשִׁית, שֶׁהָיָה יוֹשֵׁב וְחוֹקֵר ״כְּלוּם אֶפְשָׁר לַבִּירָה בְּלֹא מַנְהִיג״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה [לט, א]

For wisdom, Torah, and prophecy are the three rungs of Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov: Wisdom — as they said [Bava Basra 16b], “a great astrology [itztagninus] was in the heart of Avraham Avinu,” etc., and “his two kidneys were like two fountains [that taught him wisdom]”; and his first drawing-near to Hashem was from the side of human wisdom, for he would sit and reason, “is it possible that a palace has no master?” — as they said in Bereishis Rabbah [39:1].171Bava Basra 16b: “A great astrology [itztagninus] was in the heart of Avraham Avinu, such that all the kings of east and west would rise early at his door.” Avos d’Rabbi Nasan 33 (and Bereishis Rabbah 61): “his two kidneys became like two fountains [ma’ayanos] and taught him wisdom” — Avraham learned Torah on his own, from within. R’ Tzadok maps Avraham to chochmah.172Bereishis Rabbah 39:1: “This is like a man traveling who saw a palace lit up [birah doleket]; he said, ‘is it possible that this palace has no master?’ — The owner peered out and said, ‘I am the master.’ So Avraham said, ‘is it possible the world has no Guide?’ — The Holy One peered out and said, ‘I am the Master of the world.’” R’ Tzadok: Avraham’s first approach to God was through human wisdom (as against Yitzchak, who received Torah from his father, and Yaakov’s prophecy).

אֲבָל ״אוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה״, וְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת יִצְחָק לֹא הָיְתָה עוֹד מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ וְחָכְמָה אֱנוֹשִׁית, שֶׁכְּבָר קִיבֵּל תּוֹרָה מֵאָבִיו; וּנְבוּאָה מִסִּטְרָא דְּיַעֲקֹב, דִּכְתִיב ״כִּי הִנֵּה ה’ נִצָּב עָלָיו״

But “the Torah issues from the side of Gevurah,” and Yitzchak’s arousal was no longer from himself and human wisdom, for he already received Torah from his father; and prophecy is from the side of Yaakov, as it is written, “and behold, Hashem was standing over him” (Bereishis 28:13)173Bereishis 28:13: at the ladder-dream — “וְהִנֵּה ה׳ נִצָּב עָלָיו וַיֹּאמַר, אֲנִי ה׳ אֱלֹקֵי אַבְרָהָם אָבִיךָ וֵאלֹקֵי יִצְחָק” — “and behold, Hashem stood over him and said: I am Hashem, the God of Avraham your father and the God of Yitzchak” — Yaakov’s first prophecy (Rashi: “stood over him — to guard him”). R’ Tzadok takes “Hashem stood over him” as the mark of prophecy, the rung of Yaakov: the prophet remains separate from God and receives His word and vision from Him who “stands over” him — as opposed to the cleaving that is eternal life. (Wisdom is the rung of Avraham, Torah of Yitzchak, and prophecy of Yaakov.).

items.h: The theme: Teshuvah overrides even what the sages, the prophets and the Torah declared unavailing — because it comes from the side of the Holy One Himself. The order in which Wisdom, Torah and Prophecy were asked is no figure of speech but the sequence of the epochs: wisdom until matan Torah, prophecy after it, and the question reaching the Holy One only with Mashiach. Then the first prohibition — “lest he stretch out his hand” — is itself nullified.

p: [ח] וּ״גְדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה״ שֶׁדּוֹחָה מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה וְהַחֲכָמִים וּפוֹרֶצֶת הַגְּבוּלִים שֶׁקָּבְעוּ — וַאֲפִילּוּ כָּל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים וּמְפֹרָשׁ בַּנְּבִיאִים וּבַתּוֹרָה שֶׁאֵין תְּשׁוּבָה מוֹעֶלֶת — מִצַּד הקב"ה בְּעַצְמוֹ, וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הַדִּיבּוּק הַגָּמוּר בּוֹ יִתְבָּרֵךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד, הוּא אוֹמֵר ״יַעֲשֶׂה תְּשׁוּבָה״ וְנִתְכַּפֵּר הַכֹּל לְגַמְרֵי

And “great is teshuvah,” which overrides the judgment of the Torah and the sages and breaches the boundaries they set — even all that the sages said, and that is explicit in the prophets and the Torah, [that] teshuvah does not avail — from the side of the Holy One Himself, and it is through complete cleaving to Him as will be in the future: He says “let him do teshuvah,” and all is atoned completely.174R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §11): “It is the beginning of cleaving to that which is above the Torah, and then he acts ‘within the line of judgment [lifnim mishuras hadin],’ for he goes out of the bound and limit of the Torah — for ‘chassid’ is a term of ‘chesed,’ meaning boundless [self-]abandon, for chesed is expansion without end.” The se’if’s “great is teshuvah” that overrides the judgment of Torah and sages: it acts from the side of the Holy One Himself, above the Torah’s own bounds.

וּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ דְּמִקֹּדֶם שָׁאֲלוּ לְחָכְמָה, לַתּוֹרָה, וְלִנְבוּאָה — אֵין זֶה שִׂיחָה בְּטֵלָה וְדֶרֶךְ מְלִיצָה, רַק כָּךְ הוּא הַשּׁוּרָה הָרְאוּיָה וְסֵדֶר הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁאָל לָהֶם קֹדֶם; וַעֲדַיִין לֹא הִגִּיעַ הַשְּׁאֵלָה להקב“ה, וְשֶׁיְּבֻלַּע הַמָּוֶת, עַד שֶׁיָּבוֹא מָשִׁיחַ הַשּׁוֹאֵל זֶה מהקב”ה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״חַיִּים שָׁאַל [מִמְּךָ] נָתַתָּ לּוֹ״, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּסֻכָּה נב.]

And that they first “asked Wisdom, Torah, and Prophecy” is no idle talk or figure of speech, but the fitting order and sequence of the rungs, that they be asked first; and the question had not yet reached the Holy One, nor [the promise] that death be swallowed up, until Mashiach comes, who “asks this of the Holy One,” as it says, “life he asked of You, You gave it him” (Tehillim 21:5)175Tehillim 21:5: “חַיִּים שָׁאַל מִמְּךָ, נָתַתָּה לּוֹ, אֹרֶךְ יָמִים עוֹלָם וָעֶד” — “He asked life of You; You gave it him — length of days forever and ever.” The Sages (Sukkah 52a) apply the verse to the King Mashiach: he “asks life” of the Holy One and is granted eternal life, “length of days forever and ever.” R’ Tzadok makes this the culminating rung: only with Mashiach does the “asking” reach the Holy One Himself (after the epochs of asking Wisdom, Torah, and Prophecy), and only then is the promise “death shall be swallowed up forever” fulfilled — the utter, retroactive rectification that no earlier rung could attain., and as they said [Sukkah 52a].176Sukkah 52a: “The Holy One will say to Mashiach ben David: ask of Me anything and I will give it; He will say, ‘I ask of You only life.’ He will reply, ‘Life — even before you asked, David your father already prophesied about you: life he asked of You, You gave it him’ (Tehillim 21:5).” R’ Tzadok: only Mashiach’s request reaches “the Holy One Himself” — the rung at which death itself is undone.

וְעַד מַתַּן תּוֹרָה — שֶׁהוּא עַד הַתְחָלַת ״שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה״ ״מֵאֵת הַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ״ [בְחָרָן] כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בע"ז ט.] — הוּא הַזְּמַן דְּשָׁאֲלוּ לְחָכְמָה וְהֵשִׁיבָה ״חֲטָאִים תִּרְדֹּף רָעָה״, כִּי אֵין תְּשׁוּבָה לַגּוֹיִם כְּלָל

And until matan Torah — which is the start of the “two thousand years of Torah,” “from the souls they made [in Charan],” as they said [Avodah Zarah 9a] — is the time of “asking Wisdom,” which answered “evil pursues sinners,” for there is no teshuvah for the nations at all.177Avodah Zarah 9a: “The world exists six thousand years: two thousand of chaos [tohu], two thousand of Torah, two thousand the days of Mashiach. From when are the ‘two thousand of Torah’ counted? From ‘the souls they made in Charan’ (Bereishis 12:5)” — when Avraham began teaching Torah and bringing souls to faith. R’ Tzadok aligns the epochs with “asking Wisdom” (until Torah), “asking Prophecy” (from Sinai), and “asking the Holy One” (Mashiach).

וּבְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע“ה הִתְחִילָה תּוֹרָה וְשֹׁרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת, שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְצִיאוּת כַּפָּרָה לְחֵטְא עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה, וְצָרִיךְ רַק קָרְבָּן לְכַפֵּר, וְזֶהוּ סֵדֶר קָרְבָּנוֹת שֶׁאָמַר הקב”ה לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע"ה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּתַעֲנִית כז:]

And with Avraham Avinu began Torah and the root of Jewishness — that there is a possibility of atonement for sin through teshuvah, needing only a korban to atone; and this is the “order of sacrifices” that the Holy One told Avraham, as they said [Taanis 27b].178Taanis 27b: “Avraham said before the Holy One: Master of the Universe, perhaps Israel will sin before You and You will do to them as to the generation of the Flood? He said: No. He said: How shall I know I will inherit it? He said: Take Me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old goat, and a three-year-old ram (Bereishis 15:9) [the covenant of the pieces]. He said: This is well while the Temple stands — when it does not stand, what will be of them? He said: I have already established for them the order of sacrifices; whenever they read them before Me I will regard it as if they offered them, and I forgive them all their sins.” R’ Tzadok: with Avraham begins atonement-through-korban (and he “chose the exiles” — the scouring sufferings — since teshuvah alone does not fully scour).

וּבְאוֹתוֹ מַעֲמָד בָּחַר לוֹ אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע"ה גַּם כֵּן הַגָּלוּיוֹת, שֶׁהֵן הַיִּסּוּרִין הַמְּמָרְקִין, דְּאֵין תְּשׁוּבָה מְמָרֶקֶת לְגַמְרֵי עַל פִּי מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה כְּפִי ד’ חִלּוּקֵי כַּפָּרָה

And at that covenant [of the pieces] Avraham also chose the exiles — which are the scouring sufferings — since teshuvah does not fully scour by the Torah’s judgment, according to the four levels of atonement.

וְזֶהוּ עַד אַחַר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהִתְחִיל זְמַן דְּשָׁאֲלוּ לִנְבוּאָה; וְדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר זָכוּ כֻּלָּם לִנְבוּאָה בִּשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ [פְּסָחִים סו.] ״אִם אֵינָן נְבִיאִים בְּנֵי נְבִיאִים הֵן״

And this [was] until after matan Torah, when the time of “asking Prophecy” began; and the desert generation all merited prophecy at the giving of the Torah — therefore they said [Pesachim 66b], “if they are not prophets, they are the children of prophets.”179Pesachim 66b: “Hillel said: ‘leave it to Israel: if they are not prophets, they are the children of prophets.’” R’ Tzadok: the desert generation attained prophecy at Sinai (hearing “I am Hashem” from the Almighty) — the epoch of “asking Prophecy,” the general “You are with me,” which rectifies the past and saves from sufferings, though not yet from death.180R’ Tzadok — parallel (Poked Akarim §2): “for the Torah is ‘from Heaven,’ [given] through the apprehension of prophecy — [and] all Israel merited, at the standing of Har Sinai, the apprehension of prophecy then, ‘and they heard Anochi and Lo Yihyeh from the mouth of the Almighty’; therefore it is ‘an inheritance for all the congregations of Yaakov,’ and all are destined to attain this in the future.” This is §3-8’s own historical claim: the supra-Torah rung of teshuvah “from the side of the Holy One Himself” belongs to the age of prophecy that opened at Sinai — where the whole desert generation heard God directly, so that “if they are not prophets, they are children of prophets” (Pesachim 66a) — an “inheritance” awaiting all Israel in the future.

וּמִצַּד הַשָּׂגַת ״אֲנִי ה’״ וְגוֹ’, דְּשָׁמְעוּ כֻּלָּם מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה, הִתְחִיל הַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבוּאָה, שֶׁהוּא דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל הַהַשָּׂגָה דְּ״אַתָּה עִמָּדִי״, שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְתַקֵּן הַקּוֹדֵם וּלְהַצִּיל מִיִּסּוּרִין גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה; אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין נִתְקָן לְגַמְרֵי לְהַצִּיל גַּם מֵהַמִּיתָה, וּתְשׁוּבָתָם ״הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַחֹטֵאת תָּמוּת״ כַּנִּזְכָּר, וְזֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ וְהוֹלֵךְ עַד מָשִׁיחַ

And from the side of the apprehension of “I am Hashem,” etc., which they all heard from the mouth of the Almighty, the apprehension of prophecy began — which is, in general, the apprehension of “You are with me,” by which they can rectify the past and be saved from sufferings too, through teshuvah; but nonetheless it is not fully rectified to save even from death, and their teshuvah [remains under] “the soul that sins shall die,” as mentioned — and this draws on until Mashiach.

דאע“פ שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה [הַנְּבוּאָה] הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע”ה דְּמִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין זֶה נִגְלֶה עֲדַיִין, וְהַרְבֵּה מְשֻׁמָּדִים וְכוֹפְרִים יֵשׁ בעו"ה מִזֶּרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֶלָּא שֶׁהִבְטִיחָנוּ יִתְבָּרֵךְ דְּ״לֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח״

For though this matter [prophecy] is the root of Yaakov, “whose bed was whole,” nonetheless in this world it is not yet manifest — there are many apostates and deniers, in our great sins, from the seed of Israel — only that He assured us, “no outcast shall be cast off from Him” (Shmuel II 14:14)181Shmuel II 14:14: the wise woman of Teko’a, pleading with David to bring back the banished Avshalom, says — “כִּי מוֹת נָמוּת וְכַמַּיִם הַנִּגָּרִים אַרְצָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא יֵאָסֵפוּ, וְלֹא יִשָּׂא אֱלֹקִים נֶפֶשׁ, וְחָשַׁב מַחֲשָׁבוֹת לְבִלְתִּי יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח” — “for we must surely die, and are like water spilled on the ground that cannot be gathered; yet God does not take away a soul, but devises means that the banished one not be cast out from Him.” Rashi: “‘God does not spare a man’ from death — therefore the king should devise means [machashavos] that his outcast not remain banished.” R’ Tzadok takes “lo yidach mimenu nidach” as God’s own assurance that no member of Yaakov’s seed is ever finally cast off: though in this world there are apostates and deniers among Israel, at the future ingathering it will be “clarified to the eye” that no seed of Yaakov is rejected at all. Two major Chassidic traditions make R' Tzadok's use of "לא ידח ממנו נדח" especially concrete. Tanya, Likkutei Amarim ch. 39 (39:20 in Sefaria), explains the assurance that even Torah learned shelo lishmah will ultimately rise: a Jew's end is certainly to do teshuvah, in this gilgul or another, "כי לא ידח ממנו נדח." The Alter Rebbe thus reads the verse not merely as a promise that God will not abandon the person, but as a promise that the person's own buried Torah and avodah will eventually return with him when he returns. Sha'ar HaEmunah VeYesod HaChasidut, Entrance to the Gate of Beit Yaakov 23:11, gives the Izhbitz-Radzin side of the same promise. The believer trusts that Hashem "חושב מחשבות לבלתי ידח ממנו נדח" and that whatever passes over him can ultimately be shown to have been for his good. Even events that presently seem impossible to reconcile can, through a clarity Hashem later opens in the mind, become the very ground of consolation. This is not a claim that every present act is good in its revealed form. It is a statement about the final Divine "machashavos" that refuse to let a Jewish soul's history end in banishment. Cf. Resisei Layla §35: even the consciously "nidachim" - those who know they are Jews yet have been driven far from the knowledge of Hashem - are promised awakening by the great shofar, because "לא ידח ממנו נדח." This sharpens the se'if's future tense: the fact that the root cannot be finally expelled will only be fully "clarified to the eye" when the outcasts actually return..

וּכְשֶׁיְּקַבֵּץ נִדָּחֵינוּ מֵאַרְבַּע כְּנָפוֹת יְבֹרַר לָעַיִן דָּבָר זֶה, דְּשׁוּם זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע"ה לֹא נִדְחֶה כְּלָל, וְאָז יִהְיֶה שְׁלֵימוֹת דַּרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב; וְהַהַשְׁלָמָה הַגְּמוּרָה יִהְיֶה לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ, שֶׁאָז יִתְבָּרֵר גְּדוֹלָה זוֹ דִּתְשׁוּבָה, שֶׁ״דּוֹחָה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה״ הוּא לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה רִאשׁוֹנָה דְּ״פֶּן יִשְׁלַח יָדוֹ״ וְגוֹ’ — דְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״פֶּן״ הוּא לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה — וְזֶהוּ שְׁלֵימוֹת הַמַּעֲלָה
