And when He gathers our outcasts from the four corners, this will be clarified to the eye — that no seed of Yaakov is rejected at all, and then the rung of Yaakov will be complete; and the utter completion will be in the days of Mashiach, when this “greatness of teshuvah” will be clarified — that “it overrides a negative commandment of the Torah” [refers to] the first prohibition, “lest [pen] he stretch out his hand,” etc. (for wherever “pen” is said it is a prohibition) — and this is the completion of the height.182R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Soferim §6): “one is called alive only when the vitality is cleaving to him [davuk bo] and not severed… the righteous, [even] in their death, are called ‘alive’ — this is ‘alive’ in the absolute sense, for there is no [true] vitality except that which is drawn [from Hashem].” This is the inner force of §3-8’s “complete cleaving to Him”: teshuvah that overrides even what the Torah and sages ruled unavailing works precisely by re-attaching the person to the Source of life — the sinner, “severed,” is as dead, and by cleaving wholly to God he is drawn back into the vitality that flows straight from Him, above every bound.

items.h: The theme: The beginning of this appeared already with Chizkiyahu, whom the Holy One wished to make Mashiach. His “finish your prophecy and go” — that one must not withhold himself from asking mercy even against a prophet’s word — was itself the disclosure that a tunnel would be opened even for Menasheh. The sages who excluded Menasheh judged from the side of the sages’ own judgment; from the side of the Holy One he was received.

p: [ט] וְהַתְחָלָתָהּ הָיְתָה כְּבָר בִּימֵי חִזְקִיָּה, שֶׁאָמְרוּ [סַנְהֶדְרִין צד.] דְּבִיקֵּשׁ הקב"ה לַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ מָשִׁיחַ, שֶׁהוּא כְּבָר הִתְחִיל לְגַלּוֹת מַעֲלָה זוֹ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, שֶׁהִיא לְמַעְלָה מִמִּשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה וְהַנְּבוּאָה

And its beginning was already in the days of Chizkiyahu, of whom they said [Sanhedrin 94a] that the Holy One “wished to make him Mashiach” — for he had already begun to reveal this level of teshuvah, which is above the judgment of the Torah and of prophecy.183Sanhedrin 94a: “The Holy One wished to make Chizkiyahu the Mashiach and Sancheriv Gog and Magog. The Attribute of Justice said before Him: Master of the Universe — Chizkiyahu, for whom You performed all these miracles and he did not utter song before You — will You make him the Mashiach?” R’ Tzadok: Chizkiyahu had already begun to reveal the level of teshuvah that stands above the judgments of Torah and prophecy.184R’ Tzadok — parallel (Dover Tzedek, Likutim §4): “[The wound] was not healed. And this was revealed to Chizkiyahu, whom the Holy One wished to make Mashiach, as the Sages said (Sanhedrin 94a) — for he too was at this level, that he said, ‘I sleep on my bed and You [do battle for us]’; meaning that all his effort was that he not need effort — that even his sleep be good — for he has no strength for effort.” Exactly the se’if: Chizkiyahu began to reveal this level of teshuvah, above the judgment of Torah and prophecy, and so “the Holy One wished to make him Mashiach.”

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּרָכוֹת י.] דְּאָמַר לִישַׁעְיָה ״כַּלֵּה נְבוּאָתְךָ וָצֵא, כָּךְ מְקֻבְּלַנִי [מִבֵּית אֲבִי אַבָּא: אֲפִילּוּ חֶרֶב חַדָּה מֻנַּחַת עַל צַוָּארוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם אַל יִמְנַע עַצְמוֹ מִן הָרַחֲמִים]״ — דְּאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר הָעוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי בַּקָּשַׁת רַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם, דְּגָדוֹל כֹּחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה לְמַעְלָה מִכָּל הַמִּשְׁפָּטִים

And as they said [Berachos 10a], that [Chizkiyahu] said to Yeshayahu, “finish your prophecy and go — thus I have received [from the house of my father’s father: even if a sharp sword rests on a person’s neck, let him not withhold himself from mercy]” — for there is nothing that stands before the request of Heaven’s mercy; the power of teshuvah is great, above all the judgments.185Berachos 10a: Yeshayahu told the ailing Chizkiyahu, “‘set your house in order, for you shall die and not live’ (Melachim II 20:1) — you shall die in this world and not live in the World to Come,” because he had not engaged in procreation (foreseeing wicked offspring). Chizkiyahu answered, “Son of Amotz, finish your prophecy and go: thus I have received from the house of my father’s father — even if a sharp sword rests on a man’s neck, let him not withhold himself from mercy.” R’ Tzadok: this is the revelation that nothing — not even a prophetic decree — stands before the request for Heaven’s mercy. R' Tzadok returns to this very Chizkiyahu-Menasheh episode in Pri Tzaddik, Bo §9. Chizkiyahu saw that a "ben delo ma'ali" would issue from him, yet Yeshayahu answered "בהדי כבשי דרחמנא למה לך"; and R' Tzadok adds that when Hashem gives children, the hidden outcome is necessarily toward good - for from Menasheh came the chain of Mashiach ben David, and even regarding Menasheh himself the dorshei reshumos found a share in the World to Come. What Chizkiyahu saw prophetically was true, but it was not the whole truth of the future chain. Likkutei Torah, Pinchas 3:22, places "כבשי דרחמנא" in a still broader Chassidic frame: the "secret of the world" is the hidden dimension of Torah and of the Divine will, drawing from a level described there as Atik, beyond what the revealed order can display. This helps define the limit R' Tzadok is drawing. Prophecy may reveal what a future child will do; it does not thereby give the prophet jurisdiction over why that soul must exist or what ultimate tikkun will emerge through generations. The command belongs to the revealed Torah; the hidden accounting belongs to Hashem.186R’ Tzadok — parallel (Ohr Zarua LaTzadik §6): “‘that which you were commanded, you should do — but with the secrets of the Merciful, why [meddle]?’ — and this is what Moshe Rabbeinu intends, the Written Torah; yet there are times of ‘a time to act for Hashem, they have annulled Your Torah.’” This is the hinge of §3-9: prophecy and the Written Torah say “do what you are commanded and do not probe the hidden,” and by that measure Chizkiyahu was in the wrong; but the rung of teshuvah he began to reveal is “above the judgment of the Torah and of prophecy” — the “time to act for Hashem” that breaches even the Torah’s own bound.
וְחֶטְאוֹ הָיָה דְּלָא נָסֵיב, לְפִי שֶׁרָאָה שֶׁיֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ מְנַשֶּׁה שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא, וְיָדַע שֶׁיַּפְלִיג לַחֲטוֹא עַד שֶׁמִּן הַדִּין לֹא יִהְיֶה שֶׁיְּקֻבַּל בִּתְשׁוּבָה
And his “sin” was that he did not marry, because he foresaw that Menasheh would issue from him and sin, and knew he would sin so exceedingly that by [strict] law he would not be received in teshuvah.
וּמִיָּד שֶׁגִּילָּה דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁל ״כַּלֵּה נְבוּאָתְךָ״ כו’, שֶׁאֵין לְהַשְׁגִּיחַ גַּם בִּנְבוּאָה — בָּזֶה נִתְגַּלָּה לוֹ מִמֵּילָא שֶׁגַּם לִמְנַשֶּׁה יוֹעִיל חֲתִירָה לְקַבְּלוֹ בִּתְשׁוּבָה

And the moment he revealed this — “finish your prophecy,” that one need not heed even prophecy — it was of itself revealed to him that for Menasheh too a “tunnel” [chasira] would avail to receive him in teshuvah.

וַחֲכָמִים שֶׁמְּנָאוּהוּ בִּכְלַל שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא — הַיְינוּ מִצַּד מִשְׁפַּט הַחֲכָמִים, אֲבָל לֹא מִצַּד מִשְׁפַּט הקב"ה, שֶׁהוּא קִיבְּלוֹ בַּמַּחְתֶּרֶת וּבְהֶעְלֵם מֵעֵינֵי כָּל חֲכָמִים וּנְבִיאִים

And the sages who counted [Menasheh] among those with no share in the World to Come [judged] from the side of the judgment of the sages — but not from the side of the judgment of the Holy One, who received him “in the tunnel,” hidden from the eyes of all sages and prophets,

דְּהוּא הָאוֹמֵר דִּתְשׁוּבָה מוֹעֶלֶת בְּכָל עִנְיָן; וְדוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת [בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין קד סע"ב] דָּרְשׁוּ עַל כֻּלָּם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, וְהַיְינוּ מִצַּד שֶׁהֵם זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע"ה דְּמִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה, ״וְלֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח״

He being the One who says that teshuvah avails in every case; and the “expounders of allusions” [Sanhedrin 104b] expounded regarding all of them that they have a share in the World to Come — from the side that they are the seed of Yaakov, “whose bed is whole,” and “no outcast is cast off.”187Sanhedrin 104b (and 90a, 103b): the Mishnah lists kings and commoners with no share in the World to Come; but “the expounders of allusions [dorshei reshumos] said: all of them enter the World to Come.” R’ Tzadok: the sages’ ruling excluded them, but from the hidden side — that they are the seed of Yaakov, “no outcast is cast off” — all have a share; and God received even Menasheh “in the tunnel,” beyond the sages’ judgment.

וְחִזְקִיָּה הוּא הַמַּתְחִיל לְעוֹרֵר דָּבָר זֶה גַּם כֵּן בְּנִיצּוּחַ סַנְחֵרִיב, שֶׁהוּא אָמַר ״הֲמִבַּלְעֲדֵי ה’״ וְגוֹ‘, כִּי הוּא הָיָה שֵׁבֶט אַפּוֹ יִתְבָּרֵךְ; אֲבָל חִזְקִיָּה הָיָה גָּנוּז בּוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ זֶה, שֶׁהָיָה רָאוּי לַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ מָשִׁיחַ — שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ כֹּחַ הִתְעוֹרְרוּת שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה כָּל כָּךְ, לְעוֹרֵר עַל יְדֵי זֶה רַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם לִשְׁבֹּר כָּל מַאַמְרֵי ה’ גַּם כֵּן

And Chizkiyahu is the one who began to arouse this also in the defeat of Sancheriv, who himself said, “is it without Hashem [that I came up against this place to destroy it]?” — for he [Sancheriv] was the “rod of His anger”; but in Chizkiyahu this root was concealed — that he was fit to be made Mashiach — that he had in him such a power of arousing teshuvah, to arouse thereby the mercy of Heaven to break even all the utterances [decrees] of Hashem.188Melachim II 18:25: Rav-Shakeh, Sancheriv’s officer, said to Chizkiyahu’s people, “is it now without Hashem that I have come up against this place to destroy it? Hashem said to me, go up against this land and destroy it.” R’ Tzadok: Sancheriv was “the rod of [God’s] anger” (Yeshayah 10:5); Chizkiyahu’s concealed root — his power to arouse a teshuvah that breaks even decrees — is what made him “fit to be Mashiach.”189R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Bo §9): “and we find in the prayer of Shlomo HaMelech regarding Israel: "if he asks for children, and You know that they anger You — do not give him"; nevertheless [he prayed so].” Exactly the se’if: there is a rung from which one answers on the strength of what is hidden — trusting a good root that the revealed reckoning would deny.

items.h: The theme: Yeshayahu’s “my secret is mine” marks this as belonging to the kivshei d’Rachmana, the hidden counsels known to Him alone. The light of teshuvah’s greatness was revealed through Chizkiyahu, but not the order of its working, which no creature can fathom. And since the matter is founded in that hidden will, there is no sin at its root — what appears to contradict the Torah’s judgments is only the difference between the revealed and the hidden.

p: [י] וּבֵירֵר זֶה בְּיִחוּד בַּמֶּה שֶּׁאָמַר ״כַּלֵּה נְבוּאָתְךָ״ כו’, וְאָז נָתַן לוֹ יְשַׁעְיָה בִּתּוֹ לְהוֹלִיד מְנַשֶּׁה, שֶׁכְּבָר הִמְצִיא וְהֵבִיא גִּילּוּי אוֹר זֶה הַמְחֻדָּשׁ שֶׁל מַעֲלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה כָּל כָּךְ, נֶגֶד שֶׁכָּל הַתּוֹרָה וּנְבוּאָה, עַד שֶׁיּוֹעִיל גַּם לִמְנַשֶּׁה

And he clarified this in particular in what he said, “finish your prophecy,” etc., and then Yeshayahu gave him his daughter to bear Menasheh — for he had already brought forth the revelation of this renewed light of teshuvah’s greatness, so great [that it stands] against all the Torah and prophecy, that it would avail even Menasheh.

אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁלַם אָז עֲדַיִין הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל ״נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים״, לִהְיוֹת בֶּאֱמֶת עַד אֵין קֵץ, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִמְחָל לְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לְגַמְרֵי עַד שֶׁיְּבֻלַּע הַמָּוֶת — דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מָשִׁיחַ

only that the spreading-out of the middah of “an inheritance without borders” was not yet complete — to be truly endless, that the whole world be pardoned utterly until “death be swallowed up” — that is, that Mashiach come.

וְאָמַר עַל זֶה ״רָזִי לִי רָזִי״, שֶׁהוּא מֵ״הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת לַה’ אֱלֹקֵינוּ״ וְכִבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא, דְּאוֹר זֶה שֶׁל מַעֲלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה כְּבָר נִתְגַּלָּה וְנִתְבָּרֵר עַל יְדֵי חִזְקִיָּה, דְּאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר עוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה; וְדוֹרוֹ ״דּוֹר דֵּעָה״ וּבַעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זַ"ל בְּשֶׁבַח דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל חִזְקִיָּה

And of this [Yeshayahu] said, “razi li, razi [my secret is mine]” (Yeshayah 24:16)190Yeshayah 24:16: “מִכְּנַף הָאָרֶץ זְמִרֹת שָׁמַעְנוּ, צְבִי לַצַּדִּיק, וָאֹמַר רָזִי לִי רָזִי לִי אוֹי לִי” — “From the corner of the earth we have heard songs, ‘Glory to the righteous!’; but I said, ‘My secret is mine, my secret is mine, woe is me!’” Rashi: the prophet heard from behind the heavenly Curtain that in the future songs would rise “from the corner of the earth” — the raising-up of the righteous; “‘razi li’ — woe is me that two secrets have been revealed to me, the secret of retribution and the secret of salvation,” for the redemption is delayed until wave upon wave of oppressors has come. R’ Tzadok takes “razi li” as the mark that the highest rung of teshuvah — already revealed to Chizkiyahu, that “nothing stands before teshuvah” — is one of the kivshei d’Rachmana, “known to Him alone and to no creature.” The continuation in Sha'ar HaEmunah VeYesod HaChasidut, Entrance to the Gate of Beit Yaakov 23:11, sheds light on Yeshayahu's "razi li." Faith in Hashem's hidden "machashavos" includes trust that a person can eventually be given a da'as in which what was formerly unbearable is understood and consoled - "הצרות ישובו נחמות." Until that da'as is opened, however, the secret remains secret. The believer does not manufacture an explanation for the hidden decree; he continues in emunah while leaving its resolution to Hashem. This is a useful Izhbitz-Radzin complement to R' Tzadok's distinction here between the revelation that teshuvah always remains possible and the still-concealed *order* by which that possibility works. Chizkiyahu could reveal the rule "do not despair of mercy"; neither he nor Yeshayahu thereby possessed the complete map of how Menasheh, destruction, exile, and the Davidic chain would be woven into redemption., for it is of “the hidden things belonging to Hashem our God” (Devarim 29:28)191Devarim 29:28: “הַנִּסְתָּרֹת לַה׳ אֱלֹקֵינוּ, וְהַנִּגְלֹת לָנוּ וּלְבָנֵינוּ עַד עוֹלָם, לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת כָּל דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת” — “The hidden things belong to Hashem our God, but the revealed things belong to us and to our children forever, to carry out all the words of this Torah.” In its plain sense the verse divides jurisdiction over sin: what is hidden is left to Heaven, and only the revealed is given to the human court to punish (Rashi notes the dots over “lanu u-le-vaneinu,” teaching that Israel was not held answerable for the hidden sins of individuals until it had crossed the Jordan and taken on mutual responsibility). R’ Tzadok reads “ha-nistaros la-Hashem” as the kivshei d’Rachmana — the hidden counsels known to God alone — from whose side the great rung of teshuvah operates, overriding the Torah’s revealed judgments with no true contradiction. Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Nitzavim 3, reads "הנסתרות לה' אלקינו והנגלות לנו ולבנינו... לעשות" as a direct rule for the boundary between hidden causation and human bechirah. A person may be tempted to say that a corrupt impulse did not truly come from him but from the spiritual atmosphere into which he was placed. The Izhbitzer answers from this verse: "ישתדל האדם לבער הרע מקרבו ולבדוק עד מקום שידו מגעת בנגלות, והשי"ת יעזור לו בנסתרות" - the human task is to uproot evil as far as his hand reaches in the revealed realm; Hashem will deal with and help him in the hidden realm. This is one of the clearest guardrails for reading the present se'if and, more broadly, the Izhbitz-Radzin discussions of foreknowledge and choice. "Kivshei d'Rachmana" are real, but they are *not* the field on which a person decides what he is permitted to do. His avodah is "the revealed things... to do all the words of this Torah." Only Hashem can disclose afterward how the hidden dimension was woven through the story. Thus "razi li" protects, rather than dissolves, the boundary of halachic responsibility. and the kivshei d’Rachmana — [yet] this light of teshuvah’s greatness was already revealed and clarified through Chizkiyahu, that “nothing stands before teshuvah”; and his generation was “a generation of knowledge” and of baalei teshuvah, as the Sages said in praise of the generation of Chizkiyahu.192Sanhedrin 20a (“‘grace is deceptive’ — the generation of Moshe; ‘beauty is vain’ — the generation of Yehoshua; ‘a woman who fears Hashem, she shall be praised’ — the generation of Chizkiyahu”) and Sanhedrin 94b (“Chizkiyahu thrust a sword at the door of the study-hall and said: whoever does not engage in Torah shall be pierced — they searched from Dan to Beersheba and found no ignoramus, from Gevas to Antipras and found no boy or girl not expert in the laws of purity and impurity”). R’ Tzadok: Chizkiyahu’s was a “generation of knowledge and of baalei teshuvah,” in which this light of teshuvah shone — though its secret remained “razi li,” known to God alone.193Berachos 10a: the Gemara recounts that when Yeshayahu told the ailing Chizkiyahu “you shall die and not live” — because he had not fulfilled the mitzvah of procreation — Chizkiyahu explained that he had foreseen through ruach hakodesh that unworthy children (Menasheh) would issue from him. Yeshayahu answered: “bahadei kivshei d’Rachmana lamah lach — why do you involve yourself with the secret counsels of the Merciful One? What you are commanded, you must do; and what is pleasing before the Holy One, let Him do.” R’ Tzadok builds his whole se’if on this: the very existence of a Menasheh is from the kivshei d’Rachmana, and therefore his teshuvah and rectification are likewise from that hidden secret — so that teshuvah’s “overriding” of the Torah’s judgments is no contradiction, but a matter reserved to God alone, to be revealed in the future. The Chassidic application of "בהדי כבשי דרחמנא למה לך" is especially important because it prevents a deterministic misreading of the entire discussion. The revealed command to Chizkiyahu was peru u'revu; his knowledge of a future Menasheh did not allow him to calculate his way out of that command. R' Tzadok states the principle in Tzidkas HaTzadik §78 with exceptional force: had Menasheh not been born, the entire holy chain culminating in Mashiach ben David would, God forbid, have been lost - even though Menasheh stood among those whom the revealed Mishnah lists as having no share in the World to Come. The hidden good of a future outcome is therefore not something a person can calculate in advance. This is fully consonant with the Mei HaShiloach on Nitzavim cited above: the hidden things belong to Hashem, while man's obligation is to work within the revealed Torah. The paradox is deliberate. Divine foreknowledge can contain a redemptive end that prophecy itself does not encompass, while human bechirah remains accountable precisely because the person is commanded to act only on the revealed word.

רַק שֶׁהוּא ״רָזִי לִי״ — רָצָה לוֹמַר יָדוּעַ לוֹ יִתְבָּרֵךְ לְבַד וְלֹא לִבְרֵיהּ בָּעוֹלָם, כִּי אֵין שׁוּם בְּרִיָּה שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, שֶׁהוּא רַק מִצַּד הקב"ה בְּעַצְמוֹ, וְעַל כֵּן אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲמֹד עַל סוֹדוֹתֶיהָ וְסֵדֶר גְּלוּיָהּ

only that it is “razi li” — meaning known to Him alone and to no creature in the world, for there is no creature that can attain this rung of teshuvah, which is only from the side of the Holy One Himself, and therefore one cannot fathom its secrets or the order of its revelation.194R’ Tzadok — parallel (Peri Tzadik, Shemos §7): “This is the apprehension of Moshe Rabbeinu, of whom [God] said, ‘no man shall see Me [and live]’; and therefore Menasheh judged [Yeshayahu] a false prophet in this — for Scripture testified, ‘no prophet arose like Moshe, who knew [Him] face to face,’ [so] that his prophetic apprehension was the level of ‘face to face,’ the place of complete unification.” The se’if’s Chizkiyahu-Yeshayahu-Menasheh: the kivshei d’Rachmana are hidden even from a prophet’s grasp — which is why Menasheh, not perceiving the secret, condemned Yeshayahu as a false prophet.

וּכְבָר יְשַׁעְיָה גִּילָּה זֶה לְחִזְקִיָּה, דְּיֵשׁ ״כִּבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרָכוֹת שָׁם], דְּיֵשׁ סוֹדוֹת שֶׁאֵין נִגְלִים לִבְרֵיהּ, כְּמוֹ לֵידַת רָשָׁע כִּמְנַשֶּׁה; וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁלֵּידָתוֹ הוּא מִסּוֹד ה’, מִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ לוֹ תְּשׁוּבָה וְתִיקּוּן גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד סוֹד ה’ שֶׁרָצָה בְּכָךְ, כַּאֲשֶׁר יִתְגַּלֶּה לֶעָתִיד סוֹדוֹ

And Yeshayahu had already revealed this to Chizkiyahu — that there are kivshei d’Rachmana, as they said [Berachos 10a] — that there are secrets not revealed to a creature, such as the birth of a wicked man like Menasheh; and through the fact that his birth is from “the secret of Hashem,” of itself he has teshuvah and rectification also from the side of “the secret of Hashem,” who willed it so, as His secret will be revealed in the future.195R’ Tzadok — parallel (Yisrael Kedoshim §9): “in every Jew there is holiness, and even the empty ones are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate; and (Shabbos 105b) a Jew who dies is like a Torah scroll that was burned — for there is no empty one in Israel who has no Torah and mitzvos.” This is the ground of §3-10’s astonishing claim that the renewed light of teshuvah “would avail even Menasheh”: however wicked, a Jew is never truly empty — a hidden fullness of good, sealed within from the “secret of God,” remains in him always, and teshuvah is what lays that buried treasure bare.

וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהַדָּבָר הָיָה מְסֻדָּר כָּךְ מִכִּבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא, אֵין כָּאן עוֹד חֵטְא, שֶׁהוּא הַיְּצִיאָה מֵהַסֵּדֶר וּרְצוֹן השי“ת, וַהֲרֵי זֶה כָּךְ יָסַד השי”ת; אִם כֵּן אֵין כָּל הַחֵטְא אֶלָּא מִצִּדּוֹ, שֶׁהוּא לֹא יָדַע דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁל סוֹד ה’ וְחָשַׁב שֶׁהוּא מַמְרֶה פְּנֵי ה’ בַּחֲטָאָיו, אֲבָל עַל הָאֱמֶת הֲרֵי אֵין כָּאן חֵטְא מֵעִיקָּרוֹ

And in any case, since the matter was so ordered from the kivshei d’Rachmana, there is here no “sin” — for [sin] is the departure from the order and will of Hashem, and behold, God Himself founded it so; if so, the whole “sin” is only from his side — that he did not know this matter of the secret of Hashem, and thought he was defying Hashem’s face with his sins — but in truth there is no sin here at its root.

וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה הֵם כָּל הַדְּחִיּוֹת סֵדֶר מִשְׁפְּטֵי הַתּוֹרָה עַל יְדֵי מַעֲלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה זוֹ שֶׁגִּילָּה חִזְקִיָּה וִישַׁעְיָה, דְּיֵשׁ ״כִּבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא״ וְסוֹד וְרָז שֶׁנִּגְלָה לוֹ יִתְבָּרֵךְ לְבַד; אע"פ שֶׁגּוּף הַסּוֹד לֹא נִתְגַּלָּה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִתְגַּלָּה דָּבָר זֶה — שֶׁיֵּשׁ סוֹד

And in this manner are all the “overridings” of the order of the Torah’s judgments through this greatness of teshuvah that Chizkiyahu and Yeshayahu revealed: that there are kivshei d’Rachmana, a secret and mystery revealed to Him alone; and though the secret itself was not revealed, nonetheless this was revealed — that there is a secret.

וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה, מִמֵּילָא אַף שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּסוֹתֵר מִשְׁפְּטֵי הַתּוֹרָה, אֵין כָּאן סְתִירָה עַל הָאֱמֶת, כִּי מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה הוּא מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבְנֵי אָדָם, אֲבָל מִצַּד הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה לֶעָתִיד לֹא הָיָה חֵטְא כְּלָל

And thereby, of itself, although it appears to contradict the Torah’s judgments, there is no contradiction in truth — for the Torah’s judgment is from the side of what is revealed to people, but from the side of the hidden, which will be revealed in the future, there was no sin at all.

וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ [שַׁבָּת פט:] ״אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ״ שֶׁ״סְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְּרֵאשִׁית״ — דְּהַיְינוּ מִצַּד ״כִּבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא״ — אָז ״כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ״ לְגַמְרֵי, שֶׁאֵין חֵטְא כְּלָל

And of this they said [Shabbos 89b], “‘if your sins be like the shanim’ — that are ordered and come from the six days of creation” — that is, from the side of the kivshei d’Rachmana — then “‘they shall be white as snow’” completely, that there is no sin at all.196Shabbos 89b: “‘Though your sins be like shanim [scarlet], they shall be white as snow’ (Yeshayah 1:18) — Rabbi Yitzchak said: [read ka-shanim] like the years [shanim] that are ordered and come from the six days of creation, [yet] ‘they shall be white as snow.’” R’ Tzadok: sins that are, in truth, “ordered from the six days of creation” (from the kivshei d’Rachmana) are, from the hidden side, no sin at all — hence utterly whitened. R' Tzadok's own Pri Tzaddik, Vayechi §4, gives a fuller explanation of this difficult derashah of "כשנים." On the human side, he says, a stain that has penetrated through and through cannot simply be washed away: "מצד האדם אי אפשר לטהר א"ע מהחטא." Therefore the promise "כשלג ילבינו" requires a purification from Hashem Himself, from the hidden supernal source. He then reads "כשנים הללו שסדורות ובאות מששת ימי בראשית" as pointing to that concealed root which will be revealed in the future. The whiteness is not produced by calling the red stain white; it is produced by a Divine purification that reaches deeper than the layer in which the stain took hold. Sefas Emes, Purim 29:3, expresses the same transformation tersely: "אם יהיו חטאיכם כשנים כשלג ילבינו" - the sins are turned into merits, and the Purim reversal is a foretaste of the future, when the entire structure raised by Haman becomes the cause of his own fall. This offers a concrete model for R' Tzadok's language: the past is whitened when the very sequence that embodied danger becomes, through teshuvah and Divine reversal, the instrument of redemption. Again, the transformation is retrospective; it does not render the original wrong permissible.197R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §42): “even the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate (end of Chagigah); nonetheless it is not revealed to the heart in actuality — this is the middah of emes, that it be made clear to him… [for at the test of faith] there is still the ‘heart of stone’ stopping the mouth of the well.” This deepens §3-10: the hidden good of even a Menasheh is genuine but locked behind a “heart of stone”; and because his very birth was “from the secret of God,” that lock can be opened — teshuvah is the emes that at last reveals to the heart what lay sealed within.

sections.en: Great is teshuvah, for it brings redemption to the world

items.h: גדולה תשובה שמביאה גאולה לעולם.
“Great is teshuvah, for it brings [hastens] the redemption” (the fourth — corresponding to Netzach).

The theme: “Bringing redemption to the world” is the spreading-out of “bringing healing” — the later praises issuing from the earlier. Healing addresses the illness within the soul, “the leaven in the dough”; redemption addresses the enslavement to the kingdoms. This is the rung of Moshe, first redeemer of Israel — but that was before the sin, and the teshuvah that restores it afterward began only with David.

p: [א] ״שֶׁמַּקְרֶבֶת״ אוֹ ״מְבִיאָה גְּאֻלָּה לְעוֹלָם״, וְזֶהוּ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת מִדַּת ״מְבִיאָה רְפוּאָה״

“That it brings near,” or “brings redemption to the world” — and this is the spreading-out of the middah of “bringing healing.”198Yoma 86b: “R’ Yochanan said: Great is teshuvah, for it brings [some texts: hastens] the redemption, as it says, ‘and a redeemer shall come to Zion, and to those of Yaakov who turn from transgression’ (Yeshayah 59:20) — why does ‘a redeemer come to Zion’? Because [there are] ‘those of Yaakov who turn from transgression.’” R’ Tzadok: redemption is the outward spreading of teshuvah’s rectification-going-forward — deliverance from the enslaving kingdoms, as healing is from the inner “leaven.” The Zohar makes the connection between teshuvah and geulah even more structural. Zohar, Nasso 4:29, explains that sin distances the final heh of the Divine Name from the vav; this separation is expressed below in the destruction of the Mikdash and Israel's exile among the nations. Consequently, "כל מאן דעביד תשובה, גרים לאחזרא ה' לאת ו', ופורקנא בדא תלייא" - whoever performs teshuvah causes the heh to return to the vav, and redemption depends upon this. It concludes: "הכל תלוי בתשובה... ואין הדבר תלוי אלא בתשובה, דאיהו שלימו דשמיה" - everything depends on teshuvah, for teshuvah is the completion of His Name. Thus the Gemara's language that teshuvah "brings the redemption" is not only causal in the ordinary sense. In the Zohar's language, the inner repair accomplished by teshuvah and the historical repair called geulah are two expressions of the same reunion: what is restored within the Divine Name is manifest outwardly as the return of Israel and the rebuilding of the place from which they were exiled. This also supplies a bridge to the earlier simanim. There the higher teshuvah was described as restoring the Divine Name "as before"; here the same restoration spreads out into history. The personal and national processes are therefore not separate topics. The inward healing of the relationship becomes, when it reaches its full extension, the redemption of the community and the world.199Cf. Sanhedrin 97b–98a, the dispute of R’ Eliezer and R’ Yehoshua whether “Israel are redeemed only through teshuvah” — the principle R’ Tzadok invokes here (“if Israel do teshuvah, they are immediately redeemed”), now applied specifically to teshuvah that brings the redemption.

דְּאֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשׁ הַקּוֹדְמוֹת מוֹלִידוֹת עוֹד שְׁלֹשׁ מַעֲלוֹת אֲחֵרוֹת, מִצַּד הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת וְהַמְשָׁכַת שֶׁפַע כְּמִדָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרֵךְ בְּכָל דָּבָר טוֹב; וְהַגְּאוּלָּה הוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַתִּיקּוּן לְהַבָּא יוֹתֵר מֵרְפוּאָה

For these first three [praises] give birth to three further levels, from the side of the expansion and drawing-down of influx — as is His way in every good thing — and redemption is a spreading of the rectification-going-forward, greater than healing.200R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §4): “Anyone who wishes to sanctify himself and comes to purify himself may merit the beginning of redemption [aschalta d’geulah], which is ‘the gate through which the righteous enter’ — the rung of Yosef HaTzaddik, who in all his ‘imaginings’ had intent for the sake of Heaven; that his wishing to be a king and ruler, as his brothers charged, was for the sake of Heaven — to draw down abundance and sustenance to them through himself, for he knew he was the ‘channel’ of the influx.” The se’if’s redemption: the spreading-out of the healing-middah — “the gate through which the righteous enter,” the drawing-down of God’s influx into every good.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּיָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר [בְּרָכוֹת יז.] ״רְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנְךָ, וּמִי מְעַכֵּב? שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת״

And this is [as] is known, what they said [Berachos 17a]: “our will is to do Your will — and who prevents? The leaven in the dough and the enslavement to the kingdoms.”201Berachos 17a: “The Sages of Yavneh would say: Master of the Universe, it is revealed before You that our will is to do Your will — and what prevents? The leaven in the dough [se’or she-ba’isah, the yetzer] and the enslavement to the kingdoms.” R’ Tzadok: healing addresses the “leaven” within; redemption addresses the “enslavement to kingdoms” without. Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Talmud, Pesachim 104a:1, quotes this very prayer - "רצוננו לעשות רצונך ומי מעכב, שאור שבעיסה ושעבוד מלכיות" - and uses it to define the inner identity of a Jew. In explaining havdalah, the Izhbitzer says that beneath the external "form and garment" there is an immense holiness fixed in the heart of every Jew: "אבל באמת הוקבע בלב כל אחד מישראל קדושה עצומה." The se'or and the foreign rule obscure what is already present; they do not create a second, equally authentic will. This fits R' Tzadok's division exactly: the leaven is the internal obstruction that healing removes, while the kingdoms are the external obstruction that redemption removes. In both cases what emerges is not a newly manufactured Jewish will, but the will that was present underneath the obstruction all along. Sefas Emes, Pesach 27:2, places the two obstructions in one chain. The admixture of good and evil introduced through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge is "שאור שבעיסה," and "מזה בא כל הגלות" - from this comes the entire exile; therefore, he says, Chazal regularly place "שאור שבעיסה ושעבוד מלכיות" together. On Pesach the matzah represents a momentary Divine suspension of that admixture: before the dough could become leavened, the light of holiness appeared and Israel went free. He adds that the first Exodus is the preparation and continuing power for the last redemption: "יציאת מצרים שהי' ראשית הגאולה, בכח זה יכולין לעורר תמיד הגאולה." R' Tzadok's sequence - healing first, geulah as its spreading outward - is almost diagrammed by this Sefas Emes: the inner admixture generates the outer exile, and its clarification opens the road to redemption. Tanya, Likkutei Amarim ch. 14, gives the same point from the side of avodah. The beinoni can tell himself that he does not truly wish to become a rasha or be separated from Hashem, because of the hidden love "כמו בלב כללות ישראל"; even the lightest Jew can surrender his life for Kiddush Hashem, and ordinary sin occurs only because a "ruach shtus" makes him imagine that the act does not sever that bond. This is a useful Chabad parallel to the Izhbitz formulation: the deepest will belongs to holiness, while the obstructing layer is real and must be fought, but is not the soul's final identity.

וְהַיְינוּ רָצוֹן הָאֲמִיתִּי הַנֶּעְלָם שֶׁבַּנֶּפֶשׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי, זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע"ה, אֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְשׁוּם חֵטְא, שֶׁהֵם רַק כְּחוּצֵי הַסּוֹבְבִים לְאָסָא, מֵרְצוֹנוֹת זָרוּת הַנִּמְשָׁכוֹת לַלֵּב עַל יְדֵי יֵצֶר הָרַע וְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם

That is, the true hidden will in the Israelite soul — the seed of Yaakov — has no connection to any sin; [the sins] are only “like the thorns surrounding the myrtle,” from alien desires drawn to the heart by the yetzer hara [from within] and by the nations [from without].202R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Soferim §17): the se’or she-ba-isah [leaven in the dough] “is that which prevents [us], as it says (Berachos 17a), before Hashem; and through [matan Torah] one merits the Torah, which is the tavlin to the yetzer — to use it only according to His will.” This is §4-1’s own proof-text unfolded: “our will is to do Your will, and who prevents? The leaven in the dough” — the inner will of the seed of Yaakov is wholly for God, and the se’or is only the alien intruder; the Torah given at Sinai is what disarms it, so the hidden will can act unhindered.

וּרְפוּאָה הוּא לְחֹלִי שֶׁבַּנֶּפֶשׁ עַצְמוֹ, לְהִינָּצֵל מֵהַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה עַצְמָהּ; וּגְאֻלָּה הוּא מִשִּׁעְבּוּד מַלְכוּיוֹת. וְזֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע"ה שֶׁהוּא הַגּוֹאֵל הָרִאשׁוֹן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל

And healing is for the illness in the soul itself, to be saved from the “leaven in the dough” itself; and redemption is from the enslavement to kingdoms; and this is the rung of Moshe Rabbeinu, who is the first redeemer of Israel.
וּבְעֵת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, שֶׁנִּתְקַן הַקּוֹדֵם, נַעֲשָׂה חֵרוּת לְגַמְרֵי מִמַּלְכֻיּוֹת וּמִיֵּצֶר הָרַע וְגַם מִמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד

And at the time of matan Torah, when the past was rectified, there came to be complete freedom from the kingdoms, from the yetzer hara, and even from the Angel of Death, as it will be in the future.203R’ Tzadok — parallel (Ohr Zarua LaTzadik §1): “all Israel who stood at Har Sinai — their zuhama [pollution] ceased — meaning the zuhama that the serpent injected [into Chavah], which is desire [ta’avah], in the language of the Sages.” This is §4-1’s freedom “at the time of matan Torah… from the yetzer hara”: the serpent’s ta’avah — the very “leaven in the dough” that alone keeps Israel from acting on “the will to do Your will” — was, at Sinai, lifted away; that is the “healing” of the soul’s own illness, before the sin brought the pollution back.

אֲבָל זֶה הָיָה קֹדֶם שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא, דְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם לֹא הָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל חֵטְא — שֶׁהֲרֵי עֲדַיִין לֹא נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה חֵטְא — רַק הָיָה הֲכָנָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה; וּלְאַחַר הַחֵטְא, שֶׁיְּעַיֵּל הַתְּשׁוּבָה לְהַחֲזִיר לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ, זֶה לֹא הָיָה עֲדַיִין

But this was before he sinned, for the Egyptian exile was not on account of sin — the Torah had not yet been given for there to be sin — it was only a preparation for matan Torah; and [teshuvah] that would restore one to this rung after the sin did not yet exist.

כִּי הֲקָמַת עֻלָּה שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע"ה, וּמִזַּרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו הֵם הַמַּגְלִים וּמְעוֹרְרִים מַעֲלוֹת וּמַדְרֵגוֹת הַתְּשׁוּבָה אַחַת לְאַחַת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר מִשְּׁלֹמֹה וְחִזְקִיָּה

For the raising of the “yoke of teshuvah” was through David HaMelech, and from his seed after him are the ones who reveal and arouse the levels and rungs of teshuvah, one by one, as was explained regarding Shlomo and Chizkiyahu.

items.h: The theme: The completion of this fourth level awaits Mashiach, yet its light already began with Zerubavel of David’s seed — “sown in Bavel,” the redeemer from within the place of exile. Redeemers are always raised among the great ones of the land of exile, as Moshe was in Pharaoh’s palace. A complete redemption would fittingly have come then, but the sin caused otherwise.

p: [ב] וּמַעֲלָה זוֹ הָרְבִיעִית, אַף שֶׁשְּׁלֵימוּתָהּ הוּא לֶעָתִיד כְּשֶׁיִּהְיֶה גְּאֻלָּה הַשְּׁלֵימָה עַל יְדֵי הַמָּשִׁיחַ מִזֶּרַע דָּוִד, שֶׁהוּא יְבָרֵר וִיגַלֶּה כָּל מַדְרֵגוֹת הַתְּשׁוּבָה כֻּלָּם עַל שְׁלֵימוּתָם הָרָאוּי — מִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּבָר הִתְחִילָה גִּילּוּי אוֹר מַעֲלָה זוֹ עַל יְדֵי זְרֻבָּבֶל בֶּן שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל שֶׁהוּא מִזֶּרַע דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע"ה

And this fourth level — though its completion is in the future, when the complete redemption will be through the Mashiach of David’s seed, who will clarify and reveal all the rungs of teshuvah in their fitting completeness — nonetheless the revelation of this light already began through Zerubavel ben She’altiel, who is of the seed of David HaMelech.204R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Lech Lecha §9): “it is impossible that he not have some side of iniquity — meaning that he is not clean of self-benefit; and this is from the side of the serpent’s counsel, as they said [Shabbos 55b],”Yishai, father of David," who [died only through the serpent’s counsel]." Exactly the se’if: the fourth level awaits the redemption through Mashiach of David’s seed — for it is precisely the residue of the serpent’s counsel, and not ordinary sin, that the final rung must clear away.
וְהוּא נְחֶמְיָה בֶּן חֲכַלְיָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא [סַנְהֶדְרִין לח.], וְנִקְרָא ״זְרֻבָּבֶל״ שֶׁנִּזְרַע בְּבָבֶל — וְהַיְינוּ לִהְיוֹת הוּא עִיקַּר הַגּוֹאֵל מִבָּבֶל

And he is Nechemyah ben Chachalyah, as it is brought [Sanhedrin 38a]; and he is called “Zerubavel” [because] “he was sown in Bavel [nizra b’Bavel]” — that is, being the essential redeemer from Bavel.205Sanhedrin 38a: “‘And the sons of Yechanyah: Asir, She’altiel his son’ (Divrei HaYamim I 3:17); another explanation: ‘She’altiel’ — that God took counsel [nish’al] with His court [about relaxing the oath against Yechanyah’s line]; ‘Zerubavel’ — that he was sown in Bavel [nizra b’Bavel]. And what was his [real] name? Nechemyah ben Chachalyah.” R’ Tzadok: Zerubavel/Nechemyah, of David’s seed, is the redeemer who sprouts within the exile. Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Prophets, Zechariah 4:1, takes the prophecy addressed to Zerubavel - "לא בחיל ולא בכח כי אם ברוחי" - as a prophecy of the very end of redemption. He contrasts Avraham and Yitzchak, whose service shook the worlds through mighty human exertion, with Yaakov, who said "האלקים הרועה אותי מעודי" and would not make even a small movement until Hashem took him by the hand and led him like a sheep after its shepherd. That, the Izhbitzer says, is "נחלת יעקב": looking and waiting for Hashem's salvation with such complete dependence that one never departs from His will. "וזהו יהיה סוף וקץ הגאולה, שיתמעטו כל הכחות מפעולות אדם, רק השי"ת יעזור את בית יעקב" - this will be the end and completion of redemption: the powers attributed to human action will recede and Hashem Himself will help the house of Yaakov. Hence Zechariah's word specifically to Zerubavel, "not by army and not by strength, but by My spirit." This is an especially close Izhbitz-Radzin companion to R' Tzadok's choice of Zerubavel as the first disclosure of this fourth rung. Zerubavel is not merely a political figure who happens to arise in Bavel. His very prophetic sign is that redemption germinates where visible power is weakest, so that the redeemer's emergence from the place of exile becomes a demonstration that the saving force was hidden there from Hashem from the beginning. The point must not be read as passivity in the revealed duties of Torah; the same Ishbitz tradition insists that a person must do what is commanded. It is, rather, the final interpretation of the success: even the strength with which one acted is recognized as "כי אם ברוחי.

וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל פָּסוּק ״שָׁם יִרְעֶה עֵגֶל״ עַל מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁגָּדֵל עִמָּם בַּמְּדִינָה, כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע"ה בְּפָלָטִין מִצְרַיִם; דִּלְעוֹלָם הַגּוֹאֵל הוּא מִגְּדוֹלֵי מְדִינַת הַגָּלוּת דַּוְקָא, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא [סַנְהֶדְרִין לט:] ״מִינֵּיהּ וּבֵיהּ אַבָּא נֵיזִיל בֵּיהּ נַרְגָּא״

And it is in the manner they expounded on the verse “there the calf shall graze” — of the Mashiach who grew up among them in the province, like Moshe Rabbeinu in the palace of Egypt; for the redeemer is always specifically from the great ones of the land of exile, as it is brought [Sanhedrin 39b], “from the forest [aba] itself the axe-handle enters to fell it [the forest].”206Sanhedrin 39b: “Ovadyah was an Edomite convert — and this is what people say: ‘from the forest itself [mineih u-veih] comes the axe-handle that fells it’ [the prophet against Edom came from Edom itself]. So too David [who felled Moav] came from Rus the Moabitess.” R’ Tzadok: the redeemer arises from the very “great ones of the land of exile” (Moshe in Pharaoh’s palace; Zerubavel in Bavel).207R’ Tzadok — parallel (Et HaOchel §13): “it is known that on Tisha b’Av Mashiach ben David was born — and this is the oil that issues from the olive [only when crushed]; the yesod, the olive and its fruit joined to malchus, is oil, and therefore it alludes to chochmah.” This is §4-2’s “complete redemption through Mashiach of David’s seed”: the redeemer who “will clarify and reveal all the rungs of teshuvah” is born precisely on the day of the destruction, from the crushed olive — the wisdom-oil pressed out of the very lowest, so that the fullest revelation rises out of the deepest fall.

וּזְרֻבָּבֶל שֶׁנִּזְרַע שָׁם, וְהַיְינוּ דְּעִיקַּר הַזְרָעָתוֹ הָיָה עַל יְדֵי מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל עַצְמוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה] ״פַּיְּיסוּ לְגַדֶּלֶת, וְגָדַלְתָּ לְמַלְכָּה, וּמַלְכָּה לַמֶּלֶךְ״

And Zerubavel who “was sown there” — his being-sown was brought about through the king of Bavel himself, as they said [in Vayikra Rabbah 19:6], “they appeased the nurse, and the nurse the queen, and the queen the king” [that Yechanyah’s wife be given him].208Vayikra Rabbah 19:6: the Sanhedrin, fearing the Davidic line would end with the childless, imprisoned Yechanyah, contrived — “let us appease the nurse, and the nurse the queen, and the queen the king” — that Nevuchadnetzar release Yechanyah’s wife to him; she immersed after her period and Zerubavel’s line continued. R’ Tzadok: the redemption’s very seed was drawn out through the king of Bavel himself — “from the forest, the axe-handle.”
דִּיכָנְיָה כְּבָר נִגְזַר עָלָיו ״כִּתְבוּ אֶת הָאִישׁ הַזֶּה עֲרִירִי״ וְגוֹ’, אֶלָּא שֶׁבְּבָבֶל גָּרְמָה לוֹ דְּהַגָּלוּת כִּיפֵּר כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [סַנְהֶדְרִין לז:]

For upon Yechanyah it had already been decreed, “write this man childless,” etc. (Yirmeyah 22:30)209Yirmeyah 22:30: “כֹּה אָמַר ה׳, כִּתְבוּ אֶת הָאִישׁ הַזֶּה עֲרִירִי, גֶּבֶר לֹא יִצְלַח בְּיָמָיו; כִּי לֹא יִצְלַח מִזַּרְעוֹ אִישׁ יֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא דָוִד וּמֹשֵׁל עוֹד בִּיהוּדָה” — “Thus said Hashem: Record this man as childless, a man who shall not prosper in his days; for none of his seed shall prosper, sitting on the throne of David and ruling again in Yehudah.” The decree is against Yechanyah (Yehoyachin / Coniah), the penultimate king of Yehudah, whom Nevuchadnetzar exiled to Bavel. Rashi: “kisvu es ha-ish ha-zeh ariri — inscribe him [as one who will] not prosper in his days,” for no son of his would reign. Yet the Sages faced an apparent contradiction: Yechanyah did have descendants — She’altiel and Zerubavel, and through them the entire Davidic line (I Divrei HaYamim 3:17). They resolve (Sanhedrin 37b–38a; Vayikra Rabbah 19:6) that the decree was annulled by his teshuvah and the atonement of exile: “ariri” held only “be-yamav,” in his days; and the intercession that reached the king of Bavel himself (the chain of the nurse, the queen, and the king — Vayikra Rabbah) obtained his wife for him, so that he begot children in captivity. R’ Tzadok makes this the paradigm of the se’if: a sealed decree — the starkest, “write this man childless” — overturned by teshuvah and galus, so that the very man decreed barren becomes the root from which the redemption sprouts (Zerubavel, “sown in Bavel”).; only that in Bavel it came about for him that “the exile atoned,” as they said [Sanhedrin 37b],210Sanhedrin 37b: “R’ Yochanan said: Exile atones for everything [galus mechaperes], as it says, ‘write this man childless, a man who shall not prosper in his days; for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting on the throne of David’ (Yirmeyah 22:30) — yet after he was exiled it is written, ‘the sons of Yechanyah: Asir, She’altiel’ — ‘Asir,’ for his mother conceived him in prison [beis ha-asurim]; ‘She’altiel,’ for God planted him [she-sethalo Kel] not in the usual manner of planting.” R’ Tzadok: the Bavel-exile atoned for Yechanyah, so that the Davidic redemption-seed resumed through him.

וְהַזְרָעָתוֹ הָיָה מוֹרֶה שֶׁכְּבָר פָּעַל גָּלוּת בָּבֶל פְּעֻלָּתוֹ, וּמִמֵּילָא מַתְחִיל מִמֶּנּוּ הַגְּאֻלָּה , בְּאֹוֽפֶן דְּשֵׁם זֶה מוֹרֶה עַל מַעֲלָתוֹ, שֶׁהַגְּאֻוֽלָּה נִצְמַח עַל יָדוֹ. וְרָאוּי הָיָה לִהְיוֹת אָז גְּאֻלָּה שְׁלֵימָה, אֶלָּא שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּרָכוֹת ד.]

and his being-sown showed that the Bavel-exile had already done its work, so that of itself the redemption begins from him — in a way that this very name indicates his greatness, that the redemption sprouts through him — and a complete redemption would fittingly have come then, only that the sin caused [otherwise], as they said [Berachos 4a].211Berachos 4a: “R’ Yaakov bar Idi said: the Holy One sought to make Chizkiyahu the Mashiach and Sancheriv Gog and Magog; the Attribute of Justice objected.” (And elsewhere: the second-Temple redemption did not become the final one because “the sin caused it.”) R’ Tzadok: a complete redemption was fitting in Zerubavel’s day, but sin prevented it, leaving the levels of teshuvah to be revealed gradually.212R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §21): “the wise understand that it is a complete miracle and a complete redemption — yet it was not in complete revelation before all flesh; and therefore this festival is called, in Scripture’s language, simcha [joy].” This is exactly §4-2’s “already began… but its completion is in the future”: the redemption of the Second-Temple era — the light that “already began through Zerubavel ben She’altiel, of David’s seed” — was a true redemption, yet still hidden, awaiting the open revelation that only the Mashiach of David’s seed will bring. Beit Yaakov on Torah, Vayeshev 19:3, describes precisely the reduced but real Davidic light of the Second Temple period. After the first Mikdash was destroyed, "נגנז גודל התקיפות הזה," yet "אור מלכות בית דוד היה מאיר עוד אור מצומצם" - the light of Davidic kingship still shone in contracted form, and Zerubavel, governor of Yehudah, stood at Israel's head. The Beit Yaakov distinguishes a holiness fixed openly in the body from a holiness present only in a more hidden, service-dependent form; the Second Temple belonged to the latter condition. This supplies an Ishbitz vocabulary for R' Tzadok's claim that the fourth greatness of teshuvah truly began with Zerubavel yet had not reached its final expansion: it was genuine Davidic light, but "מצומצם," a contracted disclosure awaiting its future completeness. Chiddushei HaRim, Vayigash 2, supplies the complementary view from the end of the process. When Yaakov discovered that Yosef was alive, he saw retroactively that the years of concealment had been for good; the Chiddushei HaRim writes that at the complete redemption it will likewise become visible "למפרע שכל עניני הגלות היה לטובתינו, ויתברר איך ומה כל פרט ופרט" - retroactively, all the matters of exile will be seen as having been for our benefit, and the role of every detail will be clarified. He adds that before the enslaver was born, the last redeemer was already born in the line of Yehudah and Peretz: Hashem "מקדים רפואה" before the wound. This gives powerful content to the siman's link between teshuvah and geulah. The final redemption is not merely exit from exile; it is the historical analogue of teshuvah's rectification of the past, when the very story of exile is reread and its hidden redemptive seed is disclosed.

items.h: The theme: The Egyptian redemption came not through teshuvah at all, but by the merit of two mitzvos; Bavel is the first exile that came on account of sin, and its redemption the first that came through teshuvah. This answers to Netzach — nitzuach, overcoming — for a nation’s power over Israel rests on the sin that stands in act. Once Israel were handed over, a further merit was needed to extract the swallowed prey, and that comes through teshuvah spreading out into fences and safeguards.

p: [ג] וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הִתְחִיל אָז עִנְיַן גְּאֻלָּה עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה, דִּגְאֻלַּת מִצְרַיִם לֹא הָיְתָה עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה כְּלָל, רַק עַל יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁרָאָה שֶׁעֲתִידִים לְקַבֵּל הַתּוֹרָה; וְכֵן נָתַן לָהֶם שְׁתֵּי מִצְוֹת — דַּם פֶּסַח וְדַם מִילָה — שֶׁיָּגֵינּוּ עֲלֵיהֶם

In any case, the matter of redemption through teshuvah began then, for the Egyptian redemption was not through teshuvah at all, only by virtue of [God’s] foreseeing that they were destined to receive the Torah; and so He gave them two mitzvos — the blood of the Pesach and the blood of circumcision — to shield them.213R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §79): “As the Sages said, that He gave them the blood of the Pesach and the blood of circumcision so that they might be redeemed.” Exactly the se’if: the Egyptian redemption was not through teshuvah at all, but by the merit of two mitzvos — the blood of the Pesach and the blood of milah — given to shield them, for the exile itself was only a preparation for the giving of the Torah.
כִּי עִיקַּר הַגָּלוּת גַּם כֵּן הָיָה רַק בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּרָכוֹת ה.] שֶׁמַּתְּנַת הַתּוֹרָה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי יִסּוּרִין, וְהֵם יִסּוּרֵי גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם

For the essence of the exile, too, was only for this — as they said [Berachos 5a] that the gift of the Torah came through sufferings, which are the sufferings of the Egyptian exile.214Berachos 5a: “Three good gifts the Holy One gave Israel, and all of them only through sufferings: Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come.” R’ Tzadok: the Egyptian exile’s sufferings were the “birth-pangs” of the gift of Torah — not a punishment for sin (there being no Torah yet to transgress) — unlike the Bavel exile, the first to come for sin.215R’ Tzadok — parallel (Likkutei Maamarim §11): “each one [came] to his particular holiness through the blood of the Pesach and the blood of milah — for from this comes the birth of yetzias Mitzrayim, that is, the emergence of the particular holiness into actuality; and these are the crowns of matan Torah, that each one had a crown and a special exaltation.” This unfolds §4-3’s “two mitzvos… to shield them”: lacking teshuvah and even deeds of their own, Israel were carried out of Egypt by the two bloods alone — the sheer birth of their latent holiness into the open — which then became the “crowns” they received when the Torah was given.

אֲבָל גָּלוּת בָּבֶל הוּא גָּלוּת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁהָיְתָה בִּשְׁבִיל הַחֵטְא, וּגְאֻלָּתוֹ הוּא גְּאֻלָּה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁהָיְתָה עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה ״שֶׁמְּבִיאָה גְּאֻלָּה״; וְזֶה נֶגֶד מִדַּת הַנֶּצַח — הַיְינוּ נִיצּוּחַ — שֶׁכָּל גְּאֻלָּה הוּא נִיצּוּחַ הָאֻמָּה הַמְּשַׁעְבֶּדֶת, שֶׁכָּל כֹּחַ שֶׁעֲבוֹדָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִצַּד הַחֵטְא שֶׁהוּא בְּפֹעַל

But the Bavel exile is the first exile that came on account of sin, and its redemption is the first redemption that came through teshuvah, “which brings redemption”; and this is over-against the middah of Netzach — meaning nitzuach [overcoming] — for every redemption is the overcoming of the enslaving nation, since all the power an oppressor has over Israel is [only] from the side of the sin that is in act.

וְעַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמְּתַקֵּן מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא לְבַד, דְּנִתְבַּטֵּל מַעֲשֵׂה הַחֵטְא בְּפֹעַל אַף שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַן הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ דִּלְמַפְרֵעַ — וַעֲדַיִין אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיַּחֲזֹר לְקִלְקוּלוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה אָז שֶׁגָּלוּ שֵׁנִית — מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד כֹּחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה בְּתִיקּוּן דִּלְהַבָּא , שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר [בְּסִימָן א] בַּהֲבָאַת רְפוּאָה, דְּהוּא גַּם כֵּן אַף שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַן בְּהֶחְלֵט, הָכִי נָמֵי הֲבָאַת גְּאֻלָּה עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה

And through teshuvah that rectifies only from here on — so that the deed of the sin in act is nullified, even though the root is not rectified retroactively (and it is still possible he will return to his corruption, as happened then, when they were exiled a second time) — nonetheless, from the side of the power of teshuvah in its forward-rectification — as was explained (Siman 1) regarding the bringing of healing, that it avails even though the root is not wholly rectified — so too is the bringing of redemption in this manner.
כִּי אֵין השי"ת מַבִּיט בָּזֶה אֶלָּא עַל מַה שֶּׁהוּא אוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה; רַק צָרִיךְ לָזֶה תְּשׁוּבָה בְּתֹקֶף יוֹתֵר, שֶׁיּוֹעִיל לְנַצֵּחַ הָאֻמָּה שֶׁכְּבָר נִמְסְרוּ לְיָדָן בְּסִבַּת הַחֵטְא

For in this Hashem looks only at what one is at that hour; only that this requires a stronger teshuvah, that will avail to overcome the nation to whom they were already handed over on account of the sin.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עַל דֶּרֶךְ ״עֲבֵירָה גּוֹרֶרֶת עֲבֵירָה״ וְ״הַבָּא לְטַמֵּא פּוֹתְחִין [לוֹ]״, שֶׁהֲרֵי שִׁעְבּוּדָם גּוֹרֵם לַחֲטוֹא עוֹד יוֹתֵר
For this is by way of “a sin drags a sin” and “one who comes to defile himself, they open [the way] for him” — for their enslavement causes them to sin yet more.

וְאָמְרוּ [פְּסָחִים קיח:] דִּ״כְלוּם יֵשׁ עֶבֶד שֶׁרַבּוֹ נוֹתֵן לוֹ מַתָּנָה וְחוֹזֵר וְנוֹטְלָהּ מִמֶּנּוּ״; וְאַף דְּגָלוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל חָלִילָה לֹא הָיָה דֶּרֶךְ מַתָּנָה כְּלָל, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֲרֵי לְפִי שָׁעָה נִגְזַר לִהְיוֹת תַּחַת יָדָם, וְצָרִיךְ עַל זֶה מִשְׁפָּט בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְנַצְּחָם וְלָצֵאת מִתַּחַת יָדָם

And they said [Pesachim 118b], “is there a slave whose master gives him a gift and then takes it back from him?”; and though Israel’s exile, God forbid, was in no way a “gift” like that, still, for the moment it was decreed that they be under [the nations’] hand — and this requires a judgment in its own right, that they be able to overcome them and go out from under their hand.216Pesachim 118b: at the Splitting of the Sea, the angel of the sea protested casting the Egyptians onto dry land (so Israel could see them dead): “‘is there a slave whose master gives him a gift [the spoils/the sight] and then takes it back?’” R’ Tzadok adapts the principle: once Israel is “handed over” to a nation for the moment, a distinct judgment is needed to overcome that nation and extract them — the work of teshuvah’s forward-guarding.

וְשֹׁרֶשׁ הַתְּשׁוּבָה, דְּהוּא הַחֲרָטָה מֵהַחֵטְא וּשְׁמִירָה מִמֶּנּוּ לְהַבָּא — הִנֵּה קַבָּלַת הַשְּׁמִירָה מִגּוּף הַחֵטְא עַצְמוֹ מֵבִיא רְפוּאָה לְמַכַּת הַחֵטְא, וְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתוֹ הוּא קַבָּלַת גְּדֵרִים וּסְיָיגִים עַל עֶצֶם הַדָּבָר שֶׁסְּבִיבוֹת הַחֵטְא, שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹא לִידֵי חֵטְא — זֶהוּ הַגּוֹרֵם גְּאֻלָּה וְנִיצּוּחַ לָאֻמָּה הַמְשֻׁעְבֶּדֶת, בִּהְיוֹתוֹ מִתְרַחֵק עַל יְדֵי זֶה מֵהַחֵטְא לְגַמְרֵי

And the root of teshuvah — regret from the sin and guarding against it going forward — behold, the acceptance of guarding from the sin itself brings healing to the wound of the sin; and its spreading-out is the acceptance of fences and safeguards around the very matter surrounding the sin, that one not come to sin — and this is what causes redemption and overcoming of the enslaving nation, in that he thereby distances himself from the sin completely.217R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §9): “as soon as Moshe Rabbeinu came and aroused them, they immediately believed in Hashem — and by the merit of emunah they were redeemed; that is, through this the light was aroused, little by little, within their hearts, until they merited to go out from darkness to a great light, for emunah is the beginning of the apprehension of the light of His Shechinah.” This is §4-3’s ruling that “the Egyptian redemption was not through teshuvah at all”: it turned on faith, not repentance — the bare belief that opened them to the light of the Torah they were “yet to receive,” redemption granted on the credit of a will not yet acted upon. Sefas Emes, Shemos 15:5, gives a particularly apt explanation of the faith that preceded the Egyptian redemption. On "ויאמן העם וישמעו" he asks why the verse does not first say that they heard and only then believed. He answers that this is like Israel's "נעשה ונשמע": the good middah is already rooted in Jewish souls, and it accompanies them even in exile, only there it exists in the form of emunah. "גם קודם השמיעה היו מאמינים ומצפים לישועת ה'... רק בגלות עיקר העבודה באמונה" - even before the hearing they believed and waited for Hashem's salvation; in exile the essential avodah is faith. After redemption that hidden quality becomes revealed action. This sharply illuminates R' Tzadok's distinction here between the redemption from Egypt and the later redemptions that follow sin and require teshuvah. Egypt was the birth of the nation before the Torah's regime of transgression and repair had been established. What existed was the latent holy orientation of Israel expressed as faith and expectation; the Exodus carried that hidden emunah into revelation, preparing "na'aseh ve-nishma" at Sinai. In this sense the first geulah is not yet the fruit of teshuvah but the revelation of the root from which later teshuvah becomes possible.

items.h: The theme: Nechemyah was the first to institute new decrees and safeguards in Israel, and after him the Men of the Great Assembly, who warned “make a fence for the Torah.” He also renewed the re-accepting of the Torah by oath, a counsel he learned from David and from Boaz, who “swore to his yetzer.” It is this judging of the yetzer, and the fences that follow from it, that hastens the redemption.

p: [ד] וּנְחֶמְיָה הוּא הָיָה הָרִאשׁוֹן לְחַדֵּשׁ גְּזֵירוֹת וּסְיָיגוֹת חֲדָשׁוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וּכְפִי הַנִּרְאֶה הָיָה הַמַּתְחִיל בָּזֶה, וְכַנִּזְכָּר בְּסִפְרוֹ קַבָּלַת אִיסּוּר מֻקְצֶה וּמַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן בְּשַׁבָּת

And Nechemyah was the first to institute new decrees and safeguards in Israel — and apparently he was the one who began this — as recorded in his book, the acceptance of the prohibition of muktzeh and of buying-and-selling on Shabbos.

וְכֵן אַחֲרָיו כָּל חֲבֵירָיו אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה הֵם בַּעֲלֵי הַתַּקָּנוֹת וְהַסְּיָיגוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהִזְהִירוּ עַל זֶה בְּפֵירוּשׁ בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים שֶׁאָמְרוּ [פ"א דְּאָבוֹת] ״וַעֲשׂוּ סְיָיג לַתּוֹרָה״

And so too after him, all his colleagues, the Men of the Great Assembly, are the masters of enactments and safeguards in Israel, and they warned of this explicitly in the three things they said [Avos 1:1], “and make a fence for the Torah.”218Avos 1:1: “Moshe received the Torah at Sinai [and handed it down through the generations to the Men of the Great Assembly]. The Men of the Great Assembly said three things: Be deliberate in judgment, raise up many disciples, and make a fence for the Torah.” R’ Tzadok: Nechemyah and his colleagues, the Men of the Great Assembly, are the founders of the “fences” — the safeguards of forward-guarding that are teshuvah’s outward spreading.219R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §15): “…until the Men of the Great Assembly arose to repair the assembly, by nullifying the yetzer of idolatry (Yoma 69b); and therefore they are called ‘Knesses HaGedolah’ — for the assembly was made great through them.” This illuminates §4-4’s “master of enactments… a fence for the need of the hour”: the Great Assembly’s fences were the repair the hour demanded — the generation that had lost the first Temple to idolatry was rebuilt by them, and their very name records that it was through their safeguards that the assembly of Israel was “made great” again.220R’ Tzadok — parallel (Peri Tzadik, Vayakhel §1): “From this we derive all the ‘shevusin’ [rabbinic Shabbos restrictions] of the thirty-nine labors themselves, where they decreed ‘this because of that,’ and lest one come to full [forbidden] labor — because it resembles that labor, and one might come to confuse [them].” The se’if’s Nechemyah and the Men of the Great Assembly, “masters of enactments and safeguards,” who instituted muktzeh and the other fences “for the need of the hour” — “and make a fence for the Torah.”

וּמוֹסִיף עֲלֵיהֶם נְחֶמְיָה בַּעֲשִׂיַּית סְיָיג דִּלְצֹרֶךְ שָׁעָה, אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לְהִתְקַיֵּים לְעוֹלָם — שֶׁהֲרֵי בְּמֻקְצֶה הִתִּירוּ וְחָזְרוּ וְהִתִּירוּ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [שַׁבָּת קכג:] ״בִּימֵי נְחֶמְיָה בֶּן חֲכַלְיָה נִשְׁנֵית מִשְׁנָה זוֹ״ — וְהַכֹּל כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁרָאָה צֹרֶךְ לִגְדֹּר הַדּוֹר שֶׁלֹּא יָשׁוּבוּ לְכִסְלָה

And Nechemyah went beyond them, making a safeguard for the need of the hour, even one not fit to endure forever — for with muktzeh they permitted, then re-forbade, as they said [Shabbos 123b], “in the days of Nechemyah ben Chachalyah this mishnah was taught” — all according to what he saw was needed to fence in the generation, that they not return to folly.221Shabbos 123b: “‘All vessels may be moved on Shabbos [for a permitted purpose]’ — R’ Yochanan said: this mishnah was taught in the days of Nechemyah ben Chachalyah [nishnes mishnah zo], as it is written, ‘in those days I saw in Yehudah men treading winepresses on Shabbos’ (Nechemyah 13:15)” — the muktzeh restrictions were tightened, later relaxed, then re-tightened, per the generation’s need. R’ Tzadok: Nechemyah pioneered even temporary fences for the hour.222R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Soferim §31): “the foundation of the Oral Torah [was laid] through the Men of the Great Assembly — for this is what ‘they accepted again in the days of Achashverosh, from love of the miracle,’ that which had first [been received] under the coercion of the overturned mountain; and the coercion was upon the Oral Torah.” This is the deeper frame of §4-4: Nechemyah and his colleagues, the Men of the Great Assembly, are not merely adding rules — they are laying the very foundation of the Oral Torah, the domain of enactment and safeguard, which the returning exiles now took up willingly, “from love.”

אַף הוּא חִידֵּשׁ עִנְיַן חֲזָרַת קַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה, שֶׁבָּאוּ עַל הֶחָתוּם בְּאָלָה וּשְׁבוּעָה לִשְׁמוֹר תּוֹרַת ה’ כַּכָּתוּב בְּסִפְרוֹ; וּמִבֵּית אֲבוֹתָיו לְמָדָהּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע"ה ״נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי וָאֲקַיֵּמָה״ וְגוֹ’, וְלָמְדוּ מִזֶּה [נְדָרִים ח.] דְּנִשְׁבָּעִין לְקַיֵּים הַמִּצְוָה לְזָרוֹזֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ

He also renewed the matter of re-accepting the Torah, when they came “to the sealed document” with oath and vow to keep the Torah of Hashem, as written in his book; and he learned it from the house of his fathers, as David HaMelech said, “I have sworn and I will fulfill it” (Tehillim 119:106)223Tehillim 119:106: “נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי וָאֲקַיֵּמָה, לִשְׁמֹר מִשְׁפְּטֵי צִדְקֶךָ” — “I have sworn, and I will fulfill it, to keep Your righteous ordinances” — David HaMelech, in the great alphabetical psalm. In its plain sense (Rashi, Radak) David binds himself by oath to observe the mitzvos. From this verse the Gemara (Nedarim 8a) derives that “one may swear to fulfill a mitzvah in order to spur himself on [le-zaruzei nafshei]” — and this although every Jew already “stands sworn from Har Sinai” (mushba ve-omeid mi-Sinai), so that a further oath adds no formal obligation; the Ran explains that it nonetheless takes effect as a permitted, even praiseworthy, device to strengthen oneself in avodas Hashem. R’ Tzadok grounds Nechemyah’s enterprise in this verse of his ancestor David: the renewed “re-accepting of the Torah” — coming “to the sealed document with oath and vow” — is precisely the oath as a forward-looking zeruz, the engine of the teshuvah of fences and safeguards. — from which they derived [Nedarim 8a] that one may swear to fulfill a mitzvah, to spur himself on.224Nedarim 8a: “From where that one may swear to fulfill a mitzvah? As it says, ‘I have sworn and I will fulfill it, to keep Your righteous ordinances’ (Tehillim 119:106) — but one is already under oath from Sinai! Rather, it teaches that one may take an oath to spur himself on [le-zarozei nafshei].” R’ Tzadok traces Nechemyah’s “sealed covenant” to David — and to Boaz, who “swore to his yetzer” (“as Hashem lives, lie down until morning,” Rus 3:13, per the Sifrei).

וְאַף הוּא קִיבְּלָהּ מִזְּקֵנוֹ בֹּעַז שֶׁאָמַר ״חַי ה’ שִׁכְבִי [עַד הַבֹּקֶר]״, וְאָמְרוּ זַ"ל [סִפְרֵי] לְיִצְרוֹ נִשְׁבַּע; וּבָא נְחֶמְיָה וּפִירְסְמָהּ לְעֵצָה זוֹ בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְכָל עִנְיָנָיו וּמַעֲשָׂיו הָיָה בְּעִנְיָן זֶה — לְהוֹסִיף גְּדֵרִים וְזֵירוּזִים אַלְּהַבָּא שֶׁלֹּא יַעַבְרוּ עוֹד — וְעִנְיָן זֶה דִּתְשׁוּבָה הוּא הַמֵּבִיא גְּאֻלָּה

And he too received it from his ancestor Boaz, who said “as Hashem lives, lie down [until morning]” (Rus 3:13)225Rus 3:13: “לִינִי הַלַּיְלָה, […] אִם יִגְאָלֵךְ טוֹב יִגְאָל, וְאִם לֹא יַחְפֹּץ לְגָאֳלֵךְ וּגְאַלְתִּיךְ אָנֹכִי, חַי ה׳; שִׁכְבִי עַד הַבֹּקֶר” — Boaz to Rus on the threshing floor: “Stay the night… if he will redeem you, good, let him redeem; but if he does not wish to redeem you, then I will redeem you myself, as Hashem lives; lie down until morning.” In its plain sense (Rashi) Boaz swears to act as redeemer and reassures her to remain in modesty until morning, “that it not be known that a woman came to the threshing floor.” R’ Tzadok relies on the aggadic reading (cited in the sefer as Sifrei; the extant midrashic locus is Vayikra Rabbah 23:11, and cf. Rus Rabbah): that all that night Boaz was assailed by his yetzer, and his oath “chai Hashem” was sworn against his yetzer — “he swore to his yetzer” that he would not touch her unlawfully. This is the ancestral root (Boaz → David → Nechemyah) of “swearing to fulfill a mitzvah” and to subdue the yetzer — binding oneself by oath as a fence against sin, the very counsel Nechemyah publicized throughout Israel. Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Matos 2, treats the very phenomenon R' Tzadok cites here - swearing in order to overcome the yetzer - as a specific Torah remedy for the moment when ordinary counsel no longer works. The Izhbitzer distinguishes the advice of Avos, "look at three things and you will not come to sin," which operates before desire surges, from the crisis "בעידנא דיצר הרע לית מאן דמדכר ליצר טוב," when the yetzer suddenly overwhelms a person. For that hour the Torah gives the counsel of neder: "חי ה' אם אעשה זאת לעבור על רצון השי"ת חס ושלום." He then cites precisely David and Boaz, "שליצרם נשבעו," and joins to them the nazir of Shimon HaTzaddik who swore, at the moment his vanity flared, to shave his beautiful hair for Heaven. This is a strong Izhbitz explanation of why the fences and oaths of this se'if belong to the rung that brings geulah. The oath does not declare the yetzer unreal; it recognizes that there are moments when inner knowledge has been eclipsed and therefore creates a revealed boundary strong enough to carry the person through the eclipse. That is the opposite of misusing Divine foreknowledge to excuse the act. The hidden Divine story is left to Hashem; at the point of bechirah the person strengthens the revealed command with an additional fence. Nechemyah's communal enactments are the national form of the same medicine that David and Boaz applied within themselves., which the Sages said [Sifrei] [means] “he swore to his yetzer”; and Nechemyah came and publicized this counsel throughout Israel, and all his affairs and deeds were in this matter — to add fences and spurs going forward, that they sin no more — and this matter of teshuvah is what brings the redemption.

וְנִרְאֶה דְּדָרְשִׁינַן עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא [בִּמְגִילָּה טו:] עַל פָּסוּק ״וּלְרוּחַ מִשְׁפָּט״ — ״זֶה הַדָּן אֶת יִצְרוֹ״, וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִׁ"י כּוֹפֵהוּ לָשׁוּב בִּתְשׁוּבָה וּמִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִצְרוֹ; וְדָבָר זֶה דִּשְׁפִיטַת הַיֵּצֶר הוּא הַמְקָרֵב גְּאֻלָּה

And it appears that we expound in the manner brought [Megillah 15b] on the verse “and for a spirit of judgment [mishpat]” — “this is the one who judges his yetzer,” and Rashi explains: he forces himself to return in teshuvah and overpowers his yetzer; and this matter of judging the yetzer is what hastens the redemption.226Megillah 15b: “‘and for a spirit of judgment [mishpat] to him who sits in judgment’ (Yeshayah 28:6) — this is one who judges his yetzer”; Rashi: “he forces himself to return in teshuvah and overpowers his yetzer.” R’ Tzadok: the “judging of the yetzer” (accepting fences and guarding oneself) is precisely what “hastens the redemption.”
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר ״וּבָא לְצִיּוֹן גּוֹאֵל, וּלְשָׁבֵי פֶשַׁע בְּיַעֲקֹב״; כִּי הֲבָאַת הַגְּאֻלָּה לְגַמְרֵי הוּא תִּיקּוּן גָּמוּר עַל הַקּוֹדֵם גַּם כֵּן, וְ״זֶה לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי״

And of this it says, “and a redeemer shall come to Zion, and to those of Yaakov who turn from transgression” (Yeshayah 59:20)227Yeshayah 59:20: “וּבָא לְצִיּוֹן גּוֹאֵל, וּלְשָׁבֵי פֶשַׁע בְּיַעֲקֹב, נְאֻם ה׳” — “And a redeemer shall come to Zion, and to those of Yaakov who turn from transgression, says Hashem” — from Yeshayah’s prophecy of the redemption. Rashi: the redeemer comes to Zion for the sake of “shavei fesha,” those who turn back from sin. This is the Gemara’s very proof (Yoma 86b) that “great is teshuvah, for it brings [hastens] the redemption” — the go’el comes because of the ba’alei teshuvah. R’ Tzadok binds the complete redemption to “shavei fesha be-Yaakov” specifically: it comes through the turning-from-sin of the seed of Yaakov, and “be-Yaakov” precisely — for “He did not do so for any [other] nation”; the complete rectification of the soul belongs to Israel and not to the nations of the world.; for the complete bringing of the redemption is a complete rectification of the past as well, and “He did not do so for any [other] nation.”228Ein Yaakov / Rif on Yoma (ch. 8): the Rif notes that the verse R’ Yochanan cites for “teshuvah hastens redemption” — “keep judgment [shimru mishpat] and do righteousness, for My salvation is near to come” (Yeshayah 56:1) — mentions not teshuvah but keeping judgment; he answers that “keeping judgment” leads to teshuvah (“when all these things come upon you and you return to Hashem your God,” Devarim 30:1–2), and so hastens the redemption. R’ Tzadok builds on this the identification of “keeping judgment” with “judging the yetzer.”

וְעַל זְמַן הַגְּאֻלָּה הַשְּׁלֵימָה נֶאֱמַר ״ה’ בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ״, וְאֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת גְּאֻלָּה שְׁלֵימָה בִּפְדוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כְּלָל; וְרַק לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ אָמְרוּ זַ"ל דְּהַמָּשִׁיחַ יָבוֹא לִיתֵּן מִצְוֹת לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, וְהֵם ״בֶּן הַנֵּכָר הַנִּלְוֶה״

And of the time of the complete redemption it says, “Hashem alone shall lead him” (Devarim 32:12)229Devarim 32:12: “ה׳ בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ, וְאֵין עִמּוֹ אֵל נֵכָר” — “Hashem alone did guide him, and there was no foreign god with Him” — from Shiras Ha’azinu, of God’s lone guidance of Israel. Rashi: “Hashem badad yanchenu — He guided them securely, alone, in the wilderness, with no foreign god’s aid; and so is He destined to settle them, dwelling alone and secure”; “ve-ein imo el nechar — none of the gods of the nations had any power to display strength and wage war against Him” (cf. Onkelos). “Badad” bespeaks Israel’s singular separateness and security under God alone (cf. “am levadad yishkon,” Bamidbar 23:9). R’ Tzadok reads it of the complete redemption: “Hashem badad yanchenu” — Israel alone, with no admixture of the nations and “no foreign god with Him” — for the nations have no portion or existence in the ultimate redemption of the soul, which is “badad,” Israel’s alone; as against the days of Mashiach, when the nations still retain “some joining” so long as they have existence. Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Ha'azinu 5, comments on this exact verse, "ה' בדד ינחנו ואין עמו אל נכר," that in this world many created things can appear as aids to Torah - wealth, possessions, and the conditions that broaden the mind - "אבל לעתיד לא יהיה שום כח רק השי"ת לבדו": in the future there will be no power at all except Hashem alone. This brings the siman's final contrast into unusually sharp focus. The complete geulah is not only that hostile powers cease to rule; even helpful secondary powers cease to claim independent standing. "Badad" means that the redemptive order is experienced directly as Hashem's guidance with no rival or auxiliary power beside Him. Taken together with the Mei HaShiloach on Zechariah cited above - "לא בחיל ולא בכח כי אם ברוחי" - the Ishbitz picture forms a single arc. Zerubavel inaugurates a redemption whose secret is already that human force is not the final cause; in the complete future that truth is totally manifest, "ה' בדד ינחנו." This is why R' Tzadok can describe the fourth rung as a spreading-out of teshuvah: the same recognition that, after return, uncovers Hashem's presence within the individual's story ultimately expands until the national story itself contains no alien power standing outside His guidance.; and there is no relation of a complete redemption in the soul’s deliverance to the nations at all; only in the days of Mashiach did the Sages say that Mashiach will come to give mitzvos to the nations, and they are the “foreigner who joins himself,”

וּמִצַּד הִתְקָרְבוּת הַיְּשׁוּעָה וְהַגְּאוּלָּה יִהְיֶה גַּם לָהֶם לִיוּוּי וְחִיבּוּר קְצָת, וְלֹא יַרְחִיקֵם השי"ת כָּל זְמַן שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לִהְיוֹת מְקוֹרָבִים; מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּעֵת גְּאֻלָּה גְּמוּרָה, אֵין לָהֶם מְצִיאוּת עוֹד כְּלָל

and from the side of the approach of the salvation and redemption there will be for them, too, some “joining” and attachment, and Hashem will not distance them so long as it is possible for them to be brought near; whereas at the time of the complete redemption, they have no existence at all.

sections.en: Great is teshuvah, for willful sins become as errors — or as merits

items.h: גדולה תשובה שזדונות נעשות כשגגות או זכויות.
“Great is teshuvah, for the willful sins become as inadvertent ones — or as merits” (the fifth — corresponding to Hod).

The theme: This is the rectification of the past, in deeds already carried out into act. Reaching, in the heart’s teshuvah, up to the soul’s root in the mind spreads the rectification down into the deeds themselves. “As inadvertent ones” comes through teshuvah from fear, which stills the heart but leaves the earlier intent standing — the difference between love, the root of “arise and do,” and fear, the root of “sit and do not.”

p: [א] ״שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוּ כִּשְׁגָגוֹת אוֹ זְכֻיּוֹת״, וְהוּא תִּיקּוּן הֶעָבַר בְּמַעֲשִׂים שֶׁיָּצְאוּ לְפֹעַל כְּבָר

“That the willful sins become as inadvertent ones or as merits” — and this is the rectification of the past, in deeds that have already emerged into act.230Yoma 86b: “Reish Lakish said: Great is teshuvah, for willful sins become for him as inadvertent ones, as it says, ‘Return, Israel, unto Hashem your God, for you have stumbled [kashalta] in your iniquity’ (Hoshea 14:2) — ‘iniquity’ is willful, yet it is called a ‘stumbling’ [inadvertent]. But Reish Lakish [also] said: Great is teshuvah, for willful sins become for him as merits, as it says, ‘and when the wicked turns from his wickedness and does justice and righteousness, by them he shall live’ (Yechezkel 33:19)! — It is not difficult: here [merits] from love, there [inadvertent] from fear.” R’ Tzadok builds the whole siman on this ahavah/yirah distinction.231Cf. the same distinction across Chassidus: Me’or Einayim (Ha’azinu) — teshuvah from fear renders willful sins “as inadvertent,” teshuvah from love renders them “as merits,” exactly R’ Tzadok’s yirah/ahavah frame; and Tanya, Likkutei Amarim ch. 7: “a teshuvah from a great love, from the depths of the heart, until the willful sins become like actual merits.”Chassidic and Maharal parallels — the mechanism of “z’donos as merits.” Maharal, Netivos Olam, Nesiv HaTeshuvah 2:17–19, explains that the sinner’s very distance becomes the measure of his later attachment: one who returns “from afar” displays a stronger deveikus, and therefore the z’don itself — the distance that he traversed — can be reckoned as a zechus. This closely complements R’ Tzadok’s claim here that teshuvah me-ahavah does not merely lighten the old act but reaches back to the will that generated it. Sefas Emes, Shabbos Shuvah 9:4, makes the distinction still more explicit: teshuvah from fear is awakened by the damage of sin and therefore weakens the sin into shogeg; teshuvah from love is awakened by longing to cleave to Torah and mitzvos, so that the sin itself becomes the cause of intensified love and added merit — “נמצא ממש זדונות נעשין כמו זכיות.” Tanya, Likkutei Amarim ch. 7, gives the same causal structure: because the soul had been “in a dry and shadowed land,” its later thirst for God is stronger, and “since through this he came to this great love,” the deliberate sins become actual merits. Shelah, Asarah Ma’amaros, Ma’amar Asiri §12, uses this distinction to reconcile the two statements about whether the baal teshuvah or the complete tzaddik is higher: ordinary teshuvah from fear does not surpass the tzaddik, whereas the rare teshuvah from love does. Chiddushei HaRim, Chayei Sarah §1, adds the temporal point that teshuvah can repair earlier days retroactively “as though he had performed mitzvos and good deeds” in them. These sources do not replace R’ Tzadok’s sharper metaphysical claim; they supply the devotional and conceptual mechanism by which the past itself becomes productive of present holiness.232R’ Tzadok — parallel (Ohr Zarua LaTzadik §4): “this is the end-deed and this is the beginning-of-thought — Esav only said [it] in his heart, while Haman brought the decree out into act; and Kayin, and Gog and Magog, are likewise ‘the end-deed [that was] in thought first.’” This gives §5-1 its mechanism: every deed’s origin lies in the thought — “the end of the deed is in the thought first” — so when teshuvah “reaches the root of the soul in the mind,” it takes hold of the deed at its very beginning; the act that “already emerged into act” is rectified from the thought-root out of which it first came.

וְעַל יְדֵי הַהַגָּעָה בִּתְשׁוּבָתוֹ שֶׁבַּלֵּב עַד שֹׁרֶשׁ הַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ, שֶׁזֶּהוּ עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד, מִמֶּנּוּ נִמְשָׁךְ וּמִתְפַּשֵּׁט גַּם כֵּן תִּיקּוּן יְצִיאַת הַמַּעֲשִׂים לַפֹּעַל
