R’ Tzadok’s use: “in this world the perfect tzaddik is the more esteemed” — for “man looks to the eyes” (the one whose eyes are beautiful — the revealed Rachel) — “but Hashem looks to the heart,” to the purity of thought and the depths, which is Leah’s hidden rung of teshuvah. — [esteeming] the one whose eyes are beautiful —
״וַה׳ יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב״ לְטָהֳרַת הַמַּחְשָׁבָה וְהַמַּעֲמַקִּים שֶׁבּוֹ

but “Hashem looks to the heart” — to the purity of thought and the depths within.489R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §39): “The essential holiness of thought [kedushas ha-machshavah] comes only from habit and from the effort of ‘the commandment of men learned by rote’ [mitzvas anashim melumadah] — which, though it accomplishes nothing in the heart, is the more beneficial for [the purity of] the thought. For from a feeling in the heart comes such enthusiasm that one can [scarcely] act with composure; but from the recognition of the intellect in thought, one is not [over]-inflamed, and it works properly, with a settled mind.” (Thus Leah’s rung — “purity of thought,” at which every steady increase of holiness in Israel is achieved — is reached precisely through disciplined, unspectacular toil.)490R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §3): “as against man, who looks to the eyes — but Hashem looks to the heart, the truth as it truly is, which is not revealed in this world.” This is §6-10’s closing measure — “‘man looks to the eyes’… ‘but Hashem looks to the heart,’ to the purity of thought and the depths within”: the esteem this world gives the openly-comely tzaddik is the sight of the eye, but the hidden truth of the heart — Leah’s rung — is seen by God alone.491R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas Shabbos §3): “‘Hashem looks to the heart’ — that the essential is the purifying of the heart to receive wisdom; for [beforehand] there are two hearts, the yetzer-ra and the yetzer-tov, [and the labor is] to become ‘one heart.’” This unfolds §6-10’s “purity of thought”: what God sees in the heart is its purification — the work of Leah’s rung, cleaving to the Divine “thought,” until the divided heart becomes one, fit to receive the light.
וְשָׁם אָמַר ״יִרְאֶה״ לְשׁוֹן עָתִיד, הָרְאִיָּה גַּם כֵּן לַלֵּב
And there [the verse] used “yireh” (will see), in the future tense — [indicating] that [ultimate] “seeing,” too, [reaches] to the heart —
[וְזֶה הָיָה בְּעֵת בְּחִירַת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה, ״הַגֶּבֶר אֲשֶׁר הֵקִים עוּלָּהּ״ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁתְּלוּיָה בַּלֵּב
[and this was at the time of the choosing of David HaMelech — “the man who raised up the yoke” of teshuvah, which depends on the heart,
דְּ״לְבָבוֹ יָבִין וָשָׁב״, וְעִיקַּר הִסְתַּכְּלוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בּוֹ לַלֵּב, אַף דְּהוּא הָיָה יְפֵה עֵינַיִם גַּם כֵּן]
for “his heart understands and repents,” and Hashem’s essential gaze upon him was to the heart, even though he too was “of beautiful eyes”].
כִּי כָּל לְשׁוֹן עָתִיד מוֹרֶה עַל הַשָּׂגָה דִּלְעָתִיד לָבוֹא
For every future-tense expression indicates an attainment [reserved] for the Future to Come,
כְּטַעַם ״אֵין ‘וְהָיָה’ אֶלָּא שִׂמְחָה״ שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן עָתִיד, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן ״וַיְהִי״

in the sense of “‘ve-hayah’ denotes only joy” — which is future tense — unlike “va-yehi” [past] (Megillah 10b)492Megillah 10b: “A tradition from the Men of the Great Assembly: wherever it says ‘va-yehi’ [and it came to pass], it denotes nothing but distress.” (Whereas ‘ve-hayah’ [and it shall be] — future tense — denotes joy.).
וְכָאן ״וַיַּרְא ה׳״ לְשׁוֹן עָבָר הוּא רְאִיָּה בְּעָלְמָא דְּאִתְגַּלְיָא
And here, “and Hashem saw” — past tense — is a “seeing” in the revealed world.
וּלְפִי שֶׁמַּפְתֵּחַ שֶׁל עֲקָרוֹת בְּיָדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ (תַּעֲנִית ב. עַיֵּין שָׁם)

And since “the key of barrenness is in His hand” (Taanis 2a, see there)493Taanis 2a: “R’ Yochanan said: Three keys are in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, that are not given over to a messenger — the key of rain, the key of the woman in childbirth [mafteach shel chayah], and the key of the resurrection of the dead.” (So the ending of barrenness — the ‘opening of the womb’ — is in His hand alone.)Izhbitz-Radzin and Chiddushei HaRim parallel - Sha'ar HaEmunah VeYesod HaChasidut 24:3-4; Chiddushei HaRim on Torah, Chayei Sara 1: The Izhbitz-Radzin identification of complete teshuvah with Binah sheds light on R. Tzadok's claim that Leah's power of "birth" is rooted in teshuvah and inner thought. Sha'ar HaEmunah teaches that when a person returns fully to the place of Binah he rises above ordinary time, and therefore can "heal the earlier" - the past is no longer a sealed block that can only be regretted. Chiddushei HaRim expresses the same transformative power more existentially: through teshuvah, "in one hour and one moment," past days can be repaired as though they had been filled with mitzvos and good deeds. This makes R. Tzadok's language of holadah particularly apt. Teshuvah is not only erasure; it is generative. From the very place in which a life seemed to have been diminished, new Torah, new avodah, and even a new reading of the past can be born. Leah, the hidden Binah-world, thus represents the womb of spiritual renewal.,
וְלָמְדוּ מִמִּקְרָא הַזֶּה דְּ״וַיִּפְתַּח״ דְּלֹא הָיָה הַהוֹלָדָה טִבְעִית כְּכָל לֵידַת בָּנִים דְּעָלְמָא
and they derived from this verse, “and He opened,” that [Leah’s] “bearing” was not natural, like the ordinary birth of “children of the world,”
רַק הוֹלָדַת נְפָשׁוֹת יְקָרוֹת מִיָּדוֹ יִת״שׁ כְּפִי מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם הָרָאוּי לָהֶם — הָיָה הַמִּשְׁפָּט רַק לְלֵאָה
but rather a bearing of precious souls from His hand, [apportioned] according to their deeds as befits them — the “judgment” [over which] belonged to Leah alone.

items.h: The theme: Reuven, born “for the seeing,” is the first of Israel’s holy ones recorded with a grave “sin” — precisely to reveal the level of teshuvah (impossible without sin). “Whoever says Reuven sinned is mistaken” — yet Scripture magnifies it to magnify teshuvah, so the sin itself becomes praise. So too Yehudah/Tamar → the House of David. Leah’s rung culminates; joined with Yaakov she rises to Chochmah.

p: [יא] וּלְפִי שֶׁהָיָה מִצַּד הָרְאִיָּה נוֹלַד רְאוּבֵן עַל שֵׁם הָרְאִיָּה
And because [Leah’s conceiving] was from the side of “seeing,” Reuven was born [and named] for the “seeing,”
כִּי ״רָאָה ה׳ בְּעׇנְיִי״ [וְכִי שְׂנוּאָה אָנֹכִי]

“for Hashem has seen my affliction” (Bereishis 29:32)494Bereishis 29:32: “וַתַּהַר לֵאָה וַתֵּלֶד בֵּן וַתִּקְרָא שְׁמוֹ רְאוּבֵן, כִּי אָמְרָה כִּי רָאָה ה׳ בְּעׇנְיִי, כִּי עַתָּה יֶאֱהָבַנִי אִישִׁי” — “…she called his name Reuven, for she said, ‘Hashem has seen my affliction, for now my husband will love me.’” Rashi: the name hints “re’u ben — see the difference between my son and the son of [Esav]”; and “ra’ah Hashem b’onyi” — He saw that she was the “hated” one (the next verse, 29:33, names Shimon “ki shama Hashem ki senuah anochi”). R’ Tzadok’s use: Reuven, Leah’s firstborn, is named for the re’iyah (“seeing”) — born “from the side of seeing,” and so the very one through whom the rung of teshuvah (which needs a prior “sin”) would first be revealed in the world. [and that “I am hated”].
וּבוֹ נִתְגַּלָּה דָּבָר זֶה, שֶׁהוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן מִזֶּרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמְקוּדָּשִׁים שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה חֵטְא עָצוּם כָּזֶה
And through him this matter was revealed — for he is the first of the sanctified seed of Israel of whom the Torah records so grave a “sin” —
וְנִתְגַּלָּה תֵּיכֶף עַל יָדוֹ מַדְרֵיגַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה בָּעוֹלָם, שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהּ בְּלֹא חֵטְא

and through him the level of teshuvah was at once revealed in the world — a level impossible [to manifest] without a sin.495R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Korach §13): “it is the kelipah of murder and anger and envy, "strange fires" — and corresponding to them, Mashiach ben David, who is Chesed, and Mashiach ben Yosef, who is the aspect of dread and fear.” Exactly the se’if: the kinds of evil among the nations are an ordered set of husks, each answered by its opposite in holiness — which is why they can be countered and not merely endured.
וְ״תַלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁחָטָא אַל תְּהַרְהֵר״, דְּוַדַּאי עָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה מִיָּד

And “[of] a talmid chacham who sinned — do not brood [over him]” (Berachos 19a)496Berachos 19a: “If you have seen a talmid chacham transgress a matter by night, do not brood over him [al te’harher acharav] by day, for he has surely repented.”, for he surely repented at once;
וְנֶאֱמַר מִיָּד ״וַיִּהְיוּ בְנֵי יַעֲקֹב שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר״ דְּנִתְקַבְּלָה תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ
and immediately it says, “and the sons of Yaakov were twelve” (Bereishis 35:22) — [showing] that his teshuvah was accepted.
וְאַף שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל (שַׁבָּת נה:) ״כָּל הָאוֹמֵר רְאוּבֵן חָטָא אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא טוֹעֶה, רַק מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב״

And even though the Sages said (Shabbos 55b)497Shabbos 55b: “R’ Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of R’ Yonasan: Whoever says Reuven sinned is simply mistaken [kol ha-omer Reuven chata eino ela to’eh]” — Scripture only accounts it to him as though [he had].498R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Chalomot §16): “(Shabbos 55b) ‘whoever says Reuven sinned is merely mistaken’ — only that, on account of his great level, Scripture reckons it against him as if he sinned, for those near [to God] are judged most exactingly; and even over this slight matter he sat in sackcloth and fasting and repented in complete teshuvah.” This is §6-11’s Reuven exactly — the recorded “sin” that “Scripture only accounts to him” is the measure of his height, and the sackcloth-and-fasting return it provoked is the whole point: the sin was made large only to make the teshuvah large., “whoever says Reuven sinned is merely mistaken; rather, Scripture [only] accounts it to him,” —
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֲרֵי הַכָּתוּב חָפֵץ בְּטוֹבַת וּבְשֶׁבַח כָּל הַבְּרִיּוֹת וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן שִׁבְטֵי יָ-הּ
nonetheless, Scripture desires the good and the praise of all creatures, and all the more so the tribes of Kah;
וְלָמָּה יְסַפֵּר בִּגְנוּתָן מַה שֶּׁלֹּא חָטְאוּ וְיִתְלֶה בּוֹ חֵטְא עָצוּם כָּזֶה לִהְיוֹת מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִלּוּ עָשָׂה
why, then, would it recount to their disgrace something they did not do, and hang upon him so grave a sin that Scripture reckons it against him as if he did it —
וּבִפְרָט שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת שָׁב אַחַר כָּךְ
especially since he truly repented afterward?
רַק לְפִי שֶׁכָּל חֶטְאוֹ הָיָה לְגַלּוֹת מַדְרֵיגַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה וּלְהוֹדִיעַ תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ
Rather, since his whole “sin” was [in order] to reveal the level of teshuvah and to make known his repentance,
אִם כֵּן בְּהֶכְרֵחַ הָיָה לְגַלּוֹת הַחֵטְא וְעוֹד לְהַגְדִּילוֹ כְּדֵי לְהַגְדִּיל כֹּחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה
it was therefore necessary to reveal the sin, and even to enlarge it, so as to enlarge the power of teshuvah;
וְזֶהוּ שִׁבְחוֹ, שֶׁאַחַר הַתְּשׁוּבָה שָׁב הַחֵטְא עַצְמוֹ לִהְיוֹת שֶׁבַח וּזְכוּת

and this is his praise: that after teshuvah, the sin itself turned into praise and merit — the recorded “sin” serving less as a stain than as the backdrop against which the power of return could first be displayed.
וְכֵן בִּיהוּדָה מֵאִתּוֹ יָצְאוּ כּוֹבְשִׁים לִבְרֹא אוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ
And likewise with Yehudah — from him issued “conquerors,” [destined] to bring forth the light of Mashiach —
וּבוֹ נִתְגַּלָּה תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת שֶׁל הַתִּיקּוּן
and through him was revealed the ultimate perfection of the rectification;
דְּאַף שֶׁהָיָה נִרְאֶה כְּחֵטְא וּבִיאַת זוֹנָה, בֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה דָּבָר קָדוֹשׁ מְאוֹד
for although [the Tamar episode] appeared as a sin, a union with a “harlot,” in truth it was a most holy matter —
דְּמָארֵיא בִּישָׁא וּפוֹעֵל רַע גּוּרְיָא טָבָא לָא נָפִיק

for “from an evil master and an evildoer, a good cub does not issue” (Bava Kama 92b)499Bava Kama 92b: among the folk-sayings that the Gemara roots in Scripture is the maxim that a worthy offspring does not issue from an unworthy source — “from an evil master and an evildoer, a good cub does not come forth.” R’ Tzadok’s use is by inversion: precisely because the House of David — “the holiest souls in Israel” — did issue from the Yehudah–Tamar union, that union, though “to the eye’s view” it looked like “a sin, a union with a harlot,” was “in truth a most holy matter”; the holy “cub” proves the holiness of its root. [and yet David issued from it].
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁמִּזֶּה יָצָא שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת בֵּית דָּוִד וּמָשִׁיחַ שֶׁהֵם נְפָשׁוֹת הַיּוֹתֵר קְדוֹשׁוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
And since from this issued the chain of the House of David and Mashiach — the holiest souls in Israel —
עַל כֵּן הָיָה הָעִנְיַן קְדֻשָּׁה יְתֵירָה מְאוֹד, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה עֲדַיִין כָּזֹאת, וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה רָאוּי לָזֶה
the matter was one of exceedingly great holiness, of a kind not seen before, [which had to be] fitting for this —
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלְּמַרְאִית הָעַיִן אֵין כֵּן
even though to the eye’s view it was not so.
וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת דַּרְגָּא דְּלֵאָה, וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרָה ״הַפַּעַם אוֹדֶה אֶת ה׳״

And this is the ultimate perfection of Leah’s rung; therefore she said [at Yehudah’s birth], “This time I will thank Hashem” (Bereishis 29:35)500Bereishis 29:35: “וַתַּהַר עוֹד וַתֵּלֶד בֵּן וַתֹּאמֶר הַפַּעַם אוֹדֶה אֶת ה׳, עַל כֵּן קָרְאָה שְׁמוֹ יְהוּדָה, וַתַּעֲמֹד מִלֶּדֶת” — “…she said, ‘This time I will thank Hashem,’ therefore she called his name Yehudah; and she ceased bearing.” Berachos 7b: “from the day the Holy One created His world, no one gave thanks to Him until Leah came and gave thanks” — she was the first ever to offer hoda’ah. R’ Tzadok’s use: with Yehudah — forebear of the House of David and Mashiach — “the ultimate perfection of Leah’s rung” was reached; her “ha-paam odeh” marks the hoda’ah / teshuvah trait brought to its fullness (whereupon she “ceased bearing” until the dudaim).,
שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְבָּרֵר עִנְיָינָהּ וּמַעֲלָתָהּ
for by then her matter and her greatness had been made clear.
וְאָז עָמְדָה מִלֶּדֶת עַד מַעֲשֵׂה הַדּוּדָאִים

And then she ceased bearing, until the episode of the dudaim,501Bereishis 30:14–18 (the dudaim): “וַיֵּלֶךְ רְאוּבֵן בִּימֵי קְצִיר חִטִּים וַיִּמְצָא דוּדָאִים בַּשָּׂדֶה, וַיָּבֵא אֹתָם אֶל לֵאָה אִמּוֹ” — Reuven found dudaim (mandrakes) and brought them to Leah; Rachel sought them, and in exchange Leah “hired” Yaakov for that night (v. 16), conceiving Yissachar — “sachar sechartich” (v. 18) — and thereafter Zevulun. R’ Tzadok’s use: after Yehudah’s birth Leah “ceased bearing until the episode of the dudaim,” when “an additional facet of her greatness” emerged — the bearing of Yissachar (the Torah-scholars) and Zevulun (their supporters), binding her rung to Torah itself.
שֶׁאָז נִתְחַדֵּשׁ גִּילּוּי עִנְיָן נוֹסָף בְּמַעֲלַת לֵאָה בְּהוֹלָדַת יִשָּׂשכָר וּזְבוּלוּן
when an additional facet of Leah’s greatness was newly revealed, in the bearing of Yissachar and Zevulun —
שֶׁהֵם לוֹמְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה וְתָמְכֵי אוֹרַיְיתָא

who are the “students of Torah” and the “supporters of Torah.”502R’ Tzadok — parallel (Likkutei Maamarim §8): “‘whoever teaches his fellow’s son Torah, Scripture accounts it as if he bore him’ — and he actually creates souls, as ‘those who feared Hashem spoke… and a book of remembrance was written,’ for through words of Torah the Holy One writes souls into the book of remembrance.” This lights up §6-11’s added greatness of Leah — the bearing of Yissachar and Zevulun, “the students of Torah and the supporters of Torah”: Torah-bearing is itself a birth — “Scripture accounts it as if he bore him,” the very idiom by which Reuven’s “sin” was accounted — so that Leah’s Torah-offspring are souls newly created.
וְהַתּוֹרָה ״נוֹבְלוֹת חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל

And the Torah is “the ripened fruit of the supernal Wisdom [Chochmah],” as the Sages said (Bereishis Rabbah 17:5)503Bereishis Rabbah 17:5: “The ‘unripe fruit’ [noveles] of the supernal light is the orb of the sun; the ‘unripe fruit’ of the supernal Wisdom is the Torah [noveles chochmah shel ma’alah — Torah].”,
וְהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵיגַת הַבִּינָה שֶׁמִּשָּׁם הַתְּשׁוּבָה דַּרְגָּא דְּלֵאָה מִצַּד עַצְמָהּ
which is higher than the level of Binah, whence [comes] teshuvah — the rung of Leah in her own right.
וּכְשֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנָּה שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת ״הֵקִים״ שֶׁהֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה כְּבָר נִשְׁלַם מַדְרֵיגָתָהּ בִּשְׁלֵימוּת
and once there issued from her the chain of the one who “raised up the yoke” of teshuvah [David], her level was completed in its fullness.
אֲבָל מִצַּד מַדְרֵיגָה גְּדוֹלָה יוֹתֵר חַבּוּרָה עִם יַעֲקֹב
But from the side of a still-higher level, [Leah] is joined with Yaakov himself;

שֶׁבְּחַבּוּרוֹ עִם לֵאָה גַּם הוּא נִתְעַלָּה לְמַדְרֵיגַת חָכְמָה, דַּרְגָּא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַמּוֹרֶה עַל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא לג.]504Bava Metzia 33a: “Those who engage in Scripture — it is a measure yet not [truly] a measure; in Mishnah — a measure for which one receives reward; in Talmud — there is no measure greater than this.”
for in his union with Leah he too was elevated to the level of Chochmah — the rung of “Yisrael,” which denotes a talmid chacham, as they said [in Bava Metzia 33a];
וְנוֹדָע דְּחָכְמָה וּבִינָה תְּרֵין רֵיעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין

and it is known that Chochmah and Binah are “two companions that never part.”505Zohar (a recurring dictum; cf. Zohar III 4a, and the Idra): Chochmah and Binah — “Abba and Imma” — are “trein re’in de-la mitpar’shin,” “two companions that never part,” ever joined in perfect union. R’ Tzadok’s use: Leah’s own rung is Binah (the source of teshuvah), but “from a still-higher level” she is joined with Yaakov and rises with him to Chochmah (the rung of “Yisrael,” the talmid chacham); and since Chochmah and Binah “never part,” the union of Yaakov and Leah is the deepest bond of all.Sefat Emet parallel - Vayeshev 33:4: Sefat Emet develops precisely the paradox R. Tzadok sees in Reuven. On "ha-yeled einenu va-ani anah ani va," he cites the Midrash that Reuven was the first to open the path of teshuvah and that Hoshea, descended from Reuven, therefore opened his prophecy with "Shuvah Yisrael." He defines complete teshuvah as the state in which, because of the sin, the person finds no place or independent existence for himself; only then does Hashem give him a new "place" of refuge. He adds that Reuven was in truth a tzaddik and that the very occurrence of his failing served so that he could teach teshuvah for the generations. This is an exceptionally close complement to R. Tzadok's "kol ha-omer Reuven chata eino ela to'eh" together with Reuven's being the first recorded Israelite paradigm of return. The point is not to deny the moral seriousness of what required teshuvah. Rather, the revealed fall and the hidden purity coexist in such a way that the fall itself becomes the occasion through which the world learns a form of return that could not have been taught by an untouched tzaddik.
רַק לְפִי שֶׁעַצְמוּת יַעֲקֹב, דַּרְגָּא דֶּאֱמֶת, הִיא הַתּוֹרָה
Only, since the essence of Yaakov — the rung of “truth” — is the Torah,
שֶׁהִיא רַק רְשִׁימוּ מֵחָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה הַמּוּשָּׂג בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which is but an “impression” of the supernal Chochmah as it is grasped in this world,
וּמִצִּידָהּ הוּא הַהַגְדָּרוֹת דַּעֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
and from its side [come] the definitions of “do” and “do not do” —
עַל כֵּן אָהַב אֶת רָחֵל
therefore [in this world] he loved Rachel.

items.h: The theme: Yaakov’s love of Rachel belongs only to olam ha-zeh; in the World to Come he is buried with Leah, at the root of supernal Chochmah (Abba and Ima that never part). Reuven and Shimon are the tikkun of seeing and hearing. Leah’s longing to bear tribes — desire channeled into holiness — is “very good.” This world is alma d’shikra: its pleasures last but a moment; only “the lip of truth is established forever.”

p: [יב] וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הָיָה רַק בְּאֹהֶל רָחֵל
And this — from the side of manifestation in this world — was only “in the tent of Rachel”;
אֲבָל לְעוֹלָם הַבָּא אֵינוֹ כֵן, שֶׁכֵּן קְבוּרָתוֹ בִּמְעָרַת הַמַּכְפֵּלָה עִם לֵאָה

but as to the World to Come it is not so, for his burial is in Me’aras HaMachpelah with Leah506Bereishis 49:31 (cf. 50:13): “שָׁמָּה קָבְרוּ אֶת אַבְרָהָם וְאֵת שָׂרָה אִשְׁתּוֹ… וְשָׁמָּה קָבַרְתִּי אֶת לֵאָה” — “there they buried Avraham and Sarah his wife… and there I buried Leah.” In his charge, Yaakov asks to be buried in Me’aras HaMachpelah beside Leah — not Rachel, who was buried “on the road to Efras” (Bereishis 35:19) — and Yaakov himself is laid there (50:13). R’ Tzadok’s use: Yaakov’s love of Rachel belonged only to “this world” and its outward manifestation; but for eternity — the World to Come — his rest is with Leah, “in the secret of Abba and Ima that never part,” his level raised to the root of supernal Chochmah. —
נִרְאֶה דִּלְעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁנִּתְעַלֵּית מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ לְשׇׁרְשׁוֹ, שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה, שָׁם אֵין הַגְדָּרוֹת
[which] shows that in the World to Come, where his level is raised to its root — the root of supernal Chochmah — there are no “definitions/limits”;
וְהֵם יַעֲקֹב וְלֵאָה בְּרָזָא דְּאַבָּא וְאִימָא דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין

and there Yaakov and Leah are in the secret of Abba and Ima that never part.507R’ Tzadok — parallel (Sichas Shedim §2): “the emergence of the power of Chochmah and Binah into actuality… [as] male and female” — Abba and Ima, the two supernal companions. This is the root to which §6-12 raises Yaakov in the World to Come — “the root of supernal Chochmah, where there are no boundaries,” where “Yaakov and Leah are in the secret of Abba and Ima that never part”: the union of Chochmah and Binah that, unlike this world’s love of Rachel, knows no limit.
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לֹא יָצָא עֲדַיִין לְגִילּוּי בְּפֹעַל דַּרְגָּא דְּלֵאָה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת עַד בִּיאַת הַמָּשִׁיחַ מִזַּרְעָהּ בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ
And in this world, Leah’s rung has not yet come forth to its full actual revelation — [not] until the coming of Mashiach from her seed, speedily in our days (see note 14 above).
וְכָל לֵידַת הַשְּׁבָטִים הֵם הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשָּׁרָשִׁים לְבַד בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And all the births of the tribes are [merely] the revelation of the “roots” [of the soul-powers] in this world.
וְשֹׁרֶשׁ רְאוּבֵן וְשִׁמְעוֹן הוּא רַק תִּיקּוּן הָרְאִיָּה וְהַשְּׁמִיעָה
And the root of Reuven and Shimon is the rectification of seeing and hearing:
דְּמִצַּד עַיִן רוֹאָה בָּא הַחֲמָדוֹת
for from the side of the seeing eye come the covetings,
וּמִצַּד אֹזֶן שׁוֹמַעַת בָּא קַבָּלַת הַתּוֹכָחָה וְהַתְּשׁוּבָה
and from the side of the hearing ear comes the acceptance of reproof and of teshuvah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל (דב״ר י, א) ״הָאֹזֶן הַזֶּה כְּקַנְקַל לַגּוּף״
as the Sages said (Devarim Rabbah 10:1): “this ear is like a kankal (conduit) for the body” [through which reproof enters].
וְכָל חֵשֶׁק לֵאָה לְהַרְבּוֹת שְׁבָטִים, וְזֶה עִיקַּר מַעֲלָתָהּ מִצַּד הַחֶמְדָּה וְהַחֵשֶׁק

And all of Leah’s yearning was to increase the tribes — this being her essential greatness, from the side of longing and desire —508R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §27): “living waters welling a fresh drop and new longings each day — ‘in the place where baalei teshuvah stand’ (Berachos 34); therefore the Euphrates corresponds to it, whose waters are fruitful and multiply, fresh drops each day.” This is §6-12’s measure of Leah — “all of Leah’s yearning was to increase the tribes, this being her essential greatness, from the side of longing and desire”: desire, when it is cheshek in holiness, is the ever-renewing wellspring of the baal teshuvah — “very good,” never a wasteland.
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּל חֵשֶׁק הוּא מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
even though all “desire” [as such] is from the side of the inclination in this world,

שֶׁהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ [בְּיוֹמָא סט:]509Yoma 69b: The “Men of the Great Assembly” are so named because “they restored the crown to its former state.” Moshe had said “the great, the mighty, and the awesome” (Devarim 10:17); Yirmeyah, seeing gentiles rampaging in the Sanctuary, omitted “awesome”; Daniel, seeing gentiles enslaving His children, omitted “mighty.” But they [the Great Assembly] said: on the contrary — this is His might, that He subdues His inclination and shows patience to the wicked; and these are His awesome deeds, for were it not for the awe of Him, how could one nation survive among the nations? דְּבִכְבִישַׁת הַיֵּצֶר לֹא אִשְׁתְּכַח בֵּיעֲתָא בַּת יוֹמָא וְנִמְנַע הַהוֹלָדָה
for they said [in Yoma 69b] that when [the Men of the Great Assembly] “imprisoned” the inclination [of arayos], not even a day-old egg could be found, and procreation ceased.
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא בִּקְדֻשָּׁה אֵין קְדֻשָּׁה לְמַעְלָה מִמֶּנּוּ וְנִקְרָא ״טוֹב מְאוֹד״
Nonetheless, when it is [channeled] in holiness, there is no holiness higher than it, and it is called “very good”;
דְּ״לֹא תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ״, וְרָצָה שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִבְרָאִין הַמַּכִּירִין כֹּחַ מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ

for “He did not create it a wasteland” (Yeshayahu 45:18)510Yeshayahu 45:18: “כִּי כֹה אָמַר ה׳ בּוֹרֵא הַשָּׁמַיִם… לֹא תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ, לָשֶׁבֶת יְצָרָהּ” — “He did not create it [the world] a tohu (wasteland); He formed it to be inhabited.” The Sages derive from “la-sheves yetzarah” the worth of settling and populating the world — the ground of the mitzvah of procreation (cf. Gittin 41b). R’ Tzadok’s use: desire, when channeled in holiness (as Leah’s yearning to raise up tribes), is “very good,” for “He did not create it a wasteland” — “He desired that there be creatures who recognize the power of His kingship.” — He desired that there be creatures who recognize the power of His kingship.
וְהִיא לֹא רָצְתָה לְהַעֲמִיד תּוֹלָדוֹת רַק מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע״ה, שֶׁיָּדְעָה דְּכוּלּוֹ זֶרַע אֱמֶת
And she wished to raise up offspring only from Yaakov Avinu, for she knew that he was wholly “seed of truth”;
וּמִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִרְאֶה זֶה חִסָּרוֹן בְּעֵינַיִן, וּבֶאֱמֶת זֶה הָיָה עִיקַּר הַמַּעֲלָה
and from the side of this world this appeared as a “flaw of the eyes,” but in truth it was her essential greatness.
וּלְכָךְ רְאוּבֵן הוּא ״רֵאשִׁית אוֹנִי״ דְּיַעֲקֹב

And therefore Reuven is Yaakov’s “first of my strength” (Bereishis 49:3)511Bereishis 49:3: “רְאוּבֵן בְּכֹרִי אַתָּה, כֹּחִי וְרֵאשִׁית אוֹנִי, יֶתֶר שְׂאֵת וְיֶתֶר עָז” — “Reuven, you are my firstborn, my strength and the first of my vigor…” Rashi: “reishis oni” is Yaakov’s very first drop. R’ Tzadok’s use: Reuven, as bechor, is “the first of my strength” in whom “all those born after him are included” — the root comprising all the “true” levels of Yaakov as they spread into this world (which is also why one is obligated to honor an older brother).;
וְיָדוּעַ דְּמַעֲלַת הַבְּכוֹר דְּבוֹ נִכְלָל כָּל הַנּוֹלָדִים אַחֲרָיו
and it is known that the virtue of the firstborn is that all those born after him are included within him —
דְּזֶהוּ טַעַם חִיּוּב כִּיבּוּד אָחִיו הַגָּדוֹל כַּנּוֹדָע מִטַּעַם הָאֲרִ״י ז״ל

which is the reason for the obligation to honor one’s older brother512Kesuvos 103a (and the Arizal): the obligation to honor one’s older brother is derived from “אֶת אָבִיךָ” (Shemos 20:12) — “the word ‘es’ comes to include your older brother” (Kesuvos 103a; Rambam, Hilchos Mamrim 6:15). The Arizal gives the mystical ground: the souls of the later children are “included” within the firstborn, who is their root — so honoring him is honoring the root that contains them. R’ Tzadok’s use: “the virtue of the firstborn is that all born after him are included within him” — Reuven the bechor comprising all the levels of Yaakov.Shem MiShmuel and Sefat Emet parallel - Shem MiShmuel, Vayetzei 9:15; Sefat Emet, Vayechi 22:3: The Rachel-Leah polarity here is illuminated by Shem MiShmuel's formulation that Rachel corresponds to alma d'isgalya while Leah corresponds to alma d'iskasya. The revealed world displays beauty, deed, and ordered attainment; the hidden world contains heights whose value is not immediately visible and is reached through inward separation from evil. This helps explain why Yaakov's attachment to Rachel belongs to the structure of this world while Leah becomes his enduring partner at the root. Sefat Emet adds that "Yaakov Avinu did not die" means that Yaakov deposited his whole power within the collective of Israel, which can awaken it in every generation. R. Tzadok's point is thus not simply biographical - that Yaakov happened to be buried with Leah. At the level of eternal Israel, Yaakov's abiding force is joined to the hidden world from which teshuvah and inner renewal emerge. Rachel represents visible perfection; Leah represents the concealed source that can regenerate life after visible perfection has failed., as is known from the teaching of the Arizal.
וְזֶהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ כְּלַל כָּל מַדְרֵיגוֹת הָאֲמִיתּוֹת לְיַעֲקֹב הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא
And this [inclusive firstborn-ness] is the root comprising all the “true” levels of Yaakov as they spread into this world, which is “the world of falsehood.”
וְעִיקַּר שִׁקְרוּת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא מַה שֶּׁכָּל הֲנָאוֹתָיו הוּא רַק כְּרֶגַע, כְּמִדַּת ״לְשׁוֹן שֶׁקֶר״
And the essential falseness of this world is that all its pleasures last but a moment, like the nature of “a lying tongue,”
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן ״שְׂפַת אֱמֶת״ מָה הוּא ״תִּכּוֹן לָעַד״

whereas “the lip of truth — is established forever” (Mishlei 12:19) — the fleetingness of this world’s pleasures being the very mark of their falseness, set against the enduring truth that Yaakov embodies.

items.h: The theme: Worldly desire is “the bread of falsehood” — fleeting; but Israel’s “seed of truth” endures forever, and even the “drops” that bore no child are not wasted. Reuven’s “impetuousness” (David’s “eating the unripe fig”) is, once clarified, a zealous haste toward a mitzvah — like the daughters of Lot, from whose one good “perida” royalty issued. Every desire within Israel’s seed is, at root, “seed of truth.”

p: [יג] וְכָל הַתַּאֲוֹת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִקְרָא עָרֵב לְאִישׁ ״לֶחֶם שֶׁקֶר״ וְגוֹמֵר מֵהַאי טַעְמָא

And all the desires of this world are [the subject of] “sweet to a man is the bread of falsehood,” etc. (Mishlei 20:17)513Mishlei 20:17: “עָרֵב לָאִישׁ לֶחֶם שָׁקֶר, וְאַחַר יִמָּלֵא פִיהוּ חָצָץ” — “Sweet to a man is the bread of falsehood, but afterward his mouth is filled with gravel.” Rashi / Metzudos: illicit or false gain is sweet at first taste but ends in bitterness (gravel). R’ Tzadok’s use: all the desires of “this world” are “lechem sheker” — their pleasure lasts only a moment and then turns to gravel; this is the mark of alma d’shikra, over against the enduring “seed of truth” of Israel. — for this [very] reason [that their pleasure is momentary];
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶאֱמַר ״וּמִסְפָּר אֶת רֹבַע יִשְׂרָאֵל״ כִּי הֵם קַיָּימִים לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד
whereas of the Children of Israel it says, “and the number of the rova [seed] of Israel” (Bamidbar 23:10), for they endure for all eternity.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר [מוּבָא בְּחַסְדֵּי אָבוֹת לְהָרַב חִיד״א] עַל פָּסוּק ״אֵלֶּה מִי יָלַד״

And as they said in the Zohar [cited in the Chida’s Chasdei Avos]514Chasdei Avos is the commentary on Pirkei Avos by the Chida — R’ Chaim Yosef David Azulai (1724–1806). R’ Tzadok cites in its name a teaching of the Zohar on the verse “these — who bore them?” (Yeshayahu 49:21): that even the “drops” from which no child was brought into actual being are not for naught, and that offspring will yet issue from them in the time to come. on the verse “these — who bore [them]?” (Yeshayahu 49:21),
דְּגַם מִכָּל טִיפִּין שֶׁאֵין בְּפֹעַל נוֹלָד אֵינָם לְבַטָּלָה, וְיִהְיוּ מֵהֶם תּוֹלָדוֹת לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא
that even from all the “drops” from which no child is actually born, none are for naught — there will yet be offspring from them in the Future to Come.
וְזֶה מִדַּת הָאֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב שֶׁאֵינוֹ ״לֶחֶם שֶׁקֶר״

And this is the trait of “truth to Yaakov,” which is not “bread of falsehood”;515R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §60): “‘sweet to a man is bread of falsehood’ — but its reverse is truth, the rung of Yaakov, and it is what brings life, as in Perek Chelek: ‘from the place whose name is truth.’” This is §6-13’s measure exactly — worldly desire is “bread of falsehood,” fleeting; but “the trait of truth to Yaakov” is no bread of falsehood, for it is drawn “from the place whose name is truth,” and so it endures and gives life, while the seed of Israel “endures for all eternity.”
אֶלָּא שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין בֵּירוּר גָּמוּר בָּזֶה אֲפִילּוּ לֶחָסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים
except that in this world there is no complete “clarification” of this, even for the most pious of the pious,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל (ויק״ר יד, ה) עַל פָּסוּק ״בְּעָווֹן״ מָלֵא

as the Sages said (Vayikra Rabbah 14:5)516Vayikra Rabbah 14:5: “R’ Acha said: Even one who is the most pious of the pious, it is impossible that he not have one ‘side’ of iniquity” — on the verse (Tehillim 51:7), “behold, in iniquity was I fashioned.” on the verse “in iniquity [was I fashioned]” — [even the greatest is] “full” [of some trace].
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן הַפְּחוּתִים עַד סוֹף כָּל הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת מִזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב
And all the more so the lowly, down to the very end of all the levels, of Yaakov’s seed —
דְּכוּלָּם ״לֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח״ דִּלְעוֹלָם
for of all of them, “no outcast shall be cast away from Him” (Shmuel II 14:14), ever;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא, וּבְשׇׁרְשׁוֹ דָּבוּק בֶּאֱמֶת

“even though he has sinned, he is [still] a Yisrael” (Sanhedrin 44a)517Sanhedrin 44a: On “Israel has sinned” (Yehoshua 7:11): “Even though [the people] have sinned, they are [still] ‘Israel’ [Yisrael af al pi she-chata, Yisrael hu].”, and in his root he cleaves to truth.
וְזֶה ״רֵאשִׁית אוֹנוֹ״ דְּיַעֲקֹב, הִתְגַּלּוּת הַקְּדֻשָּׁה דְּעַיִן רוֹאָה שֶׁמֵּחֲמָתוֹ הַלֵּב חוֹמֵד
And this is Yaakov’s “first of his strength” [Reuven]: the revelation of the holiness of the “seeing eye,” from which the heart covets —
דְּגַם זֶה כּוּלּוֹ זֶרַע אֱמֶת

that this too is entirely “seed of truth.”518R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §58): “This is the attribute of the truth of Yaakov, of whom all are ‘seed of truth’ — for this is [precisely] the trait of truth: that it is wholly so, ‘reaching from end to end,’ with nothing in it ‘from without,’ for ‘the lip of truth is established forever’ (Mishlei 12:19). And this [enduring truth] is what Yaakov, of blessed memory, established — the full ‘stature’ of the Assembly of Israel, all of them ‘seed of truth.’”
וּמַה שֶּׁנִּגְלָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לֹא כֵן, הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַמְּהִירוּת
And what is revealed in this world as “not so” is only from the side of “haste,”
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא (סנהדרין קז.) בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה ״אָכְלָה פַּגָּה״

along the lines of what is brought (Sanhedrin 107a)519Sanhedrin 107a: “Bathsheva daughter of Eliam was fitting for David from the six days of creation — only that she came to him through pain [b’machov, before her time].” (As Rashi renders it, “he ate the fig unripe” — he took prematurely what was destined to be his; hence Reuven’s “impetuous as water.”) regarding David HaMelech, that “he ate the unripe fig [before its time]” —
וְזֶהוּ ״פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם״ [וּמַיִם מוֹרֶה תַּאֲוָה כַּנּוֹדָע]

and this is [Reuven’s] “impetuous as water” (Bereishis 49:4)520Bereishis 49:4: “פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם אַל תּוֹתַר, כִּי עָלִיתָ מִשְׁכְּבֵי אָבִיךָ…” — “Impetuous as water, you shall not have superiority, for you ascended your father’s bed…” — Yaakov’s words to Reuven. Rashi: “pachaz ka-mayim” — the haste and impetuosity with which you acted. R’ Tzadok’s use (with the known reading that “water denotes desire”): Reuven’s “impetuousness” is only the outward “haste”; once it is clarified that all was “a matter of mitzvah,” the same haste becomes zeal toward a mitzvah — “zealous and rewarded.” [and “water” denotes desire, as is known].
וּלְכְשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה וְיִתְבָּרֵר דְּהַכֹּל דְּבַר מִצְוָה, הֲרֵי זֶה מְהִירוּת לְמִצְוָה, וְ״זָרִיז וְנִשְׂכָּר״ קָרֵינָא לֵיהּ
But when it is [ultimately] revealed and clarified that all is a matter of mitzvah, then this “haste” is a haste toward a mitzvah, and we call him “zealous and rewarded”;
דְּאֵין לְךָ גָּרוּעַ מִבְּנוֹת לוֹט
for you have nothing more degraded than the daughters of Lot,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ ז״ל (נזיר כג.) מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקָּדְמָה לְמִצְוָה קָדְמַתָּה אַרְבָּעָה דוֹרוֹת לַמַּלְכוּת

and yet the Sages said (Nazir 23a) that because521Nazir 23a–b (on the daughters of Lot, Bereishis 19:30–38): “a person should always hasten to a matter of mitzvah, for on account of the one night by which the elder [daughter] preceded the younger, she preceded her by four generations to royalty.” The elder bore Moav (ancestress of Rus → David), and so “preceded” the younger — whose line (via Ammon → Naamah) reached royalty only later, through Rechavam. R’ Tzadok’s use: “you have nothing more degraded than the daughters of Lot,” yet because the elder “preceded in the mitzvah” of perpetuating the world, royalty issued from her — the “hidden holiness” of a seemingly base act, clarified only afterward. [the elder daughter] “preceded [the younger] in the mitzvah,” she preceded her by four generations to royalty [the Davidic line came from her].522R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §33): “and of Lot it says ‘who went with Avram’ — meaning [he too was] in [Avraham’s] trait, but he is the dross and evil within it; ‘separate from me’ — go to your lot, to the evil and the dross, and I will go my way in the name of the living God.” This is the ground of §6-13’s daughters of Lot: Lot carries Avraham’s very trait, only debased to “dross” — so that within that most-degraded line lies a good root, one holy “perida,” which, once separated from its impure source, issues as the royalty of David.
וְהַיְינוּ אַחַר שֶׁיָּצָא הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ הַטּוֹב שֶׁהָיָה וְנִקְלַט בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְנִתְגַּלָּה הַקְּדֻשָּׁה הַגְּנוּזָה בְּדָבָר זֶה
That is, [only] after the good root that was [latent within it] emerged and was absorbed into Israel, and the hidden holiness in this matter was revealed —
מִצַּד הַקְּדֻשָּׁה נִקְרָא קְדִימָה לְמִצְוָה
from the side of [that] holiness it is called “precedence in the mitzvah,”
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשָּׁם רוּבּוֹ כְּכוּלּוֹ מַמָּשׁ הָיָה כָּלוּל בְּמַחְשָׁבוֹת רָעוֹת
even though there [in the act itself] the greater part — virtually all of it — was bound up in evil thoughts,
שֶׁהֲרֵי לֹא נִבְחַר מִכָּל אַחַת מֵהֶם אֶלָּא פְּרִידָה אַחַת טוֹבָה
for from each of them only one good “perida” was selected.
וְנִקְרָא ״פְּרִידָה״ (בב״ק לח:) לְשׁוֹן יוֹנָה וּלְשׁוֹן פֶּרֶד, דְּהָא וְהָא אִיתֵיהּ

And it is called “perida” (Bava Kama 38b)523Bava Kama 38b: the Holy One restrained Israel from warring with Moav and Ammon, saying, “two good peridos I have to bring forth from them — Rus the Moabite and Naamah the Ammonite.” A “perida” is a precious offshoot. R’ Tzadok expounds the word doubly — from yonah (dove) and from pered (mule): Knesses Yisrael is likened to a dove, while the “other god,” barren like a mule, “does not reproduce”; the single good “perida” (Rus / Naamah) had to be separated from its impure root before the royalty of Israel could issue from it. — a term [connoting both] a “dove” (yonah) and a “mule” (pered) — for both are present in it:
כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְיוֹנָה אַמְתִּילָא
Knesses Yisrael is likened to a dove,
וְאֵל אַחֵר דְּאִסְתְּרִיס נִמְשָׁל לְפֶרֶד שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹלִיד
while the “other god,” which is “castrated,” is likened to a mule that does not reproduce,
וּמוֹרֶה עַל זִימָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כְּסוּס כְּפֶרֶד״ וְגוֹמֵר

and denotes lewdness, as it says, “like a horse, like a mule” (Tehillim 32:9)524Tehillim 32:9: “אַל תִּהְיוּ כְּסוּס כְּפֶרֶד אֵין הָבִין, בְּמֶתֶג וָרֶסֶן עֶדְיוֹ לִבְלוֹם” — “Be not like a horse or a mule, without understanding, whose adornment must be curbed with bit and bridle.” Meforshim: do not let yourself be governed like a brute beast. R’ Tzadok’s use: the pered (mule) — a sterile kilayim of “horse and donkey” — is the emblem of the “other god” that “does not reproduce” and “denotes lewdness”; hence “k’sus k’fered,” over against the fruitful “dove” of Knesses Yisrael.,
וְהוּא מַמְזֵר וְכִלְאַיִם ״סוּס וַחֲמוֹר״
and it [the mule] is a “mamzer” and a kilayim [crossbreed] of “horse and donkey.”
וְכֵן הֵם מִצַּד שָׁרְשָׁם כֵּן
And so are they [the nations], from the side of their root;
רַק אַחַר שֶׁנִּפְרְדָה מִשָּׁרְשָׁהּ, דְּ״גֵר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר כְּקָטָן שֶׁנּוֹלַד״

but once [that good “perida”] separated from its [impure] root — for “a convert who converts is like a newborn child” (Yevamos 22a)525Yevamos 22a: “A convert who converts is like a newborn child [ger she-nisgayer k’katan she-nolad].” (Severed from his former, impure root.)Sefat Emet parallel - Vayera 30:3: Sefat Emet's explanation of "zera emes" strongly complements the discussion of enduring seed and the bris. He writes that the souls of Israel extend "from beginning to end," and that truth requires the body itself to become a fitting vessel for the light of the neshamah. Bris milah removes the "sefas sheker," the false covering introduced through sin, so that the child is born as "zera emes." Emes, in this account, is continuity: the Divine root, the embodied middle, and the final destiny must belong to one unbroken line. This gives depth to R. Tzadok's contrast between transient desire - "the bread of falsehood" - and Israel's seed of truth. Taavah seeks an immediate experience cut off from enduring purpose; bris gathers the power of desire into a line that reaches beyond the moment and bears fruit. Even where there has been failure, the root of Israel remains oriented toward that continuity, which is why teshuvah can reclaim what appeared wasted and return it to the line of emes. —
יָצָא מֵהֶם מַלְכוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנִמְשָׁל לְיוֹנָה
there issued from them the royalty of Israel — the root of Knesses Yisrael, likened to a dove —
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק] בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה בְּעוֹבָדָא דְּשַׁבִּי
as they said [in Perek Chelek] regarding David HaMelech, in the incident of the captive.
וְקַל וָחוֹמֶר בֶּן בְּנוֹ שֶׁל קַל וָחוֹמֶר לְכָל הַתַּאֲוֹת שֶׁבְּזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלָּם, שֶׁהֵם כּוּלָּם זֶרַע אֱמֶת

and [this is] a kal va-chomer of a kal va-chomer concerning all the “desires” within the seed of Israel — for they are all “seed of truth.” — so that no craving within a Jew is intrinsically foreign; each is a holy “drop” awaiting its clarification.

items.h: The theme: Reuven’s blessing “yechi ve-al yamus” — deathlessness, since death flows from desire; the teshuvah-rung of Leah transforms (not merely subdues) and completes the “seeing.” Shimon = the reception of “hearing” (reproof); Levi = “this time my husband will be joined.” The order of the soul’s perfections: first the eye, then the ear. Yehudah = the “voice of prayer” (David’s rung).

p: [יד] וְעַל כֵּן בִּרְכַּת רְאוּבֵן ״יְחִי וְאַל יָמֹת״

And therefore the blessing of Reuven is “Let him live and not die” (Devarim 33:6)526Devarim 33:6: “יְחִי רְאוּבֵן וְאַל יָמֹת, וִיהִי מְתָיו מִסְפָּר” — “Let Reuven live and not die, and let his men be counted” — Moshe’s blessing to Reuven. Rashi: “let him live in this world and not die in the World to Come” — that the episode of Bilhah not be remembered against him. R’ Tzadok’s use: since “death is drawn from desire” (“the counsel of the serpent”), the perfection of Reuven’s rung — the rung of teshuvah, which transforms desire — is exactly what brings “chayei ad” (eternal life): “and let him not die.”,
שֶׁהַמִּיתָה נִמְשָׁךְ מֵהַתַּאֲוָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל דְּזֶהוּ עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ
for death is drawn from desire, as I wrote above — this being “the counsel of the serpent”;
אֲבָל שְׁלֵימוּת הַבְּרָכָה בְּדַרְגָּא דִּרְאוּבֵן הִיא הַמְּבִיאָה ״חַיֵּי עַד״
but the perfection of the blessing, at the rung of Reuven, is what brings “eternal life.”
וְסִיֵּים ״וְאַל יָמֹת״, דְּבֶאֱמֶת הֲרֵי יֵשׁ ״חַיֵּי עוֹלָם נָטוּעַ״ בְּכָל זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל
And [Moshe] concluded “and let him not die,” for in truth there is “eternal life implanted” within all the seed of Israel,
וְהַמִּיתָה רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְבַד
and death is [only] in this world alone.
וּכְמוֹ דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע״ה ״לֹא מֵת״, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת מִיתָה וּקְבוּרָה
Just as Yaakov Avinu “did not die,” yet there was, in the revealed [realm], a “death” and burial;
אֲבָל מִצַּד הַבְּרָכָה הוּא הַבֵּירוּר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן דְּלֹא יָמוּת כְּלָל כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בִּימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ

but from the side of the blessing [comes] the clarification, in this world too, that he shall not die at all, as will be in the days of Mashiach.527R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §38): "“these are the names of the sons” — the name that father and mother called them; “these are the names of the anointed priests” — the name that others called him." Exactly the se’if: a man bears more than one name, and the rung of “let him live and not die” belongs to the name given at his root — not to the one the world assigns him.
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הִתְגַּלּוּת רֵאשִׁית אוֹנוֹ דְּיַעֲקֹב, שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הָאֱמֶת דְּתִכּוֹן לָעַד
And this is from the revelation of Yaakov’s “first of his strength,” the root of truth that “is established forever”;
וְאֵין שָׁם מִיתָה וּבִטּוּל כְּלָל, דְּאִם כֵּן אֵינוֹ לָעַד
and there is there no death or nullity at all — for [otherwise] it would not be “forever.”
וְהַהִתְגַּלּוּת זֶה רַק עַל יְדֵי דַּרְגָּא דְּלֵאָה, דְּהַיְינוּ לְאַהְפְּכָא וְלֹא לְאַכְפְּיָא

And this revelation [comes] only through the rung of Leah — that is, “to transform528Zohar (I 4a; a theme developed widely): the highest service is “l’ithapcha chashocha li-nehora” — “to transform darkness into light” — over against the lower “l’ithkafya,” merely to subdue the darkness. R’ Tzadok’s use: the revelation of deathless “eternal life” comes “only through the rung of Leah — that is, l’ahapcha (to transform), not [merely] l’achpaya (to subdue)” — a teshuvah that turns the evil itself into good, thereby completing the rectification of “seeing.”529R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas Shabbos §5): “to gather in all the sparks and l’ahpacha — to turn everything to ‘very good’; and R’ Meir, whose anonymous Mishnah follows him, the root of the Oral Torah, merited this light — the light within the darkness.” This is §6-14’s “the rung of Leah — to transform, not [merely] to subdue”: the baal-teshuvah power that does not conquer the darkness but turns it to light, “very good,” so that the “seeing” is completed — the coveting eye itself becoming a vessel of the light within.” [evil into good], not [merely] “to subdue”;
וּמִזֶּה נִשְׁלַם הָרְאִיָּה שֶׁהוּא מֵעִנְיָינִים שֶׁחוּץ לַגּוּף
and through this the [rectification of] “seeing” is completed, [seeing] being of matters external to the body.
וַעֲדַיִין קָרְאָה שִׁמְעוֹן ״כִּי שָׁמַע ה׳ כִּי שְׂנוּאָה אָנֹכִי״, עֲדַיִין לֹא נִתְבָּרֵר בִּפְנִימִיּוּת

And still she named [her next son] Shimon, “for Hashem has heard that I am hated” (Bereishis 29:33)530Bereishis 29:33: “וַתַּהַר עוֹד וַתֵּלֶד בֵּן, וַתֹּאמֶר כִּי שָׁמַע ה׳ כִּי שְׂנוּאָה אָנֹכִי, וַיִּתֶּן לִי גַּם אֶת זֶה, וַתִּקְרָא שְׁמוֹ שִׁמְעוֹן” — “‘for Hashem has heard that I am hated’… and she called his name Shimon.” R’ Tzadok’s use: Shimon is named for shmiah (hearing) — “the reception of the external thing into the body”; and the fact that Leah still spoke of herself as “hated” shows that “it had not yet been clarified inwardly” — the hearing (Shimon) must still complete the seeing (Reuven). — [showing] it had not yet been clarified inwardly.
דְּיָדוּעַ דְּהָרְאִיָּה הוּא הַשָּׂגַת הָאָדָם בְּדָבָר שֶׁחוּצָה לוֹ, וְהַשְּׁמִיעָה הוּא קַבָּלַת הַדָּבָר שֶׁחוּצָה לוֹ לְגוּפוֹ
For it is known that “seeing” is a person’s apprehension of a thing outside himself, while “hearing” is the reception of the external thing into his body;
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא כְּקַנְקַל לַגּוּף, דְּכָל הַגּוּף מְקַבֵּל חַיִּים עַל יָדוֹ, וְעַל יָדוֹ הוּא הַכְּנִיסָה לַגּוּף
and therefore [the ear] is “like a conduit for the body,” for the whole body receives life through it, and through it is the “entry” into the body.
וְכֵן הֵם סֵדֶר הַתְחָלַת הַשְּׁלֵימוּיוֹת
And such is the order of the beginning of the perfections:
בַּתְּחִלָּה בָּרְאִיָּה, לִהְיוֹת כָּל מַה שֶּׁרוֹאֶה מֵעִנְיָינֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַכֹּל הִסְתַּכְּלוּתוֹ וּרְאִיָּיתוֹ הוּא רַק לְכֹחַ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַגָּנוּז בְּגַוַּום
first in “seeing” — that all he sees of the matters of this world, his whole looking and seeing is [directed] only to the power of Hashem hidden within them,
דְּ״אַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כּוּלָּם״

for “You give life to them all” (Nechemiah 9:6)531Nechemiah 9:6: “אַתָּה הוּא ה׳ לְבַדֶּךָ, אַתָּה עָשִׂיתָ אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם… וְאַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם” — “You alone are Hashem; You made the heavens… and You give life to them all.” From the Levites’ great confession-prayer. R’ Tzadok’s use: the rectified “seeing” is that all one beholds of this world is directed “only to the power of Hashem hidden within” each thing — “Atah mechayeh es kulam” — so that whatever the body then receives, it receives from the Source of all life, and is thereby itself sanctified.532R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §262): “for in truth he did not die — it appears that he was genuinely wholly clean all his days; and this is impossible except through words of Torah, which cause him to vomit up his mother’s milk, even the pleasure of childhood.” Exactly the se’if: deathlessness is not an exemption granted from outside but the effect of a life wholly held by Torah — the hidden Life “established forever” in the one who lives by it..
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִמֵּילָא כָּל מַה שֶּׁהוּא מְקַבֵּל מֵהָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְגוּפוֹ הוּא מְקַבֵּל מִמְּקוֹר חִיּוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמְחַיֶּה אוֹתָם
And through this, of itself, whatever he receives from this world into his body he receives from the Source of vitality that gives them life;
וּמִמֵּילָא גַּם גּוּפוֹ מִתְקַדֵּשׁ עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּכָל כֹּחוֹתָיו הַפְּנִימִיִּים
and of itself his body too is thereby sanctified, in all its inner powers.
וְאָז מִסְתַּלֵּק הַשִּׂנְאָה דִּלְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן גַּם כֵּן, וְגוֹרֵם הַדְּבֵיקוּת הַגָּמוּר דְּ״הַפַּעַם יִלָּוֶה אִישִׁי״
And then the “hatred” of the eye’s-view also departs, and it brings about the complete cleaving of “this time my husband will be joined to me” (Bereishis 29:34, at Levi’s birth),
שֶׁכְּבָר נַעֲשָׂה כָּל גּוּפוֹ מְרוּבֶּה וּמִשְׁכָּן לִכְבוֹד שָׁמַיִם
for by then his whole body has become “increased” and a dwelling for the honor of Heaven;
וְזֶהוּ כָּל חֶלְקָהּ שֶׁל לֵאָה בַּבָּנִים
and this is Leah’s entire “portion” in the [first three] sons.
אַךְ חֵלֶק זֶה אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד דַּרְגָּא דְּאַכְפְּיָא, לִהְיוֹת צַדִּיק בְּכָל דְּרָכָיו

But this portion can be attained also from the side of the rung of “subduing” — to be “a tzaddik in all his ways”533Tehillim 145:17: “צַדִּיק ה׳ בְּכָל דְּרָכָיו, וְחָסִיד בְּכָל מַעֲשָׂיו” — “Hashem is righteous in all His ways, and kind in all His deeds” (from Ashrei). The phrase “tzaddik b’chol drachav” is the byword for the tzaddik gamur, righteous in every path. R’ Tzadok’s use: the “portion in the [first three] sons” can be reached even by the rung of subduing (achpaya) — “to be a tzaddik in all his ways,” the portion that reaches Rachel too; but the rung of teshuvah (Leah) adds an “addition” beyond it.;
הוּא חֵלֶק הַמַּגִּיעַ לְרָחֵל גַּם כֵּן
this is a portion that reaches Rachel as well,
אֲבָל עַל יְדֵי דַּרְגָּא דִּתְשׁוּבָה יֵשׁ הוֹסָפָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
but through the rung of teshuvah there is an “addition,” as mentioned above.
וּבִיהוּדָה הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת דַּרְגָּא דִּתְשׁוּבָה, וּבִרְכָתוֹ הוּא ״שְׁמַע ה׳ קוֹל יְהוּדָה״

And in Yehudah is the revelation of the rung of teshuvah, and his blessing is “Hear, Hashem, the voice of Yehudah” (Devarim 33:7)534Devarim 33:7: “וְזֹאת לִיהוּדָה… שְׁמַע ה׳ קוֹל יְהוּדָה, וְאֶל עַמּוֹ תְּבִיאֶנּוּ” — “‘Hear, Hashem, the voice of Yehudah’…” — Moshe’s blessing to Yehudah. Rashi: [hear] the prayers of the kings of Yehudah’s line — David and his descendants — as they go out to battle. R’ Tzadok’s use: Yehudah’s whole rung is the attainment of the “voice” — but with him it is the “kol tefillah” (the voice of prayer), the rung of David, as distinct from the primary “kol Yaakov,” which is the voice of Torah.;
דְּכָל מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ בְּהַשָּׂגַת הַקּוֹל ״קוֹל יַעֲקֹב״

for his whole level is in the attainment of the “voice” — “the voice of Yaakov”535Bereishis 27:22: “הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב וְהַיָּדַיִם יְדֵי עֵשָׂו” — “the voice is the voice of Yaakov, but the hands are the hands of Esav.” Bereishis Rabbah 65:20 (cf. Gittin 57b): “kol Yaakov” is the voice [of Torah and prayer] in the synagogues and study-halls — when it is heard, “the hands of Esav” have no power. R’ Tzadok’s use: “the voice of Yaakov” is essentially the voice of Torah; Yehudah’s (David’s) “voice” is its counterpart in prayer — “prayer being the mode by which the fallen self reaches upward, as Torah is the mode by which the Divine reaches down.”Sefat Emet and Chiddushei HaRim parallel - Sefat Emet, Vayeshev 33:4; Chiddushei HaRim on Torah, Chayei Sara 1: Two Ger sources bring out the life-giving character of Reuven's teshuvah. Sefat Emet says that Reuven "opened teshuvah" and thereby became the model from whom Hoshea could proclaim "Shuvah Yisrael." The complete baal teshuvah feels that sin has left him with no independent "place," and it is precisely then that Hashem grants him a new place. Chiddushei HaRim adds that teshuvah can repair past days "in one hour and one moment" as though they had been filled with mitzvos. This combination closely fits the blessing "yechi Reuven ve-al yamus" as R. Tzadok reads it. Reuven's life is not guaranteed because no breakdown occurred; rather, his distinct contribution to Israel is that breakdown need not become death. Teshuvah can supply a new place from which life begins again and can even restore life to the days that seemed already forfeited. —
רַק שֶׁאֶצְלוֹ הוּא הַקּוֹל דִּתְפִלָּה דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן קוֹל יַעֲקֹב הוּא קוֹל דְּתוֹרָה

except that with him it is the “voice of prayer,” the rung of David, whereas the [primary] “voice of Yaakov” is the voice of Torah. — prayer being the mode by which the fallen self reaches upward, as Torah is the mode by which the Divine reaches down.

items.h: The theme: The perfection of Torah, too, is in Leah’s seed (Levi and Yissachar). Chochmah is the wisdom revealed into the world (“ripened fruit of the supernal Wisdom”); Binah is the wisdom hidden in the heart — Yissachar’s “understanding of the times.” The written Torah is fixed and unchanging, but in the depths of the heart there is sometimes “a time to act for Hashem” — the domain of hafla’ah (the nazir), grasped through the Binah of the heart.

p: [טו] וּשְׁלֵימוּת הַתּוֹרָה גַּם כֵּן אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּזַרְעָא דְּלֵאָה
And the perfection of Torah, too, is only in the seed of Leah,
דְּלֵיכָּא צוּרְבָא מֵרַבָּנָן דְּמוֹרֵי אֶלָּא מִלֵּוִי וּמִיִּשָּׂשכָר (יומא כו.)

for “there is no Torah scholar who renders rulings except from [the tribes of] Levi and Yissachar” (Yoma 26a)536Yoma 26a: “Rava said: You will not find a Torah scholar who renders halachic rulings [morei hora’ah] except [from those descended] from [the tribe of] Levi or from [the tribe of] Yissachar.”.537R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §198): “This is [the meaning of] ‘the sons of Yissachar, knowers of understanding [binah] for the times’ — [a knowledge] drawn from the binah that is in the heart, where mercy and love for [one’s fellow] creatures reside. Whereas Chochmah is the love of the Torah [itself] — and this is in Levi in particular, from whom issued Moshe Rabbeinu; and in general the Kohanim and Levi’im are the judges.” (Exactly the division this se’if draws: Levi’s Chochmah is the revealed wisdom of Torah, while Yissachar’s Binah is the wisdom concealed in the heart.)
וְעִיקַּר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הוּא מִלֵּוִי, שֶׁמִּזַּרְעוֹ הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַתּוֹרָה לְפֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם
And the essence of the giving of the Torah is from Levi, for from his seed comes the revelation of the Torah into actuality in the world:
מַתַּן תּוֹרָה עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה, וְהַכֹּהֲנִים בָּהֶם נֶאֱמַר ״יוֹרוּ מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ״ וְגוֹמֵר
the giving of the Torah was through Moshe Rabbeinu [of Levi], and of the Kohanim it says, “they shall teach Your judgments [to Yaakov],” etc. (Devarim 33:10) —
[וְעַיֵּין בְּסֵפֶר יוּחֲסִין דְּגַם בְּדוֹרוֹת תַּנָּאִים וְאָמוֹרָאִים הָיוּ עִיקַּר מְיַיסְּדֵי הַתּוֹרָה כֹּהֲנִים בְּכָל דּוֹר]
[and see the Sefer Yuchsin, that even in the generations of the Tanna’im and Amora’im, the chief founders of the Torah were Kohanim, in every generation].
וְזֶהוּ חָכְמָה הַמִּתְגַּלֵּית בָּעוֹלָם, שֶׁהוּא ״נוֹבְלוֹת חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה״
And this is the Chochmah revealed in the world — “the ripened fruit of the supernal Wisdom.”
אֲבָל הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב כָּל חָכָם, שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְגַלּוֹתָהּ וּלְהוֹצִיאָהּ מִכֹּחַ לְפֹעַל, זֶה נִקְרָא בִּינָה
But the wisdom in the heart of every sage, which he cannot [fully] reveal and bring from potential to actuality — that is called Binah,
שֶׁזָּכוּ לָהּ בְּנֵי יִשָּׂשכָר ״יוֹדְעֵי בִינָה לָעִתִּים לָדַעַת מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה יִשְׂרָאֵל״

which the sons of Yissachar merited: “who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel should do” (Divrei HaYamim I 12:33)538Divrei HaYamim I 12:33: “וּמִבְּנֵי יִשָּׂשכָר יוֹדְעֵי בִינָה לַעִתִּים לָדַעַת מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה יִשְׂרָאֵל, רָאשֵׁיהֶם מָאתַיִם וְכָל אֲחֵיהֶם עַל פִּיהֶם” — “And of the sons of Yissachar, men of understanding for the times, to know what Israel should do; their chiefs were two hundred, and all their brethren [acted] at their word.” R’ Tzadok’s use: Yissachar’s rung is Binah — the wisdom held within the heart that a sage cannot fully draw out into actuality. They “knew what Israel should do” not in order to teach and rule it as fixed law, “but to know by knowledge alone”; and through their knowing, all Israel too knew what to do “according to the times.” —
לֹא לְלַמֵּד וּלְהוֹרוֹת מַה יַּעֲשׂוּ, רַק לָדַעַת בִּידִיעָה לְבַד
not to teach and instruct what to do, but [only] to “know,” by knowledge alone;
וְעַל יְדֵי הַיְדִיעָה שֶׁלָּהֶם יָדְעוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן מַה יַּעֲשׂוּ
and through their “knowing,” the Children of Israel too knew what to do.
כִּי ״לָעִתִּים״ הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁהוּא ״עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת״ וְדָבָר שֶׁל שָׁעָה
For “the times” means that which is “a time to act,” a matter of the moment;
כִּי הַתּוֹרָה הוּא חוּקִּים קְצוּבִים וּגְדֵרִים שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁתַּנֶּה תָּמִיד כָּל יְמֵי עוֹלָם
for the Torah [proper] is fixed statutes and bounds that never change, for all the days of the world.
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת בְּפֹעַל, אֲבָל בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב, דְּהוּא ״עָקֹב״ מִכֹּל, הוּא מִשְׁתַּנֶּה בְּכָל רֶגַע

This [fixity] is from the side of revealed actuality; but in the depths of the heart — which is “the most crooked/deep of all” (Yirmeyah 17:9)539Yirmeyah 17:9: “עָקֹב הַלֵּב מִכֹּל וְאָנֻשׁ הוּא מִי יֵדָעֶנּוּ” — “The heart is the most deep of all, and it is grievously sick — who can know it?” The root akov connotes the tortuous, unfathomable inner recesses. R’ Tzadok’s use: over against the Torah’s fixed outer statutes, “in the depths of the heart — which is ‘the most deep of all’ — it changes at every moment”; it is there, in the heart’s hidden Binah, that the singular “time to act” is discerned. — it changes at every moment,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יֵשׁ לִפְעָמִים ״עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה׳ הֵפֵרוּ״ וְגוֹמֵר

and through this there is sometimes “a time to act for Hashem — they have voided Your Torah” (Tehillim 119:126)540Tehillim 119:126: “עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה׳ הֵפֵרוּ תּוֹרָתֶךָ” — “It is a time to act for Hashem — they have made void Your Torah.” The Sages read the verse in both directions and invoked it to sanction committing the Oral Torah to writing — “a time to act for Hashem” overriding the rule that oral teachings not be set down (Gittin 60a; Temurah 14b; and see Berachos 63a). R’ Tzadok’s use: the Torah proper is “fixed statutes and bounds that never change for all the days of the world,” yet “in the depths of the heart” there is at times an “eis la’asos,” a need of the very moment that does not accord with the Torah’s general rule and is entrusted to the Binah of the heart..
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה פָּרָשַׁת נְדָרִים, וְנִקְרָא ״אִישׁ כִּי יַפְלִיא״

And regarding this the Torah stated the section of vows, and [the nazir] is called “a man who sets himself apart [yafli]” (Bamidbar 6:2)541Bamidbar 6:2: “אִישׁ אוֹ אִשָּׁה כִּי יַפְלִא לִנְדֹּר נֶדֶר נָזִיר לְהַזִּיר לַה׳” — “A man or woman who sets himself apart [ki yafli], to vow a nazirite’s vow, to abstain for Hashem.” The nazir’s vow is framed by the root פ-ל-א (hafla’ah — a wondrous setting-apart); as R’ Tzadok puts it, “nezirus was given only for hafla’ah.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the parashah of vows was entrusted precisely to the one “who knows how to set apart” — to grasp, through the Binah of the heart, the hidden “wonder” of what befits this particular soul at this particular hour, beyond the universal decree of the Torah.;
וְלֹא נִיתְּנָה נְזִירוּת אֶלָּא לְהַפְלָאָה
and nezirus was given only for “hafla’ah” (a wondrous setting-apart),
וְיָדוּעַ דְּהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּחָכְמָה
and it is known that this is the rung of Chochmah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״הִנְנִי יוֹסִיף לְהַפְלִיא״ וְגוֹמֵר ״וְאָבְדָה חָכְמַת״ וְגוֹמֵר

as it says, “Behold, I will yet do wondrously [haflei va-fele] — and the wisdom of its wise men shall perish,” etc. (Yeshayahu 29:14)542Yeshayahu 29:14: “הִנְנִי יוֹסִף לְהַפְלִיא אֶת הָעָם הַזֶּה הַפְלֵא וָפֶלֶא, וְאָבְדָה חָכְמַת חֲכָמָיו וּבִינַת נְבֹנָיו תִּסְתַּתָּר” — “Behold, I will further do wondrously with this people, wondrous upon wonder — and the wisdom of its wise shall perish, and the discernment of its prudent shall hide itself.” Here the same root pele denotes not revelation but withdrawal — wisdom “perishing” and “hiding.” R’ Tzadok’s use: “pele is a term of concealment”; the supernal Chochmah is hidden in this world, and only its “impression” is grasped in the heart’s Binah — the very word that names the nazir’s “wondrous setting-apart” also bespeaks the hiddenness of that wisdom..
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ ״מְסָעֵף פֻּארָה״, ״וּבְכָל תְּבוּאָתָהּ תְּשָׁרֵשׁ״

And this is along the lines of “lops off the bough” (Yeshayahu 10:33)543Yeshayahu 10:33: “הִנֵּה הָאָדוֹן ה׳ צְבָאוֹת מְסָעֵף פֻּארָה בְּמַעֲרָצָה, וְרָמֵי הַקּוֹמָה גְּדוּעִים וְהַגְּבֹהִים יִשְׁפָּלוּ” — “Behold, the Master, Hashem of Hosts, lops off the bough with terrible force; the tall of stature are hewn down and the lofty laid low.” The verb mesa’ef is built on sa’if (a bough), yet here it means to strip the boughs away. R’ Tzadok’s use: paired with Iyov 31:12 to establish that “every root in Lashon HaKodesh denotes a thing and its opposite” — sa’if is both “bough” and “the removal of the bough,” just as le-hafli is both “to set wondrously apart” and “to remove the setting-apart.” and “in all its produce it takes root [teshareish]” (Iyov 31:12)544Iyov 31:12: “כִּי אֵשׁ הִיא עַד אֲבַדּוֹן תֹּאכֵל, וּבְכָל תְּבוּאָתִי תְשָׁרֵשׁ” — “For it is a fire that consumes down to Avaddon, and would uproot all my increase.” Though teshareish is built on shoresh (root), here it means to tear out by the root; R’ Tzadok cites the clause as “וּבְכָל תְּבוּאָתָהּ תְּשָׁרֵשׁ,” applying it to the “bough.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the partner-verse to Yeshayahu 10:33 — shoresh denotes both “to take root” and “to uproot the root,” the self-reversing quality of the holy tongue by which “le-hafli” itself can mean the removal of the hafla’ah. —
דְּרוֹצֶה לוֹמַר הֲסָרַת הַסָּעִיף וְהַשֹּׁרֶשׁ
which [can equally] mean the removal of the bough and of the root;
וְכֵן ״לְהַפְלִיא״ רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר הֲסָרַת הַהַפְלָאָה
and likewise “le-hafli” [can] mean the removal of the “hafla’ah” —
וְכָל שֹׁרֶשׁ בִּלְשׁוֹן הַקּוֹדֶשׁ מוֹרֶה עַל דָּבָר וְהִפְכּוֹ כַּנּוֹדָע

for every root in Lashon HaKodesh denotes a thing and its opposite, as is known.545R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Nasso §6): “And the word pele bears two senses: one, from the term nifla — wondrous and hidden; and also the sense of revelation and explicitness, as in "nezirus is given only through hafla’ah," and "a minor who knows how lehaflos."” The se’if’s very point: hafla’ah is one of those words that in Lashon HaKodesh “denotes a thing and its opposite” — the concealment that is itself the mode of revelation.
וּ״פֶלֶא״ הוּא לְשׁוֹן הֶעְלֵם, כִּי חָכְמָה עֶלְיוֹנָה נֶעֱלֶמֶת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, רַק רְשִׁימוּ שֶׁלָּהּ מוּשָּׂג בַּבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב
And “pele” is a term of concealment, for the supernal Chochmah is hidden in this world — only its “impression” is grasped in the Binah of the heart.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הַלֵּב יוֹדֵעַ ״מָרַת נֶפֶשׁ״, יוּכַל לְהַגְדִּיר גְּדֵרִים לְעַצְמוֹ כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁרָאוּי לוֹ לְאוֹתוֹ נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִי וּלְאוֹתוֹ זְמַן פְּרָטִי

And through this the heart “knows its own bitterness” (Mishlei 14:10)546Mishlei 14:10: “לֵב יוֹדֵעַ מָרַת נַפְשׁוֹ, וּבְשִׂמְחָתוֹ לֹא יִתְעָרַב זָר” — “The heart knows its own bitterness, and in its joy no stranger may share.” Each heart’s inner state is known to it alone. R’ Tzadok’s use: because “the heart knows its own bitterness,” it “can set bounds for itself according to what is fitting for that particular soul and that particular time” — the personal, non-universal measure of Binah, entrusted to the one who can grasp the hidden “wonder according to the times.”, and can set boundaries for itself according to what is fitting for that particular soul and that particular time.547R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §22): “And this is "of the sons of Yissachar, who know understanding for the times, to know what Israel should do" — that they have no fixed matter, but rather gaze at every time with the Binah that is in the heart, to know what the will of Hashem is at that time, what Israel should do.” Exactly the se’if: the written Torah has “rates and bounds that never change,” but Yissachar’s rung reads, out of the heart’s Binah, what this soul and this hour require.Izhbitz-Radzin parallel - Sha'ar HaEmunah VeYesod HaChasidut, Entrance to the Gate of Beit Yaakov 24:3-4: This source is almost a direct commentary on R. Tzadok's Yissachar-Binah structure. Sha'ar HaEmunah cites "u-miBnei Yissachar yodei binah la'itim" and explains that the possessors of Binah know how to "heal the earlier" - to heal time itself. Complete teshuvah returns a person to Binah, a level above the ordinary sequence of time, where past, present, and future are not experienced as mutually sealed compartments. From there, what preceded can be repaired. This complements R. Tzadok's distinction between revealed Chochmah and the wisdom hidden in the heart. Yissachar does not merely know more information; his Binah is a faculty for penetrating the inward meaning of the time and discovering what the present moment asks of Israel. That is why his Torah belongs naturally to Leah, the mother of teshuvah. The heart that understands the time can also reinterpret the past and direct the future.
וְאֵינָם עִנְיָינִים כּוֹלְלִים לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁתִּגְזֹר עֲלֵיהֶם הַתּוֹרָה
These are not universal matters that the Torah decrees upon all Israel;
רַק מְסָרָתַם לְמִי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לְהַפְלִיא וּלְהַשִּׂיג הַפֶּלֶא הַנֶּעְלָם בְּהַרְגָּשַׁת הַבִּינָה לָעִתִּים
rather, [the Torah] entrusted them to the one who knows how to “set apart” and to grasp the hidden “wonder” through the feeling of Binah, “according to the times” —
עַל יְדֵי זֶה מַה שֶּׁרָאוּי בְּאוֹתוֹ עֵת וּבְאוֹתוֹ רֶגַע מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ כְּפִי מִשְׁפָּט הַכּוֹלֵל שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה

[to discern] thereby what is fitting for that time and that very moment, [even] where it does not accord with the general rule of the Torah. — a latitude reserved for the rare soul whose inner Binah can read the singular need of the hour.

items.h: The theme: Da’as joins Chochmah and Binah — ruach ha-kodesh, wisdom that enters the heart beyond the intellect. Torah “from the lips outward” (Doeg) does not endure — even the “good angel” it created made him forget; but Torah absorbed in the heart cannot be forgotten. The needle-point opening is yirah (man’s task); Hashem then opens it “like the Ulam-hall” and pours in longing without limit — the reward of the Future.

p: [טז] וְדָבָר זֶה נִקְרָא דַּעַת, שֶׁהוּא הַמְחַבֵּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה
And this matter is called Da’as, which joins Chochmah and Binah;

וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י [בְּפָרָשַׁת תִּשָּׂא]548Rashi, Shemos 31:3 (Ki Sisa): on Betzalel’s endowment “b’chochmah u-vi-svunah u-v’da’as,” Rashi glosses each faculty: “Chochmah — what a person hears from others and learns; Tevunah — understanding a matter of one’s own mind out of the things learned; Da’as — ruach ha-kodesh.” R’ Tzadok’s use: Da’as, which joins Chochmah and Binah, is precisely this ruach ha-kodesh — an apprehension unattainable by one’s own intellect, “drawn down” into the heart from the supernal Holy One. דְּ״דַעַת״ הוּא רוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ
and Rashi explained [on Parashas Ki Sisa] that “da’as” is ruach ha-kodesh.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּדָבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג כְּלָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מֵעַצְמוֹ, רַק עַל יְדֵי הַמְשָׁכַת רוּחַ מִקּוֹדֶשׁ הָעֶלְיוֹן בְּרָזָא דְּחָכְמְתָא
That is, this cannot be attained at all in this world by oneself, but only through the drawing-down of a spirit from the supernal Holy One, “in the secret of Wisdom.”

וְכַנּוֹדָע בָּרַמְבַּ״ן [בְּבָבָא בַתְרָא יב.]549Bava Basra 12a: R’ Avdimi of Haifa: “from the day the Temple was destroyed, prophecy was taken from the prophets and given to the Sages” — meaning, “though taken from the prophets, from the Sages it was not taken.” Ameimar added: “a sage is greater than a prophet, as it says ‘and a prophet [navi] has a heart of wisdom’ (Tehillim 90:12) — who is compared to whom? the lesser to the greater.” (R’ Tzadok cites this in the name of the Ramban.) דְּרוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ הוּא הַשָּׂגַת חָכְמָה הַבָּאָה בְּלֵב הָאָדָם מַה שֶּׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת שִׂכְלוֹ
As is known from the Ramban [on Bava Basra 12a], that ruach ha-kodesh is an apprehension of wisdom that comes into a person’s heart — something above the grasp of his [ordinary] intellect.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה הִיא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת שֵׂכֶל הָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
That is, the supernal Chochmah is above the grasp of man’s intellect in this world,
וְהַהַשָּׂגָה זוֹ אֵינוֹ בָּא לָאָדָם מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ כְּלָל, רַק מִצַּד הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, וְהַיְינוּ הַהַרְגָּשָׁה, דְּבַלֵּב הוּא כֹּחַ הַהַרְגָּשָׁה

and this apprehension does not come to a person from the side of the mind’s wisdom at all, but from the side of the Binah of the heart — that is, [inner] “feeling,” for in the heart lies the faculty of feeling.
וְכָל חָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁל דּוֹאֵג מֵהַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ, הַיְינוּ דְּלֹא נִכְנַס לַלֵּב וְלֹא פָּעַל הֶרְגֵּשׁ בּוֹ, דְּאָז ״הַמָּאוֹר שֶׁבָּהּ מַחֲזִירוֹ לַמּוּטָב״

And all the wisdom of Doeg was “from the lips outward” — that is, it did not enter his heart nor arouse feeling in him; for [only] then does “the light within [the Torah] restore him to the good” (Yerushalmi Chagigah 1:7)550Yerushalmi Chagigah 1:7: “[Hashem said:] Would that they had forsaken Me but kept My Torah — for the light within it [ha-ma’or she-bah] would have restored them to the good.”.
כִּי חָכְמָה הַנִּגְלֵית אֶפְשָׁר לְכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל לְהַשִּׂיג מִצַּד הַנִּגְלֶה
For the revealed wisdom every Jew can attain, from the revealed side;
אֲבָל עַל זֶה אָמְרוּ [בְּפֶרֶק בַּמֶּה מַדְלִיקִין] ״מוּטָב שֶׁלֹּא הֶעֱלֵיתָ״

but regarding this they said [in Perek Bameh Madlikin, Shabbos 31a–b], “better that you had not brought it up [without the ‘preservative’ of yiras Shamayim]”551Shabbos 31a–b: Even one who has learned Torah and done mitzvos — if “the fear of Hashem is his treasure,” yes; if not, no. A parable: a man told his agent, “bring up a kor of wheat to the loft”; he did. “Did you mix in a kav of chumton [a preservative]?” “No.” “Then it were better you had not brought it up.” Shabbos 88b: “To those who go to the right in it [the Torah] — an elixir of life; to those who go to the left — a poison of death.” Yoma 72b: “‘why is there a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, seeing he has no heart?’ — woe to the enemies of Torah scholars who engage in Torah and have no fear of Heaven — ‘and this is the Torah which Moshe set’ — if he merits, it becomes for him an elixir of life; if not, a poison of death.” —
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּיוֹמָא עב:] דְּ״לַמַּשְׂמְאִילִים בָּהּ״ כו׳
and as they said [in Yoma 72b] concerning “those who go to its ‘left’ [without proper intent],” etc. —
וְאֵין זֶה חָכְמָה בֶּאֱמֶת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״לָמָּה זֶּה מְחִיר בְּיַד כְּסִיל לִקְנוֹת חָכְמָה וְלֶב אָיִן״
and this is not [true] wisdom, as it says, “why is there a price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?” (Mishlei 17:16).
דְּהָעִיקָּר הוּא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ לֵב כְּלִי קִיבּוּל לְהַחָכְמָה, שֶׁהוּא הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב
For the essential thing is that he have a “heart” that is a vessel to receive the wisdom — which is the fear [of Hashem] in the heart;
דְּאָז הוּא ״סַמָּא דְּחַיֵּי״ לַמַּיְימִינִים לִהְיוֹתָהּ חַיֵּי עוֹלָם
for then it is “an elixir of life” for those who “go to its right,” being eternal life.
אֲבָל הַחָכְמָה שֶׁל הַמַּשְׂמְאִילִים אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא ״מְחִיר לִקְנוֹת חָכְמָה״, וְלֹא חָכְמָה בֶּאֱמֶת, כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ קַיָּים לָעַד בּוֹ
but the wisdom of “those who go to its left” is only “a price to acquire wisdom,” not true wisdom, since it does not endure within him forever —
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּדוֹאֵג דְּ״מַלְאָךְ הִשְׁכִּיחוֹ״

as they said of Doeg, that “an angel made him forget.”552R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §234): “As they said (Sanhedrin 106b) of Doeg, ‘all his Torah was from the lips outward’ — meaning that his brain and heart were full of foreign thoughts and musings, through evil speech [lashon hara]. And in truth thought precedes speech; and one who desires and strives to be clean of foreign thoughts, the Holy One helps him as well to be saved from idle words. Only Doeg hated David, who merited ‘the daughter of the King — that is, prayer,’ which was his [David’s] rung.” (Torah “from the lips outward” is Torah that never reaches the heart — the opposite of the Da’as that unites Chochmah and Binah and enters the heart.)
אֲבָל לַמַּיְימִינִים אָמְרוּ בְּהֵיפֶךְ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ [וְהוּבָא בַּתַּשְׁבַּ״ץ קָטָן] דְּ״מַלְאָךְ מַזְכִּירוֹ״ הַכֹּל
But of “those who go to its right” they said, conversely, in the Midrash [cited in the Tashbetz Katan], that “an angel reminds him” of everything.
וּפֵירוּשׁ ״מַלְאָךְ״ הוּא הַנּוֹצָר מֵהַלִּימּוּד, דְּמִכָּל מִצְוָה נוֹצָר מַלְאָךְ

And the meaning of “angel” is [the one] created from the learning, for from every mitzvah an angel is created (Avos 4:11)553Avos 4:11: “R’ Eliezer ben Yaakov says: One who performs one mitzvah acquires for himself one advocate [praklit echad], and one who commits one transgression acquires for himself one accuser.” —
רְצֹה לוֹמַר כֹּחַ רוּחָנִי הַמִּתְקַיֵּים בְּדָבָר זֶה שֶׁהוּא עוֹסֵק בְּתוֹרַת ה׳
that is, a spiritual force that endures through this [engaging] in Hashem’s Torah,
דְּמִדִּבּוּרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא עִיקַּר קִיּוּם הַמַּלְאָכִים
for from words of Torah is the essential sustenance of the angels.
וְאוֹתוֹ מַלְאָךְ עַצְמוֹ הוּא שֶׁהִשְׁכִּיחוֹ, כְּטַעַם ״סַמָּא דְּמוֹתָא״ שֶׁהִיא עַצְמָהּ נַעֲשֵׂית [כָּךְ] מִשּׁוּם דְּפוֹשְׁעִים יִכָּשְׁלוּ בָהּ

And [with Doeg] that very angel is what made him forget — in the sense of “a poison of death,” which [Torah] itself becomes [for such a one], “because transgressors stumble in it” (Hoshea 14:10)554Hoshea 14:10: “מִי חָכָם וְיָבֵן אֵלֶּה נָבוֹן וְיֵדָעֵם, כִּי יְשָׁרִים דַּרְכֵי ה׳, וְצַדִּקִים יֵלְכוּ בָם וּפֹשְׁעִים יִכָּשְׁלוּ בָם” — “for the ways of Hashem are straight; the righteous walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them” (the closing verse of Hoshea). R’ Tzadok’s use: the very same Torah is “an elixir of life” to those who “go to its right” and “a poison of death” to those who “go to its left” — for “transgressors stumble in it”; thus Doeg’s own Torah, never absorbed into the heart, became the instrument of his ruin..
וְאִלְמָלֵא תוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל דּוֹאֵג לֹא הָיָה בָּא לְכָל מַה שֶּׁבָּא נֶגֶד דָּוִד וְנוֹב
For were it not for Doeg’s [own] Torah, he would not have come to all that he came to against David and [the city of] Nov;
דְּהַכֹּל גָּרַם לוֹ מַה שֶּׁהָיָה ״אַבִּיר הָרוֹעִים״ וְרֹאשׁ סַנְהֶדְרִין

for all of it was brought about by his being “mightiest of the shepherds”555Shmuel I 21:8: “וְשָׁם אִישׁ מֵעַבְדֵי שָׁאוּל בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא נֶעְצָר לִפְנֵי ה׳, וּשְׁמוֹ דֹּאֵג הָאֲדֹמִי, אַבִּיר הָרֹעִים אֲשֶׁר לְשָׁאוּל” — “and a man of Shaul’s servants was there that day, detained before Hashem, and his name was Doeg the Edomite, the mightiest of the shepherds that belonged to Shaul.” Doeg was head of the Sanhedrin (Sanhedrin 106b). R’ Tzadok’s use: precisely his greatness — “mightiest of the shepherds” and head of the Sanhedrin — is what made his fall so complete; were it not for his own [misused] Torah, he would never have come to all that he did against David and Nov. and head of the Sanhedrin.
וְעַל כֵּן זֶה עַצְמוֹ הִשְׁכִּיחוֹ, אַף שֶׁהָיָה מַלְאָךְ טוֹב הַנּוֹצָר מִמִּצְוָה — דְּאֵין עֲבֵירָה מְכַבָּה תוֹרָה

Therefore this very [Torah] made him forget — even though it was a “good angel” created from a mitzvah, and “a sin does not extinguish Torah” (Sotah 21a)556Sotah 21a: “R’ Yosef expounded: A transgression extinguishes a mitzvah, but a transgression does not extinguish Torah [aveirah mechabah mitzvah, ve-ein aveirah mechabah Torah].” (Torah’s protection outlasts the sin.) —
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהָיָה מַשְׂמְאִיל בָּהּ, הַטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ גָּרַם לְהַשְׁכִּיחוֹ
nonetheless, because he “went to its left,” the very good within it caused him to forget.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּמַיְימִין, עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הָרוּחָנִי שֶׁבְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא נִזְכָּר הַכֹּל, אַחַר שֶׁנִּפְשַׁט מֵהַגַּשְׁמִי וְחוֹמֶר הַמַּשְׁכִּיחַ
Not so with one who “goes to the right”: through the spiritual force within the words of Torah, all is remembered, once it is stripped of the physical and of the “matter” that causes forgetting.
וְהַשִּׁכְחָה הוּא רַק בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִבְלָע בַּלֵּב
And forgetting occurs only with something not “absorbed” into the heart;
דְּמַה שֶּׁעוֹשֶׂה רֹשֶׁם בַּלֵּב אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁכָּח
for what leaves an impression on the heart cannot be forgotten;
אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הַכֹּל נִבְלָע מִיָּד בַּלֵּב לִהְיוֹת מוּרְגָּשׁ בְּכָל אֵבָרִים
only that not everything is at once absorbed into the heart so as to be felt in all the limbs.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ לֵב מֵבִין אֲפִילּוּ רַק בְּדָבָר אֶחָד, שֶׁנִּפְתְּחוּ שַׁעֲרֵי הַלֵּב כְּחוּדָהּ שֶׁל מַחַט, הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא פּוֹתֵחַ כְּפִתְחוֹ שֶׁל אוּלָם

But nonetheless, whoever has an “understanding heart” even in a single matter — such that the gates of the heart are opened [even] like the point of a needle — the Holy One opens [it wide] “like the opening of the Ulam-hall” (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2)557Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2: “The Holy One says to Israel: Open for Me an opening of repentance [as small] as the eye of a needle, and I will open for you an opening through which wagons and carriages may enter” — [that is, an opening as wide] as the opening of the Ulam-hall.,
דְּ״רוּחַ אַמְשִׁיךְ רוּחַ״
for “spirit draws spirit,”
וְעִיקַּר מִשְׁכַּן הָרוּחַ הוּא בַּלֵּב, וּבוֹ הוּא כֹּחַ הַהַמְשָׁכָה לְאִתְעֲרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא
and the essential dwelling of the “spirit” is in the heart, and in it lies the power to draw forth an “awakening from Above,”
כְּטַעַם ״צוּר לְבָבִי״ דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
