in the sense of “the Rock of my heart” (Tehillim 73:26)558Tehillim 73:26: “כָּלָה שְׁאֵרִי וּלְבָבִי, צוּר לְבָבִי וְחֶלְקִי אֱלֹהִים לְעוֹלָם” — “my flesh and my heart fail; the Rock of my heart and my portion is God forever.” R’ Tzadok’s use (with the teaching that “the Holy One is the heart of Israel”): the Holy One is the “Rock of my heart,” so the heart is the very seat from which the “awakening from Above” is drawn down — “spirit draws forth spirit.” — that the Holy One is “the heart of Israel.”
וְהַפֶּתַח כְּחוּדָהּ שֶׁל מַחַט הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּיַד הָאָדָם וּמַה שֶּׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׁוֹאֵל מֵעִמּוֹ

And the “needle-point opening” comes about through the fear [of Hashem] in the heart — which is [what is] in a person’s hand, and what the Holy One asks of him.559R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Soferim §13): “The essential striving of a person in this world is in yiras Shamayim, as is explicit in the verse, "what does Hashem ask of you but to fear"… for one who performs the mitzvos merely from his habit from youth — "a commandment of men learned by rote" — cannot be called a tzaddik on that account.” Precisely the se’if’s division: the needle-point opening is yirah, the one thing left to a person’s own hand, and it is exactly what mere rote cannot supply.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַה שֶּׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא פּוֹתֵחַ הוּא תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק וְהַצִּמָּאוֹן שֶׁבַּלֵּב לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
And afterward, what the Holy One “opens” is the intensity of longing and thirst in the heart for the words of Torah;
דִּכְפִי תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק כֵּן הוּא הַבְלָעַת הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בַּלֵּב
for according to the intensity of the longing, so is the “absorption” of the words of Torah into the heart.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא מִצַּד הָאָדָם וַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, לִהְיוֹת כּוֹסֵף וְחוֹשֵׁק אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְגַם זֶה יֵשׁ לָהּ גְּבוּל
And this [longing] is from the side of man and his service in this world — to yearn and long for Him — and this too has a limit;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַקִּיבּוּל שָׂכָר דְּלֶעָתִיד לָבֹא הוּא הַבְלָעַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְגַמְרֵי בַּלֵּב בְּלִי גְּבוּל
whereas the reward of the Future to Come is the complete absorption of the words of Torah into the heart, without limit,
כְּטַעַם ״וְלֹא יְלַמְּדוּ עוֹד אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ״

in the sense of “and no longer shall a man teach his fellow [saying, know Hashem, for they shall all know Me]” (Yirmeyah 31:33)560Yirmeyah 31:33: “וְלֹא יְלַמְּדוּ עוֹד אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ וְאִישׁ אֶת אָחִיו לֵאמֹר דְּעוּ אֶת ה׳, כִּי כוּלָּם יֵדְעוּ אוֹתִי לְמִקְּטַנָּם וְעַד גְּדוֹלָם” — “and no longer shall a man teach his fellow or his brother, saying, Know Hashem — for they shall all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.” The prophecy of the covenant of the Future, when the Torah is inscribed “upon their hearts.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the reward of the Future is the complete, limitless absorption of the words of Torah into the heart — that which is fully absorbed needs no “angel to remind” it, for one never forgets what one has wholly become..
וְזֶהוּ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ דְּ״הַמַּלְאָךְ מַזְכִּירוֹ״, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מַה שֶּׁנִּבְלָע אֵין צָרִיךְ לְהַזְכִּירוֹ

And this is what they meant that “the angel reminds him” [in this world] — whereas that which is [fully] absorbed [in the Future] needs no reminding at all.561R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah §5): “this alluded to the light of the holy Torah that was then bestowed — precisely that which the Greeks sought, "to make them forget Your Torah."” The se’if’s forgetting is here given its historical form: an enemy can reach only Torah that has not been absorbed inward, for what the heart has taken in cannot be made to be forgotten.Sefat Emet parallel - Eikev 24:3: Sefat Emet's treatment of moach, lev, and yirah closely parallels R. Tzadok's description of da'as as wisdom that truly enters the heart. He writes that the essential recognition of the Creator is in the moach and lev, and that yirah is the outer key that opens both; once the covering of the heart is removed, the Divine attachment already planted in the Jewish soul becomes revealed. He therefore calls yirah "re'iyah" - the capacity to see the truth. This helps distinguish the Torah that remains "from the lips outward" from Torah that becomes da'as. Information can be present in the intellect and even on the tongue without reorganizing the inner person. Yirah gives the knowledge existential weight: it opens the heart to receive what the mind knows, so that the Torah becomes part of the person's own inward reality. R. Tzadok's critique of Doeg is therefore not anti-intellectual. It is a demand that chochmah pass through the gate of yirah and enter the lev, where Chochmah and Binah are joined as da'as. — for Torah taken into the heart becomes part of the self, and one never “forgets” what one has become.

items.h: The theme: Yirah is the gate; the inner courtyard is Leah’s — through the intensity of cheishek (longing), which never satiates (“my soul thirsts for the living God”). After completion one returns to the beginning (like re-learning Shas more deeply) — this is receiving reward. The dudaim arouse longing. “Lo sachmod” (last commandment) is rooted in “Anochi” (first): one who knows all is from Hashem does not covet what is not his.

p: [יז] וְהַיִּרְאָה הוּא הַשַּׁעַר לַה׳ ״וְצַדִּיקִים יָבֹאוּ בוֹ״

And the fear [of Hashem] is “the gate to Hashem — the righteous shall enter through it” (Tehillim 118:20)562Tehillim 118:20: “זֶה הַשַּׁעַר לַה׳, צַדִּיקִים יָבֹאוּ בוֹ” — “this is the gate to Hashem; the righteous shall enter through it.” R’ Tzadok’s use: yirah (fear) is that “gate” — the entry-point to Hashem, yet only “the gate to the courtyard”; the courtyard itself is reached in the seed of Leah, through the intensity of cheishek (longing).,
דַּרְגָּא דְּיוֹסֵף דִּ״ירֵא אֱלֹקִים״

the rung of Yosef, of whom [it is said] “I fear God” (Bereishis 42:18)563Bereishis 42:18: Yosef to his brothers — “זֹאת עֲשׂוּ וִחְיוּ, אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים אֲנִי יָרֵא” — “do this and live: I fear God.” R’ Tzadok’s use: Yosef, of whom “I fear God” is said, is the rung of yirah — the “gate” through which the righteous enter, the safeguard that precedes the inner service of longing.;
וְהִיא תַּרְעָא לְדַרְתָּא לְבַד
but it [fear] is [only] “the gate to the courtyard,”
אֲבָל הַדַּרְתָּא הוּא בְּזַרְעָא דְּלֵאָה עַל יְדֵי תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק

whereas the “courtyard” itself is [attained] in the seed of Leah, through the intensity of longing.564R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §248): “The essence of man is the longing [cheishek] in the heart, in which lies his superiority over the angels; and it is what is called ‘yetzer’ — [both] the good inclination and the evil inclination. When he strengthens his longing toward the good, this is good; and if not, [toward evil]. And the Sages said (Sukkah 52a), ‘the greater [a person], the greater his inclination’ — for the greatness of one over another is only according to the greatness of his longing for the good, that is, the power of the inclination; for the good and evil inclinations are ‘this-opposite-that’ in the two chambers of the heart, according to the longing in his heart.”
וּלְפִי שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁקַט מִמֶּנָּה הַחֵשֶׁק לְהַעֲמִיד שְׁבָטִים
And since the longing to raise up tribes never subsided in her,
שֶׁעִנְיַן חֵשֶׁק זֶה הוּא מַמָּשׁ מַה שֶּׁאָמַר הַכָּתוּב ״צָמְאָה נַפְשִׁי לֵאלֹהִים לְאֵל חָי״

for this longing is literally what the verse means, “my soul thirsts for God, for the living God” (Tehillim 42:3)565Tehillim 42:3: “צָמְאָה נַפְשִׁי לֵאלֹהִים לְאֵל חָי, מָתַי אָבוֹא וְאֵרָאֶה פְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים” — “my soul thirsts for God, for the living God; when shall I come and appear before God?” R’ Tzadok’s use: this “thirst” is the very cheishek that never subsided in Leah — the longing to raise up tribes; it is the ultimate intensity of longing “which has no satiety at all,” ever renewing from the first rung, like one who finishes the whole Shas and returns to its beginning. —
כִּי צוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע״ה חֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד, וּשְׁבָטִים הֵם כְּלַל הַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים

for the “form of Yaakov Avinu” is engraved566Bereishis Rabbah 68:12 (and Chullin 91b): “you are the one whose icon is engraved on high” (at hu she-ikonin shelcha chakukah le-maalah) — the “form of Yaakov” is engraved beneath the Throne of Glory, and the angels “ascend and gaze upon his image above.” R’ Tzadok’s use: because Yaakov’s form is engraved on the Throne, the tribes are “the sum of the resting of the Shechinah among the lower worlds”; so Leah’s unquenchable longing to bear tribes is a longing to extend that indwelling into this world. on the Throne of Glory, and the tribes are the sum of the resting of His Shechinah among the lower [worlds].
וְגַם אַחַר שֶׁבֵּירְרָה כָּל שְׁלֵימוּת מַדְרֵיגוֹתֶיהָ וְעָמְדָה מִלֶּדֶת בְּפֹעַל, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁבַּלֵּב לֹא נִשְׁקַע עֲדַיִין
And even after she had clarified all the fullness of her levels and had ceased bearing in actuality, nonetheless the longing in her heart had not yet subsided;
כִּי זֶה תַּכְלִית תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שְׂבִיעָה כְּלָל
for this is the ultimate intensity of longing, which has no satiety at all,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל פָּסוּק ״אוֹהֵב כֶּסֶף לֹא יִשְׂבַּע כֶּסֶף״ מִצְווֹת לֹא יִשְׂבַּע

as they expounded on “one who loves silver [kesef] is not sated with silver” (Koheles 5:9)567Koheles 5:9: “אֹהֵב כֶּסֶף לֹא יִשְׂבַּע כֶּסֶף” — “one who loves silver is never sated with silver.” The Sages expounded (Koheles Rabbah 5:9; cf. 1:13): “one who loves mitzvos is never sated with mitzvos.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the mark of true longing — that it “has no satiety at all”; the more one attains, the more the cheishek renews, “not sated with mitzvos,” craving anew from the very first rung.: “he is not sated with mitzvos” —
הַיְינוּ מִמַּדְרֵגָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁבַּהַתְחָלָה
[longing anew] from the very first level of the beginning;
דְּאַחַר הַשְּׁלֵימוּת חָזַר לְהַתְחָלָה, כְּמוֹ אָדָם שֶׁסִּיֵּים לִימּוּדוֹ כָּל הַשַּׁ״ס וְחָזַר לְהַתְחָלָה לִלְמֹד פַּעַם שְׁנִיָּה בְּעִיּוּן עָמֹק יוֹתֵר
for after completion one returns to the beginning — like a person who finishes learning the whole Shas and returns to the start to learn it a second time, with deeper study.
וְדָבָר זֶה דַּחֲזָרָה אַחַר שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַטְעִים לָאָדָם שֶׁטּוֹב מִפְּרִי מַעֲשָׂיו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְהוּא קִיבּוּל שָׂכָר
And this “return” after completion is [how] Hashem gives a person a “taste” of the good from the fruit of his deeds in this world — and it is [a form of] receiving reward.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמְרָה ״נָתַן שְׂכָרִי אֲשֶׁר נָתַתִּי שִׁפְחָתִי״
And this is what she said, “God has given my reward, in that I gave my handmaid [to my husband]” (Bereishis 30:18):
זֶהוּ הַתְחָלַת הַצִּמָּאוֹן שֶׁלָּהּ אַחַר הַהַשְׁלָמָה לְהַרְבּוֹת שְׁבָטִים עַל כָּל פָּנִים מִשְׁפַּחְתָּהּ וְיִהְיוּ נִקְרָאִים עַל שְׁמָהּ
this was the [renewed] beginning of her thirst, after the completion, to multiply tribes at least of her own family, that they be called by her name.
וְדוּדָאִים אָמְרוּ דִּמְסוּגָּלִים לְהֵירָיוֹן, הַיְינוּ דִּמְעוֹרְרִים חֵשֶׁק, לְשׁוֹן ״דּוֹדִים״
And of the dudaim they said that they are propitious for conception — that is, they arouse longing (the word being a term of “dodim,” love),
כִּי פְּעָמִים מְנִיעַת הַהֵירָיוֹן מִצַּד מִיעוּט הַחֵשֶׁק וְהַתַּאֲוָה
for sometimes the prevention of conception is on account of a diminishment of longing and desire.
וּרְאוּבֵן שֶׁהוּא בֵּירוּר נִקְיוֹן הָרְאִיָּה דְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב, בְּמַה שֶּׁעַיִן רוֹאָה וְלֵב חוֹמֵד הוּא הַכֹּל לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
And Reuven — who is the clarification of the purity of “seeing” of Yaakov’s seed, [such] that “the eye sees and the heart covets” [and] all is for the sake of Heaven —
מָצָא הַדּוּדָאִים בַּשָּׂדֶה מָקוֹם הֶפְקֵר שֶׁלֹּא בְּאִיסּוּר
found the dudaim “in the field,” an ownerless place, with no transgression.
כִּי כָּל חֵשֶׁק לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם צָרִיךְ שְׁמִירָה שֶׁלֹּא יַחְשֹׁק בְּמַה שֶּׁאֵין שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹ
For all longing “for the sake of Heaven” requires a safeguard, that one not covet what does not belong to him;
דְּעַל זֶה אַזְהָרַת ״לֹא תַחְמֹד״ שֶׁהִיא אַחֲרוֹנָה בַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת

and regarding this is the admonition “you shall not covet,” which is the last of the Ten Commandments568Shemos 20:14 (the tenth commandment): “לֹא תַחְמֹד בֵּית רֵעֶךָ, לֹא תַחְמֹד אֵשֶׁת רֵעֶךָ… וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר לְרֵעֶךָ” — “you shall not covet your fellow’s house… nor anything that is your fellow’s.” R’ Tzadok’s use: all longing “for the sake of Heaven” needs the safeguard of “lo sachmod” — not to covet what is not one’s own; and “their end is embedded in their beginning,” for one who truly recognizes the first commandment, “Anochi Hashem your God,” knows that “from Your own they give to You” and does not covet what is not his..
וְנָעוּץ סוֹפָן בִּתְחִלָּתָן
And “their end is embedded in their beginning” (Sefer Yetzirah 1:7):
דְּמִי שֶׁמַּכִּיר דְּ״אָנֹכִי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ״ אֵינוֹ חוֹמֵד וּמִתְאַוֶּה בְּמַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ
for one who recognizes “I am Hashem your God” [the first commandment] does not covet or desire what is not his,
כִּי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁ״מִשֶּׁלְּךָ יִתְּנוּ לְךָ״ וְאֵין אָדָם נוֹגֵעַ בַּמּוּכָן לַחֲבֵירוֹ, מֵאַחַר דְּ״ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ״ מַנְהִיגְךָ

for he knows that “from Your own they give to You” (Avos 3:7)569Avos 3:7: “R’ Elazar of Bartosa says: Give Him of His own, for you and yours are His [ten lo mi-shelo, she-atah ve-shelcha shelo]; and so it says of David (I Divrei HaYamim 29:14), ‘for everything is from You, and from Your own hand have we given to You.’”, and no man touches what is prepared for his fellow — since “Hashem your God” guides you.570R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §41): “Anochi precedes lo yihyeh lecha — for through the complete contemplation of "Anochi," from the clear faith in Hashem that He is, one is saved from "lo yihyeh" and guarded from every kind of removal and harm.” Exactly the se’if’s root: the last utterance is secured by the first — one who truly holds “Anochi Hashem your God” is thereby delivered from coveting what was never assigned to him.
וְהָא בְּהָא תַּלְיָא, שֶׁאָמְרוּ דְּהַחוֹמֵד סוֹף לַעֲבֹר עַל כָּל עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת
And each depends on the other, for they said that one who covets will in the end transgress all Ten Commandments;
כִּי עִיקַּר חֲטָאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא בַּתַּאֲווֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ לֹא עָבְדוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֶלָּא לְהַתִּיר לָהֶם עֲרָיוֹת

for the essential sins of Israel are in [the realm of] desires, as they said, “they served idols only in order to permit themselves illicit relations” (Sanhedrin 63b)571Sanhedrin 63b: “R’ Yehuda said in the name of Rav: The Israelites [of that generation] knew that idolatry had no substance; they served idolatry only in order to permit themselves illicit relations in public.”.
וְחֶמְדָּה הָאֲסוּרָה הוּא כְּשֶׁחוֹמֵד מַה שֶּׁאֵין רָאוּי לוֹ
And forbidden coveting is when one covets what is not fitting for him,
וְאַף מַה שֶּׁרָאוּי לוֹ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין רָאוּי עַכְשָׁיו רַק לְאַחַר זְמַן
and even what is fitting for him, but not fitting now, only after a [proper] time —
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סנהדרין קז.) שֶׁאָכְלָה פַּגָּה

as they said (Sanhedrin 107a)572Sanhedrin 107a: Again the teaching that Bathsheva “was fitting for David from the six days of creation,” only that she came to him prematurely — “the unripe fig eaten before its time.” (So too here: forbidden coveting includes desiring even what is fitting for oneself, but before its proper time.), that “he ate the unripe fig,”
הוּא דּוּגְמַת נִידָּה דְּגַם כֵּן עַכְשָׁיו אֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לוֹ
which is like [the case of] a niddah, who [though his wife] is likewise, just now, not permitted to him,
וְדוּגְמַת חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל [בְּבֵיצָה] שֶׁלֹּא יָכוֹל לְהַמְתִּין
and like the sin of Adam HaRishon, of whom the Sages said [in Beitzah] that he “could not wait” [until Shabbos].
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן רְאוּבֵן ״פַּחַז כַּמַּיִם״, שֶׁהוּא רֵאשִׁית הַחֶמְדָּה וּבֵירוּרָהּ בְּתִיקּוּן חֵטְא דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
And this is the matter of Reuven, “impetuous as water” — for he is the “beginning” of coveting and its clarification, in the rectification of the sin of Adam HaRishon,
עַד שֶׁיִּתּוֹקַן וְיִבֻּלַּע הַמָּוֶת ״וְאַל יָמֹת״
until it be rectified and “death be swallowed up” — “and let him not die.”
וְזֶהוּ ״דּוּדָאִים בַּשָּׂדֶה״, דְּאַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ מִכָּל מָקוֹם כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוּא הֶפְקֵר יָכוֹל לַחְמֹד לוֹ

And this is “the dudaim in the field”: that although it is not [strictly] his, nonetheless, since it is ownerless, he may covet it [permissibly].573R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Matos §8): “In the first utterance it says "Anochi Hashem your God" — and it was not said in the language of command… and so was engraved in the souls of Israel the revelation of Godliness, until the last utterance, "lo sachmod" — for through the revelation of Godliness in ten rungs the heart is made hollow and empty of every kind of coveting and desire of this world.” The se’if’s “lo sachmod is rooted in Anochi,” stated as a process: the ten utterances hollow the heart until nothing is left to covet.Shem MiShmuel parallel - Vaetchanan 4:15, citing Rambam, Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 2:2: Shem MiShmuel brings the Rambam's classic description of the path to love and fear: contemplation of Hashem's wondrous works first produces love, praise, and an intense desire to know Him - the state expressed by David's "tzamah nafshi l'Elokim l'El chai" - and the very same contemplation then causes the person to recoil in awe, recognizing his smallness before the Perfect Knower. This complements R. Tzadok's presentation of yirah as a gate into Leah's inward world of unending longing. The two movements are not contradictory. True longing grows precisely because the object of longing cannot be possessed or exhausted, while true yirah prevents longing from collapsing into self-satisfaction. One approaches and discovers distance; the distance itself increases thirst; the renewed thirst drives a deeper approach. That circular movement explains R. Tzadok's language that after a person reaches completion he returns again to the beginning. The "gate" is not a threshold crossed once but a permanent protection of the infinitude of the relationship. — for desire itself is not the sin; desire fixed on what is not one’s own is.

items.h: The theme: Rachel “envied” — desiring the dudaim not truly hers; this led her to cede the tzaddik’s couch (the very opposite of coveting), rectifying the trait of jealousy: not the “evil eye” that would deny others, but a “good eye” letting Leah bear more. Leah’s pure-hearted “you shall come to me” (like Yaakov’s “give me my wife”) won her the sons of Yissachar — wisdom dripping from Chochmah into the Binah of the heart (“va-yeda Elokim”).

p: [יח] וְרָחֵל ״קִנְאָה בַּאֲחוֹתָהּ״

And Rachel “envied her sister” (Bereishis 30:1)574Bereishis 30:1: “וַתֵּרֶא רָחֵל כִּי לֹא יָלְדָה לְיַעֲקֹב, וַתְּקַנֵּא רָחֵל בַּאֲחֹתָהּ, וַתֹּאמֶר אֶל יַעֲקֹב הָבָה לִּי בָנִים וְאִם אַיִן מֵתָה אָנֹכִי” — “and Rachel saw that she had borne Yaakov no children, and Rachel envied her sister, and said to Yaakov, ‘Give me children — and if not, I am as dead.’” R’ Tzadok’s use: envy is the very opposite of coveting, yet Rachel “envied” this coveting — desiring the dudaim, which in truth did not belong to her; this is “coveting what is not one’s own,” and it is precisely her rectification of it (ceding the tzaddik’s couch, a “good eye”) that is the subject of this se’if.,
וְיָדוּעַ קִנְאָה הוּא הֵיפֶךְ תַּאֲוָה וְחֶמְדָּה
and it is known that envy is the opposite of desire and coveting;
וְהִיא קִנְּאָה בְּחֶמְדָּה זוֹ וּבָקְשָׁה לָקַחַת דּוּדָאֵי בְּנָהּ
yet she “envied” [i.e., desired] this coveting, and asked to take the dudaim of [Leah’s] son.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת זֶה לֹא הָיָה שַׁיָּיךְ לָהּ, וְזֶהוּ חֶמְדָּה בְּמַה שֶּׁאֵין שַׁיָּיךְ לָהּ

But in truth this did not belong to her — and this is “coveting what does not belong to one.”575R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §31): “envy is toward those who are not his beloved, yet in any case [toward those] of his acquaintance and the people of his land — for one is envious only of one who resembles him, and not of a stranger.” This sharpens the se’if’s difficulty and its answer: Rachel could envy only Leah, her very sister and like — which is why the rectification had to come by giving her what was hers.
וּלְפִי שֶׁהִיא בָּקְשָׁה חֶמְדָּה וְאֵין זֶה מִדָּתָהּ
And because she sought “coveting,” which is not her [proper] trait,
וְלֹא יָדְעָה דְּאֶצְלָהּ הַחֶמְדָּה הוּא שֶׁאֵין שַׁיָּיךְ לָהּ וְאָסוּר
and she did not realize that for her the coveting is [precisely of] what does not belong to her, and is forbidden —
גָּרַם לָהּ לְזִלְזוּל עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּמִשְׁכָּבוֹ שֶׁל צַדִּיק, שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ הַחֶמְדָּה לְגַמְרֵי
it caused her, thereby, to “make light” of the couch of the tzaddik [ceding that night to Leah] — which is the very opposite of coveting.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא דְּגַם מַה שֶּׁהָיָה לוֹ נִיטַּל, אֶלָּא דְּשָׁם הוּא עוֹנֶשׁ בְּעַל כָּרְחוֹ
And along the lines of what is brought, that “even what he [already] had was taken from him” — except that there it is a punishment, against his will;
אֲבָל כָּאן דְּהִיא כִּיוְּונָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וְחָלִילָה לֹא חָמְדָה מַה שֶּׁאֵין רָאוּי לָהּ בֶּאֱמֶת
but here, since she [Rachel] intended for the sake of Heaven, and — Heaven forbid — did not [truly] covet what was unfitting for her,
דְּהֲרֵי הִיא נְתָנַתַם לָהּ, רַק דְּלֹא הָיָה רָאוּי לָהּ בְּחִנָּם אֶלָּא בְּשָׂכָר, הִיא בְּעַצְמָהּ נָתְנָה שֶׁלָּהּ מִדַּעְתָּהּ
for indeed she [Leah] gave them to her — only that it was not to come to her for free, but for a “price” — she [Rachel] herself gave what was hers, willingly.
וְזֶהוּ תִּיקּוּן מִדַּת הַקַּנַּאי
And this is the rectification of the trait of the “jealous one”:
דְּיָדוּעַ מִדַּת הַקַּנַּאי יַסְכִּים לְסַלֵּק טוֹבָה מֵאֲחֵרִים אַף שֶׁגַּם לוֹ לֹא יִהְיֶה וְיִגְרַע עוֹד יוֹתֵר
for it is known that the jealous one would agree to remove good from others, even though he too will not have it, and will lose even more;
אֲבָל הִיא הָיָה לָהּ טוֹבַת עַיִן לָתֵת לְלֵאָה שֶׁתֵּלֵד יוֹתֵר, רַק שֶׁגַּם הִיא יִהְיֶה לָהּ עַל כָּל פָּנִים
but she [Rachel] had a “good eye,” to let Leah bear more — only that she too should have [children] at least;
וּבִשְׂכַר זֶה קִנְּאָה הַדּוּדָאִים, הַיְינוּ הַחֶמְדָּה עַל יְדֵי סִילּוּק הַקִּנְאָה מִלֵּאָה

and in reward for this she “acquired” the dudaim — that is, [she rectified] the coveting by removing the “envy” toward Leah.576R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §190): “In this, Yaakov Avinu’s bed was ‘complete’ and all his seed was truth. And in the language of the Sages, a ‘fine eye’ or a ‘good eye’ [ayin tovah] means generosity of heart and not being jealous — and so in the language of Scripture, ‘the good of eye [shall be blessed], for he has given [of his bread to the poor]’ (Mishlei 22:9); and its opposite is the ‘evil eye.’” (This defines the very rectification of the se’if: Rachel’s ceding of the couch converts jealousy into the ayin tovah — the open-handed eye that begrudges nothing to another.)
וּבָזֶה זָכְתָה לֵאָה לְיִשָּׂשכָר, שֶׁהוּא קִיבּוּל הַשָּׂכָר, אַחַר שֶׁסִּילְּקָה רָחֵל קִנְאָתָהּ מִמֶּנָּה
And through this Leah merited Yissachar — who is “the receiving of reward” — after Rachel removed her envy from her;
דְּבְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּתְנוּ חֲכָמִים עֵינֵיהֶם כו׳, שֶׁזֶּה מוֹנֵעַ הַטּוֹב

for “wherever the Sages set their eyes [there is death or poverty],” etc.577Nedarim 7b: “וְתַנְיָא: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּתְנוּ חֲכָמִים עֵינֵיהֶם — אוֹ מִיתָה אוֹ עוֹנִי” — “and it is taught: wherever the Sages set their eyes [in reproach], [there follows] either death or poverty.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the “eye” of the Sages, cast in disfavor, withholds good and brings harm — the “evil eye”; over against it stands Rachel’s “good eye,” which let Leah bear more, and it is by removing that envy that Leah merited Yissachar, “the receiving of reward.” — [an “evil eye”] which withholds the good;

וּ״בִרְצוֹת ה׳ דַּרְכֵי אִישׁ״ וְגוֹמֵר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר רַבִּי עַל רַבִּי חִיָּיא [בְּמוֹעֵד קָטָן טז:]578Moed Katan 16b: R’ Chiya taught his two nephews, Rav and Rabbah bar bar Chana, publicly in the marketplace; Rebbi was displeased, and R’ Chiya accepted a reprimand upon himself. When he later came before Rebbi, Rebbi read over him the verse “when Hashem favors a man’s ways, He reconciles even his enemies to him” (Mishlei 16:7).

and “when Hashem favors a man’s ways [even his enemies make peace with him]” (Mishlei 16:7)579Mishlei 16:7: “בִּרְצוֹת ה׳ דַּרְכֵי אִישׁ, גַּם אוֹיְבָיו יַשְׁלִם אִתּוֹ” — “when Hashem favors a man’s ways, even his enemies make peace with him.” R’ Tzadok’s use (with what Rebbi said of R’ Chiya, Moed Katan 16b): once Rachel’s envy was removed and a “good eye” prevailed, the way was open for blessing — “even his enemies make peace with him” — and Leah could bear Yissachar, free of the “evil eye” that withholds the good., as Rebbi said of R. Chiya [in Moed Katan 16b].
וְנִתְבָּרֵר אָז טָהֳרַת לְבָבָהּ בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרָה ״אֵלַי תָּבוֹא״
And then the purity of her [Leah’s] heart was clarified in her saying, “you shall come to me” (Bereishis 30:16),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר יַעֲקֹב ״הָבָה אֶת אִשְׁתִּי״
just as Yaakov said, “Give me my wife” —
לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה כַּוָּונָתוֹ אֶלָּא לְהַעֲמִיד תּוֹלָדוֹת, לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בּוּשָׁה, אַף הִיא כֵּן
since his intent was only to establish offspring, no shame applies — so too with her;
וּתְבָעַתּוּ בְּפֶה שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּבְּרוּת הַחֵשֶׁק לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם גָּמוּר

and she “demanded” of him explicitly — which is the intensification of longing, wholly for the sake of Heaven.580R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach §4): “the yetzer hara was created for the good, only that man ruins it and makes it evil. For the root of the yetzer hara is envy, desire and honor — and all of them are needed in holiness as well: envy we find, "the envy of scribes increases wisdom"…” Exactly the se’if: Rachel’s envy was not the trait’s corruption but its holy use — jealousy turned into the intensification of longing, wholly for Heaven.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכְתָה לְבָנִים דַּאֲפִילּוּ בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה לֹא אִשְׁתְּכַח כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל

And through this she merited children the like of whom were not found even in the generation of Moshe, as the Sages said581Eruvin 100b: R’ Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of R’ Yochanan: any woman who [modestly] solicits her husband to the mitzvah will have children the like of whom did not exist even in the generation of Moshe — Of Leah it is written (Bereishis 30), “and Leah went out to meet him and said, ‘to me you shall come, for I have surely hired you’” — and (I Divrei HaYamim 12), “and of the sons of Yissachar, those who knew understanding of the times.” This teaches that “the woman solicits with the heart and the man solicits with the mouth, and this is a good trait in women” [Rashi: she shows him affection]. [Leah’s forthright request, for the mitzvah’s sake, earned her the uniquely wise sons of Yissachar.] —
דְּחָכְמָתָם הוּא מֵחָכְמָה עֶלְיוֹנָה הַנּוֹטֶפֶת לַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁבּוֹ הַיְדִיעָה, רְצֹה לוֹמַר הַהַרְגָּשָׁה
for their wisdom [Yissachar’s] is from the supernal Chochmah that “drips” into the Binah of the heart, in which is the “knowing” — that is, the [inner] feeling —
כְּטַעַם ״וַיֵּדַע אֱלֹהִים״

in the sense of “and God knew” (Shemos 2:25)582Shemos 2:25: “וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וַיֵּדַע אֱלֹהִים” — “and God saw the children of Israel, and God knew.” R’ Tzadok’s use: Yissachar’s wisdom is the supernal Chochmah that “drips” into the Binah of the heart — grasped not as taught information but as an inner “knowing,” a felt perception, in the sense of “va-yeda Elokim” — a knowing of intimate awareness rather than mere data.Izhbitz parallel - Mei HaShiloach, Nitzavim 6: Mei HaShiloach gives an especially fitting parallel to R. Tzadok's claim that the yetzer itself can be turned toward holiness. On "u-mal Hashem Elokecha es levavcha," he explains that the very cheshek a person formerly had for things that were not good in Hashem's eyes can, after complete teshuvah, be repaired by Hashem and redirected into love of Hashem, desire for Torah, and eagerness for the mitzvos. The evil desire is not simply amputated; its energetic core is clarified and returned to its proper object. This complements R. Tzadok's discussion of Rachel's kinah and the general principle that the root of the yetzer was created for good. A middah becomes destructive when its force is attached to the wrong object or experienced as an autonomous demand. Teshuvah can uncover the holy capacity concealed in that same force - ambition as zeal for avodah, jealousy as longing for holiness, desire as cheshek for Torah. The later discovery of a holy root does not sanctify the earlier misuse; it requires the actual work of return through which the desire is reoriented and made into a servant of Hashem.. — the deepest wisdom entering not as taught information but as a felt “knowing” of the heart.

items.h: The theme: Reuven = seeing clarified; Yissachar = knowing without seeing; Zevulun (“yizbeleini”) = a permanent indwelling, not only at the moment of union — “Abba and Ima that never part.” The sea = unquenchable longing (of olam ha-zeh), stilled by the sand-boundary (Gevurah); from that sand comes clear glass (the aspaklaria), so that in the Future even yirah — man’s own task — is granted from Heaven without effort.

p: [יט] וּבִרְאוּבֵן נִתְבָּרֵר הָרְאִיָּה, וּבְיִשָּׂשכָר הַיְדִיעָה בְּלֹא רְאִיָּה
And in Reuven the “seeing” was clarified, and in Yissachar the “knowing” without seeing,
דְּזֶהוּ הַיְדִיעָה דְּבִינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְאִיָּה נִגְלֵית כְּלָל
for this is the “knowing” of the Binah of the heart, [attained] not through any revealed seeing at all,
רַק עַל דֶּרֶךְ ״וְלִבִּי רָאָה הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה״

but along the lines of “and my heart has seen much wisdom” (Koheles 1:16)583Koheles 1:16: “דִּבַּרְתִּי אֲנִי עִם לִבִּי לֵאמֹר… וְלִבִּי רָאָה הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה וָדָעַת” — “I spoke with my heart, saying… and my heart has seen much wisdom and knowledge.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this “seeing of the heart” is Yissachar’s rung — the “knowing” of the heart’s Binah, attained without any revealed, external seeing; the “second beginning,” of receiving reward, in the perfection of spiritual sight.;
שֶׁהִיא הַהַתְחָלָה שְׁנִיָּה דְּקִיבּוּל שָׂכָר בִּשְׁלֵימוּת הָרְאִיָּה הָרוּחָנִית

this being the “second beginning,” of receiving reward, in the perfection of spiritual “seeing.”584R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §43): “a sage is greater than a prophet — he can attain more, only that it is not a revealed and clear attainment like the attainment of prophecy, which is called "the seer," for it is like seeing through glass and a speculum; but then it was reversed from seeing to light, as they said, "the Jews had light" — this is Torah — that the Torah should be light illumining their eyes without seeing at all.” Exactly the se’if’s glass-from-sand: what is now a seeing through a speculum becomes, in the Future, light itself.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ זְבוּלוּן ״הַפַּעַם יִזְבְּלֵנִי אִישִׁי״, קִיבּוּל שָׂכָר נֶגֶד לֵוִי ״הַפַּעַם יִלָּוֶה אִישִׁי״

And afterward Zevulun — “this time my husband will make me his zevul [abode]” (Bereishis 30:20)585Bereishis 30:20: “וַתֹּאמֶר לֵאָה זְבָדַנִי אֱלֹהִים אֹתִי זֵבֶד טוֹב, הַפַּעַם יִזְבְּלֵנִי אִישִׁי כִּי יָלַדְתִּי לוֹ שִׁשָּׁה בָנִים, וַתִּקְרָא אֶת שְׁמוֹ זְבֻלוּן” — “and Leah said, ‘God has granted me a goodly gift; this time my husband will make me his abode [yizbeleini], for I have borne him six sons,’ and she called his name Zevulun.” R’ Tzadok’s use: “yizbeleini” (an abode) is a permanent cleaving, even not at the time of union — corresponding to, yet surpassing, Levi’s “yilaveh” (joining at the time of union): the fixed indwelling of supernal Chochmah in the chambers of the heart. — a “receiving of reward” corresponding to Levi’s “this time my husband will be joined [yilaveh] to me.”
וְ״יִלָּוֶה״ הַיְינוּ דְּבֵיקוּת בִּשְׁעַת חִיבּוּר, וְ״יִזְבְּלֵנִי״ הַיְינוּ דְּבֵיקוּת גַּם שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת חִיבּוּר
“Yilaveh” (joining) is cleaving at the time of union, whereas “yizbeleini” (abode) is cleaving even not at the time of union —
כְּמַעֵר אִישׁ וְלוֹיָתוֹ, רַק דִּירָה תְּמִידִית
not “like the union of a man and his companion [at times],” but a permanent dwelling —
עַל דֶּרֶךְ אַבָּא וְאִימָא תְּרֵין רֵיעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין
along the lines of “Abba and Ima, two companions that never part.”
וְזֶהוּ תָּמְכֵי דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דְּחָכְמָה עִילָּאָה, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָהּ דִּירָה קֶבַע וְקַיֶּימֶת בְּחַדְרֵי לִבּוֹ
And this is [Zevulun,] the “supporters of Torah” of supernal Chochmah — that it have a fixed, enduring dwelling in the chambers of his heart,
כְּעִנְיַן ״בָּנֹה בָנִיתִי בֵּית זְבוּל לָךְ מָכוֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ עוֹלָמִים״

in the sense of “I have surely built You a house of zevul, a foundation for Your dwelling forever” (Melachim I 8:13)586Melachim I 8:13: “בָּנֹה בָנִיתִי בֵּית זְבֻל לָךְ, מָכוֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ עוֹלָמִים” — “I have surely built You a house of abode [beis zevul], a foundation for Your dwelling forever” (Shlomo, at the dedication of the Beis HaMikdash). R’ Tzadok’s use: the “zevul” of Zevulun is this fixed, enduring dwelling — that the supernal Chochmah have “a foundation for Your dwelling forever” within the chambers of a person’s heart..587R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §76): “‘This time my husband will dwell with me’ [yizbeleini] (Bereishis 30:20) — an expression of a dwelling-place; therefore they said in Chagigah (12b) that in [the heaven called] Zevul the Beis HaMikdash stands built, for there is ‘the foundation for Your dwelling’ — a dwelling-place for the Shechinah; and this is through Zevulun, who is its support.” (This grounds the se’if’s reading of yizbeleini as a permanent indwelling: Zevulun’s very name is the fixed ‘house of zevul’ in which the Shechinah abides.)
וְהוּא ״לְחוֹף יַמִּים יִשְׁכּוֹן״

And he “shall dwell at the shore of the seas” (Bereishis 49:13)588Bereishis 49:13: “זְבוּלֻן לְחוֹף יַמִּים יִשְׁכֹּן, וְהוּא לְחוֹף אֳנִיּוֹת וְיַרְכָתוֹ עַל צִידֹן” — “Zevulun shall dwell at the shore of the seas, and he shall be a haven for ships, and his flank upon Tzidon” (Yaakov’s blessing). R’ Tzadok’s use: the “sea” denotes unquenchable longing, but Zevulun dwells at its shore — the sand-boundary (Gevurah) that stills the “roaring of the seas,” and from whose sand comes the clear glass of the aspaklaria.,
דְּיָדוּעַ יָם מוֹרֶה תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שְׂבִיעָה
for it is known that “the sea” denotes the intensity of longing that has no satiety,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כָּל הַנְּחָלִים הוֹלְכִים אֶל הַיָּם וְהַיָּם אֵינֶנּוּ מָלֵא״

as it says, “all the rivers flow to the sea, yet the sea is not full” (Koheles 1:7)589Koheles 1:7: “כָּל הַנְּחָלִים הֹלְכִים אֶל הַיָּם וְהַיָּם אֵינֶנּוּ מָלֵא, אֶל מְקוֹם שֶׁהַנְּחָלִים הֹלְכִים שָׁם הֵם שָׁבִים לָלָכֶת” — “all the rivers flow to the sea, yet the sea is not full; to the place where the rivers flow, there they flow again.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the sea “not full” is the longing of this world that “has no satiety” — full of turmoil, with no rest until one reaches dry land.;
וְהַיְינוּ חֵשֶׁק דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא טְרָדוֹת
this being the longing of this world, which is full of turmoil,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל דְּכָל יוֹרְדֵי יָם אֵין לָהֶם נַיְיחָא עַד שֶׁיַּעַמְדוּ בַּיַּבָּשָׁה
and as the Sages said, that all who “go down to the sea” have no rest until they stand on dry land.
וְזֶהוּ הֲמִיּוֹן הָאֻמּוֹת שֶׁהוּא כִּשְׁאוֹן יַמִּים בִּשְׁקִיעָה יְתֵירָה בְּכָל חַמְדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם קֵץ

And this is the “tumult of the nations, like the roaring of the seas” (Yeshayahu 17:12)590Yeshayahu 17:12: “הוֹי הֲמוֹן עַמִּים רַבִּים כַּהֲמוֹת יַמִּים יֶהֱמָיוּן, וּשְׁאוֹן לְאֻמִּים כִּשְׁאוֹן מַיִם כַּבִּירִים יִשָּׁאוּן” — “Ah, the tumult of many peoples — they roar like the roaring of the seas — and the din of nations, that roar like the roaring of mighty waters.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the “roaring of the seas” is the tumult of the nations, sunk exceedingly in the endless, boundless desires of this world. — sunk exceedingly in all the endless desires of this world.
וְעַל כֵּן הַיָּם רָאָה אֲרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף, שֶׁהוּא הַהַגְדָּרָה מֵחַמְדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וַיָּנֹס וְנַעֲשָׂה יַבָּשָׁה

Therefore “the sea saw” the coffin of Yosef — who is the “bounding-in” from the desires of this world — “and fled” (Tehillim 114:3)591Tehillim 114:3: “הַיָּם רָאָה וַיָּנֹס, הַיַּרְדֵּן יִסֹּב לְאָחוֹר” — “the sea saw and fled, the Jordan turned back” (from Hallel). The Sages asked, “what did it see, that it fled?” and answered: the coffin of Yosef (Midrash — Bereishis Rabbah 87; Mechilta, Beshalach). R’ Tzadok’s use: the sea — the endless desires of this world — “fled” and became dry land before the coffin of Yosef, who is the “bounding-in” (self-mastery) that guards against the desires of this world., and became dry land.
אֲבָל זְבוּלוּן הוּא ״לְחוֹף״ הַחוֹל אֲשֶׁר בִּגְבוּל יַמִּים, גְּבוּרָה דְּמָארֵךְ
But Zevulun is at “the shore” — the sand at the boundary of the seas — [the aspect of] “the might of your Master”;
דִּכְמְלֹא חוּטָא דְּחוֹל אֵין יָכוֹל לַעֲבֹר כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּהַסְּפִינָה]

that “the sea cannot cross even the breadth of a thread of sand,” as they said [in Perek HaSefinah, Bava Basra 73a]592Bava Basra 73a: [One wave said to another:] “go out and see the might of your Master! by a mere thread’s-breadth of sand [I am held back] and cannot pass, as it says (Yirmeyah 5), ‘will you not fear Me, says Hashem — who set the sand as a boundary to the sea, an everlasting decree that it cannot pass.’” [A thread’s-breadth of sand holds back the raging sea — “a boundary forever.”] —
דְּזֶהוּ מִצַּד מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה הַמְצַמְצֶמֶת לַתַּאֲוֹת וּמַשְׁבִּית שְׁאוֹן יַמִּים

for this is from the side of the trait of Gevurah, which “contracts” the desires and stills the roaring of the seas.593R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vaera §11): “our essential service is to rectify its ruin and to bring these two aspects into holiness alone, as it is written, "let your heart not envy sinners, but rather the fear of Hashem all the day" — that in the fear of Hashem one must be envious… and this is the matter of the Behemos on a thousand hills, the wild ox and the Leviathan, prepared for the tzaddikim in the Future when the yetzer hara is burned away.” The se’if’s sea and its boundary: the endless waters are not destroyed but bounded, and their creature is kept for the Future.
וּמֵאוֹתוֹ חוֹל נַעֲשָׂה זְכוּכִית לְבָנָה, הוּא אַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא הַמְּאִירָה דְּמַחֲוֵי לְהוּ יִצְחָק הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ
And from that same sand is made “clear glass” — the aspaklaria ha-me’irah through which “Yitzchak shows them the Holy One with their [own] eyes” [in the Future],
כִּי ״עַיִן בְּעַיִן יִרְאוּ בְּשׁוּב ה׳ צִיּוֹן״

for “eye to eye they shall see when Hashem returns to Zion” (Yeshayahu 52:8)594Yeshayahu 52:8: “קוֹל צֹפַיִךְ נָשְׂאוּ קוֹל יַחְדָּו יְרַנֵּנוּ, כִּי עַיִן בְּעַיִן יִרְאוּ בְּשׁוּב ה׳ צִיּוֹן” — “the voice of your watchmen! they raise their voice, together they sing for joy, for eye to eye they shall see when Hashem returns to Zion.” R’ Tzadok’s use: in the Future even the physical eyes will become spiritual, seeing “eye to eye” through the aspaklaria ha-me’irah — and then “fear is a small matter,” granted from Heaven without any effort.,
דְּגַם עֵינֵי הַגַּשְׁמִים שָׁבוּ לִהְיוֹת רוּחָנִים, וְאָז הַיִּרְאָה מִלְּתָא זוּטַרְתִּי

for even the physical “eyes” [will] return to being spiritual, and then “fear is a small matter” (Berachos 33b)595Berachos 33b: On “and now, Israel, what does Hashem your God ask of you, but to fear [Him]” (Devarim 10:12): “Is fear of Heaven a small matter [milsa zutarta]? Yes — for Moshe it is a small matter.” (For one who has attained the rung, awe of Heaven becomes “small.”)Izhbitz-Radzin and Sefat Emet parallel - Sha'ar HaEmunah VeYesod HaChasidut 24:3-4; Sefat Emet, Eikev 24:3: The combination of Yissachar, Binah, and a form of knowledge deeper than ordinary sight is developed in Sha'ar HaEmunah, which explains "yodei binah la'itim" as the power to grasp and even "heal" time from the place of Binah. This is a knowing that does not depend on visible surface alone; it reads the inward demand of the moment. Sefat Emet adds that yirah is itself a form of re'iyah: by removing the covering from moach and lev, fear enables a person to see the Divine truth concealed within his own soul. These two formulations help clarify R. Tzadok's sequence of Reuven, Yissachar, and Zevulun. Reuven begins with rectified seeing; Yissachar reaches an inward understanding that can know what is not visible; Zevulun carries that inward bond into the changing movements of "going out" and worldly encounter. Mature avodah does not depend on constant visionary clarity. Once the heart has become a dwelling for the Divine, a person can move through concealment and still remain joined to the inner truth that Binah has taught him to recognize..
וְעַל כֵּן הַכֹּל צְרִיכִין לוֹ עַל יְדֵי חִלָּזוֹן לִתְכֵלֶת, שֶׁהוּא מוֹרֶה עַל יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר [סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת שְׁלַח]
And therefore “all are dependent on him” [Zevulun], through the chilazon [that yields] techeiles — which denotes yiras Shamayim, as they said in the Zohar [end of Parashas Shelach];
כִּי סוֹף הַקִּיבּוּל שָׂכָר דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא שֶׁגַּם הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁהוּא בְּיַד אָדָם, וְהוּא כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם, גַּם זֶה יִנָּתֵן לוֹ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם בְּלֹא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת כְּלָל

for the culmination of the reward of this world is that even the fear [of Hashem], which is [normally] in a person’s own hand — the whole of a person’s effort — even this will be granted him from Heaven, without any effort at all. — the final frontier of reward being that even the one thing left to man, his own reverence, is at last given as a gift.

items.h: The theme: Leah’s seed (love/longing) also attain yirah — the techeiles-thread (“you shall see it and remember”), for forgetting stems from the absence of fear. Fear fixes a thing in the heart, and what is in the heart cannot be forgotten. Hence “whoever saw David recalled his learning”: a king’s awe is not that of flesh-and-blood but of Malchus drawn from the Kingship of Heaven — David being the “fourth leg of the Merkavah.”

p: [כ] וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת זַרְעָא דְּלֵאָה, שֶׁהֵם עִיקַּר עֲבוֹדָתָם בְּאַהֲבָה וְחֵשֶׁק, וְזוֹכִים גַּם לְיִרְאָה שֶׁהוּא עֲבוֹדַת זַרְעָא דְּרָחֵל
And this is the ultimate perfection of Leah’s seed: that their essential service is in love and longing, and [yet] they also merit fear — which is the service of Rachel’s seed.
וְחוּט דִּתְכֵלֶת דְּצִיצִית, הַיְינוּ הִתְעוֹרְרוּת יִרְאָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם, דִּ״רְאִיתֶם אוֹתוֹ וּזְכַרְתֶּם״

And the thread of techeiles of the tzitzis is [precisely this] arousal of fear from Heaven, as in “you shall see it and remember” (Bamidbar 15:39).596R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §16): “And for this [purpose] is the mitzvah of tzitzis in practice — ‘that you may remember [and do all My commandments] and not stray [after your own heart]’ (Bamidbar 15:39) — which does not remove the desire entirely, so that it should not enter the heart at all; rather, [it enjoins one] not to stray after cravings and the willfulness of his heart, but to thrust it away from his heart at once. And this [comes] by way of the remembrance that the tzitzis brings — like that student in Menachos (44a) whose very tzitzis ‘slapped him across the face’ [and stopped him from sin].” (R’ Tzadok makes explicit the mechanism of the techeiles-thread that this se’if invokes: it is not the uprooting of desire but the instant refusal to pursue it.)
דְּהַשִּׁכְחָה בָּאָה מִצַּד הֶעְדֵּר הַיִּרְאָה, וְזֶה אַתְחַלְתָּא דְּכָל רַע
For forgetting comes on account of the absence of fear, and this is “the beginning of all evil,”
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְהָיָה אִם שָׁכֹחַ״ וְגוֹמֵר [״וְהָלַכְתָּ אַחֲרֵי אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים״]

as it says, “and it shall be, if you forget — [and go after other gods]” (Devarim 8:19)597Devarim 8:19: “וְהָיָה אִם שָׁכֹחַ תִּשְׁכַּח אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ, וְהָלַכְתָּ אַחֲרֵי אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים…” — “and it shall be, if you forget Hashem your God and go after other gods…” R’ Tzadok’s use: forgetting stems from the absence of fear, and it is “the beginning of all evil” — the slide to “other gods”; hence the techeiles-thread (“you shall see it and remember”) arouses the fear that fixes a thing in the heart, whence it can never be forgotten. —
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהַיִּרְאָה תַּרְעָא לְדַרְתָּא דְּצַדִּיקִים
[just] as fear is “the gate to the courtyard” of the righteous.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַיִּרְאָה בָּא הַזְּכִירָה, כִּי דָּבָר שֶׁאָדָם יָרֵא הוּא נִקְבָּע בַּלֵּב
And through fear comes remembering, for a thing a person fears becomes fixed in the heart;
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ [יוֹמָא עב:] ״וְלֶב אָיִן״ עַל הֶעְדֵּר הַיִּרְאָה, וְדָבָר שֶׁהוּא בַּלֵּב תָּמִיד אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִשְׁכֹּחַ בּוֹ
and therefore they said [in Yoma 72b] “and he has no heart” concerning the absence of fear — for a thing that is always in the heart cannot be forgotten.
וְזֶה טַעַם מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ חז״ל (ויק״ר כ, א) עַל פָּסוּק ״וְטוֹב רֹאִי״, כָּל הָרוֹאֶה דָּוִד נִזְכָּר לְתַלְמוּדוֹ

And this is the reason for what the Sages said (Vayikra Rabbah 20:1)598Vayikra Rabbah 20:1: “‘And he was of goodly appearance [tov ro’i]’ (Shmuel I 16:12) — R’ Yitzchak said: ‘of goodly appearance’ in halachah — whoever saw [David] was reminded of his learning [nizkar l’talmudo].” on the verse “and of goodly appearance [tov ro’i]” (Shmuel I 16:12): whoever saw David was reminded of his learning.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּעִנְיַן צִיוּוּי הַתּוֹרָה בַּמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁתְּהֵא אֵימָתוֹ עָלֶיךָ, אֵין הַכַּוָּונָה אֵימַת בָּשָׂר וָדָם כִּפְשׁוּטֵיהּ

And the matter of the Torah’s command regarding a king, that “his awe be upon you” (Sanhedrin 22a)599Sanhedrin 22a: On “you shall surely set a king over you” (Devarim 17:15): that his awe be upon you [she-tehei eimaso alecha]., does not mean the awe of flesh-and-blood in its plain sense,
דְּעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר ״מִי אַתְּ וַתִּירְאִי מֵאֱנוֹשׁ יָמוּת״ וְגוֹמֵר

for regarding that it says, “who are you, that you fear a mortal man” (Yeshayahu 51:12)600Yeshayahu 51:12: “אָנֹכִי אָנֹכִי הוּא מְנַחֶמְכֶם, מִי אַתְּ וַתִּירְאִי מֵאֱנוֹשׁ יָמוּת” — “I, I am He who comforts you; who are you, that you fear a mortal man.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the awe a king of Israel commands is not the fear of flesh-and-blood — of that it says “who are you, that you fear a mortal man” — but a fear drawn from the Kingship of Heaven, for “the kingship of a king of Israel is drawn from the Kingship of Heaven.”;
רַק דְּמֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַלְכוּתוֹ נִמְשֶׁכֶת מִמַּלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם
rather, the kingship of a king of Israel is drawn from the Kingship of Heaven,
וְכַיָּדוּעַ דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה הוּא מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת דְּהָיָה דָּבוּק בְּמִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּכְטַעַם ״וַיֵּשֶׁב שְׁלֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּא ה׳״

and as is known, the rung of David HaMelech is the trait of Malchus, [for] he was bound to the trait of His kingship — in the sense of “and Shlomo sat on the throne of Hashem” (Divrei HaYamim I 29:23).601R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayera §1): “"The Holy One created His world only that they should fear before Him," as it says, "and God has made it so that they should fear before Him" — and this is the revelation of the glory of His kingship, as in "you shall surely set a king over you" — that his awe be upon you — which is the Name Adnus: "and if I am Master, where is My fear?"” Exactly the se’if: the awe of a king is not the dread of flesh and blood but the revealed glory of the Kingship of Heaven, drawn down through Malchus.
וְעַל כֵּן מְבָרְכִין ״שֶׁחָלַק מִכְּבוֹדוֹ לִירֵאָיו״ עַל כָּל מֶלֶךְ מִמַּלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יִהְיֶה אֵיזֶה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה
And therefore one recites the blessing “that He has apportioned of His glory to those who fear Him” over any king of Israel, whoever he may be;
דִּבְהֶכְרֵחַ מִצַּד הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁשּׁוֹפֵעַ עָלָיו מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ אֲשֶׁר בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה, דְּמִכֹּחָהּ זָכָה לְמַלְכוּת
for necessarily, from the side of kingship, the trait of His kingship “which rules over all” flows upon him — for by its power he attained kingship —
מַקִּיפָתּוֹ יִרְאָה גְּדוֹלָה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִמִּדָּה זוֹ כַּיָּדוּעַ בַּזֹּהַר

[and so] a great fear, drawn from this trait, encompasses him, as is known in the Zohar.602R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Hashanah §17): “"Zachor" corresponds to the brain on the right, and there is the place of remembering — yet even in the brain, in which there is memory, forgetting can still occur at distant intervals. But "Zachor" that is [the rung] beyond — "in which there is no forgetting and forgetting does not abide" — as it says, "there is no forgetting before the Throne of Your glory"… then there is no forgetting at all whatsoever.” Exactly the se’if: ordinary memory can lapse, but what is fixed by fear is bound to a rung where forgetting has no foothold.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי [לְעֵיל סִימָן ב׳] דְּעַל כֵּן מֶלֶךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁכָּרַע (בִּתְפִלַּת עֲמִידָה, בְּרָכוֹת לד:) שׁוּב אֵינוֹ זוֹקֵף מִצַּד תּוֹקֶף הַיִּרְאָה

And as I wrote [above, in siman 2], that therefore a king, once he has bowed [in the Amidah] (Berachos 34b)603Berachos 34b: “A king, once he has bowed [in the Amidah], does not straighten up again until he finishes the entire prayer [melech, keivan she-kara, shuv eino zokef].”, does not straighten up again — from the intensity of [his] fear.
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה שֶׁהוּא רֶגֶל רְבִיעִית דְּמֶרְכָּבָה, שֹׁרֶשׁ לְמִידָה זוֹ, כָּל הָרוֹאֵהוּ מִסְתַּלֵּק מִמֶּנּוּ הַשִּׁכְחָה לְגַמְרֵי
And David HaMelech — the “fourth leg of the Merkavah,” the root of this trait — whoever beheld him, forgetting departed from him entirely.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנִּזְכָּר לְתַלְמוּדוֹ, דְּדָרְשׁוּ מִמִּלַּת ״וְטוֹב״, דְּאֵין ״טוֹב״ אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה
And this is [the meaning of] “he was reminded of his learning,” which they expounded from the word “and good [tov]” — for “good” is nothing but Torah,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּמְנָחוֹת נג:]604Menachos 53b: “Let the good one come and receive the good, from the Good, for the good ones”: “the good one” — Moshe; “the good” — the Torah, as it says “for I have given you a good teaching [lekach tov]” (Mishlei 4:2); “the Good” — the Holy One; “the good ones” — Israel. ״מִקְרָא דְּלֶקַח טוֹב״
as they said [in Menachos 53b] from the verse “a good teaching [lekach tov]” (Mishlei 4:2);
דְּמִשְׁלֵי דִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה גִּילָּה שֵׁם זֶה לַתּוֹרָה, וְכֵן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה אָמַר ״טוֹב לִי תוֹרַת פִּיךָ״

for Shlomo HaMelech’s Mishlei revealed this “name” for the Torah, and likewise David HaMelech said, “the Torah of Your mouth is good to me” (Tehillim 119:72)605Tehillim 119:72: “טוֹב לִי תוֹרַת פִּיךָ מֵאַלְפֵי זָהָב וָכָסֶף” — “the Torah of Your mouth is good to me, more than thousands of gold and silver.” R’ Tzadok’s use: David HaMelech named the Torah “tov” (good) — for “tov” essentially alludes to the tzaddik, “one of good deeds, fenced-in with fear of Heaven”; hence “there is no tov but Torah,” and merely to behold such a tzaddik (David) restores one’s own Torah to memory.Sefat Emet parallel - Eikev 24:3: Sefat Emet's phrase "yirah otiyot re'iyah" gives a precise Chassidic frame for R. Tzadok's use of techeiles, seeing, remembering, and fear. He explains that the bond with Hashem is already planted within Israel, but the physical covering blocks its disclosure; yirah is the key that opens the gates of moach and lev and allows a person to see the truth. This makes "u-re'isem oto u-zekhartem" more than a mnemonic technique. Holy sight generates yirah, and yirah in turn fixes what is seen within the heart so that it is not lost to forgetfulness. R. Tzadok's claim that what truly enters the heart is not forgotten follows naturally: forgetting is a sign that the knowledge remained external, while yirah converts perception into an inward orientation. The techeiles-thread thus stands at the boundary between revealed sight and hidden memory. One sees a finite physical sign, but the purpose is to awaken a fear that opens the heart to the infinite Divine reality toward which the sign points..
דְּעִיקַּר שֵׁם ״טוֹב״ רֶמֶז לְצַדִּיק כְּטַעַם אָמְרוּ ״צַדִּיק כִּי טוֹב״ כַּנּוֹדָע
For the name tov essentially alludes to the tzaddik, in the sense of “say of the tzaddik that he is good,” as is known —
וְהַיְינוּ בַּעַל מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים וְגָדוּר בְּיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
that is, one of good deeds, “fenced-in” with fear of Heaven. — so that merely to behold such a one is itself a lesson, jogging the beholder’s own Torah back into memory.

items.h: The theme: The Written Torah (“Toras Hashem”) is the “study of the deed”; the Oral Torah (“toraso — his own Torah”) is the essence of Torah’s greatness — chiddushei Torah, which Hashem “loves — the gates of Zion distinguished in halachah.” Given as an outright gift (“no longer in Heaven”), it lets a person grasp the “body of the King.” Its root is in Yehudah/David (“Malchus = the mouth = Torah she-be’al peh”); hence Boaz/Rus and the “mechokek.”

p: [כא] וְנוֹדָע דַּחֲלוּקִים בְּכָל מָקוֹם בַּעֲלֵי תוֹרָה וּבַעֲלֵי מִצְווֹת
And it is known that everywhere a distinction is drawn between “masters of Torah” and “masters of mitzvos,”
כִּי הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לִהְיוֹת כָּל כָּךְ בַּעַל מִצְווֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים מִפְּנֵי שְׁקִידָתוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה
for one immersed in Torah cannot be so much a “master of mitzvos and good deeds,” on account of his diligence in Torah;
אֶלָּא דְּהַתּוֹרָה עַצְמָהּ הִיא כּוֹלֶלֶת כָּל טוֹב
except that the Torah itself comprises all good.
וְאוּלָם עִנְיַן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת ״תּוֹרַת ה׳״ אֵינָהּ אֶלָּא לִימּוּד הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
However, the matter of the Written Torah, which is called “the Torah of Hashem,” is nothing but the “study of the deed”;
וּמִצַּד זֶה מַעֲשֶׂה גָּדוֹל שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר הַמְכֻוָּן

and from this side, “deed is great,” being the essential intent (cf. Kiddushin 40b)606Kiddushin 40b: “R’ Tarfon and the Elders were [asked]: Which is greater, study or action? R’ Akiva answered: Study is greater — for study leads to action [talmud gadol, she-meivi lidei maaseh].”.
אֲבָל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַנִּקְרָא ״תּוֹרָתוֹ״ זֶהוּ עִיקַּר גְּדוּלַּת הַתּוֹרָה
But the Oral Torah, which is called “his [own] Torah,” is the essential greatness of Torah,

דְּ״כָל חֲפָצִים לֹא יִשְׁווּ בָהּ״ אֲפִילּוּ חֶפְצֵי שָׁמַיִם [– מִצְווֹת, מו״ק ט:]607Moed Katan 9b: The Sages reconciled “all your desires [chafatzecha] cannot equal her” (implying heavenly matters can equal Torah) with “all desirable things [chafatzim] cannot equal her” (implying even heavenly matters cannot): the one speaks of a mitzvah that can be performed by others [there Torah study takes precedence], the other of a mitzvah that cannot be performed by others [which takes precedence over Torah study].
for “all desirable things cannot equal it” (Mishlei 3:15) — even “the desires of Heaven,” i.e. mitzvos (Moed Katan 9b);
וְ״אוֹהֵב ה׳ שַׁעֲרֵי צִיּוֹן הַמְצוּיָּינִים בַּהֲלָכָה״ מִכָּל מִשְׁכְּנוֹת יַעֲקֹב

and “Hashem loves the gates of Zion, distinguished in halachah, more than all the dwellings of Yaakov” (Berachos 8a on Tehillim 87:2)608Berachos 8a: “R’ Chiya bar Ami said in the name of Ulla: Since the day the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed, the Holy One has in His world only the four cubits of halachah alone” — for “Hashem loves the gates [of Tzion] distinguished in halachah [ha-metzuyanim ba-halachah] more than all the synagogues and houses of study” (on Tehillim 87:2, “Hashem loves the gates of Tzion more than all the dwellings of Yaakov”). —
הַכֹּל הוּא עַל חִידּוּשִׁין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
all of this refers to chiddushei Torah in the Oral Torah,
שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמַר ״לֶקַח טוֹב נָתַתִּי לָכֶם״
of which He said, “a good teaching [lekach tov] I have given you” (Mishlei 4:2),
הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁנָּתַתִּי מַתָּנָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל דְּ״לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִיא״ מֵעַתָּה

that is, what I gave as a “gift” to Israel — that “it is no longer in Heaven” (Devarim 30:12)609Devarim 30:12: “לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא לֵאמֹר מִי יַעֲלֶה לָּנוּ הַשָּׁמַיְמָה…” — “it is not in Heaven, that you should say, ‘who will ascend to Heaven for us and get it for us’…” R’ Tzadok’s use: the Oral Torah was given to Israel as an outright “gift” — “it is no longer in Heaven”; hence chiddushei Torah are man’s own, and (as the Gemara has it) the halachah can even follow the earthly sages against the Heavenly Academy..
וּמְתִיבְתָּא דִּרְקִיעַ נֶחְלְקוּ עִם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בַּהֲלָכָה [בְּהַפּוֹעֲלִים]
And [thus] the Heavenly Academy disputed with the Holy One in halachah [in Perek HaPo’alim, Bava Metzia 86a],
וּפָסַק הָרַמְבַּ״ם שָׁם הֲלָכָה כִּמְתִיבְתָּא דִּרְקִיעַ, וְלָקְחוּ לְוִיכּוּחַ חָכָם מֵהַאי עָלְמָא דַּוְקָא

and the Rambam ruled there that the halachah follows the Heavenly Academy, and they took a sage specifically from this world to decide the dispute610Bava Metzia 86a: They were disputing in the Heavenly Academy: “if the bright spot [baheres] preceded the white hair — impure; and if the white hair preceded the bright spot — pure. [In a case of] doubt — the Holy One says ‘pure,’ and all the Heavenly Academy say ‘impure.’” They said, “who shall decide? — Rabbah bar Nachmani, for he declared, ‘I am unique in [the laws of] nega’im, I am unique in [the laws of] ohalos.’” They sent the Angel of Death to bring him — [For the Torah’s ruling belongs to the sages of this world.] —
כִּי כְּבָר נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לַתַּחְתּוֹנִים מַתָּנָה גְּמוּרָה שֶׁנִּקְרָא ״תּוֹרָתָם״

for the Torah had already been given to those below as an outright gift, which is called “their [own] Torah.”611R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §17): “"Torah preceded the world" — that is the Written Torah… but the Oral Torah has no relation except to Israel, and therefore it was not written down; and therefore, "by the mouth of these words I have made a covenant with you" — and they expounded [Shemos Rabbah], upon the things that are oral, that they are a covenant and a bond with Israel in particular.” Exactly the se’if: the Oral Torah is “their own Torah,” a gift bound to Israel alone — which is why it is no longer in Heaven and why it lets a person grasp “the body of the King.”
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה הוּא נִקְרָא ״טוֹב״, דְּהוּא עֶצֶם הַטּוֹב הַכּוֹלְלוּת כָּל טוֹב שֶׁבְּכָל מִינֵי מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים
And from this side it is called “good” — for it is the very essence of good, comprising all the good in every kind of good deed.
וְזֶה טַעַם ״טוֹב לִי״ וְגוֹמֵר ״מֵאַלְפֵי זָהָב וָכָסֶף״
And this is the meaning of “the Torah of Your mouth is good to me — more than thousands of gold and silver” (Tehillim 119:72),
וְכֶסֶף הֵם אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה כַּנּוֹדָע
“gold and silver” being love and fear, as is known.
וְ״אַלְפֵי״ הוּא תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And “thousands” [alpei] is the ultimate perfection [attainable] in this world,
דְּכָל בִּרְכָאן דְּהַאי עָלְמָא הוּא בְּמִסְפַּר ״אֶלֶף״ שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד עוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה
for all the blessings of this world are in the count of “a thousand,” which corresponds to the World of Asiyah;
כִּי הַמִּסְפָּרִים יְחִידוֹת עֲשִׂירִיּוֹת מֵאוֹת אֲלָפִים הֵם נֶגֶד אַרְבַּע עוֹלָמוֹת אבי״ע [אֲצִילוּת בְּרִיאָה יְצִירָה עֲשִׂיָּה]

for the [orders of] number — units, tens, hundreds, thousands — correspond to the Four Worlds, ABiYA (Atzilus, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah).612R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Acharei Mos §5): “the Written Torah is "Torah that issues from Chochmah"… and included within them is the Oral Torah, which is from the dew of Atika, from Keser — which is above the brain.” Exactly the se’if’s ranking: the Written Torah is the “study of the deed” drawn from Wisdom, while the Oral Torah is rooted higher than the mind that receives it — which is why it, and not the Written, is “the essence of Torah’s greatness.”
וְ״תּוֹרַת פִּיךָ״ הַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, דְּ״מַלְכוּת פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ״

And “the Torah of Your mouth” is the Oral Torah, for “Malchus is the ‘mouth’ — we call it the Oral Torah”613Tikkunei Zohar (the “Patach Eliyahu” introduction): “Malchus — [the] ‘mouth,’ Torah she-be’al peh [the Oral Torah] we call it.” R’ Tzadok’s use: since Malchus is the “mouth,” the “Torah of Your mouth” (Toras picha) is the Oral Torah — David’s own rung (Malchus), and he is the root of the Oral Torah; hence “good to me” (David) specifically.;
וְהַיְינוּ ״טוֹב לִי״ דַּוְקָא, שֶׁזֶּהוּ דַּרְגָּא דִּידֵיהּ, וְהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ לְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה

and this is precisely “good to me” — for this is [David’s] own rung, and he is the root of the Oral Torah.614R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §184): “The beginning of [engaging in] words of Torah is the longing [cheishek], as it says, ‘in the Torah of Hashem is his desire’ — and then it is called ‘the Torah of Hashem’; and afterward comes the attainment, called ‘and in his [own] Torah he meditates’ [u’ve-soraso yehgeh] (Avodah Zarah 19a) — and [there] the longing is greater still.” (The Written Torah is “the Torah of Hashem”; through longing and toil it becomes toraso — the learner’s own.)
וְזֶה טוֹב מִכָּל עֲבוֹדַת הָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּאַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה שֶׁהֵם רַק גַּדְפִין
And this [Oral Torah] is better than all of a person’s service in this world through love and fear — which are but “wings”;
אֲבָל ״מַאן דְּאָחִיד בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא שֶׁהוּא גּוּפָא דְּמַלְכָּא, אָחִיד בְּכוֹלָּא״
but “one who grasps the Torah, which is the ‘body of the King,’ grasps everything” (Zohar).
וַאֲחִיזָה הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ הִתְאַחֲדוּת הָאָדָם בַּתּוֹרָה
And [true] “grasping” is only through the Oral Torah, which is the [personal] union of the person with the Torah;
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִקְרָא ״תּוֹרָתוֹ״ דְּהַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁהוּא מְחַדֵּשׁ
through this it is called “his [own] Torah” — that is, what he innovates —
דְּזֶהוּ עִיקַּר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, מַה שֶּׁכָּל תַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה

for this is the essence of the Oral Torah: “whatever a seasoned student will one day innovate” in words of Torah (Yerushalmi Peah 2:4)615Yerushalmi Peah 2:4: “Even that which a seasoned student [talmid vasik] is destined to teach one day before his master was already said to Moshe at Sinai.”Kedushas Levi — the Oral Torah is the gift of Israel’s own chiddush: Kedushas Levi, Yisro §22, describes the two Torahs in a manner remarkably close to this se’if. Torah shebiksav was entrusted through Moshe in fixed written form, whereas Torah shebe’al peh includes the interpretation transmitted to Moshe together with “כל שתלמיד ותיק עתיד לחדש.” He then draws the consequence: Hashem gave Israel such authority out of His love and choice of them that, according to the Torah as the tzaddikim of the generation truly interpret it, so the Divine order is conducted. This does not mean that a chacham invents a second Torah detached from Sinai; the very novelty he uncovers was rooted at Sinai, yet it becomes “his Torah” only through the labor of his own mind and heart. That formulation sharpens R’ Tzadok’s distinction here. The greatness of Torah shebe’al peh is precisely that the received Divine word becomes a personal acquisition without ceasing to be Divine. “Lo bashamayim hi” is therefore not a distancing of Torah from Heaven but the completion of the matanah: Heaven wills that the earthly chacham grasp, interpret, and decide. In this sense the talmid’s chiddush is the point at which the gift is fully received — the Torah is no longer merely before him as Toras Hashem, but lives within him as toraso.;
וּכְשֶׁמַּשִּׂיג הַחִידּוּשִׁים הַשַּׁיָּיכִים לְחֶלְקוֹ הֲרֵי זֶה אָחִיד בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא
and when one attains the innovations that belong to his [soul-]portion, he is [truly] “grasping the Torah.”
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ ז״ל (רות רבה ג, ז) עַל פָּסוּק ״וַיִּיטַב לִבּוֹ״ בְּבֹעַז דְּעָסַק בַּתּוֹרָה גַּם כֵּן מִלְּשׁוֹן ״וַיִּיטַב״

And therefore the Sages said (Rus Rabbah)616Rus Rabbah (on Rus 3:7): “‘And his heart was good [va-yitav libo]’ (Rus 3:7) — [it is expounded] that Boaz occupied himself with words of Torah [before eating and drinking].” (The “goodness of the heart” is the attainment of the Oral Torah that lies in the heart of each one.) on the verse “and his heart was good [va-yitav]” (Rus 3:7) regarding Boaz — that he [also] engaged in Torah, [derived] too from the term “va-yitav”;
וְטוֹבָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב הוּא הַשָּׂגַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁבַּלֵּב כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
and the “goodness in the heart” is the attainment of the Oral Torah that is in the heart of each and every one,
דְּשָׁם הוּא עִיקַּר הַשָּׂגַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, כְּטַעַם לְשׁוֹן רַז״ל ״אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי פְּלוֹנִי״
for there [in the heart] is the essential attainment of the Oral Torah — as in the Sages’ expression, “according to the view of Rabbi so-and-so.”
וְאָז נִזְדַּמְּנָה לוֹ רוּת הַנִּקְרֵאת ״אִמָּהּ שֶׁל מַלְכוּת״
And then Rus — called “the mother of royalty” — became available to him [Boaz];
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן ״יְהוּדָה מְחוֹקְקִי״, וְגַם מִמֶּנּוּ ״מְחוֹקֵק מִבֵּין רַגְלָיו״

and therefore [it says] “Yehudah is my lawgiver [mechokeki]” (Tehillim 60:9)617Tehillim 60:9: “לִי גִלְעָד וְלִי מְנַשֶּׁה… יְהוּדָה מְחֹקְקִי” — “Gilad is mine and Menasheh is mine… Yehudah is my lawgiver [mechokeki].” R’ Tzadok’s use: the “lawgiver” (mechokek) — the authority of the Oral Torah — is rooted in Yehudah/David; so too “a lawgiver from between his feet” issues from him, the Oral Torah whose root is in the seed of Yehudah., and also “the lawgiver from between his feet” (Bereishis 49:10)618Bereishis 49:10: “לֹא יָסוּר שֵׁבֶט מִיהוּדָה וּמְחֹקֵק מִבֵּין רַגְלָיו, עַד כִּי יָבֹא שִׁילֹה” — “the scepter shall not depart from Yehudah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh comes” (Yaakov’s blessing to Yehudah). R’ Tzadok’s use: the “mechokek” of Yehudah is the attainment of the Oral Torah, whose root was in the seed of Yehudah — the line that produced Boaz, Rus (“the mother of royalty”), and David. [comes] from him —
בְּהַשָּׂגַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה דְּשָׁרְשָׁהּ הָיָה בְּזַרְעָא דִּיהוּדָה

in the attainment of the Oral Torah, whose root was in the seed of Yehudah. — the true crown of Torah being not the received text but the innovation a soul draws out from within it, which is uniquely its own.

items.h: The theme: Shlomo first made “handles” for the Torah — a handhold to grasp its depths through the Binah of the heart, not the Written Torah’s surface alone (“revealed and sealed”). All the Torah of this world is still “hevel” before the Torah of Mashiach — not disparagement, but the “seven hevalim”: like the vapor that carries the taste of the dish, or the breath that holds the hidden letters of speech. Olam ha-zeh is the revealed “world of falsehood”; its truth is utterly concealed.

p: [כב] וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה הוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁעָשָׂה אָזְנַיִם לַתּוֹרָה
And Shlomo HaMelech was the first to “make handles [oznayim] for the Torah,”
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל (עירובין כא:) דְּהָיְתָה כְּקוּפָּה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ אָזְנַיִם

as the Sages said (Eruvin 21b)619Eruvin 21b: “Rava expounded (on Koheles 12:9), ‘and beyond [that], Koheles [Shlomo] was wise, he also taught the people knowledge’ — he made ‘handles’ [oznaim, ear-loops] for the Torah [asa’ah k’min oznaim la-Torah].” (By ordinances such as eruvin and washing the hands, he gave the Torah “handles” by which to grasp it.) that [before him] it was “like a basket that has no handles” [nothing to grasp it by].
הַיְינוּ בֵּית אֲחִיזָה לִהְיוֹת ״אָחִיד בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא״

That is, a “handhold” by which to “grasp the Torah,”620R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash §4): “"from the day the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed, the Holy One has nothing in His world but the four amos of halachah alone"; and likewise before the Beis HaMikdash was built there were also the four amos of halachah — that is, the holiness of Israel in its completeness.” This grounds the se’if’s “handles”: when the revealed House is absent, the only handhold on the Torah’s depths is the halachah grasped by the heart.
דְּזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק עַל יְדֵי הַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב וְהַשָּׂגָתוֹ בַּבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַתּוֹרָה
which is possible only through the feeling of the heart and its apprehension by the Binah of the heart in the depths of the Torah,
וְלֹא מִצַּד יְדִיעַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב לְבַד דִּכְתִיבָה וּמַנְּחָא
and not from the knowledge of the Written Torah alone, which “is written and set down,”
דְּהִיא ״גָּלוּי וְסָתוּם״
for it is “revealed and [yet] sealed”:
הַיְינוּ גִּילּוּי מִצַּד הַנִּגְלֶה אֲבָל מַעֲמַקֶּיהָ סְתוּמִים וַחֲתוּמִים מְאוֹד
revealed on its outer side, but its depths exceedingly closed and sealed;
וְרַק ״אִישׁ תְּבוּנָה יִדְלֶנָּה״

and only “a man of understanding draws it up” (Mishlei 20:5)621Mishlei 20:5: “מַיִם עֲמֻקִּים עֵצָה בְלֶב אִישׁ, וְאִישׁ תְּבוּנָה יִדְלֶנָּה” — “counsel in the heart of a man is [like] deep waters, but a man of understanding draws it up.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the depths of the Torah are “revealed and yet sealed,” reached only by the Binah of the heart — “a man of understanding draws it up,” having the inner faculty to “join rope to rope” and reach the depths, as the Sages said of Shlomo.,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ בִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב ״לְסַפֵּק חֶבֶל בְּחֶבֶל״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל עַל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה

one who has the Binah of the heart to “join rope to rope” [to reach the depths], as the Sages said of Shlomo HaMelech.622R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Ki Tisa §3): “that at the hour of the Giving of the Torah all Israel were fit for the crown of priesthood… angels came and bound upon them two crowns — one corresponding to "we shall do" and one corresponding to "we shall hear."” Exactly the se’if: the crowns are conferred as a set, each answering to a distinct faculty — which is why Torah, kingship and priesthood stand as three, with the priestly crown drawn from above them.
וְכָל תּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה ״הֶבֶל״ הוּא עֲדַיִין בִּפְנֵי תּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל (קהלת רבה יא)

And all the Torah of this world is still “vapor [hevel]” before the Torah of Mashiach, as the Sages said (Koheles Rabbah 11:8)623Koheles Rabbah 11:8: “The Torah that a person learns in this world is ‘vapor’ [hevel] before the Torah of Mashiach.”.
לְשׁוֹן ״הֶבֶל״ אֵינוֹ גְּנַאי, כִּי הוּא בְּסוֹד שִׁבְעָה הֲבָלִים שֶׁאָמַר קֹהֶלֶת עַל כָּל עִנְיָינֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה

The term “hevel” is no disparagement, for it belongs to the secret of the “seven hevalim” that Koheles pronounced624Koheles 1:2: “הֲבֵל הֲבָלִים אָמַר קֹהֶלֶת, הֲבֵל הֲבָלִים הַכֹּל הָבֶל” — “vanity of vanities, said Koheles; vanity of vanities, all is hevel [vapor].” The Sages count seven expressions of “hevel” in this verse (Koheles Rabbah 1:2), corresponding to the seven lower middos and the “days of building.” R’ Tzadok’s use: “hevel” is no disparagement — this world is the “vapor” (hevel) rising from the pot, which carries the taste of the dish still cooking; a true “sample” of the enduring World to Come. over all the matters of this world,
כּוּלָּם הַנִּכְלָלִים בְּשֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת וְשִׁבְעָה יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן
all of which are comprised in the seven [lower] middos and the “seven days of building.”
וְהַכֹּל הוּא דּוּגְמַת הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא הַקַּיָּם לָעַד
And all of it is a “sample” of the World to Come, which endures forever;
רַק שֶׁעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא דּוּגְמַת הַהֶבֶל הַיּוֹצֵא מֵהַקְּדֵירָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ טַעַם הַתַּבְשִׁיל
only that this world is like the “vapor” rising from the pot, which carries the taste of the dish,
אוֹ הַהֶבֶל הַיּוֹצֵא מֵהַפֶּה בְּעֵת הַדִּבּוּר, דְּגַם בַּהֶבֶל כָּלוּל אוֹתִיּוֹת הַדִּבּוּר אֲבָל בְּהֶעְלֵם עָצוּם מְאוֹד שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה כְּלָל

or the “breath” that issues from the mouth in speech — for even in the breath the letters of speech are contained, but in exceedingly deep concealment, not revealed at all.625R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §59): “for this is the foundation of creation — that there be concealment and not complete clarification, such that it cannot be denied — in order that there be room for choice.” Exactly the se’if’s olam ha-zeh: the “world of falsehood” is not an accident of this world but its very design; its truth must stay hidden, or choice itself would be impossible.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא עוֹלָם הַנִּגְלֶה וְנִרְאֶה לַעֵין וּמַרְאִין עָלָיו בְּאֶצְבַּע בְּמִלַּת ״זֶה״
And even though this world is the revealed world, seen by the eye, “pointed to with a finger” by the word “zeh” (this),
הִנֵּה מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁלּוֹ נִקְרָא עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ שְׁקָרִים
nonetheless, from the side of its [outer] manifestation it is called “the world of falsehood,” which is all falsehoods,
וְהָאֱמֶת שֶׁבּוֹ שֶׁהִשְׁלִיךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אַרְצָה הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם

and the truth within it — which Hashem “cast to the earth” (Daniel 8:12)626Daniel 8:12: “וְצָבָא תִּנָּתֵן עַל הַתָּמִיד בְּפָשַׁע, וְתַשְׁלֵךְ אֱמֶת אַרְצָה, וְעָשְׂתָה וְהִצְלִיחָה” — “and a host was set over the daily [offering] through transgression, and it cast truth to the ground, and it acted and prospered.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this world is “the world of falsehood,” for the truth within it — which Hashem “cast to the earth” — is in utter concealment; even the Torah’s full truth is disclosed now only as a faint “vapor” of the Torah of Mashiach.Tanya — the Written Torah is revealed, yet its inner will remains sealed until Torah shebe’al peh: Tanya, Iggeres HaKodesh §29, explains that the ratzon ha-elyon clothed in the mitzvos of the Written Torah is itself “מופלא ומכוסה, טמיר ונעלם,” and becomes disclosed only through Torah shebe’al peh. His example is tefillin: the written verse commands “ukeshartam” and “totafos,” but leaves the concrete form, location, materials, dimensions, and details concealed until the Oral Torah interprets them. The same is true, he says, of all positive and negative commandments. This is a precise Chabad parallel to R’ Tzadok’s phrase that Torah shebiksav is at once “galui v’sasum.” Its words are exposed to every reader, yet the Divine will embedded in those words is not exhausted by their surface. Torah shebe’al peh supplies the “handle” by which the hidden content can actually be grasped and lived. The comparison also clarifies R’ Tzadok’s use of hevel. The revealed word is not false or deficient; like breath carrying unarticulated letters, it bears within itself an abundance not yet unfolded. The future Torah of Mashiach is therefore not a replacement of the present Torah, but the fuller disclosure of what its present letters already contain in concealment — the truth cast into this world becoming transparent rather than hidden beneath its outward form. — is in utter concealment.
וְאַף אַחַר שֶׁנָּתַן ״אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב״ — הַתּוֹרָה דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ ״אֱמֶת״ — הָאֲמִיתּוּת הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם
And even after He gave “truth to Yaakov” — the Torah, of which “truth” is written — the [full] truth remains in utter concealment;
וּמַה שֶּׁמִּתְגַּלֶּה לְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָאֲמִיתִּים בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דּוּגְמַת הַהֶבֶל הַיּוֹצֵא מִתּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ
and what is revealed to the true sages of Israel in every generation is but a “sample” of the “vapor” that issues from the Torah of Mashiach,
שֶׁהוּא יִהְיֶה שְׁלֵימוּת הַדִּבּוּר דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
which will be the [ultimate] perfection of “speech” — the Oral Torah. — so that even our sharpest insight today is only the faint vapor of a dish still cooking, whose full flavor waits for Mashiach.

items.h: The theme: After Levi (who brings the Written Torah down through Moshe) comes Yehudah — the perfection of the Oral Torah through Mashiach, who “inscribes it on the heart.” “Halachah” is the guidance of walking in this world (Levi and Yissachar), for a world that is “like a shadow.” In the Bais HaMikdash, conduct was by Torah-and-Prophets (revelation from Heaven); the full Oral Torah unfolds only later — man’s true chiddushim being concealed ru’ach ha-kodesh, yet reckoned as a human attainment.

p: [כג] וְעַל כֵּן אַחַר לֵוִי, שֶׁבּוֹ כָּלוּל כֹּחַ הוֹרָדַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב לָאָרֶץ עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה, נוֹלַד יְהוּדָה
And therefore, after Levi — in whom is comprised the power of bringing the Written Torah down to earth through Moshe Rabbeinu — Yehudah was born,
שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה עַל יְדֵי הַמָּשִׁיחַ
who is the perfection of the Oral Torah through Mashiach;
וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת כּוּלּוֹ כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד
and this is the ultimate perfection of all, as it will be in the Future.
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״יְהוּדָה מְחוֹקְקִי״, כִּבְיָכוֹל ״מְחוֹקֵק אוֹתִי״
And therefore he is called “Yehudah is my lawgiver [mechokeki]” — as it were, “who inscribes Me” —
כִּי ״אוֹרַיְיתָא וְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא חַד״

for “the Torah and the Holy One are one.”627“Oraysa v’Kudsha Brich Hu chad” — the Torah and the Holy One are one (Zohar; cf. Tanya, Likutei Amarim ch. 4): the Torah is not a mere instrument that God fashioned, but an emanation of His own wisdom and will, which are utterly one with Him. Background and meforshim: the Tanya (ch. 4) draws the contrast — a mortal king is grasped only through his garments and decrees, which are separate from him, whereas the Holy One “and His wisdom are one,” so that whoever grasps a halachah of the Torah thereby embraces God Himself; the Nefesh HaChaim (Sha’ar 4) develops the same principle at length. R’ Tzadok’s use: because “Oraysa v’Kudsha Brich Hu chad,” calling Yehudah “mechokeki” (“who inscribes Me”) is no mere figure of speech — to inscribe the Torah on the hearts of Israel is to inscribe the Divine Presence itself within them; this is the ultimate perfection of the Future.
וְהַחִיקּוּק דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּלִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לֶעָתִיד ״עַל לוּחַ לִבָּם אֶכְתְּבֶנָּה״ שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁכְּחוּ עוֹד

And the “inscribing” of the words of Torah upon the hearts of Israel — as it says of the Future, “upon the tablet of their heart I will write it” (cf. Yirmeyah 31:32)628Yirmeyah 31:32 (Sefaria 31:33): “כִּי זֹאת הַבְּרִית אֲשֶׁר אֶכְרֹת אֶת בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל אַחֲרֵי הַיָּמִים הָהֵם נְאֻם ה׳, נָתַתִּי אֶת תּוֹרָתִי בְּקִרְבָּם וְעַל לִבָּם אֶכְתְּבֶנָּה” — “for this is the covenant I shall make with the House of Israel after those days, says Hashem: I have set My Torah within them, and upon their heart I will write it.” Background: this is Yirmeyah’s prophecy of the “new covenant” of the Redemption — the Torah so internalized that, as the very next verse says, “they shall no longer teach one another… for they shall all know Me,” never again to be forgotten. Meforshim: R’ Tzadok’s wording “on the tablet of their heart” fuses this verse with Mishlei 3:3, “כָּתְבֵם עַל לוּחַ לִבֶּךָ” — “write them upon the tablet of your heart.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this future inscribing-upon-the-heart is the work of Yehudah/Mashiach — the perfected Oral Torah, engraved so deep within that it can never be forgotten., that they forget no more —
זֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי יְהוּדָה

this is through Yehudah.629R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §13): “The Oral Torah was not written down, for the Oral Torah is [the teacher’s] very heart — and what is in the heart cannot be written; as they said in Sanhedrin (35a).
