Only the mouth is ‘the pen of the heart,’ [and by it] one is able to bring [Torah] into the heart of his fellow and his student — for ‘words that come from the heart enter the heart.’” (Precisely the se’if’s picture of Yehudah/Mashiach who “inscribes the Torah on the heart”: the Oral Torah is by nature heart-written, passing living from heart to heart rather than from page to page.)
אֲבָל אַסּוֹקֵי שְׁמַעְתָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּהִלְכְתָא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְהִילּוּךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם
But the “drawing of a teaching to its halachic conclusion” in this world — for the “walking” of people —
דְּ״בְלֶכְתְּךָ״ הַיְינוּ בַּדֶּרֶךְ הַיְינוּ טִירְדָא דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
[relates to] “when you walk [by the way]” — which is the toil of this world —
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל (סוטה כא.) עַל פָּסוּק ״בְּהִתְהַלֶּכְךָ תַּנְחֶה אֹתָךְ״, דְּהַיְינוּ הִילּוּךְ דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה

and as the Sages said (Sotah 21a)630Sotah 21a: On “when you walk about, it shall lead you; when you lie down, it shall watch over you; and when you awake, it shall converse with you” (Mishlei 6:22): “‘when you walk about, it shall lead you’ — in this world; ‘when you lie down, it shall watch over you’ — in the grave; ‘and when you awake, it shall converse with you’ — in the World to Come.” on the verse “when you walk about, it shall lead you” (Mishlei 6:22), [referring] to the “walking” of this world;
וְזֶהוּ לְשׁוֹן ״הֲלָכָה״ שֶׁהוּא הַנְהָגַת הַהִילּוּךְ, הוּא בְּלֵוִי וְיִשָּׂשכָר

and this is the term “halachah,” which is “the conduct of walking” — [and] it is in Levi and Yissachar.631R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Lag BaOmer §2): “and on this they expounded, "the halichos [ways] of the world are His" — read not halichos but halachos; and it is not that the verse is being emended, but that the meaning of "halachos" is likewise from the term "halichos" — to know the ways of Hashem and to walk in them.” Exactly the se’if: “halachah” is the conduct of walking — the Torah of a world in which one must still move, step by step, through a shadow.
הַיְינוּ הַנְהָגָה דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְשֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַמּוּשָּׂגִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְצוֹרֶךְ הַנְהָגַת הָאָדָם בּוֹ
That is, the conduct of the Written and Oral Torah as grasped in this world, for the practical guidance of a person within it,
כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא ״כְּצֵל יָמֵינוּ עֲלֵי אָרֶץ״

in keeping with [the nature of this world, which is] “like our days, a shadow upon the earth” (Divrei HaYamim I 29:15)632Divrei HaYamim I 29:15: “כִּי גֵרִים אֲנַחְנוּ לְפָנֶיךָ וְתוֹשָׁבִים כְּכָל אֲבֹתֵינוּ, כַּצֵּל יָמֵינוּ עַל הָאָרֶץ וְאֵין מִקְוֶה” — “for we are strangers before You, and sojourners like all our fathers; our days upon the earth are like a shadow, and there is no hope [of escaping death].” Background: David’s public confession at the great assembly where Israel donated gold and silver for the future Beis HaMikdash — all wealth is truly God’s, and man is only a passing sojourner. Meforshim: Rashi (citing Midrash Koheles Rabbah 1:2) sharpens the image — our days are not even like the lasting shadow of a tree, nor like the momentary shadow of a bird in flight, but “like the shadow of a bee’s wings, which has wings yet casts no shadow at all”; and “there is no mikveh” means “there is none who has any hope that he will not die.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the shadow is but a “sample” and outline of the true form — the soul that endures into the World to Come; hence the guidance of this shadow-world is “halachah,” the conduct of “walking” through it..
כְּמוֹ הַצֵּל שֶׁהוּא דּוּגְמָא וְגָוֶון לְבַד מִצּוּרַת אָדָם הָאֲמִיתִּי שֶׁהוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַנִּשְׁאֶרֶת קַיֶּימֶת לְעוֹלָם הַבָּא
Like a shadow, which is but a “sample” and outline of the true form of the man — which is the soul that endures into the World to Come,
כַּנּוֹדָע דְּעָלֶיהָ הוּא עִיקַּר חֲלוּת שֵׁם ״אָדָם״
for, as is known, the name “adam” essentially applies to it [the soul];
אֲבָל הַגּוּף דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִקְרָא רַק ״בְּשַׂר אָדָם״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר, וְהוּא הַצָּרִיךְ הַגְדָּרָה
whereas the body of this world is called only “the flesh of a man,” as they said in the Zohar — and it is what requires “bounding-in” [halachic definition].
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״צַדִּיקִים יֵלְכוּ בָם״, דְּהַהֲלִיכַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְצַדִּיקִים הַמּוּגְדָּרִים עַל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם
And as it says, “the righteous walk in them” (Hoshea 14:10) — for the “walking” of this world in words of Torah is only for the righteous, who are “bounded-in” [disciplined] in their deeds.
וּבִזְמַן הַבַּיִת הָיָה עִיקַּר הַהַנְהָגָה עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וּנְבִיאִים, דְּהַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן הִתְגַּלּוּת מִשָּׁמַיִם
And in the time of the [First] Temple, the primary “conduct” was through the Written Torah and the Prophets — which is likewise a revelation from Heaven.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבָּאוּ דָּוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה וְחִידְּשׁוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כַּמָּה דְּבָרִים, עֲדַיִין הָיָה בְּמַדְרֵיגַת כְּתוּבִים
And even though David and Shlomo came and innovated many matters of Oral Torah, it was still at the level of “Kesuvim” [inspired Writings],
כִּי הַשָּׂגָה שֶׁלָּהֶם הוּא רְשִׁימוּ מִתּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
for their attainment is [but] an “impression” of the Torah of Mashiach [as it appears] in this world,
דְּאָז יַעֲשֶׂה ״אֱלֹקִים חֲדָשָׁה בָּאָרֶץ״ דְּ״נְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵב גָּבֶר״

for then “God will create a new thing on earth: a female shall encircle a male” (Yirmeyah 31:21)633Yirmeyah 31:21 (Sefaria 31:22): “עַד מָתַי תִּתְחַמָּקִין הַבַּת הַשּׁוֹבֵבָה, כִּי בָרָא ה׳ חֲדָשָׁה בָּאָרֶץ נְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵב גָּבֶר” — “how long will you hide yourself, O backsliding daughter? For Hashem has created a new thing on the earth: a female shall encircle a male.” Background: the prophet calls wayward Israel (“the backsliding daughter”) to return, promising a “new creation” — a reversal of the natural order. Meforshim: Rashi offers two readings — by the plain sense, the “female” (Israel) will court the “male” (the Holy One), going about to seek Him (in the idiom of Shir HaShirim 3:2, “I will seek him”); and in the name of R’ Yehudah HaDarshan, the “female” who until now takes only a small share like a daughter will in the end inherit everything “like a firstborn son who inherits all.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the future revelation in which the Oral Torah (Malchus, the “female”) will “encircle” and openly manifest — the receiving rung rising to be “felt to the eye” like the giver, no longer in concealment..
הַיְינוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה יִהְיֶה גַּם כֵּן מוּרְגָּשׁ לַעֵין
That is, the rung of the Oral Torah [Malchus] will then also be “felt to the eye” [openly revealed],
דְּהַכֹּל כְּמוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּהֶעְלֵם, וְהָאָדָם חוֹשֵׁב שֶׁהוּא מְחַדֵּשׁ דָּבָר בְּחָכְמָתוֹ
whereas [now] everything, as in this world, is in concealment, and a person thinks he is innovating something by his own wisdom —
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא בֶּאֱמֶת רוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ כָּל מַה שֶּׁהוּא מְחַדֵּשׁ דִּבְרֵי אֱמֶת
even though, in truth, all that he innovates of true words [of Torah] is ru’ach ha-kodesh,
דְּאִתְאַמְרָא הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי כְּוָותֵיהּ
for “the halachah was [already] stated to Moshe at Sinai in accordance with him,”
וּמִמַּה שֶּׁגִּילָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה כָּל מַה שֶּׁתַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ
and from what Hashem revealed to Moshe — “everything a seasoned student would one day innovate” —
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא נֶחְשָׁב לְהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם

nonetheless, in this world it is reckoned as a human attainment.634R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §77): “for even one who is fit for prophecy and ruach ha-kodesh receives it only by way of the greatest of the generation, as it says of the elders, "and I shall draw from the spirit that is upon you."” The se’if’s paradox exactly: a person’s true chiddushim are concealed ruach ha-kodesh, yet they come through a human channel and are therefore reckoned, in this world, as a human attainment.Kedushas Levi — when prophecy recedes, the light of Torah shebe’al peh begins to shine: Kedushas Levi, Homily for Purim §22, reads “kiyemu v’kiblu” as the historical turning-point from prophecy to the revealed flowering of the Oral Torah. Until Mordechai, he writes, “היה מאיר אור תורה שבכתב”; from Mordechai onward, as prophecy ceased, “התחיל להאיר אור תורה שבעל פה,” and the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah began to establish the order of prayer. His point is not that the earlier generations lacked an Oral tradition. Rather, while nevuah remained openly available, the dominant light descended from Above in a form that could be written as the word of the prophet; when that channel closed, the hidden light began to appear through Israel’s own interpretive labor. This complements R’ Tzadok’s Levi–Yehudah structure exactly. Levi/Moshe represents Torah brought down from Heaven; Yehudah/David/Mashiach represents the Torah engraved into the human heart and spoken from within it. The disappearance of open revelation is therefore also the condition for a new form of revelation: what appears to be the chacham’s own halachic judgment can carry concealed ruach ha-kodesh, while still being reckoned to him as genuine attainment and responsibility. The Divine voice has not vanished; it has entered the human mouth and heart deeply enough that the words can truly be called his Torah. — the chiddush feeling like one’s own discovery precisely because Heaven veils its hand, leaving man the dignity of “finding” what was in fact always given.

items.h: The theme: This world’s good is “stored away within it,” attained only through effort. In the Bais HaMikdash, with the Shechinah revealed, the Oral Torah did not yet spread; but the churban “cast down the glory of Israel,” bringing forgetting — and precisely through forgetting they had to delve deeper. So the Oral Torah expands with each generation’s concealment: Anshei Knesses HaGedolah, the greater spread of Bayis Sheni, and after its churban the Tannaim — “R’ Akiva’s eye saw what Moshe’s did not,” he being the “armor-bearer of Mashiach.”

p: [כד] וְזֶהוּ כָּל עִנְיַן עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דְּ״טוֹבִיָּה גָּנִיז בְּגַוֵּיהּ״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל

And this is the whole matter of this world — that “its good is stored away within it635“Toviah ganiz b’gaveih” — “its good is stored away within it”: R’ Tzadok cites this Aramaic dictum in the name of Chazal to define the very nature of this world — its good does not lie on the surface but is hidden deep within, disclosed only through a person’s own effort (as the se’if continues, “only through his effort does he choose the good”). Background and parallel: the same principle underlies the primordial light that the Holy One “stored away” (ganuz) for the righteous of the Future (Chagigah 12a) — the good is concealed precisely so that it must be quarried out by toil. R’ Tzadok’s use: this concealment is the engine of avodah, and therefore the deepened concealment that followed the churban (forgetting) does not diminish but expands the Oral Torah — each generation compelled to delve the more.,” as the Sages said —
שֶׁהוּא בִּגְנִיזָה וְהֶעְלֵם, וְרַק הָאָדָם מִצַּד הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ בּוֹחֵר בַּטּוֹב

that it is [present] in concealment and hiddenness, and only through a person’s own effort does he choose the good.636R’ Tzadok — parallel (Likutei Maamarim §12): “As it is written (Sanhedrin 37b), that ‘they are redeemed only through teshuvah’; and so with the Torah it says, ‘you toiled and you found,’ and ‘it is not in Heaven’ (Devarim 30:12) — but only in the hands of the Children of Israel, according to their toil and their grasp.” (This world’s good, like the depths of the Oral Torah, is “stored within it” and yielded only to effort.)637R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Soferim §36): “and so they said [Sanhedrin 24a], "He has set me in dark places" — this is the Talmud of Bavel; for the Talmud is the delving into the depths of the words of Torah, which is "deep — who can find it"… and because one must sink his thoughts deeply into it, thereby his every utterance becomes words of Torah — for wherever a person’s thought is engaged and cleaving, there he himself entirely is.” Exactly the se’if’s mechanism: the darkness of exile is not an obstacle to the Oral Torah but the very pressure that drives the delving.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּזְמַן הַבַּיִת שֶׁהָיָה גִּילּוּי שְׁכִינָה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים
Not so in the time of the [First] Temple, when there was a revelation of the Shechinah among the lower [worlds];
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא הָיָה אָז הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כָּל כָּךְ עַד אַחַר הַחוּרְבָּן
and therefore the Oral Torah did not spread so much then, [only] after the churban —
דְּ״הִשְׁלִיךְ מִשָּׁמַיִם תִּפְאֶרֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל״ הִיא הַתּוֹרָה דְּנִקְרֵאת כֵּן כַּנּוֹדָע

for “He cast down from heaven the glory [tiferes] of Israel” (Eichah 2:1)638Eichah 2:1: “אֵיכָה יָעִיב בְּאַפּוֹ אֲדֹנָי אֶת בַּת צִיּוֹן, הִשְׁלִיךְ מִשָּׁמַיִם אֶרֶץ תִּפְאֶרֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְלֹא זָכַר הֲדֹם רַגְלָיו בְּיוֹם אַפּוֹ” — “how the Lord in His anger has beclouded Bas Tziyon; He cast down from heaven to earth the glory [tiferes] of Israel, and did not remember His footstool on the day of His anger.” Background: the opening of the second kinah of Eichah — the churban, in which God hurled Israel’s glory down from its heavenly height. Meforshim: Rashi explains “from heaven to earth” — “after He had raised them up to the heavens, He cast them to the earth all at once, not little by little — from a high roof to a deep pit (mei-igra rama le-vira amikta)”; and “His footstool” is the Beis HaMikdash. R’ Tzadok reads “tiferes Yisrael” as the Torah (which is called tiferes, as is known), so the verse speaks of the Torah “cast down” — the onset of forgetting. R’ Tzadok’s use: the churban’s casting-down of the glory brought forgetting, and precisely that forgetting forced Israel to delve the deeper — so the Oral Torah expands with each generation’s concealment. — [namely,] the Torah, which is called thus, as is known —
״וְלֹא זָכַר הֲדוֹם [רַגְלָיו]״ וְגוֹמֵר, דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא הַשִּׁכְחָה
“and did not remember His footstool,” etc. — through which came forgetting;
וְעַל יְדֵי הַשִּׁכְחָה הוּצְרְכוּ לְהַעֲמִיק עִיּוּנָם יוֹתֵר בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה

and through the forgetting they were compelled to deepen their study the more in the words of Torah.639R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Mishpatim §1): “for in the Babylonian exile was the essential founding of the Oral Torah, through the Men of the Great Assembly… when Torah was forgotten from Israel, Ezra came up from Bavel and founded it… Hillel the Babylonian came up and founded it… and afterward, in the days of the Amoraim, the Babylonian Talmud, which is the essence of our Oral Torah.” Exactly the se’if’s law of expansion: each forgetting forced a deeper founding, and the Oral Torah grew by precisely what was lost.
וְכָל הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת הִתְגַּלּוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי הַשִּׁכְחָה וְהַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁנּוֹסָף בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר
And all the fresh unfolding of the Oral Torah comes about only through the forgetting and concealment added in each and every generation;
וְכָל מַה שֶּׁהַשִּׁכְחָה מִתּוֹסֶפֶת, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה מִתּוֹסֶפֶת, דְּצְרִיכִים לְהַעֲמִיק יוֹתֵר וּלְחַדֵּשׁ יוֹתֵר
and however much the forgetting increases, the Oral Torah increases [correspondingly], for they must delve deeper and innovate more.
וְאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה הֵם שֶׁהִתְחִילוּ לְיַיסֵּד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אַחַר חוּרְבָּן רִאשׁוֹן
And the Men of the Great Assembly are those who began to establish the Oral Torah after the First Destruction;
וְגַם בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי דְּלֹא שָׁרְתָה שְׁכִינָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל (יומא ט:), הָיָה הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה יוֹתֵר מִבְּבַיִת רִאשׁוֹן

and [even] in the Second Temple, in which the Shechinah did not rest, as the Sages said (Yoma 9b)640Yoma 9b: “The First Temple was destroyed because of three things — idolatry, illicit relations, and bloodshed; [but] the Second Temple, in which they were engaged in Torah and mitzvos and acts of kindness, was destroyed because of baseless hatred [sinas chinam] in it.” (So even without the resting of the Shechinah, the Second-Temple era saw the Oral Torah spread.), the Oral Torah spread more than in the First,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּפִרְקֵי הֵיכָלוֹת] דְּעִיקַּר זִיוָוהּ דְּתוֹרָה הָיָה בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי, וְיֵעָיֵין שָׁם בְּאֹרֶךְ כָּל לְשׁוֹנוֹ

as they said [in Pirkei Heichalos] that the essential “radiance” of the Torah was in the Second Temple — and see there, at length, its full wording.641Pirkei Heichalos (ch. 27–28): R’ Yishmael said in the name of R’ Akiva citing R’ Eliezer: from the day the Torah was given until the last Temple was built, “the Torah was given, but its splendor was not given” — its radiance, its might, and its glory were not given until the last Temple was built and the Shechinah rested within it. And there (ch. 28) [the Holy One said:] “I know what you seek — you seek abundant Torah, and long for a wealth of Talmud and many halachic traditions — to multiply halachos like the sand of the sea — and to establish yeshivos in the gates to expound what is forbidden and permitted” — and in the end the Holy One consented to their request. [The Torah’s full “radiance,” its Oral expansion, was granted with the Second Temple and increased in the generations after.]Tanya — galus and concealment create the work of halachic birur: Tanya, Iggeres HaKodesh §26, gives a conceptual explanation for the phenomenon R’ Tzadok traces historically. The Alter Rebbe identifies the exile of the Shechinah with Malchus being clothed in kelipas nogah, and says that precisely then “עיקר עסק התורה” is the labor of iyun and pilpul in halachah — separating permitted from forbidden and pure from impure. A halachah whose reason was previously hidden is, through the earthly scholar’s analysis, lifted out of the concealment that covered it. He adds that the supernal beings themselves come to hear the chiddushei Torah of those below, because only embodied human beings can perform this particular birur. Thus the darkness is not merely an unfortunate background against which Torah happens to survive. It creates the very task through which new depths of Torah are disclosed. This closely complements R’ Tzadok’s sequence from churban and forgetting to the increased expansion of Torah shebe’al peh. Forgetting forces a descent into difficulty, machlokes, kushya, and sustained analysis; but those are also the places where hidden chochmah is recovered. R’ Akiva’s superiority in certain depths to what Moshe initially apprehended is not a contradiction to Sinai: the later generation encounters layers of concealment that demand, and therefore elicit, forms of Torah disclosure that the earlier revealed order did not yet require.
וְאַחַר חוּרְבַּן בַּיִת שֵׁנִי נִתְרַחֲבָה עוֹד יוֹתֵר בְּדוֹרוֹת תַּנָּאִים וְאָמוֹרָאִים
And after the destruction of the Second Temple it broadened yet more, in the generations of the Tannaim and Amoraim,
עַד שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל [בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה] דְּרָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וַחֲבֵירָיו מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה

until the Sages said [in Vayikra Rabbah] that “the eye of R’ Akiva and his colleagues saw what the eye of Moshe did not see642Bamidbar Rabbah 19:6 (the sefer brackets it as “Vayikra Rabbah”; the extant midrash is Bamidbar Rabbah 19:6, and Midrash Tanchuma, Chukas 8): on the Parah Adumah, Hashem tells Moshe “to you I reveal the reason of the cow, but to others it is a chok,” adding that matters concealed now will be beheld in the Future — “דְּבָרִים שֶׁלֹּא נִגְלוּ לְמֹשֶׁה נִגְלוּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וַחֲבֵרָיו; וְכָל יְקָר רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ — זֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וַחֲבֵרָיו” — “things not revealed to Moshe were revealed to R’ Akiva and his colleagues; ‘and his eye beheld every precious thing’ (Iyov 28:10) — this is R’ Akiva and his colleagues.” Meforshim / source-note: the “eye that saw” is drawn from Iyov 28:10, “v’chol yakar ra’asah eino.” R’ Tzadok’s use: as concealment deepened after the churban, the later sages had to see “more” than the earlier — R’ Akiva, founder of the Oral Torah’s principles and details, perceived what even Moshe did not, for he was the “armor-bearer of Mashiach,” the vessels of whose Torah he prepared..”
וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הוּא הַמְיַיסֵּד כְּלָלֵי וּפְרָטֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אָז, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי דִּשְׁקָלִים]
And R’ Akiva is the founder of the general principles and particulars of the Oral Torah of that [era], as they said [in Yerushalmi Shekalim];
וְהוּא הָיָה נוֹשֵׂא כֵּלָיו דְּבֶן כּוֹזִיבָא, כִּי הוּא הַמּוּכָן לִהְיוֹת נוֹשֵׂא כֵּלָיו דְּמָשִׁיחַ
and he was the “armor-bearer” of Ben Koziva [Bar Kochba], for he was the one prepared to be the “armor-bearer” of Mashiach —
כִּי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהִשִּׂיג הוּא דּוּגְמַת כֵּלִים לְתוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ

for the Oral Torah that he attained is like the “vessels” for the Torah of Mashiach. — each churban, by deepening the concealment, forcing a deeper delving, so that the very loss becomes the engine of the Oral Torah’s growth.

items.h: The theme: Leah’s ceasing to bear (after Yehudah) is a concealment that prepares a deeper revelation — every birth is light, every pause is thirst. Zevulun (“in your going out”) is even greater than Yissachar: cleaving to Hashem even amid worldly affairs. Bnei mitzvos stand “beside” bnei Torah — a “shade.” David is Adam-David-Mashiach, the essential man who casts the shadow. The nations grasp only “a mountain” (revealed height); Israel is the inner “house” — the “ceiling” over the Shechinah.

p: [כה] וּלְכָךְ לֵאָה גַּם כֵּן עָמְדָה מִלֶּדֶת אַחַר לֵידַת יְהוּדָה
And therefore Leah, too, ceased bearing after the birth of Yehudah;
וְעַל יְדֵי זוֹ הָעֲמִידָה מִלֶּדֶת נַעֲשָׂה הֲכָנָה לְלֵידַת יִשָּׂשכָר
and through this ceasing to bear, a “preparation” was made for the birth of Yissachar,
שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כַּבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, לְהִילּוּךְ שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
who is the attainment of the Oral Torah [as] the Binah of the heart, for the “walking” in this world —
דְּהַיְינוּ אַלִּיבָּא דְּהִלְכְתָא הִילּוּךְ הַלֵּב בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
that is, “in accordance with the halachah,” the “walking” of the heart in this world.
וְכָל לֵידַת שְׁבָטִים הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר, וְהָעֲמִידָה מִלֶּדֶת הוּא הֶעְלֵם הַהִתְגַּלּוּת
And every birth of a tribe is a revelation of light, and the ceasing to bear is a concealment of the revelation;
וְעַל יְדֵי הַהֶעְלֵם, וּמִצִּמָּאוֹן שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ הַהֶעְלֵם, בָּא גִּילּוּי הַשָּׂגָה זוֹ לָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and through the concealment — and through the thirst that arises out of it — the revelation of this attainment comes into this world.
וְאָז אַחַר כָּךְ מִתְגַּלֶּה אוֹר דִּזְבוּלוּן, שֶׁהוּא כְּטַעַם ״כְּצֵל הַחָכְמָה בְּצֵל הַכֶּסֶף״

And then afterward the light of Zevulun is revealed, in the sense of “in the shade of wisdom, in the shade of money” (Koheles 7:12)643Koheles 7:12: “כִּי בְּצֵל הַחָכְמָה בְּצֵל הַכָּסֶף, וְיִתְרוֹן דַּעַת הַחָכְמָה תְּחַיֶּה בְעָלֶיהָ” — “for [to be] in the shade of wisdom is [to be] in the shade of money; and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its possessor.” Background: Koheles teaches that wisdom shelters a person much as wealth does — yet wisdom is the superior shelter, for it “gives life.” Meforshim: the commentators read the two clauses as a comparison — as money casts a protective “shade,” so does wisdom, and wisdom’s advantage is that “techayeh be’aleha,” it keeps its owner alive. R’ Tzadok’s use: the two shades are two rungs — the “shade of money” is Zevulun (the longing to serve God even amid worldly commerce), and the “shade of wisdom” is Yissachar’s Torah, the greater; in the World to Come it is disclosed that the mitzvos-masters’ service was but a “shade” beside the Torah-masters..
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הִקְדִּים זְבוּלוּן לְיִשָּׂשכָר ״בְּצֵאתְךָ וְיִשָּׂשכָר בְּאֹהָלֶיךָ״

And nonetheless [Moshe] placed Zevulun before Yissachar: “rejoice, Zevulun, in your going out, and Yissachar in your tents” (Devarim 33:18)644Devarim 33:18: “וְלִזְבוּלֻן אָמַר: שְׂמַח זְבוּלֻן בְּצֵאתֶךָ, וְיִשָּׂשכָר בְּאֹהָלֶיךָ” — “and of Zevulun he said: rejoice, Zevulun, in your going out, and Yissachar, in your tents.” Background: part of Moshe’s parting blessing to the tribes. Meforshim: Rashi (from Bereishis Rabbah 99) explains that Zevulun and Yissachar formed a partnership — Zevulun dwells at the seashore, sails out for commerce, and “puts food into the mouth of Yissachar,” who sits and toils in Torah; Moshe therefore placed Zevulun first, “for Yissachar’s Torah came about through Zevulun.” R’ Tzadok’s use: Zevulun’s “going out” — remaining cleaved to God even amid worldly affairs — is a greater level than Yissachar’s inwardness, hence its precedence; yet the essential wisdom is Yissachar’s, hidden in the heart, while Zevulun’s is the revealed joy, perceptible even to the nations.,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַדְרֵיגָה יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה, שֶׁגַּם בְּצֵאתוֹ בְּעִנְיָינֵי הָעוֹלָם יִהְיֶה דָּבוּק בֵּאלֹקִים חַיִּים וּמֶלֶךְ עוֹלָם

which is a greater level: that even in “going out” into worldly matters, one remains cleaving to the living God, the King of the world.645R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Masei §4): "“for you are coming to the land of Canaan” — in the Midrash: “what is Canaan? A land of commerce [perakmatya], in which they trade,” as you say, “whose merchants are princes.”" Exactly the se’if: the Land itself is named for commerce, so Zevulun’s worldly engagement is no descent from Yissachar’s tent but the appointed setting in which cleaving must be achieved.Sefas Emes — Zevulun carries Torah specifically into the place of ‘going out’: Sefas Emes, Sukkos 2:11, asks the obvious question on “שמח זבולון בצאתך”: why should Zevulun rejoice in the very portion that takes him away from the beis midrash into commerce? He answers that the joy and longing for Torah established before the departure protect the person after he has gone out. Even merchants who cannot remain occupied with Torah throughout the year can fix Torah in the heart so deeply that their worldly engagement does not become total forgetfulness. This is an especially apt complement to R’ Tzadok’s elevation of Zevulun above a merely sheltered spirituality. Yissachar’s holiness is visible in the tent; Zevulun’s test is whether the same inward bond survives “betzeisecha,” when attention is dispersed among markets, money, travel, and ordinary responsibility. The Sefas Emes makes the transition itself the avodah: a person goes outward while carrying an inward point that he refuses to abandon. Thus worldly occupation need not be a second, spiritually neutral life alongside Torah. When the departure is governed by prior attachment, the commerce becomes the arena in which Torah proves that it has entered the person rather than remaining only in his surroundings. This gives content to R’ Tzadok’s claim that true deveikus can be greater precisely amid the affairs of olam hazeh.646R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §224): “though in the second paragraph it afterward says "and you shall gather in your grain," from which they learned, "conduct with them the way of the world" — it is stated in the plural; and they said there, many did as R’ Shimon bar Yochai and it did not succeed for them, for it is impossible for the multitude and for the whole world to be like R’ Shimon bar Yochai.” Exactly the se’if’s Zevulun: worldly engagement is not a lesser concession but the appointed path of the many — and cleaving to God within it is the greater feat.
וְאַף עַל פִּי דְּ״טוֹב לִי תוֹרַת פִּיךָ מֵאַלְפֵי זָהָב וָכָסֶף״, שֶׁהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּצֵל הַכֶּסֶף דִּזְבוּלוּן
And even though “the Torah of Your mouth is good to me more than thousands of gold and silver” — which is the rung of the “shade of money” of Zevulun,
שֶׁהוּא הַכִּיסּוּפִין לַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ בְּצֵאתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דְּזֶהוּ עַסְקָן שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי מִצְווֹת
[the shade of money being] the longing for His service [even] in going out into this world — which is the “occupation” of the masters of mitzvos —
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (ויק״ר כה, ב) דְּעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַעֲשׂוֹת צֵל [וְחוּפּוֹת לְבַעֲלֵי הַמִּצְווֹת אֵצֶל בַּעֲלֵי תוֹרָה בְּגַן עֵדֶן] מִמִּקְרָא זֶה

as they said (Vayikra Rabbah 25:2)647Vayikra Rabbah 25:2: “R’ Huna and R’ Yirmiya said in the name of R’ Chiya bar Abba: In the Future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make shade and canopies [tzel va-chuppos] for the masters of mitzvos [baalei ha-mitzvos] beside the masters of Torah [bnei Torah] in Gan Eden — as one [verse teaches] (Koheles 7:12), ‘for in the shade of wisdom, in the shade of money.’” (So Zevulun’s “shade of money” stands beside Yissachar’s “shade of Torah.”) that in the Future the Holy One will make “shade [and canopies] for the masters of mitzvos beside the masters of Torah in Gan Eden,” from this verse.
וְהַצֵּל הוּא מִצַּד ״צֵל יָמֵינוּ״ דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And the “shade” is [only] from the side of “our days are a shadow” of this world;
וּבָעוֹלָם הַבָּא דְּנִגְלֶה דְּזֶה צֵל לְבַד, צֵל הַחָכְמָה גָּדוֹל, וְיִחוּס דְּבַעֲלֵי מִצְווֹת הוּא רַק מַה שֶּׁהֵם אֵצֶל בַּעֲלֵי תוֹרָה

and in the World to Come, where it is revealed that this [worldly service] is but a “shade,” the “shade of wisdom [Torah]” is the greater — and the standing of the masters of mitzvos is only that they are “beside” the masters of Torah.648R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Miketz §9): “"for in the shade of wisdom [is as] in the shade of money"…” The se’if’s “shade” precisely: the masters of mitzvos stand beside the masters of Torah as a shade stands to the form that casts it — real, dependent, and taking its shape wholly from what stands above it.
וְזֶהוּ ״טוֹב לִי״ דַּוְקָא, לְדַרְגָּא דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה דְּהוּא מָשִׁיחַ בְּעַצְמוֹ
And this is precisely “good to me” — for the rung of David HaMelech, who is himself Mashiach,
וְהִשִּׂיג מַדְרֵיגַת גִּילּוּי עֶצֶם הָאָדָם עוֹשֶׂה הַצֵּל, דְּהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת צוּרַת אָדָם
who attained the level of revealing the “essential man” that casts the shadow — the perfection of the “form of Adam,”
דְּיָדוּעַ דְּהוּא רָאשֵׁי תֵּיבוֹת ״אָדָם — אָדָם דָּוִד מָשִׁיחַ״
for it is known that [Adam] is the acronym of Adam–David–Mashiach.
אֲבָל מִקְרָא דְּ״שְׂמַח [זְבוּלוּן בְּצֵאתֶךָ]״, שֶׁהוּא הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁמִּצַּד הַגִּילּוּי שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
But the verse “rejoice, [Zevulun, in your going out]” — [expressing] the joy that comes from the [outer] revelation in this world —
עִיקַּר הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב הוּא נֶעֱלֶמֶת, וְהַגִּילּוּי אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּמַעֲשֶׂה וּפְעוּלוֹת נִגְלֵית
[here] the essential wisdom of the heart is concealed, and the revelation is only in [outward] deed and revealed actions.
אַף מַעֲלַת בַּעֲלֵי תוֹרָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת
Even the standing of the masters of Torah in this world is [as such] only from the side of [outer] revelation —
דְּעִסְקָם בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא קִיּוּם מִצְוַת תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא אַחַת מִתַּרְיַ״ג מִצְווֹתָיו שֶׁל תּוֹרָה
[in] that their engagement in Torah is the fulfillment of the mitzvah of Talmud Torah, one of the 613 mitzvos of the Torah.
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַגִּילּוּי לְכָל הָעַמִּים שֶׁאֵין קְרוּאִים ״אָדָם״
And this is from the side of the “revelation” [perceptible] to all the nations, who are not called “adam”;
דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם הַרְגָּשָׁה בִּפְנִימִיּוּת הַצּוּרָה ״אָדָם״
for Israel have an inner “feeling” in the innermost of the “form of adam,”
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מַדְרֵיגָה הַגְּלוּיָה לָעַמִּים ״הַר יִקְרָאוּ״ הָעִיקַּר עַל יְדֵי זְבוּלוּן

whereas the level revealed to the nations — “they shall call [it] a mountain”649Devarim 33:19: “עַמִּים הַר יִקְרָאוּ, שָׁם יִזְבְּחוּ זִבְחֵי צֶדֶק, כִּי שֶׁפַע יַמִּים יִינָקוּ וּשְׂפֻנֵי טְמוּנֵי חוֹל” — “peoples will call to the mountain; there they will offer righteous offerings; for they draw from the abundance of the seas and from the hidden treasures buried in the sand.” Background: the continuation of Zevulun’s blessing — his sea-trade draws peoples to the mountain (Har HaMoriah). Meforshim: Rashi glosses “amim” as [the peoples] “of the tribes of Israel” who gather to Har HaMoriah; R’ Tzadok, by contrast, reads “amim” as the nations of the world, who apprehend only the outward “mountain” — a height “marked and conspicuous by being higher than all around it.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the nations reach only the revealed “har” (as Avraham named the place a “mountain”), whereas Israel alone possess the inner “house.” — is chiefly through Zevulun.
וְזֶהוּ ״הַר יִקְרָאוּ״ כְּאַבְרָהָם שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ ״הַר״, דְּהוּא ״אַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם״

And this is “they shall call [it] a mountain” — like Avraham, who called it a “mountain” (Bereishis 22:14)650Bereishis 22:14: “וַיִּקְרָא אַבְרָהָם שֵׁם הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא ה׳ יִרְאֶה, אֲשֶׁר יֵאָמֵר הַיּוֹם בְּהַר ה׳ יֵרָאֶה” — “and Avraham called the name of that place ‘Hashem yireh,’ as it is said this day, ‘on the mountain of Hashem He will be seen.’” Background: after the Akeidah, Avraham names the future Temple site. Meforshim: the Gemara (Pesachim 88a) contrasts the three patriarchs — Avraham called the place a “mountain” (har), Yitzchak a “field” (sadeh), and Yaakov a “house” (bayis); the ultimate name is Yaakov’s “house.” R’ Tzadok’s use: Avraham, “the father of a multitude of nations,” named it “har” — the outward height that the nations, too, can reach; the higher, inner “house” belongs to the seed of Yaakov., for he is “the father of a multitude of nations,”
וְהֵם אֵין מַשִּׂיגִים אֶלָּא מַדְרֵיגַת ״הַר״ שֶׁהוּא גִּילּוּי רָשׁוּם וּמְצוּיָּין בְּמַה שֶּׁהוּא גָּבוֹהַּ מִכֹּל
and they [the nations] apprehend only the level of “mountain” — a revelation marked and conspicuous by being higher than all around it.
אֲבָל דַּרְגָּא דִּזְבוּלוּן ״יִזְבְּלֵנִי״ לְשׁוֹן דִּירָה שֶׁהוּא בַּבַּיִת
But the rung of Zevulun, “yizbeleini” — a term of “dwelling” — is [expressed] in a “house,”
הַשַּׁיָּיךְ לְזַרְעָא דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע״ה שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ ״בַּיִת״

which belongs to the seed of Yaakov Avinu, who called it a “house” (Bereishis 28:17)651Bereishis 28:17: “וַיִּירָא וַיֹּאמַר מַה נּוֹרָא הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה, אֵין זֶה כִּי אִם בֵּית אֱלֹהִים, וְזֶה שַׁעַר הַשָּׁמָיִם” — “and he was afraid, and said: how awesome is this place! this is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.” Background: Yaakov’s words on waking from the ladder-dream, at the site of the future Beis HaMikdash. Meforshim: per that same Gemara (Pesachim 88a), Yaakov alone called the place a “house” (bayis) — the innermost, enclosed rung, surpassing Avraham’s “mountain” and Yitzchak’s “field.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the “house of Yaakov” is the rung of Zevulun’s “dwelling” (yizbeleini) — Israel as the very structure that houses the Shechinah, “for the place of His Shechinah is only within them.”;
דְּהַשְּׁבָטִים הֵם תִּקְרָתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל (תנחומא שמות ג) עַל פָּסוּק ״יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקוֹרָאָי״

for the tribes are “the ceiling of the world,” as the Sages said (Tanchuma Shemos 3)652Midrash Tanchuma, Shemos 3: explaining why the tribes are listed in varying orders in different places, the midrash says they are set side by side “because they are the ceiling (tikrah) of the world; and one who fits a ceiling properly sets the thick end of one beam beside the thin end of another… And whence do we know they are the ceiling of the world? — as it says, ‘Listen to Me, Yaakov, and Israel My mekorai’ (Yeshayah 48:12)” — reading mekorai (מקוראי) as “My ceiling.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the tribes are “the ceiling of the world” — Israel “make a ceiling” over the Shechinah, and through the “house of Yaakov” His Presence dwells among the lower worlds, its place being only within them. on “Israel — My ‘ceiling’ [mekorai]”,
וְעַל יָדָם נִבְנֶה הַבַּיִת ״בֵּית יַעֲקֹב״ לִהְיוֹת שְׁכִינָתוֹ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים
and through them the “house” — “the house of Yaakov” — is built, for His Shechinah to dwell among the lower [worlds].
דְּזֶהוּ ״מְקוֹרָאָי״ כִּבְיָכוֹל, עוֹשִׂים תִּקְרָה עָלָיו עַל גַּבֵּי שְׁכִינַת כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
For this is “My ceiling,” as it were — [that Israel] “make a ceiling” over the Shechinah of His glory —
כִּי מְקוֹם שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא רַק בְּקִרְבָּם
for the place of His Shechinah is only within them. — Israel are thus not merely those who stand beneath the Divine “mountain,” but the very roof that houses the Shechinah within.

items.h: The theme: Leah is the akeres ha-bayis — in full revelation, the Beis HaMikdash (essentially, the days of Mashiach). The main indwelling of the Shechinah is in the chambers of the heart — “the four amos of halachah,” which is the treasury of yiras Shamayim (each needs the other). The two-way link: “if no fear, no wisdom” (the gate, by effort) and “if no wisdom, no fear” (awe drawn from Above) — a “great awe” from which one cannot forget.

p: [כו] וְלֵאָה הִיא עֲקֶרֶת הַבַּיִת ״אֵם הַבָּנִים״
And Leah is the “mainstay of the house,” “the mother of the children”;
וּבְגִילּוּי גָּמוּר הוּא הַבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, וְזֶה עִיקָּרוֹ בִּימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ
and in full revelation this is the Beis HaMikdash — whose essence [belongs] to the days of Mashiach.
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הָיָה גִּילּוּי מְעַט בַּבַּיִת שֶׁבָּנָה שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה
And in this world there was a small revelation in the House that Shlomo HaMelech built,
וְהָיָה רַק לְשָׁעָה בִּזְמַנּוֹ, דְּהָיָה סִיהֲרָא בְּאַשְׁלְמוּתָא

but it was only for a [brief] time, in his generation, when “the moon was at its fullness653“Sihara b’ashlemusa” — “the moon at its fullness”: a Zoharic idiom. In Kabbalah the moon symbolizes Malchus — the Davidic kingship and the Shechinah — which waxes and wanes like the moon. Background: Shlomo’s reign was the peak of the Jewish monarchy, “the moon at its fullness,” when the Beis HaMikdash stood and the kingdom was whole. R’ Tzadok’s use: yet this fullness lasted only “for a brief time, in his generation” — Shlomo himself became “king and then a commoner” (Sanhedrin 20b), and straightaway the kingship of the House of David was split; the full and enduring indwelling of the Shechinah in the “house” belongs to the days of Mashiach.”;
וְגַם הוּא ״מֶלֶךְ וְהֶדְיוֹט״, וְתֵיכֶף אַחַר כָּךְ נֶחְלְקָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד

and even he [became] “king and then a commoner” (Sanhedrin 20b)654Sanhedrin 20b: “Shlomo was ‘a king and [then] a commoner’ [melech ve-hedyot]” — he reigned over the upper and the lower [worlds], and in the end reigned only over his staff., and immediately afterward the kingship of the House of David was divided.
אֲבָל עִיקַּר גִּילּוּי שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים הוּא בְּחַדְרֵי הַלְּבָבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל

But the essential revelation of His Shechinah among the lower [worlds] is in the chambers of the hearts of Israel,655R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §52): “the distress of Rachel — that Leah is the one who bears the tribes in actuality, while Rachel all her days desired and yearned for the bearing of tribes, and in actuality bore only [two].” Exactly the se’if: the akeres ha-bayis is the one in whom the bearing actually happens — the living source — which is why it is Leah, and not Rachel, who lies with Yaakov.
דְּכִיוֵּון אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קׇדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים
for [each] “directs his heart toward the Holy of Holies.”
וּבְגִילּוּי הוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (ברכות ח.) ״אֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה״
And in [terms of] revelation, this is what they said (Berachos 8a): “the Holy One has nothing [in His world] but the four amos of halachah”;
וְהוּא עַצְמוֹ הָאוֹצָר שֶׁל יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
and this itself is the “treasury” of fear of Heaven,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ גַּם כֵּן דְּ״אֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ אֶלָּא יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם בִּלְבַד״ (שבת לא:)

for they also said, “the Holy One has nothing in His world but fear of Heaven alone” (Shabbos 31b)656Shabbos 31b: “The Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in His world but the fear of Heaven alone [ein lo la-Kadosh Baruch Hu b’olamo ela yiras shamayim bilvad], as it says (Iyov 28:28), ‘and He said to man: behold, the fear of the Lord — that is wisdom.’” —
דְּהָא בְּלָא הָא לָא סַגִּי
for one without the other does not suffice.
רַק זֶהוּ אוֹצָר הַגָּנוּז בְּחַדְרֵי הַלֵּב וּמִתְגַּלֶּה בְּפֹעַל בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה, לְאַסּוֹקֵי שְׁמַעְתָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּהִלְכְתָא
Only that this is a treasury stored in the chambers of the heart, which manifests in practice in “the four amos of halachah” — in drawing a teaching to its halachic conclusion —
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַסִּימָן לְמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּקִרְבּוֹ אוֹצָר שֶׁל יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם

which is the “sign” of one who has within him a treasury of fear of Heaven.657R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Masei §9): “"I have a good gift in My treasury and its name is Shabbos" — and one must understand: did they not say that the Holy One has nothing in His treasury but the treasury of the fear of Heaven alone, and of that it cannot be said that it is a good gift to give to Israel, since the fear of Heaven is in a person’s hand alone, as they said, "all is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven"?” This is exactly the se’if’s two-way link: fear is the one thing left to man’s effort, and yet it is what Heaven keeps in its treasury — so that each side needs the other.Mei HaShiloach — chochmah and yirah must continually generate one another: Mei HaShiloach I, Beshalach §2, explains the Mishnah “אם אין חכמה אין יראה, אם אין יראה אין חכמה” as a dynamic balance. Chochmah gives a person tokef — inner firmness and confidence — but without yirah that very strength can become the delusion that his wisdom stands independently of Hashem. Conversely, a person who possesses only fear without the strengthening clarity of chochmah has not yet reached true yirah; his fear can remain imagination and anxiety rather than awe of God. The Ishbitzer therefore reads “bayam bayabashah” and “bayabashah besoch hayam” as the required interpenetration of the two states: the sea signifies yirah and tefillah, the dry land signifies the firmness of Torah, and each must be found within the other. This deepens R’ Tzadok’s two-directional account here. The first yirah is the human gate — the small opening of submission by which one enters. Chochmah is then given from Above; but that chochmah itself produces a higher yirah, now born from perception rather than mere restraint. The cycle continues. Hence the Shechinah’s dwelling in the heart is neither achieved by human effort alone nor simply imposed from Heaven. The person opens the treasury through yirah; the Divine chochmah that enters enlarges his capacity for awe, and the enlarged awe becomes a still deeper vessel for wisdom.
וְ״אִם אֵין יִרְאָה אֵין חָכְמָה״ — הִיא הַתַּרְעָא דִּבְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם

And “if there is no fear, there is no wisdom” (Avos 3:17)658Avos 3:17: “R’ Elazar ben Azaryah says: If there is no wisdom, there is no fear; if there is no fear, there is no wisdom [im ein chochmah ein yirah, im ein yirah ein chochmah].” — this [fear] is the “gate,” [attained] through a person’s own effort;
וְ״אִם אֵין חָכְמָה אֵין יִרְאָה״ — הוּא מוֹרָא שָׁמַיִם שֶׁעָלָיו
and “if there is no wisdom, there is no fear” — this is the awe of Heaven [that comes] upon him [from Above],
שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי הַהַכָּרָה בְּחָכְמָתוֹ דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נֶגְדּוֹ תָּמִיד, מִמֵּילָא יַגִּיעַ אֵלָיו הַיִּרְאָה
which comes about through recognizing, by his wisdom, that Hashem is always before him — whereby the fear reaches him of itself,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב [בְּהַגָּהָה דְּרֵישׁ אוֹרַח חַיִּים]

as [the Rema] wrote [in the gloss at the beginning of Orach Chaim].659Rema (R’ Moshe Isserles), in his gloss at the opening of Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chayim 1:1, teaches on the verse “I have set Hashem before me always” (Tehillim 16:8) that “this is a great principle in the Torah and among the virtues of the righteous who walk before God.” A person’s conduct when alone in his house is not as it is before a great king; and when one takes to heart that the great King, the Holy One, blessed is He, whose glory fills the whole earth, stands over him and sees his deeds, “immediately the awe and the submission in the fear of Him reach him” (the Rema citing Rambam, Moreh Nevuchim III:52) — the fear that “reaches him of itself” to which R’ Tzadok alludes here.
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא ״וּבְמוֹרָא גָּדוֹל״ זוֹ גִּילּוּי שְׁכִינָה

And along the lines of what is brought, that “and with great awe” (Devarim 26:8)660Devarim 26:8: “וַיּוֹצִאֵנוּ ה׳ מִמִּצְרַיִם בְּיָד חֲזָקָה וּבִזְרֹעַ נְטוּיָה וּבְמֹרָא גָּדֹל וּבְאֹתוֹת וּבְמֹפְתִים” — “and Hashem brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great awe, and with signs and wonders.” Background: this verse is from the “Arami oved avi” passage of the first-fruits declaration (Devarim 26:5–10), which the Pesach Haggadah expounds phrase by phrase. Meforshim: the Haggadah (Magid), darshening this verse, teaches “u-v’mora gadol — this is the revelation of the Shechinah,” deriving it from the parallel “great awesome deeds” (mora’im gedolim) said of the Exodus in Devarim 4:34. R’ Tzadok’s use: “great awe” is the fear that descends from a revealed Divine Presence — and since “gadol” (great) connotes a spreading-forth without end, it is a fear from which one can never come to forget, unlike the lesser fear a person must generate by his own effort (“the gate”). — “this is the revelation of the Shechinah”;
דְּעַל יְדֵי הַהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּא בְּתוֹקֶף הַיִּרְאָה הַנִּקְרָא מוֹרָא גָּדוֹל
for through the [Divine] revelation comes the intensity of fear that is called “great awe.”
וְיָדוּעַ דְּ״גָדוֹל״ מוֹרֶה הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת עַד אֵין קֵץ
And it is known that “great” [gadol] indicates a spreading-forth without end;
וְהַיְינוּ יִרְאָה שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִשְׁכֹּחַ מִמֶּנָּה כְּלָל

and this is a fear from which it is impossible to forget at all.661R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Kuntres Amalah shel Torah §5): “"three good gifts" — Eretz Yisrael, Torah, and the World to Come — all of them through sufferings; and they are in the merit of the three Avos, who bequeathed the root of their good traits to their children, to be fixed in the depths of their hearts: the three holy points… "and the fear of Hashem is the beginning of wisdom."” The se’if’s two-way link precisely: fear is “the beginning of wisdom,” yet it is itself an inheritance fixed in the depths of the heart — so neither side stands without the other. — the fear that descends as a gift from the revealed Presence, unlike the fear a person must manufacture by his own effort, being the one that never lapses.

items.h: The theme: Zevulun’s “fear” (after Yissachar’s “wisdom”) lets one “absorb” the sea’s abundance — all worldly desire — into holiness, without cleaving to the “husk.” Yosef’s fear is by choice; but when Hashem fixes His Shechinah in the heart, the techeiles-thread encompasses him and he draws only the holiness (“the hidden treasures in the sand”). Israel are “sand” — the boundary of the sea — and “count by the moon,” in concealment (secrets hidden).

p: [כז] וְזֶהוּ הַיִּרְאָה דִּזְבוּלוּן הַבָּא אַחַר הַחָכְמָה דְּיִשָּׂשכָר
And this is the “fear” of Zevulun, which comes after the “wisdom” of Yissachar,
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהוּא בַּיִת לְגִילּוּי שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
through his being a “house” for the revelation of His Shechinah;
דְּהַכֹּל צְרִיכִין לוֹ בָּזֶה לִקְלֹט יִרְאָה זוֹ דִּזְבוּלוּן עַל יְדֵי חִלָּזוֹן הַגּוֹרֵם זְכִירָה
for all are dependent on him in this — to “absorb” this fear of Zevulun through the chilazon that induces remembering.
וְהוּא עוֹלֶה מֵהַיָּם, וְ״שֶׁפַע יַמִּים יִינָקוּ״ עַל יְדֵי זֶה
And it [the chilazon] rises from the sea, and “the abundance of the seas they suck” (Devarim 33:19) through it —
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁפַע כָּל מִינֵי חַמְדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה יִינְקוּ הֵם לִקְלֹט הַכֹּחַ שֶׁל קְדֻשָּׁה הַמְקַיְּימִים וּמַמְצִיאִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה

that is, [from] the abundance of all kinds of desirable things of this world they “suck,” to absorb the power of holiness that sustains them and brings [them] into being in this world.662R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §66): “the seven [defective] vessels correspond to Yaakov… but fish are likewise entirely pure, and there are no tereifos in them [that is, none of the defects belonging to Israel themselves, though both are Israel].” Exactly the se’if’s Zevulun: what is drawn up out of the sea — the realm of concealment — comes up wholly pure, with no husk clinging to it.
דְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ נִבְרָא בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת אֲלֵיהֶם

For the entire world was created for the sake of Israel663“The whole world was created for the sake of Israel”: a foundational teaching of Chazal. Rashi, in his opening comment on the Torah (Bereishis 1:1), explains that God created the world “for the sake of Israel, who are called reishis, and for the sake of the Torah, called reishis”; the midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 36:4) likewise teaches that the world endures in the merit of Israel. R’ Tzadok’s use: because the world thus “belongs” to Israel, its abundance is theirs to elevate — to “absorb the power of holiness that sustains it and brings it into being”; but should they sink into it as an end in itself, they sever both it and themselves from its Source., [and so] it has a “belonging” to them;
אֶלָּא שֶׁאִם יַשְׁקִיעוּ עַצְמָם בָּזֶה לְבַד יָבוֹאוּ לִיפָּרֵד חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מֵאַחְדוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
except that if they sink themselves into this [worldly abundance] alone, they will come, Heaven forbid, to be sundered from His unity,
כְּטַעַם ״שָׁמַנְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר וַיִּטּוֹשׁ [אֱלוֹהַּ עָשָׂהוּ]״ וְגוֹמֵר, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְרָם לְבָבֶךָ וְשָׁכַחְתָּ [אֶת ה׳]״

in the sense of “you grew fat — and he forsook [the God who made him]” (Devarim 32:15)664Devarim 32:15: “וַיִּשְׁמַן יְשֻׁרוּן וַיִּבְעָט, שָׁמַנְתָּ עָבִיתָ כָּשִׂיתָ, וַיִּטֹּשׁ אֱלוֹהַּ עָשָׂהוּ, וַיְנַבֵּל צוּר יְשֻׁעָתוֹ” — “and Yeshurun grew fat and kicked — you grew fat, thick, gross — and he forsook the God who made him, and spurned the Rock of his salvation.” Background: from the song of Ha’azinu — Moshe’s warning that material abundance would lead Israel to rebel. Meforshim: the verse itself traces the descent — satiety (“you grew fat”) breeds “kicking” against Heaven, which ends in forsaking God; wealth ungoverned by gratitude produces rebellion. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the danger of “sinking oneself” into the abundance of this world alone — one is thereby “sundered from His unity”; only Zevulun’s fear (the techeiles-thread) lets a person absorb the holiness within the abundance without being severed from its Source.Noam Elimelech — techeiles and the sea teach a yirah that sets a holy boundary: Noam Elimelech, Shelach §18, develops Chazal’s chain “techeiles resembles the sea, the sea the firmament, and the firmament the Throne of Glory.” He reads the sea as yirah: Hashem placed a boundary for it, and despite the force of its waves it does not pass the limit decreed for it. The firmament, by contrast, expresses a joyous love; together the two repair the person’s ‘wings.’ This illuminates R’ Tzadok’s use of Zevulun, the sea, the sand, and the thread of techeiles. The issue is not to destroy the sea’s abundance — desire, commerce, physical vitality, and the wealth of the world — but to give it a boundary that makes its energy serve rather than overwhelm. Yirah is therefore not withdrawal from shefa; it is the capacity to receive shefa without losing the distinction between the gift and its Source. The sand holds back the sea, and the techeiles draws the eye from sea to sky to Kisei HaKavod. In R’ Tzadok’s terms, that is what permits Zevulun to draw from “shefa yamim” while extracting only the kedushah concealed in it. Without the boundary, abundance becomes “vayishman Yeshurun vayiv’at”; with the boundary, the same abundance is absorbed into avodah., and “and your heart grows haughty, and you forget [Hashem]” (Devarim 8:14)665Devarim 8:14: “וְרָם לְבָבֶךָ וְשָׁכַחְתָּ אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ, הַמּוֹצִיאֲךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם מִבֵּית עֲבָדִים” — “and your heart grows haughty, and you forget Hashem your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.” Background: Moshe warns that prosperity in the Land — “you shall eat and be satisfied” — can breed a haughty heart. Meforshim: the verse pairs “haughtiness of heart” directly with “forgetting”; the commentators note that self-sufficiency (as the next verses put it, ascribing success to “my own strength and the might of my hand”) is the very root of forgetting God. R’ Tzadok’s use: forgetting is the fruit of a heart “grown haughty” over worldly abundance — the exact opposite of the fear (the techeiles-thread) that “removes forgetting.”.
וְעִיקַּר דַּרְגָּא דְּיִרְאַת אֱלֹקִים דְּיוֹסֵף הוּא לִהְיוֹת צַדִּיק מוּגְדָּר וְנִבְדָּל בְּכָל חַמְדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And the essential rung of the “fear of God” of Yosef is to be a tzaddik who is “bounded-in” and separated in [the face of] all the desires of this world;
אֲבָל זֶהוּ בִּירֵא שָׁמַיִם מִצַּד בְּחִירָתוֹ כְּיוֹסֵף

but this is [a fear attained] in a God-fearing person, by his own choice, like Yosef.666R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Sivan §3): “"and they journeyed from Refidim and camped in the wilderness" — meaning that they had no other will but the will of the Omnipresent; and the twelve months correspond to the twelve tribes.” The se’if’s “fear” of Zevulun exactly: only where a man has no competing will of his own can the abundance of the “sea” be absorbed without his cleaving to it.
אֲבָל כַּאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִקְבַּע שְׁכִינָתוֹ בְּקֶרֶב לִבּוֹ שֶׁהַיִּרְאָה מַקִּיפָתּוֹ
But when Hashem fixes His Shechinah within his heart, such that the fear [itself] encompasses him,
מִמֵּילָא זֶהוּ הַחוּט שֶׁל תְּכֵלֶת דְּחִלָּזוֹן הַגּוֹרֵם זְכִירָה וּמֵסִיר הַשִּׁכְחָה
then automatically this is the “thread of techeiles” of the chilazon that induces remembering and removes forgetting;
אָז יוּכַל לִינֹק הַקְּדֻשָּׁה לְבַד מִשֶּׁפַע יַמִּים וְלֹא יִדְבַּק בַּקְּלִיפָּה הַסּוֹבֶבֶת לַפְּרִי
then he can “suck” the holiness alone from the abundance of the seas, and will not cleave to the “husk” that surrounds the fruit,
כִּי יַשִּׂיג ״שְׂפוּנֵי טְמוּנֵי חוֹל״
for he will attain “the hidden treasures concealed in the sand” (Devarim 33:19).
דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְשְׁלוּ לְחוֹל מִצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם
For Israel are likened to “sand” from the side of concealment.
דְּמַה שֶּׁהֵם כְּכוֹכְבֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם הוּא מִצַּד הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹרָם לֶעָתִיד לְעֵין כֹּל
For their being “like the stars of the heavens” is from the side of the revelation of their light in the Future, before all eyes;
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁיּוֹרְדִים יוֹרְדִים עַד לֶעָפָר, הֵם כְּחוֹל גְּבוּל לַיָּם

but when they “descend,” they descend to the very dust — [and then] they are “like the sand, a boundary for the sea667Yirmeyah 5:22: “הַאוֹתִי לֹא תִירָאוּ נְאֻם ה׳… אֲשֶׁר שַׂמְתִּי חוֹל גְּבוּל לַיָּם חָק עוֹלָם וְלֹא יַעַבְרֶנְהוּ, וַיִּתְגָּעֲשׁוּ וְלֹא יוּכָלוּ וְהָמוּ גַלָּיו וְלֹא יַעַבְרֻנְהוּ” — “will you not fear Me, says Hashem…? I who set the sand as a boundary for the sea, an eternal decree it cannot pass — though its waves toss, they cannot prevail; though they roar, they cannot pass it.” Background: the prophet rebukes Israel’s lack of fear, pointing to the standing wonder that mere sand holds back the raging sea — a testimony to God’s power that ought to evoke awe (the verse opens, literally, “Me you do not fear?”). Meforshim: the commentators note the marvel that the frailest barrier — loose grains of sand — restrains the mightiest force, by Divine decree alone. R’ Tzadok’s use: Israel are that “sand” — the boundary that keeps the “sea” of the nations’ desires from flooding the world (as it did in the generation of the Flood); their very lowliness and concealment is what holds the line.,”
שֶׁלֹּא לְהַנִּיחַ אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם בְּחַמְדוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם לִשְׁטוֹף כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ כְּמוֹ בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל, וְהֵם הַגְּבוּל בָּזֶה
so as not to let the nations, in their desires, flood the whole world as in the generation of the Flood — and they [Israel] are the “boundary” in this.
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה הוּא כֹּחַ הַהֶעְלֵם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל (שמו״ר א, כא) עַל פָּסוּק ״וַיִּטְמְנֵהוּ בַּחוֹל״ אֵלּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל

And from this side is the “power of concealment,” as the Sages said (Shemos Rabbah 1:28)668Shemos Rabbah 1:28: On “and he hid him in the sand” (Shemos 2:12): “these are Israel,” who are likened to the sand of the sea (cf. Bereishis 22:17). (Their strength lies in the power of “concealment.”) on the verse “and he hid him in the sand” (Shemos 2:12): “these are Israel.”
הַיְינוּ דְּעִנְיַן הַהַטְמָנָה וְהַהֶעְלֵם הוּא רַק בָּהֶם שֶׁמּוֹנִין לַלְּבָנָה שֶׁפְּעָמִים מִתְכַּסֵּית, וְהִיא בְּאִתְכַּסְיָא, וְרָזוֹהִי כְּסִיִּין

That is, the matter of “hiding” and concealment [pertains] only to them, who “count by the moon,”669Sukkah 29a: in the passage on the significance of eclipses, the Gemara teaches that “Israel reckon [their calendar] by the moon, while the nations of the world reckon by the sun.” Background: Israel’s festivals follow the lunar cycle — the moon, which waxes, wanes, and is at times wholly covered. R’ Tzadok’s use: the moon is the emblem of Israel’s “concealment” — like the moon that is periodically hidden, Israel’s greatness is veiled in this world and revealed only in the Future; and it is precisely this hiddenness (monin la-levanah) that is their power to draw the holy spark unseen from the “sea” of worldly abundance. which at times is covered — and it is “in concealment,” and “its secrets are hidden,”
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּסוֹף שַׁבָּת קנו.]
as they said [Shabbos 156a].
וְזֶהוּ סוֹד מַה שֶּׁאִיתָא (ע״ז ע.) ״רוֹב גַּנָּבֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״

And this is the secret of what is brought (Avodah Zarah 70a)670Avodah Zarah 70a: “Certain thieves came to Pumbedita and opened many barrels [of wine]. Rava said: The wine is permitted. What is the reason? Most of the thieves [there] are Jews [rubba ganavei Yisrael ninhu]” — so it is not presumed that a gentile handled the wine. (Israel’s very “power of concealment.”), “most thieves are [of] Israel” —
דְּמַאן דִּבְלִבָּנָה אִי גָּנֵיב מַצְלַח, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם דְּמוֹנִין לַחַמָּה רָזוֹהִי גַּלְיָין

for “one [born under the sign] of the moon, if he steals, succeeds [in concealment]” — whereas the nations, who count by the sun, “their secrets are revealed.” — Israel’s very power of concealment is what lets them draw the holy spark out of the sea of worldly abundance without being caught in its husk.671Shabbos 156a: “One born under the moon will be a man who bears illnesses, builds and demolishes, demolishes and builds [like the waxing and waning moon], eats what is not his and drinks what is not his, and whose secrets are hidden [like the moon that does not shine]; if he steals, he succeeds — One born under the sun will be a radiant man [shining like the sun], who eats of his own and drinks of his own, and whose secrets are exposed; if he steals, he does not succeed.” [Israel “count by the moon” — the sign of concealment; the nations “by the sun” — of open revelation.]672R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash §9): “and from the side of the kindness and love they merited in Egypt, they were drawn after the Holy One into the wilderness and did not say "what shall we eat there" — and Hashem remembers it for them.” Exactly the se’if: Israel are drawn after Hashem by what stands above their own grasp — going into an unsown land without asking, which is precisely the verse’s praise.

items.h: The theme: Even Esav had some grip within Yaakov — “his hand grasping the heel of Esav.” Esav is a “Yisrael mumar”: born of Yitzchak and Rivkah with no evil forebear, yet only Yaakov became “Yisrael in essence,” unchangeable. Great souls were hidden in Esav (R’ Akiva — “tzayid be-fiv”), but only “in his heels,” the lowest rung. David was fit to emerge with Yaakov (“ruddy, yet fair-eyed”), but “a time when man ruled man” turned that potential into Esav — and from that heel Mashiach will yet come.

p: [כח] וַאֲפִילּוּ עֵשָׂו שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אֲחִיזָה קְצָת בְּיַעֲקֹב, דְּיָדוֹ אוֹחֶזֶת בַּעֲקֵבוֹ

And even Esav has some “grip” in Yaakov — “his hand grasping the heel of Esav” (Bereishis 25:26)673Bereishis 25:26: “וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יָצָא אָחִיו וְיָדוֹ אֹחֶזֶת בַּעֲקֵב עֵשָׂו, וַיִּקְרָא שְׁמוֹ יַעֲקֹב” — “and afterward his brother emerged, his hand grasping the heel of Esav, and he called his name Yaakov.” Background: at the twins’ birth Yaakov is named for the “heel” (akev) of Esav that his hand held. Meforshim: the Sages take the grasping hand as a sign that Yaakov would ultimately seize what was Esav’s (as the midrash develops on this very phrase). R’ Tzadok’s use: Yaakov’s very name expresses a “grip” on Esav’s heel — the point at which even Esav has “some hold” within holiness, and conversely the place where the hidden root of Yaakov (and of David) lies.;
וְעִיקַּר שְׁמוֹ ״יַעֲקֹב״ הוּא עַל שֵׁם אֲחִיזַת הֶעָקֵב דְּעֵשָׂו

and Yaakov’s very name is on account of “grasping the heel” of Esav.674R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §62): “"and he called his name Yaakov" — this name indicates "his hand grasping the heel" of Esav, of which they said, "who will seize the kingship after us"… but in this world he has no dominion — this is when "the voice is not the voice of Yaakov" in Torah… for Esav was the revealed good, as they said on "for game was in his mouth."” Exactly the se’if: the “tzayid be-fiv” is Esav’s outward good, and Yaakov’s hold on it is only at the heel — the lowest and last point.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּעֵשָׂו נִקְרָא [בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּקִדּוּשִׁין] ״יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר״
This is why Esav is called [in the first chapter of Kiddushin] “an apostate Jew,”
כִּי מִצַּד שֶׁהָיָה זֶרַע יִצְחָק וְרִבְקָה שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בּוֹ צַד רַע כָּל מֵאֲבוֹתָיו כְּבְיִשְׁמָעֵאל, וְנִימוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה
for, being the seed of Yitzchak and Rivkah — with no “evil side” from a forebear as Yishmael had, [Yitzchak] circumcised on the eighth day —
הָיָה מִלֵּידָה חָל עָלָיו שֵׁם ״יִשְׂרָאֵל״
the name “Yisrael” applied to him from birth;
דְּגַם אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק נִקְרְאוּ ״יִשְׂרָאֵל״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל (נדרים לא.)
for Avraham and Yitzchak too are “called Yisrael,” as the Sages said (Nedarim 31a).
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם לֹא זָכוּ עֲדַיִין לְשֵׁם זֶה אֶלָּא לְעַצְמָם לְבַד
Except that they had not yet merited this name save for themselves alone;
אֲבָל שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֵּן קָבוּעַ לְדוֹרוֹת שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְקַלְקֵל כְּלָל, זֶה זָכָה רַק יַעֲקֹב שֶׁנִּקְרָא יִשְׂרְאֵלִי בְּעֶצֶם
but that it be fixed for [all] generations, impossible ever to be spoiled — this only Yaakov merited, who is “a Yisrael in essence,”
דְּעַצְמוּתוֹ כָּךְ וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת עוֹד

for such is his very essence, and it can no longer be changed.675R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §259): “and Esav, who is the root of falsehood and the grip upon the world of falsehood, in the days of Yaakov our father, who is the root of truth and the very opposite of this world — only that "his hand grasps the heel," and at the end of this world.” The se’if’s “Yisrael mumar” in its sharpest form: Esav’s whole standing is in a world whose truth is inverted, and Yaakov reaches him only at his last extremity.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאָדָם שֶׁיּוֹלִיד בְּהֵמָה, כָּךְ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל מִזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע״ה לְהוֹלִיד גּוֹי
And just as it is impossible for a man to beget an animal, so it is impossible for a Jew of Yaakov’s seed to beget a gentile;
וַאֲפִילּוּ יִשְׁתַּמֵּד עֲדַיִין יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא
and even if he apostatizes, he is still a Jew (cf. Sanhedrin 44a),
וְזַרְעוֹ שֶׁמִּיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית מְשׁוּמֶּדֶת אַחֲרָיו כֵּן
and his seed, from an apostate Jewess, is likewise so after him.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן עֵשָׂו הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּד וּלְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת לִהְיוֹת גּוֹי גָּמוּר

whereas Esav was able to apostatize and change, to become a full gentile.676R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §13): “And in Kiddushin (18a) it is brought that Esav is a ‘Yisrael mumar’ [an apostate Jew] — meaning that before he went out to evil ways the name ‘Israel’ rested upon him, and he was circumcised at eight days, except that [afterward] he apostatized. And although with a Jew, even an apostate, ‘though he has sinned, he is [still] a Jew’ — this [inseverability] is only in the seed of Yaakov, in whom the ‘cord of inheritance’ is already fixed with ‘three strands’ [the three Avos] and can no longer be severed; but in the seed of Yitzchak [i.e., Esav], although he was at first called by the name Israel, once he apostatized [he was cut off].”
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מַה שֶּׁמִּלֵּידָה הָיָה יִשְׂרָאֵל, זֶה לֹא עַל חִנָּם הָיָה, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה גָּנוּז בּוֹ הַרְבֵּה נְשָׁמוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת
Nonetheless, his being “Yisrael” from birth was not for nothing, for in truth many great souls were hidden within him.
וְכַיָּדוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִ״י ז״ל עַל פָּסוּק ״צַיִד בְּפִיו״ דְּהָיָה בּוֹ נִשְׁמַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא יְסוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה

As is known from the Arizal on “[Esav had] game in his mouth” (Bereishis 25:28)677Bereishis 25:28: “וַיֶּאֱהַב יִצְחָק אֶת עֵשָׂו כִּי צַיִד בְּפִיו, וְרִבְקָה אֹהֶבֶת אֶת יַעֲקֹב” — “and Yitzchak loved Esav, for game [tzayid] was in his mouth, and Rivkah loved Yaakov.” Background: by the plain sense, Yitzchak favored Esav because Esav brought him venison. Meforshim (Kabbalah): the Arizal reads “tzayid be-fiv” as a hint that great souls were “trapped” — tzayid, a hunt — within Esav, among them the soul of R’ Akiva, foundation of the Oral Torah. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is why Esav bore the name “Yisrael” from birth — truly great souls were hidden in him; but only “in his heels,” the lowest rung, whereas in Yaakov they are the very essence.Me’or Einayim — Yaakov’s hand on Esav’s heel is a work of extraction, not identification: Me’or Einayim, Toldos §24, citing the Arizal, explains Yitzchak’s perception of “tzayid befiv” as an apprehension of holy souls trapped within Esav — specifically mentioning the soul of R’ Akiva. He then asks why Yaakov and Esav had to be joined so closely from conception. His answer is a principle of birur: to lift something fallen below, one must be able to reach the place where it lies. Yaakov therefore entered the same womb and “his hand grasped the heel of Esav” in order to seize and elevate the sparks of holiness embedded there. The heel is the point of contact, not the definition of Yaakov’s identity. This fits R’ Tzadok’s formulation with unusual precision. Esav can possess a genuine Israelite spark and can even conceal within himself a soul as exalted as R’ Akiva, while still not becoming ‘Yisrael in essence.’ The holy point in Esav is precisely what Yaakov is destined to reclaim. This also explains why the relationship must be spoken of carefully: the existence of a buried spark does not sanctify the shell that imprisons it. On the contrary, Yaakov’s task is to distinguish the two. The future emergence of Torah and Mashiach from places apparently belonging to Esav is therefore the completion of “yado ochezes ba’akev” — the hidden kedushah is extracted from the heel and returned to the root to which it truly belongs. — that the soul of R’ Akiva, the foundation of the Oral Torah, was in him,
וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר שֶׁבָּא מִנֵּירוֹן קֵיסָר הוּא מִצֶּאֱצָאָיו

and R’ Meir, descended from Nero Caesar678Gittin 56a: the Gemara relates that Nero Caesar, sent against Yerushalayim, saw omens that he would be held to blame for its destruction, so he fled, converted, “and R’ Meir descended from him.” R’ Tzadok’s use: that R’ Meir — the anonymous voice of the Mishnah, the essence of the Oral Torah — issued from the very line of Rome/Esav shows how the holiest attainment lay hidden in Esav’s “heel,” waiting to be drawn out., is of his descendants,
וּסְתַם מִשְׁנָה כְּוָותֵיהּ, שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה — הַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת שֶׁנִּקְרָא ״הֲלָכוֹת״

and “an anonymous Mishnah is [the view] of R’ Meir679Sanhedrin 86a: R’ Yochanan taught that the anonymous rulings of the Oral Torah all stem from R’ Akiva’s school — “an anonymous Mishnah is R’ Meir, an anonymous Tosefta is R’ Nechemiah, an anonymous [teaching in] Sifra is R’ Yehudah, an anonymous [teaching in] Sifrei is R’ Shimon — and all of them are according to R’ Akiva.” R’ Tzadok’s use: since “an anonymous Mishnah is R’ Meir” — and R’ Meir sprang from Esav’s line — the very backbone of the Oral Torah (the anonymous Mishnayos, the fixed “halachos”) traces to the great souls hidden within Esav.” — which is the essence of the Oral Torah, the Mishnayos that are called “halachos.”
אֲבָל אֶצְלוֹ הָיָה זֶה רַק בַּעֲקֵבָיו
But in [Esav] this was only “in his heels”;
רְצֹה לוֹמַר מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ אֵצֶל הָאָדָם עִיקַּר מְכֻוָּן זֶה נִקְרָא בְּכָל מָקוֹם ״שֶׁדָּשׁ בַּעֲקֵבָיו״
that is, whatever is not a person’s essential intent is everywhere called “what he tramples with his heels,”
וְשָׁם הֵם הַחֲטָאִים כְּטַעַם ״רַגְלֶיהָ יוֹרְדוֹת [מָוֶת]״ וְגוֹמֵר, וְהוּא הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה שֶׁבְּקוֹמַת אָדָם

and there lie the sins, in the sense of “her feet descend [to death]” (Mishlei 5:5)680Mishlei 5:5: “רַגְלֶיהָ יֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת, שְׁאוֹל צְעָדֶיהָ יִתְמֹכוּ” — “her feet descend to death; her steps take hold of She’ol” (said of the seductress, the ishah zarah). Background: Mishlei warns that following the “strange woman” leads downward to death and the grave. R’ Tzadok’s use: the “feet” — the lowest rung of a person’s “stature” — are where sin lodges, “her feet descend to death”; correspondingly, in Esav (a “base man”) only the “heel” holds any good, his essence being the reverse. — the lowest rung of the “stature of Adam.”
וְאֵצֶל קוֹמַת אָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל מְעַט הַטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא בֶּעָקֵב, כִּי עִיקַּר הַקּוֹמָה שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא הַהֵיפֶךְ מִזֶּה
And in the “stature” of a base man, the little good in him is in the “heel,” for the essence of his stature is the opposite [evil];
וְ״סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה״, דְּזֶה הָיָה תְּחִלַּת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה בִּיצִירָתוֹ
and “the last of deeds is [already] in the first of thought” — for this [good] was the “beginning of thought” in his formation.
וְכַנּוֹדָע [מִסֵּפֶר גַּלֵּי רָזַיָּא] דִּתְחִלַּת יְצִירָה הָיָה רָאוּי לָצֵאת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה עִם יַעֲקֹב
And as is known [from Galei Razaya], that at the beginning of creation David HaMelech was fit to emerge [together] with Yaakov,
שֶׁהָיָה גַּם הוּא ״אַדְמוֹנִי״, רַק ״עִם יְפֵה עֵינַיִם״, שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְקְנוּ בּוֹ הָעִנְיָינִין דְּלֵאָה
for David too was “ruddy,” but “with fair eyes” (Shmuel I 16:12) — [meaning] the “matters of Leah” were already rectified in him,
וְהָיָה הַתִּיקּוּן הַגָּמוּר לְאַלְתַּר
and the complete rectification would have been at once.
אֶלָּא שֶׁ״לַכֹּל זְמַן וְעֵת לְכָל חֵפֶץ״ מִצַּד מִדַּת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא תַּחַת הַזְּמַן

Except that “for everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose” (Koheles 3:1)681Koheles 3:1: “לַכֹּל זְמָן, וְעֵת לְכָל חֵפֶץ תַּחַת הַשָּׁמָיִם” — “for everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven.” Background: Koheles’ meditation that all things have their appointed time. R’ Tzadok’s use: “under heaven” is the realm of time; David’s complete rectification (emerging together with Yaakov) could in principle have been “at once,” but “a time for every purpose” — the constraint of a time-bound world — deferred it. — from the side of this world, which is “under time”;
וְ״יֵשׁ עֵת אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַט הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם [לְרַע לוֹ]״ וְגוֹמֵר, דְּהוּא שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל כַּנּוֹדָע [בְּסֵפֶר הַגִּלְגּוּלִים]

and “there is a time when man ruled over man [to his detriment]” (Koheles 8:9)682Koheles 8:9: “…עֵת אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַט הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם לְרַע לוֹ” — “…a time when one man ruled over another to his detriment.” Background: Koheles observes the harm of one person dominating another. R’ Tzadok’s use (per the Arizal’s Sefer HaGilgulim): this “time when man ruled man” is the dominion of the “base man” — and it was this that turned David’s potential into Esav instead, so that David’s soul “did not yet emerge from the balance.” — the dominion of the “base man,” as is known [in Sefer HaGilgulim].
עַל כֵּן לֹא יָצְאָה אָז נִשְׁמַת דָּוִד עֲדַיִין מֵהַטִּיקְלָא וְנִתְהַפֵּךְ לְעֵשָׂו
Therefore the soul of David did not yet emerge from the “balance,” and [that potential] turned instead into Esav.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם בַּעֲקֵבוֹ יָבוֹא מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ שֶׁיִּתְפֹּס הַמַּלְכוּת אַחֲרָיו
Nonetheless, “at his heel” [after him] Mashiach will come, who will seize the kingship after him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל [בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סג, ט] עַל פָּסוּק ״יָדוֹ אוֹחֶזֶת [בַּעֲקֵב עֵשָׂו]״

as the Sages said [in Bereishis Rabbah 63:9683Bereishis Rabbah 63:9: on “his hand grasping the heel of Esav,” a Roman hegemon asked a sage of the House of Siloni, “who will seize the kingdom after us?” He took a blank sheet, wrote “and afterward his brother emerged, his hand grasping the heel,” and they marveled, “old words from the mouth of a new elder!” — meaning that after Esav’s (Rome’s) dominion, Yaakov’s line will grasp the kingship. R’ Tzadok’s use: it is precisely “at the heel” — after Esav — that Mashiach, the hidden root of David, will rise to seize the kingship; for the “heel” corresponds to the World of Asiyah [Action], “the perfection of the deed.”] on “his hand grasping the heel of Esav”;
וְהַיְינוּ דְּשָׁם בֶּעָקֵב גָּנוּז תְּחִלַּת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה וְשֹׁרֶשׁ דָּוִד, שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד עוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה דְּהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה

that is, there in the “heel” is hidden the “beginning of thought” and the root of David — corresponding to the World of Asiyah [Action], which is the perfection of the deed. — so that the very lowest “heel,” where Esav took hold, is precisely where the root of David lay hidden, and whence Mashiach will yet rise.

items.h: The theme: Esav’s grip is like the swine “stretching out its hooves” — presenting himself as a tzaddik. The nations do have some light mitzvos, but “the kindness of the nations is a sin,” done only for self-aggrandizement. Esav uses Israel’s “power of concealment” in reverse — to hide his evil. Yet Yaakov grasped even Esav’s “heel” and drew it in; Esav “counts by the sun,” his secrets revealed — “how Esav was searched out, his hidden things laid bare.”

p: [כט] וּמִצַּד זֶה הוּא אֲחִיזַת עֵשָׂו דְּ״פָשַׁט טְלָפָיו״ כַּחֲזִיר, דְּהַיְינוּ עֲקֵיבוֹ
And from this [heel] is the “grip” of Esav, who “stretches out his hooves” like the swine — that is, his heel;
וְאָמְרוּ ז״ל (ויק״ר יג, ה) ״מַצַּעַת הַבִּימָה״ דְּמַרְאֶה עַצְמוֹ כְּצַדִּיק

and the Sages said (Vayikra Rabbah 13:5)684Vayikra Rabbah 13:5: “‘And the swine’ (Vayikra 11:7) — this is Edom; it stretches out its [split] hooves as if to say, ‘See, I am pure [tahor]’” — making a show of righteousness while [in truth robbing and extorting]. [that the swine] “spreads out [its split hooves, as if to say, ‘I am kosher’]” — [Esav] presents himself as a tzaddik.685R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayera §9): “that he was circumcised at ninety-nine — and this is that Israel was born; the root of the holiness of Israel appeared, which is the three Avos; and Michael and Gavriel are right and left, Chesed and Gevurah.” Exactly the se’if: Yaakov’s wholeness is a matter of root and not of attainment — which is why his rung is temimus, with no appetite for an honor that would have to be acquired.

דְּמִקְצָת מִצְווֹת קַלּוֹת יֵשׁ בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּבָבָא בָתְרָא י.]686Bava Basra 10b: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai asked his students the meaning of “charity exalts a nation, but the kindness of the peoples is sin” (Mishlei 14:34). The answers held that the charity and kindness the nations perform is “sin” for them, since they do it only for self-aggrandizement; and R’ Nechunya ben HaKanah’s reading was deemed best — that charity and kindness are for Israel, and for the nations a “sin[-offering]” — for “just as the sin-offering atones for Israel, so charity atones for the nations of the world.” עַל פָּסוּק ״דִּבְיֹבֶשׁ קְצִירָהּ״
For the nations do have some “light” mitzvos, as they said [Bava Basra 10a] on the verse “when its harvest withers” (Yeshayahu 27:11);
אַף דְּגַם זֶה אֱמֶת דְּ״חֶסֶד לְאוּמִּים חַטָּאת״ הוּא לָהֶם
though it is also true that “the kindness of the nations is a sin” for them (Mishlei 14:34),
דְּכָל מַה שֶּׁעוֹשִׂין אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְהִתְיַיהֵר כִּדְאִיתָא שָׁם, וְלִפְשֹׁט טְלָפַיִם
since all they do is only to “aggrandize themselves,” as is brought there — and to “stretch out the hooves” [for show];
וּלְגַבֵּי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם נִקְרָא רָשָׁע בָּזֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה]
and regarding the nations, one is [even] called “wicked” for this, as they said [in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah].
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד הַגִּילּוּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין נִיכָּר

Nonetheless, from the side of [outer] revelation in this world, it is not [outwardly] recognizable.687R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §28): “for the ten utterances comprise ten holy middos, whose opposite is the ten nations given to Avraham, who cleaved to their opposite in holiness; and "the first of the nations is Amalek" — the beginning and the keser of the kelipah.” This grounds the se’if’s reversal: the husk has its own “crown,” an outward summit that mimics the holy order precisely in order to be mistaken for it.
וְזֶהוּ כֹּחַ עֵשָׂו עַל יְדֵי שֹׁרֶשׁ קְצָת טוֹב שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ בַּתּוֹלָדָה, דְּנַעֲשָׂה לוֹ ״סַמָּא דְּמוֹתָא״ וּ״פוֹשְׁעִים יִכָּשְׁלוּ בָהּ״
And this is the “power” of Esav — through the root of a little good he had from birth — which became for him “a poison of death,” [since] “transgressors stumble in it”;
דְּעַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַעֲלִים הַקְּדֻשָּׁה בָּהֶם, נִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ הוּא בְּאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ לְהַעֲלִים הָרַע שֶׁבּוֹ
for [corresponding] to the “power of concealment” Israel have — to conceal the holiness within them — he uses that same power to conceal the evil within him,
וְלִהְיוֹת ״רָזוֹהִי כְּסִיִּין״ דְּהַיְינוּ הָרַע כְּסִיִּין
and to have “his secrets hidden” — that is, his evil is hidden.
וּ״שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם״ הָיָה לְרַע לוֹ

And “the dominion of man over man” was “to his [own] detriment,”688R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Sukkos §21): “for all the force of their generosity and giving is not in the innermost heart, but only to arouse accusation against Israel — "the kindness of the nations is a sin"; unlike Israel, whose… giving is in joy, in the innermost point of the heart, as it says, "and you shall draw water in gladness."” Exactly the se’if: the nations’ mitzvos are real deeds with a hollow interior — done for self-aggrandizement, they become an accusation rather than a merit.Sefas Emes — Esav’s falsehood survives only by borrowing a beginning of truth: Sefas Emes, Toldos 26:3, reads “וידו אוחזת בעקב עשו” through the maxim that falsehood has no legs. A lie that contains no truth at its beginning cannot endure at all; therefore Esav must possess “something at his head,” but his end is “adei oveid.” Yaakov, by contrast, is “Sefas emes tikon la’ad” — truth that reaches and repairs all the way to the heel and the end. This supplies a sharp conceptual complement to R’ Tzadok’s image of the swine stretching out its split hoof. The deception works only because it displays a real-looking point of purity. Similarly, the nations may perform acts that resemble mitzvos or kindness; the outward form can contain enough truth to sustain the claim. The falsehood lies in making that partial truth represent the whole while the hidden interior remains directed to self. Yaakov’s response is not to deny that there is any true point in Esav.
