His hand takes hold of precisely that point and carries truth through to its conclusion. The distinction between Yaakov and Esav is therefore not simply ‘truth versus zero truth,’ but enduring truth versus borrowed truth that cannot survive to the end. What is holy in Esav is destined to be gathered into Yaakov; what is merely the pose of holiness is ultimately exposed.
דְּבֶאֱמֶת עַל יְדֵי זֶה קָלַט יַעֲקֹב גַּם כָּל מַה שֶּׁבֶּעָקֵב דְּעֵשָׂו, גַּם כֵּן לְקַבֵּל הַטּוֹב שֶׁבִּפְשִׁיטַת טְלָפָיו
for in truth, through this, Yaakov “absorbed” also all that was in the “heel” of Esav — to take even the good in his “stretched-out hooves,”
רַק שֶׁאֶצְלוֹ אֵינוֹ דֶּרֶךְ פְּשִׁיטַת טְלָפַיִם, רַק ״גּוּפוֹ אָחִיד בֵּיהּ״
only that with him [Yaakov] it is not by way of “stretching out hooves” [outward display], but rather “his [very] body grasps it.”
וְדַרְגָּא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל — רְצֹה לוֹמַר תַּלְמִיד חָכָם דְּאָחִיד בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא — זֶה ״לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי״

And the rung of “Yisrael” — meaning a talmid chacham who “grasps the Torah” — of this, “He has not done so for any [other] nation” (Tehillim 147:20)689Tehillim 147:20: “לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי, וּמִשְׁפָּטִים בַּל יְדָעוּם, הַלְלוּ יָהּ” — “He has not done so for any [other] nation; and His statutes — they know them not. Halleluyah.” Background: the closing verse of the psalm — God gave His word, His laws and statutes, to Yaakov/Israel alone; no other nation was granted them. Meforshim: by the plain sense, the Torah’s mishpatim are Israel’s unique portion, and “the nations do not know them” — which is why the verse crowns the psalm with praise. R’ Tzadok’s use: the rung of “Yisrael” — the talmid chacham who “grasps the Torah” from within — is that of which “He has not done so for any nation”; only the outer rung of “Yaakov” (bare mitzvah-deed, seen by the eye) has any counterpart among the nations and in Esav..
רַק דַּרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב, שֶׁהֵם עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ, דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בַּעֲלֵי מִצְווֹת לְבַד בְּפֹעַל מַעֲשֶׂה הַנִּגְלֵית בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
[But] the rung of “Yaakov” — the amei ha-aretz, Jews who are “masters of mitzvos” alone, in revealed deed in this world —
זֶה יֶשְׁנוֹ גַּם בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וּבְעֵשָׂו מִצַּד הִתְגַּלּוּת לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן
this is present also among the nations and in Esav, from the side of revelation to the eye;
דְּעִיקָּרוֹ הוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּעֵשָׂו לְשׁוֹן ״עֲשִׂיָּה״
for its essence is the rung of Esav, a term of “doing,”
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֶצְלוֹ הוּא רַק בְּעָקֵב עֲשִׂיָּה לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן
except that with him it is only in the “heel” of doing, [and only] to the eye.
וְיַעֲקֹב אָחַז גַּם בְּעָקֵב זֶה וּמְשָׁכוֹ אֵלָיו
And Yaakov grasped even this “heel” and drew it to himself;
וְעֵשָׂו בֶּאֱמֶת ״רֵיקָן מִכֹּל״, כִּי הוּא מוֹנֶה לַחַמָּה דְּ״רָזוֹהִי גַּלְיָין״
and Esav is in truth “empty of everything,” for he “counts by the sun,” whose “secrets are revealed”;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר ״אֵיךְ נֶחְפְּשׂוּ עֵשָׂו נִבְעוּ מַצְפֻּנָיו״

and of this it says, “how Esav was searched out, his hidden things laid bare” (Ovadiah 1:6)690Ovadiah 1:6: “אֵיךְ נֶחְפְּשׂוּ עֵשָׂו, נִבְעוּ מַצְפֻּנָיו” — “how Esav has been searched out, his hidden treasures laid bare!” Background: from Ovadiah’s single-chapter prophecy of the downfall of Edom (Esav) — his concealed stores will be ransacked and exposed, with nothing left hidden. Meforshim: by the plain sense, Esav’s secret hoards of wealth are plundered and brought to light. R’ Tzadok’s use: though Esav borrowed Israel’s “power of concealment” to mask his evil — “his secrets hidden” — that veil is only skin-deep; “how Esav was searched out, his hidden things laid bare” — in truth he is “empty of everything,” his emptiness revealed to all.,
דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ כֹּחַ הַהַצְפָּנָה, גַּם זֶה הוּא רַק לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן לְבַד נִרְאֶה כְּרָז וְסוֹד נֶעֱלָם, וּבֶאֱמֶת גַּלְיָין וְנִבְעוּ לַכֹּל

for although he had a “power of concealment,” even that is only to the eye — it [merely] appears as a hidden secret, but in truth [his contents] are revealed and laid bare to all. — Esav borrows Israel’s gift of concealment only to mask his own emptiness, but the borrowed veil is thin and cannot finally cover it.

items.h: The theme: Leah is alma d’iskasya. To the eye Esav seemed to hold that “power,” and Yaakov the tam seemed the reverse — so people thought the elder daughter fit for the elder son. But in her depths Leah has no bond with Esav at all, and Yaakov is inwardly “his brother in cunning.” Her perfection culminates in Zevulun, and she was even fit to bear Yosef — the perfection of the baal teshuvah, whose very sins become merits.

p: [ל] וְלֵאָה הִיא עָלְמָא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא, וְחָשְׁבוּ הַבְּרִיּוֹת דִּ״גְדוֹלָה לַגָּדוֹל״
And Leah is the “concealed world”; and people thought “the elder [daughter] for the elder [son],”
דִּלְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן הָיָה נִרְאֶה בְּעֵשָׂו כֹּחַ זֶה

for to the eye’s view this “power” appeared to be in Esav.691R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §61): “Esav is the firstborn as regards birth, which is the emergence into act — as in the creation of the world, "at first there was darkness"… and this world of Esav, in which darkness prevails, is first; but in the formation, which is alma d’iskasya — the thought of creation and the world’s conception — the right precedes.” Exactly the se’if: to the eye of the revealed world Esav comes first and seems to hold the power; in the concealed world, which is Leah’s, the order is reversed.
וְיַעֲקֹב מִצַּד הַתְּמִימוּת הָיָה נִרְאֶה לְהֵיפֶךְ
And Yaakov, from the side of [his] wholeness [temimus], appeared the reverse,
דְּהַתָּם הוּא שֶׁכְּפָיו כֵּן לִבּוֹ

for the “tam” is one whose heart matches his outward [hands]692Bereishis 25:27: “וַיִּגְדְּלוּ הַנְּעָרִים, וַיְהִי עֵשָׂו אִישׁ יֹדֵעַ צַיִד אִישׁ שָׂדֶה, וְיַעֲקֹב אִישׁ תָּם יֹשֵׁב אֹהָלִים” — “and the lads grew up, and Esav became a man who knew hunting, a man of the field, while Yaakov was a wholesome man [ish tam], dwelling in tents.” Background: the two brothers’ contrasting natures — Esav the hunter of the open field, Yaakov the “tam” who sat in the tents [of study]. Meforshim: Rashi glosses “tam” — “he was not expert [in deceit]; as his heart, so his mouth; one who is not sharp to deceive is called tam.” R’ Tzadok’s use: precisely because Yaakov is “tam” — his inner heart matching his outward conduct — he appeared to the world’s eye to lack Esav’s “power,” so that people supposed Leah “belonged” to Esav; yet in the hidden depths Yaakov is inwardly “his brother in cunning,” and the true rung of “Yisrael” is the concealed wisdom of the heart, which no outward eye perceives.;
וְרַק דַּרְגָּא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מַעֲמַקֵּי הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁ״אִישׁ תְּבוּנוֹת יִדְלֶנָּה״ דְּאֵין נִגְלֶה לְפֹעַל

but only the rung of “Yisrael” is the depths of the wisdom in the heart, which “a man of understanding draws up,” [and] which is not [outwardly] revealed.693R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayeitzei §10): “"where the birds nest" — in what place? In Lebanon — and these are the two birds spoken of in several places, the upper ones, which issue from Lebanon, which is the concealed [world].” The se’if’s alma d’iskasya precisely: Leah’s perfection is rooted in the upper, hidden place from which the revealed pairs issue — never visible in the order the eye reads.Leah and the hidden world — why the baal teshuvah can reveal a root deeper than visible purity: Shem MiShmuel, Vayeitzei 9:15, explicitly identifies Rachel with alma d’isgalya and Leah with alma d’iskasya. He associates Rachel’s revealed illumination with aseh tov and Leah’s higher hidden illumination with sur me’ra. The Ishbitz teaching on Berachos 34b (Mei HaShiloach II) adds the teshuvah dimension: the tzaddik gamur has a more purified body, but the soul of the baal teshuvah is hewn from a higher place; through the cry and broken heart of teshuvah it can reach an ‘omek amok’ beyond ordinary human daas. These sources clarify R’ Tzadok’s paradox that Leah, apparently the side whose affinity was misunderstood and assigned to Esav, is in her depth wholly alien to him and can culminate in the very perfection of teshuvah. Alma d’iskasya means that the decisive truth of the person is not always readable from the visible history. Yet the hidden root is not a shortcut around avodah. It becomes manifest through sur me’ra, brokenhearted return, and transformation. This is why R’ Tzadok can speak of the baal teshuvah’s sins eventually becoming merits without confusing him with Esav’s concealment of evil. Esav hides corruption beneath an outward claim; Leah’s world hides a holiness that is uncovered by genuine correction. One concealment falsifies the surface, while the other reveals that the surface was never the final measure of the soul.

וּבֶאֱמֶת גַּם דַּרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב הוּא כֵן, דְּאַף דְּהוּא תָּמִים מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ ״אָחִיו אֲנִי בְּרַמָּאוּת״694Megillah 13b: “‘And Yaakov told Rachel that he was her father’s brother’ — but was he her father’s brother? he was her father’s sister’s son! Rather, he said to her, ‘will you marry me?’ She said, ‘yes, but my father is a swindler and you cannot best him.’ He said, ‘I am his brother [equal] in swindling.’ She said, ‘and is it permitted for the righteous to resort to swindling?’ He said, ‘yes — “with the pure be pure, and with the crooked be wily” (II Shmuel 22).’ — He gave her sign-tokens; and in the end, when Leah [was substituted and] Rachel wished that she not be shamed, Rachel gave her the tokens.” [Yaakov’s “cunning” is a hidden depth used only “with the crooked.”]

And in truth the rung of Yaakov is likewise so: for though he is “tam,” nonetheless they said [that he told Rachel] “I am his [Lavan’s] brother in cunning”;695Megillah 13b: “‘And Yaakov told Rachel that he was her father’s brother’ — but was he her father’s brother? he was her father’s sister’s son! Rather, he said to her, ‘will you marry me?’ She said, ‘yes, but my father is a swindler and you cannot best him.’ He said, ‘I am his brother [equal] in swindling.’ She said, ‘and is it permitted for the righteous to resort to swindling?’ He said, ‘yes — “with the pure be pure, and with the crooked be wily” (II Shmuel 22).’ — He gave her sign-tokens; and in the end, when Leah [was substituted and] Rachel wished that she not be shamed, Rachel gave her the tokens.” [Yaakov’s “cunning” is a hidden depth used only “with the crooked.”]
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה רִימָּהוּ לָבָן לָתֵת לוֹ לֵאָה דֶּרֶךְ רַמָּאוּת וְלֹא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת
and through this, Lavan “tricked” him into [receiving] Leah by way of cunning, not openly.
כִּי מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת הָיָה נִרְאֶה לְעֵינֵי הָעוֹלָם דְּשַׁיָּיכָה לְעֵשָׂו
For from the side of [outer] revelation it appeared to the world’s eyes that she “belonged” to Esav,
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת מִצַּד מַדְרֵיגָתָהּ בְּאִתְכַּסְיָא הִיא עֲקֶרֶת הַבַּיִת בֵּית יַעֲקֹב בְּבִנְיַן הַשְּׁבָטִים
but in truth, from the side of her level “in concealment,” she is the akeres ha-bayis of the house of Yaakov, in the building of the tribes,
וּמִצַּד הַמַּעֲמַקִּים אֵין לָהּ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְעֵשָׂו כְּלָל

and from the side of the depths she has no connection to Esav at all.696R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §112): “and the reason he wanted this as a sign — whether the matter had issued from Hashem; unlike Eliezer, who had a different sign, for in a match one must look for a sign.” Exactly the se’if: what the outward eye reads as fitting is not the true pairing — the match must be read by a sign that discloses what issued from Above, which is why Leah’s depth has no bond with Esav at all.
וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת מַדְרֵיגָתָהּ שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם בְּלֵידַת זְבוּלוּן, לִינֹק ״שְׂפוּנֵי טְמוּנֵי [חוֹל]״
And this is the ultimate perfection of her level, completed at the birth of Zevulun — to “suck the hidden treasures [of the sand],”
דְּבָרִים יְקָרִים הַטְּמוּנִים בַּשֵּׂכֶל שֶׁיְּצִיאָתָם לְפֹעַל הוּא בִּזְבוּלוּן
precious things hidden in the mind, whose bringing-forth into actuality is in Zevulun,
שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא גִּילּוּי הַמַּטְמוֹן הַזֶּה דְּגִילּוּי שְׁכִינָה שֶׁבְּקֶרֶב לִבָּם
in whom is the revelation of this “buried treasure” — the revelation of the Shechinah that is within their hearts.
וְדַגַּם הַ״מּוֹרָא הַגָּדוֹל״ וְיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם, שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית שְׁאֵלַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵהָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And [so] too, the “great awe” and fear of Heaven — which is the ultimate that Hashem “asks” of a person in this world —
הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת בְּלִבְבָם מֵעַצְמוֹ נִמְשָׁךְ מִמֵּילָא מִגִּילּוּי הַשְּׁכִינָה
is in truth drawn into their hearts of itself, automatically, from the revelation of the Shechinah.
וְזֶהוּ הַקִּיבּוּל שָׂכָר נֶגֶד לֵוִי, אֲבָל שִׁמְעוֹן נִכְלָל בִּרְכָתוֹ וְנַחֲלָתוֹ בִּיהוּדָה
And this is the “receiving of reward” corresponding to Levi; but Shimon — his blessing and portion are subsumed within Yehudah.

וְהָיְתָה רְאוּיָה לֵאָה לְהוֹלִיד גַּם אֶת יוֹסֵף, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל דְּנִתְחַלֵּף בְּדִינָה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁדָּנָה לֵאָה דִּין בְּעַצְמָהּ697Berachos 60a: “‘And afterward she bore a daughter and called her name Dinah’ — what is ‘afterward’? Rav said: after Leah passed judgment upon herself, saying, ‘twelve tribes are destined to issue from Yaakov; six have come from me and four from the handmaids — that is ten; if this one is male, my sister Rachel will not be even like one of the handmaids!’ Immediately [the fetus] was turned into a female.” (And per Targum Yonasan, the fetuses were exchanged — Yosef passing to Rachel’s womb and Dinah to Leah’s.)

And Leah was [even] fit to bear Yosef as well, as the Sages said, that [Yosef] was “exchanged” for Dinah when Leah “rendered a judgment upon herself” [wishing her sister Rachel not be lesser than the maidservants].698Berachos 60a: “‘And afterward she bore a daughter and called her name Dinah’ — what is ‘afterward’? Rav said: after Leah passed judgment upon herself, saying, ‘twelve tribes are destined to issue from Yaakov; six have come from me and four from the handmaids — that is ten; if this one is male, my sister Rachel will not be even like one of the handmaids!’ Immediately [the fetus] was turned into a female.” (And per Targum Yonasan, the fetuses were exchanged — Yosef passing to Rachel’s womb and Dinah to Leah’s.)
וְזֶה הָיָה הַקִּיבּוּל שָׂכָר נֶגֶד שִׁמְעוֹן וִיהוּדָה
And this was the “receiving of reward” corresponding to Shimon and Yehudah;
דִּשְׁלֵימוּת מַדְרֵיגַת בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר חֲטָאָם — [שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית] — וְהַכֹּל זְכִיּוֹת, וְהוּא שָׁב לִהְיוֹת צַדִּיק גָּמוּר

for the perfection of the baal teshuvah level is [reached] when their [very] sins — [which were, as it were, arranged and set in place from the six days of creation] — all [become] merits, and he returns to being a complete tzaddik. — the deepest teshuvah reaching so far back that the sins themselves prove to have been “arranged from the six days of creation,” and turn wholly to merit.

items.h: The theme: The full “clarification” that Yosef and Yehudah are one root awaits the Future (“the wood of Yosef and Yehudah, one to the other”). In this world they appear opposite: Yehudah’s line begins with Er and Onan, Shimon’s with Shittim/Zimri — bris-corruption and cohabiting with a gentile, whose prohibition the Torah left implicit. In truth, the seed of Israel has no connection to a gentile woman; any “longing” is one-sided (Potifar’s wife, Turnusrufus’s wife) — until conversion, when she becomes “a new creature.”

p: [לא] וְעִיקַּר בֵּירוּר זֶה לְעֵין כֹּל יִהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד
And the essential clarification of this [that Yosef and Yehudah are one root] will be, before all eyes, in the Future,
וְאָז יְקָרֵב הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ ״עֵץ יוֹסֵף וִיהוּדָה אֶחָד אֶל אֶחָד״ לִהְיוֹת חֲבֵירִים

when Hashem will bring near “the wood of Yosef and [of] Yehudah, one to the other, to be companions” (Yechezkel 37:19)699Yechezkel 37:19: “הִנֵּה אֲנִי לֹקֵחַ אֶת עֵץ יוֹסֵף אֲשֶׁר בְּיַד אֶפְרַיִם וְשִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל חֲבֵרָיו, וְנָתַתִּי אוֹתָם עָלָיו אֶת עֵץ יְהוּדָה, וַעֲשִׂיתִם לְעֵץ אֶחָד, וְהָיוּ אֶחָד בְּיָדִי” — “behold, I take the wood of Yosef, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel his companions, and I will set them upon it — the wood of Yehudah — and make them into one wood, and they shall be one in My hand.” Background: from Yechezkel’s prophecy of the “two sticks” (37:15–19) — the prophet takes two pieces of wood inscribed for Yosef (Ephraim) and for Yehudah and joins them into one, a sign of the future reunification of the divided kingdoms of Israel and Judah into one people under one king (Mashiach). Meforshim: the commentators read the two sticks as the two monarchies — the ten tribes under Ephraim/Yosef, and Yehudah — to be reunited in the Redemption; R’ Tzadok’s phrase “one to the other” (echad el echad) is drawn from the adjacent verse (37:17), “and bring them near one to another into one stick.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the full “clarification” that Yosef and Yehudah — who appear as opposites in this world — are truly one root will be revealed “before all eyes” only in the Future, when God joins “the wood of Yosef and Yehudah, one to the other, to be companions.”.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דַּעֲדַיִין הָאֲמִיתּוּת בְּהֶעְלֵם, הֵם הֲפָכִים

Not so in this world, where — the truth being [still] concealed — they [appear as] opposites.700R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash §15): “to instruct before him — and it is brought in the Midrash,”to establish for him a house of study."" Exactly the se’if: Yosef and Yehudah appear opposed — deed against heart — yet the first thing sent ahead into exile is the house of study, in which the two are already one.Shem MiShmuel — the future joining of Yosef and Yehudah repairs the root of their apparent opposition: Shem MiShmuel, Korach 2:21, reads Yechezkel’s two sticks — the wood of Yosef and the wood of Yehudah becoming ‘one in My hand’ — as the final tikkun of the root from which later divisions grew. He links that future unity to the healing of the sale of Yosef and cites the parallel promise that Ephraim will no longer envy Yehudah and Yehudah will no longer oppress Ephraim. This is a close complement to R’ Tzadok’s insistence that the two lines are one at their source even though this world presents them as opposites. Yosef is the visibly guarded yesod, the tzaddik whose sanctity is expressed through restraint and purity; Yehudah is the line in which failure, confession, and teshuvah become the road to Malchus. If one judges only by the revealed form, each can seem to invalidate the other. The prophetic future does not erase either model. It makes them ‘one wood’: the tzaddik’s purity and the baal teshuvah’s depth are seen as two expressions of one Divine root. This also frames the difficult material that follows concerning Yehudah, Shimon, and bris. R’ Tzadok is not lowering the Torah’s prohibitions; he is tracing how the very line whose revealed history contains grave failure can, through teshuvah and clarification, disclose a unity with Yosef that was hidden all along.
כִּי הַתְחָלַת הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת יְהוּדָה בְּצֶאֱצָאָיו, שֶׁבָּזֶה הוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כֹּחוֹת אָבוֹת הַנֶּעֱלָמִים לְפֹעַל, הָיָה עֵר וְאוֹנָן
For the beginning of Yehudah’s spreading-forth into his offspring — in which the hidden powers of the Avos come into actuality — was [with] Er and Onan,
שֶׁהֵם פָּגְמוּ הַבְּרִית בְּמַעֲשֶׂה דְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל
who “corrupted the covenant” in the manner of the generation of the Flood.
וּמִזֶּרַע שִׁמְעוֹן הָיָה הַכ״ד אֶלֶף שֶׁנָּפְלוּ בַּשִּׁטִּים, וְגַם נְשִׂיא שִׁבְטוֹ, וְהוּא פְּגַם דְּבִיאַת אֲרַמִּית

And from the seed of Shimon were the 24,000 who fell at Shittim, and also the prince of his tribe [Zimri] — this being the “corruption” of cohabiting with a gentile woman.701R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §90): “"concerning the matter of Peor and concerning the matter of Kozbi"… for they were fenced-in as regards forbidden relations, only that they reasoned there is no prohibition with the nations, as with the daughter of Yisro — yet in any case he begets a child for idolatry.” Exactly the se’if’s point: the prohibition of cohabiting with a gentile woman is the one the Torah left implicit, and its true severity lies in what is begotten, not in the act alone.
דִּשְׁנֵי אֵלֶּה לֹא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ אַזְהָרַת אִיסּוּרָן בְּפֵירוּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה, רַק עוֹנְשָׁן לְבַד
For these two — [bris-corruption and cohabiting with a gentile] — their prohibition is not explicitly stated in the Torah, only their punishment;
וַהֲרֵי בְּכָל מָקוֹם ״לֹא עָנַשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִזְהִיר״

and everywhere [the rule is] “[the Torah] did not punish unless it [first] warned702“The Torah did not decree punishment without first issuing a warning” (a governing rule of the Gemara; see, e.g., Yoma 81a; Sanhedrin 54a): a fixed principle that no act is punishable under the Torah unless the Torah first stated an explicit prohibition (azharah) against it — so wherever Scripture records only a punishment, the Gemara must seek out the corresponding warning. R’ Tzadok’s use: since the two “corruptions” here — bris-corruption and cohabiting with a gentile woman — carry only a stated punishment and no explicit prohibition, the very halachah “was hidden” (even from Moshe, until Pinchas recalled it); this reflects that, in the deepest truth, the seed of Israel has no real “connection” to a gentile woman at all — there is, as it were, nothing there to formally forbid..”
וְעַל כֵּן נִתְעַלְּמָה מִמֶּנּוּ הֲלָכָה מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה עַד שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ פִּנְחָס ״כָּךְ לִמַּדְתָּנוּ דְּקַנָּאִים פּוֹגְעִין [בּוֹ]״

And therefore the halachah “was hidden” from Moshe Rabbeinu, until Pinchas said to him, “thus you taught us, that ‘zealots strike him.’”703Sanhedrin 82a: [Zimri] seized her [Kozbi] by her forelock and brought her before Moshe. He said, “son of Amram — is this one forbidden or permitted? and if you say forbidden — who permitted the daughter of Yisro to you?” The halachah was hidden from him [Moshe] — And it is written, “and Pinchas saw” — what did he see? Rav said: “he saw the deed and remembered the halachah.” He said to [Moshe], “great-uncle, did you not teach us on your descent from Sinai, ‘one who cohabits with an Aramean woman — zealots may strike him’?” [The prohibition was left unstated, and the halachah “was hidden” until Pinchas recalled it.]704R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Matos §12): “and in the incident of Zimri they showed him that sometimes, for a certain need, one must use precisely the trait of anger and zeal — therefore this halachah, that "the zealous strike him," was hidden from him [Moshe], since this matter of zealotry had no relation to him at all; rather Pinchas came and took what was fitting for him.” Exactly the se’if: the law of kana’in pog’in bo is left unstated in the Torah because it belongs to a rung outside the ordinary revealed order.
דְּבֶאֱמֶת אֵין בּוֹ עוֹנֶשׁ מְפוֹרָשׁ, דְּמִצַּד הָאֲמִיתּוּת אֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת לְזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל עִם בַּת נֵכָר כְּלָל, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיַּחְשֹׁק בָּהּ

For in truth there is no explicit [Torah] punishment [for it], since from the side of the truth the seed of Israel has no connection whatsoever to a gentile woman, and it is impossible for him [truly] to desire her;
וְהִיא בּוֹ יֵשׁ לָהּ שַׁיָּיכוּת מַה
[rather,] it is she who has some “connection” to him.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּאֵשֶׁת פּוֹטִיפֶרַע דְּרָאֲתָה בְּאִצְטַגְנִינוּת כו׳, וְהַחִיבּוּר הָיָה עַל יְדֵי בִּתָּהּ
as they said of the wife of Potifar, that she “saw by astrology [that she was to have offspring from Yosef],” and the [true] union [with Yosef] was [ultimately] through her daughter [Osnas];
וְכֵן כְּאֵשֶׁת טוּרְנוּסְרוּפוּס וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דְּלוּלֵי זֶה לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ זֶה בַּאֲנָשִׁים כָּאֵלּוּ

and likewise with the wife of Turnusrufus and R’ Akiva [whom she later married as a convert] — for otherwise, [such attraction] has no relevance to men such as these.705Bereishis Rabbah 85 (on the wife of Potifar): [R’ Yehoshua ben Levi said] she saw by her astrology that she was destined to raise up a child from [Yosef], but did not know whether from herself or from her daughter — and the union was fulfilled through her daughter Osnas. Avodah Zarah 20a (on R’ Akiva): he saw the wife of the wicked Turnusrufus — and he spat, laughed, and wept: spat, for she came from a putrid drop; laughed, for she was destined to convert and he would marry her; and wept, that such beauty would ultimately decay in the dust. [R’ Akiva’s reaction shows the “longing” was one-sided and future-oriented — she would convert and marry him.]
וְכֵן בְּדוֹר כְּדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר, דִּלְעוֹלָם הָרַע שׂוֹנֵא אֶת הַטּוֹב, וְאֵין אָרוּר מִדַּבֵּק בְּבָרוּךְ
And so [it is] with a generation like the generation of the Wilderness: evil always hates the good, and “the accursed does not cleave to the blessed”;
וְשָׁמַעְתִּי מְדוּיָּק לְשׁוֹן זֶה, וְלֹא אָמַר בְּהֵיפֶךְ ״אֵין בָּרוּךְ״ כו׳, דְּרוֹצֶה לוֹמַר דְּגַם הָאָרוּר אֵין רוֹצֶה

and I heard [it noted] precisely that this wording706The source is the Ishbitzer (Mei HaShiloach), R’ Tzadok’s rebbe. R’ Tzadok’s “v’shamati” (“and I heard”) characteristically signals a teaching received from his teacher, R’ Mordechai Yosef Leiner of Izhbitz, author of the Mei HaShiloach. The idea here — that even the “accursed” gentile does not truly desire the union, and that a gentile’s apparent “longing” masks a hidden root-connection disclosed only in the Future — is the Ishbitzer’s teaching on Zimri and Kozbi. See Mei HaShiloach, Parashas Balak (on “v’hinei ish mi-bnei Yisrael… ha-Midyanis”): before the deed he is called “a man of the Children of Israel,” but afterward “a man of Israel” — “for in the Future the Holy One will clarify that this soul was bound to him at his root, as is brought in the writings of the Arizal”; and Mei HaShiloach, Parashas Pinchas (on “va-yar Pinchas”): “she was his soulmate (bas zug) from the six days of creation, as explained in the writings of the Arizal… but the depth of the root of the matter was hidden from [Pinchas].” R’ Tzadok’s continuation here — the Arizal on Shechem (“chashkah nafsho”), reincarnated in Zimri — draws directly on these passages. — and not the reverse — means that even the “accursed” one does not [truly] desire [the union].
וְכֵן נוֹדָע מֵהָאֲרִ״י ז״ל בִּשְׁכֶם דְּ״חָשְׁקָה נַפְשׁוֹ״ כו׳, דְּהָיָה לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת וְנִתְגַּלְגֵּל בְּזִמְרִי
And so it is known from the Arizal regarding Shechem, of whom “his soul longed [for Dinah]” — that he [having a hidden root-connection] was later reincarnated in Zimri.
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִתְגַּיְּירוּ אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת, רַק אַחַר כָּךְ ״גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר כְּקָטָן שֶׁנּוֹלַד״
Except that, in any case, so long as they have not converted they have no connection [to holiness]; only afterward — “a convert who converts is like a newborn child.”
וְעַל כֵּן רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רַק דְּשָׂחַק וְיָדַע דְּשַׁיָּיכָה לוֹ, דְּעַל כֵּן נִתְעוֹרֵר בָּהּ הַחֵשֶׁק
And therefore R’ Akiva only “smiled” [when he beheld Turnusrufus’s wife], knowing she [would eventually] belong to him — which is why the longing was aroused in her;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בּוֹ לֹא פָּעֲלָה כְּלוּם לְהַעֲלוֹת אַף הִרְהוּר כָּל שֶׁהוּא בַּלֵּב, וְשֶׁיִּצְטָרֵךְ לְאֵיזֶה כְּפִיַּית יֵצֶר כְּלָל
but in him she effected nothing — not so much as to raise any stray thought, [such] that he would need any “subduing of the inclination” at all,
כֵּיוָן דִּבְגֵיוּתָהּ אֵין לָהּ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת עִמּוֹ
since in her gentile state she has no connection to him;
וְדַי הָיָה לוֹ בִּרְקִיקָה לְבַד [שֶׁהוּצְרַךְ לָהּ לִהְיוֹתוֹ בֶּן גֵּרִים]
and a mere “spitting” [in disgust] sufficed for him — which he needed [only] because he was himself the son of converts.
וְאוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד [בִּמְנָחוֹת] שֶׁהוּצְרַךְ לְצִיצִיּוֹתָיו שֶׁיִּטְפְּחוּ וְיִמְנָעוּהוּ

And that student [in Menachos] who needed his tzitzis to “slap him in the face” and hold him back707Menachos 44a: A man scrupulous in the mitzvah of tzitzis heard of a harlot overseas who took four hundred zuz as her fee; he sent it and set a time. When he came and sat upon the bed, “his four tzitzis came and slapped him across the face”; he slipped down and sat upon the ground, and she did likewise. She pressed him to explain, and he told her of the mitzvah of tzitzis — “which testified before me four times, ‘the Torah of Hashem my God.’” In the end she sought out his beis midrash, converted, and married him — “and the very couches she had spread for him in prohibition, she [now] spread for him in permission.” —
שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת ״שְׂפוּנֵי טְמוּנֵי״ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם חִיבּוּר עִם גּוֹי
[this] is the revelation of the “hidden treasures” of Israel, that they have no [true] union with a gentile.
לְפִי שֶׁכְּבָר נִשְׁתַּקַּע קְצָת בְּהוֹצֵי דְּסוֹבְכִים לְאָסָא
[The tzitzis were needed] because he had already sunk a little into “the thorns that encircle the myrtle”;
וְהִיא גַּם הִיא נִשְׁתַּקְּעָה בִּזְנוּת וְלֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁתִּתְגַּיֵּיר, רַק עַל יְדֵי סִיבָּה זוֹ
and she [the harlot] too was sunk in immorality, and could not have converted except through this very episode —
שֶׁתַּצִּיעַ מַצָּעוֹת בְּאִיסּוּר, עַד שֶׁיִּתְעוֹרֵר בּוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם דְּיַהֲדוּת הַגָּמוּר
that she “prepared the couches” [for] a forbidden [act], until the hidden root of complete Jewishness was aroused in him;
וּבָזֶה מָשַׁךְ גַּם נִיצוֹץ הַטּוֹב דְּגָנִיז בְּגַוֵּיהּ שֶׁיִּתְעוֹרֵר בְּקִרְבָּהּ הָרָצוֹן לְהִתְגַּיֵּיר
and thereby he [also] drew forth the spark of good hidden within her, so that the desire to convert be aroused in her,
וְזָכָה שֶׁתַּצִּיעַ לוֹ הַמַּצָּעוֹת בְּהֶיתֵּר
and he merited that she [ultimately] prepare those [same] couches for him in permission [as his wife].
וְלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בָּזֶה ״לֶאֱכוֹל פַּגָּה״
And [the concept of] “eating an unripe fig [before its time]” does not apply here;
דְּרַק בְּזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל שַׁיָּיךְ פַּגָּה, דְּהוּא אוֹתָהּ הַפְּרִי רַק דְּעַתָּה לֹא הִגִּיעַ הַזְּמַן
for “an unripe fig” applies only to the seed of Israel — [where] it is the [same] fruit, only that its time has not yet come;
אֲבָל גּוֹיָה שֶׁנִּתְגַּיְּירָה הִיא בְּרִיָּה חֲדָשָׁה וּפָנִים חֲדָשׁוֹת, וְאֵין זֶה אוֹתָהּ הַפְּרִי פַּגָּה כְּלָל

but a gentile woman who converts is “a new creature,” a “new face” — and this is not [merely] that same fruit unripe, at all. — so that the Jewish “unripe fig” is the right fruit at the wrong time, whereas the convert is not that fruit at all, but an altogether new one.

items.h: The theme: “Shelo asani goy”: some Jewish souls come by reincarnation into gentiles — distinct from a convert’s soul, which is from another chamber. Converts are kelipas nogah, turning from evil to good, extracted from the “woman of harlotry”; and even a soul caught in her net has a hidden longing to cleave to Israel. So too with Midyan: the generation of knowledge, refined by Torah and mann, could not truly lust — which is why Bilaam’s eye was blinded.

p: [לב] אֲבָל יָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁאוֹמְרִים ״שֶׁלֹּא עָשַׂנִי גּוֹי״

But it is known [regarding] what we say [in the blessing] “who did not make me a gentile708Menachos 43b: the source of the morning identity-blessings — the beraisa (R’ Meir / R’ Yehudah) that a person must bless each day “she-asani Yisrael,” and in the accepted nusach “shelo asani goy,” “shelo asani ishah,” “shelo asani bur/aved.” Background: these blessings affirm the distinctiveness of the Jew’s very being. R’ Tzadok’s use: the negative wording “who did not make me a goy” (rather than “who made me a Jew”) already hints at his point — that some Jewish souls do descend, by way of gilgul, into gentiles; hence one thanks God that he was not “made a gentile.”,”
דְּיֵשׁ נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבָּאִים בְּסוֹד הַגִּלְגּוּל בְּגוֹיִם
that there are Jewish souls who come, by way of the secret of reincarnation, [into] gentiles.
וְזֶה אֵין לוֹ עִנְיָן לְגֵרִים
And this has no bearing on [ordinary] converts,
דְּנֶפֶשׁ הַגֵּר הוּא מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר וְלֹא מִמַּחְצַב הַנְּשָׁמוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
for the soul of a convert is from another place, not from the “quarry” of the souls of Israel;
וְזֶה יֵשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת עִם נַפְשׁוֹת הַגּוֹיִם עַצְמָם וּמִטִּיקְלָא דִּידְהוּ, שֶׁהוּא בְּחֶדֶר אַחֵר כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת [ע״ז ה.] בְּשֵׁם הָרַ״ר אֶלְחָנָן

and this [convert’s soul] has a connection to the souls of the gentiles themselves, and to “their scale” — which is in “another chamber,” as Tosafos said [Avodah Zarah 5a] in the name of R’ Elchanan.709R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayechi §15): “to provoke the good inclination against the evil inclination, and to prevent a person from forbidden acts; and the utterance "Anochi" — which is to bring holiness into the heart — was not said in the language of command, but in the language [of statement].” Exactly the se’if: the convert’s root is kelipas nogah, which turns toward the good — and what turns it is not a command imposed from without but a holiness brought into the heart.
וְכַנּוֹדָע גַּם כֵּן עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַסּוֹד דְּהֵם בְּסוֹד קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ דְּמִתְהַפֶּכֶת מֵרַע לְטוֹב
And as is known, too, by way of the secret, that they [converts] are in the secret of kelipas nogah, which “turns over” from evil to good —
שֶׁהוּא סוֹד ״נֹגַהּ לוֹ סָבִיב״

the secret of “a brightness [nogah] round about it” (Yechezkel 1:4)710Yechezkel 1:4: “וָאֵרֶא וְהִנֵּה רוּחַ סְעָרָה בָּאָה מִן הַצָּפוֹן, עָנָן גָּדוֹל וְאֵשׁ מִתְלַקַּחַת וְנֹגַהּ לוֹ סָבִיב, וּמִתּוֹכָהּ כְּעֵין הַחַשְׁמַל מִתּוֹךְ הָאֵשׁ” — “and I saw, and behold, a stormwind came from the north, a great cloud and a flashing fire, with a brightness [nogah] round about it, and from its midst like the gleam of chashmal from within the fire.” Background: the opening of Yechezkel’s Merkavah vision. Meforshim: in Kabbalah “nogah” is the intermediate kelipah — the “brightness” encircling the holiness, half-good and half-evil, able to be “turned” wholly to good. R’ Tzadok’s use: converts are rooted in kelipas nogah, the “nogah lo saviv” — the shell that surrounds the holy and can be flipped from evil to good.,
שֶׁהֵם הָרְשָׁעִים ״אֲשֶׁר סָבִיב יִתְהַלָּכוּן״ סָבִיב לַקְּדֻשָּׁה

[for] they are the wicked “who walk round about” (Tehillim 12:9)711Tehillim 12:9: “סָבִיב רְשָׁעִים יִתְהַלָּכוּן, כְּרֻם זֻלּוּת לִבְנֵי אָדָם” — “the wicked walk round about, when vileness is exalted among men.” Background: the psalm laments an age in which the wicked hold sway. R’ Tzadok’s use: read with the nogah imagery, the wicked “walk round about” the holiness — positioned at its periphery, like the shell encircling the fruit. — around the holiness,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ ״צִוָּה לְיַעֲקֹב סְבִיבָיו צָרָיו״

along the lines of “He commanded concerning Yaakov that his foes be round about him” (Eichah 1:17)712Eichah 1:17: “פֵּרְשָׂה צִיּוֹן בְּיָדֶיהָ אֵין מְנַחֵם לָהּ, צִוָּה ה׳ לְיַעֲקֹב סְבִיבָיו צָרָיו, הָיְתָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם לְנִדָּה בֵּינֵיהֶם” — “Tziyon spreads out her hands, there is none to comfort her; Hashem has commanded concerning Yaakov that his foes be round about him; Yerushalayim has become a niddah among them.” Background: from the first kinah of Eichah — Yaakov hemmed in by his enemies “round about.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this too is the “surrounding” of holiness by the shell — the foes set around Yaakov, at his boundary, as kelipas nogah that encircles the holy..
וּמֵהֶם הֵם הַגֵּרִים, דְּגָלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל זֶה — לְהוֹסִיף גֵּרִים

And from them come the converts — [for] “Israel was exiled” for this: to add converts (Pesachim 87b)713Pesachim 87b: “R’ Elazar said: The Holy One, blessed be He, exiled Israel among the nations only in order that converts be added to them [ela kdei she-yitosfu aleihem gerim], as it says (Hoshea 2:25), ‘and I will sow her for Me in the land.’”Tanya — kelipas nogah is a mixed middle that can be clarified and raised: Tanya, Likutei Amarim ch. 7, defines kelipas nogah as an intermediate realm between the three completely impure kelipos and kedushah. It contains good mixed with evil; therefore at times it descends and is included with the impure side, and at times its good is separated and it rises into holiness. The Alter Rebbe illustrates this with ordinary permitted physical things: when used merely for bodily appetite they remain in nogah, but when directed to avodas Hashem their vitality can itself ascend. This provides a useful conceptual parallel to R’ Tzadok’s language here about converts and the extraction of holiness from a mixed exterior. The categories should not simply be equated — R’ Tzadok is discussing the origins of souls and geirus, while Tanya is explaining the spiritual status of permitted worldly vitality — but the underlying structure is similar. A mixed domain is not fixed by its present location. Its hidden good can be separated from the evil surrounding it and incorporated into kedushah. That model helps explain why R’ Tzadok can describe a soul or spark as caught in an alien environment without treating the environment itself as holy. The point of the descent is birur: once the good is truly detached from the old identification, it does not remain a sanctified fragment of the shell; it rises into a new belonging.;
עַל יְדֵי שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל דִּקְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ, שֶׁהִיא ״אֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים״ הַמְהַלֶּכֶת בָּתַר ״אֵשֶׁת חַיִל״ כְּקוֹפָא בָּתַר בַּר נָשׁ כַּנּוֹדָע

through the dominion of the “base man” of kelipas nogah, which is a “woman of harlotry” that “walks after” the “woman of valor,” like an ape after a man, as is known.714R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Chalomot §13): “on the verse "and be whole" — [the parable of] the noblewoman: "there is no dross in you except the nail of the little finger; pare it a little and be whole."” The se’if’s kelipas nogah exactly: what stands between a soul and Israel is not its substance but a thin outer rim — pared away, what remains was whole all along.
וְשׁוֹלֶטֶת בְּאֵשֶׁת חַיִל ״לְרַע לוֹ״, דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוֹצִיאוּ בִּלְעָהּ מִפִּיהָ — הֵם נַפְשׁוֹת הַגֵּרִים הַנִּקְלָטִים מֵהָרַע לְטוֹב

and it “rules over the woman of valor to [its own] detriment,” for through this they [Israel] “extract its swallowed [prey] from its mouth” — these being the souls of the converts, [re]absorbed from evil to good.715R’ Tzadok — parallel (Likkutei Maamarim §15): “for Avraham was the first of the converts — that he was born of the nations according to natural descent, and afterward recognized [his Creator] and converted; and with regard to the nations, recognition through one’s own striving is called "what a person illumines"… yet Avraham merited afterward the name "ezrachi," that he is not a convert, and they said, "Avraham is called Yisrael."” Exactly the se’if: the convert’s soul comes from “another chamber,” and its whole ascent is the passage from a self-kindled light to a native one.
וּשְׁלִיטָתָהּ הֵם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הַנִּתְפָּשִׂים בְּרִשְׁתָּהּ לְהִתְגַּלְגֵּל בַּגּוֹיִם וְאֵין מִתְגַּיְּירִים
And [the object of] its dominion are the souls caught in its net, to be reincarnated among the gentiles and not convert;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיהוּ לָא חָזֵי — מַזָּלֵיהּ חָזֵי, וְיֵשׁ לוֹ חֵשֶׁק לְהִתְדַּבֵּק בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל

but nonetheless, “even though he [himself] does not see, his mazal sees” (Megillah 3a)716Megillah 3a: “Even though [a person] himself does not see, his mazal sees [iyhu lo chazi, mazalei chazi].” (One is affected even by what he does not consciously perceive — hence Bilaam’s power to sense.) — and he has a longing to cleave to Israel.
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ הָיָה הָעִנְיָן הַזְּנוּת דִּבְנוֹת מִדְיָן
And of this kind was the matter of the “harlotry” with the daughters of Midyan;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב [בְּסֵפֶר תִּפְאֶרֶת יוֹנָתָן פָּרָשַׁת פִּנְחָס] דְּחָלִילָה לַחְשֹׁד זִמְרִי וּשְׁאָר דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר — דֵּעָה, אוֹכְלֵי מָן — שֶׁיֶּחְטְאוּ בְּתַאֲווֹת מְגוּנּוֹת

and as [R’ Yonasan Eybeschutz] wrote [in Tiferes Yehonasan, Parashas Pinchas], that God forbid to suspect Zimri and the rest of the generation of the Wilderness — a generation of knowledge, eaters of the mann — of sinning through debased desires;
רַק כָּל חֲטָאִים שֶׁלָּהֶם הָיָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם עַל יְדֵי אֵיזֶה טָעוּת וּשְׁגָגָה שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּאֹרֶךְ עַל פִּי דַּרְכּוֹ

but rather all their “sins” were for the sake of Heaven, through some error or inadvertence — see there at length, according to his approach.717Tiferes Yehonasan (Parashas Pinchas) — R’ Yonasan Eybeschutz asks why Moav sent the daughters of Midyan to entice Israel rather than their own daughters, and explains (per his approach) that Balak — a greater diviner than Bilaam — foresaw that from a union of an Israelite with a daughter of Moav would issue the one destined to “remove wickedness from the world”: namely Boaz and Ruth the Moabite, from whom came David HaMelech, who would “cast Moav to the ground.” R’ Tzadok cites this to show that even those apparent “sins” were, at root, “for the sake of Heaven” (see there at length).
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הֵם סָמְכוּ עַל זֶה גּוּפֵיהּ
But in truth, they [themselves] relied on this very [point]:
שֶׁיָּדְעוּ דִּכְבָר גָּדְלוּ אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה עַל הַתּוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה וּבַאֲכִילַת מָן שֶׁנִּזְדַּכֵּךְ גּוּפָם לְגַמְרֵי, וְנִבְלְעוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּגוּפָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל

that they knew they had already grown up for forty years upon Torah and [Divine] service and eating the mann, by which their bodies were wholly refined and the words of Torah “absorbed” into their bodies, as the Sages said;
וְהִכִּירוּ בְּעַצְמָם דִּנְקִיִּים מִתַּאֲווֹת לְגַמְרֵי וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּתְאַוּוּ לִזְנוּת לְדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and they recognized in themselves that they were entirely clean of [base] desires, and that it was impossible for them to lust after immorality — after something that is not the will of Hashem.
וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה נִסְמֵית עֵינוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע שֶׁאָמַר ״וּמִסְפָּר אֶת רֹבַע יִשְׂרָאֵל״
And it was on account of this [holiness] that “the eye of that wicked one [Bilaam] was blinded,” who said, “and the number [rova] of Israel” (Bamidbar 23:10),
דְּרָאָה שֶׁכָּל תַּאֲווֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם גַּם כֵּן בִּקְדֻשָּׁה וְחָבִיב אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

for he saw that all their “desires,” too, are in holiness, and are precious before Hashem. — what Bilaam took for Israel’s vulnerability was in fact their invulnerability: even their cravings could not be truly base.

items.h: The theme: Bilaam’s counsel to entice via the daughters of Midyan rested on a hidden truth: the very “joining with the daughters of Moav” would one day yield David and Mashiach (through Rus, after conversion). Bilaam knew the time had not come — the women were “unripe,” without conversion — so he induced the union prematurely, cleaving to the “side of death.” Kozbi held a spark of Dinah; Moshe/Yosef and the “priest of Midyan” are the secret of Yesod Abba vs. its “husk,” the “woman of strife.”

p: [לג] וְנָתַן עֵצָה לְהַכְשִׁילָם בִּבְנוֹת מִדְיָן
And [Bilaam] gave counsel to cause them to stumble through the daughters of Midyan.
דְּרַק בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהוּא וְהִיא מִזֶּרַע קֹדֶשׁ וּדְבוּקִים בִּקְדֻשָּׁה וּקְרוּאִים ״בְּנֵי אֵל חָי״, כָּל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם הֵם פְּעוּלַת צַדִּיק לְחַיִּים וְדָבוּק בְּחִיּוּת חֵי הָעוֹלָמִים

For only among the Children of Israel, where both he and she are of holy seed, cleaving to holiness and called “sons of the living God718Hoshea 2:1: “וְהָיָה מִסְפַּר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּחוֹל הַיָּם… וְהָיָה בִּמְקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם לֹא עַמִּי אַתֶּם, יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם בְּנֵי אֵל חָי” — “and the number of the Children of Israel shall be like the sand of the sea… and it shall be, in the place where it was said to them, ‘you are not My people,’ it shall be said to them, ‘sons of the living God.’” Background: Hoshea’s word of consolation — Israel, though rebuked, will be restored and named “sons of the living God” (the Sages take this as proof that even when called “not My people” they remain His children). R’ Tzadok’s use: only among Israel — both partners “of holy seed,” called “sons of the living God” — is a marital union “the deed of a tzaddik, unto life,” bound to the vitality of the Life of the worlds.,” are all their acts “the deed of a tzaddik, unto life719Mishlei 10:16: “פְּעֻלַּת צַדִּיק לְחַיִּים, תְּבוּאַת רָשָׁע לְחַטָּאת” — “the wage of a tzaddik is unto life; the produce of a wicked man is unto sin.” Background: Mishlei contrasts the fruits of the righteous (life) with those of the wicked (sin). R’ Tzadok’s use: he reads “peulas tzaddik l’chaim” of the marital act itself — among Israel it is “a deed of a tzaddik, unto life”; but with “the daughter of a foreign god” the same act becomes “tevu’as rasha l’chatas,” bound to the side of death.,” bound to the vitality of the Life of the worlds.
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁיִּדְבַּק בְּבַת אֵל נֵכָר שֶׁהִיא מִסִּטְרָא דְּמוֹתָא, גָּרַם מִיתָה לָהֶם וְלְכ״ד אֶלֶף

But when one cleaves to “the daughter of a foreign god,” who is from the side of death720Malachi 2:11: “בָּגְדָה יְהוּדָה… כִּי חִלֵּל יְהוּדָה קֹדֶשׁ ה׳ אֲשֶׁר אָהֵב, וּבָעַל בַּת אֵל נֵכָר” — “Yehudah has dealt treacherously… for Yehudah has profaned the holiness of Hashem which He loves, and has married the daughter of a foreign god.” Background: Malachi rebukes the returnees for intermarriage — “marrying the daughter of a foreign god.” Meforshim: the Sages apply “bas El neichar” to the gentile woman and to the very charge of the Zimri episode (Sanhedrin 82a). R’ Tzadok’s use: cleaving to “the daughter of a foreign god” is “from the side of death” — it brought death upon the 24,000, for the offspring “is like her” and never counts as the “seed of Israel.”, it brought death upon them — upon the 24,000 —
כִּי בִּהְיוֹת וָלָד כְּמוֹתָהּ הֲרֵי אֵין זֶה נִקְרָא ״רֹבַע יִשְׂרָאֵל״ כְּלָל, מַה שֶּׁבָּא לְגוּף הַגּוֹיָה
for since the offspring [would be] like her, this is not called “the seed of Israel” at all — [being] what enters the body of the gentile woman.
הוּא יָדַע זֶה, דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּתְחַבְּרוּ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ אֵיזֶה שַׁיָּיכוּת
He [Bilaam] knew this — that they could not join unless there were some [root-]connection;
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר ״לְכָה אִיעָצְךָ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה הָעָם הַזֶּה לְעַמְּךָ בְּאַחֲרִית [הַיָּמִים]״ וְגוֹמֵר
and this is what he said, “Come, I will counsel you [as to] what this people will do to your people in the End [of Days]” (Bamidbar 24:14);
וְרַז״ל דָּרְשׁוּ ״אִיעָצְךָ״ עֵצָה דִּזְנוּת, וְלִכְאוֹרָה הֲרֵי סִיּוּם הַכָּתוּב אֵינוֹ כֵן

and the Sages expounded “I will counsel you” [as] the counsel of harlotry (Sanhedrin 106a)721Sanhedrin 106a: “‘Come, I will counsel you [what this people will do to your people]’ (Bamidbar 24:14) — [Bilaam advised Balak:] the God of these [Israel] hates immorality; set out women before them in harlotry [and they will stumble].” (The “counsel of harlotry” — the daughters of Moav and Midyan.)Mei HaShiloach — a holy potential does not become permissible before its proper time, person, and place: Mei HaShiloach I, Shemini §5, formulates a principle especially important for this se’if: a person must discern “העת והנפש והמקום” so that an act is aligned with the will of Hashem, because a middah or act that is right in one setting is not thereby fit at all times. He illustrates this from Pinchas: the law of kana’in pog’in bo applied only at the exact moment of the act; had the circumstances changed, the legal and spiritual judgment would have changed with them. The Ishbitzer therefore demands not only intensity but exact timing, and the ability to leave a middah immediately when its proper moment passes. This is a powerful safeguard for R’ Tzadok’s discussion of Bilaam’s counsel. Bilaam perceived a future truth — that kedushah, Davidic kingship, and ultimately Mashiach would emerge through Moav — and weaponized that truth by forcing it into the wrong time and form, before conversion and outside the Torah’s permitted order. The later holiness of Rus does not retroactively make the earlier union permissible. It proves the opposite: a potential that belongs to Divine purpose must still arrive through the divinely appointed gate. In Ishbitz terms, knowing a hidden root is never enough; one must also know the et, nefesh, and makom. Otherwise a glimpse of future holiness becomes precisely the temptation by which a person attaches himself to the side of death. — though seemingly the verse’s continuation is not so [it speaks of the End of Days].
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת ״אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה״ וְגוֹמֵר הָיָה עַל יְדֵי דָּוִד וּמָשִׁיחַ הַבָּאִין מִזֶּרַע רוּת, שֶׁהָיָה עַל יְדֵי הִתְחַבְּרוּת עִם בְּנוֹת מוֹאָב

But in truth, “what [this people] will do” [in the End] would come about through David and Mashiach, who descend from the seed of Rus — which itself came about through a “joining” with the daughters of Moav.722R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §45): “"it is the way of the man to conquer and not [the woman]"… and therefore the entire building of the House of David came about through an arousal from the woman — like the daughters of Lot, and Tamar, and Rus, and the wife of Yishai.” Exactly the se’if’s hidden truth: the very “joining” Bilaam exploited is the channel through which the House of David was in fact destined to be built — only that he forced the hour before its time.
וְהִתְחַבְּרוּת מַחְלוֹן וְכִלְיוֹן הָיָה קֹדֶם שֶׁנִּתְגַּיְּירוּ, דְּאַחַר כָּךְ הוּא שֶׁנִּתְגַּיְּירָה רוּת
And the “joining” of Machlon and Kilyon [with Rus and Orpah] was before they converted, for only afterward did Rus convert;
וְהֵם מֵתוּ בֶּאֱמֶת בְּלֹא בָּנִים, אֲבָל הֵם גָּרְמוּ לְיִיבּוּם וּגְאוּלַת בֹּעַז וְהוֹלָדַת זֶרַע קֹדֶשׁ אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיְּירָה

and they indeed died childless, yet they brought about the yibum and the “redemption” of Boaz, and the bearing of holy seed after she had converted.723R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §16): “and the wisdom and the recognition of good and evil were given to every person — and this corresponds to the Torah.” Exactly the se’if: the union with the daughters of Moav was a “sin for the sake of Heaven” whose end only the Torah’s larger light discloses — for the discernment of good from evil is the Torah’s own gift, not the eye’s.724R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §52): “"and Rus the Moaviah her daughter-in-law with her, who returned" — regarding her the term "returned" is not apt but "came"; only that the intensity of her righteousness made her equal to [Naomi], and "returned" — as though she had been an Israelite from birth, from the womb.” Exactly the se’if’s “after she had converted”: what Bilaam sought prematurely, Rus attained in its time — so completely that Scripture speaks of her as a returner, not a newcomer.
וְהֵם רָאוּ זֶה מֵאִצְטַגְנִינוּתָם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב [בְּסֵפֶר תִּפְאֶרֶת יוֹנָתָן שָׁם] דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה טָעָה זִמְרִי גַּם כֵּן, יְעֻיַּין שָׁם עַל פִּי דַּרְכּוֹ

And they [Balak and Bilaam] saw this by their astrology; and as [R’ Yonasan Eybeschutz] wrote [in Tiferes Yehonasan, there], through this Zimri too erred — see there, according to his approach (see note 26 above).
וּבִלְעָם יָדַע דְּזֶה יִהְיֶה בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים וַעֲדַיִין לֹא הִגִּיעַ עִתּוֹ
And Bilaam knew that this [holy union with Moav] would be [only] in the End of Days, and its time had not yet come;
וִיעָצוֹ שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה עַתָּה מַה שֶּׁיַּעֲשׂוּ ״לְעַמְּךָ״ וְגוֹמֵר בְּהִתְחַבְּרוּת לִבְנוֹתָיו
so he counseled [Balak] to do now what they [would ultimately] do — [inducing] a “joining” with his daughters;
וְעַתָּה שֶׁהוּא ״פַּגָּה״ וּבְלֹא גֵּירוּת יִדְבְּקוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּסִטְרָא דְּמוֹתָא
[reasoning that] now, being “unripe” and without conversion, they would thereby cleave to the side of death;
וְלֹא הִגִּיעַ עֵת הַתִּיקּוּן עֲדַיִין כְּבִימֵי בֹּעַז
for the time of the rectification had not yet arrived, as it did in the days of Boaz.
וְהֵם טָעוּ בָּזֶה וְלֹא יָדְעוּ דְּיָלְדָה כְּמוֹתָהּ
And they [the sinners] erred in this, not realizing that “the offspring [is] like her” [the gentile mother];
וְחָשְׁבוּ דְּיַכְנִיסוּם לִקְדֻשָּׁה כְּשֶׁהִרְגִּישׁוּ הַחֵשֶׁק בְּקִרְבָּם עַל יְדֵי דְּיֵשׁ אֵיזֶה שַׁיָּיכוּת
and they thought they would bring them [the women] into holiness, when they felt the “longing” within them — [reasoning] that there was some [root-]connection.
וְכַיָּדוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִ״י ז״ל דִּבְכָזְבִּי הָיָה נִיצוֹץ דִּינָה, וְכֵן מִסְּתָמָא בִּשְׁאָר בְּנוֹת מִדְיָן נִתְחַלְּקוּ עַנְפֵי נִיצוֹץ זֶה וְכַיּוֹצֵא
And as is known from the Arizal, that in Kozbi there was a spark of Dinah; and likewise, presumably, among the other daughters of Midyan branches of this spark were distributed, and the like.
כִּי עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁנִּתְגַּדֵּל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה בְּמִדְיָן וְנָשָׂא בַּת יִתְרוֹ כֹּהֵן מִדְיָן הָרֹאשׁ וְהַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבָּהֶם
For [consider] that Moshe Rabbeinu was raised in Midyan and married the daughter of Yisro, priest of Midyan, the head and greatest among them —
וְהוּא נִתְגַּיֵּיר וְזָכָה שֶׁנִּקְרָא פָּרָשָׁה בַּתּוֹרָה עַל שְׁמוֹ ״פָּרָשַׁת יִתְרוֹ״, וּבְאוֹתָהּ פָּרָשָׁה נֶאֶמְרָה מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
and [Yisro] converted and merited that a parashah is called by his name, “Parashas Yisro,” in which the Giving of the Torah is related.
דְּעִנְיַן שֶׁנִּמְכַּר יוֹסֵף לַמְּדָנִים, וְאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר [יִתְרוֹ סח.] מֹשֶׁה וְיוֹסֵף בְּרָזָא חַד, וְכֹהֵן מִדְיָן רָזָא דְּאֵשֶׁת מְדָנִים עַיֵּין שָׁם

For the matter of Yosef being sold to the “Medanim” — and they said in the Zohar [Yisro 68a] that Moshe and Yosef are “one secret,” and the “priest of Midyan” is the secret of the “woman of Midyan,” see there.
וְהָעִנְיָן פֵּירֵשׁ [בְּלִיקּוּטֵי תוֹרָה] שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד יְסוֹד אַבָּא שֶׁבִּקְדֻשָּׁה, דְּשָׁם תּוֹקֶף הָאַהֲבָה דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין
And [the Arizal] explained [in Likkutei Torah] that it corresponds to Yesod Abba in holiness, where the intensity of love “never parts”;
וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ בַּקְּלִיפָּה ״אֵשֶׁת מְדָנִים״, ״יִתְפָּרְדוּ [כָּל פּוֹעֲלֵי אָוֶן]״ וְגוֹמֵר, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּאֹרֶךְ

and corresponding to it in the “husk” is the “woman of strife [eishes medanim],” [of which is said] “all evildoers shall be scattered” (Tehillim 92:10)725Tehillim 92:10: “כִּי הִנֵּה אֹיְבֶיךָ ה׳, כִּי הִנֵּה אֹיְבֶיךָ יֹאבֵדוּ, יִתְפָּרְדוּ כָּל פֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן” — “for behold, Your enemies, Hashem, for behold, Your enemies shall perish; all evildoers shall be scattered.” Background: from the Psalm of the Shabbos day — the wicked, though they flourish for a time, are ultimately scattered and destroyed. R’ Tzadok’s use: the “husk” opposite Yesod Abba is the “woman of strife” (eishes medanim) — where the holy “love that never parts” becomes its very opposite, “yispardu kol po’alei aven,” a scattering; the intensity that binds inseparably in holiness is, in the shell, a strife that divides. — see there at length. — the same intense “love” that in holiness binds inseparably becomes, in the husk, a strife that scatters.726Zohar, Yisro 68a: R’ Abba said: it is not written of Yisro “priest of On” but “priest of Midyan” — it is all one; at first he was called “priest of On” [Yosef’s father-in-law], and afterward “priest of Midyan” — and “priest of Midyan” hints at the secret of “the woman of strife [eishes medanim].” Likkutei Torah (of the Arizal), beginning of Parashas Yisro: Know that there is in the Sitra Achra a “priest of Midyan,” corresponding to Yesod Abba of holiness; for there in holiness it is love, but in the kelipah it is enmity and strife — and no light was granted to unite them, and they remained in separation — this is “the workers of iniquity shall be scattered”; whereas above, in the secret of Abba and Imma, “they never part.” [Yesod Abba is the root of undivided love; its counterfeit in the kelipah is “the woman of strife,” whose “workers of iniquity are scattered.”]

items.h: The theme: Had Leah then borne Yosef (the Yesod), joined to Yaakov he would be Yesod Abba — total, unbreakable union of all the tribes. Yesod Abba (from Chochmah) transcends “Yesod Ze’er” (deed). Yosef’s “evil report” saw only the surface; in the depths all the tribes cleave to Hashem (“all Israel have a share”). But this “extra” attainment this world — created with Din (contraction) — could not yet bear; so Leah’s self-din turned the fetus into a female (Din is of the “vessel/receiver”).

p: [לד] וְאַחַר שֶׁזָּכְתָה לֵאָה לִזְבוּלוּן דְּ״יִזְבְּלֵנִי״
And after Leah merited Zevulun, [of] “yizbeleini” —
אִלּוּ הוֹלִידָה אַחַר כָּךְ גַּם אֶת יוֹסֵף, שֶׁהוּא הַיְסוֹד דִּקְדֻשָּׁה, וּמִצַּד חִיבּוּר לֵאָה [עִם] יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה נִקְרָא ״יְסוֹד אַבָּא״
had she then borne Yosef as well — who is the Yesod of holiness, and [who,] from the side of Leah’s union with “Yisrael” [Yaakov], would be called “Yesod Abba” —
הָיָה תַּכְלִית הַתִּיקּוּן דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין לְגַמְרֵי
it would have been the ultimate rectification of “never parting” completely,
וְתוֹקֶף הָאַהֲבָה דְּגַם כָּל הַשְּׁבָטִים הָיוּ אוֹהֲבִים אוֹתוֹ, וְהָיוּ מִתְאַחֲדִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד

and the intensity of love [would have been such] that all the tribes, too, would love him, and they would be united as [they will be] in the Future.727R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Bamidbar §4): “Aharon is the shushvina d’matronisa, and therefore they too are called avos. Of Yosef it is brought in the Zohar, "Yaakov and Yosef are as one" — and Yosef too is called av [father].” Exactly the se’if’s Yesod Abba: Yosef joined to Yaakov is no longer a “son” among the tribes but takes on the rung of father — the unbreakable foundation on which the whole building stands.
כִּי ״יְסוֹד אַבָּא״ נִקְרָא הַיּוֹצֵא מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה, לֹא כִּ״יְסוֹד זְעֵיר״ שֶׁהוּא שֵׁשׁ קְצָווֹת דְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, שֶׁיּוֹצֵא מִצַּד כֹּחַ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה לְבַד
For “Yesod Abba” is that which issues from the side of Chochmah, not like “Yesod [of] Ze’er,” which is the six extremities of the six days of “action,” issuing from the power of deed alone.
דְּזֶהוּ עִנְיַן צַדִּיק שֶׁעִיקָּרוֹ בַּמַּעֲשֶׂה וְהַהַגְדָּרָה כְּיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁעִיקַּר מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ הַגְדָּרַת הַמַּעֲשִׂים
For this is the matter of a “tzaddik” whose essence is in deed and “bounding-in,” like Yosef HaTzaddik, whose essential level is the disciplining of deeds;
וְעַל כֵּן הֵבִיא דִּיבַּת הַשְּׁבָטִים רָעָה שֶׁאֵין מוּגְדָּרִים בַּמַּעֲשֶׂה כְּמוֹהוּ
and therefore he brought “an evil report of the tribes” [seeing] that they were not [as] “bounded-in” in deed as he.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הֵם דְּבוּקִים בֵּאלֹקִים חַיִּים וְכָל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
But in truth they cleave to the living God, and all their deeds are for the sake of Heaven;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּגְלֶה שֶׁל הַמַּעֲשֶׂה לֹא כֵן, הַמַּשְׂכִּיל יָבִין דְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבָם בֶּאֱמֶת דָּבוּק בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
and even though the revealed [surface] of the deed is not so, the discerning one understands that the depths of their hearts truly cleave to Him.
וְזֶהוּ דְּרָשַׁת ״דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת״ [בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק] דְּ״כוּלָּם יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא״
And this is the exposition of the “expounders of reshumos” [in Perek Chelek, Sanhedrin 105a]: that “all of them [Israel] have a share in the World to Come,”
כָּל אוֹתָם שֶׁהֵם מִזֶּרַע אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב, חוּץ מִבִּלְעָם

all those of the seed of Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov — except for Bilaam728Sanhedrin 105a: in Perek Chelek, the “expounders of impressions” (dorshei reshumos) taught that all of the seed of Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov have a share in the World to Come — Bilaam alone excepted (cf. the Mishnah’s list of exceptions, Sanhedrin 90a). R’ Tzadok’s use: “reshumos” (impressions) denotes the rung of Chochmah, above Binah — the “World to Come”; the supernal Chochmah of the mind is not itself “felt,” only its “impression” is felt in the heart. From the side of that Chochmah there is no “dross” in Yaakov’s seed at all — the discerning one perceives that, however their deeds appear on the surface, the depths of their hearts cleave wholly to God..
וּ״רְשׁוּמוֹת״ נִקְרָא דַּרְגָּא דְּחָכְמָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִבִּינָה שֶׁהוּא עוֹלָם הַבָּא כַּנּוֹדָע, וְהוּא לִבָּא דְּשָׁם הַהַרְגָּשָׁה
And “reshumos” [impressions] denotes the rung of Chochmah above Binah — the “World to Come,” as is known — and it is the “heart,” where feeling resides;
אֲבָל חָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ אֵינָהּ מוּרְגֶּשֶׁת, רַק הָרְשִׁימוּ מִמֶּנָּה מוּרְגָּשׁ בַּלֵּב שֶׁרִישׁוּמוֹ נִיכָּר מִצַּד חִיבּוּר מוֹחָא וְלִבָּא שֶׁהֵם תְּרֵין רֵעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין

but the Chochmah of the mind is not “felt”; only its “impression” is felt in the heart — whose imprint is discernible through the union of “mind and heart,” which are “two companions that never part.”729R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Bamidbar §2): “the number of the hosts of the Torah and the hosts of the Mishkan — the union of the Holy One and His Shechinah; and it is brought in the Zohar, the secret of the unification is like the encircling of the altar.” The se’if’s “two companions that never part” in its structural form: the counting itself is an act of binding, so that what is numbered is held in a single, unbreakable union.Sefas Emes — Yosef’s own tikkun transformed the way he saw the other shevatim: Sefas Emes, Vayeishev 7:6, gives a striking reading of “vayavei Yosef es dibasam ra’ah.” A tzaddik’s task, he writes, is to raise the good deeds of Israel before the Creator. Yosef had not yet reached his full perfection; before his descent and his nisayon he could still bring their negative report. After the ordeal, when he became ‘Yosef HaTzaddik,’ he raised only their good, and then the brothers could once again be together with their father. This complements R’ Tzadok’s distinction between Yosef’s initial surface judgment and the deeper truth of the tribes. Yosef’s mistake was not that standards of bris and holiness are unreal. His own later life proves how absolute those standards are. Rather, his perfection required learning how to see the covenantal good beneath another Jew’s confusing outward state without abolishing judgment of the act. The mature tzaddik becomes an advocate who uncovers the point fit to be elevated. That is closely related to R’ Tzadok’s Yesod Abba: a deeper daas in which the shevatim’s various paths no longer appear as mutually excluding identities. The higher union is not blindness to sin; it is sight deep enough to distinguish the sin from the indestructible root of the sinner.
וּמִצַּד הַשָּׂגַת הַחָכְמָה אֵין בְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב שׁוּם פְּסֹלֶת כְּלָל
And from the side of the attainment of Chochmah, there is no “dross” whatever in the seed of Yaakov;
וְאַף דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם תַּקָּנָה בִּתְשׁוּבָה — שֶׁרוֹמֶזֶת לְעוֹלָם הַבָּא כַּנּוֹדָע — הֵם מִתְתַּקְּנִים בִּפְתִיחַת תַּרְעָא דְּחָכְמְתָא, שֶׁהִיא לְמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה

and even matters that have no remedy through teshuvah — [teshuvah,] which alludes to the “World to Come” [Binah] — are rectified in the “opening of the gate of Chochmah,” which is above the level of teshuvah.730R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §12): “The elevation of the yesod of the male to Yesod Abba comes afterward, on Sukkos — the culmination of Rosh Hashanah — for from the intensity of fear comes the intensity of the joy of ‘the season of our rejoicing,’ whence they draw ru’ach ha-kodesh at the Simchas Beis HaSho’evah: a spirit from the supernal holiness, which is Chochmah Ila’ah [the supernal Wisdom].” (This locates the se’if’s Yesod Abba: it is drawn from Chochmah Ila’ah — the “opening of the gate of Chochmah” that stands above teshuvah — which is why it effects the total, unbreakable union that Yesod Ze’er [deed] cannot.)
וּמִדַּת יְסוֹד יָדוּעַ שֶׁהוּא הַהִתְקַשְּׁרוּת וְהַהִתְחַבְּרוּת שֶׁבֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם, שֶׁזֶּהוּ יְסוֹד הַבְּרִיאָה וְהָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
And the trait of Yesod is the bonding and joining between Israel and their Father in Heaven — which is the “foundation” of creation and the whole world,
כְּמוֹ כָּל בִּנְיָן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ יְסוֹד בְּתַחְתִּיתוֹ שֶׁעָלָיו עוֹמֵד כָּל הַבִּנְיָן
like any building, which has a foundation at its base upon which the whole building stands.
וְגַם כָּל בִּנְיַן הַבְּרִיאָה יֵשׁ לוֹ יְסוֹד שֶׁעָלָיו נִתְכּוֹנֵן, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם״ שֶׁעָלָיו הָעוֹלָם עוֹמֵד

And the whole edifice of creation, too, has a foundation upon which it is established, as it says, “a tzaddik is the foundation of the world” (Mishlei 10:25)731Mishlei 10:25: “כַּעֲבוֹר סוּפָה וְאֵין רָשָׁע, וְצַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם” — “when the storm passes, the wicked is no more, but a tzaddik is the foundation of the world.” Background: Mishlei contrasts the fleeting wicked with the enduring righteous. Meforshim: the Sages (Yoma 38b) take “tzaddik yesod olam” to mean that the world stands upon the righteous — even one tzaddik sustains it. R’ Tzadok’s use: the sefirah of Yesod is this very “foundation” — the bond joining Israel to their Father in Heaven, “upon which the whole edifice of creation stands,” just as Noach (“ish tzaddik”) remained to re-found the world after the Flood., upon whom the world stands,
וְלוּלֵי כֵן הָיָה הָעוֹלָם חוֹזֵר לְתֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ
and without it the world would revert to chaos and void.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל דְּנִשְׁאַר רַק נֹחַ אִישׁ צַדִּיק דְּמִמֶּנּוּ הוּשְׁתַת הָעוֹלָם אַחַר כָּךְ
As in the generation of the Flood, when there remained only Noach, a “righteous man,” from whom the world was [re]founded afterward.
וְהוּא הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה כְּלַפֵּי כְּלַל אֲצִילוּת קָדְשׁוֹ, שֶׁאֵין מוּשָּׂג לְאָדָם אֶלָּא כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּרִיאָה תַּחְתּוֹנָה כְּלַפֵּי נִבְרָאִים עֶלְיוֹנִים
And it [Yesod] is the lowest rung relative to the whole of His holy Atzilus — for [only] that is graspable to man, insofar as it is a “lower creation” relative to the higher creations.
אֶלָּא שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא הִתְחַבְּרוּת תַּחְתּוֹנִים וְעֶלְיוֹנִים, שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ, עַל יְדֵי חִיבּוּר נַפְשׁוֹ וְרוּחוֹ עִם גּוּפוֹ
Except that in it is the joining of lower and upper, heaven and earth — through the joining of one’s nefesh and ruach with his body;
וְכָל הִתְחַבְּרוּת תַּחְתּוֹן בְּעֶלְיוֹן הַיְינוּ בְּמִדָּה אַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁל עֶלְיוֹן
and every joining of a “lower” to an “upper” is [precisely] at the “last trait” of the upper.
אֶלָּא שֶׁאַחַר הַנְּסִירָה דְּנַעֲשׂוּ אַנְפִּין בְּאַנְפִּין
Except that after the “sawing-apart” [nesirah], when [Ze’er and Nukva] became “face to face,”
אִלּוּ לֹא חָטָא וְנִכְנַס לְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת בִּקְדֻשָּׁה, שֶׁאָז עֲלִיּוֹת הָעוֹלָמוֹת
had [Adam] not sinned, but entered the day of Shabbos in holiness — when [there occur] the “ascents of the worlds” —
הָיָה מִתְעַלֶּה לְגַמְרֵי לִהְיוֹת ״נְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵב גָּבֶר״ כְּלֶעָתִיד, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ רֵעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין לְעוֹלָם וּמְחוּבָּרִים לְגַמְרֵי
[the world] would have been wholly elevated to “a female shall encircle a male,” as in the Future — that they be “companions that never part,” completely joined.
אֶלָּא שֶׁזֶּהוּ שֶׁפַע הַשָּׂגָה יְתֵירָה שֶׁאֵין הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה רָאוּי לָהּ, שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין
But this is an abundant, “extra” attainment, of which this world is not [yet] worthy — for it was created with the trait of Din —
רְצֹה לוֹמַר מִדַּת צִמְצוּם הָאוֹר מֵהַשָּׂגָה דְּמַה שֶּׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה — וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ כְּדַאי לָהּ, נִתְעַלֵּם
meaning the trait of “contraction” of the light — [withholding] the apprehension of what is above the grasp of this world; and that for which it is unworthy is [therefore] concealed.
וְזֶהוּ ״שֶׁדָּנָה לֵאָה דִּין בְּעַצְמָהּ״
And this is [the meaning of] “that Leah rendered a judgment [din] upon herself”:
הִכְנִיסָה בָּהּ מִדַּת הַדִּין וְהַצִּמְצוּם דְּהַשָּׂגָה
she brought into herself the trait of Din and of the “contraction” of apprehension —

שֶׁמִּצַּד הַדִּין לֹא הָיָה זֶה הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אָז כְּדַאי עֲדַיִין לְהִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר הַזֶּה בָּעוֹלָם, שֶׁיּוּגְמַר שְׁלֵימוּת הַתִּיקּוּן דְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב לְגַמְרֵי, אֵיךְ הֵם לֹא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין כְּלָל מִמֶּנּוּ יִתְבָּרַךְ

for from the side of Din, this world was not yet worthy of the revelation of this light — [namely,] that the perfection of the rectification of Yaakov’s seed be completed entirely, [showing] how they never part at all from Him.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְהַפֵּךְ לִנְקֵבָה, שֶׁכָּל מִדַּת הַדִּין הוּא מִסִּטְרָא דְּנוּקְבָא כַּנּוֹדָע
And through this [self-judgment, the fetus] “turned into a female” — for all Din is from the side of the Nukva, as is known,
כִּי מִדַּת הַצִּמְצוּם הוּא מִצַּד הַמְקַבֵּל שֶׁהוּא הַכְּלִי לְקִיבּוּל, שֶׁהַכְּלִי מְצַמְצֶמֶת שֶׁפַע הַהַשְׁפָּעָה, וְלֹא מִצַּד הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ

for the trait of “contraction” is from the side of the “receiver,” which is the “vessel” for receiving — for the vessel constricts the flow of influence — and not from the side of the “giver.” — the delay of the full light is thus no withholding from Above, but a limit of the vessel below, not yet able to hold so great a revelation.

items.h: The theme: The exiles and the delay of the rectification are from Din — the Name A-D-N-Y (Malchus/Knesses Yisrael), with its 24 permutations (12 “day,” 12 “night”). The month Av “begets the judgments,” yet its name (Av = father) is their sweetening root — abundant Chesed: Avraham “chose the exiles,” for every begetting requires contraction. Israel’s sufferings yield “a good end and hope.” Dan’s mazal is Aryeh, joined to Yehudah (“beginning and end joined as one”).

p: [לה] וְכָל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת וְעִיכּוּב הַתִּיקּוּן הַגָּמוּר הוּא מִצַּד מִדַּת הַדִּין וְדִינָא דְּמַלְכוּתָא יִת״שׁ
And all the exiles, and the delay of the complete rectification, are from the side of the trait of Din and “the law of [His] kingship,”
הָרוֹמֵז לְשֵׁם הָאֲדֹנוּת בְּאֶחָד מִכ״ד צֵירוּפָיו
which alludes to the Name of Lordship [A-D-N-Y] in one of its twenty-four permutations —
שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמְקַבֶּלֶת עוֹל מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּאַהֲבָה יוֹמָם וָלַיְלָה כָּל י״ב חָדְשֵׁי הַשָּׁנָה

which is the trait of Knesses Yisrael, that accepts the yoke of His kingship with love, day and night, all twelve months of the year.732R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §209): “They instituted [before the Amidah] ‘A-D-N-Y, open my lips’ (Tehillim 51:17) — for the Name A-D-N-Y denotes His Shechinah that is within the hearts of the Children of Israel; and we ask that She open the mouth — not that the mouth speak of itself, but only what the heart opens within it. And the Holy One is ‘the heart of Israel,’ as it says, ‘the Rock of my heart’ (Tehillim 73:26).” (This grounds the se’if’s reading of A-D-N-Y as Malchus / Knesses Yisrael: the Name is the Shechinah indwelling Israel’s hearts, and its constriction in exile is the din the se’if traces.)
[וְעַל כֵּן הֵם כ״ד צֵירוּפִים, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן שֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה רַק י״ב, נֶגֶד מִדַּת יוֹם לְבַד, שֶׁהוּא מִדָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ ״שֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן ה׳״

[And therefore they are twenty-four permutations, whereas the Name Havayah has only twelve — corresponding to the trait of “day” alone, which is His own trait, “a sun and a shield is Hashem” (Tehillim 84:12)733Tehillim 84:12: “כִּי שֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן ה׳ אֱלֹהִים, חֵן וְכָבוֹד יִתֵּן ה׳, לֹא יִמְנַע טוֹב לַהֹלְכִים בְּתָמִים” — “for Hashem God is a sun and a shield; grace and glory Hashem gives; He withholds no good from those who walk in wholeness.” Background: the closing praise of the psalm — God gives light like a sun and protects like a shield, withholding no good from the upright. R’ Tzadok’s use: the “sun” is the trait of “day,” corresponding to the Name Havayah (twelve permutations); over against it, the Nukva (Knesses Yisrael) is “night” — the moon that receives the sun’s light — and therefore hers are twenty-four permutations, day and night joined.;
וְסִטְרָא דְּנוּקְבָא הוּא מִדַּת לַיְלָה — שְׁלִיטַת הַלְּבָנָה הַמְקַבֶּלֶת אוֹר הַחַמָּה, וְהוּא חִיבּוּר יוֹם וְלַיְלָה
and the side of the Nukva is the trait of “night” — the rule of the moon, which receives the light of the sun; and this is the joining of day and night,
עַל כֵּן אֶצְלָהּ הַי״ב הֵם כ״ד, רְצֹה לוֹמַר הַשָּׂגַת עַצְמָהּ וְהַשָּׂגַת הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ, שֶׁהֵם חוֹמְרָהּ וְצוּרָתָהּ
so with her the twelve become twenty-four — her own apprehension and the apprehension of the “giver,” which are her “matter” and her “form”;
וְעַל כֵּן מַזְכִּירִין מִדַּת יוֹם בַּלַּיְלָה וּמִדַּת לַיְלָה בַּיּוֹם בְּבִרְכַּת קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע]
and therefore we mention the trait of day at night and the trait of night by day, in the blessings of Krias Shema.]
וְנִרְאֶה לִי כִּי הַצֵּירוּפִים ״אֲדֹנָ״י״ וְ״דִינָ״א״ שֶׁהֵם אוֹתִיּוֹת ״דִּין״ סְדוּרִים יַחַד
And it seems to me that the permutations A-D-N-Y and D-Y-N-A — which are the letters of “din” arranged together —
וְהָ״א״ דְּהוּא ״אַלּוּפוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם״ הַגָּנוּז בְּגַוֵּיהּ בִּתְחִלָּתָהּ הוּא נֶגֶד חוֹדֶשׁ אָב

and the alef — “the Chief [Alufo] of the world,” hidden within it — at its beginning, corresponds to the month of Av.734R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar §2): “"just as when Av enters we diminish in joy, so when Adar enters we increase in joy"; and in Sefer Yetzirah it is brought that the month of Adar was formed with the letter kuf and the month of Av with the letter tes — and it is brought in the Zohar, "tes is Netzach-Hod-Yesod."” Exactly the se’if: Av is the month in which the judgments are begotten, and its very letter marks it as the point where the lower channels close.
דְּנִרְאֶה לִי שֶׁנִּקְרָא כֵן לְפִי שֶׁאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע״ה בָּחַר הַגָּלֻיּוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל

For it seems to me that it is called [Av] because Avraham Avinu “chose the exiles,” as the Sages said (cf. Nedarim 32a)735Nedarim 32a (and the tradition that Avraham “chose the exiles” for his descendants): the Gemara there treats why Avraham’s children were subjected to exile, and R’ Tzadok reads it as Avraham’s own choice — that he “chose the exiles.” R’ Tzadok’s use: though Avraham’s trait is Chesed, he chose exile out of longing for the perfection of the name “father” (Av) — for a father must beget, and every begetting requires the “contraction” (Din) that exile embodies; hence the month “Av” both “begets the judgments” and, as their very root, sweetens them.;
וְהַיְינוּ דְּ״אַבְרָהָם הוֹלִיד אֶת יִצְחָק״, דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ חֶסֶד הוּא הוֹלִיד מִדַּת הַדִּין וְהַצִּמְצוּם, וְכָל הוֹלָדָה הוּא כְּפִי הִשְׁתּוֹקְקוּת הַמּוֹלִיד

and this is “Avraham begot Yitzchak”: that though his own trait is Chesed, he “begot” the trait of Din and contraction — for every “begetting” is according to the yearning of the begetter.736R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar §5): “and in the Yerushalmi and in the Midrash it is brought that on Tishah B’Av, on the very day of the churban, Mashiach was born at once — and this is for the reason stated; only that the time had not yet come for the rectification to be as it should, but at any rate Israel [then had it].” Exactly the se’if’s Av as father: the month that begets the judgments is the same month that begets their sweetening — the begetting and the exile are one act.
וְאַבְרָהָם הוּא הַנִּקְרָא ״אַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם״, וּבַתְּחִלָּה אַב לַאֲרָם וְאַחַר כָּךְ לְכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
And Avraham is the one called “father of a multitude of nations” — at first “Av [father] to Aram,” and afterward to the whole world.
דְּמִלַּת ״אָב״ הוּא עִיקַּר שְׁמוֹ, הַמּוֹרֶה עַל עִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁהוּא אַב הָעוֹלָם וְרֹאשׁ לַאֲבוֹת הָעוֹלָם
for the word “Av” is the essence of his name, indicating that he is the father of the world and the head of the fathers of the world.
דְּמַה שֶּׁיִּצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב גַּם כֵּן אָבוֹת הוּא רַק מִצַּד כֹּחַ אַבְרָהָם הַגָּנוּז בְּגַוַּום, כִּי הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ לְעִנְיַן ״אָב״
For that Yitzchak and Yaakov, too, are “Avos” is only from the power of Avraham hidden within them, for he is the root of the concept of “father,”
דְּהַיְינוּ הַהוֹלָדָה שֶׁהוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַבָּא מִצַּד הַחֶסֶד
which is “begetting” — a spreading-forth that comes from the side of Chesed.
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּצַּד שֶׁפַע הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת אֵין מָקוֹם לְהוֹלָדָה וְהַהֶבְדֵּל בֵּין אָב לְבֵן
Except that from the [pure] abundance of spreading-forth, there is no “place” for begetting or for the distinction between father and son —
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ ״אִלְמָלֵא אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁחָטְאוּ אָנוּ לֹא בָאנוּ״ אוֹ ״כְּמִי שֶׁלֹּא בָּאנוּ״ לְעוֹלָם
along the lines of “had our ancestors not sinned, we would not have come,” or “like those who never came” into the world.
וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה תְּחִלָּתוֹ עָקָר, דְּכָל הוֹלָדָה הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַהִצְטַמְצְמוּת שֶׁהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּמִדַּת הַדִּין
And therefore his beginning was “barren” — for every begetting comes only from “contraction,” the rung of Din.
וְאַף דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע״ה מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ הוּא רַב חֶסֶד, בָּחַר בַּגָּלֻיּוֹת מִצַּד חֵשֶׁק שְׁלֵימוּת מִדָּתוֹ
And although Avraham is, in himself, “abundant in Chesed,” he “chose the exiles” out of longing for the perfection of his trait —
שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת שֵׁם ״אָב״ שֶׁמּוּכְרָח לְהוֹלִיד בָּנִים, וּמוּכְרָח לְהוֹלִיד מִדַּת הַצִּמְצוּם וְהָבִיאָהּ לְעוֹלָם
the perfection of the name “father,” who must beget children, and so must “beget” the trait of contraction and bring it into the world.
וְעַל כֵּן שֵׁם הַחוֹדֶשׁ ״אָב״ הַמּוֹלִיד הַדִּינִין
And therefore the name of the month is “Av,” which “begets” the judgments;
וּלְהַמְתִּיק הַדִּינִין — שֶׁהוּא הַכְנָסָתָן בְּשָׁרְשָׁן — קְרָאוּהוּ ״אָב״, שֶׁהוּא שׇׁרְשָׁן הַמּוֹלִידָן שֶׁהוּא אַדְּרַבָּא רַב חֶסֶד
and to “sweeten” the judgments — to return them to their root — they called it “Av,” which is their root, their “begetter,” which is, on the contrary, “abundant in Chesed.”
כִּי כָּל יִסּוּרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגָלֻיּוֹתֵיהֶם הוּא לָתֵת לָהֶם עַל יְדֵי זֶה ״אַחֲרִית וְתִקְוָה״ טוֹבָה הַנִּמְשָׁכִים מִמִּדַּת הַחֶסֶד

For all the sufferings of Israel and their exiles are [in order] to give them, thereby, a good “end and hope” (Yirmeyah 29:11)737Yirmeyah 29:11: “כִּי אָנֹכִי יָדַעְתִּי אֶת הַמַּחֲשָׁבֹת אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי חֹשֵׁב עֲלֵיכֶם נְאֻם ה׳, מַחְשְׁבוֹת שָׁלוֹם וְלֹא לְרָעָה, לָתֵת לָכֶם אַחֲרִית וְתִקְוָה” — “for I know the thoughts that I think toward you, says Hashem — thoughts of peace and not of evil — to give you a future and a hope.” Background: from Yirmeyah’s letter to the Babylonian exiles — the exile itself is purposed toward a good end. R’ Tzadok’s use: all Israel’s sufferings and exiles are “to give them a good end and hope,” drawn from Chochmah — the hidden chasadim joined to the letters of “din,” whose “end” turns to the wonders of the days of Mashiach.Shelah — the din of exile is rooted in rescue and a road toward life: Shelah, Aseres HaDibros, Pesachim, Matzah Ashirah 4:46, states the principle “אין רע יורד מלמעלה”: even what appears as evil can be a rescue from a harsher consequence for which the person is otherwise exposed. He cites the Midrashic teaching that Avraham chose subjection to the kingdoms for his descendants so that they be spared Gehinnom, and then links suffering itself to “דרך חיים תוכחות מוסר.” The Shelah does not call pain pleasant, nor does he deny that it must be experienced as judgment. His point is that the judgment can be ordered toward preservation and life. This fits R’ Tzadok’s insistence that the dinim of galus are born from a root of Chesed — Av, the fatherly source, ‘begetting’ contraction precisely for the sake of an achris v’tikvah. The contraction is real: exile limits, separates, and obscures. Yet if its root is chesed, then the final meaning of the contraction is not destruction but formation. A child can exist as a distinct child only because unlimited expansion makes room for boundary; similarly, Israel’s history can pass through din in order to emerge with a clarified and enduring form. The sweetness of the din is therefore not found by denying the darkness, but by returning it to the Av-source from which its good purpose descends., drawn from the trait of Chesed.
