Nonetheless, “He heard her voice” too, that she could “be built up” through this — for thereby the power of that drive was weakened.793R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §66): “until they said, "such is the way of the yetzer hara: today it says [do this]…"; and a transgression drags a transgression after it, and every transgression drags its like, from its own kind — and therefore "do not be sated with the desire of eating, and you will not sin with the desire of forbidden relations."” The se’if’s chain exactly: because each drive draws its own kind, weakening it at its first emergence weakens it wherever it would later appear.

דְּכָל הַגָּדוֹל מֵחֲבֵירוֹ יִצְרוֹ גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ, דִּכְפִי תּוֹקֶף הַמַּעֲלָה כָּךְ תּוֹקֶף הַחִסָּרוֹן מִסִּטְרָא דְּעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע, שֶׁהֵם לְעוּמַּת זֶה הָרַע נֶגֶד הַטּוֹב וּמַקְבִּיל לְעוּמָּתוֹ כַּיָּדוּעַ

For “the one greater than his fellow, his drive is greater than his” (Sukkah 52a)794Sukkah 52a: “R’ Yochanan said: The one who is greater than his fellow, his [evil] inclination is greater than his [kol ha-gadol mei-chaveiro, yitzro gadol heimenu].” — for according to the intensity of the “elevation,” so the intensity of the “deficiency,” from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, where they are “one opposite the other,” the evil corresponding to the good.
וְדָן שֶׁהוּא יָרוּד שֶׁבַּשְּׁבָטִים מִצַּד הַמַּעֲלָה, גַּם הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁבּוֹ יָרוּד וְאֵין הַיֵּצֶר תַּקִּיף כָּל כָּךְ בּוֹ
And Dan, who is the “lowliest of the tribes” in respect of elevation, the deficiency in him too is “low,” and the drive is not so strong in him;
וּלְפִי שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְחַלֵּק מִמֶּנּוּ לְדָן שֶׁיָּצָא תְּחִלָּה נֶחֱלַשׁ גַּם בְּיוֹסֵף אַחַר כָּךְ

and since [that drive] had already been “apportioned off” from him to Dan, who came forth first, it was weakened in Yosef too, afterward.795Be’er Moshe (R’ Moshe Yechiel Epstein of Ozherov), Neviim — Shoftim, p. 246: וכן אמרו (סנהדרין קג, ב): מפני מה לא מנו את מיכה [בין] אלה שאין להם חלק לעולם הבא? מפני שפיתו מצויה לעוברי דרכים… כל העולם מתארחין אצלו The Be’er Moshe brings the Gemara’s own astonishing verdict on Michah: the man whose idol stood in Israel was nevertheless not counted among those with no share in the World to Come — because his bread was available to wayfarers. This bears directly on the se’if’s reading of Michah as “mistaken” rather than wicked: the Jewish root held, and it is the hospitality issuing from that root, not the idol, that fixed his standing.
וְאַף שֶׁבּוֹ עִיקַּר תָּקְפּוֹ וְהַתְחָלָתוֹ בִּיצִיאָה לְפוֹעַל, דְּמַה שֶּׁהָיָה בְּדָן הָיָה עַל יְדֵי יָרׇבְעָם, וְכֵן בְּנֵי דָן לָקְחוּ מִמִּיכָה

And though in him [Dan] is its main force and its “beginning” in coming to actuality — for what was [manifest] in Dan was through Yerovam, and the children of Dan [likewise] took [the idol] from Michah —
מִכָּל מָקוֹם שֹׁרֶשׁ יוֹסֵף הוּא עִיקַּר תּוֹלְדוֹת יַעֲקֹב זֶרַע אֱמֶת, וְאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת בֶּאֱמֶת לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְלֹא לַגּוֹיִם כְּלָל
nonetheless the “root of Yosef” is the essence of the “generations of Yaakov,” true seed, having no [real] connection to idolatry or to the nations at all;
וּמִמֶּנּוּ קָמוּ מְלָכִים דְּגַם בָּהֶם יֵשׁ בַּשֹּׁרֶשׁ תּוֹקֶף הַיִּרְאָה וְהַכָּרַת הַחִסָּרוֹן וּלְבִלְתִּי רוּם לְבָבוֹ
and from him arose kings [the house of Yosef], in whose root too is the “intensity of fear” and the recognition of “lack,” and “that his heart not be raised”;
וְהַגֵּיאוּת הוּא רַק בַּ״הוֹצֵי הַסּוֹבְבִים״ לְאָסָא וְלֹא חִסָּרוֹן בְּעֶצֶם
and the “haughtiness” is only in the “surrounding fronds” [the outer entourage], as with Asa — not a deficiency in essence.
אַךְ דָּן שֶׁהוּא הַיָּרוּד וְ״רַגְלֶיהָ יוֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת״ רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן, נֶחֱשַׁב אֶצְלוֹ זֶה כְּחִסָּרוֹן בְּעֶצֶם ״שֶׁלְּבָבוֹ פֹנֶה״ וְגוֹמֵר

But Dan, who is the “lowly” one — and “her feet descend to death,” God spare us — this is reckoned in him as a “deficiency in essence,” “whose heart turns away” (Devarim 29:17). — the greater the soul the fiercer its opposing drive; so Yosef’s royal line carries a real but subordinate pull, while in lowly Dan the same flaw sinks to the very “feet,” where it becomes essential.

items.h: The theme: No settled inheritance fell to Dan until the era of Michah’s idol — for the Land is a bequest from the Avos, accepted only by those with the root of holiness. Israel’s holiness was fully clarified only in David’s generation, and Dan’s late inheritance reflects that. Scripture places the account after Shimshon — the remedy before the blow — and keeps noting that “there was no king in Israel.”

p: [מג] וְעַל כֵּן לֹא נָפַל לְשֵׁבֶט הַדָּנִי נַחֲלָה בְּתוֹךְ שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד פֶּסֶל מִיכָה
And therefore no [settled] inheritance fell to the tribe of Dan among the tribes of Israel until [the era of] Michah’s idol,
שֶׁהָיוּ מְבַקְשִׁים אָז עֲדַיִין נַחֲלָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּעִנְיָן [בְּסֵפֶר שׁוֹפְטִים]
for they were still “seeking an inheritance” then, as is stated in the matter [Shoftim ch. 18].
דְּנַחֲלַת הָאָרֶץ לְזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא יְרוּשָּׁה מֵאָבוֹת, מוֹרֶה עַל שֹׁרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִתּוֹלַדְתָּם
For the inheritance of the Land to the seed of Israel is a “bequest from the Avos,” indicating the root of the holiness of Israel from their very birth,
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִקְרָא אֱלֹקֵי הָאָרֶץ, וְכֵן הַתּוֹרָה עִיקָּרָהּ בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבָּ״ן

for Hashem is called “God of the Land,” and the Torah, too, has its essence in Eretz Yisrael, as the Ramban wrote796Ramban, Vayikra 18:25 (on “וַתָּקִא הָאָרֶץ אֶת יֹשְׁבֶיהָ,” “and the Land vomited out its inhabitants”): the Ramban expounds his celebrated principle that “the essence of all the commandments is for those who dwell in the Land of Hashem” — the mitzvos kept in exile being but a “sign” lest they be forgotten against the return. Background: the verse warns that the Land itself expels those who defile it. R’ Tzadok’s use: since “the inheritance of the Land is a bequest from the Avos,” the Land “spewed out all the nations and accepted only” Israel, who bear “the root of the holiness of their fathers”; hence Dan’s late inheritance signals that the root of his holiness (and its shadow-deficiency) surfaced only later.Sefas Emes — return is possible because the sin is accidental to the inherited root of Israel: Sefas Emes, Nitzavim 5:2, reads ‘אתם נצבים היום כולכם’ as describing an eternal standing of Klal Yisrael before Hashem. The work of each individual is to nullify himself to that whole. Because the Torah’s statement is itself enduring — ‘שפת אמת תכון לעד’ — even the wicked can return: ‘החטא רק במקרה שנפרש מכללות ישראל ולכן יכול לחזור לשורשו, כמאמר לירושת אבותי אני חוזר.’ Sin is a contingent separation from the collective; teshuvah is a return to the inherited root of the fathers. This is an exceptionally close complement to R’ Tzadok’s language in the present se’if. The Land is not merely territory distributed by lot but ‘ירושת אבות,’ a bequest whose reception reflects the underlying covenantal root. Dan’s delayed inheritance can therefore symbolize a delayed clarification of how his particular place belongs within that inherited holiness. The Sefas Emes also guards against reading R’ Tzadok’s discussion as though a tribe’s historical failures could erase its essential share. If sin is a separation from the klal rather than a destruction of the root, the final movement must be return — to the Avos, to the klal, and to the place that expresses that root. Eretz Yisrael can ‘vomit out’ impurity precisely because its deepest relationship to Israel is prior to and more enduring than any particular failure..
וְזֶהוּ קְדֻשַּׁת הָאָרֶץ שֶׁהִשְׁקִיאָה כָּל הַגּוֹיִם וְלֹא קִיבְּלָה אֶלָּא בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם שֹׁרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת אֲבוֹתָם שֶׁזָּכוּ עַל יָדָם לְהַבְטָחַת נַחֲלַת הָאָרֶץ

And this is the holiness of the Land, which “spewed out” all the nations and accepted only the Children of Israel, who possess the root of the holiness of their fathers, through whom they merited the promise of the Land’s inheritance.797R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §37): “as in the first chapter of Berachos, that they merited Eretz Yisrael through sufferings, which "sweeten the flesh" — that is, the bodily portion in a person, against which stands the portion of deeds; and only through this is there the awaiting of the final purpose.” Exactly the se’if: the Land is not simply allotted but acquired — it is accepted only by those in whom the bodily portion has been made fit to hold it.

וּמַה שֶּׁלֹּא נִכְבַּשׁ הַכֹּל בִּימֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עַד יְמֵי דָּוִד, הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִתְבָּרְרָה קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲדַיִין לְגַמְרֵי עַד דּוֹר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל

And that not all [the Land] was conquered in the days of Yehoshua [but only] by the days of David — that is because the holiness of Israel was not yet fully “clarified” until the generation of David HaMelech, who is the “perfection of Knesses Yisrael.”
וּבְנֵי דָן שֶׁלֹּא נִתְבָּרֵר חֶלְקָם וְנַחֲלָתָם בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִתְבָּרֵר עֲדַיִין שֹׁרֶשׁ מַעֲלַת קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּקִרְבָּם עַד אָז

And the children of Dan, whose portion and inheritance in Eretz Yisrael was not [early] clarified — that is because the root of the elevated holiness of Israel within them was not yet clarified until then;
כִּי נִתְבָּרֵר מַעֲלָתָם, וּלְעוֹלָם הַמַּעֲלָה מוֹשֶׁכֶת הַחִסָּרוֹן עִמָּהּ, וְנִתְגַּלָּה אָז גַּם כֵּן חִסְרוֹנוֹ שֶׁמֵּחֲמָתוֹ לֹא מָצְאוּ נַחֲלָה עַד אָז

for [when] their elevation was clarified — and elevation always “draws the deficiency along with it” — then their deficiency, too, was revealed, on account of which they had found no inheritance until then;
וּלְפִי שֶׁזֶּה חִסָּרוֹן בְּשֹׁרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת עַל כֵּן אִיחֲרוֹ הַכָּתוּב
and since this is a deficiency in the very root of “Jewishness,” Scripture therefore “delayed” it.
וְסִידֵּר סִיפּוּר זֶה אַחַר סִיפּוּרֵי שִׁמְשׁוֹן אַף שֶׁקָּדַם לוֹ הַרְבֵּה, כְּמִדַּת הַכְּתוּבִים לְהַקְדִּים הָרְפוּאָה לַמַּכָּה
And [Scripture] arranged this account after the accounts of Shimshon, though it [chronologically] preceded him by much — as is the way of Scripture “to place the remedy before the blow”;
כִּי שִׁמְשׁוֹן הוּא הָיָה הַיּוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל שֶׁבְּשֵׁבֶט דָּן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וּבוֹ הָיָה תִּיקּוּנָם

for Shimshon was the greatest of the tribe of Dan in this world, and in him was their rectification.798R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §55): “"according to their families" — for they took their portion in the Land according to families, and therefore [that phrase] precedes "by their fathers’ houses"; unlike the counting of the sons of Levi, who took no portion.” Exactly the se’if: inheritance in the Land follows the root of the family line, which is why a tribe whose root-standing was unsettled received no settled inheritance until its time.
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגַּם הוּא בָּחַר בִּבְנוֹת הָעֲרֵלִים וְנִרְאֶה כְּאִלּוּ יֵשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת עִם עֲרֵלִים
For even though he too “chose the daughters of the uncircumcised,” and it seemed as though he had a “connection” with the uncircumcised,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַכָּתוּב הֵעִיד עָלָיו כִּי ״מֵאֵת ה׳ הָיְתָה זֹּאת״ לִנְקוֹם אַדְּרַבָּה עַל יְדֵי זֶה מֵהֶם וּלְהַכְנִיעָם, וּלְרַע לוֹ לְאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל

nonetheless Scripture testified of him that “it was from Hashem799Shoftim 14:4: of Shimshon’s marriage to a Philistine woman — “וְאָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ לֹא יָדְעוּ כִּי מֵה׳ הִיא, כִּי תֹאֲנָה הוּא מְבַקֵּשׁ מִפְּלִשְׁתִּים” — “his father and mother did not know that it was from Hashem, for He was seeking a pretext against the Philistines.” Background: Scripture testifies that Shimshon’s seemingly wayward choice was providential. R’ Tzadok’s use: though Shimshon “chose the daughters of the uncircumcised” and seemed to have a “connection” with them, “it was from Hashem” — to the very opposite end: to take vengeance upon them and subdue them, “to the detriment of the base man” — the pattern of Malchus Tata’ah, which consumes evil from within.” (Shoftim 14:4) — on the contrary, to take vengeance thereby upon them and to subdue them, “to the detriment” of the base man.
וְנֶאֱמַר שָׁם בָּעִנְיַן מִיכָה, וְכֵן בָּעִנְיָן הַתְחָלַת סִיפּוּר דִּבְנֵי דָן אַחַר כָּךְ ״דְּבַיָּמִים הָהֵם אֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״

And it is stated there, in the matter of Michah — and likewise at the start of the account of the children of Dan afterward — “in those days there was no king in Israel” (Shoftim 17:6; 18:1)800Shoftim 17:6; 18:1: the account of Michah’s idol, and of the Danite migration, each opens, “בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם אֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל” — “in those days there was no king in Israel” (17:6 adds: “each man did what was right in his own eyes”). Background: the refrain of Sefer Shoftim’s closing chapters, framing an age of disorder before the monarchy. R’ Tzadok’s use: since “from the side of Malchus is the perfection of Knesses Yisrael,” a “deficiency in the root of Jewishness” (Dan’s idolatry) could arise only “when there is yet no king,” while the “edifice of the stature” of Knesses Yisrael stood incomplete..

וְהַיְינוּ כִּי מִצַּד מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת הוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת חִסָּרוֹן בָּזֶה בְּשֹׁרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר עֲדַיִין אֵין מֶלֶךְ וְלֹא נִשְׁלַם עֲדַיִין בִּנְיַן קוֹמַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁלֵימוּת

That is, because from the side of Malchus is the “perfection of Knesses Yisrael,” and there can be a deficiency in the root of “Jewishness” only when “there is yet no king,” and the “edifice of the stature” of Knesses Yisrael is not yet complete.
וְעַל כֵּן עָמַד פֶּסֶל מִיכָה רַק כָּל זְמַן הֱיוֹת בֵּית אֱלֹקִים בְּשִׁילֹה, שֶׁהוּא בְּשֵׁבֶט אֶפְרַיִם אֲשֶׁר ״לֹא יִבְחַר בּוֹ״ לְנַחֲלָה

And therefore Michah’s idol “stood” only as long as the House of God was in Shiloh — which is in the tribe of Ephraim, “which He did not choose” for [the permanent] inheritance801Tehillim 78:67–68: “וַיִּמְאַס בְּאֹהֶל יוֹסֵף, וּבְשֵׁבֶט אֶפְרַיִם לֹא בָחָר; וַיִּבְחַר אֶת שֵׁבֶט יְהוּדָה, אֶת הַר צִיּוֹן אֲשֶׁר אָהֵב” — “He rejected the tent of Yosef, and chose not the tribe of Ephraim; but He chose the tribe of Yehudah, Mount Zion which He loves.” Background: Asaf’s psalm — the Sanctuary passed from Shiloh (in Ephraim) to Zion (in Yehudah). R’ Tzadok’s use: Michah’s idol “stood only as long as the House of God was in Shiloh,” in Ephraim, “which He did not choose” for the permanent inheritance — before “Yerushalayim, the inheritance,” was chosen and the election of Israel fully clarified. (cf. Tehillim 78:67),
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִבְחַר יְרוּשָׁלַיִם שֶׁהוּא הַנַּחֲלָה
and as long as Yerushalayim, which is “the inheritance,” had not yet been chosen.
הַיְינוּ שֶׁעֲדַיִין לֹא נִתְבָּרֵר בְּחִירַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְגַמְרֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּתוֹכָם לְנַחֲלָה קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּימָא
That is, the “choosing of Israel” was not yet fully clarified — that His Shechinah dwell among them as a fixed and enduring inheritance;
וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה אָז מְצִיאוּת פֶּסֶל מִיכָה שֶׁהוּא הַבִּיעוּט בְּאָנֹכִי שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל

and therefore there existed then the “reality” of Michah’s idol — the “kicking at Anochi,” which is [the very] root of the holiness of Israel. — Dan’s long homelessness thus mirrors his soul: only when Israel’s full “stature” stood — with a king and a chosen Jerusalem — could this deepest flaw at the root even surface and be assigned its place.

items.h: The theme: The churban fell in Av, which stands opposite Dan: his deficiency belongs to all Israel, one complete stature, but shows most in him. The Danites are “bitter of soul,” for Israel’s joy is only “before Hashem,” and idolatry breeds bitterness. Shimshon’s bitter end required Yaakov’s prayer, yet his death subdued them all the more — and only Moshe’s blessing for the future calls Dan “Aryeh,” when he rejoins Yehudah.

p: [מד] וְחוּרְבַּן הַנַּחֲלָה וּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ דִּירוּשָׁלַיִם הָיָה גַּם כֵּן בְּחוֹדֶשׁ אָב שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד דָּן, שֶׁמִּצִּידוֹ הוּא זֶה
And the destruction of the inheritance and of the Beis HaMikdash of Yerushalayim was likewise in the month of Av, which is “opposite Dan” — for it is “from his side”;
כִּי כָּל הַשְּׁבָטִים כְּלוּלִים זֶה בָּזֶה וְהַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁבּוֹ יֶשְׁנוֹ גַּם כֵּן בִּכְלַל הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, רַק שֶׁבּוֹ נִתְגַּלָּה בְּיוֹתֵר
for all the tribes are “included one in another,” and the deficiency in him exists also in the whole of Knesses Yisrael — only that in him it was “revealed” most,
כִּי כָּל הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל קוֹמָה אַחַת שְׁלֵימָה
for the whole of Knesses Yisrael is “one complete stature.”
וּמִשֶּׁנִּכְנַס אָב מְמַעֲטִין בְּשִׂמְחָה, וְכֵן בְּנֵי דָן נִקְרְאוּ שָׁם בַּכָּתוּב [בְּסֵפֶר שׁוֹפְטִים] ״מָרֵי נֶפֶשׁ״

And “when Av enters, we diminish in joy” (Taanis 26b)802Taanis 26b (Mishnah): “When [the month of] Av enters, we diminish in joy [mishe-nichnas Av mema’atin b’simcha].”Mei HaShiloach — the last camp of Dan is bound to the first camp of Yehudah: Mei HaShiloach II, Bamidbar §2, explains the order of the degalim by focusing on the apparent inequality between Yehudah in the east and Dan, who traveled last in the north. Yet Betzalel of Yehudah and Oholiav of Dan were both filled with wisdom for the Mishkan. The lesson of ‘איש על דגלו,’ he writes, is that each person’s true honor is to stand in the place where Hashem wills his particular revelation to occur, without jealousy. He then cites the Zohar on Moshe’s blessing ‘דן גור אריה’: Dan is deliberately tied to Yehudah so that ‘the beginning and the end’ of the four camps are bound in one place — Yehudah is ‘גור אריה יהודה,’ and Dan too becomes ‘גור אריה.’ This is a direct Izhbitz parallel to R’ Tzadok’s closing movement in the se’if. Dan’s present position as the tail is not his final definition. Precisely the last camp must eventually reveal its bond with the first, and the tribe associated with Shimshon’s serpent-like Din is destined to receive the leonine title of Yehudah. The future tikkun is therefore not the abolition of Dan’s distinct place but the revelation that the lowest edge of the camp was always organically attached to Malchus. The bitterness and distance of the present are healed when the ‘end’ knows itself as part of the same one body as the ‘beginning.’; and likewise the children of Dan are called there in Scripture [Shoftim 18:25] “bitter of soul [marei nefesh]803Shoftim 18:25: when Michah pursued the Danites to reclaim his idol, they warned him off — “פֶּן יִפְגְּעוּ בָכֶם אֲנָשִׁים מָרֵי נֶפֶשׁ, וְאָסַפְתָּה נַפְשְׁךָ וְנֶפֶשׁ בֵּיתֶךָ” — “lest men bitter of soul [marei nefesh] fall upon you, and you gather in your life and the life of your household.” Background: the migrating Danites, bearing Michah’s graven image, are called “bitter of soul.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this “bitterness” is the mark of Dan — “for the joy of Israel is only before Hashem,” and idolatry, “in truth distanced” from the Jewish soul, breeds sadness and bitterness of soul; hence the churban itself fell in Av, “opposite Dan.”” —
שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם לֵב שָׂמֵחַ מֵהַגּוֹרֵם טוֹבַת נֶפֶשׁ

for they have no “joyful heart” from that which occasions “good of soul.”804R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar §1): “"just as when Av enters we diminish in joy, so when Adar enters we increase in joy" — and Rashi explained: days of miracles were they for Israel, Purim and Pesach.” Exactly the se’if: the diminishing in Av is not an arbitrary mourning but the calendar’s own registration of where Israel’s joy is blocked, precisely as Adar registers where it is opened.
כִּי שִׂמְחַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא רַק לִפְנֵי ה׳, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וּשְׂמַחְתֶּם שָׁם לִפְנֵי ה׳״, וְנֶאֱמַר ״שִׂמְחוּ בַה׳״ וְגוֹמֵר, וְכֵן בְּהַרְבֵּה מִקְרָאוֹת

For the joy of the Children of Israel is only “before Hashem,” as it says, “and you shall rejoice there before Hashem805Devarim 12:12; Tehillim 97:12: “וּשְׂמַחְתֶּם לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם” — “and you shall rejoice before Hashem your God” (Devarim 12:12); “שִׂמְחוּ צַדִּיקִים בַּה׳” — “rejoice, O righteous, in Hashem” (Tehillim 97:12). Background: two of the “many verses” that locate Israel’s true rejoicing “before Hashem” alone. R’ Tzadok’s use: the joy of the Children of Israel is “only before Hashem” — a joy of the soul, bound to closeness with God; therefore idolatry, its very opposite, “occasions bitterness of soul,” and the Danites, tied to that drive, are “bitter of soul.”” (Devarim 12:12), and “rejoice in Hashem” (Tehillim 97:12), and so in many verses.
וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה גּוֹרֶמֶת עַצְבוּת וּמְרִירוּת נֶפֶשׁ לְנֶפֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁמְּרוּחֶקֶת בֶּאֱמֶת מֵהֶם

And idolatry occasions sadness and “bitterness of soul” to the “soul of Jewishness” of the Children of Israel, which is in truth “distanced” from it.806R’ Tzadok — parallel (Yisrael Kedoshim §3): “"you shall be holy"… and in this language also in Toras Kohanim, on the verse "and you shall be holy to Me" — and behold, it counts two [terms]: perushim and kedoshim — only that in any case it included them together.” The se’if’s “distanced” exactly: separation and holiness are two distinct things, and a separation that does not arrive at holiness leaves only the distance.
וְשִׁמְשׁוֹן סוֹפוֹ גַּם כֵּן גָּרַם גָּלוּת לְעַצְמוֹ בֵּין הָעַמִּים עַד שֶׁמָּאַס בְּחַיָּיו וְאָמַר ״תָּמוֹת נַפְשִׁי״ וְגוֹמֵר
And Shimshon, in his end, likewise brought “exile” upon himself among the nations, until he “despised his life” and said, “let my soul die [with the Philistines]” (Shoftim 16:30) —

שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד מְרִירוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ עַל מַה שֶּׁרָאָה עַצְמוֹ כָּבוּשׁ תַּחַת יָדָם, וְהוּא ״טוֹחֵן בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִים״ כִּדְרָשַׁת רַז״ל (סוֹטָה י.) שֶׁאֲנָסוּהוּ לָבוֹא עַל בְּנוֹתֵיהֶם וְשֶׁיּוֹלִידוּ מִמֶּנּוּ בָּנִים עֲרֵלִים

which was from the “bitterness of soul” over seeing himself “subdued under their hand,” “grinding in the prison-house” — as the Sages expounded (Sotah 10a)807Sotah 10a: On “and he was grinding in the prison-house” (Shoftim 16:21): “R’ Yochanan said, ‘grinding’ [techinah] denotes nothing but transgression” — teaching that the Philistines subjected Shimshon to degradation while he was in their power. that they forced him upon their daughters, that they might beget from him uncircumcised sons.
וּמִצַּד מְרִירוּתוֹ הָעָצוּם עַל זֶה נִתְרַצָּה בְּמִיתַת נַפְשׁוֹ עִם פְּלִשְׁתִּים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כְּאִלּוּ חָשַׁב חַס וְשָׁלוֹם חֶלְקוֹ עִמָּהֶם עַל יְדֵי מַעֲשָׂיו
And from his immense bitterness over this, he “consented” to die together with the Philistines, God forbid — as though he thought, God forbid, that his “portion” was with them, through his deeds.
דְּעַל כֵּן הוּצְרַךְ יַעֲקֹב לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עָלָיו ״לִישׁוּעָתְךָ קִיוִּיתִי״

Therefore Yaakov needed to pray for him, “for Your salvation I hope” (Bereishis 49:18)808Bereishis 49:18: amid the blessing of Dan, Yaakov abruptly interjects — “לִישׁוּעָתְךָ קִוִּיתִי ה׳” — “for Your salvation I hope, O Hashem.” Meforshim: Rashi (from the Midrash) — Yaakov, foreseeing Shimshon of Dan and his downfall, prayed: “I do not await deliverance through Shimshon, who is temporal, but through Your salvation.” R’ Tzadok’s use: Yaakov “needed to pray for him,” so that Shimshon — though so subdued among the Philistines that he despaired of life — “was not sunk among them at all, and none of his seed remained”; on the contrary, his very death “brought about their subjugation all the more.” —
שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת לֹא נִשְׁתַּקַּע כְּלָל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בֵּינֵיהֶם וְלֹא נִשְׁאַר מִזַּרְעוֹ כְּלוּם
that in truth he was not “sunk” among them at all, God forbid, and none of his seed remained [among them].
וְאַדְּרַבָּה עַל יְדֵי גָּלוּתוֹ זֶה וּכְבוּשָׁתוֹ בְּיָדָם כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁהוּצְרַךְ לְהָמִית אֶת עַצְמוֹ, גָּרַם לְהַכְנִיעָם בְּיוֹתֵר
On the contrary, through this “exile” of his, and his being so subdued in their hand that he had to kill himself, he “brought about their subjugation” all the more,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כִּי רַבִּים אֲשֶׁר הֵמִית בְּמוֹתוֹ״ וְגוֹמֵר, דְּכָל שְׁלִיטָתָם לְרַע לָהֶם
as it says, “for the dead he slew at his death were more [than those he slew in his life]” (ibid.) — for all their [seeming] “dominion” is to their own detriment.
וְלֹא נִתְגַּלָּה בְּיָמָיו עֲדַיִין הָ״א״ שֶׁבַּסּוֹף הַדִּינָא דְּמַלְכוּתָא, וְגַם יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע״ה לֹא גִּילָּהוּ
And in his days the alef at the end [of Dina] — the “law of kingship” — was not yet revealed, and Yaakov Avinu too did not reveal it.
רַק מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה בְּבִרְכָתוֹ, שֶׁהוּא הַבְּרָכָה דְּלֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא, קְרָאוֹ ״אַרְיֵה״ מִצַּד הִתְגַּלּוּת מַדְרֵיגַת הָעִיגּוּלִים

Only Moshe Rabbeinu, in his blessing — which is “the blessing of the Future to Come” — called him “Aryeh” [“Dan is a lion’s whelp809Devarim 33:22: in Moshe’s blessing of the tribes — “וּלְדָן אָמַר, דָּן גּוּר אַרְיֵה, יְזַנֵּק מִן הַבָּשָׁן” — “and of Dan he said: Dan is a lion’s whelp, that leaps forth from the Bashan.” Background: where Yaakov had likened Dan to a serpent, Moshe calls him a lion. R’ Tzadok’s use: only Moshe — whose blessing is “the blessing of the Future to Come” — names Dan “Aryeh,” from the revelation of the rung of “circles,” when Dan will be rejoined to Yehudah the lion, “the end fixed in the beginning,” so that even the “tail of the lion” is itself the lion.,” Devarim 33:22], from the revelation of the rung of “circles [igulim],”
כְּשֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָחוֹל לַצַּדִּיקִים לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא, וְיִהְיֶה דָּן מְחוּבָּר יַחַד עִם יְהוּדָה לִהְיוֹת ״נָעוּץ הַסּוֹף בַּתְּחִלָּה״

when the Holy One will “make a circle-dance [machol] for the righteous in the Future810Taanis 31a: “R’ Elazar said: In the Future the Holy One will make a circle-dance [machol] for the righteous, and He will sit among them in Gan Eden, and each one will point with his finger and say, ‘Behold, this is our God, for whom we hoped.’” Background: the closing aggadah of Taanis — the righteous encircling the Divine Presence. R’ Tzadok’s use: in this “circle” (igulim), where beginning and end join as one, Dan is “joined together with Yehudah” — the very theme of the fifteenth of Av, when “the tribes were permitted to intermarry,” all becoming “one people”; and then “there will no longer be ‘bitter of soul’ at all.”,” and Dan will be joined together with Yehudah — “the end fixed in the beginning.”
וְזֶהוּ הַיּוֹם טוֹב דְּט״וּ בְּאָב שֶׁבּוֹ הוּתְּרוּ שְׁבָטִים לָבוֹא זֶה בָּזֶה

And this is the festival of the fifteenth of Av, on which “the tribes were permitted to intermarry one with another” (Taanis 30b)811Taanis 30b: “R’ Shimon ben Gamliel said: There were no days of joy for Israel like the fifteenth of Av, for on it the tribes were permitted to intermarry with one another [hutru shevatim lavo zeh ba-zeh].”,
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא הִתְאַחֲדוּת כָּל הַשְּׁבָטִים יַחַד, דְּמוֹרֶה הֱיוֹת כּוּלָּם ״עַם אֶחָד״ וְלֹא כָּל שֵׁבֶט עַם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
for through this is the “unification of all the tribes together,” which indicates that they are all “one people,” and not each tribe a people unto itself;
וּמִמֵּילָא כּוּלָּא חַד וְגַם ״זַנְבָא דְּאַרְיֵה״ הוּא
and consequently “all is one,” and even the “tail of the lion” [Dan] is [the lion].
וְאָז יִהְיֶה גַּם ט״וּ בְּאָב לְשָׂשׂוֹן וּלְשִׂמְחָה וְלֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד ״מָרֵי נֶפֶשׁ״ כְּלָל

And then the fifteenth of Av, too, will be “for gladness and joy,” and there will no longer be “bitter of soul” at all. — in the great circle-dance of the Future the tail rejoins the head, and the very month of mourning turns to joy.

items.h: The theme: Adar stands opposite Yosef — “may they multiply like fish,” two Adars answering his two tribes — and “when Adar enters we increase in joy,” for Yosef is the root of joy in Hashem. Yosef could bear no union with a gentile, holiness being separation itself, and he was the most “bounded-in” in the revealed act. So even Shlomo’s marriages were in truth utterly distant, aimed only at drawing converts in.

p: [מה] וּמִשֶּׁנִּכְנַס אֲדָר שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד יוֹסֵף עַל שֵׁם ״וְיִדְגּוּ לָרֹב״

“And when Adar enters” — which is “opposite Yosef,” on account of “and may they multiply like fish [v’yidgu]812Bereishis 48:16: in Yaakov’s blessing of Ephraim and Menashe — “וְיִדְגּוּ לָרֹב בְּקֶרֶב הָאָרֶץ” — “and may they multiply like fish [v’yidgu] in the midst of the land.” Meforshim: Rashi — like the fish of the sea, which the waters cover so that the evil eye has no dominion over them, so may Yosef’s seed increase. R’ Tzadok’s use: the month Adar is “opposite Yosef,” “on account of ‘may they multiply like fish’”; and just as Yosef is counted as two tribes (Ephraim and Menashe), so there are two months of Adar — for in Yosef is “the root of joy in Hashem,” and therefore “when Adar enters, we increase in joy.”Zohar — Yosef and joy are linked through the return of the Shechinah to Yaakov: Zohar, Vayeishev 3:29, states the principle that the Shechinah does not rest in a place of sadness but in a place of joy. It then proves the point from Yaakov: during the years in which he mourned Yosef the Shechinah departed from him; when the good news of Yosef arrived, ‘ותחי רוח יעקב אביהם’ — his spirit revived, and the state in which revelation could rest returned. This supplies a Zoharic foundation for R’ Tzadok’s association of Yosef with the root of simchah. Yosef is not merely the object of Yaakov’s private happiness. His being alive restores ruach and Shechinah; the disclosure of Yosef is itself the transition from atzvus to a vessel for Divine presence. That connection also helps explain why R’ Tzadok places Yosef opposite Adar, the month in which joy increases. Yosef’s characteristic kedushah is separation and guardedness, but it is not a constricted holiness. When the covenant is protected, vitality can flow without fear of being swallowed by the outside. The resulting simchah is therefore not indulgence but the spaciousness of a life reconnected to its source. Adar’s joy and Yosef’s yesod meet in this point: holiness becomes so secure in its root that Divine life can expand openly rather than remain hidden behind mourning and anxiety.” (Bereishis 48:16) —
וְכֵן הֵם שְׁנֵי אֲדָרִין שֶׁכֵּן יוֹסֵף נִמְנֶה שְׁנֵי שְׁבָטִים, מַרְבִּין בְּשִׂמְחָה

and correspondingly there are two [months of] Adar, just as Yosef is counted as two tribes [Ephraim and Menashe] — “we increase in joy” (Taanis 29a)813Taanis 29a (Mishnah): “When Adar enters, we increase in joy [mishe-nichnas Adar marbin b’simcha].”.
כִּי בּוֹ הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַשִּׂמְחָה בַּה׳, דְּעַל יָדוֹ הוּא יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ וְחִבּוּר כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם עַל יְדֵי הַצַּדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם

For in him is the root of “joy in Hashem” — for through him is the union of the Holy One and His Shechinah, and the joining of Knesses Yisrael to their Father in Heaven, through “the tzaddik, foundation of the world.”814R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §65): "“the cucumbers” etc. — perhaps it was then their practice to prepare the fish as we do now, with onions and celery; therefore it did not say “and.”" Exactly the se’if: Adar answers to Yosef, whose blessing is “may they multiply like fish” — and it is the fish, the hidden and unruled creature, that stands at the center of the reckoning.
שֶׁיּוֹסֵף לֹא סָבַל שׁוּם הִתְחַבְּרוּת עִם גּוֹיָה וְהוֹצִיא דִּיבַּת אֶחָיו שֶׁנּוֹשְׂאִין עֵינֵיהֶם בִּבְנוֹת הָאָרֶץ
For Yosef could not bear any “joining” with a gentile woman, and [therefore] brought “an evil report of his brothers” [suspecting] that they cast their eyes on the “daughters of the land”;
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד גּוֹדֶל רִיחוּקוֹ בָּזֶה, שֶׁזֶּה כָּל קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם מוּבְדָּלִים מֵהָעַמִּים, וּ״קְדֻשָּׁה״ הוּא לְשׁוֹן הַבְדָּלָה

and this too was from the greatness of his “distancing” in this — for this is the whole holiness of Israel, that they are “separated from the peoples815Vayikra 20:26: “וִהְיִיתֶם לִי קְדֹשִׁים כִּי קָדוֹשׁ אֲנִי ה׳, וָאַבְדִּל אֶתְכֶם מִן הָעַמִּים לִהְיוֹת לִי” — “and you shall be holy to Me, for I, Hashem, am holy, and I have separated you from the peoples to be Mine.” Meforshim: Rashi (on Vayikra 19:2, “kedoshim tihyu”) — “be separated [perushim]”; holiness is an expression of havdalah, of separation. R’ Tzadok’s use: “this is the whole holiness of Israel — that they are separated from the peoples”; and Yosef, who “could bear no joining with a gentile,” embodied that separation most of all “in the revealed act,” bounded-in more than all his brothers.,” and “kedushah” is an expression of “separation.”
וְכָל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב מוּבְדָּלִים מֵהֶם לְגַמְרֵי בְּעֶצֶם, אֲבָל בְּפוֹעַל וּמַעֲשֶׂה הַנִּגְלֶה אֵצֶל בְּנֵי אָדָם הָיָה יוֹסֵף מוּגְדָּר יוֹתֵר מִכּוּלָּם

And all the seed of Yaakov are utterly separated from them in essence; but in the “revealed act” [visible] to people, Yosef was more “bounded-in” than all of them.816R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Ki Seitzei §10): “and on that day was the creation of the fish, and the blessing of the fish, in which the multiplication is very great, for they are hidden from the eye; and as they said [Taanis 8b], that blessing is found only in a thing hidden from the eye.” Exactly the se’if’s “may they multiply like fish”: Yosef’s blessing is of the kind that increases precisely by being unseen — the very opposite of a blessing that must be displayed.
וְכֵן זַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו אֲפִילּוּ הַגְּרוּעִים, דְּעַל כֵּן יָרׇבְעָם הֵרִים יָד בִּשְׁלֹמֹה עַל שֶׁנָּשָׂא בַּת פַּרְעֹה וְעָשָׂה הַמִּילּוֹא בִּשְׁבִילָהּ

And so [with] his seed after him, even the “inferior” ones: therefore Yerovam [of Ephraim, Yosef’s line] “raised a hand” against Shlomo, over his marrying the daughter of Pharaoh and building the “Millo” for her sake.

וַעֲדַיִין לֹא נִתְבָּרֵר אָז דָּבָר זֶה דְּגַם שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה הָיָה מְרוּחָק מֵהֶם בְּתַכְלִית, וּדְכָל כַּוָּונָתוֹ הָיָה לְהַכְנִיסָם תַּחַת כַּנְפֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה מַה שֶּׁאֶפְשָׁר לְהַכְנִיס מֵהֶם וּלְהוֹצִיא בִּלְעָם מִפִּיהֶם

And it was not yet clarified then that Shlomo HaMelech too was utterly distant from them, and that his whole intent was to bring them beneath the wings of the Shechinah — whatever could be brought in of them — and “to extract their swallowed [prey] from their mouth.”817R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayechi §9): “"and the name of my fathers, Avraham and Yitzchak" — this is the aspect of good deeds, and it is the totality of the aspect of the "field of apples," which has the aspect of taste and fragrance — for the supernal fathers desired it and rectify it.” The se’if’s tzaddik exactly: Yosef is the point at which the fathers’ rectifying desire reaches the field below — which is how Knesses Yisrael is joined, through him, to her Father.
כִּי לְפִי הַנִּגְלֶה לֹא הָיָה כֵן, וְלֹא לְפִי הַנִּגְלֶה לְעֵינֵי בָּשָׂר לְבַד שֶׁהֲרֵי גַּם הַכָּתוּב סִיפֵּר בִּגְנוּתוֹ בָּזֶה
For according to the “revealed,” it was not so — and [one should] not [judge] only by what is revealed to “eyes of flesh,” for even Scripture “told of his disgrace” in this.
וְאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה בִּקְשׁוּ לִמְנוֹתוֹ מֵאוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
And the Men of the Great Assembly “wished to count him [Shlomo]” among those who have no share in the World to Come, God forbid,
עַד שֶׁהוֹדִיעוּם מִשָּׁמַיִם דְּלֹא מַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵיהֶם

until they were “informed from Heaven” that “My thoughts are not your thoughts” (Yeshayah 55:8)818Yeshayah 55:8: “כִּי לֹא מַחְשְׁבוֹתַי מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵיכֶם, וְלֹא דַרְכֵיכֶם דְּרָכָי, נְאֻם ה׳” — “for My thoughts are not your thoughts, nor your ways My ways, says Hashem.” Background: God’s assurance that His designs transcend human reckoning. R’ Tzadok’s use: when the Men of the Great Assembly “wished to count Shlomo” among those without a share in the World to Come (Sanhedrin 104b), they were “informed from Heaven” by this verse — for the sages judged him “according to the revealed” of this world, whereas the truth of God’s wisdom (that Shlomo’s foreign marriages were a drawing-in, not a falling-away) will be disclosed only “in the days of Mashiach and the World to Come.”;
דְּאַף שֶׁכְּפִי הַנִּגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְעוֹלָם הָעֲשִׂיָּה שָׁפְטוּ עָלָיו מַה שֶּׁשָּׁפְטוּ, זֶהוּ כְּפִי הַחָכְמָה וְהַיְדִיעָה הַמִּתְגַּלֵּית לַחֲכָמִים וּנְבִיאִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה

for though, according to the “revealed” in this world and the World of Asiyah, they judged of him what they judged, that is [only] according to the wisdom and knowledge revealed to sages and prophets in this world,
וְלֹא כְּפִי אֲמִיתּוּת חָכְמָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁאָז יִהְיֶה חִיבּוּר אַבָּא וְאִמָּא בִּיסוֹד אַבָּא וְיַשִּׂיגוּ חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה

and not according to the truth of His wisdom, which will be revealed in the days of Mashiach and the World to Come — when there will be the “union of Abba and Ima in Yesod Abba,” and they will attain the Supernal Wisdom. — what the sages of this world could judge only by the revealed surface, the light of Mashiach will reverse: Shlomo’s foreign marriages were in truth a drawing-in, not a falling-away.

items.h: The theme: Had Yosef been born to Leah, the tikkun would already have been complete. But Leah, wishing to complete Rachel’s stature, rendered judgment upon herself — and the fetus “turned into Dinah,” the letters of Din. Her totality is harsh Din and contraction, whence the affair of Shechem; yet after death the truth emerged, that she is the root of the Nukva of holiness.

p: [מו] וְאִלּוּ זָכוּ וְנוֹלַד יוֹסֵף מִלֵּאָה, כְּבָר הָיָה אָז כֵּן תִּיקּוּן כָּל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב בִּשְׁלֵימוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד, וְזַרְעָא דְּרָחֵל הָיָה בִּנְיָמִין לְבַד

And had they merited, and Yosef been born to Leah, then the rectification of all Yaakov’s seed would already have been complete, as it will be in the Future, and Rachel’s seed would have been Binyamin alone.
וּלְפִי שֶׁרִיחֲמָה עַל רָחֵל וְרָצְתָה לְהַשְׁלִים קוֹמָתָהּ שֶׁהִיא קוֹמַת הַשְּׁכִינָה שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה דִּינָא קַשְׁיָא, עַל יְדֵי זֶה דָּנָה דִּין בְּעַצְמָהּ

And because [Leah] had mercy on Rachel and wished to “complete her stature” — which is the “stature of the Shechinah,” whence comes “harsh judgment” — through this she “rendered a judgment upon herself,”
וִיהוּדִית דְּמִצַּד מִדַּת הַדִּין הַקָּשֶׁה עֲדַיִין לֹא הִגִּיעַ זְמַן הַתִּיקּוּן הַגָּמוּר
and “judged [yehudis]” that, from the side of harsh Din, the time of the complete rectification had not yet arrived;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְהַפֵּךְ לְדִינָה אוֹתִיּוֹת ״דִּין״ עַל מִדָּתָהּ
and through this [the fetus] “turned into Dinah” — the letters of “Din” — after her trait.
וְהָ״ה״ בַּסּוֹף הִיא ״ה״ אַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁבַּשֵּׁם שֶׁרוֹמֶזֶת לְנוּקְבָא וּשְׁכִינָה

And the hei at the end [of Dinah] is the “final hei” of the Name, which alludes to the Nukva and the Shechinah.819R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §42): “from the tidings of Yitzchak’s birth — that the holy trait of Gevurah would come into the world — automatically, "when this one rises that one falls," for Sedom is the dross within the trait of Gevurah, and the evil in it is to be evil to people.” Exactly the se’if: where Gevurah enters, its dross is displaced — and Leah, rendering judgment upon herself, drew that harsh Din into the very name of the child.Tzidkas HaTzadik — Leah is the hidden world of teshuvah, whose beauty is not visible on the surface: R’ Tzadok himself gives an important parallel in Tzidkas HaTzadik §164. There he explains that teshuvah belongs to ‘עלמא דאתכסיא,’ a hidden world whose preciousness and beauty are not evident to ordinary human sight. Yaakov is told ‘כי שנואה לאה,’ and the world assumed ‘the older to the older,’ associating Leah outwardly with Esav; but her tears over that very prospect are, for R’ Tzadok, ‘the secret of teshuvah.’ Rachel, by contrast, is ‘יפת תואר ויפת מראה,’ the beauty of the revealed world and the visible tzaddik. Yet he continues that the principal ‘births’ — new Torah and renewed souls for the will of Hashem — issue through Leah’s rung of teshuvah. This parallel clarifies the present se’if’s difficult movement from Leah’s Din to Dinah and then to the later revelation of Leah as the root of the holy Nukva. The apparent harshness is not the last word. Leah’s identity is hidden precisely because teshuvah itself works through what first appears deficient, rejected, or painful and reveals a deeper capacity for new life. The transformation of the fetus into Dinah can therefore symbolize contraction without implying that Leah’s essence belongs to the side of corruption. Her hidden world contains the power by which Din itself becomes the womb of future correction.
רַק שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה אֶצְלָהּ בַּסּוֹף וְאַחֲרִית, וּכְלָלוּתָהּ הוּא ״דִּין״ הַקָּשֶׁה וְצִמְצוּם גָּמוּר מֵהִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר הַשְּׁכִינָה
Except that this [the hei] was in her only at the “end,” while her totality is “harsh Din” and complete “contraction” from the revelation of the Shechinah’s light;
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה גָּרַם מַעֲשֵׂה שְׁכֶם שֶׁנִּדְבְּקָה בּוֹ עַד שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל מִמֶּנָּה דְּהַנִּבְעֶלֶת לְגוֹי קָשֶׁה לִפְרוֹשׁ

which brought about the “affair of Shechem,” that she “clung to him” — until the Sages said, of her, that “one who has cohabited with a gentile finds it hard to part.”820R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Shemos §4): “"one who guards Shabbos from profaning it" and "guards his hand from doing any evil"; and they expounded in the Mechilta that he is guarded from the transgression — and it appears that this alludes in particular to this blemish, which is called "evil."” The se’if’s difficulty exactly: what is at stake in “cohabiting with a gentile” is not one prohibition among others but the blemish the Torah names simply “evil,” from which a person must be guarded, not merely warned.
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ עַל ״בֶּן הַכְּנַעֲנִית״ זוֹ דִּינָה שֶׁנִּבְעֲלָה לִכְנַעֲנִי, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה גַּם הִיא ״כְּנַעֲנִית״ כְּאִלּוּ נִדְבְּקָה בּוֹ לְגַמְרֵי חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כְּמוֹהוּ

And so they said, that “the son of the Canaanite woman” (Bereishis 46:10) [refers to] this Dinah, who had cohabited with a Canaanite — and through this she too is “a Canaanite,” as though she clung to him entirely, God forbid, like him.821Bereishis Rabbah 80:11: “‘And they took Dinah’ — R’ Yudan said: they dragged her out [reluctant to leave]. R’ Huna said: a woman who has cohabited with an uncircumcised man finds it hard to part [from him]. R’ Huna said: [Dinah] said, ‘and I, where shall I carry my shame?’ — until Shimon swore to her that he would take her [as a wife] (and this was before the giving of the Torah). This is [the meaning of] what is written (Bereishis 46), ‘and Shaul son of the Canaanite woman’ — the son of Dinah who had cohabited with a Canaanite — And the Rabbanan say: Shimon took her and buried her in the land of Canaan.”
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ [בְּב״ר] ״חֲדָא הֲוֵי לֵיהּ״ וְהַלְוַאי קְבָרָהּ
And therefore they said [in Bereishis Rabbah] “he had one [daughter],” and “would that he had buried her” —
דִּלְמַרְאִית עַיִן בְּעוֹלָם הָעֲשִׂיָּה הָיָה נִרְאֶה כֵן, וְעַל כֵּן וּלְוַאי קְבָרָהּ
for to the “outward eye,” in the World of Asiyah, it appeared so, and therefore “would that he had buried her”;
וְאַחַר הַקְּבוּרָה וְהִסְתַּלְּקוּתָהּ מֵעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא ״עַלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא״ נִתְגַּלָּה הָאֱמֶת — ״ה״ אַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁבָּהּ
but after burial, and her departure from this world — which is “the world of falsehood” — the truth was revealed: the “final hei” within her,
שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר ״ה׳ בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ״ וְאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת וְחִיבּוּר לִבְנֵי נֵכָר כְּלָל
which is the root of Knesses Yisrael, “Hashem alone guides him” (Devarim 32:12), having no connection or “joining” to “strangers” at all.
וּבַת אַחַת שֶׁהָיְתָה לוֹ לְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע״ה מִצַּד מִדַּת הָאֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב וַדַּאי הִיא שֹׁרֶשׁ נוּקְבָא דִּקְדֻשָּׁה
And the one daughter that Yaakov had — from the side of “the trait of truth to Yaakov” — is certainly the “root of the Nukva of holiness.”
רַק לְפִי שֶׁהָאִשָּׁה הֵבִיאָה מִיתָה לָעוֹלָם, דְּבָהּ אֲחִיזַת הַחִיצוֹנִים כַּנּוֹדָע דְּרַגְלֶיהָ ״יוֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת״
Only that “the woman brought death to the world” — for in her is the “grip of the outer [forces],” as is known, “her feet descend to death”;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּב״ר] דְּאֵין ״ס׳״ בְּפָרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית עַד בְּרִיאַת הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁנִּבְרָא הַשָּׂטָן עִמָּהּ

and as they said [in Bereishis Rabbah], that there is no [letter] samech in Parashas Bereishis until the creation of the woman — that “the Satan was created with her822Bereishis Rabbah 17:6: the Midrash observes that no letter samech appears in the Torah from “In the beginning” until the creation of the woman — the first samech being “וַיִּסְגֹּר בָּשָׂר תַּחְתֶּנָּה” (“and He closed up the flesh in its place,” Bereishis 2:21) — and teaches: “once the woman was created, the Satan was created with her.” Background: the samech (ס), a closed, encircling letter, marks the entry of concealment and of the adversary. Meforshim: the Midrash elsewhere (Bereishis Rabbah 17:8; and the Mishnah, Shabbos 2:6) teaches that “the woman brought death to the world” through Chava; and the Sages identify this “Satan” with the yetzer hara and the Angel of Death (Bava Basra 16a) — one adversary under three names. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is why “in her is the grip of the outer forces” and “her feet descend to death” — the woman is the “vessel of contraction [tzimtzum],” the power that contracts and conceals the light; the very samech/Satan born with her is the “trait of Din” that constricts the radiance of the Shechinah.,”
וְהוּא יֵצֶר הָרַע וְהוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת שֹׁרֶשׁ כָּל הָרַע שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִצַּד מִדַּת הַדִּין שֶׁבָּהּ
and he is the “evil inclination,” and he is the “angel of death,” the root of all the evil in this world — drawn from the side of the “trait of Din” in her,
רְצֹה לוֹמַר כֹּחַ הַצִּמְצוּם שֶׁהוּא מִסִּטְרָא, שֶׁהִיא הַכְּלִי קִיבּוּל לְצַמְצֵם הָאוֹר וּלְהַעֲלִימוֹ
that is, the “power of contraction,” which is from “her side” — for she is the “vessel of receiving,” to contract the light and conceal it.
וְאֵין בָּהֶם שׁוּם הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר דְּתוֹרָה רַק מִצַּד חִיבּוּרָן לְבַעֲלֵיהֶן וְלִבְנֵיהֶן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרָכוֹת] ״הָנֵי נָשֵׁי בְּמַאי זָכְיָין״ כו׳
And there is in them [women] no “revelation of the light of Torah” except through their “joining” to their husbands and children, as they said [in Berachos], “these women — how do they merit?” —
דְּרַק עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִזְדַּכְּכוֹת, אֲבָל מִצַּד עַצְמָן אֵין בָּהֶם הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר מֵאִיר

for only through this are they “refined,” but of themselves there is in them no “shining light.”823Berachos 17a: Rav said to R’ Chiya, “In what do women merit? — In bringing their children to learn Torah in the beis knesses, and sending their husbands to study in the beis midrash, and waiting for their husbands until they return from the beis midrash.” Background: the Gemara assumes that women, exempt from the mitzvah of Torah study, seem to lack its great merit. Meforshim: the Iyun Yaakov and Maharsha explain that they share fully in that merit by enabling it — “one who causes a mitzvah to be done is as one who does it” — so their portion equals the learner’s own. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is exactly his point — of herself the woman has “no revelation of the light of Torah,” being the “vessel of contraction”; her light shines only “through her joining to her husband and children,” through whom she is “refined.”
וּמִצַּד גּוֹדֶל הַהֶעְלֵם עַל יְדֵי זֶה ״אֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים״ מִתְתַּקְּנָא בְּרָזָא דְּ״אֵשֶׁת חַיִל״ כַּיָּדוּעַ בַּזֹּהַר
And by virtue of the greatness of the “concealment,” through this the “woman of harlotry” is “rectified” in the secret of the “woman of valor,” as is known in the Zohar.
וְיֵשׁ ״אֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים״ וְ״אֵשֶׁת מְדִינִים״ וְהֵם הַקְּלִיפּוֹת שֶׁנֶּגֶד רָחֵל וְלֵאָה, כִּי ״זֶה לְעוּמַּת זֶה עָשָׂה אֱלֹקִים״
And there is a “woman of harlotry” and a “woman of strife” — and they are the “husks” corresponding to Rachel and Leah, for “God has made this over against that” (Koheles 7:14);
וְאֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים הוּא הֵפֶךְ רָחֵל, וְאֵשֶׁת מְדִינִים הוּא הַהֵיפֶךְ מִלֵּאָה, וְזֶה מְבוֹאָר מִתּוֹךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְמַעְלָה
the “woman of harlotry” is the opposite of Rachel, and the “woman of strife” the opposite of Leah, as is clear from what I wrote above.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הָיָה הָרָצוֹן לְהִתְגַּלּוּת יְסוֹד דְּאַבָּא בָּעוֹלָם, אֶלָּא שֶׁדָּנָה דִּין וְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת קִטְרוּג מִדַּת הַדִּין, גָּרַם הִתְעוֹרְרוּת אָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל בְּאוֹתָהּ מַדְרֵיגָה

And when the “will” arose for the revelation of Yesod Abba in the world — except that she “rendered a judgment,” and an “arousal of the accusation of Din” [ensued] — it caused an “arousal of the base man” at that very rung,
כַּיָּדוּעַ דִּלְעוֹלָם שְׁלִיטַת אָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל בְּאָדָם דִּקְדֻשָּׁה הוּא בְּאוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר עַצְמוֹ וְאוֹתָהּ מַדְרֵיגָה עַצְמָהּ שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגְדּוֹ וּלְעוּמָּתוֹ
as is known, that the dominion of the “base man” over the “man of holiness” is always at that very “limb” and that very rung which is “opposite it and corresponding to it”;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְעוֹרֵר כֹּחַ ״אֵשֶׁת מְדִינִים״ שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ קְצָת שַׁיָּיכוּת בְּאוֹתִיּוֹת ״דִּין״ שֶׁבְּדִינָה

and through this was aroused the power of the “woman of strife [eishes medinim],” which had some “connection” to the letters of “Din” that are in “Dinah.” — the two husks are custom-fitted to the two matriarchs: “harlotry” shadows Rachel’s revealed world, “strife” shadows Leah’s hidden one, each evil made precisely over against its good.

items.h: The theme: The Midianites are Avraham’s seed through Keturah, carrying off the “dross” of his Chesed. But since they issued after the circumcision, Yitzchak’s birth and the Akeidah, that Chesed was already constrained toward Din — hence the name Midyan, from strife. Unlike the “woman of harlotry,” who separates entirely, the “woman of strife” can only stir surface friction; and as Avraham’s seed they even long to cleave to Israel, but on their own terms.

p: [מז] וְהַמְּדִינִים הֵם זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע״ה מִבְּנֵי קְטוּרָה, וְעַל כֵּן נִכְלָלִים בִּכְלַל יִשְׁמְעֵאלִים בְּסִיפּוּר מְכִירַת יוֹסֵף

And the Midianites are the seed of Avraham Avinu, from the children of Keturah, and are therefore included among the “Ishmaelites” in the account of the sale of Yosef;824R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §89): “those who atone for others — their reward is measure for measure, that they merit for their own — that is, for their seed after them; and this is "and it shall be for him and for his seed."” Exactly the se’if: the line of Keturah carries off the “dross” of Avraham’s Chesed, for what a father transmits reaches his seed by measure — and the holy line is secured only through Yitzchak.Tiferes Shlomo — extracting holy sparks requires stricter fidelity to Torah, not imitation of the shell: Tiferes Shlomo, Purim §99, develops the doctrine of birur with an important warning. When the nations are subdued, he explains, the holy sparks swallowed within them emerge and can enter Israel; but precisely because those sparks had been clothed in deeply corrupt environments, the Torah warns ‘השמר לך פן תנקש אחריהם’ — do not be ensnared by imitating the nations after their defeat. He concludes that the Divine command must be followed without adding or subtracting: one must extract the holy life without importing the alien form that had surrounded it. This distinction is highly relevant to R’ Tzadok’s description of Midyan. Midyan can possess a genuine point of affinity — a residue of Avraham’s line and therefore a desire to attach to Israel — while the form in which that desire presents itself is strife and prohibited attachment. The presence of a holy root inside a mixed structure does not make the structure holy. On the contrary, it creates the need for a more exact birur. The Tiferes Shlomo therefore supplies a useful boundary for the next se’if as well: discovering future holiness within a nation, person, or desire is never a reason to imitate its present forbidden expression. The spark is to be removed from the shell and returned to Torah; otherwise the seeker of hidden holiness can become captive to the very husk he meant to refine.
וְיֵשׁ בָּהֶם גַּם כֵּן זוּהֲמָא דְּיִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּתַאֲווֹת רָעוֹת וְזִימָּה שֶׁהוּא הַפְּסֹלֶת דְּמִדַּת הַחֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע״ה

and there is in them, too, the “defilement of Ishmael” — evil desires and lewdness — which is the “dross” of the trait of Chesed of Avraham Avinu.825R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Chayei Sarah §6): “"and your end shall greatly increase" — this is Avraham, who took a wife and fathered with her several sons at the last.” Exactly the se’if: Keturah’s children issue from Avraham’s later period — after the circumcision, Yitzchak, and the Akeidah — and it is this that constrains the Chesed they inherit.
רַק לְפִי שֶׁהֵם יָצְאוּ מֵאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע״ה אַחַר שֶׁנִּימּוֹל וְאַחַר לֵידַת יִצְחָק וְהָעֲקֵידָה דְּאִתְכְּלִילוּ אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק
Only, since they issued from Avraham after he was circumcised, and after the birth of Yitzchak and the Akeidah, in which “Avraham and Yitzchak were merged,”
וְזָכָה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע״ה גַּם לְדַרְגָּא דְּיִצְחָק כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹקִים אַתָּה״, וּלְצַמְצֵם הַחֲסָדִים שֶׁלֹּא יִתְפַּשְּׁטוּ לְמָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ

and Avraham merited also the rung of Yitzchak, as it says, “for you are one who fears God826Bereishis 22:12: at the Akeidah, the angel stays Avraham’s hand — “כִּי עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה, וְלֹא חָשַׂכְתָּ אֶת בִּנְךָ” — “for now I know that you are one who fears God, and you have not withheld your son.” Meforshim: Rashi — “now I know” means “now I have made [it] known [to all]” that you love Me; the Ramban explains that the trial brought Avraham’s latent fear “from the potential into the actual,” so that it be rewarded as a deed and not as intention alone. R’ Tzadok’s use: through the Akeidah “Avraham merited also the rung of Yitzchak” — the trait of yirah and Gevurah — learning “to contract the chasadim so they not spread to a place where they are not needed”; hence the sons of Keturah, born to him only afterward, bear a contracted desire, called “Midyan” (from din), unlike Ishmael’s unbounded lust.” (Bereishis 22:12), and to “contract” the chasadim so they not spread to a place where they are not needed —
עַל כֵּן נִקְרְאוּ ״מִדְיָן״ שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן ״דִּין״ וּ״מְדָנִים״ הַמּוֹרֶה פְּסֹלֶת גְּבוּרָה רָעָה וְהֵיפֶךְ הַתַּאֲוָה

therefore they are called “Midyan,” an expression of “din” and “medanim [strife],” indicating the “dross of evil Gevurah,” the opposite of [mere] desire.827R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §38): “for the birth of Yishmael is the clarification of the filth of the love and longing of Avraham Avinu — meaning that he is the dross of the longings and desires, as it says in the Zohar on "He shone forth from Har Paran."” Exactly the se’if: the Midianite line carries the same “dross of Chesed” as Yishmael — the residue left when Avraham’s love is clarified.
כִּי תַּאֲוָותָם הָיְתָה מְצוּמְצֶמֶת קְצָת, בְּהֶפְקֵר גָּמוּר לֹא כְּיִשְׁמָעֵאל, רַק זְנוּת בֵּית מִדְיָן
For their desire was somewhat “contracted” — not [given over] to utter licentiousness like Ishmael, but only the “harlotry of the house of Midyan,”
רַק שֶׁהָיָה לְעוֹרֵר מְדָנִים בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם עַל יְדֵי זֶה, וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרְאוּ ״מִדְיָן״ דְּזֶה כָּל יִשְׁעָם וְחֶפְצָם
[whose purpose] was [only] to “stir strife” between Israel and their Father in Heaven thereby — and therefore they are called “Midyan,” for this is their whole aim and desire.

כִּי יְסוֹד אַבָּא רְצֹה לוֹמַר הִתְקַשְּׁרוּת גָּמוּר דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְהַפְרִיד חִיבּוּר זֶה לְגַמְרֵי עַל יְדֵי הֲסָתַת ״אֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים״ דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא הַמַּפְרִיד וְגוֹרֵם שִׁילּוּחַ וְגָלוּת

For Yesod Abba means “complete bonding that never parts,” and it cannot fully sunder this “joining” through the incitement of the “woman of harlotry” — the thing that “separates” and causes “banishment and exile”;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הֲסָתַת ״אֵשֶׁת מְדִינִים״ הוּא רַק בִּדְבָרִים הַמְעוֹרְרִים קְטָט וְרַק לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן
whereas the incitement of the “woman of strife” is only in things that “stir friction,” and only “to outward appearance.”
כִּי מִצַּד אוֹתָהּ מַדְרֵיגָה אֵין עוֹד מָקוֹם לִזְנוּת גָּמוּר, שֶׁהוּא הַפְרָדָה ״כִּי תִזְנֶה הָאִשָּׁה מֵאִישָׁהּ״, דְּזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּדוֹר דֵּעָה כְּדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר

For from the side of that rung there is no longer room for “complete harlotry,” which is “separation” — “when a woman goes astray from her husband” — for this is impossible in a “generation of knowledge” like the generation of the Wilderness.
רַק שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת מָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה אַחַר כָּךְ דְּאוֹתָם שֶׁלֹּא יָדְעוּ אִישׁ הֶחֱיוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לָהֶם וְנִדְבְּקוּ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל

Only that they had “some connection” — as it was afterward, that “those who had not known a man” [of the Midianite women] the Children of Israel “kept alive828Bamidbar 31:18: after the war against Midyan, Moshe instructs — “וְכֹל הַטַּף בַּנָּשִׁים אֲשֶׁר לֹא יָדְעוּ מִשְׁכַּב זָכָר, הַחֲיוּ לָכֶם” — “but all the young women who have not known a man’s embrace, keep alive for yourselves.” Meforshim: Rashi (from the Sifrei) — the fit ones were passed before the tzitz, whose face would pale over any who had sinned, so as to discern who “had not known a man.” R’ Tzadok’s use: those Midianite women “who had not known a man” the Children of Israel “kept alive… and they cleaved to Israel” — for as Avraham’s seed they harbor “a longing to cleave to Israel”; had they not first “known” [union] through harlotry and prohibition, they could have cleaved “in a permitted manner.”” for themselves, and they cleaved to Israel.
וְאִלּוּ גַּם הֵם לֹא יָדְעוּ תְּחִלָּה בִּזְנוּת וְאִיסּוּר, הָיוּ נִדְבָּקִים אַחַר כָּךְ בָּהֶם בְּהֶיתֵּר
And had these too not “known” [connection] first through harlotry and prohibition, they would have cleaved to them afterward in a permitted manner;
דְּמִצַּד הֱיוֹתָם זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם אַחַר שֶׁזָּכָה לְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלִיקָּרֵא ״אֶזְרָחִי״ יֵשׁ לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת וְחֵשֶׁק לִידָּבֵק בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל

for by virtue of their being Avraham’s seed — after he merited the name Israel and to be called “the Ezrachi [native]829Bava Basra 15a: among the “ten elders” by whose hand [portions of] Tehillim were composed, the Gemara identifies “Eisan ha-Ezrachi” (Tehillim 89:1) as Avraham Avinu. Meforshim: Rashi — Eisan (“mighty”) and Ezrachi denote Avraham, mighty in the fear of God; and the ezrach is the deep-rooted “native,” as in “ezrach ra’anan,” a firmly-rooted flourishing tree (Tehillim 37:35). R’ Tzadok’s use: though Avraham began as a wandering “sojourner,” he “merited the name Israel and to be called the Ezrachi [native]” — rooted and settled in holiness; and by virtue of this very rootedness his seed, even Midyan, retain “a connection and a longing to cleave to Israel.”” — they have a “connection” and a longing to cleave to Israel.
אֶלָּא שֶׁחֶשְׁקָם לִהְיוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל נִדְבָּקִים בָּהֶם כְּמוֹת שֶׁהֵם בְּגוֹיּוּתָם, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה יָדָם עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנָה
Except that their longing is that Israel cleave to them, as they are in their “gentile-ness,” so that “their hand be uppermost”;
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן ״אֵשֶׁת מְדִינִים״ הָרוּחָנִית לִמְשׁוֹל בְּבַעְלָהּ, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מְעוֹרֶרֶת מְדִינִים וּקְטָטוֹת

and this is the matter of the spiritual “woman of strife” — to “rule over her husband,” and through this she “stirs strife and quarrels.” — the “woman of strife,” unlike the “woman of harlotry,” cannot truly sever Israel from their Father; being of Avraham’s own seed she even longs to cleave, but only on her own terms, seeking the upper hand.

items.h: The theme: This was Bilaam’s whole counsel — “the smooth-tongued,” who flattered Israel in order to drive them from the world. He revealed their immense future elevation and thereby instilled a license to do whatever the heart wished, reasoning that a depth which cleaves to God cannot be contradicted by any deed. But the Torah issues from Yesod Abba, and transgressing it outwardly, even for Heaven’s sake, arouses the eishes medinim.

p: [מח] וְזֶה הָיָה כָּל עֵצַת אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע שֶׁנִּקְרָא ״מַחֲלִיק לָשׁוֹן״
And this was the whole counsel of that wicked one, who is called “the smooth-tongued [machalik lashon]” —
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּדְבָרִים רַבָּה] דְּזֶה בִּלְעָם שֶׁהֶחֱלִיק לָשׁוֹן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּדֵי לְטׇרְדָן מֵהָעוֹלָם

as they said [in Devarim Rabbah], that this is Bilaam, who “smoothed his tongue830Devarim Rabbah 1 (Parashas Devarim): the Midrash contrasts Moshe, who rebuked Israel out of love, with Bilaam — “the smooth-tongued [machalik lashon]” (cf. Mishlei 28:23) — who blessed them out of hatred, “in order to drive them from the world.” Meforshim: R’ Acha bar Chanina explains that God assigned the rebukes to Moshe (their lover) and the blessings to Bilaam (their hater), lest Israel protest “an enemy rebukes us” or the nations say “their friend merely flatters them” — so that both rebuke and blessing be believed; the Midrash-commentators add that Bilaam’s very flattery was the deadlier weapon, for by exalting Israel he sought to make them haughty and fall (as they did at Shittim, Bamidbar 25). R’ Tzadok’s use: this was Bilaam’s “whole counsel” — he “revealed to them their immense elevation” (that no sin will ever separate them) precisely in order to instill license “to do whatever was in their hearts, even against the Torah,” reasoning that their inmost cleaving to the living God can be undone by no deed.Mei HaShiloach — Korach’s error is the precise antinomian inference Bilaam tries to plant: Mei HaShiloach I, Korach §2, explains Korach’s claim that a garment wholly of techeiles should require no tzitzis as a spiritual argument. Techeiles signifies yirah, and Korach reasoned from the deepest truth that ‘הכל בידי שמים’ — even human desire and action ultimately have their source in Hashem. If so, he argued, how can a person truly do something against the Divine will, and why is the external discipline of tzitzis still necessary? The Ishbitzer’s answer is crucial: in this world Hashem deliberately hides that deepest mode of providence because He desires human avodah. At the level available to the person, he must live as a baal bechirah and submit himself to yirah and mitzvah; if the total Divine determination were exposed in advance, no genuine avodah would grow. This is almost the exact theological temptation R’ Tzadok attributes here to Bilaam. Bilaam tells Israel a true statement about their ultimate inseparability from Hashem and converts it into a false permission to violate the Torah now. The Mei HaShiloach shows why that move is illegitimate even within Izhbitz itself. Hidden foreknowledge may illuminate events retrospectively, after avodah and teshuvah; it cannot be used prospectively to cancel the revealed command. ‘Everything is from Hashem’ is not a substitute for tzitzis, yirah, halachah, or bechirah in the world where man is commanded to serve.” to Israel [with flattery] in order to “drive them from the world.”831R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Soferim §15): “Certainly the Torah did not write a falsehood [when Bilaam] said of himself, ‘one who knows the knowledge of the Most High’ [yodea da’as elyon]; only that all his knowledge was ‘from the lips outward,’ and once he brought it out from the lips, perforce nothing remained with him, and he was driven off and went, as it says, ‘behold, I am going [to my people]’ (Bamidbar 24:14). And even though he knew, by the knowledge of the Most High, that [Hashem] loves Israel and that they endure for all eternity — with all this he did not desist from counseling schemes to make them stumble.” (Exactly the se’if’s Bilaam: ‘the smooth-tongued,’ whose ‘knowledge’ is all lip-deep flattery; he saw Israel’s imperishable elevation and used the very seeing to try to drive them from the world.)832R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Bo §12): “Israel who stood at Har Sinai — their filth ceased, which availed even to bring holiness into the animals; and Bilaam, who was as the kelipah of Amalek, could not comprehend that there should be holiness in such a matter.” Exactly the se’if’s counsel: Bilaam could see Israel’s elevation but not what it was — so he could report it truly and still turn it into a license.
רְצֹה לוֹמַר גִּילָּה לָהֶם מַעֲלָתָם הָעֲצוּמָה בָּאַחֲרִית שֶׁשּׁוּם חֲטָאִים לֹא יַפְרִידוּם וְחֹשֶׁךְ לֹא יַחְשִׁיכוּם
That is, he “revealed to them their immense elevation” — that in the End no sins will separate them, and no darkness will darken them —
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הִכְנִיס בְּלִבָּם לַעֲשׂוֹת כָּל מַה שֶּׁבִּלְבָבָם, וְאַף אִם לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן הוּא נֶגֶד הַתּוֹרָה
and through this he “instilled in their hearts” to do whatever was in their hearts, even if to outward appearance it is against the Torah,
לְפִי שֶׁבִּלְבָבָם יָדְעוּ שֶׁהֵם דְּבוּקִים בְּכָל מַעֲמַקֵּיהֶם בֶּאֱמֶת בֵּאלֹקִים חַיִּים, וַדַּאי כָּל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם אֵינֶנּוּ מִתְנַגֵּד זֶה

[reasoning] that since in their hearts they know they truly cleave, in all their depths, to the living God, surely none of their deeds contradicts this.833R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh §12): “and it counts there, regarding Achan, all the severe transgressions he transgressed against the five books of the Torah, and he was one who drew his foreskin forward… and at first glance one must understand why they attributed to him the sins that are not explicit.” The se’if’s mechanism exactly: where a man is told his elevation is unconditional, the sins that follow are the unwritten ones — precisely those no verse had to forbid him.
וְהַתּוֹרָה הִיא ״נוֹבְלוֹת חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה״ וְיוֹצֵאת מִיסוֹד אַבָּא
But the Torah is “the fallen-fruit [novlos] of Supernal Wisdom,” and issues from Yesod Abba;
וְכַאֲשֶׁר עוֹבֵר עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן אַף שֶׁבְּלִבּוֹ לְשָׁמַיִם, מְעוֹרֵר מְדִינִים וּקְלִיפָּה דְּ״אֵשֶׁת מְדִינִים״ שֶׁנֶּגֶד יְסוֹד אַבָּא

and when one transgresses the words of Torah “to outward appearance,” even if in his heart [he intends] for Heaven, he “arouses strife” — the husk of the “woman of strife,” which is opposite Yesod Abba.
וְעַל כֵּן ״מִדְיָן״ וַ״עֲמָלֵק״ מְחוּבָּרִים כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים כַּמְבוֹאָר בַּמִּקְרָאוֹת, כִּי גַּם עֲמָלֵק מִתְעוֹרֵר נֶגֶד זֶה כַּיָּדוּעַ, וּמְבוֹאָר אֶצְלֵנוּ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר בְּסוֹד הַפּוּרִים

And therefore “Midyan” and “Amalek” are joined together several times, as is evident in the verses — for Amalek too is “aroused” against this, as is known, and it is explained by us elsewhere in the “secret of Purim.”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה קִטְרוּג הָמָן עַל מַה שֶּׁלֹּא עָשׂוּ אֶלָּא לְפָנִים בְּהִשְׁתַּחֲוָיָה לַצֶּלֶם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל (מְגִילָּה יב.)

As Haman’s “accusation” was over what they [Israel] had done “only outwardly [lifnim]” in bowing to the image [in Nevuchadnetzar’s day], as the Sages said (Megillah 12a)834Megillah 12a: [R’ Shimon bar Yochai’s students asked why the Jews of that generation were liable to destruction; one answer:] “because they bowed to the image [of Nevuchadnezzar]” — but they did so only outwardly [lifnim], and so [Hashem] too dealt with them only outwardly [and did not truly destroy them]. —
כִּי הוּא ״רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם״, וּתְחִלַּת הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הוּא ״מִדְיָן״, וְזֶהוּ הַתְחָלַת הָרַע
for he [Amalek] is “the first of the nations” (Bamidbar 24:20), and the “beginning of the spreading-forth” is Midyan — and this is the “beginning of evil.”
וַעֲמָלֵק הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הָרַע וְכָלוּל בּוֹ כָּל מִינֵי רַע שֶׁל כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת כּוּלָּם
And Amalek is the “root of evil,” and included in him are all the kinds of evil of all the nations together;
עַל כֵּן אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא רֵאשִׁיתָם וּפוֹשֵׁט טְלָפַיִם, אַחֲרִיתוֹ עֲדֵי אוֹבֵד לְגַמְרֵי
therefore, although he is “their first” and “spreads his hooves” [feigning purity], “his end is destruction” entirely (Bamidbar 24:20);
וּשְׁאָר כָּל אוּמּוֹת כָּל אַחַת כּוֹלֵל רַע מְיוּחָד לְבַד שֶׁבּוֹ שָׁרְשׁוֹ וְעִיקַּר אֲחִיזָתוֹ
whereas each of the other nations includes [only] one particular evil alone, in which is its root and its main “grip.”
וְשֹׁרֶשׁ ״מִדְיָן״ הוּא לְעוֹרֵר מְדִינִים נֶגֶד שֹׁרֶשׁ יְסוֹד יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּ״אוֹרַיְיתָא וְיִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלּוֹ חַד״ הַיּוֹצֵא מִיסוֹד אַבָּא וְיִשְׂרָאֵל סָבָא

And the root of “Midyan” is to “stir strife” against the root of the Yesod of Israel — for “the Torah and Israel are entirely one,” issuing from Yesod Abba and “Yisrael Saba.” — Bilaam’s flattery was thus the subtlest poison: a true doctrine — that their depths never separate — twisted into license to defy the very Torah that binds them, arousing the strife only outward transgression can stir.

items.h: The theme: Why Yosef was sold “as a slave”: the tribes did not yet know that Yaakov’s bed was whole, and seeing Yosef “desiring to rule” they suspected the dross of the middle-line trait. They meant to sell him to the Ishmaelites, but he passed to the Midianites and then to Egypt. Yet “their thought was for evil, and God intended it for good” — his test with Potifar’s wife clarified Israel’s holiness and separateness.

p: [מט] וְעַל כֵּן ״לְעֶבֶד״ נִמְכַּר יוֹסֵף לָהֶם

And therefore Yosef was sold to them “as a slave.”835Tehillim 105:17: of the descent to Egypt — “שָׁלַח לִפְנֵיהֶם אִישׁ, לְעֶבֶד נִמְכַּר יוֹסֵף” — “He sent a man before them; Yosef was sold as a slave.” Meforshim: Rashi and Radak — God “sent” Yosef ahead by means of his sale, to prepare sustenance for the family’s descent; the very selling “as a slave” was the providential instrument. R’ Tzadok’s use: Yosef was sold specifically “as a slave” — “the dominion of man over man to his detriment” — for the brothers, supposing that Yaakov’s line bore “dross” as Avraham’s and Yitzchak’s had, sold him to be subdued; yet this very subjugation set the “clarification” of Israel’s holiness in motion.
דְּעִנְיַן מְכִירָתוֹ — שֶׁהַשְּׁבָטִים לֹא יָדְעוּ דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע״ה מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה, וְחָשְׁבוּ דְּגַם בּוֹ יָצָא פְּסֹלֶת כְּמֵאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק
For the matter of his sale [was thus]: the tribes did not [yet] know that Yaakov’s “bed was whole,” and thought that “dross” had issued from him too, as from Avraham and Yitzchak [Ishmael and Esav];
וְדִימּוּ עַל יוֹסֵף כִּי רָאוּהוּ חָפֵץ לִמְשׁוֹל בָּהֶם

and they “imagined” [this] of Yosef, since they saw him “desiring to rule over them.”836R’ Tzadok — parallel (Dover Tzedek, Mishlei §1): “The Name Havayah is the essential Name of Hashem, comprising all the vitality bestowed into creation — which is the ‘middle line’ [kav emtzai] of all creation. And Yosef, too, holds fast to this rung, for ‘the radiance of his countenance resembled his father’s’; and the tzaddik is the ‘guardian of the covenant,’ the rung of Yosef, in whom the [Divine] Name prevails.” (This is why the brothers’ suspicion in the se’if fell on Yosef in particular: he embodies Yaakov’s own ‘middle line’ — the tzaddik-Yesod whose face mirrors his father’s — so that in him, of all the sons, they thought to detect the ‘dross’ of that very trait.)
וְחָשְׁבוּ דְּזֶהוּ פְּסֹלֶת מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע״ה ״קַו הָאֶמְצָעִי״ הַמְחוּבָּר מֵחֶסֶד וּגְבוּרָה, כִּי גֵּיאוּת הוּא מִתַּאֲוָה וְחַשְׁקוּת רָעוֹת וּמִכַּעַס וּגְבוּרוֹת רָעוֹת

And they thought this was the “dross” of Yaakov’s trait — the “middle line,” compounded of Chesed and Gevurah — for “haughtiness [gei’us]” comes from desire and evil cravings [Chesed’s dross], and from anger and “evil gevuros.”837R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayeishev §10): “for the covenant of the tongue and the covenant of the flesh correspond, as is known; and after he saw what came of this — that they sold him to Egypt — then he became embittered in his soul, that he had caused it by blemishing in the trait of Yesod.” Exactly the se’if: the “evil report” and the selling are one matter — the suspicion the brothers formed and Yosef’s own speech both turn on the same trait.
וּלְפִי שֶׁכָּל מִינֵי רַע מְחוּבָּרִים יַחַד, וּמִי שֶׁשָּׁרְשׁוֹ בְּאֵיזֶה רַע פְּרָטִי יֵשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְכָל מִינֵי רַע
And since “all kinds of evil are joined together,” and one whose root is in some particular evil has a “connection” to all kinds of evil,
עַל כֵּן אַף שֶׁהִכִּירוּ בּוֹ שֶׁהוּא מוּגְדָּר מִתַּאֲווֹת חָשְׁבוּ דְּאֵין זֶה בֶּאֱמֶת

therefore, even though they recognized in him that he was “bounded-in” from [base] desires, they thought “this is not [so] in truth.”838R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayeishev §1): “this is the very matter that touches you, which is in your power to rectify… and by this they showed him that through the power of your Torah you can rectify the totality of the souls of Israel.” The se’if’s reversal precisely: the very point at which the brothers suspected Yosef of “desiring to rule” is the point at which the rectification of the whole was in fact placed in his hand.
וּבְסִטְרָא דְּרַע אִם נִרְאֶה בְּגַוְונוֹ אֵיזֶה דָּבָר טוֹב יָדוּעַ דִּפְנִימִיּוּתוֹ הוּא מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ
For on the “side of evil,” if some good thing appears in its “hue,” it is known that its “inwardness” is the very opposite;
וּלְפִי שֶׁבְּדָבָר זֶה הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הָרוֹעַ הוּא חָפֵץ לְהַעֲלִים כְּדֶרֶךְ ״עַלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא״ שֶׁמַּרְאֶה הַכֹּל הֵיפֶךְ הָאֱמֶת
and since in this matter he is at the “extreme of evil,” he “wishes to conceal” [it] — in the manner of “the world of falsehood,” which shows everything the opposite of the truth.
וְעַל כֵּן חָשְׁבוּ לְמָכְרוֹ לְיִשְׁמְעֵאלִים שֶׁהֵם שֹׁרֶשׁ הָרַע דְּתַאֲוָה
And therefore they planned to sell him to the “Ishmaelites,” who are the “root of the evil of desire”;
וְלֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדָם שֶׁנִּמְכַּר לַמְּדִינִים שֶׁהֵם הַחֲפֵצִים בְּכָךְ לְעוֹרֵר מְדִינִים נֶגֶד יְסוֹד קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל לוֹמַר שֶׁגַּם בָּהֶם יֵשׁ פְּסֹלֶת וְשֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם חִיבּוּר לָעַמִּים

but it did not “succeed in their hand,” [for] he was [instead] sold to the “Midianites,” who “desire this” — to stir strife against the foundation of Israel’s holiness, to say that “in them, too, there is dross,” and that they have a “connection” to the nations.
וְעַל כֵּן הֵם חָזְרוּ וּמְכָרוּהוּ לְמִצְרַיִם ״עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ״, לוֹמַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ חִיבּוּר לִיסוֹד הָרַע גַּם כֵּן, כִּי הֵם נֶגֶד הַתְחָלַת הַהֶבְדֵּל שֶׁבֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים

And therefore they [the Midianites] in turn “sold him to Egypt,” “the nakedness of the land,” to say that he has a “connection” to the “foundation of evil” as well — for they [Egypt] are “opposite” the “beginning of the separation” between Israel and the nations.
וּבִהְיוֹת הַשְּׁבָטִים ״שִׁבְטֵי יָ-הּ״ וְ״תִקְרָתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם״ וַדַּאי אֵין מַחְשְׁבוֹתָם מַחְשְׁבוֹת הֶבֶל וּפְעוּלוֹתָם מִקְרִיִּים
And since the tribes are “the tribes of God” and “the ceiling of the world,” surely their thoughts are not “vain thoughts,” nor their deeds “haphazard”;
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל (ב״ר עד, יז) ״כְּשֶׁרָצִיתָ נָתַתָּ בְּלִבָּם לִשְׂנוֹא״

and all the more so, per what the Sages said (Bereishis Rabbah 84:17)839Bereishis Rabbah 84:18 (the base cites 84:17): “R’ Yehoshua ben Baisus in the name of R’ Yehuda bar Simon: it is written (Yeshayahu 63:17), ‘why do You make us stray, Hashem, from Your ways’ — when You willed, You placed in their hearts to love, and when You willed, You placed in their hearts to hate.” (So the brothers’ hatred of Yosef was, at root, directed from Above.), “when You willed, You placed [it] in their hearts to hate.”
כִּי הָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת עֲדַיִין דָּבָר זֶה צָרִיךְ לְבֵירוּרִים
For in truth this matter still required “clarifications”;
כִּי עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לֹא הָיָה עֲדַיִין בְּחִירָה גְּמוּרָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא נִתְבָּרֵר עֲדַיִין שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם פְּסֹלֶת
for until the Torah was given, there was not yet “complete chosenness” in Israel, and it was not yet clarified that there is no “dross” in them.

וְהַבֵּירוּר הָיָה הָעִיקָּר עַל יְדֵי הַבְדָּלָתָם מֵהָעַמִּים, וְהַתְחָלַת הַבֵּירוּר בָּזֶה הָיָה צָרִיךְ בְּיוֹסֵף שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ הַפְּרָטִית הַכְּלוּלָה בִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִדָּה זוֹ דְּהַגְדָּרָה מִבְּנוֹת הָאָרֶץ

And the “clarification” was essentially through their “separation from the nations”; and the beginning of it “needed to be” in Yosef, whose particular trait — [as] included in Knesses Yisrael — is precisely this: “boundedness-in” from the “daughters of the land.”
וְכַאֲשֶׁר נִתְבָּרֵר הוּא בָּזֶה בְּ״אֵשֶׁת פּוֹטִיפַר״, נִתְבָּרֵר דְּמַחְשְׁבוֹתָם לְרָעָה ״הָאֱלֹקִים חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטוֹבָה״

And when he was “clarified” in this, with the “wife of Potifar,” it was clarified that “their thoughts for evil, God intended for good” (Bereishis 50:20)840Bereishis 50:20: Yosef reassures his brothers after Yaakov’s death — “וְאַתֶּם חֲשַׁבְתֶּם עָלַי רָעָה, אֱלֹהִים חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטֹבָה, לְמַעַן עֲשֹׂה כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה לְהַחֲיֹת עַם רָב” — “and you intended evil against me, but God intended it for good, to bring about, as this day, the saving of many lives.” Meforshim: the Ramban — the brothers’ deed and the Divine plan coincided, each bearing its own reckoning, so that Yosef holds them accountable while affirming the good that came of it. R’ Tzadok’s use: once Yosef was “clarified” through the trial of Potifar’s wife, it emerged that “their thoughts for evil, God intended for good” — the sale that seemed to “connect” Yaakov’s seed to the nations in truth proved their utter separateness and holiness.Beis Yaakov — ‘God intended it for good’ is a retrospective clarification, not the brothers’ prospective license: Beis Yaakov on Torah, Vayeitzei 67:3, distinguishes two modes that are indispensable for reading ‘ואתם חשבתם עלי רעה, אלהים חשבה לטובה.’ Yaakov’s own middah is ‘לפני’: he seeks to see the will of Hashem within the act before doing it and refuses to rely on a later heavenly clarification that an outwardly troubling act will somehow be repaired. David’s line can reveal an ‘אחרי’ — a later clarification in which Hashem shows how even what was not consciously ordered can be brought into good. Yosef, whose countenance resembled Yaakov’s, therefore tells his brothers ‘התחת אלהים אני’: according to Yosef’s own path, the act as it appeared at the time was not something he could have chosen on the strength of a future tikkun; only afterward did Hashem reveal how their intention and the event were woven into life-saving good. This is a precise Izhbitz complement to R’ Tzadok’s account of the sale. Providence can take a deed born from error and make it the instrument of the Egyptian descent, Yosef’s test, and Israel’s clarification. But that retrospective Divine good does not collapse the distinction between good and evil at the moment of choice. The brothers remain accountable for what they thought, while Hashem remains sovereign over what their deed ultimately became. —

דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְבָּרֵר קְדֻשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב וְזַרְעוֹ, דְּגָרַם בָּזֶה לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לָהֶם מָזוֹן וְקִיּוּם הַחִיּוּת לִקְלוֹט מְעַט הַחִיּוּת שֶׁבְּמִצְרַיִם ״עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ״ נֶגֶד הַיְסוֹד דְּצַדִּיק

for through this the holiness of Yaakov and his seed was clarified, and he “caused” thereby to bestow upon them [Egypt] sustenance and “the maintenance of life” — to “absorb” the little vitality in Egypt, “the nakedness of the land,” [which stands] opposite the Yesod of “the tzaddik.”
וְעַד שֶׁלַּבַּסּוֹף עֲשָׂאוּהָ ״כִּמְצוּלָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דָּגִים״, אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְבָּרְרוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁנוֹת הַשִּׁיעְבּוּד שֶׁהָיוּ גְּדוּרִים בַּעֲרָיוֹת וּבְחִיבּוּר עִם מִצְרַיִם
