Until at last they “made it [Egypt] like a depth in which there are no fish841Berachos 9b: on “and Hashem gave the people favor in the eyes of Egypt” (Shemos 12:36), the Gemara teaches that at the Exodus Israel so emptied Egypt of its wealth that “they made it like a depth in which there are no fish [ki-metzulah she-ein bah dagim].” Meforshim: Rashi — they drained Egypt of its treasures so completely that nothing of worth remained, like a deep that has been fished out. R’ Tzadok’s use: this was the culmination of the “clarification” — after Israel were “fenced-in from immorality” through the years of servitude, they “extracted” the last vitality from Egypt, “the nakedness of the land,” leaving the husk empty, “a depth without fish,” and thereby “merited redemption.”” — after all Israel were “clarified” in the years of the servitude, being “fenced-in from immorality” and from joining with the Egyptians,
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לִגְאוּלָה
through which they merited redemption.
דְּרַק אַחַת הָיְתָה מִשִּׁבְטוֹ שֶׁל דָּן שֶׁפִּרְסְמָהּ הַכָּתוּב, דְּאוֹתוֹ שֵׁבֶט הָיָה עֲדַיִין צָרִיךְ לְבֵירוּרִים קְצָת עַד שִׁמְשׁוֹן
For only “one” [transgressor] was there — from the tribe of Dan [Shelomis bas Divri] — whom Scripture “publicized”; for that tribe still required some “clarification,” until Shimshon.
וְעַל כֵּן מַחְשֶׁבֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים הוּא שֶׁגָּרְמָה מְכִירַת יוֹסֵף וְהַצְרָכַת הַבֵּירוּרִים, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה גָּרְמוּ הַתְחָלַת הִתְעוֹרְרוּת שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל שֶׁהוּא בַּמְּדִינִים

And therefore the “thought of the tribes” is what caused the sale of Yosef and the “necessity of the clarifications,” and through this they caused the “beginning of the arousal” of the dominion of the “base man” — which is in the Midianites.
וְעַל כֵּן גָּרְמוּ גַּם כֵּן עוֹנֶשׁ בַּעֲשָׂרָה הֲרוּגֵי מַלְכוּת, שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בָּאָדָם לְרַע לוֹ, דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוֹצִיאוּ נִיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת הַרְבֵּה כַּנּוֹדָע

And therefore they also “caused” the punishment of the “Ten Martyrs [Asarah Harugei Malchus],” which was likewise “the dominion of man over man to his [own] detriment” — for through this “many holy sparks were extracted,” as is known.
וְכֵן הַתְחָלַת שְׁלִיטַת אָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל אַחַר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי בְּנוֹת מִדְיָן שֶׁהֵם הַתְחָלַת הָרַע
And likewise the “beginning” of the dominion of the “base man” after the Giving of the Torah was through the “daughters of Midyan,” who are the “beginning of evil”;
וְעַל כֵּן מִיתַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה הָיְתָה תְּלוּיָה בְּנִקְמַת הַמִּדְיָנִים, כִּי הוּא בְּסוֹד הַדַּעַת הַמְחַבֵּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה כַּנּוֹדָע

and therefore the “death of Moshe Rabbeinu” was “made dependent” on the vengeance of the Midianites842Bamidbar 31:2: God commands Moshe — “נְקֹם נִקְמַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאֵת הַמִּדְיָנִים, אַחַר תֵּאָסֵף אֶל עַמֶּיךָ” — “avenge the vengeance of the Children of Israel against the Midianites; afterward you shall be gathered to your people.” Meforshim: Rashi — although Moshe heard that his death was “bound up” with this act, he carried it out “with joy, without delay”; and it was Midyan, not Moav, that was punished, for they “stirred the strife” through their daughters. R’ Tzadok’s use: Moshe’s death hinged upon avenging Midyan because he is “in the secret of Daas,” which joins Chochmah and Binah — and Midyan, the “woman of strife,” assails precisely that inner union (Yesod Abba); hence the “beginning of the base man’s dominion” after Sinai came through “the daughters of Midyan,” the “beginning of evil.” — for he is in the secret of Daas, which “joins Chochmah and Binah,” as is known. — the brothers’ misjudgment set the whole machinery of exile and clarification in motion, so that even Yosef’s slavery served to prove, once and for all, that Yaakov’s seed has no true bond with the nations.

items.h: The theme: While Israel were in Egypt — a nation within a nation, like a fetus with no vitality of its own — Moshe had to be in Midyan, the husk surrounding Yesod Abba, drawing his vitality through Tzipporah. Yisro, the priest and head of Midyan, had already distanced himself from evil. He is the head of righteous converts; and Israel is exiled “to add converts,” the good extracted and the husk left empty.

p: [נ] וְעַל כֵּן כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲדַיִין בְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם
And therefore, all the while that Israel were still in the exile of Egypt —
וְאָמְרוּ ז״ל (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב קיד) עַל פָּסוּק ״גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי״ שֶׁהָיוּ בְּקִרְבָּם מַמָּשׁ, מוּקָּפִים מֵהֶם לְגַמְרֵי כְּעוּבָּר יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חִיּוּת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ

and the Sages said (Shocher Tov 114) on the verse “a nation from the midst of a nation” (Devarim 4:34) that they were literally “within them,” entirely surrounded by them, like a fetus in its mother’s womb, which has no vitality of its own843R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Soferim §20): “[In Egypt they were in] complete servitude — for ‘what a slave acquires, his master acquires’ — so that all the holiness of Israel was swallowed up within them; as the Midrash (Shocher Tov 107) expounds on the verse ‘a nation from within a nation’ [goy mikerev goy], that they were like a fetus in its mother’s womb — and ‘a fetus is reckoned as its mother’s thigh’ — such was the [dependent] force of Israel’s holiness within them.” (Exactly the se’if’s image: in Egypt Israel had ‘no vitality of its own,’ a fetus enclosed within the mother, its holiness wholly bound up in the husk until the time to ‘come out.’) —
הוּכְרַח הוּא לִהְיוֹת בְּמִדְיָן, שֶׁהִיא הַקְּלִיפָּה הַמַּקֶּפֶת יְסוֹד אַבָּא, שֶׁבּוֹ חִיבּוּר אַבָּא וְאִמָּא, שֶׁשָּׁם הִיא הַעֲלָמַת חִיבּוּר זֶה
he [Moshe] “had to be” in Midyan — the “husk” that surrounds Yesod Abba (in which is the “union of Abba and Ima”), where the concealment of this union takes place;
וּמִשָּׁם הָיָה חִיּוּתוֹ עַל יְדֵי צִפּוֹרָה שֶׁחָמְדָה בּוֹ כְּחֵשֶׁק בְּנוֹת מִדְיָן לִידָּבֵק בְּזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל

and from there was his vitality, through Tzipporah, who “desired him” — like the longing of the daughters of Midyan to cleave to the seed of Israel.844R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Sivan §4): “and Avraham our father fulfilled the whole Torah before it was given.” Exactly the se’if’s Yisro: the “priest and head” who is drawn near belongs to a world in which the name of Avraham still reaches — for a rung of Torah existed and was recognizable before Sinai, outside the camp.
וְיִתְרוֹ הוּא הַכֹּהֵן וְהָרֹאשׁ שֶׁבָּהֶם שֶׁבּוֹ עִיקַּר כֹּחַ הָאוּמָּה, אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּתְנַדָּה אָז מֵאֶצְלָם עוֹד טֶרֶם בָּא מֹשֶׁה אֵלָיו
And Yisro is the “priest and head” among them, in whom is the essential power of the nation — except that he had already been “ostracized” from them, even before Moshe came to him,
וּכְבָר נִתְרַחֵק מֵהָרַע אֶלָּא שֶׁעֲדַיִין לֹא נִתְקָרֵב אֶל הַטּוֹב

and had already “distanced himself from the evil,” except that he had not yet “drawn near to the good.”845R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §69): “what does [the soul] derive pleasure from? This is the scent — and therefore it is in the nose, for there is the dwelling of the neshamah, as it says, "the breath of life in his nostrils."” Exactly the se’if: while Israel in Egypt were “a fetus with no vitality of its own,” Moshe’s vitality had to come from outside through Tzipporah — the faintest channel, like scent, which is the soul’s own nourishment.
וְהוּא הָיָה בְּאוֹתָהּ עֵצָה דְּפַרְעֹה לְעַכֵּב יְצִיאַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעַם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָם אֶלָּא שֶׁבָּרַח

And he was among that “counsel of Pharaoh” — to prevent Israel’s going out as a nation of their own — except that “he fled.”846Shemos Rabbah 1:32: Yisro was a priest of idolatry who “saw there was no substance in it,” rejected it, and resolved to repent even before Moshe came. He told his townsmen, “until now I served you [as priest]; now I am old — choose another,” and handed over the idolatrous vessels. They ostracized him — that none should associate with him, work for him, or shepherd his flocks — “therefore he sent out his daughters to shepherd.” Sotah 11a: R’ Chiya bar Abba said in the name of R’ Simai: three were party to that counsel [of “let us deal wisely with them”] — Bilaam, Iyov, and Yisro. Bilaam, who advised it, was slain; Iyov, who kept silent, was sentenced to sufferings; and Yisro, who fled, merited that among his descendants were those who sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone [the Sanhedrin].
וְשָׁם ״אֵיתָן מוֹשָׁבוֹ״, רְצֹה לוֹמַר נִתְעוֹרֵר בּוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ הַקָּבוּעַ בּוֹ מִשׇּׁרְשׁוֹ שֶׁיָּצָא מֵ״אֵיתָן״ זֶה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ

And “his dwelling is eisan847Bamidbar 24:21: beholding the Keini (the descendants of Yisro), Bilaam lifts his parable — “אֵיתָן מוֹשָׁבֶךָ, וְשִׂים בַּסֶּלַע קִנֶּךָ” — “firm [eisan] is your dwelling-place, and set your nest in the rock.” Meforshim: Rashi — the “Keini” are the children of Yisro, and Bilaam marvels at their good fortune, that they came to be “set” so firmly among Israel (some seated in the Chamber of Hewn Stone); “eisan” bespeaks strength and permanence. R’ Tzadok’s use: “his dwelling is eisan” means that there was aroused in Yisro “the root fixed in him from his origin” — that he issued from “Eisan,” Avraham Avinu (Eisan ha-Ezrachi), “the father of all converts”; hence Yisro is the “head of the righteous converts.” [firm]” (Bamidbar 24:21) — meaning, there was aroused in him the “root fixed in him from his origin,” that he issued from this “Eisan” — Avraham Avinu,
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן אֲבִיהֶם שֶׁל כָּל הַגֵּרִים
who is also the “father of all converts.”
וְיִתְרוֹ הוּא הָיָה הָרֹאשׁ לְגֵרֵי הַצֶּדֶק, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִזַּרְעוֹ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין נִקְרָא זַרְעוֹ אֶלָּא יַעֲקֹב
And Yisro was the “head of the righteous converts,” for he too is of his [Avraham’s] seed — even though “only Yaakov is called his seed”;

זֶה נִתְבָּרֵר אַחַר שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם וְנִבְחֲרוּ לְעַם מְיוּחָד, אֲבָל בִּהְיוֹתָם בְּמִצְרַיִם כְּעוּבָּר בְּבֶטֶן אִמּוֹ הָיָה עֲדַיִין שֵׁם זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם עַל כָּל מִי שֶׁהָיָה מִזַּרְעוֹ

this was clarified [only] after they went out of Egypt and were chosen as a “distinct nation”; but while in Egypt, like a fetus in the womb, the name “seed of Avraham” still applied to all who were of his seed.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין זֶה בֶּאֱמֶת — הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ ״שְׂפַת אֱמֶת״ אֲשֶׁר ״תִּכּוֹן לָעַד״ — אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם מָקוֹם הָיָה לוֹ מְצִיאוּת גָּמוּר ״עַד אַרְגִּיעָה״
And although “this is not [ultimately] true” — that is, it is not “the lip of truth” that “endures forever” (Mishlei 12:19) — nonetheless it had a “complete existence” “for a moment” [ad argia],
שֶׁהֲרֵי הָיָה אָז מְצִיאוּת לְגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם, וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה מָקוֹם לְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת אוֹר בְּיִתְרוֹ מֵאַחַר שֶׁנִּתְרַחֵק מֵהֶם עוֹד קֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
for there was then a “reality” to the Egyptian exile, and therefore “room” for an arousal of light in Yisro — since he had distanced himself from them even before the Giving of the Torah.

וְעַל כֵּן הוּא רֹאשׁ הַגֵּרִים שֶׁבָּא מִכֹּחַ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם שֶׁהָיָה ״תְּחִלָּה לְגֵרִים״, אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא זָכָה לִהְיוֹת אַחַר כָּךְ אֶזְרָח בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָב לָאוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית, וְיִתְרוֹ נִשְׁאַר בְּמַדְרֵגַת תְּחִלָּה לְגֵרִים

And therefore he is the “head of converts,” coming from the power of Avraham, who was “the first of converts” — except that Avraham merited afterward to be “a native in Israel” and “father of the Israelite nation,” while Yisro remained at the level of “the first of converts.”
וְהָיָה יוֹשֵׁב בְּתוֹךְ עֲמָלֵק כַּמְפוֹרָשׁ בָּעִנְיַן שָׁאוּל

And he “dwelt within Amalek,” as is explicit in the account of Shaul848I Shmuel 15:6: before striking Amalek, Shaul warns the Keini — “לְכוּ סֻּרוּ רְדוּ מִתּוֹךְ עֲמָלֵקִי פֶּן אֹסִפְךָ עִמּוֹ, וְאַתָּה עָשִׂיתָה חֶסֶד עִם כָּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל” — “‘Go, depart, go down from among the Amalekite, lest I sweep you away with him’ — for you did kindness with all the Children of Israel.” Meforshim: Rashi — the “Keini” here are the descendants of Yisro, who “dwelt within Amalek”; Shaul spared them for the kindness Yisro had shown Moshe. R’ Tzadok’s use: Yisro, “the first of converts,” and Amalek, “the first of the nations,” are “adjacent in their rung” — the good and evil sides of the nations set side by side; so Yisro “dwelt within Amalek,” the good side waiting to be “extracted” and brought “beneath the wings of the Shechinah.”Mei HaShiloach — converts are still received because the cosmic birur is not yet complete: Mei HaShiloach I, Berachos 27b:3, reads the dispute over whether Ma’ariv is optional or obligatory through the unfinished work of galus. He notes that when an Ammonite convert came before the sages and was ruled eligible to enter the congregation, the very ruling demonstrated that ‘עדיין לא נגמר הבירור’ — the clarification is not yet complete. In the days of Mashiach converts will no longer be accepted, whereas now they are accepted because ‘עדיין יש ניצוצות קדושה הצריכים להתלקט,’ holy sparks still remain to be gathered. This is an exact Izhbitz parallel to R’ Tzadok’s explanation of Yisro as ‘ראשית גרים’ and of exile as the setting in which the good side of the nations can be extracted and brought beneath the wings of the Shechinah. Yisro’s adjacency to Amalek is therefore not accidental symbolism. So long as the birur is unfinished, good and evil can stand in unnerving proximity; the task is to separate them without confusing them. Yisro leaves the counsel of Pharaoh, leaves Midyan’s idolatrous priesthood, and ultimately comes to Torah. The very possibility of such movement testifies that the nations are not yet a closed, final category. Galus persists while sparks remain outside; geulah corresponds to the completion of that gathering, when the lines are finally clarified and no further conversion is needed. [warning the Keinites to depart from among Amalek].

כִּי סְמוּכִים בְּמַדְרֵגָתָם: זֶה ״רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם״, וְזֶה ״רֵאשִׁית גֵּרִים״ צַד הַטּוֹב שֶׁבַּגּוֹיִם כַּאֲשֶׁר יִזְכּוּ לָצֵאת וּלְהִתְבָּרֵר לָצֵאת מֵהֶם וּלְהַכְנִיסָם תַּחַת כַּנְפֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה

For they are “adjacent” in their rung: this one [Amalek] is “the first of the nations,” and that one [Yisro] is “the first of converts” — the “good side” of the nations, when they merit to “come out” and be clarified, to come out from them and be brought “beneath the wings of the Shechinah.”
כִּי הַתְחָלַת הַתּוֹרָה וְהָאוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית הוּא יוֹצֵא מִיסוֹד אַבָּא, עַל דֶּרֶךְ ״יִשְׂרָאֵל עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה״, וְכָל יְצִיאָה לְפוֹעַל הוּא דֶּרֶךְ הַיְסוֹד כַּנּוֹדָע

For the “beginning” of the Torah and the Israelite nation issues from Yesod Abba, along the lines of “Israel arose in [His] thought,” and every “emergence into actuality” is by way of the Yesod, as is known.
וּמִשָּׁם גַּם כֵּן לְעוּמַּת זֶה הַתְחָלַת הָרַע, וּכְשֶׁהַטּוֹב מִתְבָּרֵר הוּא קוֹלֵט עִמּוֹ גַּם מִן הָרַע מַה שֶּׁאֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת נִקְלָט מִמֶּנּוּ וּלְהִתְחַבֵּר אֶל הַטּוֹב

And from there, too, “over against it,” is the “beginning of evil”; and when the good is clarified, it “absorbs with itself” also of the evil — whatever can be absorbed from it and joined to the good.
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא (פְּסָחִים פז:) ״לֹא גָּלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶלָּא לְהוֹסִיף עֲלֵיהֶם גֵּרִים״
As it is stated (Pesachim 87b), “Israel were exiled only in order to add converts to them,”
כִּי זֶה כָּל צוֹרֶךְ הַגָּלֻיּוֹת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בָּאָדָם לְרַע לוֹ, שֶׁבְּצֵאתוֹ יוֹצִיא עִמּוֹ כָּל נִיצוֹץ טוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ וְיַשְׁאִירוּ ״כִּמְצוּלָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דָּגִים״

for this is the whole “need of the exiles” — that there be “the dominion of man over man to his [own] detriment,” so that in [Israel’s] going out, one “takes out with him” every good spark in it, and leaves it “like a depth in which there are no fish.” — exile is thus a kind of mining: Israel descends among the nations only to draw out the buried sparks, and departs leaving the husk emptied of all worth keeping.

items.h: The theme: Through his Midyan exile Moshe absorbed Yisro — the power set against Yesod Abba, which resists Israel’s becoming one nation, and which Sinai turned into the nations’ hatred. Yet since the nations too are His creatures, that power has a good side: the converts. Yisro, feeling himself elevated, still recognized that it was nothing without joining Israel — and so became the first convert.

p: [נא] וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה עַל יְדֵי גָּלוּתוֹ בְּמִדְיָן קָלַט עִמּוֹ אֶת יִתְרוֹ שֶׁהוּא מִכֹּחַ הַפְּסֹלֶת שֶׁנֶּגֶד יְסוֹד אַבָּא
And Moshe Rabbeinu, through his “exile in Midyan,” “absorbed with him” Yisro — who is from the power of the “dross” that is opposite Yesod Abba,
שֶׁאֵין מַנִּיחַ לָצֵאת לְפוֹעַל מַה שֶּׁבְּמַחְשַׁבְתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹי אֶחָד וְלִיתֵּן לָהֶם תּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת שֶׁהוּא הַמְחַבֶּרְתָּם יַחַד
[the power] that “does not permit to come into actuality” what is in His “thought” — to make Israel “one nation” and to give them Torah and mitzvos, which “join them together”;
וְהֵם חֲפֵצִים לְעוֹרֵר מְדִינִים וְלִמְנוֹעַ חִיבּוּר זֶה, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה יְרִידָה חוּרְבָּה וְשִׂנְאָה לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּפֶרֶק אַרְבַּע מִיתוֹת] (שַׁבָּת פט.)

and they “desire to stir strife” and to prevent this “joining” — for through it [Sinai] “descended destruction and hatred to the nations of the world,” as they said (Shabbos 89a)849Shabbos 89a–b: “What is ‘Har Sinai’? The mountain upon which hatred [sinah] descended to the nations of the world” (for their refusal of the Torah). (The base cites Shabbos 89a.).
וּלְפִי שֶׁהָאוּמּוֹת גַּם כֵּן בְּרִיּוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ, עַל כֵּן יֵשׁ בְּאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ גַּם כֵּן צַד מָה הַטּוֹב שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הַגֵּרִים בְּאוֹתָהּ אוּמָּה הַנִּקְלָטִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
And since the nations, too, are His creatures, there is in that very “power” also “some good side” — from which come the “converts” in that nation, who are “absorbed into Israel.”

וְהַטּוֹב שֶׁבְּמִדְיָן, שֶׁהוּא הַכֹּחַ שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִהְיוֹת פֵּירוּד וּמְדָנִים וְלֹא חִיבּוּר וְגוֹי אֶחָד מְיוּחָד לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם, קָלַט מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה לְעוֹרֵר מְדָנִים בֵּין הָאוּמּוֹת לְאָבִינוּ שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם

And the “good of Midyan” — the power that “wishes for separation and strife,” not “joining” as “one nation dedicated to their Father in Heaven” — Moshe “absorbed,” [turning it] to “stir strife between the nations and our Father in Heaven”;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ז.) בִּיקֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא תִשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָה עַל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, וְהוֹרִיד חוּרְבָּה וְשִׂנְאָה לָהֶם

as they said (Berachos 7a)850Berachos 7a: “R’ Yochanan said in the name of R’ Yosei: Three things Moshe requested of the Holy One, blessed be He, and they were granted him — he requested that the Shechinah rest upon Israel [and not upon the nations of the world], and it was granted him.”, [Moshe] “requested that the Shechinah not rest upon the nations of the world,” and “brought down destruction and hatred” upon them,851R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §48): “The Sages said (Shabbos 89b) that it is called ‘Har Sinai’ because ‘hatred [sinah] descended upon the nations of the world’ through it — by the trait of Nitzachon (contention/triumph), which is the rung of Moshe Rabbeinu, ‘whose face was like the face of the sun’ (Bava Basra 75a).” (This is the very power the se’if traces through Moshe’s Midyan exile: Sinai — the Torah that makes Israel ‘one nation’ — of itself ‘brings down hatred’ upon the nations, the force opposed to their being drawn in.)
וְשֶׁאֲפִילּוּ יִרְצֶה גּוֹי לְהֵטִיב מַעֲשָׂיו לְגַמְרֵי לֹא יוּכַל כְּלָל
and that “even if a gentile should wish to perfect his deeds entirely, he could not at all” —
דַּאֲפִילּוּ חֲסִידֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת שֶׁמֶץ וָאֶפֶס וְקָצֵהוּ לִקְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יִתְגַּיְּירוּ וּבְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְתַכַּנּוּ
for even the “pious of the nations” have no connection — “not a trace or an iota or an edge” — to the holiness of Israel, unless they convert and “are called by the name Israel”;
וְזֶהוּ הַטּוֹב שֶׁבְּכֹחַ מְדָנִים זֶה, לְעוֹרְרוֹ נֶגֶד אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם

and this is the “good” within this “power of strife” — to arouse it “against the nations.”852R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas Shabbos §6): “and at the Giving of the Torah, when their filth ceased, they merited the first affection, from "the kisses of His mouth" — in the two utterances that were in public, as it says at the end of Zevachim, that the nations too sensed something [of it].” Exactly the se’if: Sinai both made Israel “one nation” and was felt by the nations — which is precisely why it “brought hatred to the nations,” and why that power had to be absorbed.

וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְעוֹרֵר יִתְרוֹ וּבָא לַמִּדְבָּר, שֶׁנִּתְעוֹרֵר בּוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ כֹּחַ דְּמִדְיָן מִצַּד הַבְּרִיאָה, שֶׁהוּא הָרִיחוּק הַגָּמוּר לְכָל מִינֵי כֹּחוֹת דְּאוּמּוֹת שֶׁהֵם כֹּחוֹת גּוּפָנִים דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לִקְדֻשָּׁה כְּלָל

And through this Yisro was aroused and came to the Wilderness — for there was aroused in him the “root of the power of Midyan from the side of Creation,” which is the “complete distancing” [directed] against all “national powers,” which are “bodily powers of this world” having no connection to holiness.853R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Shemos §1): “he mentions there the names of the tribes on account of their allusion to the redemption, which is the purpose of the exile — and all of it a preparation for the Giving of the Torah; and as in Berachos, that three gifts [come] through sufferings.” The se’if’s Midyan exile exactly: the sojourn among the nations is not an interruption of Moshe’s mission but its preparation — the exile is how the gift is acquired.Izhbitz parallel - Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Yitro 3; Yitro 2: The Ishbitzer gives a particularly close explanation of the same 'good power' that can be extracted from Yisro's Midyanite root. On the Midrash's contrast, 'strike the scoffer' - Amalek, but 'the simple one will become wise' - Yisro, he explains that both traits begin as deficiencies: the leitz mocks every truth, whereas the peti is open to every influence. Yet the latter defect can itself be redirected, because one who is open can eventually receive the truth and repair the root of his deficiency. Yisro therefore moves from having experimented with avodah zarah to 'atah yadati ki gadol Hashem' and conversion. In a second teaching the Ishbitzer says that even Yisro's first 'hearing' was sent to him by Hashem; nevertheless, because Yisro recognized that 'la-Hashem ha'aretz u-melo'ah' and yearned to cleave to Israel, Heaven credited the hearing to him as though it had begun from his own initiative. This closely complements R' Tzadok here: the power of Midyan is not redeemed by blurring the distinction between Israel and the nations. Its good is extracted precisely when the outsider recognizes the distinction and converts the very power of separation into a movement toward joining Israel.

וּמַה שֶּׁהֵם חָשְׁבוּ שֶׁבְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל, אַדְּרַבָּא עַל יָדָם הוּא עִיקַּר בֵּירוּר הַהֶבְדֵּל וְהָרִיחוּק בֵּינֵיהֶם, וְשֶׁאֵין לְשׁוּם אוּמָּה וְלָשׁוֹן אֶפְשָׁרוּת לִידָּבֵק בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּלָל אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יִתְגַּיְּירוּ

And what they thought — that “the house of Israel is like all the nations” — on the contrary, through them [the converts] is the essential “clarification of the distinction,” that no nation or tongue can cleave to Hashem at all, unless they convert.
וְעַל כֵּן הוּכְרַח לַעֲזוֹב מִשְׁכָּנוֹ בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, רְצֹה לוֹמַר שֶׁהָיָה בְּעֵינֵי עַצְמוֹ כְּבָר בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת מִתְרוֹמֵם מִכָּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And therefore he “had to leave his dwelling in the height of the world” — meaning, in his own eyes he was already “at the ultimate of perfection,” “elevated” above all matters of this world;
דְּעַל כֵּן נִידּוּהוּ וְרִיחֲקוּהוּ בְּנֵי מִדְיָן דְּהָיָה מְרוּחָק מֵהֶם
which is why the Midianites “ostracized and distanced” him — for he was [already] distant from them;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הִשִּׂיג כִּי עֲדַיִין אֵין זֶה כְּלוּם אִם לֹא יֵלֵךְ לְהִתְחַבֵּר עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל דַּוְקָא כְּדֵי לְהַשִּׂיג מִקְּדֻשָּׁתָם שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי

nonetheless he “attained” [the recognition] that this is still “nothing” if he does not “go to join specifically with Israel,” to “attain of their holiness” — which “He did not do so for any [other] nation.”
וְזֶהוּ כֹּחַ הַטּוֹב שֶׁבְּמִדְיָן לְהַכִּיר רִיחוּק הָאוּמּוֹת וְשֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהִתְגַּיֵּיר
And this is the “good power” of Midyan: to “recognize the distancing of the nations,” and that “one must convert.”
אִם כֵּן הוּא הַגֵּר הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה וְשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קֵרְבוֹ, כִּי בּוֹ בְּכֹחוֹ שֶׁבְּתוֹלַדְתּוֹ הוּא הַתְחָלַת עִנְיַן הַגֵּרוּת
If so, he is “the first convert at the Giving of the Torah,” whom Hashem “drew near” — for in him, in the power of his very “nature,” is the “beginning of the matter of conversion.”
רַק שֶׁבְּכֹחַ הָרַע רוֹצִים לְדַמּוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל לָהֶם, וּבְכֹחַ הַטּוֹב הוּא שֶׁיַּכִּירוּ רִיחוּקָם וְיֵירָצוּ לִיכָּלֵל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
Only that in the “power of evil,” they wish to “liken Israel to themselves”; whereas in the “power of good,” they “recognize their distance” and “wish to be included in Israel.”

וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַיְסוֹד וְהִתְקַשְּׁרוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם בְּקֶשֶׁר אַמִּיץ דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין לְעָלְמִין, נִתְגַּדֵּל בְּמִדְיָן לְבַטֵּל הַקְּלִיפָּה הַסּוֹבֶבֶת לְהַעֲלִים וּלְהִתְנַגֵּד קֶשֶׁר זֶה

And Moshe Rabbeinu — root of the Yesod, the “bonding of Israel to their Father” in a “firm bond that never parts” — was “raised in Midyan” to nullify the “husk that surrounds,” to conceal and oppose this bond;
וְהוּא הִתְאַמֵּץ נֶגֶד זֶה לִהְיוֹת ״חַרְבָּם תָּבוֹא בְלִבָּם״ וּלְרַע לוֹ

and he “prevailed against it,” so that “their sword shall enter their own heart854Tehillim 37:15: of the wicked who plot against the righteous — “חַרְבָּם תָּבוֹא בְלִבָּם, וְקַשְּׁתוֹתָם תִּשָּׁבַרְנָה” — “their sword shall enter their own heart, and their bows shall be broken.” Background: David’s psalm, in which the schemes the wicked draw against the just recoil upon themselves. Meforshim: Rashi and the Radak — the very weapon the wicked unsheathe to harm the righteous turns back and pierces their own heart, their bows shattered. R’ Tzadok’s use: Moshe, root of the Yesod and of Israel’s unbreakable bond to their Father, “prevailed against” the surrounding husk of Midyan — turning its own power of strife back upon it, “their sword shall enter their own heart,” so that “all their dominion is to their own detriment.”” (Tehillim 37:15) — “to its own detriment.” — the very power of “separation” that Midyan wields to divide Israel from God, Moshe reclaims and turns outward, to seal off the nations instead and gather in only their converts.

items.h: The theme: Through this Moshe accepted the erev rav — converts who wished to leave the nations for Israel, whom Hashem called “your people.” Yet they made the Calf, not desiring a future in which Hashem alone guides and there are no converts at all. Converts are “hard for Israel as a sapachas,” clinging like a lesion and briefly distancing the Shechinah — which is just what Moshe’s first sign, the hand made leprous and then restored, was showing him.

p: [נב] וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְעוֹרֵר שֹׁרֶשׁ הַגֵּרִים, וְלָכֵן קִיבֵּל הָעֵרֶב רַב שֶׁהֵם הַגֵּרִים מֵאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁרָצוּ לְהִתְרַחֵק מֵהָאוּמּוֹת וּלְהִתְחַבֵּר עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל

And through this the “root of converts” was aroused, and therefore [Moshe] “accepted the erev rav” — who are the “converts from the nations” who wished “to distance themselves from the nations and to join with Israel.”855R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach §2): “but the wisdom of Israel is Torah in its essence — which instructs and teaches his heart the way he should go,” unlike a wisdom that does not instruct or teach the heart. Exactly the se’if’s distinction: those who “separate themselves from the nations and join with Israel” receive the outward attachment, but what is at issue is whether the Torah reaches and teaches the heart.
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קְרָאָם ״עַמְּךָ״, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אֵינָם בִּכְלַל עַם ה׳

And Hashem called them “your people” [Moshe’s, Shemos 32:7] — for in truth they are “not included in the people of Hashem.”856R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Tazria §11): “as it says in the Mechilta, that one who guards Shabbos is assured that he is guarded from transgression; and this is as it says, "in your mouth and in your heart to do it" — and we said that it does not say "and in your deeds," for the completion of the deed is from Hashem, and Hashem wants from a person [the mouth and the heart].” Exactly the se’if: what Hashem asks is mouth and heart, and it is precisely there that the erev rav remained outside — their joining reached the deed but not the heart.
רַק כֹּחַ זֶה שֶׁל קִיבּוּל גֵּרִים קָלַט מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה מִמִּדְיָן עַל יְדֵי בַּת יִתְרוֹ, וְהוּא רַק כֹּחַ טוֹב שֶׁבָּאוּמּוֹת
Only that this “power of accepting converts,” Moshe “absorbed from Midyan” through the daughter of Yisro — and it is only “the good power within the nations.”
וְהֵם שֶׁעָשׂוּ הָעֵגֶל שֶׁאֵינָם חֲפֵצִים בַּשְּׁלֵימוּת הַגָּמוּר כְּלֶעָתִיד, דְּאָז ״ה׳ בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ״ וְלֹא יִהְיֶה גֵּרִים כְּלָל
And they are the ones who “made the calf” — for they “do not desire the complete perfection” as in the Future, when “Hashem alone will guide him” and “there will be no converts at all.”
וְעִיקַּר הִתְעוֹרְרוּת מְדִינִים דְּמִדְיָן שֶׁבַּבְּרִיאָה הוּא נֶגֶד הַגֵּרִים, דְּהַשָּׂגַת הָאוּמּוֹת הוּא רַק בָּהֶם וְהֵם יֵשׁ לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת עֲדַיִין עִמָּהֶם

And the essential “arousal of strife” of “Midyan of Creation” is “against the converts” — for “the attainment of the nations” is only in them, and they [converts] “still have a connection with them” [the nations],
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין צד.) ״גִּיּוֹרָא עַד עֲשָׂרָה דָּרֵי לָא תְבַזֵּי [אֲרַמָּאָה]״ כו׳, כִּי אֵין לָהֶם דְּבֵקוּת גָּמוּר בֵּאלֹקִים חַיִּים

as they said (Sanhedrin 94a)857Sanhedrin 94a: “Rav said: This is what people say [as a proverb]: ‘Before a convert, up to ten generations, do not disparage a gentile in his presence [giyora ad asara dari la tivzeh armai kameih].’” (Said of Yisro, who “winced” [va-yichad] at the downfall of Egypt, from whom he descended — a convert retains a bond to his origins for [ten] generations.), “before a convert, up to ten generations, do not disparage [an Aramean]” — for they do not have “complete cleaving” to the living God;
וְעַל כֵּן הֵם גַּם כֵּן חֲפֵצִים לְעוֹרֵר מְדָנִים וּלְבַטֵּל הַדְּבֵקוּת הַגָּמוּר מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
and therefore they too “desire to stir strife” and “to nullify the complete cleaving” of Israel.
וּשְׁלֵימוּתָם הוּא רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר יִרְצוּ לְהִתְדַּבֵּק בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְגַמְרֵי, וְאָז קָשִׁים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּסַפַּחַת שֶׁהוּא נֶגַע הַדְּבוּקָה בְּעוֹר הַבָּשָׂר

And their “perfection” is only when they “wish to cleave to Israel entirely”; and then “they are hard for Israel as a sapachas” (Yevamos 47b)858Yevamos 47b: “R’ Chelbo said: Converts are as hard for Israel as a sapachas [a skin-affliction/scab] [kashim gerim l’Yisrael k’sapachas].”Izhbitz parallel - Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Berakhot 27b:3; cf. Tiferet Shlomo, Purim 99: The Ishbitzer's reading of the dispute over Ma'ariv gives a conceptual background to R' Tzadok's treatment of gerim and the erev rav. He explains that before the final birur, when the world is not yet completely clarified, converts are still accepted because 'there are still holy sparks that must be gathered'; only in the Messianic future, when the clarification is complete, will converts no longer be accepted. Thus gerus itself belongs to an unfinished world in which holiness remains intermingled outside Israel and must still be drawn home. Tiferet Shlomo develops the same language of nitzotzos but adds an important caution: when holy sparks emerge from the nations, their surrounding admixture can also accompany them, and Israel must guard itself so that the alien element is not absorbed together with the holy spark. That balance fits the present se'if with unusual precision. Moshe's acceptance of the erev rav was not a mistake in recognizing that something holy sought attachment to Israel; the danger lay in the incompleteness of the birur, so that attachment to Israel could coexist with a residue that later sought the Golden Calf. R' Tzadok's 'sapachas' image therefore describes not gerus itself, God forbid, but the danger of an incompletely clarified attachment that clings externally before the inner root has been fully transformed. — a lesion “clinging to the skin of the flesh.”
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה חוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה מוֹשָׁבוֹ, כִּי גּוֹרְמִים לְרִיחוּק שְׁכִינָה דְּאֵינָהּ שׁוֹרָה אֶלָּא עַל מִשְׁפָּחוֹת הַמְיוּחָסוֹת, וּמְבַטְּלִים גַּם כֵּן הַדְּבֵיקוּת הַגָּמוּר

And therefore “his dwelling is outside the camp” [as with the metzora] — for they “cause a distancing of the Shechinah,” which “rests only upon well-lineaged families,” and they “nullify” also the “complete cleaving”;
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא רַק לְשָׁעָה דְּמִיָּד נִרְפָּא הַנֶּגַע
except that this is “only temporary,” for “the lesion is immediately healed.”
וְזֶה הָיָה אוֹת רִאשׁוֹן דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה בְּנִגְעֵי יָדוֹ וְשָׁבָה כִּבְשָׂרוֹ

And this was the “first sign” of Moshe Rabbeinu — the “leprosy of his hand,” and “it returned like his [own] flesh” (Shemos 4:7)859Shemos 4:6–7: Moshe’s first sign — “וַיּוֹצִאָהּ וְהִנֵּה יָדוֹ מְצֹרַעַת כַּשָּׁלֶג… הָשֵׁב יָדְךָ אֶל חֵיקֶךָ… וְהִנֵּה שָׁבָה כִּבְשָׂרוֹ” — “he brought out his hand, and behold, it was leprous as snow… [then] ‘return your hand to your bosom’… and behold, it had returned like his [own] flesh.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Sages read the leprous hand as a rebuke — Moshe was stricken with tzara’as, the affliction of the slanderer (for having “slandered” Israel by doubting their faith), and its healing bespoke forgiveness. R’ Tzadok’s use: the sign was shown “in his hand” — “that which accepts the converts,” for “acceptance is attributed to the hand”; the hand made leprous and then “returned like his flesh” taught that the converts, like a passing lesion, “harm Israel only for a moment” and leave no lasting wound — “and therefore he did not worry, and accepted them.”;
וְעַל יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁאָמַר ״הֵן לֹא יַאֲמִינוּ לִי״, שֶׁחָשַׁד חִסָּרוֹן אֱמוּנָה בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגַם הוּא בִּכְלַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל

[given] through his saying “behold, they will not believe me” (Shemos 4:1)860Shemos 4:1 (and Shabbos 97a): Moshe demurred — “וְהֵן לֹא יַאֲמִינוּ לִי, וְלֹא יִשְׁמְעוּ בְּקֹלִי” — “but behold, they will not believe me, nor heed my voice.” Meforshim: Reish Lakish (Shabbos 97a) — “one who suspects the worthy is smitten in his body,” for God had already attested that Israel are “believers, children of believers”; Moshe, doubting their faith, was answered, “they will believe… but you, in the end, will not believe” — and forthwith his hand turned “leprous as snow.” R’ Tzadok’s use: Moshe’s very suspicion of a “lack of faith” in Israel arose “from the husk of Midyan,” from which he had not yet fully parted — the husk whose way is precisely to suspect Israel — and from this came, too, his thought that “the converts have a connection with the Children of Israel.”, for he “suspected a lack of faith in the Children of Israel” — and he too is “included among the Children of Israel”;
וּלְפִי שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ חִסָּרוֹן אֱמוּנָה בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם מַאֲמִינִים גָּרַם לְחָשְׁדָם בְּחִסָּרוֹן אֱמוּנָה בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and since there was in him a “lack of faith” [in the fact] that the Children of Israel are “believers,” it “caused” him to suspect them of a “lack of faith in Hashem.”
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַקְּלִיפָּה דְּמִדְיָן, שֶׁעֲדַיִין לֹא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ אָז מִמֶּנָּה לְגַמְרֵי, שֶׁהֵם הַחוֹשְׁדִים כֵּן לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
And this is “from the side of the husk of Midyan” — from which he had not yet fully “parted” then — for they are the ones who “so suspect the Children of Israel”;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה חָשַׁב גַּם כֵּן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לַגֵּרִים חִיבּוּר עִם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
and through this he “also thought” that “the converts have a connection with the Children of Israel.”
וְעַל כֵּן הֶרְאָה לוֹ הַנְּגָעִים בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁהִיא הַמְקַבֶּלֶת הַגֵּרִים, וּבְכָל מָקוֹם הַקִּיבּוּל מְיוּחָס לַיָּד, וּכְמוֹ ״אַתָּה נוֹתֵן יָד לְפוֹשְׁעִים״

And therefore He “showed him the lesions in his hand” — which is “that which accepts the converts”; and everywhere “acceptance is attributed to the hand,” as in “You extend a hand to transgressors” [to accept their repentance].
וְהֶרְאָה לוֹ אַחַר כָּךְ שָׁבָה לִבְשָׂרוֹ, דְּבַסּוֹף לֹא יַזִּיק כְּלוּם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְכָל מַה שֶּׁקִּלְקְלוּ הַגֵּרִים הָיָה רַק לְשָׁעָה, וְעַל כֵּן לֹא חָשׁ וְקִבְּלָם

And He “showed him afterward” that “it returned to his flesh” — that “in the end it will do no harm at all to Israel,” and that “all the damage the converts caused was only temporary” — and therefore he “did not worry, and accepted them.” — the leprous-then-healed hand was the sign itself: converts, like a passing lesion, cling and unsettle for a moment, but leave no lasting wound in Israel.

items.h: The theme: Yisro came drawn by Hashem for the sake of a “good spark,” which is the whole purpose of the husk. “You shall be our eyes”: the Sanhedrin are the eyes of the congregation, and Yisro’s descendants sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone. Moshe had not wanted to appoint a Sanhedrin at all — he wished to illumine every Jew’s own eyes — but that inner light is Israel’s alone, so the appointing of judges entered the Torah through a convert.

p: [נג] וְיִתְרוֹ בָּא מֵעַצְמוֹ מֵהִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁקֵּירְבוֹ
And Yisro “came of his own accord,” from an “arousal of Hashem,” who “drew him near”;

כִּי כְּמוֹ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה בָּאוּמּוֹת שֶׁהֲרֵי יֶשְׁנָם בָּעוֹלָם מִפְּנֵי אֵיזֶה נִיצוֹץ טוֹב שֶׁבָּהֶם, כָּל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁרָצָה בַּגֵּרִים מִפְּנֵי אֵיזֶה נִיצוֹץ טוֹב שֶׁבָּהֶם וְהוּא יִתְרוֹ

for just as Hashem “willed the nations” [to exist] — since they exist on account of “some good spark” in them — all the more did He “will the converts,” on account of some good spark in them, which is Yisro.861R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §10): “this world is good mixed with evil and evil with good, and there is no oneness in it — rather every thing is compounded of two opposites; and therefore [a thing] entirely turned white is pure.” Exactly the se’if’s “good spark”: in a world where nothing is unmixed, the husk exists for the sake of the good held inside it, and Yisro is the case in which that good is drawn out and absorbed.
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה קְלִיפָּה הַסּוֹבֶבֶת לַפְּרִי, וְתַכְלִית הַקְּלִיפָּה מִפְּנֵי אֵיזֶה טוֹב הַנִּקְלָט מֵהֶם לִקְדֻשָּׁה
For Hashem willed that there be in this world “a husk surrounding the fruit,” and the “purpose of the husk” is on account of “some good absorbed from them into holiness”;
הֲרֵי יֵשׁ בָּהֶם אֵיזֶה דָּבָר טוֹב הַנִּטְפָּל לִקְדֻשָּׁה, וְזֶהוּ נֶפֶשׁ הַגֵּר שֶׁרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּקְּלִיפָּה שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ יִהְיֶה הַעֲלָמַת הַפְּרִי
so there is in them some good thing “attached to holiness” — and this is the “soul of the convert,” [for whom] Hashem “willed the husk,” through which comes the “concealment of the fruit.”
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לְיִתְרוֹ ״וְהָיִיתָ לָּנוּ לְעֵינָיִם״, כִּי הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין נִקְרְאוּ ״עֵינֵי הָעֵדָה״

And this is what [Moshe] said to Yisro, “and you shall be for us as eyes” (Bamidbar 10:31)862Bamidbar 10:31: Moshe urges Chovav (Yisro) to remain — “אַל נָא תַּעֲזֹב אֹתָנוּ… וְהָיִיתָ לָּנוּ לְעֵינָיִם” — “please do not leave us… and you shall be for us as eyes.” Meforshim: Rashi offers two readings — “you shall be as beloved to us as our own eyes,” and “you shall enlighten our eyes”; the Sifrei — “whatever is hidden from our eyes, you shall illumine for us.” R’ Tzadok’s use: “the Sanhedrin are called ‘the eyes of the congregation’” — those who supervise the people; from Yisro’s seed came heads of Sanhedrins seated in the Chamber of Hewn Stone, and it was fitting that he “be for us as eyes,” for the convert’s sight is a light received from without. — for the Sanhedrin are called “the eyes of the congregation”;863R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Soferim §10): “So it is with the Sages of Israel, who are called ‘the heads of the generation’ and ‘the eyes of the congregation’ (Bava Basra 4a); and this is what they said (Bava Metzia 96b) [regarding] the ‘representative of David’ of the Israel of that generation — for all the ordinances of law depend upon them, and through them the enactments set in order for the community take effect, as though [the community itself] had enacted them.” (This is the se’if’s ‘you shall be our eyes’: the Sanhedrin are the ‘eyes of the congregation,’ the seeing faculty of all Israel — the role for which Yisro’s counsel fitted the judges.)
וְכֵן אִיתָא [בְּב״ר סג] עַל פָּסוּק ״עַם יְפֵה עֵינַיִם״ מִדַּעַת סַנְהֶדְרִין, וּמִזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל יִתְרוֹ יָשְׁבוּ בְּלִשְׁכַּת הַגָּזִית וְהָיוּ רָאשֵׁי סַנְהֶדְרָאוֹת

and so it is stated [in Bereishis Rabbah 63], on the verse “a people fair of eyes” [read as] “from the counsel of the Sanhedrin”; and from the seed of Yisro “sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone” and were “heads of Sanhedrins.”864R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah §15): “and in the deeds of the Chashmonaim, in the decree of Greece, of whom it was expounded "and darkness" — that they darkened the eyes of Israel — meaning that they sought to nullify from them the light of the Oral Torah.” Exactly the se’if’s “you shall be our eyes”: Israel’s “eyes” are the Sanhedrin and the Oral Torah they carry, and to darken those eyes is the standing aim of the outside power.
וְגַם הוּא ״יִיתֵּר״ פָּרָשָׁה אַחַת בַּתּוֹרָה וְהוּא פָּרָשַׁת סַנְהֶדְרִין וְהַמְנָאַת שׁוֹפְטִים
And he too “added [yiter]” one “portion” to the Torah — the “portion of the Sanhedrin” and the “appointing of judges.”
כִּי הָעַיִן מוֹרֶה בְּכָל מָקוֹם עַל הַהַשְׁגָּחָה וְשִׂימַת לֵב עַל הַדָּבָר, כְּמוֹ ״וְאָשִׂימָה עֵינִי עָלָיו״, ״עֵינֵי ה׳ אֶל צַדִּיקִים״ וְכַדּוֹמֶה

For the “eye” everywhere indicates “supervision” and “attention,” as in “and I will set my eye upon him” (Bereishis 44:21)865Bereishis 44:21; Tehillim 34:16: “וְאָשִׂימָה עֵינִי עָלָיו” — “that I may set my eye upon him” (Yosef, of Binyamin), and “עֵינֵי ה׳ אֶל צַדִּיקִים” — “the eyes of Hashem are toward the righteous.” Background: two of the verses in which “eye” connotes not mere sight but watchful care. Meforshim: Rashi (on Bereishis 44:21) — “I will set My eye upon him for good”; the “eye” bespeaks attentive supervision (hashgachah). R’ Tzadok’s use: “the eye everywhere indicates supervision and the setting of the heart upon a matter” — and so the Sanhedrin, the “eyes of the congregation,” are “those who supervise” every affair of Israel, as in the eglah arufah: “our hands did not shed it” — that we did not see him and let him go., “the eyes of Hashem are toward the righteous” (Tehillim 34:16), and the like.

וְהַסַּנְהֶדְרִין הֵם הַמַּשְׁגִּיחִים עַל הָעֵדָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״יָדֵינוּ לֹא שָׁפְכוּ״ וְגוֹמֵר, שֶׁלֹּא רְאִינוּהוּ וְהִנַּחְנוּהוּ כו׳ (סוֹטָה מה:), כִּי עַל הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין לְהַשְׁגִּיחַ בְּכָל דָּבָר

And the Sanhedrin are “those who supervise the congregation,” as it says [in the eglah arufah], “our hands did not shed [this blood]” (Devarim 21:7) — “that we did not see him and let him go” (Sotah 45b)866Sotah 45b (Mishnah): In the declaration of the eglah arufah, the elders say: “‘our hands did not spill this blood, nor did our eyes see’ (Devarim 21:7)” — [meaning] “he did not come into our hands and we sent him off without food, and we did not see him and leave him without escort.” (The elders are “the eyes of the congregation,” answerable for what they “see.”) — for it is incumbent on the Sanhedrin “to supervise in every matter.”
וְדָבָר זֶה חִידֵּשׁ יִתְרוֹ שֶׁאָמַר ״נָבֹל תִּבֹּל״ וְגוֹמֵר

And this matter Yisro “innovated,” when he said, “you will surely wear away” (Shemos 18:18)867Shemos 18:18: Yisro’s counsel to Moshe — “נָבֹל תִּבֹּל, גַּם אַתָּה גַּם הָעָם הַזֶּה אֲשֶׁר עִמָּךְ, כִּי כָבֵד מִמְּךָ הַדָּבָר” — “you will surely wear away — both you and this people that is with you — for the matter is too heavy for you.” Meforshim: Rashi — “navol tibol” means you will wither as a leaf wilts in the heat; you cannot bear it alone, so appoint judges beneath you. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the “portion Yisro added” — the appointing of judges (the Sanhedrin). Moshe, of himself, “did not wish to appoint a Sanhedrin”; he would rather “illumine every Jew’s eyes,” that each see his own faults — the light of the Future, when “no longer will each man teach his fellow.” But that inner sight is possible only for Israel; the convert must “receive from Israel,” and so this “increment” entered the Torah through Yisro.Izhbitz parallel - Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Yitro 1; cf. Kedushat Levi, Yitro 22: On 'Moshe listened to the voice of his father-in-law and did all that he said,' the Mei HaShiloach remarks that Yisro himself did not know the full depth of what his own counsel contained; the words were, as it were, spoken through him, while Moshe perceived their true reach. This is an especially fitting complement to R' Tzadok's 'you shall be for us as eyes.' Yisro can introduce the counsel that produces the system of judges, but its Torah-depth is grasped and established through Moshe. Kedushat Levi adds a second dimension: Torah shebe'al peh includes 'all that a seasoned student will one day innovate,' and Hashem entrusted Israel with the extraordinary power that the Torah as interpreted by the righteous sages of the generation becomes the operative halachic word. The two sources together sharpen R' Tzadok's distinction. Yisro's contribution is neither accidental nor merely administrative; it becomes a vessel for the 'eyes of the congregation.' Yet the 'eye' is not an autonomous wisdom imported from outside. The counsel is absorbed into Moshe's Torah, and from there into the Sanhedrin, whose vision is the Torah's own inner perception. This explains how the good spark of a convert can genuinely add to the revealed structure without becoming an independent source alongside Sinai. —
דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה לֹא רָצָה לְהַמְנוֹת סַנְהֶדְרִין, אַף דְּיָדַע שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְבַד לְהַשְׁגִּיחַ עַל שִׁשִּׁים רִיבּוֹא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל פְּרָטֵי עִנְיְנֵיהֶם
for Moshe “did not wish to appoint a Sanhedrin,” even though he knew it impossible for him alone to supervise 600,000 of Israel in all the particulars of their affairs;

הוּא רָצָה לְהַנְהִיגָם בְּעִנְיָן זֶה שֶׁיָּאִיר עֵינֵיהֶם שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לִרְאוֹת כָּל אֶחָד נִגְעֵי עַצְמוֹ בְּעַצְמוֹ, וְיִהְיֶה כָּל אֶחָד עֵינָיו בְּרֹאשׁוֹ וְלֹא יִצְטָרְכוּ לְעֵינֵי הָעֵדָה כְּלָל

he wished to “lead them” so as to “illumine their eyes,” that each could “see his own afflictions himself,” and each would have “his eyes in his head,” and they would “not need the eyes of the congregation” at all.
וְזֶהוּ אוֹר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד דְּלֹא יִלְמְדוּ עוֹד אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ, וְזֶהוּ שְׁלֵימוּת מִדַּת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה שֶׁהוּא רַבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
And this is the “light” of the Future, [when] “no longer will each man teach his fellow” (Yirmeyah 31:33) — and this is the “perfection of the trait of Moshe,” “the master of Israel,”
שֶׁרָצָה לְלַמְּדָן בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת עַד שֶׁלֹּא יִצְטָרְכוּ לְרַב עוֹד
who “wished to teach them” to the “ultimate perfection,” until they would “no longer need a teacher.”
אֲבָל אוֹר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר אֶלָּא לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֲבָל הַגֵּרִים בְּהֶכְרֵחַ לָהֶם לְקַבֵּל מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
But this “light” is possible “only for the Children of Israel”; whereas the “converts” of necessity “must receive from the Children of Israel,”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ דִּלְעָתִיד מָשִׁיחַ יָבוֹא רַק לְלַמֵּד לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם דְּהֵם יִצְטָרְכוּ לִימּוּד גַּם אָז
as they said, that “in the Future, Mashiach will come only to teach the nations” — for “they will need teaching even then.”
וּלְפִי שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין הִתְגַּלּוּת הַפְּרִי אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ הַקְּלִיפָּה, עַל כֵּן נֶעֱלַם כֹּחַ זֶה גַּם בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְעַל כֵּן הִסְכִּים לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

And since, in this world, there is no “revelation of the fruit” except “by way of the husk,” this “power [of inner sight]” is “concealed” even in the Children of Israel — and therefore Hashem “agreed with him.”

וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְרָא שֶׁהוּא ״יִיתֵּר״ הַפָּרָשָׁה בַּתּוֹרָה, כִּי אֵין זֶה מִצַּד עֶצֶם הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא מִצַּד עֶצֶם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, רַק מִצַּד הַיִּתּוּר וְהַתּוֹסָפוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ עַל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּגֵּרִים נִתְיַיתֵּר וְנוֹסַף גַּם כֵּן פֵּירוּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה

And nonetheless it is called that he “added [yiter]” the portion in the Torah — for this is not “from the essence of the Torah” (which is from the “essence of the souls of Israel”), but only from the “addition and increment” upon the souls of Israel [contributed] through the converts — [and correspondingly] an “explanation was added” in the Torah as well. — Moshe would have had every Jew see with his own eyes; the Sanhedrin is a concession to a world of husks, and it entered the Torah fittingly through the first convert, whose sight is only from without.

items.h: The theme: The root of the converts’ souls in the Torah is Parashas Yisro, who “covered Israel’s eyes” — yet by Hashem’s will, in order to raise distinguished souls as eyes for the congregation. Matan Torah itself was written in a portion bearing his name, Yisro being an expression of “surplus.” For in this world Torah is clothed in garments — ink upon parchment, the mitzvos in physical acts — and converts attain only the garments.

p: [נד] וְנִרְאֶה לִי כִּי שׇׁרְשֵׁי נַפְשׁוֹת הַגֵּרִים בַּתּוֹרָה הוּא בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ דְּיִתְרוֹ
And it seems to me that the “roots of the souls of the converts” in the Torah are in this portion of Yisro;

וְהוּא גָּרַם כִּיסּוּי עֵינַיִם דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיָה רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כֵּן וּלְרוֹמְמָם עַל יְדֵי זֶה נְפָשׁוֹת מְיוּחָדוֹת לִהְיוֹת לְעֵינַיִם לָעֵדָה, וְעַל יָדָן זָכָה גַּם הוּא לָזֶה

and he “caused a covering of the eyes” of Israel — except that this was “Hashem’s will,” to “elevate,” through it, distinguished souls to be “eyes for the congregation” — and through them he too “merited this.”
וְעַל כֵּן נִכְתַּב מַתַּן תּוֹרָה בְּפָרָשָׁה הַנִּקְרֵאת עַל שְׁמוֹ, וְהַשֵּׁם ״יִתְרוֹ״ הוּא עַל ״יִתּוּר״ שֶׁהִיא חוּץ לַתּוֹרָה
And therefore the “Giving of the Torah” was written in the portion “called by his name,” and the name “Yisro” is [from] “yitur [addition]” — which is “outside the Torah [proper].”
וַהֲרֵי מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הוּא עִיקַּר הַתּוֹרָה, רַק עִנְיַן סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה הַכְּתוּבָה בִּדְיוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי קְלָף זֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן רַק מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַמַּעֲלִים וּמַסְתִּיר אוֹר הָאֲמִיתִּי

And behold, the “Giving of the Torah” is the “essence of the Torah”; only the matter of a “Torah scroll written in ink upon parchment” is also only “from the side of this world,” which “conceals and hides the true light”868R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Emor §8): “this is the trait of Keser, which is above apprehension and human intellect — and then "He made darkness His covering"; and from the beginning of the utterance "let there be light" is the first trait, called supernal Chochmah, as it says, "wrapped in light like a garment" — teaching that He wrapped Himself.” The se’if’s “conceals and hides the true light” precisely: the garment is the condition of any revelation at all, and above it the light has no garment because it has no receiver. —
דְּלֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא נֶאֱמַר ״וְעַל לוּחַ לִבָּם אֶכְתְּבֶנָּה״, וְעַל כֵּן לֹא יִצְטָרְכוּ לִמְלַמֵּד
for of the Future it is said, “and upon the tablet of their heart I will write it” (Yirmeyah 31:32), and therefore they will “not need a teacher.”
וְרַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁנִּתְחַלֵּף ״עוֹר״ בְּעַד ״אוֹר״, כְּמוֹ ״כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר״ דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן תְּמוּר ״כָּתְנוֹת אוֹר״ שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ קֹדֶם הַחֵטְא

And [it is] only in this world, where “skin [or]” was exchanged for “light [or]” — like the “garments of skin” of Adam869R’ Tzadok — parallel (Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Eruvin, os ו–ז): on the sugya of R’ Meir (Eruvin 13a–b), R’ Tzadok writes: “This is what they said [in Bereishis Rabbah 20], that in R’ Meir’s Torah was written ‘kasnos or’ [with an alef] — for the ‘garments [kasnos]’ are the clothing that conceals the body, and ‘or’ with an alef means that even through the garment [the light] illumines and makes the body shine.” And he explains R’ Meir’s very name: he is called “Meir” [Hebrew, “illumines”] because “he illumines the eyes of the sages in the revealed halachah,” and “Nehorai” [Aramaic] for the hidden light of Torah, “which the ministering angels do not grasp” — “his name bespeaks the surpassing measure of his radiance, which is in the concealed and the deep.” (Precisely the se’if’s theme: the Torah of this world is clothed in “garments of skin,” yet the one who is himself “full of light” perceives the inner radiance even through the garment.), in place of the “garments of light” he had before the sin870Bereishis 3:21; Bereishis Rabbah 20:12: after the sin, “וַיַּעַשׂ ה׳ אֱלֹהִים לְאָדָם וּלְאִשְׁתּוֹ כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר וַיַּלְבִּשֵׁם” — “and Hashem God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin [or, with an ayin], and clothed them.” Meforshim: the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 20:12) reports that “in R’ Meir’s Torah scroll it was found written ‘kasnos or’ with an alef — garments of light,” the luminous garments Adam had worn before the sin, exchanged afterward for “garments of skin.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this world is one in which “or (skin) was substituted for or (light)”; correspondingly, the Torah of this world — “from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil” — is “clothed in garments of skin and parchment” (a scroll of ink upon hide), its inner light concealed, until the Future, when “upon the tablet of their heart I will write it.” —
כֵּן הַתּוֹרָה דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִסִּטְרָא דְּעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע, טָמֵא וְטָהוֹר כָּשֵׁר וּפָסוּל, מְלוּבֶּשֶׁת בְּכָתְנוֹת עוֹר וּקְלָף

so the “Torah of this world,” from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil — “impure and pure, fit and unfit” — is “clothed in garments of skin and parchment.”871R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Beha’alotcha §10): “"Woe to the people who say that the Torah comes to relate mere narratives and commonplace words"… "in this manner, the Torah has a body and [garments]."” Exactly the se’if: the Torah’s essence was written into a portion bearing a convert’s name because in this world the light must arrive clothed — the garment is not the Torah, but without it the Torah could not be given here at all.
וְכֵן כָּל מִצְווֹתָיו מְלוּבָּשִׁים בְּעִנְיָנִים מַעֲשִׂיִּים דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַגּוּפָנִי, וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַתּוֹרָה וְ״חַיֵּי עוֹלָם שֶׁנָּטַע בְּתוֹכֵנוּ״
And likewise all His mitzvos are “clothed” in “practical matters” of this corporeal world — and this is the “essence of the Torah,” “eternal life which He planted within us.”

וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא רַק לְבוּשׁ לְהַפְּנִימִיּוּת, מִכָּל מָקוֹם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהָאָדָם בִּלְבוּשׁ נַעֲשֶׂה גַּם זֶה הַלְּבוּשׁ מִצַּד הַתּוֹרָה, וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַקְּלִיפָּה הַסּוֹבֶבֶת לַפְּרִי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה

And although it is only a “garment” for the inwardness, nonetheless, in this world, where “man is [clad] in a garment,” this “garment” too is “made from the side of the Torah” — and this is “from the side of the husk that surrounds the fruit” in this world.872R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §53): “R’ Meir was able to distinguish and separate the inner [kernel] from the husk, for he was ‘full of light’ [me’ir], as his name implies — which is why in his Torah scroll it was written ‘garments of light’ [kasnos ohr] with an aleph (Bereishis Rabbah, end of §20): that even the ‘garment of skin’ [kasnos or] was full of light. And this is like the light of a torch, which draws to itself every small light that comes near it — so [R’ Meir] could draw toward himself the inner light that was within Acher. Therefore one should contemplate teshuvah before study, for then he is called a tzaddik (Kiddushin 49b) and merits the ‘light sown [for the righteous]’ — that what he learns be sown within his heart, to sprout abundant light within him.”Further Chassidic context - Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Yitro 5; Tanya, Iggeret HaKodesh 29:22-24: The Ishbitzer explicitly asks why Yisro's arrival is written before Matan Torah even according to the opinion that he actually came afterward. He answers that the Torah wished to demonstrate, before describing Revelation itself, how far the power of Torah can reach: even Yisro, who had been exceedingly distant and had served every form of idolatry, could through genuine longing draw so near that the parashah of Matan Torah bears his name. He reads the name Yisro as a hint to 'chemlah gedolah vi-yeseirah' - an additional compassion by which the Divine light spreads even to the distant. This directly supports R' Tzadok's play on Yisro as 'surplus': the surplus is not extraneous matter alongside Torah, but Torah's capacity to clothe and extend its light to a place that previously stood outside. Tanya supplies the complementary side of the garment metaphor. The Alter Rebbe explains that the supernal Will clothed in the Written Torah is often sealed and hidden until Torah shebe'al peh reveals its concrete form - tefillin, Shabbos labor, and the detailed halachic structure. Thus a garment is not merely a concealment of the light; it is also what makes the hidden will usable and knowable below. R' Tzadok's formulation that gerim attain the 'garments' can therefore be read as a real mode of attachment, while still preserving his distinction between the garment and the innermost root.

וְעַל כֵּן נִכְתַּב בְּפָרָשַׁת יִתְרוֹ, שֶׁמִּצַּד הַזֶּה שֶׁבָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דָּבָר ״יִתּוּר״ הַמְקַיֵּים לְדָבָר הָעִיקָּר, מִצַּד הַזֶּה נִתְלַבְּשָׁה הַתּוֹרָה גַּם כֵּן בַּלְּבוּשִׁים הַלָּלוּ, וְהַגֵּרִים אֵין מַשִּׂיגִים אֶלָּא הַלְּבוּשִׁים

And therefore it was written in “Parashas Yisro” — for from this aspect, that Hashem created in this world a thing of “yitur [surplus]” that “sustains the essential thing,” from this aspect the Torah too was “clothed in these garments,” and the “converts attain only the garments.”

וּבַהֲלִיכָה בַּמִּדְבָּר, שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעוּ עֲדַיִין לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁשָּׁם יִזְכּוּ לְבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְהַשָּׂגַת הַפְּנִימִיּוּת, הָיָה הוּא לָהֶם לְעֵינַיִם מִצַּד הַשָּׂגַת הַלְּבוּשׁ

And in the “journey through the Wilderness,” when they had not yet reached Eretz Yisrael — where they would merit the building of the Beis HaMikdash and the “attainment of the inwardness” — he [Yisro] was “for them as eyes,” from the side of the “attainment of the garment.”
וְעַל כֵּן זָכָה לְדוּשְׁנָהּ שֶׁל יְרִיחוֹ עַד זְמַן בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, שֶׁאָז הֵאִיר אוֹר דְּגִילּוּי שְׁכִינָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנִתְרַחֲקוּ הַגֵּרִים מִנַּחֲלָתָהּ

And therefore [his descendants] “merited the fertile plain of Yericho” — until the time of the building of the Beis HaMikdash, when the “light of the revelation of the Shechinah” shone in Eretz Yisrael, and the “converts were distanced from her inheritance.” — the convert grasps the Torah’s outer garment, never its inner light; so Yisro served as Israel’s “eyes” only for the wilderness years, until the Mikdash’s inner radiance made his borrowed sight no longer needed.

items.h: The theme: From the “garments of Torah” come all its dinim, which reached Israel through Moshe’s being raised in Midyan — and so his death was bound up with avenging Midyan, who had concealed the Torah’s light. Pinchas, of Yisro’s line, was the one who checked it: “from the forest itself comes the axe-handle.” The garment is the Nukva that clothes the man, which is why Dinah was reincarnated in Kozbi — and where Zimri erred in his inference.

p: [נה] וּמִצַּד הַלְּבוּשִׁים דְּתוֹרָה הֵם כָּל דִּינֵי דִּינִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ, וְזֶה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי גִּידּוּל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה בְּמִדְיָן

And from the side of the “garments of Torah” are all the “laws of judgments [dinei dinim]” in it — and this [came] through Moshe’s “being raised in Midyan.”873R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Toldos §8): “that which begets the renewal of Torah is Scripture and Mishnah, which are "the dew of heaven and the fat of the earth"; and this is "from the dew of heaven" — this is Scripture, which is from Heaven, from the Holy One who gave the Torah, and not from the side of a person’s toil.” Exactly the se’if: the dinim that clothe the Torah are generated from the given text itself, which is why the one raised outside could become the vessel through which they came down.
וְעַל כֵּן נִתְלָה מִיתָתוֹ בְּנִקְמַת הַמִּדְיָנִים, כִּי הֵם גָּרְמוּ כִּיסּוּי וְהַעֲלֵם אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And therefore his “death was made dependent on the vengeance of the Midianites,” for they “caused the covering and concealment of the light of the Torah”;
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם בִּקְדֻשָּׁה, אֲבָל מִצַּד הָרַע שֶׁבָּהֶם רָצוּ לְהַעֲלִים לְגַמְרֵי שֶׁיִּתְעָרְבוּ בַּגּוֹיִם
and this is “from the side of the [holy] root” in them; but “from the side of the evil” in them, they “wished to conceal entirely,” that [Israel] “mingle among the nations.”
וּפִנְחָס שֶׁבָּא מִיִּתְרוֹ עִיכֵּב בְּדָבָר זֶה, וּמִנֵּיהּ וּבֵיהּ אַבָּא נִיזֹל נַרְגָּא

And Pinchas, who “descended from Yisro,” “held back” this matter — “from the [forest] itself comes the axe[’s handle]”;874R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Toldos §5): “that he prayed for himself, and did not even pray for children, as it says in the Zohar; and only for Sedom did he pray — and his prayer is called "standing."” Exactly the se’if: the law was hidden from Moshe and grasped by Pinchas — for a man’s reach in prayer and in halachah is bounded by what belongs to his own portion, and not by his greatness.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם שֹׁרֶשׁ הַהַעֲלָמָה נִשְׁאַר, וְזֶה גָּרַם מִיתַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה שֶׁהוּא הַעֲלֵם הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹרוֹ

and nonetheless the “root of the concealment remained,” and this “caused the death of Moshe,” which is the “concealment of the revelation of his light.”875R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas Shabbos §2): “it is not in a person’s hand but in the hand of the Holy One, as it says, "Your hands established"; and from the fact that it brings the verse "my tent is despoiled," it is clear that it refers to the [First] Beis HaMikdash that was destroyed — which is why it is called "My tent."” The se’if’s concealment exactly: what conceals the Torah’s light is not in human hands to undo, and its removal likewise awaits Him.
וְהוּצְרַךְ לִצְרוֹר לַמִּדְיָנִים מִקּוֹדֶם, שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹאוּ אַחַר זְמַן לְהַעֲלִים לְגַמְרֵי מִצַּד הָרַע שֶׁבָּהֶם
And it was “necessary to harass the Midianites beforehand,” lest they come, in time, “to conceal entirely,” from the side of the evil in them.
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּהַלְּבוּשׁ הוּא סִטְרָא דְּנוּקְבָא הַמְסוֹבֶבֶת גֶּבֶר וּמַלְבִּישְׁתּוֹ, וְעַל כֵּן דִּינָה נִתְגַּלְגְּלָה בְּכָזְבִּי בַּת נְשִׂיא מִדְיָן שֶׁכִּזְּבָה בְּאָבִיהָ

As is known, the “garment” is the “side of the Nukva,” which “surrounds the man and clothes him”; and therefore “Dinah was reincarnated in Kozbi,” daughter of the prince of Midyan, who “belied her father” [kizvah b’aviha],876Sanhedrin 82a–b: Rav Sheishess said: her name was not Kozbi but Shveilnai bas Tzur; why was she called Kozbi? — because she “deceived [kizvah]” through her father. The tribe of Shimon came to Zimri ben Salu, “we are judged with death-penalties and you sit silent?” He gathered 24,000 and went to Kozbi, saying, “yield to me.” She replied, “I am a king’s daughter; my father commanded me to yield only to the greatest among them.” He said, “I too am a tribal prince, and greater than [Moshe].” He seized her forelock and brought her before Moshe: “Ben Amram — is this one forbidden or permitted? and if you say forbidden — who permitted Yisro’s daughter to you?” The halachah “was hidden from him,” and all wept — “and behold they were weeping at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.” “And Pinchas saw” — Rav said: “he saw the deed and remembered the halachah,” and said, “great-uncle, did you not teach me on your descent from Sinai that ‘one who cohabits with a gentile woman — zealots may strike him’?” [Moshe] answered, “let the reader of the letter be its agent.” And Pinchas was a grandson of Yisro, for Elazar had married a daughter of “Putiel” — Yisro.Izhbitz parallel - Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Matot 6: The Ishbitzer returns to the episode of Midyan and makes the safeguard in R' Tzadok's discussion explicit. When Moshe rebuked Pinchas and the army for keeping the Midianite women alive, the Mei HaShiloach says that Moshe showed Pinchas that he too had momentarily touched the same error as Zimri: perceiving that a soul contains a holy point and therefore concluding that it may already be brought into holiness through one's own present action. Zimri's claim, 'who permitted Yisro's daughter to you?,' was based on his conviction that Kozbi possessed a real root of holiness, just as Moshe had known that Tzipporah belonged to him. The Ishbitzer does not deny the hidden root; he says that in this world 'the Holy One did not choose this matter,' and that Moshe, in the later war, saw that the apparently salvageable Midianite women were forbidden at that moment despite an underlying connection. This is precisely the distinction needed for R' Tzadok's language of the Torah's dinim as garments. The garment of halachah is not a lower truth that may be discarded once a person senses a deeper spark. It is the authoritative disclosure of how the Divine will is to be lived now. Pinchas' greatness was that he remembered the halachah at Shittim; Moshe's rebuke later taught him that even holy perception must remain subordinate to that present halachic boundary.
שֶׁהָיָה נְשִׂיא וְשֹׁרֶשׁ כֹּחַ הָרַע שֶׁבְּמִדְיָן, וְרָצָה לְהַכְשִׁיל יִשְׂרָאֵל וּלְהַמְשִׁיכָם לְמָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת וְלִהְיוֹת כְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם
who was the “prince and root of the evil power of Midyan,” and “wished to cause Israel to stumble,” to “draw them to a place where they have no connection,” and to “be like all the nations.”
אֲבָל הִיא לֹא שָׁמְעָה לוֹ וְדָבְקָה רַק בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ שַׁיָּיכוּת (לְשֵׁבֶט שִׁמְעוֹן), וְהִיא הָיְתָה מִתְרַצֵּית לְהִתְגַּיֵּיר גַּם כֵּן אִלּוּ רָצָה זִמְרִי, ״מִי הִתִּיר לָךְ״

But “she did not listen to him,” and “cleaved only to a place where she had a connection” ([the tribe of] Shimon), and she “would have consented to convert” as well, had Zimri wished — “who permitted [her] to you?”
כִּי גַּם הִיא דּוּגְמָתָהּ חֲפֵצָה לִידָּבֵק בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, לֹא לְהַמְשִׁיךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָהֶם
for she too, in her “likeness [to Dinah],” “desired to cleave to Israel,” not to “draw Israel to them.”
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא תְּפָשָׂהּ בִּבְלוֹרִיתָהּ שֶׁהוּא ״דַּרְכֵי הָאֱמוֹרִי״, וְכַאֲשֶׁר הִיא עֲדַיִין בְּגוֹיּוּתָהּ
Except that he “seized her by her forelock” — which is “the ways of the Amorite” — while she was “still in her gentile-ness.”

כִּי הוּא (זִמְרִי) גִּלְגּוּל שְׁכֶם, וְהִרְגִּישׁ בְּדָבָר זֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ נַפְשׁוֹת גּוֹיִם מִתְגַּלְגְּלוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְיִשְׂרָאֵל בַּגּוֹיִם, וְדִימָה מִזֶּה דְּאֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת גַּם כֵּן קְלִיטָה לְנִיצוֹצִין קַדִּישִׁין גַּם בְּעוֹדָן בְּגֵיּוּתָן

For he [Zimri] is the “reincarnation of Shechem,” and “sensed this matter” — that there are “gentile souls reincarnated in Israel, and Israel among the gentiles” — and “inferred from this” that “absorption of holy sparks is possible even while they are still in their gentile-ness,”
וּבִפְרָט בְּמִדְיָן שֶׁסָּמוּךְ לַעֲמָלֵק
and especially in Midyan, which is “adjacent to Amalek.”
וּבַעֲמָלֵק בֵּיאַרְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִקְלוֹט הַנִּיצוֹצִין קַדִּישִׁין שֶׁבּוֹ אֶלָּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה, דְּבוֹ כְּתִיב ״תִּמְחֶה״

And regarding Amalek I explained elsewhere that it is “impossible to absorb the holy sparks in him except in this manner” — for concerning him it is written “you shall blot out [the memory of Amalek]” (Devarim 25:19)877Devarim 25:19: the command against Amalek — “תִּמְחֶה אֶת זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק מִתַּחַת הַשָּׁמָיִם, לֹא תִּשְׁכָּח” — “you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens; do not forget.” Meforshim: because Amalek is “the root of all evil,” his very “memory” must be erased; and the Mechilta teaches that “we do not accept converts from Amalek.” R’ Tzadok’s use: since Amalek’s evil is total, “it is impossible to absorb the holy sparks within him except by compulsion and unintentionally,” never willingly — and only through a woman (“the ground of the world”), where a gentile comes upon a bas Yisrael and the child is kosher, as indeed “of the descendants of Haman, some taught Torah in Bnei Brak” (Gittin 57b).;
וְאָמְרוּ [בַּמְּכִילְתָּא] דְּאֵין מְקַבְּלִין גֵּרִים מֵעֲמָלֵק, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מִבְּנֵי בָּנָיו שֶׁל הָמָן לָמְדוּ תִּינוֹקוֹת בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם (בְּנֵי בְּרַק, בְּגִיטִּין נז:)

and they said [in the Mechilta] that “we do not accept converts from Amalek”; yet, nonetheless, “of the descendants of Haman, [some] taught children in Yerushalayim” (in Bnei Brak — Gittin 57b)878Gittin 57b: “From the descendants of Haman there were those who learned Torah in Bnei Brak; from the descendants of Sisera, those who taught children in Yerushalayim; from the descendants of Sancheriv, those who taught Torah in public.” (The “good spark” absorbed even from the husk of the nations.).

וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דְּהָיָה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁבָּא גּוֹי אֶחָד מִבְּנֵי בָּנָיו עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּהַוָּלָד כָּשֵׁר וְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם קָרוּי גַּם כֵּן ״בֶּן הַגּוֹי״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּתּוֹרָה ״וְהוּא בֶּן אִישׁ מִצְרִי״

And perforce this was because “a gentile of his descendants came upon a bas Yisrael” — [where] “the child is kosher and is a Jew,” yet is nonetheless also “called the son of the gentile,” as it says in the Torah, “and he was the son of an Egyptian man” (Vayikra 24:10)879Vayikra 24:10: of the blasphemer — “וַיֵּצֵא בֶּן אִשָּׁה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית, וְהוּא בֶּן אִישׁ מִצְרִי, בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל” — “and the son of an Israelite woman went out — and he was the son of an Egyptian man — among the Children of Israel.” Meforshim: Rashi (from the Midrash) — he was the son of the Egyptian taskmaster whom Moshe had slain, born to Shelomis bas Divri of the tribe of Dan; the child of a gentile father and a Jewish mother is a kosher Jew, yet Scripture still calls him “son of an Egyptian man.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the one narrow channel by which a holy spark is reclaimed from the nations — “a gentile upon a bas Yisrael,” where “the child is kosher and is a Jew,” yet is “also called the son of the gentile”; whereas “a Jew upon a gentile woman — her child is like her.”.
וְחָשַׁב דְּגַם בְּמִדְיָן כֵּן חֲבֵירוֹ, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן הַתְחָלַת הַגּוֹיִם, הַקְּלִיטָה עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה דַּוְקָא. וְטָעָה בָּזֶה דְּגַם שָׁם חֲלִילָה לִהְיוֹת בְּרָצוֹן

And he “thought” that in Midyan too — its “fellow,” also a “beginning of the nations” — the “absorption” [would be] specifically in this manner. And “he erred in this,” [thinking it possible] there too, God forbid, “willingly”;
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִקְלוֹט הַנִּיצוֹצִין קַדִּישִׁין מֵעֲמָלֵק אֶלָּא בְּאֹנֶס וְשֶׁלֹּא בְּמִתְכַּוֵּין, וּכְעִנְיַן ״לְבַסּוּמֵי בְּפוּרַיָּא עַד דְּלָא יָדַע״

but it is “impossible to absorb the holy sparks from Amalek except by compulsion and unintentionally” — like the matter of “becoming intoxicated on Purim until one does not know880Megillah 7b: Rava’s dictum — “חַיָּיב אִינִישׁ לְבַסּוּמֵי בְּפוּרַיָּא עַד דְּלָא יָדַע בֵּין אָרוּר הָמָן לְבָרוּךְ מָרְדֳּכַי” — “a person is obligated to become intoxicated on Purim until he does not know [the difference] between ‘cursed is Haman’ and ‘blessed is Mordechai’.” Meforshim: the commentators explain that on Purim one reaches a rung “beyond knowing,” where even Haman’s [Amalek’s] evil is subsumed within the praise of God. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the sole mode in which the holy sparks may be drawn out of Amalek — “by compulsion and unintentionally,” in a state of “not knowing,” beyond the deliberate mind; Zimri’s error was to imagine that one might reclaim Midyan’s sparks willingly, in full consciousness, which is impossible..”

וְזֶהוּ רַק בְּאִשָּׁה דְּ״קַרְקַע עוֹלָם״ הִיא, וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל ״אֹנֶס״, וְגַם זֶה רַק בְּגוֹי עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּהַוָּלָד כָּשֵׁר, אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל הַגּוֹיָה הֲרֵי וַלְדָּהּ כְּמוֹתָהּ

And this is only through a woman, who is “the ground of the world” [passive] — and what I wrote above [is] “compulsion”; and even this is only [when] a “gentile [comes] upon a bas Yisrael,” where “the child is kosher” — but [when] a Jew [comes] upon a gentile woman, “her child is like her.”
וְשׇׁרְשׁוֹ שֶׁהָיָה נֶפֶשׁ הַגּוֹי גָּרַם לוֹ טָעוּת זֶה
And his “root,” that he was [reincarnated from] a “gentile soul” [Shechem], “caused him this error.”

וּלְפִי שֶׁלֹּא אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא ״דֶּרֶךְ חַתְנוּת״, אַף דְּיָדַע דְּהוּא אִיסּוּר חָמוּר גַּם שֶׁלֹּא דֶּרֶךְ חַתְנוּת, חָשַׁב דִּלְכָךְ לֹא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ הָאִיסּוּר לְפִי שֶׁפְּעָמִים יֵשׁ שֶׁאֵינוֹ אִיסּוּר

And since the Torah “prohibited only ‘by way of marriage,’” even though he knew that “it is a severe prohibition even not by way of marriage,” he “thought” the prohibition “was not made explicit” [in that form] because “sometimes there is [a case] where it is not a prohibition.”
וּבֶאֱמֶת מַה שֶּׁלֹּא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ הוּא לְפִי שֶׁזֶּה דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת כְּלָל לְזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״אָנֹכִי״ וְגוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא אָמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן צִיווּי
But in truth, the reason it “was not made explicit” is that “this is a thing that has no connection at all to the seed of Israel” — in the manner that “Anochi” was said “not in the imperative.”

אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם כָּתְבוּ בַּתּוֹרָה לְפִי שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ שֹׁרֶשׁ לְחִסָּרוֹן זֶה גַּם כֵּן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּשֵׁבֶט דָּן, אַף דְּהוּא רַק מִצַּד עוֹבִי הַחוּמְרִיּוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל, סוֹף סוֹף הוּא חִסָּרוֹן לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן וְהוּצְרַךְ לִיכָּתֵב

Except that nonetheless it was “written in the Torah,” since there is nonetheless a “root for this deficiency” also in Israel, in the tribe of Dan — even though it is only “from the side of the thickness of materiality,” as I wrote above — [and] in the end it is a “deficiency to outward appearance,” and so it “needed to be written.” — Zimri’s fatal error was to read a true principle — that holy sparks can be reclaimed from the nations — into a case where it does not hold, mistaking the one narrow channel of reclamation for a general license.

items.h: The theme: The 613 mitzvos are 613 “counsels” against each tribe’s root-deficiency — the eleven arurim against eleven tribes, with Shimon alone left neither cursed nor blessed. But a deficiency such as Shittim is unbelievable in Yaakov’s seed: idolatry is no real joining, whereas union with a foreign woman is a real cleaving. So it cannot be as it appears — Shimon’s holy root is deeply concealed, which is why hearing, the sense that grasps the hidden, is his.

p: [נו] וְכָל תרי״ג מִצְווֹת הַתּוֹרָה הֵם תרי״ג ״עֵטִין״ לְזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶגֶד כָּל הַחִסְרוֹנוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם בְּשָׁרְשָׁם

And all the 613 mitzvos of the Torah are “613 counsels [eitin]” for the seed of Israel, “against” all the deficiencies that they have in their root.881R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Ki Tavo §14): “as it says, in the addition Moshe said them of himself and by ruach ha-kodesh; and therefore he said them in the singular — meaning that there are rectifications in this for each individual by himself, and one has no relation to the other.” Exactly the se’if: the mitzvos are “counsels” aimed at a root-deficiency, and a counsel is necessarily individual — which is why the whole is stated one by one.
וְכָל שֵׁבֶט יֵשׁ לוֹ חִסָּרוֹן מְיוּחָד, דְּעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר י״א ״אֲרוּרִים״ נֶגֶד י״א שְׁבָטִים

And each tribe has a “particular deficiency” — regarding which are stated the “eleven curses [arurim]” (Devarim 27) “against” the eleven tribes.882R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Toldos §7): “the matters of this world; for the first three [traits] are of the World to Come, and the trait of Malchus is joined to "Bereishis," [as] Keser is the crown of Malchus — and therefore he said, corresponding to them, blessings [and curses].” Exactly the se’if: the eleven arurim answer to eleven tribal deficiencies, and it is Malchus — Yehudah’s portion — that stands apart from the count, which is why Shimon is folded into it.883R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Chalomot §27): “that the Torah spelled out the curses and the arurim of Har Eival, and not the blessings of Har Gerizim — for what they said of the Torah, "it is written and set down," is revealed to all; these are the revealed matters.” Exactly the se’if: the eleven arurim stand written precisely because they answer to deficiencies that must be named — while the corresponding blessings remain unwritten.

וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּהוּא נֶגֶד הַחִסְרוֹנוֹת שֶׁבְּשֹׁרֶשׁ כָּל שֵׁבֶט, כִּי ״אָרוּר״ לְשׁוֹן חִסָּרוֹן, וְנֶגֶד שִׁמְעוֹן לֹא כָּתוּב ״אָרוּר״ לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה לְבָרְכוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב [רָשִׁ״י פָּרָשַׁת תָּבוֹא (כז, כד)]

And I heard that it corresponds to the deficiencies884From the Ishbitzer (Mei HaShiloach): the teaching R’ Tzadok “heard” — that the 613 mitzvos, the “613 counsels” (taryag eitin), stand over against the particular root-deficiency of each tribe — is his rebbe’s, R’ Mordechai Yosef of Izhbitz (see §8 above). in the “root of each tribe” — for “arur [cursed]” is an expression of “lack”; and corresponding to Shimon, “arur” is not written, because [Moshe] “did not wish to bless him885Rashi, Devarim 27:24 (citing R’ Moshe HaDarshan): “there are here eleven verses beginning with ‘arur [cursed]’ — corresponding to the eleven tribes; but for Shimon he did not write ‘arur,’ because [Moshe] did not wish to bless him before his death, when he blessed the other tribes — and so he did not wish to curse him either.” Background: the arurim of Ki Savo (Devarim 27:15–26) number eleven, Shimon alone unmentioned. Meforshim: Rashi elsewhere (Devarim 33:7) gives the reason Moshe withheld Shimon’s blessing — “he held [the deed of] Shittim against him.” R’ Tzadok’s use: each “arur” marks the root-deficiency of a tribe (as he “heard”); Shimon’s is left unwritten because his deficiency — the deed of Shittim (Zimri) — “is a matter that cannot be clothed in writing,” too concealed to appear on the revealed page.,” as Rashi wrote [Parashas Tavo, Devarim 27:24].
וְאֵין דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה בָּאִים בְּמִקְרֶה, וְנִרְאֶה מִזֶּה כִּי הוּא דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְלַבֵּשׁ בִּכְתָב וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְכָתְבוֹ
And “the words of Torah do not come by chance,” and it appears from this that it is “a matter not clothed in writing,” and “impossible to write.”
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת חִסָּרוֹן כָּזֶה הַנִּמְצָא בָּהֶם בְּמַעֲשֵׂה דְּשִׁטִּים אִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלָל לְהַאֲמִין שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב
For in truth, such a deficiency as was found in them in the “deed of Shittim” [Zimri], it is “entirely impossible to believe” would exist in the “seed of Yaakov.”
כִּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֵינוֹ חִיבּוּר בֶּאֱמֶת רַק כְּפִי הַדִּמְיוֹן שֶׁמְּדַמֶּה זֶה לֶאֱלֹקוּת, אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא עֵץ וָאֶבֶן בְּעָלְמָא
For “idolatry” is not a real “joining,” but only according to the “imagination” that “likens it to divinity” — but in truth it is “mere wood and stone,”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּשְׁלוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ עַל הָעֵגֶל ״לִמְגַפֶּפֶת לְסָרִיס״
and as they analogized in the Midrash, regarding the [golden] calf, to “one who embraces a eunuch” [an act with no issue].
