אֲבָל הַבָּא עַל בַּת אֵל נֵכָר דְּהָיוּ לְבָשָׂר אֶחָד, שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְהוֹלִיד בְּדוֹמֶה לִשְׁנֵיהֶם גּוּף שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם שׁוּתָּפִים בּוֹ, זֶה חִיבּוּר וּדִיבּוּק גָּמוּר

But one who “comes upon the daughter of a foreign god,” where “they become one flesh,” able “to beget [a child] resembling both” — a body in which both are “partners” — this is a “complete joining and cleaving.”
וְכֵן תּוֹרָה כָּתְבָה בּוֹ לְשׁוֹן ״וְדָבַק בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ״, ״לְמַטֵּה אֲבוֹתָיו יִדְבָּקוּ״ וְכַדּוֹמֶה

And so the Torah “wrote of it the expression ‘and he shall cleave to his wife’” (Bereishis 2:24), “they shall cleave to the tribe of their fathers” (Bamidbar 36:7)886Bereishis 2:24; Bamidbar 36:7: the Torah reserves the language of “cleaving [deveikus]” for a true, bonded union — “וְדָבַק בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ, וְהָיוּ לְבָשָׂר אֶחָד,” “and he shall cleave to his wife, and they shall become one flesh” (2:24); and “אִישׁ בְּנַחֲלַת מַטֵּה אֲבֹתָיו יִדְבְּקוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,” “each shall cleave to the inheritance of his fathers’ tribe” (36:7). R’ Tzadok’s use: union with “the daughter of a foreign god” is a “complete cleaving,” for the two “become one flesh,” a body in which both are partners — unlike idolatry, which “the Midrash likens to one who embraces a eunuch,” a barren act that begets nothing. Hence the deficiency of Shittim, were it truly as it appears, would be an unthinkable “cleaving” of Israel — who cleave to the living God — to its very opposite.Izhbitz clarification - Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Balak 9: On Zimri's challenge to Moshe, the Ishbitzer gives one of the clearest formulations of the prospective/retrospective distinction that is essential when reading this entire passage. Zimri argued that just as Moshe knew Tzipporah had a portion in the World to Come, he too saw that Kozbi had a future holy root. The Mei HaShiloach answers with 'do not boast of tomorrow, for you do not know what a day will bring': even if one perceives that in the future a matter will be clarified for good, one still does not know 'how Hashem conducts the present.' Moshe's union with Tzipporah was permitted because Hashem illuminated for him how to act in the present; Zimri had no such authorization. Only afterward can Heaven disclose that a hidden soul-root was genuinely connected. This exactly complements R' Tzadok's assertion that Shittim cannot represent the true root of Shimon. The hidden holiness explains why the fall is not the tribe's essence; it does not retroactively give a person license to enact the fall. Before and during action the Torah's revealed command and the obligation of bechirah govern absolutely. Only after the fact, and only through Divine clarification and teshuvah, may a deeper providential root be uncovered. The source therefore protects R' Tzadok's very daring language from an antinomian reading while preserving the Izhbitz claim that the outward appearance is not always the final truth., and the like.
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל הַדְּבֵקִים בֵּאלֹקִים חַיִּים אֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לִידָּבֵק בְּמַה שֶּׁכְּנֶגֶד זֶה
And Israel, who “cleave to the living God,” how is it “possible for them to cleave to that which is opposite this”?
וְהַכְּתָב הוּא דָּבָר הַגָּלוּי לַכֹּל, וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַחִסָּרוֹן כְּפִי הַנִּגְלֶה מֵהַמַּעֲשֶׂה הוּא דָּבָר שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר
And “writing” is a thing “revealed to all”; and for the deficiency to be “as revealed from the deed” is “impossible.”

אֲבָל יֵשׁ דְּבָרִים בְּגוֹ וְאֵין הַחִסָּרוֹן כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת, כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ כֹּחַ קְדֻשַּׁת שֵׁבֶט שִׁמְעוֹן נֶעֱלַם מְאֹד בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כִּי הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ ״עָלְמָא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא״ הַנֶּעֱלָם

But “there are matters within,” and the deficiency is “not as it is in the revealed” — for the “root of the power of the holiness of the tribe of Shimon” is “greatly concealed” in this world, for it is the “root of the concealed world [alma d’iskasya].”
כִּי שֵׁשֶׁת בְּנֵי לֵאָה וּבַת אַחַת הֵם נֶגֶד שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכָל דָּבָר שֵׁשׁ קְצָווֹת דְּדְכוּרָא וְנוּקְבָא כַּיָּדוּעַ
For the “six sons of Leah and one daughter” correspond to the “seven traits” — for in everything there are “six extremities of the male,” and [the] Nukva [female], as is known.
וְשִׁמְעוֹן נֶגֶד מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁהוּא מִדָּה הַמְצַמְצֶמֶת וּמַעֲלֶמֶת הַדָּבָר, וְעַל כֵּן נוֹסַף בּוֹ הַכֹּחַ עַל הַהֶעְלֵם עַל הָעוֹלָם
And Shimon corresponds to the “trait of Gevurah,” which is “the trait that contracts and conceals the thing” — and therefore there was “added in him the power” of “concealment” over the world.
וְכֵן כֹּחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה אֵין לוֹ תְּפִיסָה בְּדָבָר גַּשְׁמִי וּמַמָּשִׁיִּי כִּרְאִיָּה, כִּי הַדִּבּוּר וְהַקּוֹל רוּחָנִי וְאֵינוֹ נִרְגָּשׁ וּמוּחָשׁ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל
And likewise, the “power of hearing” has no “grasp of a physical, tangible thing” like sight — for “speech and voice are spiritual,” and are “not felt or sensed” in this world at all.
וְעַל כֵּן חוּשׁ הַשְּׁמִיעָה רוּחָנִי יוֹתֵר מִכָּל הַחוּשִׁים, שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ תְּפִיסָה רַק בְּדָבָר רוּחָנִי וְלֹא בְּגַשְׁמִי כְּלָל
And therefore the “sense of hearing is more spiritual than all the senses,” having “grasp only in a spiritual thing,” and “not in a physical [thing]” at all.
וּבִשְׁמִיעָה יוּכַל הָאָדָם לָדַעַת מַטְמוֹנוֹתָיו וּסְתָרָיו שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ שֶׁבְּלִבּוֹ נֶעֱלָם וְטָמִיר שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע לוֹ בְּדִבּוּרוֹ
And through “hearing,” a person can “know the hidden treasures and secrets of his fellow” — that which “in his heart is concealed and hidden” — [when] he “hears it in his speech”;
מַה שֶּׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר בִּרְאִיָּה וּשְׁאָר חוּשִׁים לְהַשִּׂיג אֶלָּא הַנִּגְלֶה לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which is “impossible” with sight and the other senses — [which] attain “only the revealed, to outward appearance.”
וְלֵידָתוֹ הָיָה עַל יְדֵי ״כִּי שָׁמַע ה׳״ וְגוֹמֵר, דְּגַם לְמַעְלָה יֵשׁ כֵּן
And his [Shimon’s] “birth” was through “for Hashem has heard” (Bereishis 29:33) — for “above, too, there is such [a distinction].”
אַף דְּה׳ ״יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב״ וְהוּא רוֹאֶה גַּם הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת, מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ חִילּוּק בֵּין רְאִיָּה לִשְׁמִיעָה

Even though “Hashem sees the heart” (I Shmuel 16:7)887I Shmuel 16:7: as Shmuel comes to anoint David, God warns him not to judge by appearance — “כִּי הָאָדָם יִרְאֶה לַעֵינַיִם, וַה׳ יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב,” “for man looks upon the eyes [the outward], but Hashem looks upon the heart.” Meforshim: Rashi — a person perceives only what is outwardly visible, whereas God discerns the inner intent. R’ Tzadok’s use: even though “Hashem sees the heart” and perceives the hidden, “there is still a distinction between seeing and hearing” — sight grasps the visible surface, but hearing reaches “what the heart conceals”; hence at Reuven’s birth, from the side of seeing, only “affliction” and “a lack of love” were named — not “hatred,” which belongs to the deeper realm of hearing (Shimon). and “sees even the hidden things,” nonetheless “there is a distinction between seeing and hearing”:
כִּי הָרְאִיָּה הוּא כְּפִי תְּפִיסַת עֵין הָרוֹאֶה בַּדָּבָר הַנִּרְאֶה, וְהַשְּׁמִיעָה הוּא רַק מַה שֶּׁהַלָּה מַשְׁמִיעַ לוֹ, וְהַמַּשְׁמִיעַ מַשְׁמִיעַ כְּפִי תְּפִיסָתוֹ וְהַשָּׂגָתוֹ

for “seeing” is according to “the grasp of the eye of the beholder” in the “visible thing,” whereas “hearing” is “only what the other conveys,” and “the conveyer conveys according to his [own] grasp and comprehension.”

וְעַל כֵּן בִּרְאִיָּה נֶאֱמַר ״כִּי רָאָה ה׳ בְּעׇנְיִי״, ״כִּי עַתָּה יֶאֱהָבַנִי״, וְלֹא נִזְכַּר לְשׁוֹן שִׂנְאָה, דְּמִצַּד רְאִיַּית הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא הָיָה נִקְרָא שִׂנְאָה רַק חִסָּרוֹן אַהֲבָה וָעוֹנִי

And therefore, with “seeing,” it says [at Reuven’s birth] “for Hashem has seen my affliction,” “for now my husband will love me” (Bereishis 29:32), and “no expression of hatred is mentioned” — for from the side of “Hashem’s seeing,” it was “not called hatred, but only a lack of love and affliction.” — sight, the most physical sense, registers only surface “affliction”; the deeper verdict of “hatred” belongs to the realm of hearing, which alone reaches what the heart hides.

items.h: The theme: Israel’s root is to be “poor,” owning nothing of themselves — like the woman, and like the moon by which they count, against the nations’ sun. Hence the yetzer provokes Israel most, for they have no power of their own to defeat it, while the nations’ very power drops them into the pit. Israel’s eyes look only to Hashem — and recognizing one’s affliction is itself the beginning of drawing near.

p: [נז] וְזֶהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם עֲנִיִּים וְדַלִּים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם כְּלוּם, דּוּגְמַת הָאִשָּׁה דְּלֵית לָהּ מִגַּרְמָהּ

And this is the “root of Israel,” who are “poor and lowly,” “having nothing” — like the woman, “who has nothing of her own”;888R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §25): “[Man’s completion is] from Hashem, who created man as a being of deficiency requiring completion. And this is the root of Israel, who ‘count by the moon’ — for they are ‘in a state of deficiency,’ and their completion is upheld from Hashem. But the nations of the world ‘count by the sun,’ which has no deficiency; since they have nothing to complete, it seems to them that they lack nothing — until they say, ‘I will ascend above the heights of the cloud, I will liken myself to the Most High’ (Yeshayahu 14:14), to resemble the sun; and this is the whole craving of the nations.” (This is the se’if’s contrast exactly: Israel are the ‘poor’ moon, owning nothing of themselves and awaiting completion from Hashem, while the nations are the self-sufficient sun that ‘imagines it needs nothing.’)
דְּעַל כֵּן הֵם מוֹנִים לַלְּבָנָה וְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לַחַמָּה, שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד זָכָר וְנוּקְבָא

and therefore “they [Israel] reckon by the moon, and the nations by the sun,” which correspond to “male and female.”889R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Bereishis §5): “even though Nisan is first of the months of the moon, and Israel count by the moon.” Exactly the se’if: Israel’s reckoning is fixed to the body that has nothing of its own — and this, not the sun’s self-sufficiency, is the sign of their root.
כִּי כָּל אוּמָּה יֵשׁ לָהּ כֹּחַ מְיוּחָד, וּבְאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ הוּא דּוּגְמַת דְּכוּרָא דְּאִית לָהּ מִגַּרְמָהּ וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל
For each nation has a “particular power,” and in that power it is “like the male, which has of its own and need not receive”;

כִּי כֵּן רָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֹּחוֹת נִפְרָדִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַמַּרְאִים עַצְמָם כְּפִי דִּמְיוֹן עוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְנִפְרָד לְגַמְרֵי, שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ כְּלוּם וְעוֹשֶׂה לְעַצְמוֹ מַה שֶּׁחָפֵץ

for so Hashem willed, that there be “separate powers” which “present themselves,” per the “imagination of this world,” as “utterly separate” — “needing nothing,” and “doing for himself what he wishes.”

אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹי אֶחָד מְיוּחָד בָּזֶה שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם כֹּחַ מֵעַצְמָם כְּלָל, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הֵם בְּתַכְלִית הָעֲנִיּוּת וְהַדַּלּוּת בְּכָל עִנְיָינִים הַנַּפְשִׁיִּים אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרָם

But Israel are “one unique nation” in this: that “they have no power of their own at all,” and thus they are at the “ultimate of poverty” in all “spiritual matters,” “were the Holy One not to help them.”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּסוּכָּה נב ע״א] שֶׁמַּנִּיחַ [יֵצֶר הָרַע] אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וּמִתְגָּרֶה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
And as they said [in Sukkah 52a], that [the evil inclination] “leaves the nations and provokes Israel”;
וְהַיְינוּ דְּהַחִסָּרוֹן דְּ״יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעוּרָיו״ הוּא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹתֵר, שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם כֹּחַ עַצְמָן לְנַצְּחוֹ

that is, the “deficiency” of “the inclination of man’s heart is evil from his youth” (Bereishis 8:21) is “greater in Israel890Bereishis 8:21: after the Flood, God resolves — “לֹא אֹסִף לְקַלֵּל עוֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה בַּעֲבוּר הָאָדָם, כִּי יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו” — “I will not again curse the ground for man’s sake, for the inclination of man’s heart is evil from his youth.” Meforshim: Rashi — “mi-ne’urav” [from his youth]: from the moment the child stirs to emerge into the world, the yetzer hara is set within him. R’ Tzadok’s use: this “evil inclination” presses upon Israel more than the nations — for the yetzer “leaves the nations and provokes Israel” (Sukkah 52a) — precisely because Israel “have no power of their own to defeat it,” and must look to God’s help alone.,” for they “have no power of their own to defeat it.”
אֲבָל נֶגֶד זֶה אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם עֵזֶר אֱלֹקִי, וְכֹחָם הוּא הַמּוֹרִידָם לִשְׁאוֹל תַּחְתִּית
But over against this, the “nations have no divine help,” and “their [own] power is what lowers them to the nethermost pit”;
מֵאַחַר שֶׁסְּבוּרִים שֶׁזֶּהוּ כֹּחָם וְעֹצֶם יָדָם וְנִפְרָדִים מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִמֵּילָא הֵם בְּתַכְלִית הָרִיחוּק מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for since they “think it is their power and the might of their hand,” and are “separated from Hashem,” they are consequently “at the ultimate of distance from Hashem.”
אֲבָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּלֵית לְהוּ מִגַּרְמַיְיהוּ, עֵינֵיהֶם צוֹפוֹת לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

But the Children of Israel, “who have nothing of their own,” “their eyes look to Hashem.”891R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §12): “it is known that the moon has no light of its own, and is a murky body — it only receives the light of the sun… "the face of Moshe was like the face of the sun" — who received the light of his face from Hashem Himself; "the face of Yehoshua like the face of the moon" — who received from Moshe.” Exactly the se’if’s “poor”: to be the moon is not a defect but a station — a body whose whole light is received, and whose glory is that it has none of its own.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר ״אֶל זֶה אַבִּיט אֶל עָנִי״ וְגוֹמֵר, דְּאֵין הַבָּטַת עֵינֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֶלָּא עֲלֵיהֶם מִפְּנֵי עׇנְיָים

And of this it is said, “to this one I look — to the poor” (Yeshayah 66:2)892Yeshayah 66:2: God declares whom He regards — “וְאֶל זֶה אַבִּיט, אֶל עָנִי וּנְכֵה רוּחַ, וְחָרֵד עַל דְּבָרִי” — “but to this one I look: to the poor and broken-spirited, who trembles at My word.” Meforshim: the Radak — of all His creation, God “looks” upon the humble and lowly of spirit, not the mighty. R’ Tzadok’s use: “the gaze of Hashem’s eyes is only upon [Israel], on account of their poverty” — for they own nothing of themselves and their “eyes look only to Him,” unlike the nations, whose self-sufficiency turns their gaze away from Heaven. — that “the gaze of Hashem’s eyes is only upon them, on account of their poverty”;
וְנֶאֱמַר ״דַּלּוֹתִי וְלִי יְהוֹשִׁיעַ״, דְּמִפְּנֵי כֵן לִי יְהוֹשִׁיעַ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֲנִי דַּלָּה וַעֲנִיָּה, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הָאוּמּוֹת

and it says, “I was brought low, and He saved me” (Tehillim 116:6)893Tehillim 116:6: “שֹׁמֵר פְּתָאיִם ה׳, דַּלּוֹתִי וְלִי יְהוֹשִׁיעַ” — “Hashem guards the simple; I was brought low, and He saved me.” Meforshim: Rashi and Radak — because “I was brought low [dalosi]” and had no strength of my own, “He saved me.” R’ Tzadok’s use: “for this very reason He saves me — because I am lowly and poor,” which is not so with the nations; and the Sages read (cf. the Hallel, Pesachim 118b), “even though I am poor in mitzvos, I am Yours, and it befits me to be saved” — for the very “beauty of salvation” is the saving of one who is lowly and in need of it. — “for this reason He will save me: because I am lowly and poor” — which is not so [with] the nations.
וּבִפְסָחִים [קיח:] ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדַּלָּה אֲנִי מֵהַמִּצְווֹת, לְךָ אֲנִי וְלִי נָאֶה לְהוֹשִׁיעַ״
And in Pesachim [118b], “even though I am poor in mitzvos, I am Yours, and it befits me to be saved”;

דְּזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן תּוֹקֶף מַעֲלָתָם, שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַדַּלּוּת הוּא חִסָּרוֹן, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא תּוֹקֶף הַמַּעֲלָה וְתַכְלִית רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא עוֹלָם הַמָּלֵא חִסְרוֹנוֹת

for this too is the “intensity of their elevation”: that although “lowliness is a deficiency,” it is [nonetheless] the “intensity of the elevation” and the “ultimate of Hashem’s will” in this world, “a world full of deficiencies,”
וְרָצָה שֶׁיַּכִּירוּ חִסְרוֹנָם וְשֶׁהוּא הָעוֹזֵר וְהַמּוֹשִׁיעַ
and He “willed that they recognize their deficiency,” and that “He is the Helper and Savior.”

וְעַל יְדֵי הַדַּלּוּת ״לְךָ אֲנִי״, דְּמַכִּיר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם יְשׁוּעָה אֶלָּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כְּמוֹ הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁעֵינֶיהָ נְשׂוּאוֹת לְבַעְלָהּ וְאֵין לָהּ אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁהוּא מַשְׁפִּיעַ
And through the “lowliness,” “I am Yours” — for he “recognizes that he has no salvation except from Hashem,” like “the woman whose eyes are lifted to her husband,” and “has only what he bestows.”
וְעַל כֵּן ״נָאֶה לִי לְהוֹשִׁיעַ״, שֶׁנּוֹי כָּל דָּבָר הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא כְּמוֹת שֶׁהוּא רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת, וְנוֹי הַיְשׁוּעָה כְּשֶׁמּוֹשִׁיעַ לְמִי שֶׁהוּא דַּל וְנִצְרָךְ לְהַיְשׁוּעָה

And therefore “it befits me to be saved” — for the “beauty of everything” is “when it is as it ought to be,” and the “beauty of salvation” is “when one saves the one who is lowly and in need of salvation.”
וְהַתְחָלַת הִתְקָרְבוּת הָאָדָם לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בָּזֶה שֶׁיַּכִּיר עׇנְיוֹ וִיחַכֶּה לַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
And the “beginning of man’s drawing near to Hashem” is in this: that he “recognize his affliction” and “await His service.”
וְזֶהוּ הַתְחָלַת הַהִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַבָּא בְּלֵב הָאָדָם עַל יְדֵי בַּת קוֹל הַיּוֹצֵא בְּכָל יוֹם ״שׁוּבוּ בָּנִים שׁוֹבָבִים״

And this is the “beginning of the arousal” that comes into the heart of man, through the “Heavenly voice that issues each day, ‘Return, wayward children’” (Yirmeyah 3:14)894Yirmeyah 3:14: the call to return — “שׁוּבוּ בָנִים שׁוֹבָבִים נְאֻם ה׳, כִּי אָנֹכִי בָּעַלְתִּי בָכֶם” — “return, O wayward children, says Hashem, for I am your Master.” Background: the Sages teach that a Heavenly voice (bas kol) “issues forth each day” proclaiming, “return, O wayward children” (Chagigah 15a). R’ Tzadok’s use: this daily voice is “the beginning of the arousal that comes into the heart of man” — for God, “seeing into the depths of Israel’s heart,” recognizes their root, “that their eyes look only to Him,” and rouses them “to recognize their affliction and await His service.”Izhbitz-Radzin parallel - Sod Yesharim, Hoshana Rabba 13:2; cf. Yismach Moshe, Re'eh 16:1: Sod Yesharim reads the very name David as a pattern of holy poverty: the dalet signifies 'לית ליה מגרמיה כלום' - that he has nothing of his own - while the vav signifies the explicit bond Hashem illuminates for one who recognizes that nothing is self-generated; remarkably, after all David's victories he still says, 'for I am poor and needy.' The work contrasts this with Gog, whose defining error is to seize strength as self-generated power. This is a striking parallel to R' Tzadok's description of Israel as the moon: their poverty is not spiritual weakness but the truth that all light is received. Precisely that confession can become the source of immense courage, because the person no longer relies on a finite power of his own. Yismach Moshe makes the same point in the practical realm of tzedakah. Even the wealthy giver is fundamentally poor, since no one brought anything into the world; the money destined for the poor was placed in his hands by Hashem, and he is merely the shaliach who transfers it. David could therefore call himself poor while king. Together the sources illuminate the paradox in this se'if: Israel's lack is itself their closeness. 'I am Yours' means that the absence of independent possession turns the eyes upward, making Hashem's salvation not an external rescue but the completion of the very form in which Israel was created. —
דִּרְאִיַּית הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מַכִּיר שׇׁרְשָׁם דְּעֵינֵיהֶם צוֹפִיּוֹת רַק אֵלָיו
for “Hashem’s seeing into the depths of the heart of Israel” — He “recognizes their root,” that “their eyes look only to Him.”
וּבְנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל נָאוֹת דְּלָהֶם נָאֶה לְהוֹשִׁיעַ, וְזֶהוּ הַנּוֹי שֶׁלָּהֶם אֶלָּא שֶׁעֲנִיּוּת הַדַּעַת מְנַוַּולְתָּן
And “the daughters of Israel are comely,” for it “befits them to be saved” — this is “their beauty” — except that “poverty of mind [da’as] disfigures them,”
שֶׁגַּם זֶה מִכְּלַל חִסְרוֹנָם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם כֹּחַ הַמִּתְעוֹרֵר לָזֶה גַּם כֵּן לְהַכִּיר חִסְרוֹנָם וְלִצְפּוֹת לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

for this too is “part of their deficiency”: that they “have no power that arouses” even for this — “to recognize their deficiency and to look to Hashem.” — Israel’s poverty is their very beauty, for it turns their eyes upward; the nations’ self-sufficiency is what dooms them, since one who imagines he needs nothing looks nowhere.

items.h: The theme: The arousal to recognize one’s poverty comes from Hashem, by way of the good inclination, for He sees the heart of Israel — “my heart is awake.” Deepening it, a person sees his distance until he imagines himself hated, which is not true and does not come from His arousal at all. Yet through that very misperception he cries out all the more, and the cry itself arouses His love.

p: [נח] וְהַתְחָלַת הַהִתְעוֹרְרוּת לָזֶה גַּם כֵּן הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי יֵצֶר טוֹב הַנִּיתָּן בָּאָדָם הַמְעוֹרְרוֹ לְטוֹב
And the “beginning of the arousal” for this, too, is “from Hashem” — through the “good inclination” placed in man, “which arouses him to good”;
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הָרְאִיָּה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ ״לֵב״ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל (שהש״ר ה, א) עַל פָּסוּק ״וְלִבִּי עֵר״

and this is through Hashem’s “seeing” the “heart” of Israel, as the Sages said (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:1)895Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2 (the base cites 5:1): On “I sleep, but my heart is awake” (Shir HaShirim 5:2): “The Congregation of Israel said before the Holy One: I sleep from the commandments, but my heart is awake for acts of kindness” — for the Holy One is “the heart of Israel,” as it says (Tehillim 73:26), “the Rock of my heart and my portion.” on the verse “but my heart is awake” (Shir HaShirim 5:2).896R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Pinchas §17): “and what is said in Ra’aya Mehemna,”whoever is not inwardly as he is outwardly, in all his limbs, inner and outer, shall not enter this chamber."" Exactly the se’if: what rouses a person is the point of Hashem within him — “my heart is awake” — and the whole measure is whether the inward and the outward answer to one another.897R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Chayei Sarah §7): “as in the Yerushalmi, "the heart and the eye are the two agents of sin" — as it is written, "give, My son, your heart to Me, and let your eyes guard My ways"; said the Holy One: if you give Me your heart and your eyes, I know that you are Mine.” Exactly the se’if: the arousal begins where Hashem looks — at the heart — and a person’s own sense of distance is measured by an organ God is not using.Izhbitz parallel - Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Yitro 2: The Ishbitzer's explanation of 'Vayishma Yisro' closely parallels R' Tzadok's account of the first stirrings of teshuvah. He says that the initial hearing did not actually originate in Yisro; Hashem sent him that hearing. Yet because Yisro had recognition of Hashem, a powerful desire to cleave to Israel, and the awareness that 'the earth and all it contains belongs to Hashem,' Heaven rewarded him by attributing even the beginning of the hearing to Yisro himself. The source gives a concrete Izhbitz model for the two levels operating in this se'if. The awakening toward good is a gift - the yetzer tov and the bat kol that call the person home. Nevertheless, the human response is real: the person can receive the arousal, deepen it, and turn his desire toward the Source. When he does so, the Divine gift becomes, as it were, his own avodah and receives the name of his act. This also helps define the danger R' Tzadok describes when introspection deepens into the false conclusion 'I am hated.' The true heavenly arousal is the movement toward return; the despairing interpretation is an added human distortion. But because the person continues to cry out rather than sever the bond, even that darkness can become the setting in which the original Divine summons is heard more deeply.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הוּא מִתְעוֹרֵר בִּרְאִיַּית עֵינַיִם גַּם לֵב הָאָדָם מִתְעוֹרֵר לְהַכִּיר עׇנְיוֹ וּלְבַקֵּשׁ אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וִישׁוּעָתוֹ
And when it [the good inclination] is “aroused, by the seeing of the eyes,” “the heart of man” too is “aroused to recognize his affliction,” and “to seek the love of Hashem and His salvation.”

וְכַאֲשֶׁר מוֹסִיף לְהַעֲמִיק בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּתוֹ וּלְהִתְבּוֹנֵן יוֹתֵר בִּדְרָכָיו, רוֹאֶה וּמַכִּיר רִיחוּקוֹ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַד שֶׁחוֹשֵׁב עַצְמוֹ שָׂנוּא וְשָׁלוֹם לִפְנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

And when he “adds to deepen his arousal” and “to contemplate more his ways,” he “sees and recognizes his distance from Hashem,” until he “considers himself hated,” God forbid, “before Hashem.”898R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev §4): “"Israel dwell in distress"… to Knesses Yisrael, "awake, why do You sleep, Hashem" — and this appears, as it were, with Hashem as sleep.” The se’if’s reversal exactly: the man who “considers himself hated” is reading his own dormancy as God’s absence — and Scripture answers by naming the concealment sleep, not hatred.
וְדָבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ מִצַּד הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי דָּבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת כְּלָל
And this matter is “not from the side of Hashem’s arousal,” for “this matter is not true at all”;
וְגַם כִּי מִצַּד הַהַכָּרָה שֶׁהוּא שָׂנוּא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא יָבֹא לְעוֹרְרוֹ, שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִצַּד אַהֲבָה אוֹ מִצַּד רַחְמָנוּת וְהֶעְדֵּר שִׂנְאָה עַל כָּל פָּנִים

and moreover, “from the side of the recognition that he is hated,” Hashem “would not come to arouse him” — for that [arousal] is “from the side of love, or of mercy” and the “absence of hatred,” at any rate.
אֲבָל הוּא מִצַּד תְּפִיסַת הָאָדָם בְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַכִּיר מַעֲמַקָּיו בֶּאֱמֶת
But it is “from the side of man’s [own] self-perception,” that he “does not truly recognize his own depths”;
וּכְפִי הִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ חוֹשֵׁב עַצְמוֹ לְשָׂנוּא וּמְרוּחָק לְגַמְרֵי מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and according to “the revealed [surface] of his heart,” he “considers himself hated and utterly distant from Hashem.”
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְעוֹרֵר יוֹתֵר לִצְעוֹק לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהוֹשִׁיעוֹ וְאֵין סוֹמֵךְ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְעוֹרְרוֹ בְּעַצְמוֹ, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מְעוֹרֵר אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
And through this he is “aroused all the more to cry out to Hashem to save him,” and “does not rely on Hashem’s arousing him of Himself” — and through this he “arouses the love of Hashem.”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּפְסָחִים קיח:] ״אֵימָתַי אֲנִי אֲהוּבָה — כְּשֶׁיִּשְׁמַע קוֹל תַּחֲנוּנַי״
As they said [in Pesachim 118b], “when am I beloved? — When He hears the voice of my supplications.”
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִשְׁתּוֹקֵק לִשְׁמוֹעַ הַקּוֹל ״קוֹל יַעֲקֹב״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״הַשְׁמִיעִנִי אֶת קוֹלֵךְ כִּי קוֹלֵךְ עָרֵב״
For Hashem “longs to hear the voice, ‘the voice of Yaakov,’” as it says, “let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet” (Shir HaShirim 2:14).

וְלָמְדוּ מִזֶּה [בִּבְרָכוֹת כד.]899Berachos 24a: “Shmuel said: a woman’s voice is ervah (nakedness), as it says ‘for your voice is sweet and your appearance comely’ (Shir HaShirim 2:14).” דְּ״קוֹל בְּאִשָּׁה עֶרְוָה״
And they learned from this [Berachos 24a] that “a woman’s voice is ervah [nakedness].”
כִּי הַקּוֹל הוּא יוֹצֵא מִפְּנִימִיּוּת וּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב, וּלְפִי שֶׁאֵין תְּשׁוּקָתָהּ שֶׁל אִשָּׁה אֶלָּא לְבַעְלָהּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּב״ר] עַל פָּסוּק ״וְאֶל אִישֵׁךְ תְּשׁוּקָתֵךְ״

For “the voice issues from the innermost and the depths of the heart,” and since “a woman’s longing is only for her husband,” as they said [in Bereishis Rabbah] on the verse “and your longing shall be for your husband” (Bereishis 3:16)900Bereishis 3:16 (and Bereishis Rabbah 20:7): to Chava, God says — “וְאֶל אִישֵׁךְ תְּשׁוּקָתֵךְ, וְהוּא יִמְשׇׁל בָּךְ” — “and your longing shall be for your husband, and he shall rule over you.” Meforshim: the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah) reads “teshukasech” [your longing] as directed to her husband alone; and the Sages (Avos d’Rabbi Nasan) observe that “all a woman’s conversation” bends toward that single desire. R’ Tzadok’s use: because “a woman’s longing is only for her husband,” her voice — issuing “from the innermost depths of the heart” — arouses his love (whence the Sages derived “kol b’ishah ervah”); and just so, “Israel’s longing is only for the Holy One,” so that their crying voice “arouses His love for them,” and the love that had been hidden is at last revealed. —
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ [בְּאדר״נ] שֶׁכָּל שִׂיחָתָן נִיאוּף, לָכֵן כְּמַיִם הַפָּנִים לַפָּנִים קוֹלָהּ מְעוֹרֵר אַהֲבָה וְתַאֲוָה בְּלֵב הָאִישׁ

therefore they said [in Avos d’Rabbi Nasan] that “all their conversation is [inclined to] immorality” — so that, “as water [reflects] face to face,” “her voice arouses love and desire in the heart of the man.”

וְכֵן אֵין תְּשׁוּקָתָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶלָּא לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, עַל כֵּן קוֹלָם מְעוֹרֵר אַהֲבָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לָהֶם, וְאָז הָאַהֲבָה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁגַּם הָאָדָם אֵין חוֹשֵׁב עַצְמוֹ לְשָׂנוּא

And likewise, “Israel’s longing is only for the Holy One,” and therefore “their voice arouses His love for them” — and then “the love is revealed,” so that “man too no longer considers himself hated.” — the cry itself is what elicits the love: as a face answers a face in water, Israel’s yearning voice draws forth the very love whose absence it had mourned.

items.h: The theme: At first the love was hidden — so Leah, having said “now my husband will love me,” returned to “I am hated”: the deepest concealment appears as its own opposite. It is precisely the cry shaped by that imagined concealment that Hashem “hears” — and so Shimon, the power of hearing, was born. Sight acts and hearing receives, which is why sight appears first at the creation of light, and hearing first with man.

p: [נט] וּמִתְּחִלָּה הָיָה הָאַהֲבָה בְּהֶעְלֵם, עַל כֵּן אַף שֶׁאָמְרָה ״עַתָּה יֶאֱהָבַנִי [אִישִׁי]״ חָזְרָה לוֹמַר כִּי ״שְׂנוּאָה אָנֹכִי״
And “at first the love was concealed”; therefore, even though [Leah] said “now my husband will love me” (Bereishis 29:32), she “went back to say” that “I am hated” (cf. 29:33) —
לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הִרְגִּישָׁה הִתְגַּלּוּת אַהֲבָה, הֲגַם שֶׁיָּלְדָה לוֹ בֵּן, כָּל זֶה חָשְׁבָה כִּי הִיא שְׂנוּאָה בְּתַכְלִית
because she “did not sense a revelation of love”; although she had borne him a son, “all this” she thought that she was “utterly hated.”
וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁל ״עָלְמָא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא״ עַד שֶׁהוּא נִדְמֶה מַמָּשׁ בְּהֵיפֶךְ, וְזֶה גּוֹרֵם שְׁמִיעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צַעֲקַת הָאָדָם כְּפִי דִּמְיוֹנוֹ בְּהֶעְלֵם

And this is the “ultimate of the concealment of the concealed world,” until it “appears literally the opposite” — and this “causes Hashem’s hearing of a person’s cry, according to his imagination, in concealment.”901R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §19): “a cloud screen dividing — this is "a betrothed maiden cried out and there was none to save her," which is the abundance of harlotry that stops up the heart from receiving light.” Exactly the se’if: the cry that seems unheard is not unheard — what stands between is a screen, and the “hearing” of Heaven is precisely what passes through it.Izhbitz-Radzin context - Beit Yaakov on Torah, Vayetzei 63:1: Beit Yaakov identifies Rachel with alma d'isgalya and Leah with alma d'iskasya. Rachel's way is what a person can understand and choose with clarity; Leah represents help that comes 'not by one's knowledge,' in a form whose goodness is not yet visible. He therefore notes that many of Leah's children's defining episodes - Reuven and Bilhah, Yehudah and Tamar, and the path from Yehudah to Malchus Beis David - initially appeared on the surface as matters a person would not willingly choose to enter. Their greatness was disclosed only after Hashem clarified the hidden intention. This is a powerful complement to R' Tzadok's treatment of Leah's 'hatred.' The concealment is so deep that the outer form can seem to say the opposite of the inner love. Yet the point is not that every troubling appearance is secretly good, nor that one may seek such situations. Beit Yaakov stresses that a person naturally wants to walk securely in the revealed good; the hidden mode is what Hashem may send and later clarify. Thus Leah's cry, and Shimon's 'hearing,' belong to a world in which the inner relationship precedes its visible proof. The more the love is hidden, the more the surface can be misread as rejection; the avodah is to cry from within that concealment until the hidden bond becomes audible.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נוֹלַד שִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁבּוֹ כֹּחַ זֶה דִּשְׁמִיעָה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
And through this Shimon was born, in whom is this “power of Hashem’s hearing.”
כִּי הַקּוֹל עַצְמוֹ הוּא נַחֲלַת וּבִרְכַּת יְהוּדָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״שְׁמַע ה׳ קוֹל יְהוּדָה״
For “the voice itself” is the “inheritance and blessing of Yehudah,” as it says, “hear, Hashem, the voice of Yehudah” (Devarim 33:7);
וּבָזֶה נִרְמַז בִּרְכַּת שִׁמְעוֹן כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר רָשִׁ״י [פָּרָשַׁת הַבְּרָכָה (לג, ז)] הַיְינוּ שְׁמִיעַת הַקּוֹל
and in this is “hinted the blessing of Shimon,” as Rashi said [Parashas Vezos HaBrachah, Devarim 33:7] — namely, the “hearing of the voice.”

כִּי הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם ״חֵלֶק אֱלוֹקַּ מִמַּעַל״, שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל הַכֹּחוֹת כּוּלָּם הַמִּתְחַלְּקִים בִּפְרָטֵי הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר ״בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ״

For the souls of Israel are “a portion of God from above,” who is “the Master of all the powers” that “divide among the particular souls of Israel” — of which it is said, “in Our image, according to Our likeness” (Bereishis 1:26)902Bereishis 1:26: at the creation of man — “נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ” — “let us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness.” Meforshim: Rashi — “b’tzalmeinu” [in Our image] means “in the mold prepared for him”; the “image” and “likeness” denote the higher, God-given faculties that set man apart. R’ Tzadok’s use: the souls of Israel are “a portion of God from above,” bearing all His powers; and “tzelem” and “demus” are “male and female” — the “giving powers and the receiving powers,” corresponding to sight (which acts) and hearing (which receives)..
וְיָדוּעַ דְּ״צֶלֶם״ וּ״דְמוּת״ הֵם דְּכַר וְנוּקְבָא, הַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ כֹּחוֹת מַשְׁפִּיעִים וּמְקַבְּלִים, כְּמוֹ רְאִיָּה וּשְׁמִיעָה

And it is known that “tzelem” and “demus” are “male and female” — that is, there are “giving powers and receiving powers,” like sight and hearing.903R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Chalomot §23): “and so of the wisdom that is in the heart it says, "and my heart saw much wisdom" — for what one senses in the heart is as though he sees it with his eyes.” The se’if’s comparison of sight and hearing exactly: in the heart the two faculties converge, so that what is only heard from without is nonetheless seen within.
הָרְאִיָּה הוּא כֹּחַ הָרוֹאֶה, וְיוּכַל לִפְעוֹל גַּם כֵּן בְּכֹחוֹ כַּיָּדוּעַ מִכֹּחַ ״עֵין הָרַע״
Sight is a “power of the beholder,” and “can also act by its power,” as is known from the power of the “evil eye”;
וּמִדָּה טוֹבָה דְּ״עֵין טוֹבָה״ מְרוּבָּה, אֲבָל דָּבָר הַנִּרְאֶה גַּשְׁמִי אֵין פּוֹעֵל בִּרְאִיָּה
and “the good measure of a ‘good eye’ is greater” — but “a physical thing seen does not act upon the sight.”
וְכֹחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה הוּא בְּהֵיפֶךְ, שֶׁהַמַּשְׁמִיעַ פּוֹעֵל בַּשּׁוֹמֵעַ, וְעִיקַּר לְשׁוֹן שְׁמִיעָה הַיְינוּ קַבָּלַת דְּבָרִים וְהוּא כֹּחַ מְקַבֵּל
And the power of hearing is the reverse: “the one heard acts upon the hearer” — and the essential meaning of “hearing” is “receiving of matters,” and it is a “receiving power.”
וְעַל כֵּן בְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית נִזְכַּר רְאִיָּה תֵּיכֶף, בִּבְרִיאַת הָאוֹר נֶאֱמַר ״וַיַּרְא אֱלֹקִים״ וְגוֹמֵר — נֶאֱצַל כֹּחַ הָרְאִיָּה עִמּוֹ, שֶׁהָרְאִיָּה הוּא בָּאוֹר

And therefore, in the Account of Creation, “seeing is mentioned immediately” — at the creation of the light it says, “and God saw” (Bereishis 1:4)904Bereishis 1:4: the first “seeing” in the Torah, at the making of light — “וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב, וַיַּבְדֵּל אֱלֹהִים בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחֹשֶׁךְ” — “and God saw the light, that it was good, and God separated between the light and the darkness.” R’ Tzadok’s use: “seeing is mentioned immediately,” at the creation of the light — “for seeing is in the light”; and sight is a “giving” power that can itself “act” (as in the “evil eye” — and, greater still, the “good eye”), yet it grasps only the revealed surface, unlike hearing, which “receives.” — the power of sight was “emanated with it,” for “seeing is in the light.”
אֲבָל שְׁמִיעָה נִזְכַּר רִאשׁוֹנָה בַּתּוֹרָה בְּאָדָם — ״וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ אֶת קוֹל ה׳ אֱלֹקִים מִתְהַלֵּךְ״ וְגוֹמֵר

But “hearing” is first mentioned in the Torah with man — “and they heard the voice of Hashem God moving about” (Bereishis 3:8)905Bereishis 3:8; Devarim 6:4; Bereishis 3:17: the first “hearing” in the Torah is with man — “וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ אֶת קוֹל ה׳ אֱלֹהִים מִתְהַלֵּךְ בַּגָּן,” “and they heard the voice of Hashem God moving about in the garden” (3:8). Meforshim: the very purpose of hearing is that man “hear the voice of Hashem,” culminating in “שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ,” “Hear O Israel, Hashem is our God” (Devarim 6:4) — Israel the receiver of the Giver’s voice. R’ Tzadok’s use: hearing is the “receiving power”; its corruption began when “the desire ruled over” man, so that he “received the voice of his wife” — “כִּי שָׁמַעְתָּ לְקוֹל אִשְׁתֶּךָ,” “because you listened to the voice of your wife” (3:17) — reversing the order, in which he should receive from God and she from him.,
דְּעִיקַּר יְצִירַת כֹּחַ זֶה הוּא לָאָדָם שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע הַקּוֹל ה׳, וְלִהְיוֹת ״שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ אֱלֹקֵינוּ״ וְגוֹמֵר, שֶׁהוּא הַמְקַבֵּל קוֹל ה׳ הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ

for the “essential creation of this power” is for man, “that he hear the voice of Hashem,” and to be “Hear O Israel, Hashem is our God” (Devarim 6:4) — [Israel being] “the receiver of the voice of Hashem,” the “Giver.”
וְזֶהוּ קוֹל הָרִאשׁוֹן הַנִּזְכָּר בַּתּוֹרָה, כִּי יְצִירַת עִנְיַן הַקּוֹל הָיָה רַק לְהַשְׁמִיעַ לָאָדָם קוֹל ה׳
And this is the “first voice mentioned in the Torah,” for the “creation of the matter of the voice” was “only to convey to man the voice of Hashem”;
וּמִצַּד עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע בּוֹ הָיָה הַתְחָלַת קִלְקוּל הָאָדָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כִּי שָׁמַעְתָּ לְקוֹל אִשְׁתֶּךָ״, שֶׁרַק עַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה הַחֵטְא

and from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, in it was “the beginning of man’s corruption,” as it says, “because you listened to the voice of your wife” (Bereishis 3:17) — for “only through this was the sin.”
וּמַה שֶּׁנּוֹצַר לִהְיוֹת הוּא מְקַבֵּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ מְקַבֶּלֶת מִמֶּנּוּ, עַל יְדֵי הַנְּטִיָּה לְתַאֲוַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הֵיפֶךְ הַסֵּדֶר
And that which was “created” [so] that “he receive from Hashem and his wife receive from him” — through the “inclination to the desire of this world,” [became] “the reverse of the order”:
כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא נִמְשָׁךְ אַחַר הַתַּאֲוֹת הֲרֵי הַתַּאֲוָה מוֹשֶׁלֶת עָלָיו וְהִיא מַשְׁפִּיעַ וְהוּא מְקַבֵּל, וּכְאִשָּׁה מְקַבֵּל לְקוֹל אִשְׁתּוֹ הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ לוֹ
for when he is “drawn after the desires,” the “desire rules over him,” and “she is the giver and he the receiver,” and “like a woman” he “receives the voice of his wife, who bestows upon him.”
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הִקְדִּים רְפוּאָה לְמַכָּה שֶׁהִיא הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁקָּדְמָה לְעוֹלָם
Except that the Holy One “placed the remedy before the blow” — which is “teshuvah, which preceded the world”;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ בָּאָה אֶלָּא אַחַר הַחֵטְא, וְעַל כֵּן שְׁמִיעָה זוֹ בְּקוֹל ה׳ נֶאֱמַר אַחַר הַחֵטְא, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא לְשׁוֹן שְׁמִיעָה הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
and although “it comes only after the sin” — and so this “hearing of the voice of Hashem” is stated after the sin — nonetheless it is the “first expression of hearing in the Torah,”
שֶׁנִּכְתַּב בַּתּוֹרָה קֹדֶם לְשׁוֹן שְׁמִיעָה דְּרַע — ״כִּי שָׁמַעְתָּ [לְקוֹל אִשְׁתֶּךָ]״
for it was “written in the Torah before the expression of hearing [associated with] evil” — “because you listened [to the voice of your wife].”
דְּהָאֱמֶת כְּפִי סֵדֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ תְּשׁוּבָה קָדְמָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה, כִּי תַּכְלִית הַחֵטְא הָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁאַחֲרָיו
For in truth, according to Hashem’s order, “teshuvah preceded in thought,” since the “purpose of the sin” was “for the sake of the teshuvah that follows it.”

וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזֶּה אֵינוֹ מִצַּד הָאָדָם, דְּאַדְּרַבָּא הָאוֹמֵר ״אֶחְטָא וְאָשׁוּב״ אֵין מַסְפִּיקִין בְּיָדוֹ, וְאָדָם הַחוֹטֵא אֵין דַּעְתּוֹ לָשׁוּב, וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַחֵטְא קָדַם בַּתְּחִלָּה, כְּפִי הָאֱמֶת שֶׁבְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַתְּשׁוּבָה קָדְמָה

And even though “this is not from the side of man” — for “one who says ‘I will sin and repent’ is not given the opportunity” (Yoma 85b)906Yoma 85b (Mishnah): “One who says, ‘I will sin and repent, I will sin and repent [echeta va-ashuv]’ — he is not given the opportunity to repent.”, and “the sinner does not intend to repent,” so perforce “in the deed, the sin comes first” — [yet] in truth, “in His thought, the teshuvah preceded.” — in the lived order sin comes first and repentance after; in the Divine order the whole point of the fall was the return, so that teshuvah, though last in time, was first in thought.

items.h: The theme: Teshuvah’s root is in “they hid themselves” — the shame of the sin, of which they said that one who transgresses and is ashamed is forgiven all his sins. It works through hearing: sin brings a hiding of the Face, and a man ashamed to gaze imagines himself hated, yet still merits to hear His voice in Torah and in the words of the Sages. The receiving-power is the root of corruption — yet His willing a receiver is itself that power’s root.

p: [ס] וְשֹׁרֶשׁ הַתְּשׁוּבָה הוּא בְּמִקְרָא זֶה דִּשְׁמִיעַת קוֹל ה׳ ״וַיִּתְחַבְּאוּ״
And the “root of teshuvah” is in this verse of “hearing the voice of Hashem,” “and they hid themselves” (Bereishis 3:8) —

שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר הַתְּשׁוּבָה — הַבּוּשָׁה מֵהַחֵטְא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּרָכוֹת יב:]907Berachos 12b: “Rabbah bar bar Chinnana the Elder said in the name of Rav: whoever commits a transgression and is ashamed of it — all his sins are forgiven him, as it says ‘that you may remember and be ashamed — when I have forgiven you for all that you have done, says Hashem God’ (Yechezkel 16:63).”Chassidic parallel - Sefat Emet, Nitzavim 5:2: The Sefat Emet explains 'you are standing today, all of you' as a permanent truth: the collective of Israel always stands before Hashem, and the work of each individual is to nullify himself into that klal. On this basis he writes that even the wicked can return, because the sin is only a contingent separation from the כלל ישראל and the person can return to his root, 'to the inheritance of my fathers I return.' He then reads 've-hasheivosa el levavecha ... ve-shavta' as returning the holy point that exists in every Jew into the heart and body, where the weight of materiality had covered its light. He adds that teshuvah reaches the Kisei HaKavod because the returning person rectifies not only his own crookedness but awakens a return and straightening through the higher worlds. This gives important context to R' Tzadok's 'shame and hiding.' Shame is not proof that the core has been lost. The person hides because the revealed self no longer matches the holy root, but the very pain of that mismatch testifies that the root remains. Hearing the Divine voice from concealment therefore becomes the first movement of reintegration: the sinner does not manufacture a new soul; he returns the ever-present point to the heart. That is why Chazal can speak of forgiveness through genuine shame - the shame is the soul's recognition that its current exterior is foreign to what it truly is. הָעוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה וּמִתְבַּיֵּישׁ בָּהּ מוֹחֲלִין [לוֹ עַל כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתָיו]
for this is the “essence of teshuvah” — “the shame from the sin,” as they said [Berachos 12b], “one who transgresses a sin and is ashamed of it, they forgive him [all his sins].”
וְזֶה בָּא עַל יְדֵי הַשְּׁמִיעָה, דְּעַל יְדֵי הַחֵטְא הוּא בְּ״הֶסְתֵּר פָּנִים״ וְאֵין זוֹכֶה לִרְאִיָּה דְּ״שִׁוִּיתִי ה׳ לְנֶגְדִּי״ הַמֵּבִיא גַּם כֵּן בּוּשָׁה
And this “comes through hearing,” for through the sin he is in “hiding of the Face,” and “does not merit the seeing of ‘I have set Hashem before me’” (Tehillim 16:8), which also “brings shame”;
וְגַם הָאָדָם עַל יְדֵי הַכָּרַת הַחֵטְא מַסְתִּיר פָּנָיו, כִּי יָרֵא מֵהַבִּיט וּבוֹשֵׁת לְאִסְתַּכּוּלֵי בְּאַפֵּיהּ, וּמִטַּעַם זֶה חוֹשֵׁב כִּי שָׂנוּא הוּא

and man too, through “recognition of the sin,” “hides his face,” for he “fears to look” and is “ashamed to gaze at His face” — and for this reason he “thinks that he is hated.”908R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Purim §4): “"where is Esther alluded to in the Torah? — "and I shall surely hide [haster astir] My face""… that this is the essence of the descent.” Exactly the se’if’s “hiding of the Face”: the concealment that follows sin is not God’s withdrawal but the very verse in which His hiddenness is itself promised — and therefore also the place where He is found.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם זוֹכֶה לִשְׁמִיעַת קוֹל ה׳ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים הַמְעוֹרְרִים בּוּשָׁה בְּלִבּוֹ

But nonetheless he “merits the hearing of the voice of Hashem” in “words of Torah and words of the Sages, which arouse shame in his heart.”909R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Chalomot §24): “for the three [haftaros] of calamity that we read — "Divrei," "Shim’u," "Chazon" — are the reproofs of the prophets, to rectify the blemishes they blemished in speech, in hearing, and in sight — for on account of this was the churban.” Exactly the se’if: shame and its rectification come by way of hearing, because hearing is one of the three channels through which the blemish was made in the first place.
וְלֹא נִכְתַּב תְּחִלָּה שְׁמִיעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה דְּקֹדֶם שֶׁיֶּחְטָא שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ כֹּחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה שֶׁנּוֹצַר בָּאָדָם, כִּי מִיָּד לְצִיווּי רִאשׁוֹן לֹא שָׁמַע

And “the first hearing was not written first” — [the hearing] “before he sinned,” which is the “root of the power of hearing created in man” — for “immediately, to the first command he did not listen”;
דְּבְכֹחַ זֶה הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ כֹּחַ הַקִּלְקוּל, דְּכֹחַ זֶה הוּא עִיקַּר כֹּחַ הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים שֶׁהֵם הַמְקַבְּלִים
for in this power is the “root of the power of corruption” — for this power is the “essential power of the lower [beings],” who are “the receivers.”
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּעַל הַכֹּחוֹת כּוּלָּם, דְּלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹמַר כֹּחַ שֶׁחוּץ מִמֶּנּוּ יִתְבָּרַךְ
Except that Hashem is “the Master of all the powers,” for one “cannot speak of a power outside of Him”;
אֲבָל רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֹּחַ מְקַבֵּל הוּא הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ לְכֹחַ הַמְקַבֵּל, שֶׁהֲרֵי יֵשׁ מְצִיאוּת לְכֹחַ זֶה בִּרְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּי הוּא וּרְצוֹנוֹ חַד
but “His will that there be a receiving power” is the “root of the receiving power,” for “this power has existence in His will,” since “He and His will are one.”

וְהַיְינוּ כֵּיוָן דְּרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִבְרָאִים הַמְקַבְּלִים, וּכְשֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה כֵן הֲרֵי נַעֲשֶׂה רְצוֹנוֹ וְנַחַת רוּחַ הוּא לְפָנָיו, הֲרֵי כִּבְיָכוֹל כְּאִלּוּ הוּא מְקַבֵּל מִנִּבְרָאִים שֶׁהֲרֵי יֵשׁ לוֹ נַחַת רוּחַ מִזֶּה

That is, since Hashem “willed that there be created beings who receive,” and when this is done “His will is done” and “there is satisfaction before Him” — [then,] as it were, “it is as though He receives from the creatures,” since “He has satisfaction from this.”
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל פָּסוּק ״תְּנוּ עֹז לֵאלֹקִים״ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְפַרְנְסִים לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם וּמוֹסִיפִים כֹּחַ בַּפָּמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה

And this is what they said, on the verse “give strength to God” (Tehillim 68:35)910Tehillim 68:35: “תְּנוּ עֹז לֵאלֹהִים, עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל גַּאֲוָתוֹ, וְעֻזּוֹ בַּשְּׁחָקִים” — “give strength to God; over Israel is His majesty, and His strength is in the heavens.” Meforshim: the Midrash (and Zohar) read “tnu oz l’Elokim” as though Israel, by their deeds, “sustain their Father in Heaven” and “add strength to the Heavenly retinue [pamalya shel ma’alah]” — for when the righteous do His will, they “give strength” to the manifestation of His kingship. R’ Tzadok’s use: since God “willed” that there be created beings who receive, the very sustaining of Creation “fulfills His will,” so that, “as it were, He receives from the creatures,” having satisfaction from them — the demus below answering the tzelem above., that “Israel sustain their Father in Heaven” and “add power in the Heavenly retinue” —
כִּי מֵאַחַר שֶׁהָיָה הָרָצוֹן בַּבְּרִיאָה הֲרֵי קִיּוּם הַבְּרִיאָה הוּא מִילּוּי הָרָצוֹן
for since “there was the will in the Creation,” the “sustaining of the Creation” is the “fulfillment of the will.”
אֶלָּא שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַבְּרִיאָה, דְּבֶאֱמֶת ״אִם צָדַקְתָּ מַה תִּתֶּן לוֹ״

Except that this matter is “only from the side of the Creation,” for in truth, “if you are righteous, what do you give Him?” (Iyov 35:7)911Iyov 35:7: Elihu’s words to Iyov — “אִם צָדַקְתָּ מַה תִּתֶּן לוֹ, אוֹ מַה מִיָּדְךָ יִקָּח” — “if you are righteous, what do you give Him? Or what does He take from your hand?” Meforshim: the commentators — a person’s righteousness confers no benefit upon God, who lacks nothing; the whole gain of the mitzvah is the person’s own. R’ Tzadok’s use: Israel’s “sustaining of their Father” holds true “only from the side of the Creation” — from the will God set, that there be receivers; but in absolute truth, “if you are righteous, what do you give Him?” — He needs nothing, and the notion of His “receiving from the creatures” is only “as it were.”.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן ״בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ״, שֶׁהֵם כָּל הַכֹּחוֹת מַשְׁפִּיעִים וּמְקַבְּלִים
And this is the matter of “in Our image, according to Our likeness” — which are “all the powers, giving and receiving.”
וְהַהַשְׁפָּעָה שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר כֹּחַ הָעֶלְיוֹנִים נִקְרָא ״צֶלֶם״, אֲבָל כֹּחַ הַקִּיבּוּל הוּא רַק ״דְמוּת״ וְדִמְיוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּעֶלְיוֹנִים דְּמוּת זֶה גַּם כֵּן וְלֹא בֶּאֱמֶת

And “bestowal,” the “essential power of the upper [beings],” is called “tzelem”; but the “receiving power” is only a “demus [likeness]” and “semblance” — that in the upper [worlds] there is “this likeness” too, but “not in truth.”
אֲבָל בָּאָדָם הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת מִצַּד מַה שֶּׁהוּא מְקַבֵּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
But in man it is “in truth,” from the side of “what he receives from Hashem.”

אֶלָּא שֶׁכֹּחַ זֶה הַנֶּאֱצַל לוֹ מִדְּמוּת שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה, הַיְינוּ כֹּחַ הַקַּבָּלָה מִתַּחְתּוֹנִים, עַל כֵּן נִשְׁרַשׁ בּוֹ כֹּחַ זֶה גַּם כֵּן דְּקַבָּלָה מִשֶּׁלְּמַטָּה הֵימֶנּוּ הָרְאוּיָה לְקַבָּלָתוֹ

Except that this power “emanated to him from the ‘likeness’ above” — namely, the “power of receiving from lower [beings]” — [and] therefore “this power too is rooted in him”: of “receiving from that which is below him,” [that which is] “fitting for his receiving.” — man alone truly “receives,” and this very receiving — fulfilling the Creator’s will that there be receivers — lets Israel, as it were, “sustain their Father,” the demus below answering the tzelem above.

items.h: The theme: This receiving-power is the root of the sin — “hearing the voice of his wife,” taking pleasure in what stands below oneself. But in its root above it is good: the ears of Heaven were opened only for Israel’s need. Receiving does not truly apply Above, yet for Israel’s sake He wrote of Himself as receiving — this is Malchus, which receives from those who crown Him, and therefore “her feet descend to death.”

p: [סא] וְזֶהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ לְכֹחַ הַחֵטְא דִּשְׁמִיעָה לְקוֹל אִשְׁתּוֹ וְקַבָּלַת הֲנָאָה וְנַחַת רוּחַ מִדְּבָרִים הַשְּׁפֵלִים וְשֶׁלְּמַטָּה הֵימֶנּוּ
And this is the “root of the power of the sin” of “hearing the voice of his wife” and “receiving pleasure and satisfaction from lowly things,” and from “that which is below him.”
שֶׁבַּשֹּׁרֶשׁ שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה הוּא טוֹב, דְּזֶהוּ עִיקַּר כֹּחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה דִּלְמַעְלָה לִשְׁמוֹעַ זַעֲקַת הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים
For “in the root above it is good” — for this is the “essential power of the ‘hearing’ above,” “to hear the cry of the lower [beings]”;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּשׁוֹחֵר טוֹב] עַל פָּסוּק ״אָזְנַיִם כָּרִיתָ לִּי״, אֵין אָזְנַיִם שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה כְּרוּיוֹת אֶלָּא לְצוֹרֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל

as they said [in Shocher Tov] on the verse “ears You have dug for me” (Tehillim 40:7)912Tehillim 40:7 (and Midrash Shocher Tov): David sings — “זֶבַח וּמִנְחָה לֹא חָפַצְתָּ, אָזְנַיִם כָּרִיתָ לִּי” — “sacrifice and offering You did not desire; ears You have dug open for me.” Meforshim: the plain sense — God “opened my ears” to hear and obey His word, for obedience is more desired than sacrifice; the Midrash (Shocher Tov) reads it of the “ears above,” that “the ears on high are opened only for the need of Israel.” R’ Tzadok’s use: the “ear” is the “vessel of receiving,” which “in truth does not apply Above at all” — yet “for the sake of Israel,” Hashem “wrote of Himself” as one who receives [their cry]; this is the trait of Malchus, which “receives from those who crown Him,” for “without them there is no place for Malchus,” and hence “her feet descend to death.”, “the ears above are opened only for the need of Israel.”913R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §35): “"peles" is the only one in which little and much are weighed alike, only that the greater weighs more; and this corresponds to the reward of transgressions. "And scales of justice" — scales, in which, when one weighs much, he must place [a counterweight] in the second [pan].” The se’if’s “ears” precisely: the same instrument that receives can be a peles that weighs all alike, or scales in which what is received must be answered from the other side.
כִּי הָאוֹזֶן הוּא כְּלִי הַקִּיבּוּל דְּלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה כְּלָל, אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל הִכְתִּיב הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁהוּא מְקַבֵּל מֵהֶם

For “the ear is the vessel of receiving,” which “does not [really] apply Above at all”; but “for the sake of Israel,” Hashem “wrote of Himself” that “He receives from them.”914R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §29): “the kabbalists wrote that the trait of day is male and the trait of night female; and therefore in the morning [we say] "emes" and in the evening "emunah"… because she receives the light.” Exactly the se’if: the receiving-power is not a defect introduced by the sin — it is a whole side of the created order, and emunah is its proper name.Izhbitz-Radzin parallel - Sod Yesharim, The Eighth Day of Pesach 2:1: Sod Yesharim describes Malchus as 'לית לה מגרמה כלום' - it possesses nothing of its own - and yet calls it the completion in which all the preceding sefirot are included. Its kingship appears from Israel's side when, within the darkness and concealment of this world, they freely crown Hashem instead of saying 'my power and the strength of my hand.' He then takes the thought one step further: even the human power to recognize and crown Hashem must itself be 'tithed' back to Him, for the deepest recognition is that the very capacity of bechirah and acknowledgment was illuminated by Hashem. This exactly complements R' Tzadok's paradox of the receiving-power. Malchus is not an independent recipient standing over against the Giver; its whole identity is reception, and nevertheless the created recipient contributes something genuinely desired - the freely offered coronation that can occur only in a world of concealment. Hence the language of 'receiving' Above is relational rather than a statement of Divine need. Hashem lacks nothing, yet He willed a created order in which Israel's response is meaningful. The same middah therefore has two edges: separated from its Source it becomes the fantasy of autonomous reception and 'her feet descend to death'; returned to its Source, its very emptiness becomes the vessel through which kingship is revealed.
וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת הַמְקַבֶּלֶת מֵאֵת הַמַּמְלִיכִים אוֹתוֹ, דְּלוּלֵי הֵם אֵין מָקוֹם לְמִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת
And this is the “trait of Malchus,” which “receives from those who crown Him” — for “without them, there is no place for the trait of Malchus”;
וְעַל כֵּן ״רַגְלֶיהָ יוֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת״
and therefore “her feet descend to death” (Mishlei 5:5).
רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר, הַיְינוּ מַדְרֵיגוֹת הַתַּחְתּוֹנוֹת הַמִּתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת בַּנִּבְרָאִים, שֶׁבָּהֶם הוּא עֲמִידַת רֶגֶל מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת מַה שֶּׁמַּלְכוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה
That is, [these are] the “lowest rungs, which spread out among the creatures,” in which is “the standing of the ‘foot’ of the trait of Malchus” — [the aspect] whereby “His kingship rules over all”;

כְּשֶׁבָּהֶם מִתְפַּשֵּׁט כֹּחַ חֵשֶׁק זֶה לְקַבֵּל מִתַּחְתּוֹנִים, זֶהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ לְהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בְּכָל מִינֵי רַע דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁכְּלָלוּתָן הַמָּוֶת שֶׁהוּא הַסִּילּוּק וּבִיטּוּל מֵעוֹלָם הַזֶּה

when in them “this power of desire spreads — to receive from lower [beings]” — this is the “root of the sinking into all kinds of evil of this world,” whose “sum is death,” “the removal and nullification from this world” —
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה עוֹנֶשׁ חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
which was “the punishment of the sin of Adam.”
דְּעַל יְדֵי הַשִּׁימּוּשׁ בְּכֹחַ זֶה דְּקַבָּלָה מִתַּחְתּוֹנִים, בִּהְיוֹתוֹ חֵלֶק נִפְרָד מִשׇּׁרְשׁוֹ, יוּכַל לָבוֹא לְפֵירוּד גָּמוּר
For through “the use of this power of receiving from lower [beings],” while it is “a part separated from its root,” it “can come to complete separation”;
וְתַקָּנָתוֹ שֶׁיִּסְתַּלֵּק וְיוּכְלַל בְּשׇׁרְשׁוֹ לְמַעְלָה שֶׁשָּׁם הוּא טוֹב
and its “remedy” is that it “be removed and included in its root above, where it is good.”
וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת ״שְׁכִינָה תַּתָּאָה״, הַיְינוּ שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים בְּפוֹעַל גָּמוּר בְּנִגְלוֹת הַמַּעֲשִׂים כּוּלָּם
And this is the trait of “Shechinah Tata’ah [the lower Shechinah]” — namely, “His Shechinah among the lower [beings],” in “complete actuality,” in “all the revealed deeds.”
אֲבָל ״שְׁכִינְתָּא עִילָּאָה״, הַיְינוּ שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּהַנִּסְתָּרוֹת וּמַעֲמַקִּים, וְהִיא הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁאֵין מִתְגַּלֵּית לְפוֹעַל
But “Shechinta Ila’ah [the upper Shechinah]” — namely, “His Shechinah in the hidden things and depths,” which is “the Binah of the heart, that is not revealed into actuality” —
מִצִּידָהּ הוּא הַתְּשׁוּבָה הַמְהַפֶּכֶת זְדוֹנוֹת לִזְכִיּוֹת
from her side is “the teshuvah that transforms deliberate sins into merits”;
וּדְהַכֹּל הָיָה שְׁמִיעָה בְּקוֹל ה׳, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהַמַּעֲמַקִּים דְּבוּקִים לְעוֹלָם בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הֲרֵי לְעוֹלָם הַחֵלֶק כָּלוּל בְּהַכֹּל

and [she reveals] “that all was [in truth] a ‘hearing of the voice of Hashem’” — for since the “depths forever cleave to Him,” therefore “the part is forever included in the Whole.” — what looks like a sinking into evil is, at its root, the very receiving-power by which Israel “crown” God; teshuvah simply lifts that power back into the source where it was always good.

items.h: The theme: Shimon’s holy root is the “likeness” of Hearing above: though Leah was “hated,” “Hashem heard” — for the hatred is only an outward appearance, hatred as such belonging to the nations. The greater the elevation, the greater the husk set against it, so hearing held the root of evil as well. All the toil of the Avos and Imahos was to rectify Adam’s sin — chiefly Leah’s, since that rectification comes through teshuvah and not through a sinless tzaddik.

p: [סב] וְזֶהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת נֶפֶשׁ שִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ דְּמוּת כֹּחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה
And this is the “root of the holiness of the soul of Shimon,” which is the “root of the ‘likeness’ of the power of hearing above”;
דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁ״שְּׂנוּאָה״, מִכָּל מָקוֹם ״שָׁמַע ה׳״

for even though [Leah was] “hated,” nonetheless “Hashem heard.”915R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos §2): “and of Yaakov it says, "and from Your love with which You loved him"… as it says, "Was not Esav a brother to Yaakov — and I loved Yaakov" — meaning a love without reason, even though Yaakov does, God forbid, as Esav’s deeds.” Exactly the se’if: the “hatred” is only the outward face, for the love that holds Yaakov is not conditioned on his deeds at all.
דְּמַה שֶּׁשְּׂנוּאָה הוּא רַק לְמַרְאִית עֵין הַהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת ״אָהַבְתִּי אֶתְכֶם אָמַר ה׳״

For “her being hated” is only “to the outward eye of the revealed” in this world; but in truth, “I have loved you, says Hashem” (Malachi 1:2),916R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §8): “They are not [outwardly] ‘in order,’ yet with all this they cleave to Hashem. And this is the sense of ‘In what way have You loved us,’ etc. — ‘and I loved Yaakov’ (Malachi 1:2) — without any reason at all, only that ‘this one is Mine and My portion.’” (This grounds the se’if’s reading: since ‘I loved Yaakov’ is a bond beyond all reason, the ‘hatred’ of Leah — ‘and Esav I hated’ — is only an outward appearance, belonging to the nations, never touching Israel, whom ‘Hashem heard.’)Chassidic parallel - Noam Elimelekh, Vayeshev 4:5: R' Elimelech of Lizhensk reads Leah's naming of her first four sons as four levels of the tzaddik. Reuven signifies the beloved 'son' who serves Hashem with love; Shimon is the next, more paradoxical level - a righteous person whose rebuke and truthfulness can make him hated by others, and precisely 'because he is hated' Hashem hears all his prayers, as in 'for Hashem has heard that I am hated.' Whatever one makes of that homiletic structure, its use of Shimon's name is directly relevant here: hatred is not evidence of distance from Hashem; it can coexist with, and even become the setting for, an especially intimate Divine hearing. R' Tzadok radicalizes the point by locating the hatred itself only in the outward appearance and by treating Shimon as the faculty of hearing in Knesses Yisrael. The Noam Elimelech helps show the Chassidic background of that move. 'Hearing' belongs exactly where visible approval is absent. Sight can be reassured by what appears before it; hearing must receive a voice from beyond the immediate surface. Thus Leah's 'ki senuah anochi' does not describe the ultimate relation but the condition in which the relation becomes audible. The higher the root, R' Tzadok says, the stronger the opposing shell; the parallel shows how the concealment of love can itself produce the cry and prayer by which the deeper relation is revealed.
וְלֹא יָרְדָה שִׂנְאָה אֶלָּא לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְאֶת עֵשָׂו שָׂנֵאתִי״

and “hatred descended only to the nations,” as it says, “and Esav I have hated” (Malachi 1:3)917Malachi 1:3: completing the prophet’s paired word — “וְאֶת עֵשָׂו שָׂנֵאתִי, וָאָשִׂים אֶת הָרָיו שְׁמָמָה, וְאֶת נַחֲלָתוֹ לְתַנּוֹת מִדְבָּר” — “and Esav I have hated, and I made his mountains a desolation, and his heritage [a place] for the jackals of the wilderness.” Background: the counterpart to Malachi 1:2 (“I loved Yaakov”) — God’s love for Yaakov set against His rejection of Esav. Meforshim: the Radak and the Sages — the “hatred” is directed only to Esav (the nations), never to the seed of Yaakov. R’ Tzadok’s use: though Leah “appeared hated” to the outward eye, “in truth, I have loved you, says Hashem”; “hatred descended only to the nations” — “and Esav I have hated” — while within Israel’s own root it is only “the deeds of Esav” that are hated; so Leah’s “hatred” is mere surface, concealing a yet greater love..
וְכֵן אֵצֶל שֹׁרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל שְׂנוּאִים מַעֲשֵׂה עֵשָׂו, וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה נִדְמֶה לְשָׂנוּא, כְּטַעַם כָּל הַגָּדוֹל מֵחֲבֵירוֹ יִצְרוֹ גָּדוֹל
And so, “with the root of Israel,” the “deeds of Esav are hated,” and from this side [Leah] “appeared hated” — by the reasoning of “the one greater than his fellow, his drive is greater”;
דִּכְפִי הַמַּעֲלָה כֵּן הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁבַּלֵּב כְּנֶגְדּוֹ הַמַּעֲלִים הַמַּעֲלָה כִּקְלִיפָּה הַסּוֹבֶבֶת לַפְּרִי, דְּ״זֶה לְעוּמַּת זֶה עָשָׂה אֱלֹקִים״

for according to the “elevation,” so the “deficiency in the heart” opposite it, “concealing the elevation,” like the “husk surrounding the fruit,” for “God made this over against that” (Koheles 7:14).
וְכֹחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה שֶׁבּוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ הַטּוֹב מִצַּד שֶׁהוּא אָדָם הַמְקַבֵּל, בּוֹ הָיָה גַּם כֵּן שֹׁרֶשׁ כֹּחַ הָרַע

And the “power of hearing,” in which is the “root of the good” — from the side that it is “man, the receiver” — in it was “also the root of the power of evil.”918R’ Tzadok — parallel (Machshavos Charutz §19): “and there came the quarrel of Kayin and Hevel, until it caused the first murder in the world — for this is the ultimate of hatred of the creatures, to destroy them, the opposite of Hashem’s intent in His world, that "He formed it to be settled" — and this is the root of Esav.” Exactly the se’if: hatred as such belongs to Esav’s root, not to Israel’s — which is why Leah’s “hated” can only be an outward appearance.
וְכָל עֲמַל הָאָבוֹת וְהָאִמָּהוֹת הָיָה לְתַקֵּן חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן כַּיָּדוּעַ, וּבְיִחוּד לֵאָה עֲקֶרֶת הַבַּיִת דְּיַעֲקֹב, כִּי בָּהּ עִיקַּר הַתִּיקּוּן
And “all the toil of the Avos and Imahos was to rectify the sin of Adam,” as is known — and especially Leah, “the mistress of Yaakov’s house,” for “in her is the essential rectification.”

דְּתִיקּוּן הַחֵטְא הוּא עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה וְעַל יְדֵי אֲנָשִׁים שֶׁהֵקִימוּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה — זַרְעָא דְּדָוִד וּמָשִׁיחַ שֶׁהוּא גְּמַר הַתִּיקּוּן, לֹא עַל יְדֵי צַדִּיק גָּמוּר שֶׁלֹּא חָטָא מֵעוֹלָם

For the “rectification of the sin” is “through teshuvah” and through “men who [are] the establishment of teshuvah” — the “seed of David and Mashiach,” which is “the completion of the rectification” — not through “a complete tzaddik who never sinned.”
וּתְחִלַּת הַתִּיקּוּן צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בְּכֹחַ וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּפוֹעַל, וְלֵידַת רְאוּבֵן וְשִׁמְעוֹן הוּא הַתִּיקּוּן שֶׁבְּכֹחַ, וְלֵוִי וִיהוּדָה הוּא בְּפוֹעַל

And the “beginning of the rectification” must be “in potential” and afterward “in actuality”; and the “birth of Reuven and Shimon” is the “rectification in potential,” while “Levi and Yehudah” are “in actuality,”
שֶׁכְּבָר נִסְתַּלֵּק הַשִּׂנְאָה בְּפוֹעַל גַּם כֵּן דְּ״הַפַּעַם יִלָּוֶה״
for [with Levi] “the hatred was already removed in actuality” too — “this time [my husband] will be joined [yilaveh]” (Bereishis 29:34);
וּמִשִּׁבְטוֹ הָיָה עַמּוּד הַתּוֹרָה וְהָעֲבוֹדָה בְּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַתִּיקּוּן בְּפוֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַגְּמַר עַל יְדֵי מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד מִיהוּדָה

and from his [Levi’s] tribe was “the pillar of Torah and service,” in Moshe and Aharon — the “beginning of the rectification in actuality” in this world; and afterward the “completion, through Mashiach ben David, from Yehudah.”
וְהַכֹּחַ הַהַתְחָלָה הוּא בִּרְאוּבֵן שֶׁהוּא הָרְאִיָּה וְהַהַשָּׂגָה ״שִׁוִּיתִי ה׳ לְנֶגְדִּי״, וּמִצִּידוֹ הַתְחָלַת הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה בַּלֵּב

And “the [potential] power, the beginning, is in Reuven” — who is “the seeing and apprehension” of “I have set Hashem before me” — and from his side is “the beginning of the arousal of teshuvah in the heart.”
וְהַגְּמַר כְּשֶׁזָּכְתָה לְהוֹלִיד שִׁמְעוֹן, שֶׁהוֹצִיא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נֶפֶשׁ זֶה חֵלֶק אֱלֹקִי וְכֹחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה דְּמִמַּעַל
And “the completion [in potential]” was “when she merited to bear Shimon” — for Hashem “brought forth this soul,” a “portion of God” and the “power of hearing from above,”
שֶׁכָּל שְׁמִיעוֹתָיו אֵינָן אֶלָּא לְצוֹרֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד הַמַּעֲמַקִּים וְלֹא כְּפִי הַהִתְגַּלּוּת
whose “hearings are only for the need of Israel,” from the side of “the depths,” and “not according to the revealed” —
שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל, דְּאִם כֵּן הָיָה זֶה תִּיקּוּן הַגָּמוּר לְחֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן וּבִלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח

for “this matter is not revealed in this world at all” — for if [it were], “this would be the complete rectification of Adam’s sin,” and “death would be swallowed up forever” (Yeshayah 25:8). — Shimon’s hidden power of hearing is too great for this world to display: its full unveiling would already be the final redemption.

items.h: The theme: The complete rectification, in actuality, comes through Yehudah’s seed; from the depths, though, it is Shimon — which is why his blessing is not given separately but folded into Yehudah’s. Through Shimon comes, in potential, Hashem’s love in the depths, the very opposite of the “hated” appearance. His deficiency is only “we did not listen” — not using his power of hearing where it was fitting.

p: [סג] וְתִיקּוּן הַגָּמוּר הוּא עַל יְדֵי זֶרַע יְהוּדָה שֶׁהוּא הַמְתַקֵּן בְּפוֹעַל
And “the complete rectification” is “through the seed of Yehudah,” who “rectifies in actuality”;
אֲבָל מִצַּד הַמַּעֲמַקִּים הוּא בְּשִׁמְעוֹן, וְעַל כֵּן אֵין בִּרְכָתוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת רַק כְּלוּלָה בְּבִרְכַּת יְהוּדָה, שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא הַהִתְגַּלּוּת וּבְשִׁמְעוֹן הוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם

but “from the side of the depths, it is in Shimon” — and therefore “his blessing is not revealed [separately],” but is “included in the blessing of Yehudah,” for “in him [Yehudah] is the revelation, and in Shimon it is in concealment.”919R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah §25): “that all the holiness of the tribes is found in each and every one, as it says, "each man according to his blessing he blessed them"; and the month of Teves is ascribed to Dan, who is the lowest of the tribes.” Exactly the se’if: a tribe’s blessing being folded into another’s is not its loss — every tribe’s holiness is present in each, so what is unrevealed in one place stands revealed in another.
אֲבָל תְּחִלַּת גְּמַר הַיְשׁוּעָה בְּהֶעְלֵם הוּא בְּכֹחַ, שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ בָּאָה אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמַּעֲמַקִּים הֵיפֶךְ הַדִּמְיוֹן שֶׁהוּא שָׂנוּא

But “the beginning of the completion of the salvation, in concealment,” is “in potential” — for through him “comes Hashem’s love for Israel, in the depths,” the “opposite of the imagination” that he is “hated.”
וְכֵן בְּלִבּוֹ נָטוּעַ אַהֲבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּאֱמֶת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלְּמַרְאִית הָעַיִן שִׂנְאַת יוֹסֵף הִתְחִיל מִמֶּנּוּ, שֶׁהֲרֵי רְאוּבֵן חָשַׁב לְהַצִּילוֹ
And so “in his heart is planted a true love of Israel” — even though “to the outward eye, the hatred of Yosef began from him,” for indeed “Reuven [alone] thought to save him” —
זֶה לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה עֲדַיִין גְּמַר הַתִּיקּוּן בְּפוֹעַל מַמָּשׁ
[and] this is because “the completion of the rectification in actual fact had not yet come.”
וְזֶהוּ הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ בְּמַה שֶּׁמִּצִּידוֹ הַתִּיקּוּן רַק בַּמַּעֲמַקִּים וְלֹא בְּפוֹעַל, וּבְהֶכְרֵחַ מוֹשֵׁךְ חִסָּרוֹן אַחֲרָיו בְּפוֹעַל

And this is “the deficiency in him”: that “from his side the rectification is only in the depths, and not in actuality,” and it “necessarily draws a deficiency after it in actuality.”920R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vaera §9): “and all the women were fenced-in by her merit; Yosef went down to Egypt… and all the males were fenced-in by his merit.” The se’if’s pattern precisely: a rectification that stands in one individual holds for the whole class — which is why the depth-rectification of Shimon need not appear under his own name.
וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר ״וַיֹּאמְרוּ אִישׁ אֶל אָחִיו אֲבָל אֲשֵׁמִים אֲנַחְנוּ״ וְגוֹמֵר ״בְּהִתְחַנְנוֹ [אֵלֵינוּ] וְלֹא שָׁמָעְנוּ״

And therefore it says, “and they said, each man to his brother, ‘indeed we are guilty’ — ‘in his beseeching us, and we did not listen’” (Bereishis 42:21)921Bereishis 42:21: in Egypt, the brothers confess — “וַיֹּאמְרוּ אִישׁ אֶל אָחִיו, אֲבָל אֲשֵׁמִים אֲנַחְנוּ עַל אָחִינוּ, אֲשֶׁר רָאִינוּ צָרַת נַפְשׁוֹ בְּהִתְחַנְנוֹ אֵלֵינוּ וְלֹא שָׁמָעְנוּ” — “and they said, each man to his brother: ’indeed we are guilty concerning our brother, whose anguish we saw when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen.’” Meforshim: Rashi (on Bereishis 37:19) identifies the “each man to his brother” as Shimon and Levi — “brothers in counsel.” R’ Tzadok’s use: Shimon’s whole deficiency is captured in “and we did not listen” — that “he did not use his power of hearing in a place where it was fitting”; never that he would heed the unworthy (that was rather Yosef’s test), for a soul whose strength is the “hearing of a portion of God” cannot listen to what is against His will.Izhbitz-Radzin parallel - Sod Yesharim, Simchat Torah 46:1; Mei HaShiloach, V'Zot HaBerachah 14: Both Radzin texts make explicit the linkage on which this se'if is built. Mei HaShiloach reads 'Shema Hashem kol Yehudah' as containing Shimon's blessing: Reuven is the 'eyes of the Shechinah,' Shimon the 'ears of the Shechinah,' and Yehudah the heart; Shimon must therefore 'hear the voice of Yehudah,' because Shimon's portion always requires clarification. Sod Yesharim expands the idea at length. Sight, it says, takes in the visible surface, while hearing can reach much deeper. Shimon's danger was precisely that he could 'hear' an exceedingly deep and distant Divine intention whose outer garment still looked contrary to the will of Hashem. Yaakov therefore said 'in their secret, let my soul not enter,' not because the depth contained no truth, but because Yaakov sought a path that would also be beautiful and recognizable on the surface. Moshe's repair was to include Shimon within Yehudah: 'Shema Hashem kol Yehudah.' Once the deep hearing of Shimon is joined to Yehudah's revealed heart and kingship, the inner intent becomes visible also in the garment. This is an exceptionally close complement to R' Tzadok's 'we did not listen.' Shimon's tikkun is not to abandon depth for surface, but to use hearing in the correct place and allow the hidden truth to be tested and clothed through Yehudah.;
וְאָמְרוּ ז״ל ״אִישׁ אֶל אָחִיו״ — שִׁמְעוֹן וְלֵוִי, שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ הָעִיקָּר בִּמְכִירָתוֹ
and the Sages said, “‘each man to his brother’ — [this is] Shimon and Levi,” who were “the principal ones in his sale.”
וְשִׁמְעוֹן הַגָּדוֹל הַמַּתְחִיל בַּדָּבָר, דְּבוֹ עִיקַּר הַשִּׂנְאָה לְיוֹסֵף, שֶׁעַל כֵּן בָּחֲרוּ יוֹסֵף מִכּוּלָּם לְאוֹסְרוֹ

And “Shimon, the eldest, [was] the one who began the matter,” for “in him was the essential hatred for Yosef” — which is why “[Yosef] chose Shimon of them all to imprison922Bereishis 42:24: “וַיִּקַּח מֵאִתָּם אֶת שִׁמְעוֹן וַיֶּאֱסֹר אֹתוֹ לְעֵינֵיהֶם” — “and he [Yosef] took Shimon from among them and bound him before their eyes.” Meforshim: Rashi — Yosef singled out Shimon because “he was the one who cast [Yosef] into the pit”; and (another view) to “separate him from Levi,” lest the two together conspire against him. R’ Tzadok’s use: “Shimon, the eldest, began the matter — in him was the essential hatred for Yosef,” his very opposite; for Yosef is wholly “in the revealed and in actuality,” while Shimon’s “whole concern is in the depths,” heeding nothing of the surface — which is why Yosef “chose Shimon of them all to imprison.”” —
כִּי הוּא מַמָּשׁ הֵיפֶךְ יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק בְּאִתְגַּלְיָא וּבְפוֹעַל, וְאֵין מַבִּיט לַמַּעֲמַקִּים, וְהוּא כָּל עֲסָקָיו רַק בַּמַּעֲמַקִּים וְאֵין מַבִּיט לְמַה שֶּׁבְּפוֹעַל

for he is “literally the opposite of Yosef HaTzaddik,” who is “in the revealed and in actuality,” “not looking to the depths”; while [Shimon’s] “concern is only in the depths, and he does not look to what is in actuality.”
וְדָבָר זֶה חִסָּרוֹן, אֲבָל הַחִסָּרוֹן רַק דְּ״לֹא שָׁמָעְנוּ״, שֶׁלֹּא שִׁימֵּשׁ בְּכֹחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה שֶׁלּוֹ בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁהָיָה רָאוּי לְשַׁמֵּשׁ בּוֹ
And this is a “deficiency”; but the deficiency is only “that ‘we did not listen’” — that “he did not use his power of hearing in a place where it was fitting to use it”;
אֲבָל לֹא שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין רָאוּי, שֶׁבָּזֶה הָיָה נִסְיוֹן יוֹסֵף דְּלֹא שָׁמַע אֵלֶיהָ
but not that “he would listen in a place where it is not fitting” — for that was the “test of Yosef,” who “did not listen to her” [Potifar’s wife].
וּגַבֵּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ כְּלָל לְנַסּוֹתוֹ בָּזֶה, כֵּיוָן דְּכֹחוֹ הוּא הַשְּׁמִיעָה דְּחֵלֶק אֱלֹקִי אֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע לְמַה שֶּׁאֵין רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
And “with Shimon it is entirely inapplicable to test him in this” — since “his power is the hearing of a ‘portion of God,’” how is it “possible that he would listen to what is not Hashem’s will”?
רַק אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יְשַׁמֵּשׁ בְּחֶלְקוֹ הַטּוֹב וְלֹא יִשְׁמַע, וּבָזֶה הָיָה נִסְיוֹנוֹ שֶׁלֹּא עָמַד בּוֹ מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא עוֹלָם הַנִּגְלֶה וְאֵין כֹּחוֹ מִתְגַּלֶּה בּוֹ

Only it is “possible that he would not use his good portion, and not listen” — and in this was “his test,” in which “he did not stand,” from the side of “this world, the revealed world,” where “his power is not revealed.”
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא הֶעֱמִיד מֶלֶךְ וְלֹא שׁוֹפֵט, כִּי אֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת לוֹ מֶמְשָׁלָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהַמֶּמְשָׁלָה מִצַּד הִתְגַּלּוּת כֹּחַ הַמְיוּחָד וְהַמַּעֲלָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ

And therefore [Shimon] “produced neither king nor judge,” for “he has no connection to rule in Israel in this world” — for “rule is from the side of the revelation of the particular power and elevation that is in him [each tribe].”

דְּבְכָל שֵׁבֶט יֵשׁ מַעֲלָה מְיוּחֶדֶת, שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר הִיא מִתְגַּלֵּית בְּאֵיזֶה נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִית מֵאוֹתוֹ שֵׁבֶט הוּא מִתְנַשֵּׂא בּוֹ עַל עַם ה׳, וּמַעֲלַת שֵׁבֶט שִׁמְעוֹן אֵין מִתְגַּלֵּית בְּפוֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה

For “in each tribe there is a particular elevation,” which, “when it is revealed in some particular soul of that tribe, he is exalted thereby over the people of Hashem” — and “the elevation of the tribe of Shimon is not revealed in actuality in this world.” — Shimon’s flaw was never that he might heed the unworthy, but that he might fail to heed the worthy; a soul whose whole strength lies in the hidden depths cannot shine in a world of surfaces, and so bears no rule.

items.h: The theme: R’ Akiva told R’ Shimon bar Yochai, “enough that I and your Creator know your power” — for he too was named Shimon, and by tradition was of that tribe, whose power stays hidden in this world. The revealed Talmud records praise of him, but not his supremacy over his peers; even the secrets he disclosed will be grasped only at the end of days. R’ Tzadok suggests this is why the Gemara’s stock name-pair is the otherwise unattested “Yosef ben Shimon.”

p: [סד] וְכַיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי ״דַּיֶּיךָ שֶׁאֲנִי וּבוֹרַאֲךָ יוֹדְעִין כֹּחֶךָ״

And of this kind [is what] Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, “it is enough for you that I and your Creator know your power923R’ Akiva concerning Rashbi: the received tradition that R’ Akiva said of R’ Shimon bar Yochai, “it is enough for you that I and your Creator know your power” — a testimony to Rashbi’s hidden greatness (compare Rashbi’s own words, Sukkah 45b, that he could exempt the whole world from judgment). R’ Tzadok reads it through Rashbi’s name, Shimon: since “we expound names,” and (as he received) the root of his soul was the tribe of Shimon — whose power stays concealed in this world — Rashbi’s supremacy over his colleagues is “not revealed at all in the surface of the revealed Talmud,” known only to his Creator and, by the ruach hakodesh within him, to R’ Akiva.R' Tzadok's broader Rashbi context - Peri Tzadik, Lag BaOmer 1:1: Elsewhere R' Tzadok himself places R' Shimon bar Yochai inside the transmission of Torah shebe'al peh. R' Akiva is the root of Oral Torah, and Rashbi calls his own teachings 'terumah from the terumah of R' Akiva's measures.' R' Tzadok explains that when a master is gathered from the world, his Torah becomes fixed in the hearts of his disciples; this is why Rashbi's passing can be marked as a hillula rather than only as loss.
