R' Tzadok is not erasing the severity of Peor - Pri Tzadik speaks precisely while acknowledging the twenty-four thousand - but distinguishing the historical manifestation from the enduring Jewish root. The phrase 'ben Shimon' is therefore not a legal fiction that makes the past disappear; it is a compressed statement that the child/clarification can disclose what the father's outward history concealed: the covenantal point that was never the essence of the fall.,” [giving] him some connection to the root of his name — nonetheless “the clarification is not in the names Yosef and Shimon [as such].”
רַק לְדוּגְמָא נָקְטוּ מִשְּׁמוֹת הַשְּׁבָטִים, וְיִהְיוּ הַשֵּׁמוֹת אֵיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שֵׁם הַמָּצוּי, דְּהַיְינוּ הַבֵּירוּר הַמָּצוּי בֵּין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
Only “for an example they took from the names of the tribes”; and “let the names be whatever the common name is” — that is, “the clarification common among the Children of Israel” —
לִהְיוֹת עַל יְדֵי זֶה מָצוּי שְׁמוֹת אָב וּבֵן, כִּי הַשֵּׁם הוּא עִיקַּר הַנֶּפֶשׁ וְהַחִיּוּת כַּיָּדוּעַ, רָאוּי לְהַמְשִׁילוֹ וּלְכַנּוֹתוֹ בְּ״יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן״

[for] through this there are “common names of father and son”; for “the name is the essence of the soul and the vitality,” as is known — [so] it is “fitting to liken it and designate it as ‘Yosef ben Shimon.’” — the stock name-pair is chosen not for its frequency but for its meaning: Yosef, the utterly separate, is the ideal “son” to reveal the hidden depths of Shimon, the “father” whose greatness stays concealed.

items.h: The theme: Why the names are not literally common: the clarification is real at the root of the souls, but is not revealed here in fact — even in Gehinnom, Avraham does not recognize one who cohabited with a gentile. This world’s judgment follows a person’s deeds, where choice lies, and not the hidden root revealed in sons. With ordinary sins the Jewish root holds and Avraham saves; this one looks like a departure from Jewishness, so no son emerges here to clarify him.

p: [עא] וְיֵשׁ לְהוֹסִיף דְּמַה שֶּׁאֵין מָצוּי אוֹתָן שֵׁמוֹת בְּפוֹעַל כָּל כָּךְ, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבֵּירוּר זֶה הַיְינוּ מִצַּד שׇׁרְשֵׁי הַנְּפָשׁוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ

And one may add [an explanation] as to why “those names are not so common in fact”: for in truth, even though “this clarification is from the side of the roots of the souls of Israel, in absolute truth,”
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ גָּלוּי מַמָּשׁ בְּפוֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּגֵיהִנָּם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע״ה לֹא מְבַשְׁקַר לֵיהּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּפֶרֶק ב׳ דְּעֵירוּבִין]

nonetheless it is “not literally revealed in fact in this world” — [so much so] that “even in Gehinnom, Avraham Avinu does not recognize him,” as they said [in the second chapter of Eruvin 19a].972Eruvin 19a: On “those who pass through the valley of Bacha” (Tehillim 84:7), the Gemara explains that even one liable at that hour to Gehinnom is raised up and received by Avraham Avinu — “except for an Israelite who cohabited with a gentile woman, [whose sin] drew his foreskin forward, so that Avraham does not recognize him” [Rashi: does not recognize that he is a Jew, for the sin drew his foreskin forward and he resembles one uncircumcised].

דְּכָל זְמַן שִׁימּוּשׁ הַאי עָלְמָא, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ בְּחִירָה וְשָׂכָר וָעוֹנֶשׁ, מִשְׁפַּט עוֹלַם הַנְּשָׁמוֹת הוּא כְּפִי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִצַּד הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת קוֹמַת הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַפּוֹעֶלֶת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁבָּהּ הַבְּחִירָה

For “as long as this world functions,” in which there is “choice, reward, and punishment,” the “judgment of the world of souls is according to a person’s effort in this world” — from “the extension of the ‘stature’ of the soul that acts in this world,” in which is the choice —
וְלֹא עַל פִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם הַמִּתְגַּלֶּה בַּבָּנִים שֶׁאֵין תָּלוּי בַּבְּחִירָה
and “not according to the concealed root, which is revealed in the sons, which does not depend on choice.”

אֶלָּא שֶׁבְּכָל עֲוֹנוֹת דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע״ה מַצִּילָם, הַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּצַּד שֶׁהוּא נִיכָּר עֲדַיִין לְזֶרַע אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע״ה, הַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ יַהֲדוּת גָּמוּר אֵין לֶעָוֹן תְּפִיסָה בּוֹ בְּעֶצֶם רַק כְּהוֹצֵי הַסּוֹבְבִים לְאָסָא

Except that “with all [ordinary] iniquities, Avraham saves them” — that is, from the side that “he is still recognizable as of the seed of Avraham,” that “there is in him a complete root of Jewishness,” [so] “the iniquity has no grip on him in essence,” but only “like the fronds surrounding the myrtle”;
עַל כֵּן עַל יְדֵי הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע״ה נִיצוֹל מִדִּינָהּ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם גַּם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּשֶׁמִּתְגַּלֶּה וּמִתְבָּרֵר שׇׁרְשׁוֹ בִּבְנוֹ

therefore, “through the root of Avraham, he is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom” — even in this world, “when his root is revealed and clarified in his son.”973R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §44): “as they said, that he saw the Shechinah at the Akeidah — and therefore "his eyes dimmed"; for when the spiritual prevails, the bodily is weakened.” The se’if’s “not revealed in fact here” precisely: the clarification is real at the root, and its very reality is what withdraws it from the eye of this world.
אֲבָל בּוֹעֵל אֲרַמִּית שֶׁקְּשׁוּרָה בּוֹ כְּכֶלֶב, כִּי מִצַּד גִּילּוּי הַחֵטְא נִרְאָה כִּיצִיאָה מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת
But “one who cohabits with an Aramean woman,” to whom “he is bound like a dog” — since, “from the side of the revealed [nature of the] sin, it appears as a departure from the root of Jewishness,”

שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵין זֶה רָאוּי שֶׁיֶּאֱרַע לְמִי שֶׁהוּא מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּעַל כֵּן אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע״ה לֹא מְבַשְׁקַר לֵיהּ שֶׁהוּא מִזַּרְעוֹ כְּלָל, וּכְאִלּוּ אֵין בּוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ נֶעֱלָם דְּיַהֲדוּת כְּלָל

for “this is not fitting to befall one of the root of Israel” — therefore “Avraham does not recognize him as of his seed at all,” and “it is as though there is in him no concealed root of Jewishness at all.”974R’ Tzadok — parallel (Resisei Layla §49): “for it has no relation to being in an Israelite body — for the orlah is called only by their name; but nonetheless it is formed together with him, and a person must cut it off.” Exactly the se’if’s distinction: what is foreign to the Jewish root is nevertheless present from birth and must be removed — whereas one in whom there is no such root at all is not in this category at all.
עַל כֵּן אֵין מִתְגַּלֶּה בְּפוֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שׇׁרְשׁוֹ הַנֶּעֱלָם בִּבְנוֹ גַּם כֵּן, דְּאָז הָיָה גַּם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע״ה מַכִּירוֹ בְּשֹׁרְשׁוֹ וּמַצִּילוֹ מִדִּין שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם

Therefore “his concealed root is not revealed in fact in this world in his son either” — for [if it were], “then Avraham too would recognize him by his root and save him from the judgment of Gehinnom.”

אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּצַּד מִשְׁפַּט הַגֵּיהִנָּם בְּגָלוּי דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ אַחַר פְּעוּלַת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ נִיכָּר בָּזֶה, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לִהְיוֹת בֵּירוּר גָּלוּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בִּבְנוֹ גַּם כֵּן

Only that “from the side of the judgment of Gehinnom in the revealed order of this world, which follows the deed,” “the root is not recognizable in this,” [so] “it is impossible for him to have a revealed clarification in this world, in his son either.”

וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ [בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין] דְּעָנְשׁוֹ דְּלֹא יִהְיֶה לוֹ ״עֵר״ בַּחֲכָמִים וּ״בֵן מַגִּישׁ מִנְחָה״, שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ בֵּן הַמְבָרֵר שׇׁרְשׁוֹ וּמְזַכֵּהוּ בְּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים, ״בְּרָא מְזַכֶּה אַבָּא״

And therefore they said [in Sanhedrin 82a] that “his punishment” is that “he shall have no ‘awakened one [er]’ among the sages,” nor “a son who offers a meal-offering” — that “he shall have no son who clarifies his root and grants him merit through good deeds975Sanhedrin 104a (“bra mezakeh abba”): explaining why the Mishnah omits the wicked Amon from the kings with no share in the World to Come (out of honor for his righteous son Yoshiyahu), yet lists Menasheh despite his righteous father Chizkiyahu, the Gemara rules: “the son confers merit upon the father [bra mezakeh abba], but the father does not confer merit upon the son, as it is written, ‘and none delivers from My hand’ (Devarim 32:39) — Avraham does not deliver Yishmael, and Yitzchak does not deliver Esav, from the judgment.” Meforshim: Rashi — a father is credited for having raised a worthy son, but cannot shield an unworthy one from his own judgment. R’ Tzadok’s use: the punishment of the boel aramis is that he has “no son who offers a meal-offering” — no son to “clarify his root and grant him merit,” for “a son grants merit to a father”; his concealed Jewish root, which would otherwise surface in such a son, cannot be revealed in this world’s outward order — though from the side of the hidden Binah it remains entirely intact.,” [in the manner of] “a son grants merit to a father.”976Sanhedrin 82a: On “there shall be no kdeishah of the daughters of Israel” (Devarim 23:18) — applied also to “one who cohabits with a gentile woman” — the verse continues, “may Hashem cut off, from the man who does this, er v’oneh from the tents of Yaakov, and one who offers a meal-offering to Hashem” (Malachi 2:12): “if he is a scholar, he shall have no ‘awakened one [er]’ among the sages, nor one ‘answering [oneh]’ among the students; if he is a Kohen, he shall have no son offering a meal-offering to Hashem.”
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל זֶה מִצַּד הַנִּגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, אֲבָל יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא וְלֹא נִמְנֶה בְּאוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
But nonetheless “all this is from the side of the revealed in this world”; “he does have a share in the World to Come,” and “is not counted among those who have no share in the World to Come,”
כִּי מִצַּד הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב הַנֶּעֱלֶמֶת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אַדְּרַבָּא שׇׁרְשׁוֹ מְבוֹרָר לְגַמְרֵי
for “from the side of the Binah of the heart, concealed in this world,” on the contrary, “his root is entirely clarified.”
וַחֲז״ל דִּבְּרוּ כְּפִי הָאֲמִיתּוּת, וְנָקְטוּ לְמָשָׁל כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא הַבֵּירוּר הַמָּצוּי בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ וְלֹא כְּפִי הַבֵּירוּר הַנִּגְלֶה בָּעוֹלַם הַדִּמְיוֹן

And the Sages “spoke according to the [absolute] truth,” and “took, as an example, [the case] as the clarification truly is, in absolute truth,” and “not according to the clarification revealed in the world of imagination.”
וְכָל דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים מְלֵאִים חָכְמָה גְּדוֹלָה, אִם בְּעִנְיַן הַלִּימּוּד וְהַיְדִיעָה לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם וּמֵבִין מִדַּעְתּוֹ, וְאִם לְעִנְיַן הַהַמְתָּקָה בֶּאֱמֶת

And “all the words of the Sages are full of great wisdom” — whether “in study and knowledge, for a scholar who understands of his own mind,” or “in the matter of ‘sweetening’ [the judgments] in truth”;
כִּי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה יֵשׁ לָהֶם כֹּחַ הַפּוֹעֵל בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת, שֶׁכּוּלָּם מִתְנַהֲגִים עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה הַיּוֹצְאָה מִפִּי חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָאֲמִיתִּים
for “words of Torah have an efficacious power in all the worlds,” which “all conduct themselves according to the Torah that issues from the mouth of the true Sages of Israel.”
וְעַל כֵּן ״לְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים מַרְפֵּא״ וּמַמְתִּיק לְכָל הַדִּינִים עַל פִּי לְשׁוֹנָם לְבַד כִּי כָּל שִׂיחָתָם תּוֹרָה

And therefore “the tongue of the wise heals” (Mishlei 12:18)977Mishlei 12:18: “יֵשׁ בּוֹטֶה כְּמַדְקְרוֹת חָרֶב, וּלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים מַרְפֵּא” — “there is one whose rash speech is like the piercings of a sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Ralbag — reckless words wound like a blade, whereas the measured speech of the wise soothes and heals; the marpei (healing) is set against the madkros charev (sword-thrusts) of careless talk. R’ Tzadok’s use: since “words of Torah have an efficacious power in all the worlds,” which conduct themselves “according to the Torah that issues from the mouth of the true Sages of Israel,” their very expression “heals and sweetens all the judgments” — so that when the Sages framed even the boel aramis by way of the wholesome example “Yosef ben Shimon,” speaking “according to the absolute truth,” they thereby “sweetened the most severe sins of Israel in their root.”Izhbitz-Radzin clarification - Mei HaShiloach Anthology, Siddur 1 (citing Tiferet Yosef, Naso): A short Izhbitz teaching on 'neshamah shenasata bi tehorah hi' gives an especially helpful map for R' Tzadok's distinction between root and revealed judgment. It says that a person contains nefesh, ruach and neshamah; no sin or blemish reaches the neshamah, whereas ruach alludes to the human power of bechirah, through which one can choose good and reject evil. The two statements belong together. The untouched purity of the neshamah is not a reason to deny culpability in the sphere of choice; rather it identifies a deeper point from which return remains possible after choice has gone wrong. That is exactly the balance required by this se'if. R' Tzadok can maintain that the hidden root of a Jew is not defined by the ugliest outward act, while also insisting that the din of this world follows the deed as it emerged through bechirah and that the root may remain unrevealed here. The Izhbitz formulation prevents the doctrine of hidden holiness from becoming an excuse before the act: ruach is specifically the arena in which man must choose. Only afterward can the enduring neshamah explain why even a severe fall does not become the final definition of the Jewish soul. In this sense, the future clarification is a revelation of identity, not a retroactive permission to have violated the revealed will of Hashem., and “sweetens all the judgments” through their expression alone — for “all their conversation is Torah”;
וְנִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁעַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ אֱמֶת שֶׁבָּהּ נִתְגַּלָּה וְנִתְבָּרֵר הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ הוּא כֵן
and “it is clarified that, according to the Torah — of which ‘truth’ is written, and in which the truth is revealed in its absolute truth — it is so.”

וְעַל כֵּן נָקְטוּ גַּם בָּזֶה לְמָשָׁל ״יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן״ כְּפִי הַבֵּירוּר הָאֲמִיתִּי, לְלַמֵּד אַגַּב אוֹרְחָא לְהַבָּאִים לִלְמוֹד, וּלְהַמְתִּיק כָּל חֲטָאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַיּוֹתֵר חֲמוּרִים בְּשָׁרְשָׁן

And therefore they “took, in this [case] too, the example ‘Yosef ben Shimon,’ according to the true clarification” — to “teach in passing, to those who come to learn,” and “to sweeten all the most severe sins of Israel, in their root.” — this world can judge only by deeds, so the gentile-cohabitor seems cut off even from Avraham; yet in the hidden Binah his Jewish root is intact, and the Sages, speaking by that deeper truth, “sweeten” even the gravest sin at its source.

items.h: The theme: Shimon’s root is in fact the opposite — the utmost separation from the peoples — and so he is folded into Yehudah, in whom that separation is complete: “whoever repudiates idolatry is called a Yehudi.” In Shimon it is greater still, which is why he was the zealot who slew Shechem. His essence is hearing, which is pure receiving — the ear being a vessel that takes only what is given it.

p: [עב] וּבֶאֱמֶת עִיקַּר שֹׁרֶשׁ שִׁמְעוֹן הוּא בְּהֵיפֶךְ, תַּכְלִית הַהַבְדָּלָה מִן הָעַמִּים
And in truth, the “essential root of Shimon is the opposite” — the “utmost separation from the peoples”;

דְּעַל כֵּן הוּא נִכְלָל בִּיהוּדָה שֶׁבּוֹ תַּכְלִית הַהַבְדָּלָה, דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָאִים כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל ״יְהוּדִים״, וּבְפֶרֶק קַמָּא דִּמְגִילָּה (יג.) ״דְּכָל הַכּוֹפֵר בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה נִקְרָא יְהוּדִי״

and therefore he is “included in Yehudah,” in whom is the utmost separation — for which reason “all Israel are called ‘Yehudim,’” and in the first chapter of Megillah (13a), “whoever repudiates idolatry is called a Yehudi.”978R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Lech Lecha §4): “as the Sages said,”as long as I have not drunk a quarter of wine my mind is not settled" — but not to become intoxicated, which confuses the mind; but in the blotting out of Amalek [it is otherwise]." Exactly the se’if: Shimon’s separation is folded into Yehudah, in whom it is complete — for the measure is exactly where a thing serves the mind and where it dissolves it, which is the whole difference between Israel and Amalek.
וּבְשִׁמְעוֹן הַהַבְדָּלָה עוֹד יוֹתֵר כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד דְּה׳ בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ וְאֵין עִמּוֹ אֵל נֵכָר
And in Shimon the separation is “even greater,” as it will be in the Future, [when] “Hashem alone will guide him, and there is no foreign god with Him” (Devarim 32:12);
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא עִיקַּר הַמְקַנֵּא עַל עִנְיַן דִּינָה וְהָרַג שְׁכֶם

and therefore he is “the principal zealot” in the matter of Dinah, and “he slew Shechem.”979Bereishis 34 (Shimon and Levi at Shechem): after Shechem son of Chamor defiled Dinah, “the two sons of Yaakov, Shimon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword and came upon the city unawares, and slew every male” (34:25), “and Chamor and Shechem his son they slew by the sword, and took Dinah from Shechem’s house” (34:26); to Yaakov’s rebuke they answered, “should he treat our sister like a harlot?” (34:31). Meforshim: Rashi — they are called “Dinah’s brothers” because they endangered themselves for her; the Ramban weighs at length the justice of the deed; and Yaakov, on his deathbed, still censures their zeal — “Shimon and Levi are brothers, instruments of violence… cursed be their wrath” (Bereishis 49:5–7). R’ Tzadok’s use: Shimon is “the principal zealot [mekane] in the matter of Dinah,” for his very soul-root is “the utmost separation from the peoples” — he could not bear that a daughter of Israel be joined to Shechem the Canaanite; and Levi “joined [nilveh] him,” though Levi’s separateness is “revealed in this world” (Kohanim and Levi’im set apart even from Israel), whereas Shimon’s — the hidden holiness of all Israel’s utter separateness — stays concealed here.
וְנִטְפַּל אֵלָיו לֵוִי שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן ״נִלְוֶה״ לְגַמְרֵי לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְשַׁעְתּוֹ, וְלֹא עָשָׂה כֵן ״כָּל גּוֹי״ דְּאֵין כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם אֶלָּא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל

And Levi “joined him,” who is likewise “wholly joined [nilveh]” to Hashem, for the moment [of that deed] — and “He has not done so for any [other] nation” (Tehillim 147:20), for there are no Kohanim and Levi’im except in Israel.980R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §48): “and Dan is [inclined] to idolatry… and so they were the first to idolatry, in the idol of Michah… and therefore they said, "you have none greater among the tribes than Yehudah, and none lower than Dan."” Exactly the se’if: the repudiation of idolatry is what makes one “a Yehudi,” and the tribes are ranged on precisely that axis — which is why Shimon’s separation is included in Yehudah.
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֶצְלוֹ הוּא רַק מִצִּידוֹ, שֶׁהוּא נִבְדָּל גַּם מִכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּאֵין כּוּלָּם כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם, וְעַל כֵּן מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ גְּלוּיָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
Except that with him [Levi] it is “only from his [own] side,” for “he is separated even from all Israel” (since not all are Kohanim and Levi’im) — and therefore his rung is “revealed in this world.”
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן שִׁמְעוֹן דְּהוּא כְּאֶחָד שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמַדְרֵיגָתוֹ הוּא מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ בְּשֹׁרֶשׁ קְדֻשַּׁת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל
Which is not so [with] Shimon, who is “as one of the [ordinary] tribes of Israel,” and whose rung is “what is in the root of the holiness of all Israel”;

וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּבְדָּלִים כָּל כָּךְ לְגַמְרֵי בְּלִי שׁוּם מְצִיאוּת חִיבּוּר, זֶה אֵינוֹ גָּלוּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁהֲרֵי מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִרְאֶה לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לָבוֹא אֶל הַגּוֹיָה וּלְהִתְחַבֵּר עִמָּהּ

and that “all Israel be so utterly separated, with no possibility of joining [a gentile] at all” — “this is not revealed in this world,” for “from the side of this world it appears to all Israel that it is possible to come upon a gentile woman and join with her.”981R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Tzav §1): “"do not bring me to a trial" — and through this [prideful] thought he came to that deed, as they said, "whoever is haughty is as though he came upon all the forbidden relations"; and afterward his heart was broken within him, in the utmost lowliness.” Exactly the se’if: the deficiency in question is bound to self-exaltation, and the separation that answers it is therefore a lowering — the very posture Shimon’s root supplies.Izhbitz parallel - Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, V'Zot HaBerachah 14: The Ishbitzer makes the Shimon-Yehudah relationship explicit. Reading 'Shema Hashem kol Yehudah' as containing Moshe's otherwise unspoken blessing to Shimon, he describes the twelve tribes as limbs of the Shechinah: Reuven is the eyes, Shimon the ears, and Yehudah the heart, possessing a lev naki u-mevorar. The blessing therefore means that Shimon - the power of hearing - must listen to the voice of Yehudah, because Shimon's portion continually requires birur. This is almost a direct gloss on the architecture of the present se'if. R' Tzadok explains Shimon's deepest root as the capacity for pure receiving, while Yehudah represents the openly recognizable Jewish rejection of avodah zarah and the heart that can give the hidden reception a revealed form. The Ishbitzer shows why those powers must be joined. Hearing reaches what sight does not yet display, but precisely for that reason it can receive a depth whose correct application has not yet been clarified in the visible world. Yehudah's heart becomes the measure by which that hearing is clothed and tested. Thus Shimon's tikkun is not to become less receptive; it is to have his exceptional receptivity pass through a clean, clarified lev. The concealed holiness of Shimon can then emerge as the opposite of assimilation: a faculty that hears only the Divine voice and rejects every alien sovereignty.
אֲבָל שִׁמְעוֹן הוּא מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ כֹּחַ זֶה הַמּוּבְדָּל לְגַמְרֵי, דְּעִיקַּר זֶה הוּא יִחוּד כֹּחַ הַשְּׁמִיעָה לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, דְּעִיקַּר שְׁמִיעָה לְשׁוֹן קַבָּלָה

But Shimon is “from the root of this utterly separated power” — the essence of which is the “concentration of the power of hearing upon Hashem”; for the essential [meaning of] “hearing” is an expression of “receiving,”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּתוּרְגָּם כֵּן כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים שְׁמִיעָה בִּלְשׁוֹן קַבָּלַת דְּבָרִים, כִּי הָאוֹזֶן עָשׂוּי כְּלִי קִיבּוּל, וְזֶהוּ לְקַבֵּל בְּתוֹכוֹ מֵהַזּוּלַת
as [Onkelos] translates “hearing” several times as “receiving of words” — for “the ear is made a vessel of receiving,” and this is “to receive within it from another.”
וְכַאֲשֶׁר אֵין מְקַבֵּל אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁפִּיעַ בָּזֶה הוּא נִבְדָּל לְגַמְרֵי מִבְּנֵי נֵכָר
And when “one receives only what the will of Hashem bestows,” in this “he is utterly separated from strangers” —
דְּזֶהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֵשֶׁת חַיִל הַמּוּבְדֶּלֶת מֵאֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים, שֶׁאֵין מְקַבֶּלֶת אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁדּוֹדָהּ נוֹתֵן לָהּ לֹא זוּלַת זֶה כְּלָל
for this is the “root of Knesses Yisrael,” the “woman of valor, separated from the woman of harlotry,” who “receives only what her Beloved gives her, nothing besides at all.”
וִיהוּדָה שֶׁמָּנוּ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה שֶׁהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִצַּד הַקַּבָּלָה הַנִּגְלֵית בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְעַל כֵּן הֶעֱמִיד מְלָכִים
And Yehudah, from whom [is counted] David HaMelech — the root of Knesses Yisrael — is “from the side of the receiving that is revealed in this world,” and therefore he “established kings.”
וְהַמֶּלֶךְ עִיקָּרוֹ לִהְיוֹת מַשְׁפִּיעַ לָעָם וְהֵם מְקַבְּלִים מִמֶּנּוּ, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם הוּא מְקַבֵּל מֵהֶם, כִּי כָּל מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ הוּא מֵהֶם
And the “king’s essence is to bestow upon the people, and they receive from him”; yet nonetheless he too “receives from them,” for “all that he has is from them,”
וְכֵן עִיקַּר מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ וּכְבוֹדוֹ הוּא מְקַבֵּל מֵהֶם מַה שֶּׁהֵם מַחֲזִיקִים אוֹתוֹ לְמֶלֶךְ
and likewise “the very trait of his kingship and his honor he receives from them” — [namely,] “that they hold him to be king.”
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד דְּבִיקוּת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת, וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה יֵשׁ מְצִיאוּת לְעַמִּים גַּם כֵּן
And this is from “the cleaving of the Children of Israel to His trait of kingship” — which is the trait of Malchus; and from this side “there is existence for the peoples too,”
רַק שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִכְנָעִין לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמְקַבְּלִים מֵהֶם, כִּי יֵשׁ לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִדַּת הַהַשְׁפָּעָה גַּם כֵּן לְזוּלַת וְהַיְינוּ לְעַמִּים הַנַּעֲשִׂים גֵּרִים גְּרוּרִים

only that “they be subordinate to the Children of Israel and receive from them” — for the Children of Israel have “the trait of bestowal, too, upon another,” namely upon “the peoples who become ‘self-attached converts.’”
אֲבָל שֹׁרֶשׁ שִׁמְעוֹן הוּא הַקַּבָּלָה לְבַד שֶׁאֵין מוּכָן לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ כְּלָל, וְעַל כֵּן גַּם כֵּן לֹא הֶעֱמִיד מֶלֶךְ וְשׁוֹפֵט שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מִדַּת הַהַשְׁפָּעָה גַּם כֵּן

But the root of Shimon is “receiving alone,” “not disposed to bestow at all” — and therefore he too “produced neither king nor judge,” in whom there is also the trait of bestowal. — Shimon is pure receiving, Knesses Yisrael taking only from her Beloved; a king, by contrast, both gives and receives — even his crown he receives from the people — so kingship belongs to Yehudah’s revealed line, not to Shimon’s hidden one.

items.h: The theme: All of this — one soul bestowing upon a lesser — belongs to this world alone. In the Future, the “circle-dance for the righteous,” all stand in a circle with no ranks, “no man teaching his fellow,” each receiving equally from Hashem alone. The nations will then have no existence, for they cannot receive from Him directly; and this is precisely Shimon’s power — pure receiving, with nothing of his own.

p: [עג] וְכָל זֶה הוּא הַכֹּל רַק מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דְּיֵשׁ לְאֵיזֶה נֶפֶשׁ הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לְהַקָּטָן מִמֶּנּוּ
And all this is only from the side of this world, where some soul has “elevation,” [such] that it can “bestow upon one lesser than it”;

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לֶעָתִיד כְּשֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה מָחוֹל לַצַּדִּיקִים יִתְגַּלֶּה מַדְרֵיגַת הָעִיגּוּלִים, שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם הַמָּחוֹל שֶׁעוֹמְדִים הַכֹּל בְּעִיגּוּל, לֹא יְהֵא חִילּוּק מַדְרֵיגוֹת וְהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת כְּלָל

which is not so in the Future, [when] “He will make a circle-dance [machol] for the righteous,” [and] the “rung of circles” will be revealed982R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Korach §1): citing the Arizal, R’ Tzadok explains that there are rungs called igulim (circles) and rungs called yosher (straight-line): the world of tohu before creation was igulim, the world of tikkun began with yosher, “and in the Future the aspect of igulim will be revealed as well. And this is the secret of what they said at the end of Taanis — ‘the Holy One will in the Future make a circle-dance [machol] for the tzaddikim’ — for ‘machol’ denotes a circle… and in the aspect of igulim there are no rungs at all, for all are equal, like a circle that has no beginning and no end [ein bo rosh v’sof].” He continues that this was precisely Korach’s error: since at Matan Torah there was a flash of the future tikkun (all hearing “Anochi” directly, “and Hashem in their midst” — He seated among them, they around Him in the circle, with no ranks), Korach claimed “all the congregation are holy… and why then do you exalt yourselves?” — treating the Future’s revealed equality as if it were already fully present, whereas in truth it awaits the Future, and Shabbos is but a taste of it (one-sixtieth of the World to Come). — for wherever there is a “circle-dance,” all “stand in a circle,”983Mei HaShiloach (the Izhbitzer) — parallel (Korach, on “u-madua tisnas’u al kehal Hashem”): R’ Tzadok’s own teacher frames the same idea: “Korach’s claim was that there is no elevation among Israel, of one over his fellow, for ‘Hashem is in their midst’ — that Hashem dwells within all of them equally [shaveh b’shaveh], as is explained in the Gemara (Taanis 31a) that in the Future the Holy One will make a machol for the tzaddikim — and a machol is [danced] in a circle, in which no one is closer [to the center] than his fellow. And [Korach] argued that now, too, it is already so.” The Izhbitzer answers with “a wise king scatters the wicked and turns the wheel [ofan] over them” (Mishlei 20:26): the very crown of Levi that granted Korach his own standing refutes his claim — the equality of the circle is the Future’s, not the present’s. [with] “no distinction of rungs or elevation at all.”984R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §65): “They knew that in the Future ‘they will not teach, each man his fellow’ [lo yilmedu ish es re’eihu] (Yirmeyah 31:33), and this rung would be that ‘the whole congregation, all of them, are holy’ (Bamidbar 16:3); and they thought they had already attained it — for in truth, had the sin not caused otherwise, they would have stood at the rung of the Future.” (This is the se’if’s ‘circle-dance for the righteous’: a rung with no ranks and ‘no man teaching his fellow,’ where ‘the whole congregation, all of them, are holy’ — the levelling of all distinctions that belongs to the Future.)985R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah §22): “and likewise in the Future, when the apprehension of Godliness will be clarified to the eye of all — when all the screens pass away and the truth is revealed.” Exactly the se’if’s circle-dance: ranks belong to a world of screens, and when the screens are gone there is no longer one who bestows and another who receives.

כִּי אָז לֹא יִלְמְדוּ עוֹד אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ וְלֹא יְקַבְּלוּ אֶחָד מֵחֲבֵירוֹ כְּלָל, רַק כּוּלָּם יְקַבְּלוּ בְּשָׁוֶה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְבַד, וְלֹא יִהְיֶה מְצִיאוּת לְכֹחַ הַהַשְׁפָּעָה לְהַזּוּלַת

For then “no longer will each man teach his fellow,” and “none will receive from another986Yirmiyah 31:33 (in some editions 31:34): the prooftext for the circle’s equality — “וְלֹא יְלַמְּדוּ עוֹד אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ וְאִישׁ אֶת אָחִיו לֵאמֹר דְּעוּ אֶת ה’, כִּי כוּלָּם יֵדְעוּ אוֹתִי לְמִקְּטַנָּם וְעַד גְּדוֹלָם” — “and no longer will each man teach his fellow, nor each his brother, saying, ‘Know Hashem,’ for they shall all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Radak — in the Messianic era the knowledge of Hashem will be so direct and universal that no one will need a teacher. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the very “rung of circles” — for then “none will receive from another at all, but all will receive equally from Hashem alone,” with “no existence for the power of bestowal upon another,” and hence no ranks and no elevation of one soul over its fellow. at all”; rather “all will receive equally from Hashem alone,” and “there will be no existence for the power of bestowal upon another.”987R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev §6): “only that the letter mem has also an open mem, which can be spoiled — as afterward, that though the yetzer hara was uprooted, it later returned to its place; and the letter samech indicates as it will be in the Future.” Exactly the se’if: in this world even an uprooting is reversible — the closed circle of the samech, with no opening and no gradation, belongs to the Future alone.Izhbitz-Radzin parallel - Beit Yaakov on Torah, Vayigash 24:5: Beit Yaakov develops precisely the image R' Tzadok uses here for the Future: 'the Holy One will make a machol for the tzaddikim.' A machol, he explains, is a circle, and in a circle there is no first and last and therefore no one stands intrinsically closer than his fellow. He connects this to Krias Shema, in which a person gives over his entire self to Hashem and recognizes that he possesses no independent power; when wisdom is known to have been received from Hashem rather than owned by the recipient, it cannot become a basis for self-exaltation. This complements the se'if's contrast between the ranked order of olam hazeh and the future revelation of igulim. Here, hierarchy is needed because Divine light is received through differentiated vessels - teacher and student, greater and lesser, giver and receiver. The future circle does not deny the distinct histories or avodah of the tzaddikim; it reveals the deeper point in which every one of them is directly turned toward the same Center. That is why R' Tzadok can connect this state specifically with Shimon's faculty of pure hearing. When reception is no longer distorted into a claim of superiority, every soul can hear from Hashem without one person's light becoming a barrier to another. The equality of the circle is therefore not flattening but the disclosure that the Source of every differentiated gift was one all along.
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא יִהְיֶה מְצִיאוּת לַגּוֹיִם גַּם כֵּן, כִּי הֵם אֵין יְכוֹלִים לְקַבֵּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַצְמוֹ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לוֹ, רַק יְכוֹלִים לְקַבֵּל מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
And therefore “there will be no existence for the nations either” — for they “cannot receive from Hashem Himself,” having “no connection to Him,” but “can only receive from the Children of Israel,”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל (שוח״ט כ״א) דְּמָשִׁיחַ יָבוֹא לְלַמֵּד וְלִמְסוֹר אֵיזֶה מִצְווֹת לַגּוֹיִם, וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה יִהְיֶה לוֹ תּוֹאַר מֶלֶךְ
as the Sages said (Shocher Tov 21), that “Mashiach will come to teach and transmit some mitzvos to the nations” — and from this aspect “he will have the title of king.”
אֲבָל לְעוֹלָם הַבָּא דְּאָז ״ה׳ בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ״ לֹא יִהְיֶה לָהֶם מְצִיאוּת כְּלָל, כִּי לֹא יִהְיֶה רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁפִּיעַ וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַבְּלִים
But in the World to Come, [when] “Hashem alone will guide him,” “they will have no existence at all,” for “there will be only Hashem bestowing, and the Children of Israel receiving.”
וְזֶהוּ כֹּחַ שִׁמְעוֹן הַקַּבָּלָה לְבַד, דְּלֵית לֵיהּ מִגַּרְמֵיהּ כְּלוּם, דָּבָר זֶה נִכְלָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בִּיהוּדָה, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ הִתְגַּלּוּת בְּפוֹעַל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ עֲדַיִין
And this is the power of Shimon — “receiving alone,” “having nothing of his own”; this matter is “included, in this world, in Yehudah,” having “no revelation in actuality of its own yet.”
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא נֶעֱלָם מוֹשֵׁךְ אַחֲרָיו חִסָּרוֹן שֶׁנִּרְאֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הֵיפֶךְ מִכֹּחַ זֶה
And from this side — that in this world it is “concealed” — it “draws after it a deficiency” that appears, in this world, as “the opposite of this power”;

וְנִמְצָא אֵין הַחִסָּרוֹן נִמְשָׁךְ בְּעֶצֶם שֹׁרֶשׁ שִׁמְעוֹן כְּלָל, שֶׁהֲרֵי הוּא אַדְּרַבָּא הֵיפֶךְ זֶה, רַק מִצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁל מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִמְשָׁךְ הַחִסָּרוֹן לְמַרְאִית עַיִן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַנִּגְלֶה

so it emerges that “the deficiency does not derive from the essence of Shimon’s root at all” — for he is, on the contrary, “its opposite” — but only “from the side of the concealment of his rung in this world does the deficiency derive, to the outward eye, in this revealed world.”
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לִיכָּתֵב עָלָיו הַחִסָּרוֹן בַּתּוֹרָה, שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵין הַחִסָּרוֹן בּוֹ וּמִצִּידוֹ כְּלָל
And therefore “it was not possible to write the deficiency about him in the Torah,” for “the deficiency is not in him or from his side at all.”
וְנִתְגַּלָּה הַחִסָּרוֹן קוֹדֶם כְּנִיסָה לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הַהִיפּוּךְ מִזֶּה, דְּעִנְיַן אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא הַמְיוּחָד לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד בְּלֹא תַּעֲרוֹבֶת עַמְמִין

And the deficiency “was revealed before the entry into Eretz Yisrael” — for Eretz Yisrael is “the opposite of this,” for the matter of Eretz Yisrael is “that which is unique to Israel alone, without admixture of peoples.”
וְעַל כֵּן הָעוֹלִים בַּתְּחִלָּה לִכְבּוֹשׁ אַחַר מוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, שֶׁהוּא הַכּוֹבֵשׁ מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הַהַגְדָּרָה

And therefore “those who went up first to conquer,” after the death of Yehoshua — who is “the conqueror, of the seed of Yosef,” which is “from the side of ‘boundedness-in’” — for the deficiency laid at Shimon’s door was never his own; it was only the cost of carrying, unrevealed in this world, the very power that in the World to Come will stand highest of all — pure receiving from Hashem with nothing interposed.

items.h: The theme: To the nations’ claim that Israel too are not so “bounded-in,” the answer is “Yehudah shall go up first,” and Yehudah’s word to Shimon, “go up with me in my lot.” The revealed victory comes not through Yosef’s boundedness but through Yehudah’s repudiation of idolatry. Yet the command to leave no root or branch is essentially Shimon’s power — and being unrevealed, it could not be commanded to him directly, so Yehudah included him.

p: [עד] אֲבָל הַנִּשְׁאָר אַחַר כָּךְ, הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁהָיָה לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם טַעֲנָה דְּגַם יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין מוּגְדָּרִים כָּל כָּךְ
But [as for] “what remained afterward” — that is, the “claim” the nations had that “the Israelites too, in this world, are not so bounded-in” —
נֶאֱמַר [בְּרֵישׁ שׁוֹפְטִים] דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָמַר ״יְהוּדָה יַעֲלֶה״ בַּתְּחִלָּה, וִיהוּדָה אָמַר לְשִׁמְעוֹן אָחִיו ״עֲלֵה אִתִּי בְּגוֹרָלִי״

it is stated [at the beginning of Shoftim] that Hashem said, “Yehudah shall go up” first988Shoftim 1:2–3: “after the death of Yehoshua,” when Israel asked who should go up first against the Canaanite, “Hashem said: Yehudah shall go up; behold, I have given the land into his hand” (1:2); “and Yehudah said to Shimon his brother: Go up with me in my lot, and let us fight the Canaanite, and I too will go with you in your lot; and Shimon went with him” (1:3). Meforshim: Rashi and the Radak — Shimon’s territory lay within Yehudah’s portion, so the two conquered together; and (the Midrash) Yehudah, whom Shimon accompanied, later repaid him. R’ Tzadok’s use: the revealed victory over the nations comes by Yehudah’s way — “repudiation of idolatry” — so “Yehudah is the first, fit for this”; but the command to leave no survivor (utter non-connection) is essentially Shimon’s power, and since Shimon’s rung is hidden, the command could not fall on him explicitly — so Yehudah “included him,” saying “I too will go with you,” the revealed carrying the hidden., and Yehudah said to Shimon his brother, “go up with me in my lot” (Shoftim 1:2–3).

כִּי מִצַּד הַגִּילּוּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁמִּצִּידוֹ הַנִּיצּוּחַ לָאוּמּוֹת לֹא דֶּרֶךְ הַגְדָּרָה מֵעֲרָיוֹת כְּיוֹסֵף רַק דֶּרֶךְ כְּפִירָה בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כִּיהוּדָה, יְהוּדָה הוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן וְהָעִיקָּר הָרָאוּי לְכָךְ

For from the side of “the revealed in this world,” through which is the “victory over the nations” — “not by way of ‘boundedness-in’ from immorality, like Yosef, but by way of ‘repudiation of idolatry,’ like Yehudah” — “Yehudah is the first and the principal one fit for this.”989R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §13): “but when it is not so — then even though he is fenced-in from envy, desire and honor, this is as though he were not fenced-in, and as though he possessed envy, desire and honor, which drive a person [from the world].” Exactly the se’if: the nations’ claim rests on the outward fence alone, and an outward fence without its root is reckoned as no fence — which is why the revealed victory must come from Yehudah, with Shimon in his lot.
אֶלָּא דְּשָׁם נִצְטַוּוּ ״לֹא תְחַיֶּה כָּל נְשָׁמָה״, שֶׁלֹּא יַשְׁאִירוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ וְעָנָף, כִּי אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת וְחִיבּוּר עִמָּהֶם, דָּבָר זֶה הָעִיקָּר הוּא כֹּחַ שִׁמְעוֹן

Except that there [in the conquest] they were commanded, “you shall not let any soul live” (Devarim 20:16)990Devarim 20:16: of the seven Canaanite nations the Torah commands, “רַק מֵעָרֵי הָעַמִּים הָאֵלֶּה… לֹא תְחַיֶּה כָּל נְשָׁמָה” — “only from the cities of these peoples… you shall let no soul live.” Meforshim: Rashi — they must be utterly destroyed, with no treaty and no survivor, “so that they not teach you to do like all their abominations” (Devarim 20:18). R’ Tzadok’s use: “that they leave no root or branch, for they have no connection or joining with them” — this utter separation is “the power of Shimon,” whose soul-root is the total separateness of Israel from the peoples; it surfaced in the conquest, though (being unrevealed) it was folded into Yehudah’s explicit command rather than commanded to Shimon by name. — “that they leave no root or branch,” for “they have no connection or joining with them” — [and] this matter is essentially “the power of Shimon.”

אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין גָּלוּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, עַל כֵּן לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לָבוֹא צִיווּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עָלָיו בְּפֵירוּשׁ, רַק יְהוּדָה כְּלָלוֹ עִמּוֹ, כִּי הֵם כְּלוּלִים יַחַד שֶׁיְּהוּדָה הוּא הַנִּגְלוֹת וְשִׁמְעוֹן הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת

Except that it is “not revealed in this world,” so it was “impossible for Hashem’s command to fall upon him explicitly”; only “Yehudah included him with himself,” for “they are included together” — Yehudah being “the revealed” and Shimon “the hidden.”991R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §12): “for from the element of earth come sloth and sadness and anger and envy.” The se’if’s division of labor exactly: the traits that must be conquered have a material root, and it is therefore the revealed tribe that must go up first — the hidden power alone cannot win a battle fought in matter.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר לוֹ ״וְהָלַכְתִּי גַם אֲנִי אִתָּךְ״, כִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן לֹא יָכוֹל לְנַצֵּחַ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת
And therefore [Yehudah] said to him, “and I too will go with you” (Shoftim 1:3) — for “Shimon by himself, too, could not achieve victory in the revealed [world].”
[וְעַל כֵּן הַשֵּׁם שִׁמְעוֹן הָיָה מָצוּי בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל, הַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַמַּעֲלָה שֶׁבְּשֹׁרֶשׁ שֵׁם זֶה
[And therefore the name “Shimon” was common in Eretz Yisrael, as I wrote above — from the side of the “elevation” in the root of this name;

אֲבָל בְּבָבֶל מָצוּי הַשֵּׁם יוֹסֵף, כִּי כֹּחַ הַהַגְדָּרָה צָרִיךְ לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בּוֹ הָעִיקָּר בִּהְיוֹתָן בֵּין הָעַמִּים לְבַל יִתְעָרְבוּ בַּגּוֹיִם וְיִלְמוֹד מִמַּעֲשֵׂיהֶם, וְזֶהוּ כָּל כֹּחַ יוֹסֵף בִּהְיוֹתוֹ לְעֶבֶד נִמְכָּר בֵּין הַמִּצְרִים שְׁטוּפֵי זִימָּה]

but in Bavel the name “Yosef” is common, for the “power of boundedness-in” must be used chiefly “while they are among the peoples,” lest they “mingle with the nations and learn from their deeds” — and this is the whole power of Yosef, in his being “sold as a slave among the Egyptians, steeped in lewdness.”]
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא הָיָה כְּבִישַׁת הָאָרֶץ עַל יָדוֹ בְּפוֹעַל, רַק בְּכֹחַ הוּא נִכְלָל בִּיהוּדָה שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ לְגַמְרֵי אַחַר מוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עַד דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה

And therefore “the conquest of the Land was not through him [Shimon] in actuality” — only “in potential he is included in Yehudah,” the “essential conqueror,” entirely, after the death of Yehoshua until David HaMelech.
וּבִימֵי שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה דְּקָיְימָא בְּאַשְׁלְמוּתָא, גַּם כֵּן ״דָּבַק לְאַהֲבָה״ בִּבְנוֹת גּוֹיִם
And in the days of Shlomo HaMelech, when “[Malchus] stood in its fullness,” he too “clung, in love,” to gentile women.
אֲבָל עַל זֶה אָמְרוּ [בִּיבָמוֹת] ״אֲנַן מִשְּׁלֹמֹה נֵיקוּ וְנִגְמוֹר״
But concerning this they said [in Yevamos 76b], “shall we stand and rule [in halachah] from Shlomo?!”
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אָז לֹא הָיָה שַׁיָּיכוּת לְחֵטְא זֶה דֶּרֶךְ חֵטְא בְּפוֹעַל, אֲבָל הוּא לֹא נָסִיב, רַק שֶׁכְּפִי מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ הֶחֱשִׁיבוּ זֶה לְחֵטְא וְהַטָּיַת הַלֵּב דְּ״הִטּוּ אֶת לְבָבוֹ״

for in truth, “then there was no relation to this sin as an actual sin” — “he did not [really] marry” [them] — only that, “according to his [lofty] rung, they reckoned this a sin,” and a “turning of the heart,” [in] “they turned away his heart” (I Melachim 11:3);992Yevamos 76b: Rav Pappa said, “shall we arise and derive [halachah] from Shlomo?!” Shlomo did not [truly] marry the foreign women [for the sake of marriage], but only “clung to them in love,” as it is written, “of the nations concerning which Hashem said — you shall not intermarry with them — Shlomo clung to them in love” (I Melachim 11:2). The apparent difficulty from “vayischaten” [“and he intermarried,” I Melachim 3:1] is resolved: out of the great love he bore them, Scripture regards it as though he had intermarried in Hashem [i.e., only in love, not in true marriage].Further Chassidic context - Bnei Yissaschar, Tamuz and Av 1:9:2: The Bnei Yissaschar builds an extended teaching on the very verse R' Tzadok invokes: 'Yehudah said to Shimon his brother: ascend with me in my lot... and I too will go with you in your lot' (Shoftim 1:3). In his scheme of the months, Nisan belongs to Yehudah and Av to Shimon. Nisan already bears the revealed character of redemption, while Av is, in the present order, the month in which that good is hidden and waits to be reversed. He therefore reads Yehudah's invitation as a prophetic joining of the two lots: in the earlier redemptions Shimon's future good is carried within Yehudah's revealed geulah, while in the ultimate redemption even the month of Shimon will be transformed into joy and Yehudah will, as it were, enter Shimon's lot. This does not duplicate R' Tzadok's particular explanation of the conquest; it adds a striking Chassidic afterlife to the same textual pairing. In R' Tzadok, Yehudah goes first because the revealed rejection of avodah zarah must lead, yet the complete uprooting of the nations' root is identified with Shimon's deeper hidden power. Bnei Yissaschar similarly treats their partnership as a union of revealed redemption with a good that is still concealed. The verse thus becomes a pattern: Yehudah gives Shimon's hidden strength a historical entrance, and Shimon's eventual clarification reveals a deeper redemption within Yehudah's first ascent.
דַּיְיקָא לֵב כְּמוֹתוֹ הַדָּבוּק לְגַמְרֵי בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כַּאֲשֶׁר הֶרְאָה בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים שֶׁשָּׁר בְּרוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ הַנּוֹבֵעַ מִלִּבּוֹ, נֶחְשַׁב גַּם זֶה לְהַטָּיָה

[for] precisely “a heart like his,” entirely cleaving to Hashem — as he showed in Shir HaShirim, which he sang “by ruach hakodesh welling from his heart” — even “this [slightest inclination] was reckoned a ‘turning.’” — measured against an ordinary man it was no sin at all; only a heart so wholly wedded to Hashem could have even its faintest leaning toward another counted a betrayal.

items.h: The theme: Before entering a high rung come trials that hold a person back — as in creation itself, “first darkness, then light,” the gloom before dawn being the deepest. Hence the deed of Shittim before entering the Land, and the foreign wives at the return from Bavel, each followed at once by light. The entry came through Yehoshua, of Yosef — for inheriting the Land turns on guarding the bris, and “your people are all righteous.”

p: [עה] אֲבָל קוֹדֶם הַכְּנִיסָה הָיָה חֵטְא בְּפוֹעַל, כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּקוֹדֶם כְּנִיסָה לְאֵיזֶה מַדְרֵיגָה יֵשׁ נִסְיוֹנוֹת הָרוֹצִים לְעַכֵּב בְּיָדוֹ

But “before the entry there was a sin in fact,” as is known, that “before entering some rung, there are trials that seek to hold [one] back”;993R’ Tzadok — parallel (Tzidkas HaTzadik §4): “He derives from the creation of the world, regarding the acceptance of the yoke of Heaven, that ‘first there is darkness’ [berisha chashucha] — one must accept the yoke of Heaven even from within the darkness, the folly, and the absence of [good] deeds; and then, in the end, he will fulfill it in ‘wealth and the light of day’ — the clear apprehension through which the deed is [afterward] drawn forth.” (Exactly the se’if’s pattern — ‘first darkness, then light’: the trials that hold a person back before a high rung are the built-in ‘darkness’ of creation, from within which the yoke must be accepted before the light can come.)

וְהוּא כִּבְרִיּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם לִהְיוֹת ״בְּרֵישׁ חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא״, וְהַקַּדְרוּתָא דְּצַפְרָא שֶׁקּוֹדֶם הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר הַבָּהִיר הוּא חֹשֶׁךְ הַיּוֹתֵר עָצוּם, וְעַל כֵּן אָז הָיָה מַעֲשֵׂה דְּשִׁטִּים

and this is “like the creation of the world” — “first darkness, and then light”994Shabbos 77b: R’ Zeira, finding R’ Yehuda in a cheerful mood and ready to answer questions about the natural world, asked him, “why do the goats walk at the head of the flock and the ewes follow?” He answered, “it is as in the creation of the world, which at first was dark and afterward light [b’reisha choshocha v’hadar nehora]” — the (dark) goats precede the (white) ewes, just as in creation the darkness of “and there was evening” preceded the light of “and there was morning.” Meforshim: Rashi — such is the order of the world, darkness first and light following. R’ Tzadok’s use: so too “before entering some rung there are trials that seek to hold one back,” for the order of ascent mirrors the order of creation — “first darkness, then light,” and “the gloom of dawn that precedes the shining light is the most intense darkness”; hence the deed of Shittim came just before entering the Land, and the foreign-wives stumble at the return to the Land in Bavel — each at once followed by the light.; and the “gloom of dawn” that precedes the shining light is the “most intense darkness” — and therefore then [before entering Eretz Yisrael] there was the “deed of Shittim.”995R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §5): “when a person goes from light into darkness, at first he does not see; but if he sits there some time, he sees… and one who is always in a place of darkness sees in it quite well.” Exactly the se’if: the trial that precedes a rung is not an obstruction placed before the light but the eye’s necessary adjustment — the deepest dark is the hour before dawn.
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ בְּגָלוּת בָּבֶל בִּשְׁעַת כְּנִיסָה לָאָרֶץ נִכְשְׁלוּ בְּחֵטְא זֶה וְשָׁבוּ, וְאָז נִגְלָה תֵּיכֶף הַנְּהוֹרָא שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד חֹשֶׁךְ זֶה

And likewise, in the Babylonian exile, “at the time of entering the Land,” they “stumbled in this sin” [of foreign wives] and “returned [from it]” — and then “the light was immediately revealed,” which is over against this darkness.996R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash §5): “as it says, "for a righteous man falls seven times and rises" — and this is that there are seven falls, through which he is clarified.” Exactly the se’if: the “deed of Shittim” before entering the Land is not an interruption of the ascent but one of its stages — the falling is what does the clarifying.
וְהַכְּנִיסָה לָאָרֶץ הָיָה אָז עַל יְדֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן נוּן, כִּי יוֹסֵף הוּא מַמָּשׁ הֵיפֶךְ זֶה, וְעִיקַּר נַחֲלַת הָאָרֶץ הוּא עַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית

And “the entry into the Land was then through Yehoshua bin Nun” [of Yosef] — for Yosef is “literally the opposite of this” — and the essence of “the inheritance of the Land is through the guarding of the bris,”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְעַמֵּךְ כּוּלָּם צַדִּיקִים לְעוֹלָם יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ״, אֶלָּא שֶׁעִם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלָּם כֵּן
as it says, “and your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever” (Yeshayah 60:21) — [teaching] that all the people of Israel are so [righteous].
וְהָרְאָיָה יְהוּדָה שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ הֲרֵי בּוֹ נִמְצָא הַחֵטְא דְּעֵר וְאוֹנָן שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ צַדִּיקִים וְנִקְרָא רַע, אֶלָּא שֶׁכָּל זֶה אֵינוֹ בַּשֹּׁרֶשׁ בֶּאֱמֶת
And the proof: Yehudah, “the essential conqueror” — behold, in him is found the sin of “Er and Onan,” “the opposite of righteous,” “called evil” — except that “all this is not in the root, in truth.”
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא [סַנְהֶדְרִין מד רע״א] ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא — יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא״, דִּקְדֻשַּׁת שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל אִי אֶפְשָׁר לֵיעָקֵר מִמֶּנּוּ אַף אִם יַרְבֶּה חֲטָאִים עַד לְמַעְלָה

In the manner it is stated [Sanhedrin 44a], “even though he has sinned, he is [still] a Jew” — for “the holiness of the name Israel cannot be uprooted from him,” even if “he multiply sins to the heights.”

וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא שָׁם בְּעָכָן דְּעָבַר עַל כָּל חֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיעַ הַחֵטְא כָּל כָּךְ לַעֲקוֹר עֶצֶם הַיַּהֲדוּת וְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהוּא הַקְּדֻשָּׁה שֶׁבְּשֹׁרֶשׁ כָּל אִישׁ יְהוּדִי מוֹרָשָׁה מֵאָבוֹת וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ ע״ה, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְשַׁנּוֹת הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ

And as it is stated there, regarding Achan, “who transgressed all five books of the Torah” — nonetheless, “the sin cannot reach so far as to uproot the essence of Jewishness and the name Israel,” which is “the holiness in the root of every Jew, a heritage from the Avos and Yaakov” — and “it is impossible to change the root.”
וְאַף שֶׁמַּרְבֶּה חֲטָאִים, הוּא הַכֹּל מִצַּד ״הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה״ וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת הַמַּקִּיפִים לְשֹׁרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת
And even though he multiplies sins, it is “all from the side of the ‘leaven in the dough’” and “the subjugation to [foreign] kingdoms,” which “surround the root of Jewishness”;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא [בְּרָכוֹת יז.] ״גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ [לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנְךָ]״ כו׳
as it is stated [Berachos 17a], “it is revealed and known [before You] that our will is to do Your will”
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה בָּרַמְבָּ״ם [סוֹף פ״ב מֵהִלְכוֹת גֵּירוּשִׁין] בְּטַעַם ״כּוֹפִין [אוֹתוֹ] עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר רוֹצֶה אֲנִי״, עַיֵּין שָׁם

And in this vein is the Rambam [end of ch. 2 of Hilchos Gerushin] on the reason for “we compel him until he says ‘I want to’” — see there.997Rambam, Hilchos Gerushin 2:20: “One whom the law requires to divorce his wife, and who refuses — a Jewish court, in every place and time, beats him until he says ‘I want to,’ and he writes the get, and it is valid.” Why is it not void as coerced? “For we call [an act] ‘coerced’ only [when] one is pressed to do a thing he is not obligated in by the Torah — but one whose evil inclination has overpowered him to nullify a mitzvah or commit a transgression, and who is beaten until he does what he is obligated to do — this is not coerced by [others]; rather he coerced himself by his own evil intent” — for at his core his will is to be a Jew and fulfill the mitzvos.Chassidic background - Kedushat Levi, Likutim 113: R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev interprets Chazal's 'beresha chashokha vehadar nehora' - first darkness and then light - as a basic order of avodas Hashem. Yirah is the gate and beginning; after a person has labored to place yiras Shamayim upon his face, ahavah can follow, and from that love a still more inward yirah can later be born. Darkness here is therefore not a sanctification of failure but the constricted first stage through which a larger illumination becomes receivable. That distinction fits R' Tzadok's rule in this se'if that before a higher rung there is a nisayon that appears as its opposite. Shittim before entry into Eretz Yisrael, or the dangerous admixture surrounding a later elevation, is the spiritual analogue of the created order in which evening precedes morning. The trial exposes whether the coming light can be carried without being captured by its counterfeit. Kedushat Levi is especially useful here because he formulates the sequence prospectively as avodah - fear, self-discipline and purification precede love. R' Tzadok's retrospective observation that darkness often precedes a new revelation should therefore not be read as permission to manufacture a fall. The Chassidic parallel instead describes the darkness as the narrow gate of preparation: a place where the opposite power is confronted and bounded so that the subsequent light can emerge as a true acquisition rather than an untested inspiration.
וְעַל כֵּן הִמְשִׁילוּ [שָׁם בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין] לְאָסָא דְּקָאֵי בֵּינֵי חִילְפֵי, כִּי הַחֲטָאִים הֵם רַק כְּחִילְפֵי הַסּוֹבְבִים לְאָסָא, אֲבָל עֶצֶם הָאָסָא לֹא נִשְׁתַּנָּה

And therefore they compared [there in Sanhedrin] [Israel] to “a myrtle standing among thorns [chilfei]” — for “the sins are only like the thorns surrounding the myrtle,” but “the essence of the myrtle is unchanged.” — the Jew’s sins are the surrounding thornbush — exile’s pressure and the “leaven in the dough” — while the fragrant myrtle at the center, his bond to God, is never so much as touched.

items.h: The theme: So too the title “tzaddik”: all Israel are called by it, their sins being only the thorns around the rose, never touching its essence. The nations are “black in essence,” their souls sunk wholly in worldly desire and knowing no other vitality. Hence they are uncircumcised in essence, while Israel are only “uncircumcised of heart” — the name Israel pertaining to a holiness of soul that cannot be severed.

p: [עו] וְכָךְ לְעִנְיַן תּוֹאַר צַדִּיק כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים כֵּן וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי [רֵישׁ סִימָן זֶה], וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחוֹטְאִים וּפוֹגְמִים בַּבְּרִית בְּפוֹעַל, הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַחִילְפֵי וְהַחוֹחִים הַסּוֹבְבִים אֶת הַשּׁוֹשַׁנָּה, אֲבָל אֵינוֹ נוֹגֵעַ בְּעֶצֶם הָאָסָא וְהַשּׁוֹשַׁנָּה

And so, with regard to the title “tzaddik,” all Israel are called thus, as I wrote [at the start of this siman]; and even though they “sin and blemish the bris in fact,” it is only “from the side of the thorns [chilfei] and the briars surrounding the rose,” but “does not touch the essence of the myrtle and the rose.”998R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Shemos §5): "“the reapers of the field” — the reapers who cut away all the thorns and briars that surround the supernal rose." Exactly the se’if: “your people are all tzaddikim” in truth, and the sins that seem to disfigure them are only the thorns encircling the rose — cut away, never part of it.999R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev §7): “one needs at least an arousal from below, in prayer, to request His help against the yetzer that seeks to kill him and cannot prevail over him — and then Hashem helps him with an arousal from Above; and this is indicated by the letter samech: "Hashem supports [somech] all the fallen."” Exactly the se’if: the sins are the thorns and not the rose, for the yetzer “seeks and cannot prevail” — it never reaches the essence, and the falling itself is met with support.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא [בְּשהש״ר] עַל פָּסוּק ״שֶׁשְּׁזָפַתְנִי הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ״, דְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שְׁחוֹרִים בְּעֶצֶם

In the manner it is stated [in Shir HaShirim Rabbah] on the verse “for the sun has gazed upon me [and darkened me]” (Shir HaShirim 1:6) — that “the nations of the world are black in essence.”1000Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:6: On “for the sun has gazed upon me,” a parable: a townswoman had a Kushite maidservant who said, “tomorrow my master will divorce his wife and marry me,” “for he [once] saw her hands blackened.” Her companion answered, “fool! if for his beloved wife, whose hands were blackened for an hour, [you imagine] he would divorce her — you, blackened from your mother’s womb, all the more so!” So the nations taunt Israel, “this nation exchanged its glory” (Tehillim 106:20); Israel reply, “if we, enslaved but briefly, were [so] penalized, you all the more” — and further, “we are like a prince whose face darkened in the desert sun, [but] with a little water his body whitens and returns to its beauty; whereas you are blackened from your mother’s womb,” for even in the womb [the gentile fetus] worshipped idols with its mother.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּהֵם שׇׁרְשָׁם כְּרַע וְעֶצֶם נַפְשָׁם שָׁקוּעַ רַק בְּתַאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁזֶּה כָּל חִיּוּתָם
That is, “their root is like [that of] evil,” and “the essence of their soul is sunk only in the desires of this world,” which is “their whole vitality”;

וְאִם לֹא יִהְיֶה לָהֶם מִילּוּי תַּאֲוָותָם לָמָּה לָהֶם חַיִּים, כִּי אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם הַרְגָּשַׁת וְהַשָּׂגַת חִיּוּת אַחֶרֶת אֶלָּא חִיּוּת הַגּוּפָנִי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְאֵין מַשִּׂיג עוֹנֶג אַחֵר אֶלָּא עִינוּגֵי הַתַּאֲווֹת הַגּוּפָנִיּוֹת

and “if they had no fulfillment of their desires, why would they [want] life?” — for “they have no sensation or apprehension of any vitality except the bodily vitality of this world,” and “attain no pleasure except the delights of the bodily desires.”1001R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Bereishis §15): “and the letter nun is an expression of falling, as it says [Berachos 4a] that nun was not said in Ashrei because it contains their downfall… "she has fallen and shall not rise again" — and the letter samech supports them.” The se’if’s rose exactly: what falls in Israel is answered immediately by a supporting letter, because the fall was never in the essence.
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמַר בַּר שֵׁישָׁךְ לְרָבָא [ע״ז סה.] ״אִית לְכוּ כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא לְעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי״

Therefore Bar Sheishach said to Rava [Avodah Zarah 65a], “do you have the like of this in the World to Come?”1002Avodah Zarah 65a: Rava brought a gift to Bar Sheishach on his festival, knowing he was no idolater. He found him “sitting up to his neck in rosewater, with harlots standing before him.” Bar Sheishach said, “have you the like of this in your World to Come?” Rava replied, “ours is finer than this — for upon you [gentiles] there is the dread of the government, while upon us there will be no dread of any government.” As Bar Sheishach was summoned away by the king, he cursed, “may the eye that wishes to see your harm burst”; Rava answered “Amen” — and Bar Sheishach’s eye burst. —
שֶׁהוּא נַחֲלַת הַצַּדִּיקִים הַפְּרוּשִׁים וּמְרוּחָקִים מִתַּאֲווֹת, וּמַה בֶּצַע לָהֶם מִתִּקּוּנָם לְהַשִּׂיג עַל יְדֵי זֶה הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
which is “the inheritance of the righteous, abstinent and distanced from desires” — [Bar Sheishach reasoning:] "what profit is there in their self-refinement, to attain thereby the World to Come,
וּמַה עוֹנֶג יוּכְלוּ לְהַשִּׂיג שָׁם אִם אֵין לָהֶם עִינוּגֵי הַתַּאֲווֹת הָאֵלּוּ שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ, כִּי הוּא לֹא הִשִּׂיג כְּלָל עוֹנֶג אַחֵר
and what pleasure could they attain there, if they lack these delights of desire that he had?" — for “he attained no other pleasure at all.”

וְעַל כֵּן כָּל הַגּוֹיִם עֲרֵלִים בְּעֶצֶם, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כָּל בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל עַרְלֵי לֵב, מִצַּד מִשְׁכַּן הַיֵּצֶר שָׁם עַל מִפְתְּחֵי הַלֵּב מִנְּעוּרָיו, לֹא עַרְלֵי בָּשָׂר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עֶצֶם הַגּוּף בְּפוֹעַל רַע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם

And therefore “all the nations are uncircumcised in essence”; not so all the House of Israel, who are [only] “uncircumcised of heart” — from the “dwelling of the [evil] inclination there, at the entrances of the heart, from his youth” — “not uncircumcised of flesh,” [such] that “the very body would in fact be evil,” God forbid.
וְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא לְעִנְיַן קְדֻשַּׁת עֶצֶם הַנֶּפֶשׁ
And the name “Israel” pertains to “the holiness of the very soul.”
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא גָּלוּי בְּפוֹעַל גָּמוּר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מֵעֵת שֶׁנִּבְחֲרוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעַם מְיוּחָד, דְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין נִיתָּק מֵהֶם עוֹד מִצַּד שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשָׁם

And this matter is “revealed in complete actuality in this world, from the time the Children of Israel were chosen as a distinct people” — for “the name Israel is no longer severed from them, by virtue of the root of their soul.”

כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מֵחֶדֶר אַחֵר מֵהַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [תּוֹסָפוֹת ע״ז ה.]1003Tosafos, Avodah Zarah 5a: R’ Tzadok cites Tosafos here for the point that the souls of Israel derive from a different — higher — “chamber” than the souls of the nations of the world., וְאֵין לְנֶפֶשׁ זֶה שַׁיָּיכוּת וְחִיבּוּר כְּלָל עִם הַנֶּפֶשׁ דְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם

For “the root of the souls of the Children of Israel is from another chamber than the souls of the nations,” as Tosafos said [Avodah Zarah 5a], and “this soul has no connection or joining at all with the soul of the nations.”
וְעַל כֵּן אֲפִילּוּ הֵמִיר לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יֵשׁ לוֹ כָּל דִּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעִנְיַן קִידּוּשִׁין וְגֵירוּשִׁין וְכַיּוֹצֵא
And therefore, “even if he apostatized to idolatry, he has the full status of a Jew” regarding kiddushin and gittin and the like —
כִּי קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּנַפְשׁוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּבָר נִתְבָּרְרָה עַל יְדֵי גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם, דְּמֵאָז נִבְחֲרוּ לְגוֹי אֶחָד בָּאָרֶץ
for “the holiness of Israel in the souls of the Children of Israel was already clarified through the Egyptian exile” — for from then they were “chosen as one nation in the land.”

אֲבָל הַשֵּׁם ״צַדִּיק״ הוּא לְעִנְיַן קְדֻשַּׁת הַגּוּף הַבְּשָׂרִי, כִּי גַּם הַגּוּפוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשׁוּנִים מִגּוּפוֹת דְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מִלֵּידָה מִבֶּטֶן וְהֵרָיוֹן, זֶה בְּשַׂר קֹדֶשׁ וְזֶה בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹרִים

But the name “tzaddik” pertains to “the holiness of the fleshly body” — for “the bodies of the Children of Israel, too, differ from the bodies of the nations, from birth, from womb and conception”: “this is holy flesh, and that is the flesh of donkeys.”1004Yechezkel 23:20: in the prophet’s parable of the two sisters Oholah (Shomron) and Oholivah (Yerushalayim), who lusted after Egypt and Assyria, it is said of the paramours — “אֲשֶׁר בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹרִים בְּשָׂרָם וְזִרְמַת סוּסִים זִרְמָתָם” — “whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys, and whose issue is like the issue of horses.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Radak — the verse marks the coarse, animal grossness of the gentile nations (here Egypt), likened to “the flesh of donkeys.” R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the source for “this is holy flesh [besar kodesh], and that is the flesh of donkeys” — that the very bodies of the Children of Israel differ in essence from the bodies of the nations “from birth, from womb and conception”; and since the title “tzaddik” pertains to the holiness of the body, it is rooted in this intrinsic difference — a holiness “not yet revealed in actuality,” while the wicked are still “blackened.”
וְדָבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ גָּלוּי עֲדַיִין בְּפוֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁהֲרֵי יֵשׁ עֲדַיִין רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֵין עֲלֵיהֶם שֵׁם צַדִּיק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And this matter “is not yet revealed in actuality in this world,” for “there are still wicked ones of Israel upon whom the name ‘tzaddik’ does not [rest] in this world”;
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁהֵם שְׁזוּפִים וּשְׁחוֹרִים עַל זֶה אָמַר ״הֲלוֹא כִּבְנֵי כּוּשִׁיִּים אַתֶּם לִי״ וְגוֹמֵר

and as long as “they are sunburnt and blackened,” concerning this it said, “are you not as the children of the Kushites to Me?” (Amos 9:7)1005Amos 9:7: “הֲלוֹא כִבְנֵי כֻשִׁיִּים אַתֶּם לִי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נְאֻם ה’” — “are you not like the children of the Kushites to Me, O Children of Israel? says Hashem” — the verse continuing, “did I not bring up Israel from the land of Egypt…?” Meforshim (plain sense): Rashi — when Israel sin, they make themselves, as it were, “like the Kushites” (dark) before Me; yet the very next words affirm that God redeemed them from Egypt and His bond to them endures. R’ Tzadok’s use: as long as the wicked of Israel remain “sunburnt and blackened,” the title “tzaddik” — the holiness of the body — does not yet rest upon them in this world; and he cites the received reading (see the following note) that the verse’s “Kushite” blackness is the blemish of the bris.Chassidic parallel - Likutei Moharan 14:3:6: R' Nachman states the root-point of this se'if with unusual directness: even the poshei Yisrael, so long as the name Yisrael is still said of them, remain Israel - 'af al pi shechata, Yisrael hu.' Precisely because they are still called 'sinners of Israel,' he says, they retain an achizah and shoresh in the supernal thought; an illumination from that root can reach the sinner and awaken teshuvah. This closely complements R' Tzadok's image of the thorn surrounding the rose. The sin is real - the person is called a poshe'a - but it does not become the ontological root from which the name Yisrael flows. The enduring root is what makes return possible rather than what makes repentance unnecessary. R' Tzadok pushes the same distinction into his discussion of the body and the bris: the outward blackening can be severe enough that the title tzaddik is not manifest in this world, yet the blemish remains a covering rather than the ultimate substance of Knesses Yisrael. Likutei Moharan helps state the logic of that claim without minimizing judgment: illumination comes from a root above the fall and summons the person back to it. The permanent Jewish name is therefore not a declaration that the deed was harmless; it is the theological reason that the deed need never be the final word about who the sinner is..
וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּמִקְרָא זֶה נֶאֱמַר עַל פְּגַם הַבְּרִית, שֶׁהַשָּׁמוּר בּוֹ נִקְרָא ״יְפֵה תוֹאַר וִיפֵה מַרְאֶה״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּיוֹסֵף

And I heard that this verse is said about1006From the Ishbitzer (Mei HaShiloach): the reading R’ Tzadok “heard” — applying this verse to the “blemish of the covenant” (pgam ha-bris) — is a teaching of his rebbe, R’ Mordechai Yosef of Izhbitz (see §8 above). “the blemish of the bris” — for one “guarded in it” is called “of fair form and fair appearance,” as is said of Yosef (Bereishis 39:6);
וְכֵן בְּכָל מָקוֹם בַּמִּקְרָא וּבְדִבְרֵי רַז״ל הַיּוֹפִי וְהַכִּיעוּר הוּא בִּקְדֻשַּׁת הַבְּרִית, שֶׁזֶּהוּ יוֹפִי הַבָּשָׂר אָדָם וְהַגּוּף

and so everywhere in Scripture and in the words of the Sages, “beauty” and “ugliness” refer to “the holiness of the bris” — for this is the “beauty of the flesh, the man, and the body.” — so the two names divide the labor between them: “Israel” already proclaims the soul’s unbreakable holiness, while “tzaddik,” the holiness of the body, still awaits the slow clarification of exile.

items.h: The theme: This verse is the haftarah of Kedoshim, which speaks of the holiness of the bris — “wherever you find a fence against immorality, you find holiness.” All Israel are holy; only outwardly are they “like the children of Kushites,” washed clean with a little water. This whole exile serves to clarify the holiness of Israel’s bodies — “and not a pebble shall fall to the ground,” for no spark is lost.

p: [עז] וּמִקְרָא זֶה הוּא הַהַפְטָרָה פָּרָשַׁת קְדוֹשִׁים הַמְדַבֶּרֶת בִּקְדֻשַּׁת הַבְּרִית, שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר הַקְּדֻשָּׁה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ״כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא גֶּדֶר עֶרְוָה אַתָּה מוֹצֵא קְדֻשָּׁה״

And this verse [Amos 9] is the haftarah of Parashas Kedoshim, which “speaks of the holiness of the bris” — the essence of holiness, as they said, “wherever you find a ‘fence against immorality,’ you find holiness” (Vayikra Rabbah 24).1007R’ Tzadok — parallel (Yisrael Kedoshim §1): “The essence of holiness is the holiness of the covenant [kedushas ha-bris], as they said in Vayikra Rabbah (24): ‘every place you find a fence against immorality [geder ervah], you find holiness’; as R’ Yehudah ben Pazi said, ‘anyone who fences himself from immorality is called holy.’” (This is the se’if’s reading of the Kedoshim haftarah: the holiness for which all Israel are called ‘holy’ is precisely the holiness of the bris — ‘wherever you find a fence against immorality, you find holiness.’)1008R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Kedoshim §2): “and afterward [the serpent] came upon Chavah and cast filth into her; and from this Adam HaRishon became one drawn in his foreskin… and [Scripture] opens "Kedoshim."” Exactly the se’if: the portion of Kedoshim opens precisely where the blemish of the bris was introduced — which is why “wherever you find a fence against immorality, you find holiness.”
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים הֵם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּפֶרֶק רע״ק וּבְפ״ק דְּחוּלִּין] ״יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים הֵם״, וְנֶאֱמַר ״קֹדֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל לַה׳״ וְגוֹמֵר

For in truth “all Israel are holy,” as they said [in Perek R’ Akiva and the first chapter of Chullin], “Israel are holy,” and it says, “Israel is holy to Hashem” (Yirmeyah 2:3)1009Yirmeyah 2:3: “קֹדֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל לַה’, רֵאשִׁית תְּבוּאָתֹה, כָּל אֹכְלָיו יֶאְשָׁמוּ, רָעָה תָּבֹא אֲלֵיהֶם” — “Israel is holy to Hashem, the first of His produce; all who consume them will bear guilt, evil will befall them.” Meforshim: Rashi — Israel is God’s own consecrated portion, like terumah or the first-fruits, so that the nations who “consume” (harm) them are held guilty. R’ Tzadok’s use: the prooftext that “in truth all Israel are holy” — their essential holiness is inviolable, and any nation that presumes upon them is punished..
וְרַק לְמַרְאִית עַיִן הֵם כִּבְנֵי כּוּשִׁים בְּ״כ״ הַדִּמְיוֹן עַל יְדֵי שְׁזִיפַת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ, וּבִמְעַט רִיחוּץ מִתְרַחֲצִים, רַק כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִתְרַחֲצוּ דּוֹמִים לִבְנֵי כּוּשִׁים

And only “to the outward eye” are they “like [k’, the kaf of comparison] the children of the Kushites,” through the “sunburn”; and “with a little washing they are washed [clean]” — only “as long as they have not [yet] washed do they resemble the children of the Kushites.”1010R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Purim §2): “as it says in Tikunei Zohar, that the Holy One covered Esther with His own letter, for she is His holiness — and this is that Esther too was of the aspect of Yosef the Tzaddik.” Exactly the se’if: the holiness at issue is the holiness of the bris, whose bearer is Yosef — and one who stands in it is “covered” by Him even while outwardly exposed.
וְהַשִּׁפְחָה הַכּוּשִׁית חוֹשֶׁבֶת לְהִתְדַּמּוֹת לָהּ וְלִירַשׁ גְּבִירְתָּהּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
And the “Kushite maidservant thinks to resemble her [the mistress] and to inherit her mistress’s [place],” God forbid.
וְעַל זֶה הוּא כָּל גָּלוּת זֶה, לְבָרֵר קְדֻשַּׁת הַגּוּפוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּקְרָאִים כּוּלָּם צַדִּיקִים
And for this is “all this exile” — “to clarify the holiness of the bodies of the Children of Israel, who are all called tzaddikim,”
וְכִדְמְסַיֵּים הַמִּקְרָא דְּשָׁם ״וַהֲנִיעוֹתִי [בְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם אֶת בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל]״ וְגוֹמֵר ״וְלֹא יִפּוֹל צְרוֹר אָרֶץ״

as the verse there concludes, “and I will shake [the house of Israel among all the nations] — and not a pebble shall fall to the ground” (Amos 9:9)1011Amos 9:9: the prophet’s closing vision — “כִּי הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּה וַהֲנִעוֹתִי בְכָל הַגּוֹיִם אֶת בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל, כַּאֲשֶׁר יִנּוֹעַ בַּכְּבָרָה, וְלֹא יִפּוֹל צְרוֹר אָרֶץ” — “for behold, I command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations, as [grain] is shaken in a sieve, yet not a pebble shall fall to the ground.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Radak — like a sieve that retains the kernels while only dust and chaff fall through, Israel is sifted among the nations, yet no worthy one is lost. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is the assurance that in all the scattering “no spark is lost” — the ingathering gathers even the scattered sparks (of “wasted seed”) from the four corners, so that “not even one pebble falls to the ground, and no outcast is banished from Him.”.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין שָׁם אֲפִילּוּ צְרוֹר אֶחָד שֶׁיִּפּוֹל לָאָרֶץ וְלֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ שׁוּם נִדָּח
For in truth “there is not even one ‘pebble’ that falls to the ground,” and “no outcast is banished from Him” (cf. II Shmuel 14:14).

כַּיָּדוּעַ בְּסוֹד ״וְקַבְּצֵנוּ יַחַד מֵאַרְבַּע כַּנְפוֹת״ כו׳, מְרוּמָּז הַשֵּׁם הַמְיוּחָד לִקְבִיצַת הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר קִיבּוּץ גָּלֻיּוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע כַּנְפוֹת הָאָרֶץ

As is known in the secret of “and gather us together from the four corners” — the Ineffable Name alludes to the “gathering of the sparks” of “wasted seed,” which is the essence of “the ingathering of the exiles from the four corners of the earth.”

דְּהַנִּיגּוּד לְכָל אַרְבַּע כַּנְפוֹת בָּא עַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם קוֹלְטִים הַשֶּׁפַע, שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹרֵד לָאָרֶץ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה — ״אֶרֶץ אֲשֶׁר ה׳ אֱלֹקֶיךָ דּוֹרֵשׁ״ הָרוֹמֵז לְאֶרֶץ עֶלְיוֹנָה

For the “scattering to all four corners” comes about because “the nations absorb the flow [shefa],” which “does not descend to the holy Land” — “a land which Hashem your God seeks out” (Devarim 11:12)1012Devarim 11:12: of Eretz Yisrael — “אֶרֶץ אֲשֶׁר ה’ אֱלֹהֶיךָ דֹּרֵשׁ אֹתָהּ, תָּמִיד עֵינֵי ה’ אֱלֹהֶיךָ בָּהּ” — “a land which Hashem your God seeks out; the eyes of Hashem your God are always upon it.” Meforshim: Rashi — God’s providence rests upon the Land continually; the Sages (Kesubos 110b and the doresh midrash) that Eretz Yisrael is under His direct, unmediated care. R’ Tzadok’s use: the phrase “the land Hashem seeks out” alludes to the “supernal Land,” the true and proper recipient of the shefa (flow); hence the flow belongs there, and its temporary descent outside the Land — absorbed by the nations — “was not fixed to remain so.”, alluding to the “supernal Land” —

שֶׁהַמַּטְרָא בַּעְלָהּ דְּאַרְעָא בִּירִידַת הַשֶּׁפַע מוֹלִידָהּ וּמַצְמִיחָהּ כְּשֶׁהוּא יוֹרֵד לְמָקוֹם הָרָאוּי, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כְּשֶׁיִּשּׁוֹפַע לַחוּץ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְבַטָּלָה, כְּטַעַם ״ה׳ צִלְּךָ״

for “the rain [matra] is the ‘husband of the earth,’” and in the descent of the flow it “gives birth and makes grow” when it “descends to the proper place” — not so when it “flows outward,” God forbid, “in vain,” in the sense of “Hashem is your shadow” (Tehillim 121:5) [mirroring man’s act];
עַל יְדֵי זֶה מוּכְרָחִים בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לָנוּעַ בֵּין הָעַמִּים
through this the Children of Israel are “compelled to wander among the peoples.”
וְהוּא עֵת אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַט הָאָדָם בָּאָדָם לְרַע לוֹ, לְאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים וְהֵם חוֹזְרִים וְקוֹלְטִים הַשֶּׁפַע שֶׁלָּהֶם בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא
And this is the “time that man ruled over man to his [own] detriment” — [to] the “base man”; for in truth “Israel are holy,” and they “return and re-absorb their flow, in whatever place it is,”

וְאַגָּבָהּ נִמְשָׁךְ גַּם מְעַט הַשֶּׁפַע שֶׁהָיָה לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מִצַּד עַצְמָם גַּם כֵּן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, עַד שֶׁהֵם יִשָּׁאֲרוּ כִּמְצוּלָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דָּגִים וְדָגָן — חַיֵּי גוּפָנִי וְנַפְשִׁי בְּחַיֵּי עוֹלָם

and “along with it,” even “the little flow the nations had of their own” is drawn “to Israel too” — until “they [the nations] remain like a depth without fish or grain” — [without] “bodily and spiritual life, and eternal life.”

וְאָז יִהְיֶה קִיבּוּץ גָּלֻיּוֹת, שֶׁיִּקּוּבְצוּ כָּל הַנִּדָּחִים מִן הַשֶּׁפַע לַחוּץ שֶׁלֹּא נִלְקְטוּ תֵּיכֶף בְּנ״ק שֶׁהִיא כְּלַל הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל דִּקְדֻשָּׁה, וְלֹא יִפּוֹל צְרוֹר אָרֶץ

And then will be “the ingathering of the exiles” — that all “the outcasts of the flow to the outside,” not immediately “gathered by [the holy Nukva], the collective of Knesses Yisrael of holiness,” will be “gathered in” — and “not a pebble shall fall to the ground.”
וּבֵירוּר זֶה דְּ״עַמֵּךְ״ זֶה [בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק חֵלֶק] עַל ״חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא״, כִּי אָז הוּא שֶׁיִּתְבָּרֵר זֶה
And this [is] the clarification of “your people,” [expounded, at the start of Perek Chelek,] concerning “a share in the World to Come” — for then it is that this will be clarified.
וּ״לְעוֹלָם יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ״, דְּיִתְבָּרֵר אַף שֶׁגָּלוּ מִן הָאָרֶץ הָיָה רַק לְשָׁעָה, וּבֶאֱמֶת יְרוּשַּׁת הָאָרֶץ הוּא לָהֶם לְעוֹלָם

And “they shall inherit the land forever” — for it will be clarified that “even though they were exiled from the Land, it was only for a moment,” and “in truth the inheritance of the Land is theirs forever.”
כִּי מַה שֶּׁהָיָה לְשָׁעָה שֶׁפַע יוֹרֵד חוּץ לָאָרֶץ הַמְיוּחֶדֶת לְקַבָּלַת הַשֶּׁפַע לֹא נִקְבַּע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לִהְיוֹת כֵּן, רַק עֲתִידִים לַחֲזוֹר לְקַבְעָא קַמָּא
For “what was, for a time, a flow descending outside the Land — designated for receiving the flow — was not fixed, God forbid, to remain so,” but “they will return to the original position.”
וְכֵיוָן דְּ״עַל פִּי ה׳ יַחֲנוּ וְעַל פִּי ה׳ יִסָּעוּ״ כְּסוֹתֵר עַל מְנָת לִבְנוֹת בִּמְקוֹמוֹ הוּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּפֶרֶק בַּמֶּה מַדְלִיקִין] גַּבֵּי מִשְׁכָּן

And since “by Hashem’s word they encamp and by Hashem’s word they journey” (Bamidbar 9:23)1013Bamidbar 9:23: of the cloud upon the Mishkan in the wilderness — “עַל פִּי ה’ יַחֲנוּ וְעַל פִּי ה’ יִסָּעוּ” — “by the word of Hashem they would encamp, and by the word of Hashem they would journey.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Ramban — every encampment and every journey was dictated by God through the cloud, never by the people’s own initiative. R’ Tzadok’s use: Israel’s exilic “journeys” are, like the Mishkan’s, “one who dismantles in order to rebuild in [another] place” (Shabbos 31b) — a purposeful relocation by Hashem’s word, not a banishment, so that the holiness travels with them., it is “like one who dismantles in order to rebuild in [another] place,” as they said [in Perek Bameh Madlikin, Shabbos 31b] regarding the Mishkan.
