Likkutei Torah therefore supplies a Chabad parallel to R' Tzadok's Binah/Malchus language: the Oral Torah has no independent 'self' that could be duplicated by foreign philosophy, yet precisely as the receptive mouth of Israel it becomes the place where the hidden Divine will is spoken.

וְהָאוֹמֵר יֵשׁ תּוֹרָה בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אַל תַּאֲמֵן, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ חָכְמָה בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, מֵחָכְמָתָם אֵין נַעֲשֶׂה דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּלָל, רַק חָכְמָה הַנּוֹבַעַת מִלֵּב בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל

And “‘whoever says there is Torah among the nations, do not believe’” — and though “there is chochmah among the nations,” “from their wisdom no words of Torah are made at all — only wisdom welling from the heart of the Children of Israel.”1100R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Bereishis §14): “for there is no light except that which issues from within the darkness — that through the concealment He caused it to be "very good"; "for You are with me," that he can speak in the second person.” Exactly the se’if: the Oral Torah is drawn by Israel’s sages out of their own hearts, from within the concealment — which is precisely why it is theirs and cannot be found among the nations.
וְלֹא בְּחִנָּם אָמְרוּ ז״ל (אֵיכָה רַבָּה ב, יז) לָשׁוֹן זֶה ״אִם יֹאמַר לְךָ אָדָם יֵשׁ תּוֹרָה [בָּאוּמּוֹת] כו׳״, וּמֵהֵיכָא תֵּיתֵי יֹאמַר כֵּן

And “not for naught did the Sages (Eichah Rabbah 2:17)1101Eichah Rabbah 2:13 (the base cites 2:17): On “her king and her princes are among the nations, there is no Torah” (Eichah 2:9): “If a person says to you, ‘there is wisdom among the nations’ — believe it; [but if he says] ‘there is Torah among the nations’ — do not believe it.” [coin] this expression, ‘if a person says to you: there is Torah [among the nations]’” — [and one may ask] “from where would [anyone] come to say so?”

אֲבָל הֵם צָפוּ בְּרוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ מַה שֶּׁעֲתִידִים הַמִּתְפַּלְסְפִים שֶׁבַּדּוֹרוֹת אַחֲרוֹנִים לוֹמַר כִּי חָכְמָה חִיצוֹנִית דִּבְנֵי יָוָן הֵם סִתְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְהוֹדִיעוּ לָנוּ שֶׁלֹּא נַאֲמִין

But “they foresaw by ruach hakodesh what the ‘philosophizers’ of the later generations would say — that the external wisdom of the sons of Greece is ‘the secrets of the Torah’ — and informed us that we should not believe [it].”
וְלֹא זֶהוּ הַדֶּרֶךְ בְּהוֹצָאַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מֵהַחִיצוֹנִים, לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חָכְמָתָם כְּמוֹת שֶׁהוּא וְלוֹמַר שֶׁזֶּהוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁנִּקְלַט מֵהֶם
And “this is not the way of extracting words of Torah from the outer [forces]” — to “accept their wisdom as it is and say that this is words of Torah absorbed from them” —

עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב פָּרְשַׁת בִּלְעָם דְּהָיָה מִנְּבִיאֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה, וּמִשֶּׁנִּתְּנָה תּוֹרָה כְּבָר נִיטְּלוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהָיָה בָּהֶם מֵהֶם

in the manner that there is, in the Written Torah, the portion of Bilaam — who “was of the prophets of the nations before the Torah was given” — and “once the Torah was given, the words of Torah that were in them were already taken from them.”1102R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Chalomot §20): “and even though his death too has, from this side, an elevation — that he will reach a higher rung — nonetheless the day of death itself is at any rate distress to him.” The se’if’s “already taken from them” precisely: what the nations once held has been withdrawn, and a loss remains a loss on its own plane even when it serves an ascent on another.

וְאָמְרוּ בְּתַנְחוּמָא [פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ] דְּעַל כֵּן נִיתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁעֲתִידִין אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לְתַרְגֵּם הַתּוֹרָה יְוָנִית וְלוֹמַר ״אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל״, וְיֹאמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא ״מִי שֶׁמִּסְטוֹרִין שֶׁלִּי בְּיָדוֹ״ כו׳

And they said in Tanchuma [Parashas Noach] that1103Midrash Tanchuma, Noach: the Sages taught that the Oral Torah was given [and deliberately not committed to writing] because “the nations of the world are destined to translate the [Written] Torah into Greek and say, ‘we are Israel’”; and the Holy One will answer, “the one who has My mysteries [mistorin] in his hand — he is My child.” Meforshim: the Midrash — the Written Torah, being open, can be copied and claimed by anyone, but the Oral Torah, transmitted only mouth to mouth and drawn from the heart, is the sign that marks Israel as God’s own. R’ Tzadok’s use: therefore the Written Torah “was revealed in writing to all who come into the world” (the nations too having some connection to it), whereas the Oral Torah “is the mysteries of the Holy One, which cannot be set down in writing at all” — the possession of Israel alone. “therefore the Oral Torah was given” — for “the nations are destined to translate the [Written] Torah into Greek and say, ‘we are Israel,’” and the Holy One will say, “‘[the one] who has My mysteries in his hand [is My child]’”
וְהַיְינוּ דִּלְתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב יֵשׁ גַּם לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת, שֶׁגַּם מִדִּבְרֵיהֶם יֵשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, דְּעַל כֵּן נִגְלֵית בִּכְתָב לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם
That is: “the Written Torah has a connection to them too — for from their words too there is [something] in words of Torah” — therefore “it was revealed in writing to all who come into the world.”
אֲבָל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא מִסְטוֹרִין שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹתוֹ בִּכְתָב כְּלָל, דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא נִכְתַּב בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב רַק ״סוֹד ה׳ לִירֵאָיו״

But the Oral Torah “is the mysteries of the Holy One, which cannot be revealed in writing at all”; therefore there was written [i.e., concealed] in the Written Torah only “‘the secret of Hashem is to those who fear Him’” (Tehillim 25:14)1104Tehillim 25:14: “סוֹד ה’ לִירֵאָיו, וּבְרִיתוֹ לְהוֹדִיעָם” — “the secret [sod] of Hashem is to those who fear Him, and His covenant, to make it known to them.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Radak — God confides His hidden counsel only to those who fear Him. R’ Tzadok’s use: this alone was set (concealed) in the Written Torah — that the Oral Torah, His “mystery,” belongs to Knesses Yisrael, “the woman who fears Hashem” (Mishlei 31:30), who from the depths of the heart look to Him; “the essence of fear is in the heart” (Yoma 72b), so that Hashem dwells within their heart and they can grasp His hidden secret concealed in the Written Torah. —
הֵם כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל ״אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה׳״, דְּמֵעִמְקֵי לְבָבָם צוֹפֶה לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, דְּעִיקַּר הַיִּרְאָה בַּלֵּב, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא [בְּיוֹמָא עב:] עַל פָּסוּק ״וְלֵב אָיִן״

they are Knesses Yisrael, “a woman who fears Hashem” (Mishlei 31:30), who “from the depths of their heart look to Hashem” — for “the essence of fear is in the heart,” as it is stated [in Yoma 72b]1105Yoma 72b: On “why is there a price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, seeing he has no heart” (Mishlei 17:16): “Woe to the enemies of the Torah scholars [a euphemism for the scholars themselves] who engage in Torah but have no fear of Heaven within them” — “no heart” being read as the absence of yirah. on the verse “but there is no heart” (Mishlei 17:16).
וְעַל יְדֵי כֵן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן בְּקֶרֶב לְבָבָם, וְלָכֵן יוּכְלוּ לְהַשִּׂיג מִסְטוֹרָיו וְסוֹד ה׳ הַגָּנוּז בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
And thereby “Hashem dwells within their heart,” and so “they can attain His mysteries and the secret of Hashem hidden in the Written Torah.”

וְהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הוּא ״נוֹבְלוֹת חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה], וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא ״נוֹבְלוֹת בִּינָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה״, דְּהִיא לִבָּא וְתַמָּן הַלֵּב מֵבִין

And the Written Torah is “the gleanings of the supernal Chochmah,” as they said [in Bereishis Rabbah]; and the Oral Torah is “the gleanings of the Binah above” — “which is the heart, and there the heart understands.”
וּמִמֶּנָּה נִשְׁפָּע הַבִּינָה לַלְּבָבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהָבִין ״דָּבָר מִתּוֹךְ דָּבָר״ שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
and “from it Binah flows to the hearts of the Children of Israel, to understand ‘one thing from another’ in the Written Torah.”

וּבַחָכְמָה שֶׁהוּא רֵאשִׁית הַגִּילּוּי דְּ״יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן״, כִּנְקוּדָּה בִּלְבַד בְּלֹא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת לְאוֹרֶךְ וְרוֹחַב, דְּעַל כֵּן רְמוּזָה בְּאוֹת י׳ שֶׁבַּשֵּׁם כַּיָּדוּעַ, יֵשׁ מָקוֹם לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לִטְעוֹת שֶׁגַּם הֵם נִגְלִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְיֵשׁ

And in Chochmah — which is “the first revelation of ‘something from nothing,’ [existing] as a mere point without spread of length and breadth,” and therefore “alluded to in the letter yod of the [Divine] Name,” as is known — “there is room for the nations to err [into thinking] that they too are revealed in this world ‘to substance.’”

וְעַל כֵּן יֵשׁ חָכְמָה בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם גַּם כֵּן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ ז״ל, עַד לֶעָתִיד דְּ״הַאֲבַדְתִּי חֲכָמִים מֵאֱדוֹם״, כִּי אָז ״ה׳ בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ וְאֵין [עִמּוֹ אֵל נֵכָר]״ וְגוֹ׳

And therefore “there is chochmah among the nations too in this world,” as the Sages said — until the Future, [of] which “‘I will destroy the wise from Edom’” (Ovadiah 1:8), for then “‘Hashem alone will lead him, and there is no [foreign god with him]’” (Devarim 32:12).
אֲבָל הַבִּינָה שֶׁהוּא הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת, רֵאשִׁית הַגִּילּוּי הַסָּתוּם לִהְיוֹת נִגְלֶה מְפוֹרָשׁ בַּלֵּב מֵבִין, תַּמָּן נָבְעוּ מַצְפּוּנָיו
But Binah — which is “the spread, the first revelation of the hidden [Chochmah], to become explicitly revealed in the understanding heart” — “there the hidden depths well forth”;
דְּעֵשָׂו וַחֲבֵירָיו כָּל שָׂרֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת אֶל הַקְּדֻשָּׁה

[whereas] “Esav and his fellows, all the ministers of the nations, have no connection whatever to the holiness [there].” — wisdom the nations may share, for Chochmah is but a point they can imagine themselves grasping; but Binah — the hidden welling-up into the understanding heart — is Israel’s alone, for Hashem dwells in their hearts, and the Oral Torah drawn from there is His very mystery, which no translation can seize.

items.h: The theme: Binah and Malchus are both alluded to in the two heh’s of the Name. This world was created with a heh — a portico open below, from which whoever wishes may exit; the nations are those who exit and do not remain. Before one sins he is the lower heh; after he sins and returns he is brought back through the upper opening and a crown is bound for him — and this is the upper heh, which alludes to teshuvah.

p: [צב] וְעַל כֵּן בִּינָה וּמַלְכוּת שְׁנֵיהֶם רְמוּזִים בְּאוֹתִיּוֹת הַהֵ״הִין דְּשֵׁם כַּיָּדוּעַ
And therefore Binah and Malchus are both alluded to in the [two] heh letters of the [Divine] Name, as is known.

דְּבַ״הֵ״א נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כָּל מִינֵי נִבְרָאִים שׁוֹנִים, וְיֵשׁ מָקוֹם לָצֵאת לְמִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּמְנָחוֹת כט:]1106Menachos 29b: R’ Yehudah Nesi’ah asked R’ Ami about the verse “trust in Hashem forever, for in Kah [the letters yod and heh] Hashem is the Rock of worlds” (Yeshayah 26:4) — why “b’Kah” rather than “Yah”? [The answer, expounded by R’ Yehudah bar R’ Il’ai:] these are the two worlds the Holy One created — one with a heh and one with a yod — derived from “these are the generations of the heavens and the earth b’hibar’am” (Bereishis 2:4): read not b’hibar’am but b’heh bera’am, “He created them with a heh” — hence this world was created with heh and Olam Haba with yod. And why was this world created with a heh? Because it resembles a portico [akhsadra], open below, so that whoever wishes to leave may leave. And why is its [left] leg suspended [not joined to the roof]? Because if one repents, he is brought back in [through the small upper opening]. And let him re-enter by the way he left? — that would not avail, as Reish Lakish taught: “if [one comes] to the scoffers, He scoffs at him; but to the humble He gives grace” (Mishlei 3:34) — one who comes to purify himself is assisted; one who comes to defile himself, an opening is made for him. And why does the heh have a crown [taga]? The Holy One says: if he returns, I bind a crown for him. Direct Chabad parallel - Likkutei Torah, Metzora 13: The Alter Rebbe formulates the symbolism of teshuvah in the very letters R' Tzadok is expounding: 'teshuvah' is 'tashuv hei legabei yud,' the return of the heh to the yud, and the 'hei ila'ah' is Binah. Sin produces a separation from the yud, the bittul of supernal Chochmah, and from that separation the chitzonim are able to draw nurture; teshuvah restores the upper heh to its relation with the yud. The immediate context in Likkutei Torah describes an awakening of ratzo and inner fire from mochin de'Imma followed by its reintegration into bittul - a return that is therefore not emotional escape but a repaired joining of Binah to its Source. This is almost the exact kabbalistic vocabulary of the present se'if. R' Tzadok reads Menachos' suspended heh as the architecture of the baal teshuvah: after exiting, he does not simply retrace the lower route but is assisted through the upper opening and crowned, corresponding to the hei ila'ah of Binah, 'libo yavin vashav.' Likkutei Torah gives the inner-letter mechanism for that ascent. The crown is not merely an honor added after repentance; the entire movement is a restoration of a severed higher relation. It also supports R' Tzadok's linking of teshuvah and Torah Shebe'al Peh: if the upper heh is Binah, then the return of the heart and the renewed expansion of Divine understanding are aspects of one repair. The greater the reintegration of Binah, the more the hidden light can flow from heart to articulated Torah rather than feeding what stands outside holiness.

For “this world was created with a heh” — [this world] being “the spread of all kinds of varied creatures” — and “there is room to exit for whoever wishes,” as they said [in Menachos 29b].1107R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Noach §7): “the utterance”let there be light," which corresponds to Chochmah when it receives from Keser by way of the tip of the upper yud." Exactly the se’if: the two heh’s are the receiving letters, and everything turns on what is drawn down into them from above — which is why a man’s standing in the open portico is measured by the heart’s longing.
וְהָאוּמּוֹת הֵם הַיּוֹצְאִים וְלֹא נִשְׁאֲרוּ שָׁם, וְאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְגוּף הַ״הֵ״א הָרוֹמֵז לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל

“And the nations are the ones who exit and do not remain there,” and “they have no connection to the body of the heh, which alludes to Knesses Yisrael.”1108R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §68): “the completeness of the receiver — as in the Midrash, "and Miriam answered them"… that the completeness of the receiver is like a woman: the bestower returns to be one who receives, as it says, Israel give strength to the heavenly host — as in the Future, "the female shall encompass the male."” Exactly the se’if: the heh that alludes to Knesses Yisrael is the letter of the receiver, and its whole promise is that the receiving side will one day encompass.

וְקוֹדֶם שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא הוּא הֵ״א הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה, וְאַחַר שֶׁיֶּחֱטָא וְיָשׁוּב דְּמַעֲיִילָא לֵיהּ בְּהַךְ וְקוֹשְׁרִין לוֹ כֶּתֶר כִּדְאִיתָא הָתָם, זֶהוּ הֵ״א עֶלְיוֹנָה הָרוֹמֶזֶת לִתְשׁוּבָה, דְּ״לִבּוֹ יָבִין וָשָׁב״ כַּיָּדוּעַ

“Before one sins, he is the lower heh; and after he sins and returns” — that “he is brought back in through the [upper opening] and a crown is bound for him,” as it is stated there [in Menachos] — “this is the upper heh, which alludes to teshuvah,” [as in] “‘his heart shall understand and repent’” (Yeshayah 6:10), as is known.1109R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §92): “"as you rebelled" — as in the matter of the quarrel, where He said to the two of them, "and you shall speak to the rock"; and Aharon did not speak… but Moshe struck.” The se’if’s open portico exactly: what was given as an opening for speech can be met with a blow instead — and the whole difference between exit and return lies in which is chosen.

וּ״בְמָקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין [כו׳]״, דְּמִתְעַלִּין עַל צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים שֶׁעוֹלִין דֶּרֶךְ פֶּתַח הָעֶלְיוֹן, וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא קוֹשֵׁר לָהֶם כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן לִידָּבֵק בַּבִּינָה אִמָּא עִילָּאָה שֶׁהִיא לְמַעְלָה מַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵיגַת צַדִּיק גָּמוּר, וְעַל כֵּן רוֹמֶזֶת גַּם כֵּן לְעוֹלָם הַבָּא

And “‘in the place where baalei teshuvah stand [the wholly righteous do not stand]’” — for “they are elevated above the wholly righteous, who ascend by way of the upper opening,” and “the Holy One binds for them a supernal crown, to cleave to Binah, Imma Ila’ah, which is far, far above the rung of a wholly righteous person” — and therefore “it alludes also to Olam Haba.”

אַף דְּהָעוֹלָם הַבָּא נִבְרָא בְּי׳, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אוֹתָם הַנּוֹחֲלִים עוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁהֵם כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, הַיְינוּ דְּלֶעָתִיד יְבוֹרַר דְּכוּלָּם עָיְילֵי בְּהַךְ, וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל רְמוּזָה בַּ״הֵ״א

Although Olam Haba was created with a yod, nonetheless “those who inherit Olam Haba — who are Knesses Yisrael” (for “all Israel have a share in Olam Haba”) — that is, “in the Future it will be clarified that they all enter through it [the heh],” and “Knesses Yisrael is alluded to in the heh.”1110Menachos 29b: “This world was created with the [letter] heh: just as the heh is open below, so [there is] an opening for all who wish to go astray [to leave]; and just as it has an opening [above] on the side, so whoever wishes to repent [may re-enter].”

אֶלָּא דְּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא הֵ״א אַחֲרוֹנָה, וְהַבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה נִרְאֶה גָּרוּעַ מִצַּדִּיק גָּמוּר וּבָא אַחֲרָיו, אֲבָל לֶעָתִיד ״ה׳ עוֹשֶׂה חֲדָשׁוֹת״ דְּ״נְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵב גָּבֶר״ וְתִתְעַלֶּה בְּסוֹד ״אֵשֶׁת חַיִל עֲטֶרֶת בַּעְלָהּ״ כַּנּוֹדָע

Except that “in this world it is the last heh,” and “the baal teshuvah appears inferior to the wholly righteous and comes after him”; but in the Future, “Hashem creates new things” — “the female shall encircle the male” (Yirmeyah 31:21) — and “she will be elevated, in the secret of ‘a woman of valor is the crown of her husband’” (Mishlei 12:4), as is known —

הַיְינוּ שֶׁתָּשׁוּב לִהְיוֹת הֵ״א רִאשׁוֹנָה, עַל יְדֵי שְׁלֵימוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁבְּלִבָּם יִזְכּוּ לִידָּבֵק בְּמִדַּת הַבִּינָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה, הַיְינוּ הַבִּינָה שֶׁהֶאֱצִיל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ בָּעוֹלָם

that is, “she will return to be the first heh” — “through the completeness of the Oral Torah in their hearts, they will merit to cleave to the trait of the supernal Binah,” namely “the Binah that Hashem emanated to flow into the world.”

כִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא ״לִבְּכֶן״ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהַשָּׂגַת הַבִּינָה שֶׁבְּלִבָּבָם הוּא הַשָּׂגַת הַמִּסְטוֹרִין דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וְהַבִּינָה הַגְּנוּזָה דְּאַכַּתִּי לְפוּמָא לָא גַּלְיָא

For “the Holy One is the heart of Israel,” and “the attainment of the Binah within their hearts is the attainment of the mysteries of the Holy One” — and “the hidden Binah which is not yet revealed to the mouth,”

אֶלָּא שֶׁהִיא מִתְגַּלֵּית עַל יְדֵי פִּיּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, עַד עֵת קֵץ שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה גַּם הַקֵּץ הָאֲמִיתִּי לְעֵין כֹּל, מִלִּבָּא לְפוּמָא דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל

“only that it is revealed through the mouths of the Children of Israel in every generation, in the Oral Torah — until the End of Days, when the true End too will be revealed to every eye, from the heart to the mouth of the Children of Israel.”
וְאָז יִהְיֶה תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וְתַכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת מַדְרֵיגַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה, דְּהָא בְּהָא תַּלְיָא
“And then will be the ultimate completeness of the Oral Torah and the ultimate completeness of the rung of teshuvah — for the one depends on the other.”
כְּפִי שְׁלֵימוּת מִדַּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה בַּלְּבָבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאֵיזֶה דּוֹר, כָּךְ הוּא הַהִתְגַּלּוּת דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁבְּחַכְמֵי אוֹתוֹ דּוֹר
“According to the completeness of the trait of teshuvah in the hearts of the Children of Israel in a given generation, so is the revelation of the Oral Torah among the sages of that generation.”

דְּעַל כֵּן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה שֶׁ״הֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה״, מִמֶּנָּה הַתְחָלַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת, שֶׁהוּא הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבְּיַד הַחֲכָמִים דַּעֲדִיפִי מִנְּבִיאִים בָּזֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּבָבָא בַתְרָא יב.] עַיֵּין שָׁם בָּרַמְבַּ״ן

Therefore David HaMelech, who “raised up the yoke of teshuvah,” is the source of “the beginning of the Oral Torah in [its] revelation” — which is “the wisdom in the hand of the Sages,” who “are superior to prophets in this,” as they said [in Bava Basra 12a] (see there in the Ramban);
וְנִזְכָּר [לְעֵיל סִימָן ג׳] דְּהוּא הַשָּׂגַת רוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ דְּנִשְׁאָר גַּם מִשֶּׁנִּסְתַּלְּקָה הַנְּבוּאָה, וְכָל הַשָּׂגַת חָכְמַת הַחֲכָמִים הוּא בְּרוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ

and it was mentioned [above, Siman 3] that “it is the attainment of ruach hakodesh, which remained even after prophecy departed” — and “all attainment of the wisdom of the Sages is through ruach hakodesh.”1111Bava Basra 12a: “From the day the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed, prophecy was taken from the prophets and given to the Sages; a Sage is greater than a prophet [chacham adif mi-navi].” — the two heh’s trace the whole arc of return: the baal teshuvah, seemingly the “last heh” who trails the tzaddik, is bound a supernal crown and in the Future becomes the “first” — for teshuvah and the Oral Torah rise together, each generation’s returning hearts unlocking that generation’s revelation.

items.h: The theme: Just as Moshe was master of all the prophets, so David was master of all possessors of ruach ha-kodesh. From him began the spread of Torah and wisdom — in great yeshivos and many disciples, not through prophecy but through the awakening of the Binah in the heart, from which the yoke of teshuvah is raised. In Rebbi’s generation all six extremities of that middah were clarified, and the whole Oral Torah was revealed in the Mishnah.

p: [צג] וְיָדוּעַ דִּכְמוֹ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה הָיָה רַבָּן שֶׁל כָּל הַנְּבִיאִים, כֵּן הָיָה דָּוִד רַבָּן שֶׁל כָּל בַּעֲלֵי רוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ

And it is known that, just as Moshe Rabbeinu “was the master of all the prophets,” so David “was the master of all the possessors of ruach hakodesh.”1112R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Noach §4): "“[one who] fears God” — the term “fear” is expounded of prayer and mercy; and so it is expounded, “who among you fears Hashem” — of one who regularly comes to the synagogue." Exactly the se’if: David is master of all possessors of ruach ha-kodesh — and the faculty at issue is the one that expresses itself in prayer, from which the whole spread of Torah afterward began. Izhbitz-Radzin context - Tiferet Yosef, Hoshana Rabba 2: Tiferet Yosef develops the distinction between seeing and hearing in a way that directly illuminates R' Tzadok's Davidic model of ruach hakodesh. Sight, he explains, takes in an external surface at once; hearing cannot receive two voices simultaneously, but it can penetrate to the depth of a matter. He reads 'hatu oznechem ulechu elai, shim'u u'sechi nafshechem... chasdei David hane'emanim' as a summons to incline the inner depth of the heart to Hashem and to follow the Divine light from its first ratzon down to the final action. When a person's inward ear is so directed, he can perceive that Hashem is continually occupied with forging an eternal covenant with Israel. He identifies this capacity with 'chasdei David': David's avodah can receive illumination even into actions whose outer garment appeared to lack light, because his inner life is surrendered to Hashem. This closely complements R' Tzadok's claim that after Moshe, master of prophecy, David becomes master of baalei ruach hakodesh and inaugurates a Torah that wells from awakened Binah in the heart. The shift is not from revelation to merely private creativity. It is from the visual clarity of prophecy to a deeper inward hearing that must be drawn through the heart and then articulated by sages. Tiferet Yosef thus helps explain why teshuvah and the growth of Torah Shebe'al Peh advance together from David onward: both require the heart to penetrate beneath the surface garment and receive the hidden Divine intention that can then become speech, teaching and renewed life.

וּמִמֶּנּוּ הַתְחָלַת הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַרְבָּצַת הַתּוֹרָה וְהַחָכְמָה בִּישִׁיבוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת וְתַלְמִידִים רַבִּים שֶׁלֹּא עַל יְדֵי נְבוּאָה, וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה בָּא לַהֲקָמַת עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה

And “from him began the spread of the dissemination of Torah and wisdom — in great yeshivos and many disciples — not through prophecy, but through the awakening of the Binah in the heart, from which comes the raising up of the yoke of teshuvah.”1113R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah I §74): “"the face of Moshe was as the face of the sun" — whose light is from his own essence, and therefore it is never lacking — and so Moshe, even though Israel sinned with the Calf, [was told] "and I shall make you a great nation"; "the face of Yehoshua as the face of the moon" — his light from another.” Exactly the se’if’s pairing: Moshe is master of the prophets because his light is his own — and David stands in the corresponding place for the possessors of ruach ha-kodesh.
וּבְדוֹר רַבִּי נִתְבָּרְרוּ כָּל הַשֵּׁשׁ קְצָווֹת דְּמִדַּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה, שֶׁהֵם כָּל הַכֹּחוֹת שֶׁבְּכֹחַ כּוּלָּם
And “in Rebbi’s generation all the six extremities of the trait of teshuvah were clarified” — which are “all the powers, [held] in potential, of them all”;
וְעַל כֵּן נִתְגַּלָּה אָז כְּלָלוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בְּחִבּוּר הַמִּשְׁנָה, דְּכוֹלֶלֶת בְּכֹחַ גַּם כָּל מַה שֶּׁיִּתְחַדֵּשׁ מֵחַכְמֵי הַדּוֹרוֹת אַחַר כָּךְ

“and therefore the entirety of the Oral Torah was then revealed in the composition of the Mishnah,” which “includes, in potential, also all that will be innovated by the sages of the [later] generations thereafter.”1114R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Chalomot §3): “that they were revealing to me certain things from the root of my soul; and among the things they told me was that the generation of Mashiach will be those very souls of the generation of the wilderness.” Exactly the se’if: the line runs from the master of prophecy through the master of ruach ha-kodesh to the later sages — one continuous root reappearing, and not a succession of unrelated generations. — as Moshe headed the prophets, David heads the masters of ruach hakodesh, his Torah flowing through the awakened Binah of the heart rather than prophecy; and once, in Rebbi’s day, the six extremities of teshuvah stood complete, the whole Oral Torah — all later innovation included — could be set down, in potential, in the Mishnah.

items.h: The theme (the closing se’if of Siman 6): Therefore, it appears to R’ Tzadok, the root of all Israel’s souls is included in the composition of the Mishnah — and included in it too are all the words of Torah that will be absorbed through the exiles among the nations, for through this comes the ingathering of the exiles. All the exiles to the four corners of the earth were for this purpose: through the sins, many holy sparks were absorbed into the dominion of the “outer” man, whose end is to its own detriment — for when Israel go out, they “swallow it from its mouth” in the ingathering, and then “all the peoples will be burnings of lime” (Yeshayah 33:12), while those who remain grasp the corner of a Jew’s garment and become “attached converts,” as Scripture and the Sages describe. That holy spark draws with it all their vitality — as the death of the Egyptian firstborn came through the revelation of the Shechinah. Many words of Torah are innovated through the intermingling among the nations in various ways, and by this the sparks are absorbed from them; all are alluded to in the Mishnah in various ways, with many deep matters not for detailing here. In any case, the general rule is true: all the Oral Torah is included in the Mishnah — in potential — coming forth into actuality over the course of the generations, until the days of Mashiach. Likewise the rungs of teshuvah — those six extremities held in potential — come forth into actuality across those generations, until Mashiach (may he be revealed speedily, amen), when the trait of Malchus is complete, bringing into actuality what is in the six extremities. Then all the rungs of teshuvah and its heights will be revealed in actual, expansive revelation; and from the rung of “lengthening of years” we will merit “and we shall live,” to the days of Mashiach and the life of Olam Haba — the world that is “wholly long” and eternal life, speedily in our days, amen. And it appears to R’ Tzadok from all this that the study of Mishnayos is a segulah for length of days. [1115: R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah §21): “the first blemish — the counsel of the serpent — and the willful sins shall become as merits; and automatically the death that the serpent brought into the world will be nullified. And this clarification cannot come about in this world until the days of Mashiach, when we shall merit eternal life.” Exactly the se’if’s close: the segulah for length of days is not a charm but this very clarification — the undoing of the serpent’s counsel, of which the Mishnah is the instrument. Chassidic context - Arvei Nachal, Lech Lecha 2:7; cf. Sefat Emet, Bo 18:2: The Arvei Nachal addresses a problem that is almost tailor-made for the closing claim of this siman. If the purpose of exile is to extract holy sparks from the entire world, how can that be accomplished in countries to which no Jew ever physically travels? His answer is that before Matan Torah sparks could be raised only through actual presence and servitude in the particular place, as in Egypt; after Matan Torah, however, 'al yedei esek haTorah yecholin lehotzi nitzotzos kedoshos min kol ha'olam, ki haTorah hu tziur kol ha'olam' - through Torah study one can draw holy sparks from the entire world, because Torah is the form of the whole world. This places R' Tzadok's closing identification of Mishnah, exile, soul-roots and ingathering into a broader Chassidic framework. The geographic scattering of Israel and the textual universality of Torah are two modes of one birur: what is dispersed through the world can be gathered through a Torah that contains the world's spiritual form. The Sefas Emes (Bo 18:2) states the parallel principle from the side of galus itself: every exile is to extract holy sparks mixed among the nations, and redemption occurs when Israel carry out the hidden illuminations for which they entered. Together these sources clarify why R' Tzadok can say that Torah insights born through Israel's intermingling among the nations are already alluded to in the Mishnah 'bekoach.' The Mishnah is not merely a record composed before later exiles; as the foundational form of Torah Shebe'al Peh, it can contain in potential the sparks that later souls and later histories will bring into actuality. On that reading, the final segulah of Mishnah for arichus yamim belongs organically to the siman: gathering scattered Torah-life back into its root is itself a movement from dispersion and death toward the 'olam shekulo aroch.']

p: [צד] וְעַל כֵּן נִרְאֶה לִי דְּשֹׁרֶשׁ כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלוּלוֹת בְּחִבּוּר הַמִּשְׁנָה, וְכֵן כְּלוּלִים בָּהּ גַּם כָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁיִּקָּלְטוּ עַל יְדֵי הַגָּלֻיּוֹת בֵּין אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא קִיבּוּץ הַגָּלֻיּוֹת

And therefore, it appears to me, “the root of all the souls of the Children of Israel is included in the composition of the Mishnah” — and “likewise included in it are also all the words of Torah that will be absorbed through the exiles among the nations,” for “through this is the ingathering of the exiles.”1116R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Sukkos §34): “the spreading of blessing in all matters — that even a coin becomes blessed, which is a thing outside the way of nature; and it is from the aspect of Aharon, as it says, "the beard of Aharon," which descends according to his measures like the dew of Chermon — "for there Hashem commanded the blessing: life forever."” Exactly the se’if: the ingathering and the length of days are one blessing, commanded where Israel are gathered together — “life forever,” at the place of joining.
דְּכָל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת לְאַרְבַּע כַּנְפוֹת הָאָרֶץ הָיָה לְצוֹרֶךְ זֶה
For “all the exiles, to the four corners of the earth, were for this need.”
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַחֲטָאִים נִקְלְטוּ הַרְבֵּה נִיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת בִּשְׁלִיטַת ״הָאָדָם״ [דְּסִטְרָא אַחֲרָא] בָּאָדָם, וְסוֹפוֹ לְרַע לוֹ כְּשֶׁיֵּצְאוּ, בָּלְעוֹ מִפִּיו בְּקִיבּוּץ גָּלֻיּוֹת

For “through the sins, many holy sparks were absorbed into the dominion of the [‘outer’] man within man” — and “its end is to its own detriment: when they [Israel] go out, [they] swallow it from its mouth, in the ingathering of the exiles.”
דְּאָז יִהְיוּ כָּל הָעַמִּים ״מִשְׂרְפוֹת סִיד״, וְהַנִּשְׁאָרִים יֹאחֲזוּ בִּכְנַף אִישׁ יְהוּדִי וְיִהְיוּ גֵּרִים גְּרוּרִים כַּמְבוֹאָר בַּכְּתוּבִים וּבְדִבְרֵי רַז״ל

for “then all the peoples will be ‘burnings of lime’” (Yeshayah 33:12)1117Yeshayah 33:12: “וְהָיוּ עַמִּים מִשְׂרְפוֹת שִׂיד, קוֹצִים כְּסוּחִים בָּאֵשׁ יִצַּתּוּ” — “and the peoples shall be as the burnings of lime, as thorns cut down that are kindled in the fire.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Radak — the nations who oppressed Israel will be consumed like lime in a kiln, like severed thorns cast to the flame. R’ Tzadok’s use: in the ingathering, once the holy sparks are reclaimed from the nations, “all the peoples will be ‘burnings of lime’” — drained of the vitality the indwelling spark had lent them — while “those who remain grasp the corner of a Jew’s garment” and become attached converts., “and those who remain will grasp the corner of a Jewish man[’s garment]” (cf. Zechariah 8:23)1118Zechariah 8:23: “כֹּה אָמַר ה’ צְבָאוֹת… אֲשֶׁר יַחֲזִיקוּ עֲשָׂרָה אֲנָשִׁים מִכֹּל לְשֹׁנוֹת הַגּוֹיִם, וְהֶחֱזִיקוּ בִּכְנַף אִישׁ יְהוּדִי לֵאמֹר: נֵלְכָה עִמָּכֶם, כִּי שָׁמַעְנוּ אֱלֹהִים עִמָּכֶם” — “in those days ten men of all the languages of the nations shall take hold of the corner of the garment of a Jewish man, saying: let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Radak — in the Messianic age the nations will cling to Israel, recognizing that the Divine Presence rests upon them. R’ Tzadok’s use: “those who remain of the nations will grasp the corner of a Jewish man’s garment and become ‘attached converts [geirim gerurim].’” “and become ‘attached converts,’” as is explained in Scripture and in the words of the Sages.
כִּי אוֹתוֹ נִיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ מוֹשֵׁךְ עִמּוֹ כָּל הַחִיּוּת שֶׁבָּהֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה מִיתַת הַבְּכוֹרִים בְּמִצְרַיִם עַל יְדֵי גִּילּוּי שְׁכִינָה
For “that holy spark draws with it all the vitality within them” — “just as the death of the firstborn in Egypt was through the revelation of the Shechinah.”
וְהַרְבֵּה דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִתְחַדְּשִׁים עַל יְדֵי הַהִתְעָרְבוּת בֵּין הָאוּמּוֹת בְּאוֹפַנִּים שׁוֹנִים, וּבְדֶרֶךְ זֶה הוּא קְלִיטַת הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת מֵהֶם
“And many words of Torah are innovated through the intermingling among the nations in various ways” — “and in this manner is the absorption of the sparks from them.”
וְהֵם רְמוּזִים כּוּלָּם בַּמִּשְׁנָה בִּדְרָכִים שׁוֹנִים, וְיֵשׁ בָּזֶה הַרְבֵּה עִנְיָינִים עֲמוּקִים מְאוֹד שֶׁאֵין כַּאן מְקוֹם בֵּיאוּרָם בִּפְרָט
“And they are all alluded to in the Mishnah, in various ways; and there are in this many very deep matters, whose detailed explanation is not the place here.”
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים זֶה אֱמֶת דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל, דְּכָל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כְּלוּלָה בַּמִּשְׁנָה, אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא בָּהּ בְּכֹחַ וְיוֹצֵאת לְפֹעַל בְּמֶשֶׁךְ הַדּוֹרוֹת עַד יְמוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ

“In any case, this is true as a general rule: all the Oral Torah is included in the Mishnah — only that it is in it in potential, and comes forth into actuality over the course of the generations, until the days of Mashiach.”
וְכֵן מַדְרֵיגוֹת הַתְּשׁוּבָה, כָּל אוֹתָם שֵׁשׁ קְצָווֹת שֶׁהָיוּ בְּכֹחַ, הֵם יוֹצְאִים לְפֹעַל בְּמֶשֶׁךְ דּוֹרוֹת הָהֵם עַד הַמָּשִׁיחַ שֶׁיִּגָּלֶה בִּמְהֵרָה בְּיָמֵינוּ אָמֵן

“And likewise the rungs of teshuvah — all those six extremities that were in potential — come forth into actuality over the course of those generations, until the Mashiach, who will be revealed speedily in our days, amen” —
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שְׁלֵימוּת מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת הַמּוֹצִיאָה לְפֹעַל מַה שֶּׁבְּכֹחַ הַשֵּׁשׁ קְצָווֹת כַּיָּדוּעַ
“when there will be the completeness of the trait of Malchus, which brings forth into actuality that which is in the potential of the six extremities,” as is known.

וְאָז יִתְגַּלּוּ כָּל מַדְרֵיגוֹת הַתְּשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲלוֹתֶיהָ בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת גָּלוּי בְּפֹעַל, וּמִמַּדְרֵגַת הַאֲרָכַת שָׁנִים ״נִזְכֶּה וְנִחְיֶה״ וְגוֹ׳ לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ וּלְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁהוּא ״עוֹלָם שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ אָרוֹךְ״ וְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם בִּמְהֵרָה בְּיָמֵינוּ אָמֵן

“And then all the rungs of teshuvah and its heights will be revealed in expansive, actual revelation; and from the rung of the ‘lengthening of years’ we will merit ‘and we shall live’” (cf. Hoshea 6:2)1119Hoshea 6:2: “יְחַיֵּנוּ מִיֹּמָיִם, בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי יְקִמֵנוּ, וְנִחְיֶה לְפָנָיו” — “He will revive us after two days; on the third day He will raise us up, and we shall live before Him.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Radak — a prophecy of Israel’s future revival and resurrection. R’ Tzadok’s use: from the rung of a mere “lengthening of years,” Israel will ascend to “and we shall live” — the full life of the days of Mashiach and the World to Come. “to the days of Mashiach and to the life of Olam Haba” — which is “‘a world that is wholly long1120“A world that is wholly long” (Kiddushin 39b; Chullin 142a): expounding the reward of “that your days may be lengthened” (Devarim 5:16; 22:7), the Gemara teaches — “‘that it may be well with you’ — in the world that is wholly good; ‘and that your days may be lengthened’ — in the world that is wholly long [olam she-kulo aroch].” Meforshim: Rashi — the Torah’s promise of “length of days” points, at its depth, to the eternal World to Come. R’ Tzadok’s use: from the “lengthening of years” granted in this world, Israel will merit “the life of Olam Haba — the world that is wholly long,” eternal life; and on this note he seals the entire siman, “that the study of Mishnayos is a segulah for length of days.”’” and “eternal life” — speedily in our days, amen.
[וְנִרְאֶה לִי מִזֶּה דְּלִימּוּד הַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת סְגֻלָּה לַאֲרִיכַת יָמִים]

[And it appears to me from this that the study of Mishnayos is a segulah for length of days.] — and so the whole siman closes in the Mishnah: it holds, in potential, every Jewish soul and every spark yet to be reclaimed from exile, unfolding into actuality across the generations until Mashiach — and from that very root R’ Tzadok draws his closing, practical seal, that the study of Mishnayos is itself a segulah for length of days.

sections.en: The seventh level: when the individual returns, he and all the world are pardoned

items.h: המדרגה השביעית והעליונה שיחיד ששב מוחלין לו ולכל העולם כולו.

The theme: The seventh and highest rung: when a single individual repents, he and the whole world with him are forgiven. Because all souls together form one complete “stature” — the stature of Adam HaRishon — no one can be wholly rectified until all Israel are. A single unrectified point is felt throughout, as pain at the tip of the smallest limb is felt by the whole body.

p: [א] הַמַּדְרֵגָה אַחֲרוֹנָה וְהַשְּׁבִיעִית בִּגְדוּלַּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה, דְּיָחִיד שֶׁשָּׁב מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ וּלְכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ

The last and seventh rung in the greatness of teshuvah: that [when] an individual repents, they forgive him and the whole world with him.1121R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayeishev §9): "“and the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters” — and it is brought in Bereishis Rabbah, this is the spirit of Mashiach… by what merit? By the merit of teshuvah." Exactly the se’if’s seventh rung: the spirit that will rectify the whole stature is itself sustained by teshuvah — so the repentance of one individual is what draws the rectification of all.
וּבַעֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת [מַאֲמַר חִקּוּר דִּין ח״א פי״ד] פֵּירֵשׁ עַל חֶלְקָם בָּעֲרֵבוּת, עַיֵּין שָׁם וּבַמְפָרֵשׁ [אוֹת ט״ז]

And in the Asarah Maamaros [Maamar Chikur Din I:14] he explained [this forgiveness] as [pertaining] to “their portion in the mutual guaranteeship” — see there, and in the commentary [§16];1122Asarah Maamaros (Maamar Chikur Din I:14): “The Sages already noted, saying that on account of a single individual who did teshuvah such as this, they forgive the entire community. The explanation [of the Rav] is: their portion in the oath [at Sinai] — being sureties one for another — is what is pardoned in his merit; and this is correct.” The commentary Yad Yehudah explains: the Rav means that the community’s being forgiven through the individual’s teshuvah refers to that very sin of that individual — and they forgive the community their guarantorship [liability], since all Israel are guarantors one for another, as the Sages expounded on “and they shall stumble one over another” (Vayikra 26:37) — [each] over his brother’s sin. R’ Tzadok rejects this reading in favor of the plain sense: the penitent’s forgiveness truly extends to the whole world.
וְאֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה לִי, וְגַם דִּבְרֵי מַהֲרְשָׁ״א בְּחִדּוּשֵׁי אַגָּדוֹת שָׁם דָּחוּק

but this does not seem [correct] to me; and the words of the Maharsha, too, in Chiddushei Aggados there, are forced.1123Maharsha, Chiddushei Aggados, Yoma 86b (on “on account of an individual [who repents] they forgive the whole world”): He proposes to explain it as the Gemara says at the end of the first chapter of Kiddushin (40b) — a person should always regard the world as half innocent and half guilty; if he performs one mitzvah, fortunate is he, for he has tipped the whole world to the scale of merit. So here: even if the world is mostly guilty, if this one does complete teshuvah out of love, his willful sins become merits, and he thereby tips the entire world to the scale of merit, so that the whole world is forgiven. R’ Tzadok finds this forced, preferring that the individual penitent’s teshuvah itself — as the “heart” of the collective stature — draws healing to all.
אֲבָל לְדַעְתִּי הַפֵּירוּשׁ כִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ, וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית מַעֲלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה וִיצִיאָתָהּ לְפֹעַל גָּמוּר בְּתַכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתָהּ שֶׁהוּא בְּלֹא מֵצָרִים

But to my mind the explanation is according to its plain sense: and this is the ultimate elevation of teshuvah, and its emergence into complete actuality, in the ultimate perfection of its expansion — which is “without bounds [meitzarim]” —
וְאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁעוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה

and “there is nothing that stands before teshuvah.”1124“There is nothing that stands before teshuvah” (Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 3:14): having enumerated those who forfeit their share in the World to Come, the Rambam rules that even they — “if he repented from his wickedness and died as a baal teshuvah, he is among the people of the World to Come; for there is nothing that stands before teshuvah [she-ein lecha davar she-omed bifnei ha-teshuvah] — even one who denied the Ikkar all his days and repented at the last has a share in the World to Come.” Meforshim: the Rambam anchors this in “Peace, peace, to the far and to the near, says Hashem — and I will heal him” (Yeshayah 57:19) — the “far one” being the lifelong sinner whom teshuvah heals and draws near; it is the boundlessness of teshuvah’s reach, halted by no prior sin. R’ Tzadok’s use: this is precisely “the last and seventh rung in the greatness of teshuvah” — teshuvah “in the ultimate perfection of its expansion, which is ‘without bounds’ [b’lo meitzarim — evoking the limitless nachalah b’li metzarim of Shabbos 118a]” — so potent that when a single individual truly repents, “they forgive him and the whole world with him.”
וּלְפִי שֶׁכָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת כּוּלָּן קוֹמָה אַחַת שְׁלֵימָה, הוּא קוֹמַת אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁבּוֹ נִכְלְלוּ נַפְשׁוֹת כָּל צֶאֱצָאָיו
And since all the souls together are one complete “stature” — [namely] the stature of Adam HaRishon, in whom were included the souls of all his descendants —
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה] עַל פָּסוּק ״אֵיפֹה הָיִיתָ בְּיָסְדִי אָרֶץ״

as they said [in Shemos Rabbah] on the verse, “Where were you when I founded the earth?” (Iyov 38:4)1125Iyov 38:4 (Midrash): on “Where were you when I founded the earth?”, the Midrash teaches that the souls of all Israel were present, included within Adam HaRishon, at the founding of the world — the basis for R’ Tzadok’s point that all souls form a single “stature” and are bound up with one another from the very beginning of Creation.Chabad context - Tanya, Likkutei Amarim, ch. 32: The Alter Rebbe gives a particularly clear Chassidic formulation of the ontological unity that R' Tzadok uses here. All Israel, he writes, are literally brothers because 'kulan mat'imos ve'Av echad lekulanah' - all their souls correspond and share one Father - and therefore 'all Israel are called actual brothers from the root of their souls in Hashem Echad; only the bodies are divided.' The division belongs to bodily embodiment; at the level of shoresh haneshamah the many are already one. He therefore explains that the indwelling of the Divine light in Knesses Yisrael requires the souls to be joined 'lemehevei echad be'echad,' because the Shechinah does not rest in a place of spiritual fracture. This supplies an exact Chassidic background to R' Tzadok's insistence that the souls are not merely a federation of individuals who happen to share responsibility, but one complete komah. If the bodies are the principle, each person appears self-contained; if the soul-root is the principle, another Jew's deficiency is a deficiency in the same living unity. The extraordinary statement that one individual's complete teshuvah can extend forgiveness beyond himself thus begins from a metaphysical premise rather than a legal fiction: the individual who returns is not an isolated point. His movement occurs within the shared root in which Knesses Yisrael is already 'one in One.' —
וְעַל כֵּן אֲפִילּוּ מִי שֶׁשָּׁב בְּכָל לְבָבוֹ לַה׳ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְתַקֵּן לְגַמְרֵי כָּל זְמַן שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלָּם לֹא שָׁבוּ כְּמוֹהוּ, לִהְיוֹת נִתְקָן כָּל הַקּוֹמָה כּוּלָּהּ

therefore, even one who has repented with all his heart to Hashem cannot be entirely rectified so long as all Israel have not repented like him — [such that] the whole stature be rectified.1126R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach §1): “Israel is like a myrtle among thorns — for what is essential and not incidental does not change in the seed, for a man does not beget an animal; and all three Avos [are needed], only that Yaakov’s superiority is that he has in him also the trait of [the others].” Exactly the se’if: the souls form one stature because what joins them is essential and not incidental — which is why no single member can be finished while the rest are not.
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ נִיצוֹץ אֶחָד מִן הַקּוֹמָה שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקָן לְגַמְרֵי, הֲרֵי חִסְרוֹנוֹ גּוֹרֵם חִסָּרוֹן לְכָל הַקּוֹמָה
And as long as there is a single spark of the stature not entirely rectified, its lack causes a lack to the whole stature —
כְּמוֹ הָאָדָם כְּשֶׁכּוֹאֵב לוֹ צִפּוֹרֶן רַגְלוֹ הוּא מַרְגִּישׁ הַכְּאֵב מִכָּל הַגּוּף

like a person, when his toenail pains him, feels the pain throughout his whole body,1127R’ Tzadok — parallel (Divrei Chalomot §9): “each one has a star in the firmament — and so it is in the Tikunim, that the righteous are like stars, and each one has his own star.” Exactly the se’if: the stature is one, yet every member of it has his own fixed place — which is precisely why a single unrectified point holds back the whole, and why one man’s teshuvah reaches all.
וְגַם חָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁבְּמוֹחוֹ וּבִינָתוֹ שֶׁבְּלִבּוֹ, אֵבָרִים הָרָאשִׁים שֶׁבּוֹ, אֵין מְיוּשָּׁבִים עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַכְּאֵב שֶׁבִּקְצֵה אֵבֶר הַיּוֹתֵר קָטָן

and even his wisdom, in his brain, and his understanding, in his heart — the chief limbs within him — are unsettled by this pain at the tip of the smallest limb.1128Cf. Shevuos 39a (and Sanhedrin 27b): “all Israel are guarantors one for another [arevim zeh ba-zeh]” — the halachic root of the mutual bond underlying this siman. Maharal reads this principle through the very image R’ Tzadok uses here: Israel “are like a single man, so that if there is a wound in one of his limbs, all the limbs feel it, since they are one body.”Chassidic parallel - Be'er Mayim Chaim, Emor 21:1:2: The Be'er Mayim Chaim states almost the same bodily model as this se'if and pushes it to the same conclusion. 'Kol Yisrael guf echad heim' - all Israel are one body. Some souls function as the head, the 'rashei alfei Yisrael'; some as the eyes; the masses correspond to the lower limbs, legs and heels, but all together form one body of 248 limbs and 365 sinews. From this he draws a striking consequence: so long as the whole of Israel has not reached shleimus, even the choicest souls and the heads of Israel are not themselves complete, because blessing rests only upon a complete thing. He cites Chazal that Shmuel was worthy of a level of Shechinah comparable to Moshe but his generation was not worthy, and reads this literally through the common body: the imperfection of the generation limited the head. Conversely, the good of Israel raises its leaders. The same passage explains arvus from this bodily unity and compares harming another Jew to a hand striking another limb of one's own body. This is an unusually exact complement to R' Tzadok's claim that one unrectified spark leaves a chisaron in the entire komah. The common body means that completion cannot be purely private. It also explains why the ultimate teshuvah of the 'heart' or head can reverberate through the whole organism: the channels of merit and deficiency already run through a single living body before the individual act of return takes place.
וְעַל כֵּן ״אֵין אָדָם צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר (יַעֲשֶׂה טּוֹב וְלֹא יֶחֱטָא)״, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּצִּידוֹ הָיָה יָכוֹל לִישָּׁמֵר לִהְיוֹת צַדִּיק גָּמוּר בְּכָל דָּבָר

And therefore “there is no righteous man on earth who (does good and never sins)” (Koheles 7:20) — even though, from his own side, he could have guarded himself to be a complete tzaddik in everything —
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לִהְיוֹת נָקִי לְגַמְרֵי כָּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין הַדּוֹר כּוּלּוֹ כו׳
it is impossible for him to be entirely clean so long as the whole generation is not [rectified], etc.
וְחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁבַּדּוֹר וּבְכָל אָדָם פְּרָטִי שֶׁגּוֹרֵעַ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר הוּא נִרְגָּשׁ גַּם בּוֹ
And the deficiency in the generation — and in each private individual that diminishes Israel in that generation — is felt in him too:
וְלֹא דַּוְקָא שֶׁאוֹתוֹ הָרַע שֶׁל אָדָם הָאַחֵר פּוֹעֵל בּוֹ, רַק שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת יֵשׁ שֶׁמֶץ מֵחִסָּרוֹן זֶה גַּם בּוֹ, מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַכֹּל קוֹמָה אֶחָד

not [merely] that the other person’s evil acts upon him, but that in truth there is a trace of this deficiency in him as well — since all is one stature. — The perfection of teshuvah, then, is inescapably communal: the lone penitent has done all he can and yet remains, of necessity, incomplete until the last spark of the shared body is healed.

items.h: The theme: The heart is the wellspring of life to the whole body: when the heart is whole, no limb is spoiled, and every hurt is felt and healed through it. “God made man upright,” but the sin spoiled the whole stature. Teshuvah works in the same way — the heart draws fresh blood and vitality to the ailing limb, so that it returns to its health and its beauty.

p: [ב] וְהַלֵּב מִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים לְכָל הַגּוּף, וְכַאֲשֶׁר הַלֵּב בִּשְׁלֵימוּת לֹא יִהְיֶה קִלְקוּל בְּשׁוּם אֵבֶר מֵאֵבְרֵי הַגּוּף

And the heart — from it are “the wellsprings of life” (Mishlei 4:23)1129Mishlei 4:23: “מִכׇּל־מִשְׁמָר נְצֹר לִבֶּךָ, כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים” — “above all that you guard, guard your heart, for from it are the issues of life.” Meforshim: Rashi — guard your heart, more than any other watch, from evil thoughts; “for from it are the issues of life,” since the vitality of the whole body depends upon the heart. Metzudas David — the heart is the wellspring of life to all the limbs, and therefore must be guarded above all. R’ Tzadok’s use: the heart is “the wellsprings of life to the whole body,” so that “when the heart is in wholeness there is no spoilage in any limb,” and every healing flows from the heart, which “draws new blood and new vitality” to the ailing limb; and in each generation there is one soul who is “the heart of that generation,” the source of its life and the awakener of its teshuvah — and David, who “raised up the yoke of teshuvah,” is “the heart of the whole of Israel,” and therefore merited kingship. to the whole body; and when the heart is in [full] wholeness, there will be no spoilage in any of the body’s limbs.1130R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Mishpatim §4): “the rectification of lashon hara — the blemish of the tongue — is through occupying oneself with Torah; and as is alluded,”this shall be the Torah of the metzora" — that he who has an evil tongue, his purification is through Torah." Exactly the se’if: the blemished limb is not amputated but healed — the very faculty that was spoiled is the channel through which vitality is drawn back into it.
וְאִם יַגִּיעַ אֵיזֶה קִלְקוּל, הַקִּלְקוּל בָּא מִדָּם שֶׁבַּלֵּב, דְּבְרֵישׁ כָּל מַרְעִין אֲנָא דָּם, וְהוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ

And if some spoilage does occur, the spoilage comes from the blood in the heart — for “at the head of all illnesses am I, blood” — and it [the blood] is “the nefesh.”1131Bava Basra 58b: “At the head [reish] of all illnesses am I, blood” — i.e., disordered blood is the root of bodily ailment. And “the blood is the nefesh” (Devarim 12:23): Scripture identifies the blood with the life-force, which R’ Tzadok maps onto the heart as the seat of the soul and the source of both sickness and healing throughout the body.
וְכֵן אֲפִילּוּ קִלְקוּל וּכְאֵב הַבָּא מִבַּחוּץ לְאֵיזֶה אֵבֶר עַל יְדֵי הַכָּאָה וְכַיּוֹצֵא שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִמְשָׁךְ מֵהַלֵּב, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַלֵּב מַרְגִּישׁ
And likewise, even a spoilage or pain that comes from without to some limb — through a blow or the like — which does not stem from the heart, nonetheless the heart feels [it]:
לֹא בִּכְאֵב הָאֵבֶר, אֶלָּא שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַכְּאֵב פּוֹעֵל אֵיזֶה שִׁינּוּי בַּדָּם, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא מַרְגִּישׁ בַּלֵּב
not [directly] by the limb’s pain, but that through the pain some change is wrought in the blood, and thereby it is felt in the heart.
וְהַתִּיקּוּן אַחַר כָּךְ לְעוֹלָם הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַלֵּב הַמַּמְשִׁיךְ דָּם חָדָשׁ וְחִיּוּת חֲדָשָׁה לְאוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר שֶׁיּוּכַל לַחֲזוֹר לִבְרִיאוּתוֹ

And the healing, afterward, is always through the heart, which draws new blood and new vitality to that limb, so that it can return to its health.1132R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash §8): “that from the deed too no blemish would remain — for the deed was for the good,”for God sent me before you to preserve life“; for Yosef himself is appeased in this, since through it he became ruler over all Egypt.” Exactly the se’if’s healing: when the heart is whole, the hurt is not merely bandaged but re-read — the deed itself is found to have carried life.
וְ״הָאֱלֹקִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר״, אֶלָּא שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא וְנִתְקַלְקֵל כָּל הַקּוֹמָה
And “God made man upright” (Koheles 7:29) — except that the sin caused [otherwise], and the whole stature was spoiled.
וְעַל זֶה הוּא הַתְּשׁוּבָה, לְתַקֵּן לִהְיוֹת יָשָׁר כְּבָרִאשׁוֹנָה, וְאָז מִמֵּילָא הוּא בְּתוֹסֶפֶת שֶׁבַח וְהִידוּר כַּאֲשֶׁר יִתְיַישֵּׁר אַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל
And for this is teshuvah — to rectify [it], to be upright as at first; and then it is, of itself, with an added measure of praise and beauty, when it is straightened after the breach.
וְעִיקַּר הַתְּשׁוּבָה הוּא בַּלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״לְבָבוֹ יָבִין וָשָׁב״, וּמִמֶּנָּה הַתִּיקּוּן לְכָל הָאֵבָרִים
And the essence of teshuvah is in the heart, as it says, “his heart shall understand and repent” (Yeshayah 6:10) — and from it [comes] the rectification to all the limbs.
וּבְכָל דּוֹר יֵשׁ נֶפֶשׁ אֶחָד שֶׁהוּא הַלֵּב שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר, וּמִמֶּנָּה תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים לְכָל הַדּוֹר, וּבוֹ הוּא הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה לְכָל הַדּוֹר

And in every generation there is one soul who is “the heart” of that generation, and from it are the wellsprings of life to the whole generation, and in it is the awakening of teshuvah for the whole generation.
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ ע״ה שֶׁ״הֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה״ הוּא הַלֵּב שֶׁל כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְעַל כֵּן זָכָה לַמְּלוּכָה

And David HaMelech, who “raised up the yoke of teshuvah” (Moed Katan 16b),1133Moed Katan 16b: Expounding “the saying of David son of Yishai, and the saying of the man raised on high [al]” (II Shmuel 23:1): “the saying of David son of Yishai — who raised up the yoke of teshuvah [ulah shel teshuvah],” for through his deeds he taught the power of repentance (al and ulah share the same letters). This is the source of R’ Tzadok’s recurring epithet for David. is the heart of the whole of Israel — and therefore he merited kingship,1134R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §23): “the completeness of love is when it is mixed with fear, as it says in Tanna d’Bei Eliyahu, "I rejoiced from within my fear, and I feared from within my joy"; and at the beginning of the chapter [in Berachos], "and rejoice with trembling" is written.” Exactly the se’if: the heart is whole only when its two motions are joined in it — and it is from a whole heart that vitality is drawn to every ailing limb.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה] ״לֵב בַּגּוּף כְּמֶלֶךְ בָּעוֹלָם״

as they said [in Sefer Yetzirah], “the heart in the body is like a king in the world.”1135Sefer Yetzirah likens the ordering of the body to the ordering of the cosmos — “the heart in the body is like a king in the world” — the heart ruling and vivifying the limbs as a king rules his realm. Hence David, the “heart” of Israel and the awakener of its teshuvah, is fittingly the bearer of kingship.Direct Chabad parallel - Tanya, Likkutei Amarim, ch. 2: Tanya gives the organic hierarchy that stands immediately behind R' Tzadok's image of one soul as the 'heart' of a generation. Although there are innumerable levels of Jewish souls, the Alter Rebbe says, in every generation there are 'rashei alfei Yisrael' whose souls are literally the aspect of head and brain in relation to the souls of the populace. He then extends the bodily analogy down to the lowest level: even the toenails of a son still derive their vitality from the brain in the head, and likewise the vitality of the souls of ordinary Jews is drawn through the souls of the tzaddikim and sages who are the 'heads of the children of Israel' in their generation. This does not erase the individuality of the limbs; it explains how differentiated members remain one organism and how life can pass from a governing organ to the whole body. R' Tzadok identifies the decisive organ here not simply as the brain but as the heart, because 'mimenu totze'os chayim' and because teshuvah is principally an awakening of the heart. The two formulations therefore complement one another: Tanya provides the Chassidic anatomy of generational interdependence, while R' Tzadok identifies Davidic teshuvah as the pulse by which renewed life enters that organism. When the generational 'heart' returns in completeness, it is not merely setting a public example; it is renewing the flow of chiyus within the body to which all the other souls belong.

items.h: The theme: Malchus is the last of the middos — the “eighth” counting up to Binah, a mere point as the crown of Yesod. Yet in its expansion into a full stature it is so cherished that He calls her “My daughter,” “My sister,” “My mother.” For His dwelling among the lower ones, in this physical world, is the whole intent of Creation — “Israel arose first in thought.”

p: [ג] וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַדָּבָר יָדוּעַ שֶׁמִּדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת הִיא הָאַחֲרוֹנָה, וְהַשְּׁמִינִית לְבִינָה לָבֹא, וּבְסוֹד עֲטֶרֶת הַיְסוֹד בִּהְיוֹתָהּ נְקוּדָּה לְבַד
And even though the matter is known — that the middah of Malchus is the last, and “the eighth” [counting up] to Binah, and in the secret of the “crown of Yesod” it is but a [single] point —
אֲבָל בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתָהּ לְקוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה — קוֹמַת הַנּוּקְבָא, עַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (בשהש״ר) שֶׁכָּל כָּךְ מְחַבְּבָהּ עַד שֶׁקְּרָאָהּ ״בִּתִּי״ וַ״אֲחוֹתִי״ וְ״אִמִּי״

yet in its expansion into a complete stature — the stature of the Nukva — of this they said (in Shir HaShirim Rabbah) that He so cherishes her that He called her “My daughter,” “My sister,” and “My mother.”1136R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Yisro §6): “and they encircle Him like a crown; and in the Zohar,”who is His mother? This is the Yovel, the supernal Ima“; and in the Midrash,”He did not cease loving them until He called them ‘My mother.’"" Exactly the se’if: the very titles “My daughter, My sister, My mother” are the measure of how cherished the expanded stature of Malchus is — the last of the middos addressed in the language of the first.1137Shir HaShirim Rabbah (on the terms of endearment in Shir HaShirim): the Holy One so cherishes Knesses Yisrael that He calls her by three names of intimacy — “My daughter,” “My sister,” and “My mother” — corresponding to her being, at once, the emanated “daughter,” the “sister” who partners the six extremities, and the “mother” who is the source and goal of the whole emanation.

הַיְינוּ דִּכְלָלוּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנַּפְשָׁם ״חֵלֶק אֱלוֹקַּ מִמַּעַל״, דְּמַאן דְּנָפַח מִתּוֹכוֹ נָפַח, וַאֲצוּלִים מֵאֲצִילַת קָדְשׁוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהֶאֱצִיל בָּעֵת שֶׁעָלָה בִּרְצוֹנוֹ לִהְיוֹת מָקוֹם לִבְרִיאַת עוֹלָמוֹת

That is: the collective of Knesses Yisrael, whose soul is “a portion of God from above” (Iyov 31:2) — for “one who breathes, breathes from within himself”1138“One who breathes, breathes from within himself” (the Kabbalistic principle; cf. Ramban, Bereishis 2:7): explaining why the neshamah is “a portion of God from above” (Iyov 31:2), the tradition holds “man de-nafach mi-tocheih nafach” — one who blows breathes out from his own inner self; so when “He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life” (Bereishis 2:7), the soul given was from His very essence. Meforshim: the Ramban (Bereishis 2:7) — “he who breathes into the nostrils of another gives into him something of his own soul… the soul in man is of Divine essence,” from the foundation of Binah, “for the breath of Shaddai gives them understanding” (Iyov 32:8). R’ Tzadok’s use: the souls of Knesses Yisrael are literally “a portion of God from above,” emanated from His holy essence “when it arose in His will to be a place for the creation of worlds” — the lowest of the emanated rungs, yet the one able to clothe the Shechinah in this physical world. — and [who are] emanated from His holy emanation, which He emanated when it arose in His will to be a “place” for the creation of worlds —

הֵם הַמַּדְרֵגָה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁבַּמַּדְרֵגוֹת הַנֶּאֱצָלוֹת, שֶׁהִיא הַמַּדְרֵגָה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר שֶׁתִּתְלַבֵּשׁ בִּלְבוּשׁ הַגּוּפָנִי דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְלִהְיוֹת שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַגּוּפָנִי

they are the last rung among the emanated rungs — the rung that can clothe itself in the physical garment of this world, so that His Shechinah [dwells] among the lower ones and in this physical world.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא תַּכְלִית וְסוֹף כָּל הִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת הָאֲצִילוּת, שֶׁרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹרוֹ גַּם בְּדָרֵי מַטָּה, וְזֶה כָּל הַמְכוּוָּן בַּבְּרִיאָה

And this is the ultimate end of the whole chain of emanation — that Hashem willed His light be revealed even in the “dwellers below” — and this is the whole intent of Creation.1139R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Miketz §14): "“between light and darkness” — this is the holiness of the month, through the illumination of the moon; “and between Israel and the peoples” — this is the holiness of the circumcision, which separates between Israel and the peoples; “and between the seventh day and the six days of work” —" Exactly the se’if: the whole purpose of Creation is a dwelling below, and the marks of that dwelling are the very separations by which the lower world is bounded and made fit to hold it.Chabad context - Tanya, Likkutei Amarim, ch. 36: The Alter Rebbe formulates the purpose of Creation in terms that are nearly identical to R' Tzadok's description of Malchus as the final rung for whose sake the whole descent exists: 'tachlis bri'as olam hazeh hu shenis'aveh HaKadosh Baruch Hu lihyos lo dirah batachtonim.' The purpose of the entire hishtalshelus, he stresses, is not the higher worlds, for from their perspective every descent is a diminution of revealed light; the purpose is specifically this lowest physical world, the place of the greatest concealment, so that darkness itself may be transformed and the Infinite light revealed precisely there. He then says that the days of Mashiach, and especially techiyas hameisim, are the tachlis and shleimus of the creation of this world 'shelechach nivra mitchilaso' - the consummation for which it was created from the beginning. This provides a powerful parallel to R' Tzadok's 'achor va-kedem' structure. The tachton is chronologically and spiritually last, yet in intention it is first; the lowest point is the destination toward which the entire chain of worlds was ordered. Malchus is therefore precious not in spite of being the final receptacle but precisely because only there does the original Divine desire reach actuality. Teshuvah's seventh rung belongs to Malchus for the same reason: the final rectification is not an escape from the lower world but the disclosure that the lower world and the collective human stature were the intended dwelling from the outset.
וְעַל כֵּן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם הַסּוֹף מִכָּל הַבְּרִיאָה, הֵם גַּם כֵּן הָרֹאשׁ וְעִיקָּר לַכֹּל, דְּ״סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה״, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל עָלוּ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה
And therefore, even though they are the end of all creation, they are also the head and essence of all — for “the end of the deed [is] in thought first,” and “Israel arose in [His] thought.”

וְזֶהוּ ״אָחוֹר וָקֶדֶם צַרְתָּנִי״, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אַחַר הַגִּיעָם לִשְׁלֵימוּתָם, שֶׁנִּשְׁלְמָה כַּוָּונַת כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה עַל יְדֵי הָאָדָם, הֲרֵי הוּא קֶדֶם וְרֹאשׁ הַכֹּל, שֶׁעַל זֶה הָיָה רֵאשִׁית הַמְכוּוָּן בִּבְרִיאַת עוֹלָם

And this is “back and front You have formed me” (Tehillim 139:5)1140Tehillim 139:5: “אָחוֹר וָקֶדֶם צַרְתָּנִי, וַתָּשֶׁת עָלַי כַּפֶּכָה” — “back and front You have formed me, and laid Your hand upon me.” Meforshim: Rashi and the Radak read it of God’s all-encompassing formation of man — fashioning him “behind and before,” enclosing him on every side. Chazal (Berachos 61a; Eruvin 18a) expound “achor va-kedem” of Adam HaRishon, created “du-partzufin” — with two faces, back and front. R’ Tzadok’s use: he reads it of man’s place in the order of creation — man is “achor,” the last of all creatures (“the end of the deed”), yet also “kedem,” the first and head (“thought first”), “for on this was the first intent in the creation of the world”; when he reaches his perfection, and the whole purpose of Creation is fulfilled through him, he is revealed as its very head.: for in truth, after they reach their perfection — when the whole intent of Creation is completed through man — he is [then] “front” and head of all, for on this was the first intent in the creation of the world.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁקְּרָאָהּ ״אִמִּי״, שֶׁהִיא הַמָּקוֹר הַמּוֹלִידָה כָּל הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת שֵׁשׁ קְצָווֹת הָאֲצִילוּת

And this is why He called her “My mother” — for she is the source that gives birth to the whole expansion of the six extremities of emanation:1141R’ Tzadok — parallel (Kometz HaMinchah II §58): “"may you become thousands of myriads" — as in the Zohar, that the blessing of Hashem is never less than a thousand… and the blessing is the utmost of the multiplication that the vessel can receive, and its filling — as with the oil of Elisha, and in the Sages’ language, "a vessel holds blessing."” Exactly the se’if: Malchus is a mere point at its root, and its whole preciousness is that, expanded into a full stature, it becomes the vessel able to hold what is poured into it.

כִּי הָעוֹמֶק אַחֲרִית הוּא עַצְמוֹ הָעוֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית, בְּסוֹד ״נָעוּץ סוֹפָן בִּתְחִלָּתָן״, דְּכָל הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הָאֲצִילוּת הָיָה כְּדֵי לְהַגִּיעַ לְהַתַּכְלִית שֶׁהוּא בִּנְיַן קוֹמַת הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים, וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַתְחָלַת הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת

for “the depth of the end” is itself “the depth of the beginning,” in the secret of “their end is embedded in their beginning” (Sefer Yetzirah 1:7)1142Sefer Yetzirah 1:7: “Ten Sefiros Belimah — their end is fixed in their beginning and their beginning in their end, like a flame bound to a coal.” R’ Tzadok invokes this for Malchus, the “end of the deed,” which is rooted in and returns to the “beginning” — the structure underlying the seventh-rung ascent of teshuvah. — for the whole expansion of emanation was in order to reach the ultimate purpose, which is the building of the stature of Knesses Yisrael and the resting of the Shechinah among the lower ones; and this [purpose] is [thus] the very root of the beginning of the expansion.

items.h: The theme: “A woman of valor” — though she is one of his ribs, taken from the low part of the body, once built into a full stature she becomes “the crown of her husband.” She and Binah are the two heh’s of the Name: the last heh comes after the six extremities, the first precedes them. That first heh is the secret of Olam Haba, in which evil is wholly removed from the world.

p: [ד] וְעַל כֵּן ״אֵשֶׁת חַיִל״, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא אַחַת מִצַּלְעוֹתָיו בְּתַחְתִּית גּוּפוֹ, מְקוֹם שֶׁהִסְגִּיר בָּשָׂר תַּחְתֶּיהָ, אַחַר שֶׁנִּבְנֵית קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה נַעֲשֵׂית ״עֲטֶרֶת בַּעְלָהּ״

And therefore “a woman of valor” — even though she is one of his ribs, at the lower part of his body, “the place where He closed up flesh beneath it” (cf. Bereishis 2:21)1143Bereishis 2:21: “וַיַּפֵּל ה’ אֱלֹהִים תַּרְדֵּמָה עַל הָאָדָם וַיִּישָׁן, וַיִּקַּח אַחַת מִצַּלְעֹתָיו וַיִּסְגֹּר בָּשָׂר תַּחְתֶּנָּה” — “And Hashem God cast a deep sleep upon the man, and he slept; and He took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.” Meforshim: Rashi — “one of his ribs [tzela]” means one of his sides, for [in the Sages’ reading] Adam was created “du-partzufin” (two-faced), and the woman was built from one side; “and closed up the flesh in its place” — over the site of the incision. R’ Tzadok’s use: the “woman of valor” — Knesses Yisrael as Malchus, the Nukva — originates as “one of his ribs, at the lower part of his body, the place where He closed up flesh beneath it,” a low and hidden place; yet once she is “built into a complete stature” she becomes “the crown of her husband” (Mishlei 12:4) — the upper heh of the Name, the secret of Olam Haba. — after she is built into a complete stature, she becomes “the crown of her husband” (Mishlei 12:4).1144R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Chayei Sarah §1): “and at the entry of Shabbos every one of Israel merits an additional soul, a new soul; and as it says in the Zohar,”a soul in which is all completeness, of the pattern of the World to Come" — and for this reason it is called Shabbos." Exactly the se’if: the first heh, which precedes the six extremities, is the secret of Olam Haba — and its foretaste is precisely the completeness that arrives from above, not from the six days’ labor.
וְהֵם סוֹד שְׁתֵּי הַהֵ״הִין דְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה, דְּיֵ״ה אַחֲרוֹנָה בָּאָה אַחַר הַשֵּׁשׁ קְצָווֹת, וְהָרִאשׁוֹנָה קוֹדֶמֶת לָהֶם, וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד, רַק זֶה הַסּוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה וְזֶה הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה

And they are the secret of the two heh’s of the Name Havayah: the last heh comes after the six extremities, and the first precedes them — and all is one, only that this [last] is “end of deed” and this [first] is “thought first.”1145R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Bereishis §1): “"and the reward of a transgression is a transgression" — meaning that from the transgression itself is made the fire of Gehinnom, as it says, "your spirit is a fire that consumes you," and as in the Midrash, a fire that issues from the body of the wicked and blazes them.” Exactly the se’if: the nations are the “dross” thrown off by Adam’s sin — the evil is not an external punishment but the sin’s own by-product, which is what Avraham’s building had to be separated from.
וְאַחַר שֶׁמַּגִּיעִים לִשְׁלֵימוּת הַסּוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה, אָז מַשִּׂיגִים הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ דְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה, דְּיֵ״ה עֶלְיוֹנָה, שֶׁהוּא סוֹד עוֹלָם הַבָּא כַּנּוֹדָע

And after one reaches the perfection of the “end of deed,” then one attains the root of “thought first” — the upper heh — which is the secret of Olam Haba, as is known.1146R’ Tzadok — parallel (Pri Tzaddik, Mishpatim §9): “and the matter is that”God made this over against that" — and just as in holiness Keser is Keser, [so in the other side]." Exactly the se’if’s two heh’s: the order is built of answering pairs, so that the “crown of her husband” is not a borrowed honor but a place opposite and answering to his.Chabad parallel - Torah Ohr, Vaera 5:36: Torah Ohr states the kabbalistic principle of this se'if almost word for word: 'sof ma'aseh hu davka bemachshavah techilah, vena'utz techilasan besofan,' and for that reason Malchus is called 'eishes chayil ateres ba'alah' and also 'eretz chefetz' - the land of desire - because the highest will is revealed specifically in it. This makes precise why R' Tzadok does not treat the ascent of the final heh as an accidental promotion of what was originally low. The end becomes a crown because the beginning was hidden in the end all along. The lower land is the arena where the intention that preceded the chain of emanation becomes an accomplished reality, and therefore its completed form can rise above the stages that merely transmitted the intention. In this light, 'ateres ba'alah' is not an inversion of the created order but its disclosure: what appeared as recipient is shown to have carried the deepest ratzon from the first. This also clarifies the relation between teshuvah and the seventh middah. Teshuvah is able to reveal a beginning within an end - a primordial Divine intent within a history that, on its surface, came later and descended lower. R' Tzadok's future transformation of the lower eretz into the upper eretz is thus the cosmic version of the same movement by which teshuvah returns a person from the last consequence of his history to the thought and will in which his true purpose began.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ [בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק חֵלֶק] ״כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא״ מִקְּרָא דְּ״יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ״

And therefore they said [at the start of Perek Chelek] “all Israel have a share in Olam Haba,” from the verse “they shall inherit the land” (Yeshayah 60:21; Sanhedrin 90a).1147Mishnah, Sanhedrin 90a (Perek Chelek): “All Israel have a share in the World to Come, as it says, ‘and your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever’ (Yeshayah 60:21).” R’ Tzadok reads “land [eretz]” as the lowest rung (Malchus) which, in the Future, is itself transformed into “the upper land” — so that inheriting the land is the inheritance of Olam Haba.Izhbitz-Radzin context - Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 6:1: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin develops Malchus in a way that strikingly complements the present se'if. Malchus is the final middah, he writes, 'shebah nigmar hahavayah mikol seder hahishtalshelus bishleimus hagamur'; it is the last point of concealment, so distant from the source that Creation can appear to possess an independent existence. Precisely that concealment makes bechirah and coronation possible: the creature can stand within apparent independence and nevertheless choose to crown Hashem. Malchus is therefore 'leis lah migarmah klum' and yet the completion of all the middos, because its entire action is an or chozer that recognizes and returns the upper will. Sod Yesharim then explains the moon's claim of two kings using one crown: since the whole Divine intention reaches completion through Malchus, she senses a genuine root-superiority. In the present world, however, evil is not yet fully clarified, so Malchus must accept tzimtzum - 'lechi u'ma'ati es atzmech.' Only in the Future, after the birurim are complete, will 'eishes chayil ateres ba'alah' be openly true and 'Keser Elyon ihu Keser Malchus' become revealed. This distinction is exactly the one R' Tzadok needs. The final heh is rooted above the six middos, but its superiority cannot yet be lived as unrestricted self-assertion. Present avodah requires constriction, humility and Torah-defined bechirah; future shleimus reveals why the lowest, after faithfully completing its task, was rooted in the highest all along.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּאֶרֶץ הִיא הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַיּוֹתֵר תַּחְתּוֹנָה, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֶּעָתִיד אֶרֶץ הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה עַצְמָהּ הִיא עַצְמָהּ מִתְהַפֶּכֶת לִהְיוֹת אֶרֶץ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה
And it is known that “land [eretz]” is the lowest rung — except that, in the Future, the lower land itself turns into the upper land;

וְהָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עַצְמוֹ מִתְהַפֵּךְ בְּהִתְחַדְּשׁוּת הָעוֹלָם לִהְיוֹת עוֹלָם הַבָּא, כַּאֲשֶׁר מִתְעַלִּים הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּהַגִּיעָם לְתַכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּתָם שֶׁיִּתְבַּעֵר הָרַע מִן הָעוֹלָם לְגַמְרֵי

and this world itself turns, in the renewal of the world, into Olam Haba — when the souls of Israel are elevated on reaching the ultimate of their perfection, so that evil is wholly removed from the world.

items.h: The theme: Mashiach is David himself — but David was the beginning of the effort from the side of “end of deed,” while Mashiach is the completion of the stature as it stands in “thought first.” Reaching the root of “thought first” itself is Olam Haba; the days of Mashiach precede it. This is the utmost perfection a person can reach while still in this world.

p: [ה] וּמֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ הוּא דָּוִד בְּעַצְמוֹ כַּיָּדוּעַ, אֶלָּא שֶׁדָּוִד הָיָה הַתְחָלַת הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת מִצַּד סוֹף הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, וּמָשִׁיחַ הוּא סִיּוּם שְׁלֵימוּת הַקּוֹמָה כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה

And the King Mashiach is David himself, as is known1148“The King Mashiach is David himself” (Yirmiyah 30:9; Yechezkel 37:24-25): the prophets call the Messianic king simply “David” — “they shall serve Hashem their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up for them” (Yirmiyah 30:9); “My servant David shall be king over them, and one shepherd shall be for them all” (Yechezkel 37:24), “and David My servant shall be prince to them forever” (37:25).
