The source is an ethical warning about recurrent human temptation, not a claim that every person commits these offenses, and not a biological, ethnic, or scientific generalization. Its immediate context concerns patterns of moral vulnerability. Rav Tzadok’s phrase ‘the common minority’ is his explanatory paraphrase of that prevalence, not a quotation from the Gemara. This distinction preserves individual responsibility: prevalence explains the choice of example but neither excuses misconduct nor predetermines any person’s actions.
וְגַם עִיקַּר שְׁלִיטַת אֵשׁ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם הוּא לְכַלּוֹת אֵשׁ דְּיִצְרָא דַּעֲרָיוֹת שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן אֵשׁ
and furthermore the primary function of the fire of Gehinnom is to purge the fire of the lust for arayos, which is likewise fire,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר [בְּהוֹשֵׁעַ ז:ד]: ״כֻּלָּם מְנָאָפִים כְּמוֹ תַנּוּר בֹּעֵרָה וְגוֹמֵר, בֹּעֵר כְּאֵשׁ לֶהָבָה״
as it is said: "They are all adulterers, as an oven heated... it burns as a flaming fire" (Hoshea 7:4, 6);
וּבְקִדּוּשִׁין [פ״א עַמּוּד א׳]: ״נוּרָא בֵּי עַמְרָם וְכוּלֵיהּ, חֲזִי דְּאַתְּ נוּרָא״

and in Kiddushin [81a]: "Fire in the house of Amram! ... See that you are made of fire!";1118Hoshea 7:4–7; Kiddushin 81a; Resisei Layla 5:1 — desire and judgment figured as fire: Hoshea portrays adulterous passion and political treachery as an oven that smolders and then blazes. Kiddushin recounts Rav Amram’s cry ‘fire in the house of Amram’; Rashi explains that he summoned the neighbors so that public shame would help him break the impulse, after which he addressed the yetzer as fire. The Bavli presents a concrete act of resistance, not resignation to desire. Rav Tzadok, in Resisei Layla 5:1, later identifies immersion in bodily desire with the darkness of this world and interprets the judgment of Gehinnom as corresponding to that immersion. His present statement that one fire consumes another is therefore a homiletic and spiritual synthesis of these images, not the plain meaning of Hoshea and not a medical or scientific description. Desire may be intense or involuntary at its onset, but chosen conduct remains accountable; Rav Amram’s response models creating barriers and seeking help before sin.
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים מוּכָח, דְּמַה שֶּׁאִיתָא שָׁם דְּאֵין שׁוֹלֵט בְּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל רַק בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, קָאֵי עַל עִסְקֵי חִנָּם שֶׁהַכֹּל יוֹרְדִין
and in any event it is proven that what is stated there—that it lacks dominion over the sinners of Israel but only over the nations—applies to these matters of unprovoked lust for which all descend,
וַעֲלֵיהֶם בְּיִחוּד שַׁיָּיךְ הָא דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מַסֵּיק לְהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַכָּרַת הַמִּילָה שֶׁבִּבְשָׂרָם, שֶׁהוּא תִּיקּוּן לִפְגַם הַבְּרִית

and regarding them specifically applies the tradition that Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, draws them out through recognizing the circumcision in their flesh, which rectifies the blemish of the Covenant.1119Bereishis 17:9–14 and Eruvin 19a — milah as covenantal sign and Avraham’s recognition: Bereishis calls circumcision ‘the sign of the covenant’ and ‘My covenant in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.’ Eruvin’s Aggadah says that Avraham raises those he recognizes as circumcised, except one whose foreskin is symbolically ‘drawn’ through relations with a gentile woman. The Gemara explicitly supplies the recognition motif; Rav Tzadok adds the interpretive claim that the covenantal mark is the tikkun corresponding to pegam habris. That is his theological synthesis, not the verse’s plain meaning. The imagery of a drawn foreskin is Aggadic and covenantal rather than a biological or racial statement, and it should not be applied to contemporary peoples as an ethnic classification. Nor does covenantal rescue permit the offense: the act remains prohibited and morally serious, and the se’if’s point concerns the enduring covenantal identity through which correction remains possible.
וּבַחֲגִיגָה שָׁם לֹא נְהִירָא לְהוּ לוֹמַר דְּהָנֵי לָאו בִּכְלַל פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְכָתְבוּ דִּבְבָבָא מְצִיעָא לָאו בְּגֵיהִנָּם מַיְירֵי, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם

And in Chagigah there it was unsatisfactory to Tosafos to say that these three are excluded from the sinners of Israel, so they wrote that in Bava Metzia it does not deal with Gehinnom at all, see there;
וְזֶהוּ לְפִי מַה שֶּׁהֶעְתִּיקוּ שָׁם הַלָּשׁוֹן סְתָם ״יוֹרְדִין וְאֵין עוֹלִין״ וְלֹא פֵּירְשׁוּ לְהֵיכָן יוֹרְדִין

and this was based on the fact that they transcribed the text there simply as "descend and do not ascend," without specifying where they descend;1120Chagigah 27a: “R’ Abahu said in the name of R’ Elazar: the fire of Gehinnom has no power over Torah scholars — [by] a kal va-chomer from the salamander: if a salamander, which is an offspring of fire, [such that] one who smears its blood [on himself], the fire has no power over him — Torah scholars, whose whole body is fire, as it is written ‘is not My word like fire, says Hashem,’ all the more so. Reish Lakish said: the fire of Gehinnom has no power over the sinners of Israel — [by] a kal va-chomer from the golden altar: if the golden altar, upon which there is only [gold] the thickness of a golden dinar, [and yet] for many years the fire had no power over it — the sinners of Israel, who are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate, as it is written ‘like a slice of pomegranate is your temple [rakasech]’ — read not ‘rakasech’ but ‘the empty ones [reikanin] among you’ — all the more so.” Tosafos: “‘The fire of Gehinnom has no power over the sinners of Israel, etc.’ — it appears to me that [this is] not [regarding] ‘the sinners of Israel with their bodies,’ for we say in Rosh Hashanah (17a) [that regarding] ‘the sinners of Israel with their bodies,’ Gehinnom is consumed and they are not consumed; rather, it speaks of some [partial] sinners, and because Avraham raises them all [from Gehinnom] except one who has relations with a gentile-woman, whose foreskin is drawn over him, as it says at the start of Osin Pasin (Eruvin 19a). And that which we say at the end of HaZahav (Bava Metzia 58b), ‘all descend and ascend except three’ — that is not speaking of Gehinnom, but of another place to be judged; and even the one judged, after twelve months they ascend, and are judged no more than a full year.”
אֲבָל אֵין לְגִירְסָה זוֹ טַעַם וּבֵיאוּר, דְּוַדַּאי צָרִיךְ לְהִתְפָּרֵשׁ לְאֵיזֶה מָקוֹם יוֹרְדִין, וּלְפָנֵינוּ הַגִּירְסָא ״יוֹרְדִין לְגֵיהִנָּם״ וְהוּא עִיקָּר וַדַּאי
but this textual reading has no coherence, for it must certainly be explained to what place they descend, and in our text the reading is "descend to Gehinnom," which is certainly the primary reading;
וְעַל גֵּיהִנָּם שַׁיָּיךְ לְשׁוֹן יְרִידָה לְפִי שֶׁעֲמוּקָה כְּגַיְא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּעֵירוּבִין שָׁם], וְאִם כֵּן הֲרֵי מְפוֹרָשׁ דְּהַךְ ״אֵין עוֹלִין״ מִגֵּיהִנָּם קָאָמַר
and regarding Gehinnom the term "descent" is fitting because it is deep as a valley as they said [in Eruvin 19a], so that if so, it is explicit that this "do not ascend" refers to Gehinnom.
וְגַם יֵשׁ לְעַיֵּין מִבּוֹעֵל אֲרַמִּית שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם דְּאֵין אַבְרָהָם מַעֲלֵהוּ, וּלְפִי דִּבְרֵיהֶם גַּם זֶה אֵינוֹ בִּכְלַל הָנֵי פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל

And one must also examine one who cohabits with a gentile woman (bo'el aramis), regarding whom they stated there that Avraham does not draw him up (Eruvin 19a), where according to their words he too is excluded from these protected sinners of Israel;
וּבְתוֹסָפוֹת [בָּבָא מְצִיעָא שָׁם] הִקְשׁוּ הָא דְּלָא חָשְׁבִינַן שָׁם, וְתֵירְצוּ דְּאֵינוֹ בִּשְׁבִיל עֲבֵירָה זוֹ לְבַד בְּלֹא עֲבֵירָה אַחֶרֶת שֶׁמֵּחֲמָתָהּ יוֹרֵד, עַיֵּין שָׁם

and in Tosafos [Bava Metzia 58b] they asked why he was not enumerated there, answering that one does not descend on account of this transgression alone without another sin, see there;1121Bava Metzia 58b: “R’ Chanina said: all descend to Gehinnom except three. ‘All’?! Can it enter your mind [that all descend]? Rather, say: all who descend to Gehinnom ascend, except three who descend and do not ascend. And these are they: one who comes upon a married woman, one who whitens his fellow’s face in public, and one who calls his fellow by a derogatory name.” Tosafos: “Thus is its explanation: all who descend ascend immediately, and the fire of Gehinnom has no power over them, as we say in Perek Osin Pasin (Eruvin 19a) [by] a kal va-chomer from the golden altar, and in the last chapter of Chagigah (27a) [where] he made a kal va-chomer from the salamander — except three who do not ascend immediately; but some of them are judged forever, such as [the heretics], and some ascend after twelve months, such as [the sinners of Israel]. And yet it is difficult that [R’ Chanina] did not count ‘the sinners of Israel with their bodies,’ such as the skull that does not don tefillin, of whom we say in Rosh Hashanah that they descend and are judged there twelve months, and afterward their body and soul are burned.”

וְלֹא הֵבַנְתִּי דִּבְרֵיהֶם: וְכִי עַל עֲוֹן דְּבוֹעֵל אֲרַמִּית אֵין לוֹ לֵירֵד גֵּיהִנָּם לְקַבֵּל עֹונֶשׁ, וְכֵיוָן שֶׁיּוֹרֵד וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אֵין מַעֲלֵהוּ הֲרֵי אֵין עוֹלֶה מִמֵּילָא גַּם בַּעֲבֵירָה זוֹ לְבַד לְפִי דִּבְרֵיהֶם

yet I cannot understand their words: does one not descend to Gehinnom to receive punishment for cohabiting with a gentile woman? And once he descends and Avraham Avinu does not draw him up, he consequently never ascends even for this sin alone according to their logic!
וּבְתוֹסָפוֹת [בְּעֵירוּבִין שָׁם] דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל ״בַּר״ תֵּירְצוּ דְּזֶה עוֹלֶה כְּשֶׁקִּבֵּל דִּינוֹ, עַיֵּין שָׁם
And in Tosafos [Eruvin 19a, s.v. bar] they resolved that he ascends once he has received his full judgment, see there;

וְזֶה לֹא יִצְדַּק רַק כְּשֶׁנֹּאמַר דְּהָנֵי אֵין עוֹלִים לְעוֹלָם, וְלֹא כְּפִי דִּבְרֵיהֶם [בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא] דְּגַם הָנֵי עוֹלִין אַחַר י״ב חֹדֶשׁ דְּאָז קִבְּלוּ דִּינָם, וְאִם כֵּן אַכַּתִּי לִיחְשְׁבֵיהּ

and this is justified only if we maintain that those three never ascend, and not as they wrote in Bava Metzia that even those three ascend after twelve months once they receive their judgment, for if so, let the Gemara still enumerate him!1122Tosafos, Eruvin (s.v. “bar”): “‘except one who comes, etc.’ — it is not applicable to count him among [the three] of HaZahav (Bava Metzia 58b) regarding three who descend to Gehinnom and do not ascend, for this one ascends when he has received his judgment. And that which [R’ Chanina] did not count there ‘the sinners of Israel with their bodies’ and the Tzedukim, etc., who do not ascend? — because they are taught in a baraisa. And even though ‘one who whitens his fellow’s face’ is counted and taught in Mesechta Avos, in any case it teaches us that ‘one who calls a derogatory name’ is [like] ‘one who whitens,’ even though he is habituated to his name.”

וַאֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא דְּזֶה דִּינוֹ בְּפָחוֹת מִי״ב חֹדֶשׁ, אַטּוּ י״ב חֹדֶשׁ נִזְכַּר הָתָם, וְכֵיוָן שֶׁאֵין עוֹלִין מִיָּד עַל יְדֵי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם רַק מִשֶּׁיְּקַבֵּל דִּינוֹ כָּל אֶחָד לְפִי דִּינוֹ הֲוָה לֵיהּ לַחְשׁוֹב לְפִי דִּבְרֵיהֶם

And even if you say that his judgment lasts less than twelve months, is twelve months mentioned there? Once he does not ascend immediately through Avraham Avinu but only after receiving his judgment, the Gemara should have listed him according to their approach.
וְהַתּוֹסָפוֹת [בָּבָא מְצִיעָא] הִכְרִיחוּ דִּבְרֵיהֶם מִמַּה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָא עַל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, וְאִי לָא נֵימָא כֵּן הָדְרָא קוּשְׁיָאתָם

And Tosafos in Bava Metzia compelled their conclusion from the fact that they stated that one who cohabits with a married woman possesses a portion in the World to Come (Sanhedrin 107a), and were we not to say so their difficulty would return;

וְגַם בַּבָּרַיְיתָא [דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שָׁם] מַשְׁמַע דְּהַכֹּל מְצַפְצְפִין וְעוֹלִים מִגֵּיהִנָּם חוּץ מִפּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּגוּפָן מִדְּמִינַּן לְהוּ בְּפוֹשְׁעֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, וְלֹא הוֹצִיא אֵלּוּ מֵהַכְּלָל:

and likewise in the Baraisa of Rosh Hashanah it implies that all cry out and ascend from Gehinnom except for bodily sinners of Israel who are equated to bodily sinners of the nations, and it did not exclude these three from the general rule.

items.h: The theme: Critique of the Rama MiFano regarding the three who descend. In Asarah Ma'amaros (Chakor Din 3:8, 16), the Rama MiFano wrote that had these three descended into Gehinnom, its fire would have consumed them entirely; therefore, they do not descend to Gehinnom at all, but are judged in a separate, non-annihilating purgatory. R' Tzadok refutes this: the Gemara in Eruvin 19a explicitly states that all sinners descend to Gehinnom for illicit sexual relations (isqei chinam), which primarily denotes a married woman. Cohabiting with a married woman is cited in Bava Metzia merely as the most prevalent example of forbidden relations, and cannot be treated as more severe than incestuous capital crimes carrying severe executions.

p: וְרָאִיתִי בַּ״עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת״ [מַאֲמַר חֲקוֹר דִּין חֵלֶק ג׳ פֶּרֶק ח׳ וּפֶרֶק ט״ז] כָּתַב: דְּהָנֵי ג׳ אִלּוּ יָרְדוּ לְגֵיהִנָּם הָיָה מְכַלֶּה אוֹתָן לְגַמְרֵי וְאֵין עוֹלִין

And I saw in Asarah Ma'amaros [Chakor Din 3:8, 16] who wrote: had these three descended into Gehinnom, it would have consumed them completely and they would never ascend;1123Rosh Hashanah 17a — separate judgment categories and Rav Tzadok’s cross-reading: The baraita distinguishes balanced persons, ‘sinners of Israel with their bodies,’ and the more radical categories of heresy, denial, separation from the community, and leading the public into sin. Those with half merits and half sins who also bear the bodily offense pass through refining fire; those with predominantly sinful deeds in that class are judged for twelve months and described as becoming ash beneath the righteous; the final group is judged for generations. The baraita itself does not list Bava Metzia’s three offenses or explain their relation to Avraham’s immediate raising in Eruvin. Rav Tzadok therefore tests Tosafos’ harmonization by comparing separate sugyos and asking whether the proposed time distinction can account for every case. His conclusion is a later interpretive analysis, not the explicit statement of Rosh Hashanah. The next se’if introduces the Asarah Maamaros’ alternative resolution, showing that Rav Tzadok is openly weighing competing models rather than presenting one as uncontested peshat.1124Bava Metzia 58b; Berachos 34b; Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 2:9 and 3:14 — severity without closing teshuvah: Bava Metzia places adultery, public humiliation, and a degrading nickname in its severe Aggadic list; the surrounding sugya calls verbal mistreatment graver than monetary exploitation and compares public humiliation to bloodshed. Yet Tosafos’ own qualification, quoted here, assumes cases without teshuvah. Rabbi Abbahu in Berachos teaches that baalei teshuvah may stand where the completely righteous cannot, while Rabbi Yochanan disputes the ranking but not the efficacy of return. Rambam states explicitly that even those described as lacking a share in the World to Come regain it when they repent, because nothing stands before teshuvah. For wrongs against another person, however, repentance also requires restitution where applicable and sincere appeasement and forgiveness. Rav Tzadok’s project of Takanas HaShavin rests on this distinction: severe rhetoric safeguards accountability, while teshuvah prevents despair. Providential purpose or eventual correction never retroactively permits the wrongdoing.
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא יָרְדוּ כִּלְשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא שָׁם מֵעִיקָּרָא, רַק נִידּוֹנִים בְּדִין אַחֵר
therefore they do not descend into Gehinnom at all, but are judged under a different divine judgment

[וְעַל פִּי דְּבָרָיו יִתְיַישְּׁבוּ דִּבְרֵי תּוֹסָפוֹת חֲגִיגָה הַנַּ״ל עַל הָנֵי ג׳ גַּם לְגִירְסָא דִּידַן, אֲבָל הֵם לֹא כִּיוְּנוּ לָזֶה וְדִבְרֵיהֶם מַשְׁמַע דְּהוּא עַל כָּל הַיּוֹרְדִים שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם

[and according to his words, the words of Tosafos in Chagigah regarding these three would be reconciled even according to our text; yet Tosafos did not intend this, their words implying that it applies to all who descend;1125Asarah Maamaros, Maamar Chakor Din III:8, 16 — “another judgment” as a proposed reconciliation: The Asarah Maamaros distinguishes between descent into Gehinnom and a different mode of judgment for the three offenses singled out in Bava Metzia 58b. In his model, ordinary Gehinnom would consume these offenders entirely, so Divine mercy does not place them there; the liability remains, but is administered through another judgment. The Bavli itself does not identify such an alternate tribunal in this passage. Rav Tzadok therefore treats the proposal as a later reconciliation, reports how it could resolve Tosafos, and then tests whether it can be squared with the broader sugyos. His disagreement is exegetical: he is not denying the gravity of the offenses, but questioning whether the sources support annihilation as their defining consequence.
וְגַם הָ״עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת״ לֹא נִסְתַּיֵּיעַ מִדִּבְרֵיהֶם אַף שֶׁרִימֵּז לָהֶם שָׁם בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק ט״ז

and the Asarah Ma'amaros did not support himself from their words, although he alluded to them at the end of ch. 16;1126Bava Metzia 58b and Tosafos, s.v. chutz mi-sheloshah — the precise meaning of “do not ascend”: The Gemara first says that all descend except three, then corrects the formulation: all who descend ultimately ascend, except three who descend and do not ascend. Tosafos rejects reading this as eternal non-ascent for all three, because the adulterer is elsewhere described as retaining a share in the World to Come. Tosafos therefore explains that ordinary offenders ascend immediately, while the three do not ascend immediately; one who committed adultery may ascend after twelve months, whereas public humiliation and a degrading nickname may involve the separate category of having no share in the World to Come. Tosafos also offers the possibility that after twelve months they are neither judged nor living in the World to Come, and concludes expressly that the discussion concerns cases without teshuvah, since teshuvah is effective for every matter. This is the textual basis for Rav Tzadok’s insistence that “another judgment” alone does not answer the question of eventual ascent.
עַיֵּין שָׁם מַה שֶּׁהֵבִיא מִשָּׁם דְּיִישְּׁבוּ קוּשְׁיָאתָם בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא בְּדִין אַחֵר, לֹא יָדַעְתִּי כַּוָּונָתוֹ כִּי לֹא נִמְצָא שָׁם זִכְרוֹן לְהַךְ קוּשְׁיָא וְלֹא יָשִׁיב עָלֶיהָ
see what he cited from there, claiming they resolved their question in Bava Metzia through a different judgment, yet I do not know his intention, for no mention of this question is found there;

רַק דִּמְפָרְשֵׁי שָׁם בְּדִין אַחֵר, וְגַם לְפֵירוּשָׁם שָׁם בְּדִין אַחֵר תִּפּוֹל הַךְ קוּשְׁיָא דְּעַל כָּל פָּנִים עוֹלִין גַּם מִשָּׁם מִדְּיֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, וְצָרִיךְ לוֹמַר כְּתֵירוּצָם בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא], עַיֵּין שָׁם

only that they explain it as a different judgment, and even according to that explanation the difficulty persists that in any event they ascend from there since they possess a portion in the World to Come, requiring the resolution of Bava Metzia], see there.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּאוֹתוֹ דִּין אֵין בְּכֹחוֹ לְכַלּוֹת כְּאֵשׁ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם הַשּׂוֹרֶפֶת וּמְכַלָּה

Meaning that this alternative judgment lacks the power to annihilate like the fire of Gehinnom which burns and consumes;1127Asarah Maamaros, Maamar Chakor Din, part 3, ch. 16: “However, all who descend ascend, except the three that R’ Chanina specified (Bava Metzia 58b), and he excluded them from the category — for according to the severity of their iniquity it would have been fitting that the fire of Gehinnom have power over them, to consume them from soul to flesh; but the Master of kindness has no desire in this, therefore Gehinnom is nullified for them, but the law of Gehinnom is not nullified — rather, the Holy One performs [the] mission through everything, for ‘very great is His camp’ [i.e., in essence R’ Chanina’s words remain expounded like the initial assumption of the Gemara]. And they raised a difficulty there in Tosafos, Perek HaZahav, from what David said to those who hated his soul: one who comes upon his fellow’s wife, his death is by strangulation, [yet] he has a share in the World to Come, and one who whitens his fellow’s face in public has no share in the World to Come? And they answered according to their approach; and what emerges from their words is that the three do not ascend immediately, and in this they are equal, but some of them do not ascend at all — and they are ‘one who whitens’ and ‘one who calls [a derogatory name].’ [And from here are the words of the Asarah Maamaros, and not the Tosafos.] And therefore they did not descend, but such is their judgment, that they neither live for the World to Come nor are judged in Gehinnom. But for us, the essential difficulty [of Tosafos] does not exist — for David says thus: one who comes upon his fellow’s wife, his death is by strangulation, and all who are put to death confess and have a share in the World to Come; and even [if] there are no witnesses and no warning, he knows in himself that such is his judgment — ‘go, read it in the schoolhouse [zil kri bei rav]’ it is — and he casts [it] upon himself and remembers to repent. But one who whitens his fellow’s face has no death-penalty of beis din; therefore the one who stumbles in it considers it a light iniquity and does not repent, and is banished from the World to Come, may the Merciful One save us.”
וּלְפִי דְּבָרָיו בְּאֵלּוּ הָיָה אֵשׁ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׁוֹלֶטֶת לְכַלּוֹת לְגַמְרֵי, וּמַשְׁמַע אֲפִילּוּ הָיָה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם דְּמִסְּתָמָא אָמַר עַל כָּל הַיּוֹרְדִין

and according to his words, over these three the fire of Gehinnom would have held dominion to consume completely, implying even if he were a Torah scholar, since he spoke generally of all who descend;1128Chagigah 27a and Eruvin 19a — the fire does not erase Torah or the mitzvos of Israel: Chagigah derives by a kal va-chomer from the salamander that the fire of Gehinnom has no dominion over Torah scholars, whose whole body is identified with the fire of Torah. The same passage, paralleling Eruvin, derives from the golden altar that the fire has no dominion over the sinners of Israel, who remain filled with mitzvos like a pomegranate. Rav Tzadok’s challenge is therefore structural: the Asarah Maamaros’ model requires these statements to contain an unstated exception for the three offenses, while their wording is general. These Aggadic analogies affirm that Torah and mitzvos are not annihilated; they do not imply freedom from judgment, suffering, restitution, or responsibility for the sin itself.
וְצָרִיךְ לִדְחוֹק גַּם לְפִי דְּבָרָיו דְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּבְתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים דְּאֵין יָכוֹל לִשְׁלוֹט הוּא חוּץ מֵאֵלּוּ
and one must force according to his words that what was stated regarding Jewish sinners and scholars that fire cannot dominate excludes these three;
אֶלָּא דִּלְפִי דְּבָרָיו יֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּעַל כָּל הַיּוֹרְדִין שָׁם קָאָמַר, וְלֹא בְּאֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין יוֹרְדִין
but according to his words one can say that it refers to all who actually descend, excluding those who do not descend.
אֲבָל דְּבָרָיו תְּמוּהִין בְּעֵינַי, וּכְפִי הַנִּרְאֶה דְּנֶעְלַם מִמֶּנּוּ גְּמָרָא דְּעֵירוּבִין הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל דְּיוֹרְדִין עַל עִסְקֵי חִנָּם דְּהַיְינוּ עֲרָיוֹת

But his words are astonishing in my eyes, and apparently the Gemara in Eruvin (19a) mentioned above was overlooked by him, which explicitly states that they descend for unprovoked matters, meaning arayos;
וּמִסְּתָמָא רָצָה לוֹמַר גַּם אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ דְּהוּא עִיקַּר עֲרָיוֹת הַמָּצוּי

and presumably this includes a married woman, which is the primary prevalent form of forbidden relations;1129Eruvin 19a with Rashi; Rambam, Hilchos Issurei Biah 1:4–6 — arayos as a shared Aggadic class, with distinct halachic penalties: Rashi explicitly glosses the phrase ‘on account of hinnam’ as arayos. Rav Tzadok accordingly reads Eruvin’s descent passage as encompassing the ordinary field of forbidden relations, and argues that Bava Metzia names a married woman as a common example rather than as the sole case. Halachically, however, the prohibitions are not interchangeable: Rambam separately enumerates arayos punished by stoning, burning, strangulation, or kareis, and states that an ordinary married woman is the sole ervah whose court-imposed death is strangulation. Rav Tzadok’s point is therefore limited to the Aggadic classification and its consequence for this discussion; it does not erase the distinct elements, evidentiary requirements, or punishments of each prohibition.
וְגַם לֹא מַשְׁמַע לְחַלֵּק בֵּין עֲרָיוֹת, דְּהוּקְשׁוּ כָּל אוֹתָן תּוֹעֲבוֹת דַּעֲרָיוֹת זֶה לָזֶה
and it also does not imply that we divide among categories of arayos, since all those abominations of forbidden relations are equated to one another (Kiddushin 67b).
וְגַם בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא דְּנָקְטוּ ״הַבָּא עַל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ״, נִרְאֶה דְּלָאו דַּוְוקָא, וְהוּא הַדִּין לְכָל עֲרָיוֹת, וְנָקַט חֲדָא הַמָּצוּי

Moreover, in Bava Metzia (58b) where they cited "one who cohabits with a married woman," it appears that it is not exclusive, the same law applying to all arayos, citing merely the most common instance;
וְאֵין נִרְאֶה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ חָמוּר בָּזֶה מִשְּׁאָר עֲרָיוֹת, אֲפִילּוּ מֵאוֹתָן שֶׁהֵם חַיָּיבֵי כָּרֵת לְבַד
and it does not seem plausible that a married woman should be more severe in this regard than other arayos, even those carrying kares alone,
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן מֵאוֹתָן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין הַחֲמוּרָה טְפֵי מֵחֶנֶק דְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
and all the more so compared to those carrying court executions (stoning and burning) which are far more severe than the strangulation of a married woman;
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ דַּחֲדָא נָקַט:
and perforce, it cited merely one common example.

items.h: סִימָן ט״ו: סְעִיפִים ס״ט–ע״ב

The theme: The redemption from Gehinnom by Avraham Avinu and the status of those who cohabit with a married woman (eshes ish) or a gentile woman (bo'el aramis). In Eruvin 19a, "condemned for that hour" (mechuvei ha-hu sha'atah) does not denote a literal sixty-minute hour, but rather the fixed duration of punishment decreed upon each soul according to his sin. While ordinary souls ascend from Gehinnom on their own once their judgment is complete, those who committed severe sexual sins cannot ascend unaided. Avraham Avinu draws them up through the sign of the Covenant (bris milah), which testifies to the innate righteousness of Israel. For one who cohabited with an Aramean woman, she clings to him like a dog (Sotah 3b) and masks his circumcision with a foreskin, preventing Avraham from recognizing him until twelve months have passed, at which point the body of the gentile woman is consumed in Gehinnom, severing her connection to him and allowing his redemption.

p: גַּם מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב עוֹד שָׁם לְתָרֵץ, דְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ: ״יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא״ הַיְינוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה, עַיֵּין שָׁם
Also, what he wrote further there to resolve, that what they stated—"they possess a portion in the World to Come"—refers to where he repented, see there;
אֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה, וְלֹא מָצִינוּ לוֹ חָבֵר בָּזֶה דְּבָא עַל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא

does not appear plausible, nor do we find any colleague who agrees with him that one who cohabits with a married woman has no share in the World to Come.1130Mishnah Sanhedrin 6:2 (43b); Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 3:14; Pri Tzadik, Chanukah 21:2 — severe judgment does not close the gate of teshuvah: The Mishnah teaches that those taken to execution are prompted to confess because confession grants a share in the World to Come. Rambam rules that even persons described by Chazal as lacking such a share regain it when they repent, because nothing stands before teshuvah. Rav Tzadok develops the same principle in Pri Tzadik: even one who became trapped in a serious blemish of sexual holiness can be repaired through teshuvah, renewed restraint, and sustained Torah; he explicitly invokes the rule that nothing stands before teshuvah. Thus the closing argument of this se’if does not minimize adultery. It distinguishes the offense’s grave punishment from a claim of inherent, irreversible exclusion from the World to Come. Teshuvah repairs only through genuine abandonment and correction of the sin; it never makes the original act permissible.1131Asarah Maamaros, Maamar Chakor Din, part 3, ch. 16: “However, all who descend ascend, except the three that R’ Chanina specified (Bava Metzia 58b), and he excluded them from the category — for according to the severity of their iniquity it would have been fitting that the fire of Gehinnom have power over them, to consume them from soul to flesh; but the Master of kindness has no desire in this, therefore Gehinnom is nullified for them, but the law of Gehinnom is not nullified — rather, the Holy One performs [the] mission through everything, for ‘very great is His camp’ [i.e., in essence R’ Chanina’s words remain expounded like the initial assumption of the Gemara]. And they raised a difficulty there in Tosafos, Perek HaZahav, from what David said to those who hated his soul: one who comes upon his fellow’s wife, his death is by strangulation, [yet] he has a share in the World to Come, and one who whitens his fellow’s face in public has no share in the World to Come? And they answered according to their approach; and what emerges from their words is that the three do not ascend immediately, and in this they are equal, but some of them do not ascend at all — and they are ‘one who whitens’ and ‘one who calls [a derogatory name].’ [And from here are the words of the Asarah Maamaros, and not the Tosafos.] And therefore they did not descend, but such is their judgment, that they neither live for the World to Come nor are judged in Gehinnom. But for us, the essential difficulty [of Tosafos] does not exist — for David says thus: one who comes upon his fellow’s wife, his death is by strangulation, and all who are put to death confess and have a share in the World to Come; and even [if] there are no witnesses and no warning, he knows in himself that such is his judgment — ‘go, read it in the schoolhouse [zil kri bei rav]’ it is — and he casts [it] upon himself and remembers to repent. But one who whitens his fellow’s face has no death-penalty of beis din; therefore the one who stumbles in it considers it a light iniquity and does not repent, and is banished from the World to Come, may the Merciful One save us.”
אֲבָל לְדַעְתִּי, לוּלֵי דִּבְרֵי תּוֹסָפוֹת דְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא, הָיָה נִרְאֶה לִי פָּשׁוּט: דְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין שָׁם: ״הַהוּא דִּמְחַיְּיבֵי הַהוּא שַׁעְתָּא״
But in my opinion, were it not for the words of Tosafos in Bava Metzia, it would have seemed plain to me: that what they stated in Eruvin there, "that refers to those who are liable for that hour";
אֵין רָצָה לוֹמַר שִׁיעוּר שָׁעָה מִכ״ד שָׁעוֹת דְּיוֹם, דְּמַה טַּעַם לְשִׁיעוּר זֶה, וְגַם לְשׁוֹן ״דִּמְחַיְּיבֵי״ מַשְׁמַע דְּאֵין מְחוּיָּיבִים בַּדִּין לְעֹונֶשׁ עֲוֹנָם יוֹתֵר

did not mean a literal measure of one hour out of the twenty-four hours of the day, for what rationale is there for such a duration? And furthermore, the phrasing "who are liable" implies that they are not liable in judgment for any further punishment for their iniquity;
וְעַל כֵּן נִרְאֶה דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר: אוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה וּזְמַן שֶׁנִּתְחַיְּיבוּ כָּל אֶחָד לְפִי חֶטְאוֹ
and therefore it appears it means: that appointed time and season for which each individual was condemned according to his sin;
וְרָגִיל בַּתַּלְמוּד לְשׁוֹן ״שַׁעְתָּא״ עַל כָּל זְמַן הַמּוּגְבָּל וְקָצוּב לָאָדָם, כְּמוֹ ״דְּקָיְימָא לֵיהּ שַׁעְתָּא״ [בְּתַעֲנִית כ״א עַמּוּד א׳] וּבְכַמָּה דּוּכְתֵּי

and the term sha'atah [hour/time] is common in the Talmud for any defined and allocated period of a person, such as "his hour stands [in good fortune]" [Ta'anis 21a] and in several places.1132Eruvin 19a and Taanis 21a - 'Those liable at that time' as a bounded period: Eruvin states that those who are liable 'at that time' in Gehinnom are raised by Avraham. In Taanis, the phrase kaima leih sha'ata describes the favorable moment or season that stood for Rabbi Yochanan, rather than a sixty-minute unit. That usage supports Rav Tzadok's lexical claim that sha'ata can denote a defined period or condition. It does not by itself determine the meaning in Eruvin; Rav Tzadok's added argument is the word 'liable,' which he reads as liability lasting only for the punishment fixed for each sin.
וּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא דְּג׳ אֵין עוֹלִין, רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר: דְּכוּלָּן כְּשֶׁנִּגְמַר זְמַן עָנְשָׁן וְקִבְּלוּ אֶת הַדִּין עוֹלִין מֵעַצְמָן

And what they stated in Bava Metzia (58b) that three do not ascend, means: all other sinners, once the duration of their punishment is completed and they have received their judgment, ascend on their own;
וְאֵלּוּ, גַּם אַחַר שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ עֹונֶשׁ הַקָּצוּב, אֵין עוֹלִין מֵעַצְמָן, וְאַף שֶׁאֵין נִידּוֹנִין עוֹד, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין עוֹלִין גַּם כֵּן
whereas these three, even after they have received their allocated punishment, do not ascend on their own, and although they are no longer judged, they nevertheless do not ascend on their own either.
וְהָנֵי ב׳ דְּאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא מְצַפְצְפִין וְעוֹלִין כְּשֶׁכָּלָה גֵּיהִנָּם, וְלֹא לְקַבֵּל חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם דְּעוֹלִין עַל כָּל פָּנִים מִשְּׁאוֹל

And those two [who insult their fellow in public or call him by an insulting nickname] who have no share in the World to Come, cry out and ascend when Gehinnom ceases—not to receive a share in the World to Come, but nevertheless ascending from Sheol in any event;1133Bava Metzia 58b; Tosafos, s.v. chutz mi-sheloshah; Rosh Hashanah 17a - judgment ending before ascent: Bava Metzia says that three offenders 'descend and do not ascend.' Tosafos rejects an undifferentiated reading of eternal non-ascent and explains that they do not ascend immediately; the adulterer may ascend after twelve months, while the other two raise the separate issue of a share in the World to Come. Rosh Hashanah uses 'they cry out and ascend' for a class that emerges after purification. Rav Tzadok develops a further distinction: ordinary offenders ascend on their own when judgment ends, whereas these three require an outside act of raising. This 'self-ascent' formulation is his synthesis, not the explicit wording of either sugya.
אוֹ אֶפְשָׁר גַּם מִקּוֹדֶם עַל יְדֵי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וְכֵן גַּם עַל יְדֵי אֵיזֶה צַדִּיק אַחֵר מִמִּשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ אוֹ מִשָּׁרְשׁוֹ שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְהַעֲלוֹתוֹ
or perhaps even prior to that through Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, and likewise through some other tzaddik from his family or soul-root who is able to draw him up.
וּבָא עַל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ, אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מַעֲלֶה אוֹתוֹ עַל יְדֵי הַמִּילָה, דְּהוּא מוֹרֶה עַל קְדֻשַּׁת הַבְּרִית בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל

And regarding one who cohabits with a married woman, Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, draws him up through the circumcision, which signifies the holiness of the Covenant in Israel as mentioned above;1134Eruvin 19a; Sanhedrin 104a; Tosafos on Sotah 10b - Avraham's rescue and righteous intercession: Eruvin explicitly names Avraham as the one who raises and receives the circumcised. Sanhedrin ordinarily states that a son can confer merit on a father, but a father does not automatically confer merit on a son. Tosafos on Sotah qualifies that prayer can nevertheless help, citing David's prayer for Avshalom. Rav Tzadok's suggestion that another tzaddik from the offender's family or spiritual root might raise him should therefore be read as a proposed mode of intercession, not as an automatic transfer of another person's merits. The language of a shared 'root' belongs to his mystical framework and is not stated in the Eruvin passage itself.
וְאֵין הָעָרְלָה נִקְרֵאת אֶלָּא עַל שֵׁם אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, דְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם עֲרֵלִים שֶׁבָּהּ זוּהֲמַת הַזִּימָּה מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ שֶׁבָּא עַל חַוָּה וְלֹא פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָתָן

and the foreskin is named only after the nations of the world, for all the gentiles are uncircumcised, possessing the defilement of depravity from the root of the Serpent who came upon Chavah and whose defilement never ceased;
וְעַל כֵּן הֵם בַּעֲבֵירָה נִקְרָאִים ״פּוֹשְׁעִים בְּגוּפָן״ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל

wherefore in sexual transgression they are termed "sinners with their bodies," as mentioned above;1135Shabbos 146a - the serpent's contamination, Sinai, and the status of converts: The Aggadah says that the serpent placed contamination in Chavah; Israel's contamination ceased when they stood at Sinai, whereas that of the nations who did not stand there did not. The Gemara immediately asks about converts and answers that although they were not physically present, their mazal was present at Sinai. Rav Tzadok uses this image to describe covenantal attachment and the source of sexual desire. It is an Aggadic-theological metaphor, not a biological classification or a license to judge the moral standing of individual people; the sugya itself expressly includes converts within the Sinai transformation.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּגַם הָעֲרֵלִים נִקְרָאִים מוּלִין כִּדִתְנַן [בִּנְדָרִים ל״א עַמּוּד ב׳]
unlike Israel, where even uncircumcised men are halachically called "circumcised," as we learned [in Nedarim 31b];
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא הוֹצִיא מֵהַכְּלָל עָרֵל גָּמוּר שֶׁלֹּא נִימּוֹל, וַאֲפִילּוּ אִם לֹא פָּשַׁע בְּכָךְ רַק שֶׁמֵּתוּ אֶחָיו מֵחֲמַת מִילָה
and therefore the Talmud did not exclude an uncircumcised Jew who was never circumcised, even if he was not negligent but his brothers died from circumcision;
וְעַל כֵּן דְּזֶה מִכָּל מָקוֹם מַבְשְׁקַר לֵיהּ, שֶׁגַּם הוּא נִקְרָא מָהוּל וְנֶחְשָׁב לְמָהוּל, שֶׁ״עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים״ שׁוֹמְרֵי הַבְּרִית

wherefore [Avraham] recognizes him in any event, for he too is named circumcised and accounted circumcised, since "Your people are all righteous," guardians of the Covenant;1136Mishnah Nedarim 31b; Shulchan Aruch, Yoreh De'ah 263:1, 5 - an uncircumcised Jew is still termed 'circumcised': The Mishnah rules that one who vows not to benefit from 'the circumcised' is prohibited even from an uncircumcised Jew and permitted to benefit from a circumcised non-Jew, because Scripture uses 'uncircumcised' as a national designation. Halachah also recognizes a genuine medical exemption: after two sons die because of circumcision, a later son is not circumcised until he is strong enough; the Shulchan Aruch still calls such a person an 'uncircumcised Jew' and lists him among those qualified to perform circumcision. Rav Tzadok draws from this terminology that covenantal identity is deeper than the visible mark. This does not remove the actual mitzvah of milah whenever it can safely and properly be fulfilled.
וְכָל חֲטָאִים דִּידְהוּ בָּזֶה רַק מִצַּד הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה
and all their sins in this area derive solely from the external "yeast in the dough."
חוּץ מִבּוֹעֵל אֲרַמִּית, שֶׁמִּתְדַּבֵּק לְגוֹיָה זֶה גּוֹרֵם דְּמַמְשִׁיךְ

Except for one who cohabits with an Aramean woman (bo'el aramis): for cleaving to a gentile woman causes him to draw down a foreskin;1137Berakhot 17a; Pri Tzadik, Tetzaveh 12 - 'the leaven in the dough' and Israel's inner will: Rabbi Alexandri prayed: 'It is revealed and known before You that our will is to do Your will; what prevents us? The leaven in the dough and the subjugation of the kingdoms.' The classical explanation identifies the leaven with the yetzer hara. In Pri Tzadik, Rav Tzadok applies this teaching to the principle that a Jew remains Israel despite sin: the inward will is directed to Heaven, while the leaven confuses the heart. Here too, describing the sin as arising from the leaven does not excuse the act or cancel responsibility; it explains why the covenantal core can persist and why teshuvah remains possible.
וְאַף דְּגַם הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת נִקְרָא מָהוּל, מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁקְּשׁוּרָה בּוֹ כַּכֶּלֶב כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּסוֹטָה ג׳ עַמּוּד ב׳] מִקְּרָא דִּ״לִהְיוֹת עִמָּהּ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ט:י׳)
and although he too is essentially called circumcised, nevertheless because she is bound to him like a dog as they stated [in Sotah 3b] from the verse "to be with her" (Bereishis 39:10),
הוּא מָשׁוּךְ בְּעָרְלָה דִּבְשַׂר הַגּוֹיָה שֶׁהָעָרְלָה נִקְרֵאת עַל שְׁמָם, וְלֹא מַבְשְׁקַר לֵיהּ לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן

he is covered by the foreskin of the flesh of the gentile woman after whose identity the foreskin is named, so that Avraham does not recognize him to outward appearances;1138Cf. Sotah 3b — the source R’ Tzadok cites: “R’ Yochanan said in the name of R’ Shimon ben Yochai: no man sins unless a spirit of folly enters him; and R’ Yehoshua ben Levi said: the ervah [with which he sinned] is bound to him like a dog,” derived from the wording that they will be “with her” — an image R’ Tzadok reads as the “drawing of the foreskin” that clings to one who attaches himself to a gentile-woman until it is severed.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם הוּא יֵשׁ לוֹ גְּאוּלָּה וְעוֹלֶה עַל יְדֵי צַדִּיקִים מִשָּׁרְשׁוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
and nevertheless he too has redemption, ascending through righteous masters from his soul-root as mentioned above,
אוֹ גַּם עַל יְדֵי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אַחַר י״ב חֹדֶשׁ לְמִיתַת הַגּוֹיָה וּכְנִיסָתָהּ בְּגֵיהִנָּם
or even through Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, after twelve months following the death of the gentile woman and her entry into Gehinnom;
דְּהִיא פּוֹשְׁעֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם בְּגוּפָן דִּלְאַחַר י״ב חֹדֶשׁ גּוּפָהּ כָּלָה וְנִשְׁמָתָהּ נִשְׂרֶפֶת, וְאֵינָהּ קְשׁוּרָה בּוֹ עוֹד וּמַבְשְׁקַר לֵיהּ

for she belongs to the bodily sinners of the nations of the world whose body after twelve months is consumed and whose soul is burned, so that she is no longer bound to him, and Avraham recognizes him;1139Mishnah Eduyos 2:10 and Rosh Hashanah 17a - the twelve-month judgment category and Rav Tzadok's application: The Mishnah gives twelve months as the general measure of the judgment of the wicked in Gehinnom. Rosh Hashanah distinguishes several classes: bodily sinners of Israel and bodily sinners of the nations are judged for twelve months, after which it uses the severe imagery of the body being consumed and the soul burned; later the Gemara defines bodily sin among the nations as forbidden sexual relations. Rav Tzadok applies that category to the gentile woman in his proposed reconstruction, so that after the attachment is ended the Jewish offender can again be recognized and raised. The Bavli does not itself connect this particular posthumous scenario to Avraham's act in Eruvin; it is Rav Tzadok's Aggadic synthesis, not a practical halachic adjudication of identifiable persons.
וּבְעֵירוּבִין דְּקָאֵי אַיּוֹרְדִין אַעִסְקֵי חִנָּם וַעֲרָיוֹת אָמְרוּ הָא דְּאַבְרָהָם אַסֵּיק, וּבָזֶה נִתְיַישֵּׁב הַכֹּל:
and in Eruvin (19a), which deals with those who descend for unprovoked lust and arayos, they stated that Avraham draws them up; and through this everything is reconciled.

items.h: The theme: Why cohabiting with an Aramean woman is omitted from the three who do not ascend in Bava Metzia 58b. Cohabiting with a gentile woman is not explicit in the Torah's chapter on forbidden relations (arayos) and carries no statutory kares, so upon completing his allocated punishment in Gehinnom, he ascends on his own without requiring external intervention. Intervention by Avraham Avinu is required only for true arayos (such as a married woman). R' Tzadok critiques the commentary Yad Yehudah on Asarah Ma'amaros, which claimed that when bodily sinners have their souls burned after twelve months (Rosh Hashanah 17a), it does not mean total consumption; R' Tzadok proves from the explicit conclusion—"and a wind scatters them and they become ashes under the soles of the feet of the righteous"—that they are literally consumed into ash.

p: וְנִיחָא הָא דְּלֹא חָשֵׁיב בּוֹעֵל אֲרַמִּית בַּגְּמָרָא כְּתֵירוּץ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת בָּבָא מְצִיעָא שָׁם
And this resolves why the Gemara did not enumerate one who cohabits with an Aramean woman among the three who do not ascend, following the resolution of Tosafos in Bava Metzia there:
דְּעַל עָוֹן זֶה לְבַד כְּשֶׁיּוֹרֵד לְגֵיהִנָּם עוֹלֶה מֵעַצְמוֹ, דְּאֵין צָרִיךְ לְמִי שֶׁיַּעֲלֵהוּ אֶלָּא בְּהָנֵי ג׳
for on account of this iniquity alone, when he descends to Gehinnom he ascends on his own, for one requires an intercessor to draw him up only regarding those three;
וּבִיאַת אֲרַמִּית אֵינָהּ בִּכְלַל בָּא עַל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ וַעֲרָיוֹת, דְּאֵין אַזְהָרָתָהּ וְכָרֵת שֶׁלָּהּ מְפוֹרָשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה, וְלֹא נֶאֶמְרָה בְּפָרָשַׁת עֲרָיוֹת, וְלֹא הוּקַּשׁ לָהֶם

and intercourse with an Aramean woman is not included in the category of a married woman and arayos, since its warning and excision are not explicit in the Torah, nor was it stated in the chapter of arayos, nor equated to them;1140Bava Metzia 58b: “R’ Chanina said: all descend to Gehinnom except three. ‘All’?! Can it enter your mind [that all descend]? Rather, say: all who descend to Gehinnom ascend, except three who descend and do not ascend. And these are they: one who comes upon a married woman, one who whitens his fellow’s face in public, and one who calls his fellow by a derogatory name.” Tosafos: “Thus is its explanation: all who descend ascend immediately, and the fire of Gehinnom has no power over them, as we say in Perek Osin Pasin (Eruvin 19a) [by] a kal va-chomer from the golden altar, and in the last chapter of Chagigah (27a) [where] he made a kal va-chomer from the salamander — except three who do not ascend immediately; but some of them are judged forever, such as [the heretics], and some ascend after twelve months, such as [the sinners of Israel]. And yet it is difficult that [R’ Chanina] did not count ‘the sinners of Israel with their bodies,’ such as the skull that does not don tefillin, of whom we say in Rosh Hashanah that they descend and are judged there twelve months, and afterward their body and soul are burned.”
וּמִשֶּׁקִּבֵּל עָנְשׁוֹ הַקָּצוּב עוֹלֶה
and once he receives his allocated punishment, he ascends;
אִם לֹא כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ עָוֹן אַחֵר דַּעֲרָיוֹת דַּוְוקָא, שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לְהַעֲלוֹתוֹ

unless he bears another specific iniquity of arayos, which necessitates Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, to draw him up.1141Sanhedrin 82a; Rambam, Hilchos Issurei Biah 12:1-8 - a distinct halachic category outside the Torah's parashah of arayos: The Torah's explicit arayos and kareis passages are in Vayikra 18 and 20. Relations with a non-Jewish woman are governed by a different complex of sources. Rambam derives a Torah prohibition for intermarriage from 'lo tischaten bam'; he treats ordinary licentious relations as subject to rabbinic lashes, while a public act is governed by the narrowly limited halachah le-Moshe mi-Sinai of kana'im pog'in bo, which a court does not instruct a person to carry out. If neither that intervention nor court punishment occurred, Rambam cites Malachi 2:11-12 as Divrei Kabbalah for a punishment described as kareis. Thus Rav Tzadok's statement that the warning and kareis are not explicit in the Torah means that this offense was not written or juxtaposed within the Torah's arayos section. It does not lessen its severity or make the several legal settings interchangeable.1142Tosafos on Bava Metzia 58b, s.v. chutz mi-sheloshah; Tosafos on Eruvin 19a, s.v. bar mi-Yisrael - why this offense is not counted among the three: Tosafos explains that Bava Metzia lists offenses which, by themselves, prevent the offender from ascending immediately even when he possesses Torah and good deeds. Relations with a non-Jewish woman function differently in the Eruvin passage: this offense does not, by itself, create the other liability that sends him to Gehinnom; rather, when additional sins already make him liable to descend, it prevents Avraham from recognizing and raising him immediately. Tosafos on Eruvin therefore says that after he receives his judgment he ascends. Rav Tzadok's phrase 'he ascends of himself' sharpens this distinction between the completion of the fixed judgment and the special rescue attributed to Avraham. The entire discussion presumes that no teshuvah was performed, as Tosafos concludes explicitly.
וּלְפִי זֶה שַׁפִּיר ״פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״, דְּאֵין אוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׁוֹלֵט עַל פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
And according to this, it is well resolved regarding the sinners of Israel, that the fire of Gehinnom has no dominion over them;
אֶלָּא דְּקָשֶׁה הָא דְּ״פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּגוּפָן״ בַּבָּרַיְיתָא דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה

except that the statement regarding "sinners of Israel with their bodies" in the Baraisa of Rosh Hashanah (17a) remains difficult.1143Eruvin 19a; Chagigah 27a; Yisrael Kedoshim 10:6 - general non-annihilation language and Rav Tzadok's covenantal reading: Eruvin and Chagigah state without an explicit exception that the fire of Gehinnom has no dominion over the sinners of Israel, who remain filled with mitzvos like a pomegranate. In Yisrael Kedoshim, Rav Tzadok directly addresses the apparent exception of one who had relations with a non-Jewish woman: the drawn foreskin and Avraham's failure to recognize him are only at the level of outward appearance. He compares this to one whose foreskin was drawn, who remains circumcised under Torah law and requires a corrective procedure only rabbinically because of appearance. This parallel explains why Rav Tzadok can maintain that the covenantal root is not destroyed even when recognition and rescue are delayed. It is an Aggadic and mystical account of enduring Jewish identity, not a denial of punishment, responsibility, or the need for complete teshuvah.1144Rosh Hashanah 17a - the exact category of 'sinners of Israel with their bodies': The baraisa states that bodily sinners of Israel and of the nations descend to Gehinnom and are judged for twelve months; afterward 'their bodies are consumed, their souls are burned, and a wind scatters them beneath the feet of the righteous.' The Gemara defines the Jewish case as a skull that never donned tefillin. It further distinguishes between one whose deeds are mostly sins, for whom it says there is no rectification within that judgment scheme, and one whose merits and sins are balanced but include this bodily sin, who passes through the refining fire. The category is therefore narrower than the phrase 'all sinners of Israel,' yet its concluding destruction language is precisely what creates Rav Tzadok's difficulty with the general teachings that the fire has no dominion over them.
וְרָאִיתִי בְּפֵירוּשׁ ״יַד יְהוּדָה״ עַל הָ״עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת״ שָׁם [בְּחֵלֶק ג׳ רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ט״ו אוֹת ב׳] כָּתַב: דְּגַם זֶה אֵין רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁנִּשְׂרֶפֶת לְגַמְרֵי
And I saw in the commentary Yad Yehudah on Asarah Ma'amaros [Part III, start of ch. 15, note 2], who wrote: this too does not mean that the soul is burned completely,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָ״עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת״ שָׁם דְּאֵין שׁוֹלֵט לְכַלּוֹתָם, רַק נִכְוֵית וְנִידּוֹנִית בְּיִסּוּרִים קָשִׁים, עַיֵּין שָׁם

and as Asarah Ma'amaros wrote there, that the fire does not dominate to annihilate them, but rather the soul is scorched and judged with severe afflictions, see there;1145Asarah Maamaros, part 3, ch. 15: “We come to those who descend to Gehinnom, with whom we began in ch. 2: it is known and famous that the fire of Gehinnom has no power over the sinners of Israel to consume them, God forbid; rather, they descend for mere terror [be’asusa], and some of them are scorched by their deeds, and [it is] removed from them; and afterward Avraham descends — who fulfilled all the mitzvos and descended into Ur Kasdim for the sanctification of the Name — and in his merit raises them.” Yad Yehuda commentary: “they descend to Gehinnom, some for mere terror and some are scorched; and this is what they said in Rosh Hashanah regarding the sinners with their bodies, that their soul is burned — not that it is burned entirely, but scorched and judged with harsh sufferings according to the measure of the sin.” And on this he raises a difficulty from the Gemara in Rosh Hashanah — see the following note.
וְתָמוּהַּ, דְּמִלְּבַד דִּלְשׁוֹן ״נִשְׂרֶפֶת״ מַשְׁמַע לְגַמְרֵי
and this is astonishing: for aside from the fact that the term "burned" implies completely,
הֲרֵי סִיְּימוּ שָׁם עַל זֶה: ״וְרוּחַ מְפַזַּרְתָּן וְכוּלֵיהּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ׳[וְעַסּוֹתֶם רְשָׁעִים כִּי יִהְיוּ] אֵפֶר תַּחַת [כַּפּוֹת רַגְלֵיכֶם] וְגוֹמֵר׳ (מַלְאָכִי ג:כא)״

behold, they concluded upon this there: "and a wind scatters them, etc., as it is said: 'and you shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet, etc.' (Malachi 3:21),"
הֲרֵי דְּנַעֲשִׂין אֵפֶר כְּכָל דָּבָר הַנִּכְלֶה עַל יְדֵי הָאֵשׁ לְגַמְרֵי:

showing clearly that they become ashes like any physical substance that is entirely consumed by fire!1146Malachi 3:21; Seder Olam Rabbah 3:2 - 'consumed, burned, scattered, and ash' as cumulative language: Rosh Hashanah grounds its final clause in Malachi: 'they shall be ashes beneath the soles of your feet.' The parallel tradition in Seder Olam likewise describes the bodies and souls of the sinners as consumed, turned to dust, expelled by Gehinnom, and scattered by the wind beneath the righteous. A form of the verb 'burned' can sometimes be used less than literally when context requires it, which is the opening for Yad Yehuda's interpretation. Rav Tzadok's objection is that here the four linked expressions - body consumed, soul burned, wind scattering, and ash - naturally indicate complete consumption. The non-total reading is therefore a theological harmonization with Eruvin and Chagigah, rather than the straightforward force of the baraisa's wording.

items.h: The theme: Reconciling the burning of bodily sinners with the eternal punishment of heretics. If the fire of Gehinnom cannot annihilate souls, why are the souls of Jewish bodily sinners burned into ashes after twelve months, while heretics (minim) are never consumed ("their fire shall not be quenched", Yeshayah 66:24)? For the heretics, Hashem miraculously preserves their existence so that their torment never ends (Sanhedrin 100b), because unending suffering is worse than death (Kesubos 33b). For Jewish bodily sinners, having their souls burned into ashes is an act of mercy, bringing an end to their agony. Mitzvos protect a soul from suffering, and cannot be used to prolong punishment to a person's detriment. Furthermore, "their fire shall not be quenched" applies to heretics among the nations, whereas for others, Gehinnom ceases.

p: וְלִכְאוֹרָה גַּם בְּלָאו הָכִי קָשֶׁה עוֹד מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ דְּ״נִשְׁמָתָן נִשְׂרֶפֶת״ מִסֵּיפָא דְּהַךְ בָּרַיְיתָא גּוּפַהּ
And superficially, even without this, what they stated—that "their soul is burned"—is further difficult from the concluding clause of that very Baraisa:
לְפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל, דְּגַם הַמִּינִין וַחֲבֵירֵיהֶם שֶׁאָמְרוּ דְּ״הֵם אֵינָן כָּלִין״, אֵין נִכְלִים לְגַמְרֵי דְּאֵין אוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׁוֹלֵט לְכַלּוֹתָם

according to what I wrote above, that even regarding heretics and their companions whereof they stated "they are not consumed," they are not annihilated completely because the fire of Gehinnom has no dominion to consume them.
וּמִיהוּ עַל זֶה יֵשׁ לוֹמַר, דְּלָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין אוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׁוֹלֵט

However, regarding this one can answer: it is not because the fire of Gehinnom lacks natural dominion,1147Rosh Hashanah 17a: “The sinners of Israel with their bodies and the sinners of the nations of the world with their bodies descend to Gehinnom and are judged there twelve months; after twelve months their body is consumed and their soul is burned and a wind scatters them beneath the soles of the feet of the righteous, as it says: ‘and you shall trample the wicked, for they shall be ashes beneath the soles of your feet.’ But the heretics and the informers and the epikorsim, who denied the Torah, and who denied the resurrection of the dead, and who separated from the ways of the community, and who cast their terror in the land of the living, and who sinned and caused the public to sin — like Yaravam ben Nevat and his fellows — descend to Gehinnom and are judged there for generations of generations, as it says: ‘and they shall go out and look upon the corpses of the men who transgressed against Me, etc.’; Gehinnom is consumed and they are not consumed, as it says: ‘and their form is for Sheol to consume.’”1148Rosh Hashanah 17a; Tosafos ad loc., s.v. ki leis lehu takanah - two outcomes contrasted within one baraisa: The baraisa first describes bodily sinners of Israel: after twelve months their bodies are consumed, their souls are burned, and they become ash beneath the feet of the righteous. It then separately lists the minim, informers, apikorsim, deniers, separatists, tyrannical leaders, and those who sin and cause the public to sin; they are judged for generations, and 'Gehinnom is consumed but they are not consumed.' Tosafos explains that even the ordinary wicked who are inscribed for Gehinnom because most of their deeds are sins are not thereby assigned eternal punishment; they are judged for twelve months and ascend. Rav Tzadok therefore reads the second clause as continued personal existence and turns it back upon the apparently annihilating language of the first clause. His difficulty rests on the deliberate contrast between the two outcomes within the same source.
רַק לְרָעָתָם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַיְּימָם, דְּחַיִּים בְּיִסּוּרִין שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם הֶפְסֵק גָּרַע מִמִּיתָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּכְתוּבּוֹת ל״ג רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב׳]
but rather to their detriment the Holy One, blessed be He, supernaturally sustains them, for living in unending torment is worse than death as they stated [in Kesubos 33b];
וּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּגוּפָן דְּנִשְׂרֶפֶת, מַעֲלִיּוּתָא הוּא לְגַבַּיְיהוּ

and for the sinners of Israel with their bodies, the burning of their soul is an advantage for them;1149Kesubos 33b - limited death and suffering without a fixed endpoint: The Gemara raises the possibility that lashes can be more severe than death, citing Rav's statement that had Chananyah, Mishael, and Azaryah been subjected to flogging they might have yielded to the image. Rav Samma answers that one must distinguish a punishment with a fixed limit from an unlimited beating. Rav Tzadok borrows this narrow principle: suffering with no cessation can be worse for the sufferer than an ending. He can therefore describe the continued existence of the exceptional wicked as punitive, while calling the burning of the bodily sinners a relative benefit because it terminates their suffering. This is an Aggadic comparison of outcomes, not a practical ranking of court punishments or a qualification of the obligation of mesirus nefesh.

וּבְסַנְהֶדְרִין [ק׳ רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב׳] מַיְיתֵי מִמִּקְרָא זֶה דְּ״אִשָּׁם לֹא תִכְבֶּה״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ס״ו:כ״ד), דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נוֹתֵן כֹּחַ בָּרְשָׁעִים לְקַבֵּל פּוּרְעָנוּתָם, עַיֵּין שָׁם

and in Sanhedrin [100b] it derives from this verse "their fire shall not be quenched" (Yeshayah 66:24) that the Holy One, blessed be He, infuses strength into the wicked to endure their retribution, see there.1150Sanhedrin 100b: “It is written, ‘and they shall go out and look upon the corpses of the men who transgressed against Me, for their worm shall not die and their fire shall not be extinguished, and they shall be an abhorrence to all flesh’ — but does not a man who puts his finger in the fire in this world get immediately scorched? Rather, just as the Holy One gives strength to the wicked to receive their punishment, so the Holy One gives strength to the righteous to receive their good.”1151Sanhedrin 100b; Yeshayahu 66:24 - God grants the capacity to endure punishment: Sanhedrin asks how the wicked can remain in an unextinguished fire when a finger placed in ordinary fire is immediately burned. It answers that the Holy One gives the wicked strength to receive their punishment, just as He gives the righteous strength to receive their reward. The teaching establishes supernatural endurance; it does not explicitly decide whether Gehinnom's fire intrinsically has dominion over every spiritual category. Rav Tzadok therefore presses the logical limit of the proof: if Chagigah teaches that accumulated mitzvos themselves prevent the fire from consuming Israel, the Sanhedrin passage proves his point only if the sustaining power overrides that protection, or if the verse is being demonstrated through the wicked of the nations who are included in its scope.
וְלִכְאוֹרָה מִזֶּה רְאָיָה דְּאוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׁוֹלֵט גַּם לְכַלּוֹתָם, אִי לָאו דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נוֹתֵן וְכוּלֵיהּ
And superficially from this there is proof that the fire of Gehinnom holds dominion to consume them as well, were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, gives strength, etc.;
דְּאִי לָאו הָכִי מַאי רְאָיָה, וַהֲרֵי שָׁם מִשּׁוּם מִצְוֹת הַמַּגִּינוֹת אֵין הָאוֹר שׁוֹלֵט לְכַלּוֹתָם

for otherwise what proof is there? Behold there, on account of their shielding mitzvos the fire lacks dominion to consume them!1152Chagigah 27a; Eruvin 19a; Yisrael Kedoshim 10:6 - the purpose of mitzvah-protection: Chagigah derives that the fire of Gehinnom has no dominion over Torah scholars and then over the sinners of Israel, who remain filled with mitzvos like a pomegranate; Eruvin connects their ascent with Avraham's recognition. These teachings do not erase judgment, but they deny final dominion of the fire over Israel's covenantal core. In Yisrael Kedoshim, Rav Tzadok similarly explains that even when a drawn foreskin prevents outward recognition, the Jew remains circumcised under Torah law at the inward level. Here he adds a teleological point: a merit that 'protects' cannot reasonably be invoked in order to prolong suffering. Its protection must operate for the person's benefit, not to his detriment.

אֲבָל יֵשׁ לוֹמַר, דְּמֵאַחַר דְּזֶה קָשֶׁה לָהֶם יוֹתֵר, וְטוֹב הָיָה לָהֶם שֶׁיִּשָּׂרְפוּ לְגַמְרֵי וְיִפָּטְרוּ מֵהַיִּסּוּרִין, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר שֶׁיִּהְיוּ הַמִּצְוֹת מַגִּינוֹת לְרָעָתָם וּלְהַרְבּוֹת יִסּוּרֵיהֶם

But one can say: since this perpetual endurance is harsher upon them, and it would be better for them to be burned completely and released from torment, it is impossible to assert that their mitzvos would shield them to their detriment and multiply their agonies!
וְגַם יֵשׁ לוֹמַר, דִּקְרָא גַּם בְּרִשְׁעֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מַיְירֵי, וְהֵם אֵין לָהֶם מִצְוֹת מַגִּינוֹת

And one can also say that the verse speaks likewise of the wicked of the nations of the world, who possess no shielding mitzvos;1153Rosh Hashanah 17a; Sanhedrin 56a; Tosafos on Rosh Hashanah 17a; Rambam, Hilchos Melachim 8:11 - the wicked of the nations and mitzvah merit: Rav defines the bodily sinners of the nations as those guilty 'of the transgression,' and Tosafos explains this as forbidden sexual relations, one of the prohibitions commanded to the descendants of Noach. Rav Tzadok's final phrase therefore should not be read as denying that non-Jews possess commandments, merit, or reward. Rambam rules that one who accepts and carefully observes the seven commandments because God commanded them through Moshe is among the righteous of the nations and has a share in the World to Come. Rav Tzadok's narrower claim is that Chagigah's particular proof - that even the 'empty' among Israel are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate - is not available as a shield for the non-Jewish wicked included in the Yeshayahu and Sanhedrin passage.

וְגַם אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר, דְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ ״גֵּיהִנָּם כָּלָה״ הַיְינוּ דְּדָיְיקוּ לְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב: ״וְאִשָּׁם לֹא תִכְבֶּה״ — אֵשׁ דִּידְהוּ אֵין כָּבָה, הָא דְּאַחֲרִינֵי כָּבָה, שֶׁכְּבָר כָּלָה גֵּיהִנָּם מִכָּל הָרְשָׁעִים:

and one can also say that what they stated, "Gehinnom is consumed," is derived precisely from the scriptural phrase: "their fire shall not be quenched"—their personal fire is not quenched, but the fire of others is quenched, for Gehinnom has already ceased for all other sinners.

items.h: The theme: The internal fire of the wicked versus the external fire of Gehinnom according to Rabbi Yehudah bar Ilai. In Bereishis Rabbah 26:6, Rabbi Yehudah teaches that in the Future there is no physical Gehinnom; rather, an internal fire emerges from the body of the wicked person and consumes him ("your breath is a fire that shall consume you", Yeshayah 33:11). The phrase "their fire shall not be quenched" refers to this internal fire of their own body. Mitzvos shield only against the external fire of Gehinnom (like the gold of the Altar), but not against the internal fire born of their own deeds. When Yeshayah states "a fire shall consume you," it means the internal fire ultimately burns the sinners into ash, proving that the external fire of Gehinnom never held destroying power over them.

p: וְנִרְאֶה דְּהוּא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן רַבִּי אִלְעָאִי [בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כ״ו], דְּאֵין גֵּיהִנָּם לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא, אֶלָּא אֵשׁ יוֹצֵא מִגּוּפוֹ שֶׁל רָשָׁע וּמְלַהֲטַתּוּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״[תַּהֲרוּ חֲשַׁשׁ תֵּלְדוּ קַשׁ] רוּחֲכֶם אֵשׁ תֹּאכַלְכֶם״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ל״ג:י״א)

And it appears that this accords with Rabbi Yehudah ben Rabbi Ilai [in Bereishis Rabbah 26:6], that there is no Gehinnom in the Future, but rather a fire goes forth from the body of the wicked person and consumes him, as it is said: "your breath is a fire that shall consume you" (Yeshayah 33:11);1154Yeshayahu 66:24; Rosh Hashanah 17a - “their fire” and the source of the contrast: The verse says that 'their worm shall not die and their fire shall not be extinguished.' Rosh Hashanah cites this verse for the exceptional classes judged for generations and then states that 'Gehinnom is consumed but they are not consumed,' deriving that latter statement from Tehillim 49:15. Rav Tzadok's inference here - that the possessive 'their fire' implies that the fire of others is extinguished - is therefore a proposed diyyuk in the verse, not the Bavli's explicit derivation. It supplies an initial way to distinguish the exceptional wicked from the ordinary wicked whose judgment ends.1155Cf. Bereishis Rabbah, ch. 26 (and Nedarim 8b) — the source R’ Tzadok cites: R’ Yehuda b“R Ilai’s view that in the time to come”there is no Gehinnom" as a fixed place; rather, “the Holy One brings the sun out of its sheath — the wicked are judged [burned] by it and the righteous are healed by it,” and the fire that consumes the wicked is one that “goes out from their own body,” as it says (Yeshayahu 33:11), “your spirit is a fire that shall consume you.”1156Bereishis Rabbah 26:6 - three distinct models of future punishment: The Midrash records three alternatives. R' Yannai and R' Shimon ben Lakish say that there will be no Gehinnom in the future; rather, the coming day itself will burn the wicked. The Rabbis maintain that Gehinnom will exist. R' Yehuda b'Rebbi Ilai says that there will be neither such a day nor Gehinnom, but a fire will emerge from the wicked person's own body and burn him, based on Yeshayahu 33:11. Rav Tzadok selects the third view to reinterpret 'their fire' as self-generated. The Midrash itself presents these as competing descriptions, not as cumulative stages of one process.
וְזֶהוּ ״וְאִשָּׁם״, הַיְינוּ הָאֵשׁ שֶׁלָּהֶם הַיּוֹצֵא מִגּוּפָם, זֶה לֹא תִכְבֶּה גַּם לֶעָתִיד שֶׁאֵין גֵּיהִנָּם שֶׁכְּבָר כָּלָה, דְּהֵם לֹא כָלוּ וְכֵן הָאֵשׁ שֶׁמִּגּוּפָם

and this is the meaning of "their fire": namely, their fire that issues from their body, this fire shall not be quenched even in the Future when there is no Gehinnom (it having ceased), for they have not ceased, nor has the fire of their body.
וְאַף דִּבִפְסָחִים [נ״ד עַמּוּד א׳] יָלְפִינַן מֵהַאי דְּ״אִשָּׁם לֹא תִכְבֶּה״ דְּאֵשׁ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם אֵין לוֹ כְּבִיָּה לְעוֹלָם, וּמְפָרֵשׁ אַאוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם
And although in Pesachim [54a] we derive from this verse "their fire shall not be quenched" that the fire of Gehinnom is never quenched, explaining it regarding the external fire of Gehinnom;
יֵשׁ לוֹמַר בָּרַיְיתָא דְּהָתָם כְּרַבָּנָן [דִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה שָׁם] דְּיֵשׁ גֵּיהִנָּם לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא, דְּשָׁם פְּלִיגֵי בָּזֶה
one can say the Baraisa there follows the Rabbis [in Bereishis Rabbah there] who hold there is a Gehinnom in the Future, for they dispute this point there;
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר הַהִיא דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין כְּבָרַיְיתָא דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה

and one can say that passage in Sanhedrin (100b) accords with the Baraisa of Rosh Hashanah.1157Pesachim 54a - the cavity and the fire of Gehinnom: Pesachim distinguishes between Gehinnom's cavity, created before the world, and its fire, created on the second day. R' Yose teaches that this fire 'has no extinguishing forever,' citing Yeshayahu 66:24. The sugya thus reads the unextinguished fire as the fire of Gehinnom itself. Rav Tzadok's answer assigns this baraisa to the Rabbis in Bereishis Rabbah, who maintain that Gehinnom exists in the future, while aligning the Sanhedrin tradition with R' Yehuda's self-generated fire. This is a harmonizing attribution across differing Aggadic traditions; Pesachim does not itself make that assignment.
[וּבִפְרָט לְפִי הַנּוּסְחָא אַחֲרָא שֶׁבְּגִילָיוֹן הַגְּמָרָא דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין [שָׁם סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳] ״רַבִּי יְהוּדָה״
[And particularly according to the marginal variant in the Gemara in Sanhedrin [100a]: "Rabbi Yehudah";
וּכְפִי נוּסְחַת הַגְּמָרָא מַשְׁמַע דְּגַם הַסִּיּוּם ״וְאַתָּה אִי וְכוּלֵיהּ״ הַכֹּל מִדְּבָרָיו, שֶׁהוּא מוֹתִיב וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לְעַצְמוֹ
and according to the textual reading of the Gemara it implies that the conclusion "and you, if, etc." is entirely his own words, where he questions and resolves for himself;
סְתָם ״רַבִּי יְהוּדָה״ הוּא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן רַבִּי אִלְעָאִי, וּלְטַעְמֵיהּ [בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה שָׁם]
and an unqualified "Rabbi Yehudah" is Rabbi Yehudah ben Rabbi Ilai, consistent with his view in Bereishis Rabbah there;
אֶלָּא דְּהַדָּבָר דָּחוּק לִהְיוֹת הַכֹּל דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וּכְפִי הַנִּרְאֶה דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר הוּא שֶׁהִשִּׂיג לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה כֵּן וְצָרִיךְ לוֹמַר ״אָמַר לוֹ: וְאַתָּה וְכוּלֵיהּ״
except that it is forced for all of it to be the words of Rabbi Yehudah, and apparently it was Rabbi Meir who challenged Rabbi Yehudah, and the text should read: "He said to him: and you, etc.";
וְשׁוּב רָאִיתִי בְּהַגָּהַת הַגְּרָ״א הִגִּיהַּ כֵּן, וְגַם מַהַרְשָׁ״א בְּחִדּוּשֵׁי אַגָּדוֹת שָׁם כָּתַב ״וְהֵשִׁיב וְכוּלֵיהּ״, עַיֵּין שָׁם]

and subsequently I saw in the emendations of the Gra that he emended the text thus, and the Maharsha in Chiddushei Aggados there likewise wrote "and he answered, etc.", see there];1158Sanhedrin 100a-b; the marginal reading, the Gra, and Maharsha - identifying the speakers: Rav Tzadok notes that the attribution of the exchange affects the proposed reconciliation. The surrounding passage is transmitted with variant speaker labels; the marginal reading has 'R' Yehuda,' while the Gra emends the wording into a dialogue, and Maharsha's expression 'and he answered' likewise treats the latter clause as a response. If the speaker is the ordinary R' Yehuda, Rav Tzadok can associate the passage with R' Yehuda b'Rebbi Ilai's position in Bereishis Rabbah. He nevertheless acknowledges that making the entire exchange one speaker's statement is forced. This is textual analysis of the sugya's attribution, not an independent ruling about the nature of Gehinnom.
וּמֵ״אִשָּׁם״ הוּא דְּדָיֵיק דְּאֵינוֹ אֵשׁ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם
and from the word "their fire" (isham) he infers that it is not the external fire of Gehinnom;
וְרַק אַאֵשׁ חִיצוֹנִי דְּגֵיהִנָּם שַׁיָּיךְ הֲגָנַת הַמִּצְוֹת דּוּגְמַת זָהָב אַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וְלֹא אַאֵשׁ שֶׁמִּגּוּפָם וּמֵעַצְמָם
and only regarding the external fire of Gehinnom does the protection of mitzvos apply (like the gold upon the Altar), but not against the internal fire born of their own body and deeds.
וּמִמַּה שֶּׁאָמַר ״לֹא תִכְבֶּה״ מַשְׁמַע דְּגַם הִיא בּוֹעֶרֶת לְעוֹלָם וְאֵין מְכַלָּה אוֹתָם
And from the phrasing "shall not be quenched," it implies that it too burns eternally without consuming them;
אַךְ מִלְּשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב ״אֵשׁ תֹּאכַלְכֶם״ דְּמַיְיתֵי מִדְרָשׁ הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, מַשְׁמַע דְּהֵם נֶאֱכָלִים לְגַמְרֵי עַל יְדֵי אוֹתוֹ אֵשׁ
yet from the scriptural phrase "a fire shall consume you" cited in the Midrash above, it implies that they are entirely consumed by that fire;
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר מַה שֶּׁאָמַר ״לֹא תִכְבֶּה״, הַיְינוּ עַד שֶׁתֹּאכְלֵם
and one can say that what it stated, "shall not be quenched," means until it consumes them;
וְרָצָה לוֹמַר: הָא דְּעַל יְדֵי גֵּיהִנָּם אֵין נֶאֱכָלִים רַק אַחַר כָּךְ עַל יְדֵי אֵשׁ דְּגוּפָן, עַל כָּרְחֲךָ מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין אֵשׁ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׁוֹלֵט
meaning: the fact that they are not consumed by Gehinnom, but only subsequently by the internal fire of their own body, perforce is because the fire of Gehinnom has no dominion to consume them;
וּמוּכָח דְּגַם בְּהוּ אֵין שׁוֹלֵט
and it is proven that even over them it lacks dominion;
וּבָרַיְיתָא דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין לְפִי זֶה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וּבָרַיְיתָא דִּפְסָחִים דְּקָאֵי אַאוּר דְּגֵיהִנָּם וּמַיְיתֵי מִגּוֹיִם:
and the Baraisa of Sanhedrin according to this accords with Rabbi Yehudah, while the Baraisa of Pesachim refers to the external fire of Gehinnom, deriving its lesson from the gentiles.

items.h: סִימָן ט״ו: סְעִיפִים ע״ג–ע״ט [1159: Chagigah 27a; Yeshayahu 33:11 - external fire, internal fire, and 'until it consumes them': Chagigah's kal vachomer concerns the 'fire of Gehinnom' and compares the sinners of Israel to the gold plating of the altar; its image is therefore an external fire that fails to dominate what mitzvos protect. Bereishis Rabbah's fire that emerges from the wicked person's own body is a different category. Rav Tzadok's final distinction - mitzvos shield from external Gehinnom fire but not from a fire generated from within - is his conceptual synthesis. His reading of 'it shall not be extinguished' as 'not until it consumes them' reconciles that phrase with 'your spirit is a fire that shall consume you' by describing uninterrupted burning until completion, rather than eternal burning after the person has been consumed.]

The theme: Analyzing the Talmudic conclusion regarding the cessation of Gehinnom. In Rosh Hashanah 17a, the Gemara concludes: "and their form shall wear away Sheol (l'valos She'ol)" (Tehillim 49:15), indicating that Sheol itself wears away while the heretics are not consumed. The Rama MiFano in Asarah Ma'amaros suggests that "they are not consumed" is ultimately to their advantage: when Gehinnom wears away, the fire ceases, releasing them from suffering into an existence devoid of pain. R' Tzadok questions this: why should severe heretics fare better than bodily sinners who are turned to ashes? Perhaps remaining without a portion in the World to Come while beholding the joy of the righteous is itself a profound torment ("these shall eat and these shall hunger... and you shall cry for sorrow of heart", Yeshayah 65:13–14).

p: אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת בַּגְּמָרָא שָׁם מְסַיֵּים עֲלַהּ: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְצוּרָם לְבַלּוֹת שְׁאוֹל״ (תְּהִלִּים מ״ט:ט״ו)
But in truth, in the Gemara there (Rosh Hashanah 17a) it concludes upon it: as it is said, "and their form shall wear away the netherworld" (Tehillim 49:15);
מַשְׁמַע דְּעַל מִ״לְּבַלּוֹת שְׁאוֹל״ יָלֵיף דְּגֵיהִנָּם כָּלָה, וְלֹא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ מִ״וְאִשָּׁם לֹא תִכְבֶּה״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ס״ו:כ״ד)
implying that from the phrase "to wear away the netherworld" it derives that Gehinnom wears away and ceases, and not as they expounded from "their fire shall not be quenched" (Yeshayah 66:24);
וְאִם כֵּן גַּם בָּרַיְיתָא דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מְפָרֵשׁ ״וְאִשָּׁם״ אַאוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם
and if so, the Baraisa of Rosh Hashanah likewise interprets "their fire" as referring to the external fire of Gehinnom.
וְכֵן מַשְׁמַע לְשׁוֹן ״וְנִידּוֹנִין בָּהּ וְכוּלֵיהּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְכוּלֵיהּ״, מַשְׁמַע דִּקְרָא דְּ״וְיָצְאוּ וְגוֹמֵר וְאִשָּׁם וְגוֹמֵר״ אַדִּין דְּבָהּ בְּגֵיהִנָּם קָאֵי

And so implies the wording "and they are judged therein, etc., as it is said, etc.," which implies that the verse "And they shall go forth... for their fire shall not be quenched" refers to the judgment executed therein within Gehinnom;1160Rosh Hashanah 17a: “The transgressors of Israel with their bodies [and the transgressors of the nations with their bodies] descend to Gehinnom [and are judged there twelve months]; afterward Gehinnom is consumed and they are [reduced to] ash” — with the concluding qualification “and their Rock is to consume in the grave.”1161Rosh Hashanah 17a; Tehillim 49:15; Rashi - the Bavli's actual prooftext: The baraisa first quotes Yeshayahu 66:24 for the exceptional classes who are judged for generations. The Gemara then adds that Gehinnom is consumed while they are not consumed, citing 've-tzuram levalos she'ol mi-zevul lo' from Tehillim 49:15. Rashi explains 've-tzuram' as 'their form' and treats the later reference to zevul as the Temple. Rav Tzadok's textual observation is therefore precise: the Bavli attaches the ending of Gehinnom to the verse in Tehillim, not to the phrase 'their fire shall not be extinguished.' His question is how the two prooftexts fit together, not whether Yeshayahu describes their punishment.
וְכֵן בַּתּוֹסֶפְתָּא [פֶּרֶק י״ג דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין, הֲלָכָה ה׳] אִיתָא: ״גֵּיהִנָּם נִנְעֶלֶת בִּפְנֵיהֶם וְנִידּוֹנִין בָּהּ וְכוּלֵיהּ״

and so in the Tosefta [Sanhedrin 13:5] it is taught: "Gehinnom is locked before them and they are judged therein, etc.";1162Tosefta Sanhedrin 13:1 - 'Gehinnom is locked before them': The Tosefta states of the informers, heretics, deniers, separatists, and those who caused the public to sin that 'Gehinnom is locked before them and they are judged there for generations,' and then: 'Sheol is consumed and they are not consumed.' This wording strongly supports Rav Tzadok's reading that Yeshayahu 66:24 describes a judgment taking place inside Gehinnom. The Tosefta says 'Sheol is consumed,' whereas the Bavli states 'Gehinnom is consumed' and cites Tehillim 49:15; both versions contrast the ending of the penal realm with the continued existence of these offenders.
וּמַה שֶּׁאָמַר ״וְאִשָּׁם״, יֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּאֵשׁ לְכָל רָשָׁע מְיוּחָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ בְּגֵיהִנָּם, וּמִשֶּׁנִּגְמַר דִּינוֹ כָּבָה אוֹתוֹ אֵשׁ, וְשֶׁלָּהֶם אֵינוֹ כָּבָה

and as for stating "their fire," one can say that there is a fire designated specifically for each wicked person in Gehinnom, and once his judgment is completed that fire is quenched, whereas their personal fire is not quenched.1163Yeshayahu 66:24; Pesachim 54a - the proposal of an individualized fire: The possessive phrase 'their fire' can grammatically suggest a fire attached to the offenders themselves. Pesachim, however, cites this verse for the fire of Gehinnom created on the second day and says that it has no extinguishing forever. Rav Tzadok's suggestion that each sinner has a designated fire which is extinguished when that person's sentence ends is therefore a harmonizing interpretation, not an explicit statement of the Gemara. It allows ordinary punishment to terminate while reserving the unextinguished fire for the exceptional classes named in Rosh Hashanah.
אַךְ לְפִי זֶה דְּהֵם מְבַלִּים הַשְּׁאוֹל, מַשְׁמַע דְּנִכְלָה לְגַמְרֵי וְאֵשׁ אַחֵר לֵיכָּא, אִם כֵּן נִפְטָרִים מִן הַדִּין, וְהַךְ ״הֵם אֵין כָּלִין״ לִמְעַלְיוּתָא הוּא
